lens.title: Compute-Matched Infilling: Does Diffusion's Two-Sided-Context Advantage Survive an NFE Budget?
lens.claim: DreamOn/Dream-Coder's reported parity-with-AR on HumanEval-Infilling is achieved at a per-case denoising cost that is never reported; when infilling quality is plotted against cumulative model tokens (our cross-family cost unit), diffusion's two-sided-context advantage over AR-FIM either (H1) persists — diffusion dominates the infilling frontier at every budget, unlike from-scratch generation where it owns only the high-quality end — or (H2) collapses, i.e. the advantage is purchased with 5-20x more compute and is a budget artifact. Either outcome is a publishable result about where masked diffusion actually wins.
lens.why_now: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326, VERIFIED ICLR 2026 Poster via OpenReview forum EQTPmqukiU, venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, has Camera_Ready_Revision) reports HumanEval-Infilling single-line 92.1 vs Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 92.6 and SantaCoder-FIM 79.0 vs 79.8 — but its abstract and vendored eval harness contain ZERO compute accounting: vendor/DreamOn/eval/eval_humaneval_infilling.sh hardcodes steps=256 with no NFE/token reporting, and sweeps only min_gen_len={4,8,16,32,64}. Meanwhile CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, 2026-06-04) established that compute-matched comparison REVERSES several published MDLM remasking rankings — but CaRE only audits open-domain text (OpenWebText/LM1B, MAUVE), never code and never infilling. We are the ones holding the exact missing intersection: a measured cumulative_model_tokens instrument that already produced our surviving Pareto-segmentation claim on from-scratch generation, plus DreamOn-v0-7B on local disk. This is the same instrument, one task-surface over.
lens.experiment: Extend scripts/generate_evalplus_dreamon.py into a HumanEval-Infilling generator emitting our existing per-case sidecar (cumulative_model_tokens, nfe, elapsed_seconds, termination reason). Grid: {DreamOn-v0-7B, Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B (fixed-canvas ctrl), Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B} x {steps 32,64,128,256,512} x {SingleLine (1033 cases), RandomSpanInfillingLight (164)}. Report pass@1 vs cumulative_model_tokens, not vs steps. AR arm: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B FIM (NOT on either disk — must download ~15GB, see assets) priced in the same unit (prompt+generated tokens per forward pass). Grade with the official human-eval-infilling package (pip reachable, HTTP 200 verified). Falsification of the flat-canvas confound: include DreamOn with mask_expansion=false at matched steps, so the length-elasticity contribution is separable from the two-sided-context contribution.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: models/DreamOn-v0-7B, models/Dream-Coder-v0-{Instruct,Base}-7B; vendor/DreamOn/eval/{evaluate,generator}.py (working DDP-sharded infilling harness); scripts/generate_evalplus_dreamon.py; our cumulative_model_tokens sidecar; 8xL20A idle (all 8 GPUs at 0% util, only ~28GB/183GB resident). DOWNLOAD (all verified reachable via hy-proxy, HTTP 200): loubnabnl/humaneval_infilling SingleLine 1.6MB / MultiLine 10.5MB / RandomSpan 2.2MB / RandomSpanLight (164 cases, already pulled to /tmp), bigcode/santacoder-fim-task, pip human-eval-infilling. MISSING AND LOAD-BEARING: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is on NEITHER disk (searched wzc1 and zwfy6 per two-disk rule) — the AR arm requires a ~15GB download, and WITHOUT it this candidate degenerates into a diffusion-only cost curve with no cross-family claim. Note .73 is already running a DreamOn infilling eval — coordinate to avoid duplicating the uncosted replication and instead own the cost axis.
lens.kill_criterion: Killed if diffusion and AR-FIM curves cross at no budget AND diffusion is within 1.3x of AR cost at matched pass@1 — that means infilling cost accounting is uninteresting because nobody was flattered by omitting it, and the honest writeup is a short negative note, not a paper. Also killed if our reproduction of DreamOn single-line lands >5 points below the published 92.1 at steps=256 (protocol not aligned; we would be measuring our own harness bug, exactly the retraction-1 failure mode). Directional pre-registration required: state before running whether we predict H1 or H2, so that neither outcome can be narrativised post hoc.
lens.builds_on: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026 Poster). Defect repaired: complete absence of compute accounting on the one task surface where the paper claims AR parity — a 'wins at unstated cost' convention that CaRE (2607.24763) proved reverses rankings elsewhere. Also repairs the harness's hardcoded benchmark_name='single-line' (vendor/DreamOn/eval/evaluate.py line ~95), which is why the published table has no RandomSpanInfilling column.

diff.sharpened_claim: On HumanEval-Infilling and SantaCoder-FIM, DreamOn's headline "parity with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B" is a fixed-nominal-steps comparison (steps=256, initial mask length 64, mask-expansion cap L_max=128) whose per-case denoising cost is never placed in a unit commensurable with the AR-FIM baseline. We re-plot the same benchmarks against cumulative_model_tokens -- the cost unit that already produced our from-scratch Pareto-segmentation result -- and report where on the infilling frontier each family actually wins. We pre-register the direction and additionally decompose the diffusion advantage into (i) length elasticity (mask_expansion on/off at matched steps) and (ii) two-sided context (fixed-canvas Dream-Coder-Instruct control), so that the frontier's shape is attributable rather than merely observed. Secondary and independently defensible: DreamOn's own harness hardcodes read_problems(benchmark_name='single-line') (vendor/DreamOn/eval/evaluate.py:95), so RandomSpanInfilling has never been reported for any diffusion infilling model; we add that column. The claim is deliberately outcome-symmetric: diffusion dominating at every budget and diffusion's advantage being a budget artifact are both results about where masked diffusion's structural advantage is real, and the cost instrument is the contribution either way.
diff.differentiation_statement: No prior work plots code-infilling quality against a cross-family compute unit for diffusion versus AR-FIM. The three nearest works each miss exactly one axis of the intersection we hold. DreamOn (ICLR 2026 Poster, first public 2025-10-08) establishes the AR-parity claim on HumanEval-Infilling/SantaCoder-FIM but prices it only in nominal steps: its Table 1 headline carries no step or token column at all, and the one place step counts appear (Sec. 5.4 / Fig. 4, "total inference steps from as high as 122.8 to just 52.4") is a diffusion-vs-diffusion broadcasting ablation on the multi-line subset, never a diffusion-vs-AR accounting. CaRE (2026-06-04, concurrent) is the compute-aware protocol that proves matched-NFE comparison reverses published MDLM rankings, but it audits remasking strategies on open-domain text (OpenWebText/LM1B, MAUVE) at 4 stochasticity levels -- no code, no infilling, no AR arm, and NFE-per-strategy rather than a cross-family token unit. "How Efficient Are Diffusion Language Models?" (2025-10-21) does compare AR and DLM throughput head-to-head but never touches infilling and reports no code-execution benchmark. The remaining infilling-adjacent works are either diffusion-only (CAL, 2026-01-31, which does report a "Stps." overhead column but only for its own length search, against fixed-length diffusion baselines, with no AR baseline) or concurrent and uncosted (ARR May 2026 submission Ni6xxPzBlz, first public 2026-06-02, which is the only work with a genuine AR-vs-diffusion infilling head-to-head -- 68.3% AR vs 54.3% diffusion execution accuracy -- but reaches its 90.2% headline by generating 16 candidates from both models with execution filtering and MBR, i.e. an uncosted ~16x multiplier on a 1.5B backbone). So: same benchmark as DreamOn, different reported axis; same cost philosophy as CaRE, different task surface, model family, and cost unit; same AR-vs-diffusion question as Ni6xxPzBlz, but at 7B, on the ICLR-published length-elastic model, and with the compute axis that paper omits. A reviewer is being asked to accept a measurement-and-attribution contribution on a published parity claim, which is a recognised genre, not a novelty claim.

followup_openings.target_paper: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026 Poster)
followup_openings.defect: The headline AR-parity table (Table 1: single-line 92.1 vs Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 92.6; SantaCoder-FIM 79.0 vs 79.8) carries no compute column. Sec. 4.2 states diffusion models use mask length 64 by default with steps=256, while AR models use their pretraining infilling templates -- i.e. the diffusion arm gets up to 256 full-canvas bidirectional forward passes (canvas expandable to L_max=128) and the AR arm gets one forward pass per emitted token, and the two are tabled side by side as comparable. Step counts do exist in the paper but only in Sec. 5.4/Fig. 4 as a diffusion-internal broadcasting ablation on the multi-line subset, never mapped onto the AR comparison and never converted to a family-neutral unit.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run the same benchmarks with our per-case sidecar (cumulative_model_tokens, nfe, elapsed_seconds, termination reason) over steps in {32,64,128,256,512}, and plot pass@1 against cumulative_model_tokens with the Qwen2.5-Coder-7B FIM arm priced in the identical unit (prompt + generated tokens re-attended per forward pass). Report matched-quality cost ratios and matched-cost quality gaps, and state whether the curves cross.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Parity claims are what motivate adopting diffusion for infilling at all. If parity costs 5-20x the tokens, the correct engineering conclusion inverts, and the field's one strongest 'diffusion structurally wins here' datapoint needs an asterisk. If parity is genuinely cheap or diffusion dominates at every budget, that is the first compute-honest evidence for a structural diffusion advantage anywhere -- much stronger than the current unpriced table.

followup_openings.target_paper: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326) -- harness defect
followup_openings.defect: vendor/DreamOn/eval/evaluate.py line 95 is literally read_problems(benchmark_name='single-line'), hardcoded. The released harness cannot evaluate the multi-line or random-span splits of HumanEval-Infilling without a source edit, and eval/eval_humaneval_infilling.sh sweeps only min_gen_len in {4,8,16,32,64} at fixed steps=256. This is the mechanical reason no diffusion infilling paper reports a RandomSpanInfilling column.
followup_openings.our_fix: Parameterise benchmark_name and add the RandomSpanInfilling split (and RandomSpanInfillingLight, 164 cases, already staged). Random spans break span-boundary alignment with the tokenizer and with function-level structure, which is precisely the regime where a fixed-canvas assumption should hurt most -- so this is also the sharpest test of the length-elasticity claim, not just a coverage gap.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts 'diffusion matches AR on infilling' from a two-cell claim into a task-surface curve, and it is cheap: the split is 2.2MB and the harness edit is one line plus a config passthrough. It also lets us say whether DreamOn's published advantage is specific to line-aligned spans -- an untested-regime finding that stands even if the cost story comes out flat.

followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, 2026-06-04, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Establishes that compute-matched comparison reverses published MDLM rankings, but only on open-domain text (OpenWebText, LM1B) with MAUVE and generative-perplexity-family metrics, on base models (LLaDA-8B-Base, Dream-7B-Base), auditing remasking strategies against each other. There is no AR baseline, no execution-graded task, and no infilling. The reversal claim is therefore demonstrated only where the quality metric is distributional and the comparison is intra-family.
followup_openings.our_fix: Test whether CaRE's reversal phenomenon survives (a) an execution-graded, non-distributional metric (evalplus/human-eval-infilling functional correctness, where MAUVE-style entropy confounds cannot operate) and (b) a cross-family comparison against AR-FIM. Adopt CaRE's discipline -- report actual NFE not nominal steps, fix temperature/top_p explicitly, control stochasticity -- while replacing NFE with cumulative_model_tokens, since NFE is not commensurable across families (a diffusion forward pass over a 512-token canvas and an AR forward pass over a 40-token suffix both count as 1 NFE). This is a cost-unit critique of CaRE itself, made from the same side of the argument.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It is the natural extension of a concurrent framework into the domain where the stakes are highest (code, where correctness is objectively gradeable) and simultaneously repairs its cost unit for cross-family use. Being concurrent, CaRE cannot preempt us; citing it as motivation while fixing its accounting unit is the strongest available framing.

followup_openings.target_paper: How Efficient Are Diffusion Language Models? A Critical Examination of Efficiency Evaluation Practices (arXiv:2510.18480, 2025-10-21)
followup_openings.defect: Concludes AR consistently out-throughputs DLMs, but evaluates only left-to-right from-scratch generation -- grep of the full text finds zero occurrences of 'infilling', 'fill-in-the-middle', or 'FIM', and the only benchmark named is GSM8K. It thus indicts DLM efficiency exclusively on AR's home turf, the identical scoping failure we diagnosed in our own prior work. Its throughput unit is also hardware- and batch-size-dependent, which it acknowledges but does not escape.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the efficiency question on the one task surface where the diffusion architecture has a structural claim (two-sided-context infilling), with a hardware-independent unit (cumulative_model_tokens) alongside wall-clock. If DLMs still lose on cost here, that materially strengthens their conclusion by removing its most obvious rebuttal ('you only tested where AR is supposed to win'). If DLMs win here, we have located the exception their paper cannot see.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Either direction is a citable sharpening of an existing efficiency critique rather than a fresh claim, and it pre-empts the reviewer objection that our own cost instrument is just re-deriving a known negative result.

followup_openings.target_paper: Discrete Diffusion Models for Code: Bidirectional Infilling and Hybrid Autoregressive-Diffusion Pipelines (OpenReview Ni6xxPzBlz, ACL ARR 2026 May, first public 2026-06-02, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: The only AR-vs-diffusion code-infilling head-to-head we found, and it reports the honest single-sample result (AR 68.3% vs diffusion 54.3% execution accuracy on standard infilling; diffusion 84% vs AR 32% on multi-site editing). But its headline numbers -- 90.2% single-line with 16 candidates, 75.6% HumanEval pass@1 with 48 candidates 'surpassing DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B despite a 4.5x smaller backbone' -- come from best-of-N with execution filtering and MBR, with no compute accounting whatsoever. A 48-candidate 1.5B pipeline is not obviously cheaper than a 1-sample 6.7B model, and the size-efficiency framing is unsupportable without that arithmetic. Backbone is Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B only, so no scale check.
followup_openings.our_fix: Price best-of-N candidate generation in cumulative_model_tokens and check whether the 'smaller backbone wins' claim survives; run at 7B where we have both families natively (DreamOn-v0-7B, Dream-Coder-v0-{Base,Instruct}-7B, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) to test scale-robustness of the regime split it reports. Their single-sample regime split (AR wins standard infilling, diffusion wins multi-site editing) is a directional prediction we can independently test at 7B on a shared cost axis -- and note it points opposite to DreamOn's parity claim, which is itself a finding worth surfacing.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the single closest work and it is concurrent, so it does not preempt us; better, it hands us a pre-registered disagreement to adjudicate (DreamOn says diffusion reaches AR parity on single-line infilling at 7B; this paper says AR beats diffusion by 14 points on infilling at 1.5B). Resolving that on a compute-matched axis is a cleaner paper than either hypothesis H1/H2 alone.

followup_openings.target_paper: Diffusion LMs Can Approximate Optimal Infilling Lengths Implicitly (CAL, arXiv:2602.00476, 2026-01-31)
followup_openings.defect: Directly competes with DreamOn on length-adaptive HumanEval-Infilling and does partially account for compute -- a 'Stps.' column showing 11-18 additional first-step forward passes, argued 'acceptable given the substantial capability improvements'. But the accounting covers only the marginal overhead of its own length search, never the total denoising cost, and every baseline is diffusion (LLaDA-Base, DreamCoder, DAEDAL). There is no AR arm anywhere, so 'acceptable overhead' is judged against no external cost reference.
followup_openings.our_fix: Add CAL-style training-free length search as a third length-handling arm alongside DreamOn's learned expand/contract and the fixed canvas, and price all three in total cumulative_model_tokens rather than marginal extra steps. This yields a three-way length-policy comparison on one cost axis -- something neither DreamOn nor CAL provides, since each compares only against fixed-length baselines.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It cleanly separates 'was the gain from length elasticity or from paying more compute' for the two competing length-adaptive methods at once, and it upgrades our falsification control (mask_expansion=false) from a binary toggle into a policy ladder. Also directly serves the mask_expansion attribution leg the candidate already plans.

related_work.citation: Wu, Z. et al. DreamOn: Diffusion Language Models For Code Infilling Beyond Fixed-size Canvas. arXiv:2602.01326; ICLR 2026 Poster.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster. Verified via OpenReview forum EQTPmqukiU: venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference', invitations include Submission19236/-/Camera_Ready_Revision. PDF header reads 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Adds two length-control states ([expand]/[delete]) to masked diffusion so the canvas grows/shrinks during denoising. Reports HumanEval-Infilling single-line 92.1 (Dream-Coder-7B 55.5 base) and multi-line 63.8, SantaCoder-FIM 79.0, vs AR Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 92.6 / 58.7 / 79.8. Ablates loss balancing, in-place deletion, deletion broadcasting; Sec 5.4 reports total diffusion steps 122.8 -> 52.4 with broadcasting (2.1x speedup) on the multi-line subset.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No compute column on the headline AR-comparison table. Step counts appear only in a diffusion-internal ablation, never mapped to the AR arm and never in a family-neutral unit. Diffusion arm fixed at mask length 64 / steps=256 while AR uses pretraining FIM templates -- an asymmetry stated in Sec 4.2 but not priced. No RandomSpanInfilling. Python only. No wall-clock or token-cost frontier.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Accounting asymmetry: 256 full-canvas bidirectional passes (canvas up to L_max=128) versus one AR pass per emitted token, tabled as directly comparable. (2) Harness hardcodes read_problems(benchmark_name='single-line') at vendor/DreamOn/eval/evaluate.py:95, so multi-line/random-span require a source edit -- structurally why the random-span column is missing everywhere. (3) eval_humaneval_infilling.sh fixes steps=256 and sweeps only min_gen_len {4,8,16,32,64}, so no step-budget sensitivity exists for the headline numbers. (4) eval/generator.py contains no NFE/token counters (grep for nfe|num_forward|step_count|cumulative finds only a top-p cumsum). (5) Single language, single benchmark family.
related_work.verified_how: OpenReview api2 notes/search (venue + venueid + Camera_Ready_Revision invitation); arXiv abs page (v1 submitted 1 Feb 2026); full PDF pulled and pdftotext'd, Tables 1-3 and Sec 4.2/5.4 read directly; vendored harness inspected on local disk at /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/vendor/DreamOn/eval/.

related_work.citation: Shah, Y., Chakraborty, A., Gupta, V. CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models. arXiv:2607.24763.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. No OpenReview record (searched notes/search for the exact title; returns only unrelated remasking papers). DBLP returns 0 hits for 'CaRE Compute-aware Remasking'. S2 lists it with empty venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: Compute-aware audit framework standardizing actual NFE, enforcing multi-metric reporting, controlling stochasticity. Applied to 7 remasking strategies x LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base x 4 stochasticity levels x 3 step budgets on OpenWebText and LM1B. Finds temperature explains most MAUVE variance; compute-matched comparison reverses several published strategy rankings; informed remasking and stochastic unmasking are in tension. Leaderboard over 12 MDLMs, 150M-8B.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Open-domain text only -- no code, no infilling, no execution-graded metric. No AR baseline: the entire audit is intra-family (remasking strategy vs remasking strategy). NFE as the unit is not cross-family commensurable. Base models only, no instruct/code-adapted checkpoints.
related_work.known_defects: NFE counts forward passes without weighting sequence length, so it cannot compare a diffusion pass over a 512-token canvas against an AR pass over a 40-token suffix -- fine for the intra-family audit it performs, unusable for the cross-family claim it motivates others to make. MAUVE and generative perplexity are distributional proxies the paper itself shows are entropy/temperature-confounded, so the 'ranking reversal' finding is demonstrated on the most confound-prone metric class available. Concurrent, so it cannot preempt.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page + citation_date meta (2026/06/04, [Submitted on 4 Jun 2026]); full abstract read; OpenReview notes/search and DBLP publ/api both queried for venue and returned no record.

related_work.citation: Diffusion LMs Can Approximate Optimal Infilling Lengths Implicitly (CAL: Calibrated Adaptive Length). arXiv:2602.00476.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv abs page shows no journal-ref and no venue comment). Not verified at any 2026 venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: Training-free length selection for diffusion infilling from first-step denoising confidence (an 'Oracle Peak' near ground-truth length plus a systematic 'Length Bias' to calibrate). Evaluates on HumanEval-Infilling single-line and multi-line plus text infilling (stories, abstracts, reviews). Reports up to +47.7% pass@1 over fixed-length baselines and beats DAEDAL; reports a 'Stps.' column indicating 11-18 additional first-step forward passes.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No AR baseline anywhere -- all comparisons are diffusion-internal (LLaDA-Base, DreamCoder, DAEDAL, fixed-length). Compute accounting covers only its own search overhead, not total denoising cost. No step-budget sweep. Cites DreamOn but does not compare compute against it.
related_work.known_defects: 'Overhead is acceptable given the substantial capability improvements' is asserted with no external cost reference, since no AR arm exists to define what acceptable means. Marginal-overhead accounting systematically flatters any method whose base cost is already large -- 11-18 extra passes on top of an unreported 256-step base is a <10% surcharge presented as the whole cost story. Same benchmark and same length-adaptivity goal as DreamOn but no head-to-head cost comparison, so the two length policies remain unranked.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page ([Submitted on 31 Jan 2026], no comments/journal-ref); full PDF pulled and pdftotext'd; overhead passage (Sec 5.2) and benchmark mentions read directly; grep confirms 12 HumanEval-Infilling references and zero Qwen2.5-Coder/AR-baseline references.

related_work.citation: How Efficient Are Diffusion Language Models? A Critical Examination of Efficiency Evaluation Practices. arXiv:2510.18480 (v3, 10 Nov 2025).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (no journal-ref, no venue comment on arXiv). Not verified at a venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: Systematic AR-vs-DLM throughput study. Concludes AR generally achieves higher throughput and DLMs consistently lag; identifies flaws in prior efficiency evaluation (single-instance inference, fixed generation length); theoretical throughput model; finds dual-cache and parallel decoding gains concentrate at small batch sizes and diminish with scale.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Evaluates only left-to-right from-scratch generation. Full-text grep finds zero occurrences of 'infill', 'fill-in-the-middle', or 'FIM'; the only benchmark named is GSM8K (3 mentions), no code-execution benchmark. So the conclusion is drawn entirely on AR's home turf.
related_work.known_defects: Scoping: indicts DLM efficiency without testing the one task family where the architecture has a structural claim (two-sided-context infilling), leaving the obvious rebuttal open. Throughput is hardware- and batch-size-dependent, which the paper flags as a problem in others' work but does not escape in its own -- no hardware-independent token or FLOP unit is adopted. No execution-graded quality axis, so it reports speed largely decoupled from correctness.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page ([Submitted on 21 Oct 2025], v3 10 Nov 2025); full PDF downloaded and pdftotext'd; grep -i for infill/FIM returned zero hits, benchmark-name grep returned only GSM8K.

related_work.citation: Discrete Diffusion Models for Code: Bidirectional Infilling and Hybrid Autoregressive-Diffusion Pipelines. OpenReview Ni6xxPzBlz, ACL ARR 2026 May Submission.
related_work.venue_status: ACL ARR 2026 May Submission (under review). Verified via OpenReview: venue='ACL ARR 2026 May Submission', venueid='aclweb.org/ACL/ARR/2026/May/Submission'. odate 2026-06-02 (first public), cdate 2026-05-21. No arXiv version found (arXiv title search for 'Discrete Diffusion Models for Code' returns 0 hits).
related_work.what_it_covers: MDLM on a Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B backbone versus AR on code. Reports a regime split: multi-site editing diffusion 84% exact match vs AR 32%; standard infilling AR 68.3% execution accuracy vs diffusion 54.3%. Hybrid multi-candidate pipeline with execution filtering + MBR: 90.2% execution accuracy on single-line infilling at 16 candidates (+21.9pp over AR alone); 75.6% pass@1 on HumanEval at 48 candidates. Execution-guided iterative refinement via error tracebacks re-masking failing regions. Oracle analysis shows AR and diffusion fail on largely disjoint subsets.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No compute accounting for the best-of-N pipeline. Single 1.5B backbone, so no scale check and no test on the ICLR-published length-elastic model. Its single-sample infilling verdict (AR > diffusion by 14 points) directly contradicts DreamOn's parity claim at 7B and the contradiction is not addressed.
related_work.known_defects: The headline 'surpasses DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B despite a 4.5x smaller backbone' compares 48 candidates from a 1.5B model against presumably 1 sample from a 6.7B model, with no arithmetic showing the smaller model is actually cheaper -- 48 x 1.5B likely exceeds 1 x 6.7B, which would invert the framing. Same 'wins at unstated cost' convention as DreamOn, one level worse because best-of-N is an explicit compute multiplier. MBR consensus and execution filtering both consume additional compute that is not separated. Concurrent, so it cannot preempt.
related_work.verified_how: OpenReview api2 notes/search returned the note with venue, venueid, invitations, cdate/odate; abstract read in full from the note content; arXiv API title search confirmed no arXiv preprint exists.

related_work.citation: Understanding Evaluation Illusion in Diffusion Large Language Models. arXiv:2606.29228 (v2, 1 Jul 2026).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (no journal-ref or venue comment on arXiv).
related_work.what_it_covers: Rigorous re-evaluation of dLLM decoding methods across evaluation settings. Finds the ranking of decoding methods is highly sensitive to prompt template choice; single-template evaluation creates an 'illusion' that decoding methods improve efficiency without quality loss; parallel decoding consistently underperforms single-token decoding, failing to beat the speed-quality tradeoff. Proposes reliable-evaluation guidelines.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Decoding/parallel-decoding methods on standard prompted generation, not infilling and not cross-family. No AR baseline priced on a shared cost axis. Prompt-template sensitivity is the axis of interest, not compute accounting per se.
related_work.known_defects: Establishes that dLLM efficiency claims are protocol artifacts but does so only within the prompted-generation setting, so the infilling surface -- where the structural argument for diffusion actually lives -- is untested. The prompt-template confound it identifies is itself a threat to our own protocol that we must control (our AR arm's FIM template choice is exactly such a lever), which makes it a methodological dependency for us rather than a competitor. Concurrent.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page ([Submitted on 28 Jun 2026], v2 1 Jul 2026); full abstract read.

related_work.citation: Any-Order Flexible Length Masked Diffusion (FlexMDMs). arXiv:2509.01025 (v2, 7 Sep 2025).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv comments field reads 'Preprint').
related_work.what_it_covers: Stochastic-interpolant extension of masked diffusion supporting token insertion, hence flexible-length generation with any-order inference retained. Matches MDM perplexity with better length statistics; ~60% higher success on synthetic maze planning; retrofits LLaDA-8B in 3 days on 16 H100s, improving GSM8K 58->67 and code infilling 52->65.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The code-infilling number (52->65) is a single cell with no benchmark protocol detail in the abstract, no AR baseline, and no compute accounting. General-purpose model, not code-specialised. No step-budget sweep.
related_work.known_defects: Length elasticity is claimed as the mechanism for the infilling gain without an ablation isolating it from added training compute, and without pricing inference. Prior to DreamOn on the length-elasticity idea, which weakens DreamOn's novelty framing but not ours (we make no length-elasticity claim; we measure the cost of one).
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page ([Submitted on 31 Aug 2025], v2 7 Sep 2025, comments 'Preprint'); full abstract read.

feas.risk: The single most likely outcome is a CONFOUNDED result that is really an arithmetic identity dressed as a measurement. I already computed the answer from measured passes plus the repo's own closed-form AR cost model, and it comes out ~2.0x on attended_context_sum for every split (2.06 / 2.06 / 2.02 on SingleLine / RandomSpan / MultiLine) because it reduces to 2M(P+M)/(MP) -- the 2 being DreamOn's expand/delete double-forward per emitted token, and the M cancelling. A paper reporting "diffusion infilling costs ~2x AR at matched quality" would be reporting the implementation's bookkeeping overhead and the cancellation of the middle length, not a property of masked diffusion. The mirror-image risk is reporting the tokens_fed column instead (14-58x) and calling it a 'budget artifact' finding, when that column is just measuring that AR has a KV cache and diffusion does not -- a known fact needing no experiment. Second most likely: a NULL, because with the step axis dead the surviving knobs move NFE by only ~2x (tt=1->2) over which quality barely moves, so the frontier is two nearly-coincident points per model and the kill_criterion's "within 1.3x at matched pass@1" fires. Third: the reproduction gate fails on sampler alignment (our own top_p 1.0->0.95 moved HumanEval 14.6 points) and 90% of the budget is spent debugging our harness rather than measuring DreamOn -- retraction 1's failure mode relocated to the protocol layer.
feas.required_control: A THREE-POINT DEGENERATE-AND-ORACLE BRACKET pushed through the byte-identical grader call before any arm is read, PLUS pre-registered dual-column cost reporting with an identity check. Concretely: (1) score an empty middle (""), (2) score a middle that verbatim copies the suffix, and (3) score middle = canonical_solution, all through the same `evaluate_infilling_functional_correctness` invocation the real arms use -- and refuse to interpret any arm until (3) is ~1.0 and (1)/(2) sit at the degenerate floor. This is the direct analogue of retraction 1 (a verifier where empty solutions scored full marks), and it is the only control that catches it, because infilling makes the failure far MORE likely than in from-scratch generation: the grader reassembles prefix + our middle + suffix, and a model that emits nothing or echoes the suffix can still produce syntactically valid, sometimes passing code -- i.e. an empty generation can score without the model having infilled anything. (2) specifically catches the two-sided-context claim collapsing into suffix-copying, which would otherwise be scored as diffusion "winning". (3) also validates that the prefix/middle/suffix splice and the tokenizer boundary are correct, which is where DreamOn's `generations.append(decode(response[0, prefix_len : prefix_len + response_length]))` slice is fragile once expand/delete has shifted positions -- an off-by-N there is retraction 2 (a stage silently discarding its input) in new clothing. Bolted onto this: BOTH tokens_fed and attended_context_sum must be declared in the pre-registration and published in both panels, together with the closed-form prediction for each ratio (2M(P+M)/(MP) and (P+M)/(P/M) respectively) shown alongside the measured value, so that any reported ratio which merely reproduces its own algebra is visibly labelled as such rather than narrated as a finding -- the retraction-3 control, applied to a denominator choice instead of a dropped-tail average.

lens.title: Span-Length Mismatch Is the Whole Story: A Length-Stratified Audit of Diffusion Infilling
lens.claim: DreamOn's headline advantage is concentrated almost entirely in cases where the ground-truth middle length is far from the canvas prior, and largely vanishes on cases where a fixed canvas happens to fit. Concretely: partitioning HumanEval-Infilling by ground-truth middle token length, the DreamOn-minus-fixed-canvas delta is a monotone increasing function of |gt_len - canvas_len|, and on the well-matched stratum the delta is statistically indistinguishable from zero. This reframes 'variable-length diffusion beats AR at infilling' as 'variable-length diffusion fixes a canvas-misspecification penalty that AR never had'.
lens.why_now: DreamOn's own framing concedes the mechanism ('This constraint severely degrades code infilling performance when the predefined mask size mismatches the ideal completion length') and it reports matching ORACLE performance achieved with ground-truth length — which means the oracle-length control EXISTS in their paper but is used to claim an upper bound, never to decompose where the gain lives. Nobody has stratified. Verified-empty arXiv queries: diffusion+multi-span (zero hits), diffusion+'oracle length' (zero relevant hits). The nearest work, 'From Interface to Inference' (arXiv:2607.26504, 2026-07-29) diagnoses exactly this class of problem as 'positional uncertainty' in fixed-canvas token-level models and proposes insertion-based MDLM — but it is CONCURRENT (public 2026-07-29, well after the 2026-05-07 cutoff), trains a 7B FlexMDM rather than auditing DreamOn, and does no length stratification of an existing released model. It corroborates that the axis is live rather than preempting us.
lens.experiment: No training. Tokenize each HumanEval-Infilling canonical middle to get gt_len; bin into quartiles. For each bin run DreamOn-v0-7B at canvas priors min_gen_len in {4,8,16,32,64} (DreamOn's own published sweep) plus a matched fixed-canvas Dream-Coder-Instruct arm and an oracle-length arm (canvas exactly = gt_len). Primary readout: per-stratum pass@1 delta with paired bootstrap 95% CI over cases (our standard aggregation), plus a regression of delta on |gt_len - canvas|. Secondary: does DreamOn's learned expand/delete actually converge to gt_len, measured as final canvas length vs gt_len per stratum — this tests whether length elasticity is calibrated or merely permissive. Use SingleLine (1033) + RandomSpanInfillingLight (164) for tractability; MultiLine (5815) as a confirmation stratum if budget allows.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: models/DreamOn-v0-7B and Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B; vendor/DreamOn harness which ALREADY exposes min_gen_len/max_gen_len/mask_expansion/delete_eos_token as dotlist args (so the sweep is config-only); our paired-bootstrap aggregation code from the CoMem/PaperA work; tokenizer for gt_len binning. DOWNLOAD: humaneval_infilling splits (1.6-10.5MB, verified 200), human-eval-infilling pip pkg. NO AR model needed — this is a within-diffusion decomposition, so the missing Qwen2.5-Coder is NOT a blocker. This is the cheapest candidate on the list and the one most robust to asset gaps.
lens.kill_criterion: Killed if the DreamOn-minus-fixed-canvas delta is statistically flat across length strata (all paired 95% CIs overlapping, no monotone trend in the regression of delta on |gt_len - canvas|). That would mean the gain is a genuine broad two-sided-context capability rather than a canvas-misspecification repair, which strengthens DreamOn and leaves us nothing to say. Also killed if fewer than ~150 cases land in the extreme mismatch stratum at every canvas prior (insufficient power for a stratified claim).
lens.builds_on: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026 Poster). Defect repaired: the paper measures the aggregate and the oracle ceiling but never decomposes WHERE its advantage comes from, so 'DLMs match AR at infilling' is reported at a level of aggregation that hides the fact that the comparison is against a self-inflicted canvas penalty. Cite arXiv:2607.26504 as concurrent corroboration of the positional-uncertainty mechanism.

diff.sharpened_claim: DreamOn's expand/delete mechanism is a length-repair device that is only weakly length-CALIBRATED, and the canvas-misspecification penalty it repairs is now known to be repairable training-free — so the correct question is not "does variable-length beat fixed-canvas" (settled) but "does DreamOn's learned length converge to the right length, and is any residual advantage over a training-free length-corrected baseline real once compute is matched?" Concretely we claim three things, none of which exists in the literature: (1) CALIBRATION: DreamOn's final canvas length is a biased, mode-collapsing estimator of gt_len — final_len is pulled toward the training length prior rather than toward gt_len, so its |final_len - gt_len| does NOT go to zero and grows with gt_len; a paired per-case regression of pass@1 on |final_len - gt_len| shows residual failures are concentrated exactly where the estimator misses. This tests whether length elasticity is calibrated or merely permissive, which neither DreamOn nor CAL nor LR-DLLM measures. (2) FAIR BASELINE: DreamOn's headline gain (single-line 55.5 -> 92.1) is measured against a fixed-canvas Dream-Coder baseline whose deficit is now known to be recoverable training-free; we re-measure the DreamOn advantage against a CAL-style calibrated-confidence length-search baseline built on the SAME Dream-Coder-Instruct backbone, under NFE/wall-clock-matched budgets that count DreamOn's expand/delete steps and the baseline's probe forward passes in one unit. (3) STRATIFIED RESIDUAL: after that fair baseline, the remaining DreamOn-minus-baseline delta is stratified by gt_len quartile with paired bootstrap CIs — locating whether any residual advantage lives in the extreme-mismatch tail or is uniform. Framing: "variable-length training buys length REPAIR but not length CALIBRATION, and once the fixed-canvas baseline is repaired training-free under matched compute, the case for training-based length control must rest on calibration it does not deliver."
diff.differentiation_statement: The candidate as written is largely pre-empted in its diagnostic half and must be re-aimed; but a differentiated version stands cleanly. Two pre-cutoff papers already own the "canvas misspecification is the story" framing. CAL (arXiv:2602.00476, 2026-01-31) publishes the oracle-vs-fixed decomposition on HumanEval-Infilling for four DLMs (LLaDA-Base 44.5 avg fixed vs 87.6 oracle; DreamCoder-Base 47.0 vs 88.1), plots first-step confidence explicitly as a function of the probe length relative to the oracle length (its "Oracle Peak" / "Length Bias" figures ARE a |gt_len - canvas| analysis), and states outright that "length discovery is the primary bottleneck." LR-DLLM (arXiv:2602.07546, 2026-02-07) already reports a coarse span-regime split of DreamOn showing exactly the non-uniformity the candidate predicts — on DreamCoder-7B, DreamOn helps single-line (55.5 -> 73.5) but HURTS multi-line (43.2 -> 36.1), and on McEval it degrades C++ single-line 57.3 -> 39.1 and Rust 52.2 -> 27.2 while leaving the mean unchanged at 37.2 — and calls this "inconsistent behavior across span regimes." So the specific headline "the DreamOn delta is a monotone increasing function of |gt_len - canvas| and vanishes on the matched stratum" is no longer novel-in-kind. What survives, and what no paper does, is threefold. (a) NOBODY MEASURES CALIBRATION. DreamOn's own text concedes only that "performance degrades slightly when there is a large discrepancy between the initial masked span and the true target length"; it never reports final_len vs gt_len. CAL/LR-DLLM/PILL all measure length ACCURACY of their own estimator, never DreamOn's realised final canvas length. Our secondary readout — final canvas length vs gt_len per stratum, and pass@1 regressed on |final_len - gt_len| rather than on |gt_len - initial_canvas| — is a genuinely unoccupied measurement, and it is the one that discriminates "calibrated" from "merely permissive." (b) NOBODY RUNS THE FAIR-BASELINE COMPARISON UNDER MATCHED COMPUTE. LR-DLLM compares LR-DLLM vs DreamOn but pins DreamOn to a single initial mask length (11) and equalises only a nominal MAX_LENGTH=128 "adjustment budget," not actual forward passes; CAL never evaluates DreamOn at all. Neither reports NFE or wall clock. Our arm — DreamOn vs a training-free length-corrected same-backbone baseline at matched total forward passes — is exactly the CaRE-style compute-aware audit (arXiv:2607.24763) that the variable-length subfield has not received, and it is the specific accounting error this project has already retracted results over. (c) SETTING/CONTROL DIFFERENCES ARE NON-TRIVIAL: CAL's own analysis excludes samples near the oracle length by construction (to fit its bias curve), so it structurally CANNOT report the matched stratum; we can. CAL evaluates *-Base checkpoints only; DreamOn is released only on the DreamCoder backbone; we hold the backbone fixed at Dream-Coder-Instruct/DreamOn-v0-7B and vary only the length mechanism, which is the single-variable control neither paper runs. And we add RandomSpanInfilling, which DreamOn never evaluated (its own tables are single-line / multi-line / SantaCoder-FIM only) and which our local tokenization shows is the only split with real mass in BOTH the matched and extreme-mismatch strata at small canvases.
diff.verification_notes: Verified by direct arXiv API + OpenReview API + DBLP, with full-text HTML pulled for DreamOn, CAL, LR-DLLM, and From-Interface-to-Inference. Numbers quoted from DreamOn Table 2 and LR-DLLM Tables 3/4 were read out of the extracted HTML, not from memory. VENUE STATUS CONFIRMED: DreamOn = ICLR 2026 Poster (OpenReview forum EQTPmqukiU, venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, has Camera_Ready_Revision invitation); FlexMDM = ICLR 2026 Poster + earlier NeurIPS 2025 SPIGM workshop; DAEDAL = ICLR 2026 Poster; DID (2603.23507) = ICLR 2026 per arXiv comment (NOT independently OpenReview-confirmed — treat as arXiv-comment-only); Set Diffusion = ICML 2026 per arXiv comment (NOT OpenReview-confirmed; ICML.cc/2026/Conference returns no venue record on OpenReview, so ICML 2026 acceptances are currently unverifiable through that channel — flag as weaker evidence). COULD NOT VERIFY: (1) LR-DLLM (2602.07546) venue. Its arXiv comment field is just the LaTeX template string "diffusion language models" and the body carries the ICML style header "Machine Learning, ICML", which is NOT an acceptance claim; DBLP lists it as CoRR 2026 only; OpenReview search returns nothing; Semantic Scholar rate-limited (429) on retry. I am recording it as PREPRINT. If ICML 2026 acceptance is later confirmed it is still pre-cutoff and the positioning does not change. (2) CAL (2602.00476) journal/conference venue. OpenReview surfaces a same-author, same-method workshop version titled "Training-Free Length Discovery for Diffusion Language Model Infilling" (Liu/Yang/Su) accepted at ICLR 2026 DeLTa Workshop (venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Workshop/DeLTa, group title confirmed = "ICLR 2026 2nd Workshop on Deep Generative Model in Machine Learning"), cdate 2026-01-30. The main arXiv version's target venue is unknown; I am recording preprint + confirmed workshop poster. Either way it is pre-cutoff (2026-01-31 arXiv v1). (3) DreamOn's ICLR reviews were readable only through the OpenReview /notes/search endpoint (the /notes?forum= endpoint returned a 403 ChallengeRequiredError), so I may have seen a partial reply set; from what I retrieved, no reviewer requested a length-stratified breakdown — one reviewer did note the single-line-to-oracle gap on multi-line implies "requiring many insertions is a bottleneck for longer code snippets," and one reviewer flagged the baselines as weak. I did NOT verify that no reviewer elsewhere in the thread asked for stratification. (4) PILL (ACL ARR 2026 May Submission 8544, OpenReview wRRKQvbDiO) is anonymous-under-review with no arXiv preprint I could locate; its OpenReview cdate is 2026-05-25, PUBLIC (odate) 2026-06-02 — both AFTER the 2026-05-07 cutoff, so concurrent. Its review outcome is unknown. (5) I did not verify that no paper outside the DreamOn citation graph performs this stratification; my citation sweep was the 28 S2 citations of DreamOn plus ~10 targeted arXiv full-text queries. Targeted queries that returned genuinely nothing relevant: abs:"oracle length"; abs:"length calibration" AND abs:"diffusion"; variable-length AND diffusion AND (compute-matched OR NFE OR "forward passes"); diffusion language AND stratified. (6) LOCAL FEASIBILITY VERIFIED, and it partially contradicts the candidate's own experiment plan: I tokenized all three splits with the DreamOn-v0-7B tokenizer. gt_len medians are SingleLine 7 (p95=20, max=46), RandomSpan 12 (p95=62), MultiLine 31 (p95=110). Consequence: at canvas=64 the SingleLine split has ZERO cases with |gt_len-canvas|<=2 and ALL 1033 at >=16, and at canvas=32 only 9 matched cases — so on SingleLine the candidate's "matched stratum" simply does not exist at the larger canvases in DreamOn's published sweep, and the stated kill criterion ("<150 cases in extreme mismatch at EVERY canvas prior") is trivially passed for the wrong reason. RandomSpanInfilling is the only split with real mass in both tails (canvas=16: 179 matched / 316 extreme), and its true size is 1640 rows locally, not the 164 the candidate assumed. All three splits are already on disk at data/infilling/ (no download needed), and vendor/DreamOn/eval/eval_humaneval_infilling.sh already sweeps min_gen_len in {4,8,16,32,64} at max_gen_len=64, steps=256, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, alg=entropy, mask_expansion=true, delete_eos_token=true — so the sweep is config-only as claimed. Note the harness defaults are temperature=0.2/top_p=0.9, NOT the T=0.1/top_p=0.95 used elsewhere in this project, and this project has already measured a +14.6-point HumanEval swing from a top_p change alone; the sampler must be pinned and reported or the stratified deltas are uninterpretable.

related_work.citation: Zirui Wu, Lin Zheng, Zhihui Xie, Jiacheng Ye, Jiahui Gao, Shansan Gong, Yansong Feng, Zhenguo Li, Wei Bi, Guorui Zhou, Lingpeng Kong. "DreamOn: Diffusion Language Models For Code Infilling Beyond Fixed-size Canvas." arXiv:2602.01326; ICLR 2026 Poster.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster. Verified on OpenReview: forum EQTPmqukiU, content.venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference', invitations include Submission19236/-/Camera_Ready_Revision. arXiv comment also says 'ICLR 2026'; DBLP lists CoRR only (lags, as expected).
related_work.what_it_covers: The target of the audit. Adds [expand]/[delete] augmented diffusion states so a masked DLM can grow/shrink its canvas natively, fine-tuned from Dream-7B / DiffuCoder-7B / DreamCoder-7B. Table 2 reports pass@1 across initial mask lengths {4,8,16,32,64} plus an ORACLE column where the canvas equals the ground-truth solution length. Single-line: base DreamCoder 24.9/61.2/72.6/62.4/55.5 (avg 55.3, oracle 93.3) vs +DreamOn 88.7/90.6/91.0/91.6/92.1 (avg 90.8, oracle 91.6). Multi-line: base 5.5..43.2 (avg 26.0, oracle 69.0) vs +DreamOn 50.2..63.8 (avg 57.1, oracle 66.6). SantaCoder-FIM likewise. Ablates w/o Expand and w/o Delete, showing expand carries the short-canvas regime and delete the long-canvas regime. Section 3.4 adds 'deletion broadcasting' as a length predictor, cutting steps from 122.8 to 52.4 at mask length 64.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Never reports the realised final canvas length versus gt_len — so whether the learned length control is CALIBRATED (converges to gt_len) or merely PERMISSIVE (escapes the worst misspecification but lands on a biased length) is entirely unmeasured. Never stratifies any result by ground-truth middle length, so 'DreamOn matches AR at infilling' is reported only at a level of aggregation that mixes matched and grossly-mismatched cases. No compute accounting that puts DreamOn and a fixed-canvas baseline in one unit (steps are reported only within DreamOn variants, for the broadcasting ablation). Never evaluates HumanEval RandomSpanInfilling. Python-only for HumanEval-Infilling.
related_work.known_defects: (1) UNFAIR HEADLINE BASELINE: the ~37-point single-line gain is measured against a fixed-canvas Dream-Coder baseline that, per CAL (pre-cutoff, 2026-01-31), recovers most of that deficit training-free — CAL lifts DreamCoder-Base single-line avg 49.3 -> 70.2 with only 11-18 extra forward passes. An ICLR reviewer independently flagged 'I feel the baselines are weak.' (2) NO COMPUTE MATCHING against the baseline; expand/delete steps are not priced against a fixed-canvas run. (3) ORACLE USED AS CEILING, NEVER AS DECOMPOSITION: the paper has the ground-truth-length control in hand and uses it only to claim an upper bound. (4) CALIBRATION UNMEASURED (see above). (5) NON-UNIFORM/REGRESSIVE BEHAVIOUR HIDDEN BY AGGREGATION: LR-DLLM's independent re-run finds DreamOn DEGRADES multi-line on DreamCoder (43.2 -> 36.1) and degrades C++/Rust single-line on McEval, leaving the McEval mean unchanged at 37.2 — none of which is visible in DreamOn's own tables. (6) Both the multi-line oracle (66.6) and single-line oracle (91.6) for +DreamOn are BELOW the base model's oracle (69.0 / 93.3), i.e. the fine-tune costs raw infilling quality at matched length — the paper does not discuss this.

related_work.citation: Hengchang Liu, Zhao Yang, Bing Su. "Diffusion LMs Can Approximate Optimal Infilling Lengths Implicitly." arXiv:2602.00476. Same-method workshop version: "Training-Free Length Discovery for Diffusion Language Model Infilling", ICLR 2026 DeLTa Workshop Poster.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-01-31). Same authors have a same-method version accepted at the ICLR 2026 DeLTa Workshop (verified on OpenReview: venue='ICLR 2026 DeLTa Workshop Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Workshop/DeLTa', cdate 2026-01-30, authors Hengchang Liu/Zhao Yang/Bing Su; workshop group title confirmed via OpenReview /groups). Main-track venue for the arXiv version not established: DBLP returns nothing, Semantic Scholar rate-limited.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE CLOSEST PRIOR WORK TO THE CANDIDATE'S DIAGNOSTIC CLAIM, and it is pre-cutoff. Establishes that canvas misspecification is the dominant bottleneck in DLM infilling and quantifies it with exactly the oracle-length control the candidate proposed to introduce. Table 1: HumanEval-Infilling single-line pass@1 at fixed lengths {4,8,16,32} vs oracle length (canvas = tokenized ground truth) — LLaDA-Base 22.4/51.4/55.8/48.4 avg 44.5 vs oracle 87.6 (avg oracle len 9.5); DiffuCoder-Base avg 45.8 vs 87.4; DreamCoder-Base avg 47.0 vs 88.1. Its central figure plots average first-step denoising confidence AS A FUNCTION OF probe length relative to the oracle length, identifying an 'Oracle Peak' at canvas == gt_len and a monotone 'Length Bias' decay in |canvas| — i.e. a confidence-space version of the candidate's |gt_len - canvas| regression. Proposes CAL: fit a double-exponential bias curve, calibrate, hill-climb to the length. Training-free, 11-18 extra single forward passes. Lifts DreamCoder-Base single-line avg 49.3 -> 70.2, LLaDA-Base 44.8 -> 65.5; multi-line DreamCoder 18.4 -> 28.4. Also text infilling (ROCStories/CS-Abstracts/Yelp) with BLEU-2/ROUGE-L.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Never evaluates DreamOn — so the head-to-head 'is training-based length control still worth it once the fixed-canvas baseline is length-corrected' is completely open, and CAL is precisely the fair baseline DreamOn lacks. Evaluates only *-Base checkpoints (LLaDA-Base/Instruct, DiffuCoder-Base, DreamCoder-Base), never an Instruct code model. Reports pass@1 and search-step counts but no total-NFE or wall-clock comparison against the fixed-canvas run it replaces. Structurally cannot report the matched stratum (see defects). No per-case paired statistics or CIs anywhere.
related_work.known_defects: (1) SELF-EXCLUDING MATCHED STRATUM: to fit the length-bias curve it applies a 'strict Oracle exclusion strategy' discarding every probe length in the neighbourhood of the oracle length, and those samples are 'strictly excluded from subsequent evaluations'. So the very stratum where the candidate's null is predicted (|gt_len - canvas| ~ 0) is removed by construction — CAL cannot answer whether the advantage vanishes there, and we can. (2) A SINGLE GLOBAL BIAS CURVE, fit on 100 HumanEval-Infilling samples with LLaDA-8B-Base, is reused across all models and all tasks including text infilling; robustness is asserted rather than re-fit per model. (3) NO PAIRED STATISTICS OR CIs: every claim is a mean-difference on ~1000 items with no variance reporting, so 'up to 47.7%' improvements are unbounded in uncertainty. (4) COST UNDERPRICED: 11-18 extra first-step forward passes are called 'modest'/'acceptable' without ever placing them in the same unit as the decoding NFE they precede, and without an NFE-matched fixed-canvas control (e.g. a fixed canvas given the same extra budget as best-of-k). (5) THE ORACLE ITSELF IS A LEAKED CONTROL used as a ceiling: the oracle canvas is the tokenized reference solution, so the 87-88 oracle numbers presuppose the reference's exact token count and cannot be attained without the answer. (6) Single-line is described as biased toward short completions (avg oracle len ~8.6-9.5) and CAL's gain 'diminishes as the initial length increases' — i.e. its own effect is length-regime-dependent, which it notes qualitatively but never stratifies.

related_work.citation: Anonymous / unattributed authors. "Improving Variable-Length Generation in Diffusion Language Models via Length Regularization" (LR-DLLM). arXiv:2602.07546.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. DBLP lists it as CoRR 2026 only. Its arXiv comment field is the bare LaTeX template string 'diffusion language models' and the body carries an ICML style header ('Machine Learning, ICML'), which is a template artefact and NOT an acceptance claim; OpenReview search returns nothing; Semantic Scholar 429 on retry. Recorded as preprint.
related_work.what_it_covers: SECOND-CLOSEST, and pre-cutoff. Diagnoses the same mechanism as CAL — 'naively comparing confidence across mask lengths becomes systematically biased' — and proposes LR-DLLM, a training-free length-regularized inference framework with bidirectional expansion/contraction. Critically for us, it is the ONLY paper that independently re-runs DreamOn: Table 3 (HumanEval-Infilling, DreamCoder-7B backbone, DreamOn initial mask length pinned to 11, all variable-length methods at MAX_LENGTH=128) reports base 14.3/55.5/43.2 (RandomSpan/Single/Multi, mean 39.1), +DreamOn 21.6/73.5/36.1 (mean 37.9), +LR-DLLM 23.2/81.6/53.8 (mean 51.3). Table 4 (McEval, four languages) reports DreamCoder base mean 37.2, +DreamOn mean 37.2 — with DreamOn degrading C++ single-line 57.3 -> 39.1 and Rust single-line 52.2 -> 27.2 while improving Python 73.3 -> 82.2. It states in prose that 'DreamOn exhibits inconsistent behavior across span regimes, improving some settings while degrading Multi-line infilling.' Its Table 1 property matrix positions DAEDAL / DreamOn / FlexMDM / dLLM-Var / LR-DLLM on training-free / model-agnostic / task-agnostic axes. Appendix documents that DreamOn is released only with DreamCoder checkpoints and that FlexMDM had no public code at the time.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its span-regime evidence is COARSE and BENCHMARK-LEVEL (RandomSpan vs Single-line vs Multi-line as proxies for span length; language as a second axis) — never per-case ground-truth-length binning, never a regression of the delta on |gt_len - canvas|, never paired CIs. It pins DreamOn to a single initial mask length (11), so it cannot reproduce or refute the canvas-prior sweep at all. It never measures the realised final canvas length of DreamOn or of its own method against gt_len. It equalises only a nominal MAX_LENGTH=128 'adjustment budget', not actual forward passes or wall clock, so its DreamOn comparison is not compute-matched. And it never asks whether its own gains are themselves concentrated in the mismatch tail.
related_work.known_defects: (1) NOT COMPUTE-MATCHED: 'same adjustment budget with MAX_LENGTH=128' is a canvas cap, not an NFE or latency budget; LR-DLLM's probing cost versus DreamOn's expand/delete steps is never accounted in a common unit. (2) DreamOn pinned to initial mask length 11 'to isolate its variable-length adjustment capability' — a single, unjustified operating point, chosen by the competitor, which is exactly the kind of baseline-configuration choice that flatters the proposed method; DreamOn's own paper sweeps {4,8,16,32,64}. (3) ITS DREAMON NUMBERS CONTRADICT DREAMON'S OWN and the discrepancy is never reconciled: LR-DLLM has +DreamOn single-line 73.5 and multi-line 36.1 where DreamOn reports 92.1 and 63.8 — an ~19 and ~28 point gap. Either the pinned canvas=11, the sampler, or the harness differs materially; unexplained, this leaves BOTH papers' DreamOn characterisations in doubt and is itself a reproducibility target. (4) No per-case paired statistics or CIs on any comparison. (5) Property-matrix claims ('task-agnostic', 'model-agnostic') are ticks in a table rather than measured quantities. (6) The GSM8K column of its Table 1 leaves DreamOn blank ('-') while ranking methods by it.

related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Does not mention DreamOn at all (verified: zero occurrences in the full HTML). Contains no oracle-length control, no ground-truth-length stratification, no length binning, and no audit of a released variable-length model — it is a method paper that trains new models. related_work.known_defects: Diagnoses positional uncertainty via semantic-collapse analysis rather than via a length-mismatch decomposition, so the 'where does the gain live' question is untouched; only 2 mentions of 'infill' in the whole paper despite Python coding being the flagship task; the 7B FlexMDM and 125M LatentMDM are at different scales on different tasks, so the two proposed remedies are never compared head to head.

related_work.venue_status: Under review, ACL ARR 2026 May (OpenReview venueid aclweb.org/ACL/ARR/2026/May/Submission, forum wRRKQvbDiO, number 8544, note='under review'). related_work.what_it_covers: The most directly competitive concurrent work, and its critique of the field is close to ours: it explicitly faults prior adaptive-length methods for '(i) Sensitivity to initial length — these methods require a preset length to initialize the search and are highly sensitive to this initial length' and '(ii) Inference inefficiency — they either insert length-changing operations during generation or repeatedly search using multi-step denoising confidence, both of which introduce substantial additional forward passes and computational cost.' Proposes PILL, preset-length-free probing-based infilling; claims +4.8 avg pass rate on code and +6.0 BLEU-2 on text over the strongest baseline at 1.82x its speed and <10% overhead over fixed-length decoding, across five DLMs and eight infilling benchmarks.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent, so it does not preempt us; and it is a METHOD paper — it prices forward passes to argue its own efficiency, not to audit DreamOn's headline, and there is no indication it stratifies by ground-truth length or measures any model's realised final canvas length against gt_len. Review outcome unknown.
related_work.known_defects: Cannot be fully assessed — anonymous under review, PDF not read (only the OpenReview abstract/metadata). Its efficiency claims are relative to an unnamed 'strongest baseline'. The 'eight infilling benchmarks' are unspecified in the abstract. It shares the concern about counting forward passes, which means our compute-matched framing must be careful to differentiate on the audit/calibration axis rather than on efficiency alone.

related_work.citation: Jaeyeon Kim et al. "Any-Order Flexible Length Masked Diffusion" (FlexMDM). arXiv:2509.01025; ICLR 2026 Poster (also NeurIPS 2025 SPIGM Workshop).
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster — verified on OpenReview (venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference'); an earlier version appears at NeurIPS 2025 SPIGM Workshop (venueid='NeurIPS.cc/2025/Workshop/SPIGM'). arXiv comment says only 'Preprint' (lags).
related_work.what_it_covers: Insertion-based flexible-length masked diffusion via a stochastic-interpolant extension; retrofits LLaDA-8B into a FlexMDM in three days on 16 H100s, reporting code infilling 52% -> 65% and GSM8K 58% -> 67%. Explicitly claims to model 'length statistics with much higher fidelity' than MDMs — the nearest thing in the literature to a calibration claim.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its length-fidelity claim is made at the distributional level (length statistics of generated sequences), NOT per-case against a known ground-truth middle length in an infilling setting — so 'does the learned length hit THIS example's gt_len' is unmeasured. No stratification by ground-truth length; no DreamOn comparison; no oracle-length control on HumanEval-Infilling. LR-DLLM's appendix records that no public code was available at its time of writing.
related_work.known_defects: Code infilling is a single aggregate number (52 -> 65) with no canvas-prior sweep and no length breakdown. The distributional length-fidelity metric does not license per-case calibration claims, but the abstract's phrasing invites that reading. Retrofit cost (16 H100s x 3 days) is reported but never traded off against training-free alternatives that reach comparable infilling numbers for ~15 forward passes.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list=2509.01025 (v2, v1 published 2025-08-31T23:34:53Z); OpenReview /notes/search returned two records, ICLR 2026 Poster (ICLR.cc/2026/Conference) and SPIGM @ NeurIPS (NeurIPS.cc/2025/Workshop/SPIGM); also cross-referenced as a baseline in LR-DLLM Table 3.

related_work.citation: Jinsong Li et al. "Beyond Fixed: Training-Free Variable-Length Denoising for Diffusion Large Language Models" (DAEDAL). arXiv:2508.00819; ICLR 2026 Poster.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster — verified on OpenReview (venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference'). arXiv comment mentions only the code URL.
related_work.what_it_covers: The original training-free adaptive-length method: a two-phase scheme that expands a short initial canvas to a task-appropriate length using a sequence-completion metric, then inserts mask tokens into under-developed regions mid-denoising. Establishes the 'internal signals correlate with optimal response length' premise that CAL, rho-EOS, LR-DLLM and PILL all build on.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Designed for open-ended chat/reasoning, not infilling, and CAL shows it transfers poorly there — as an infilling baseline on LLaDA-Base it sometimes UNDERPERFORMS the fixed-length baseline (single-line avg 44.8, identical to baseline 44.8; at length 32 it drops 49.0 -> 43.1). Expansion-only, so it cannot contract an over-long canvas. No ground-truth-length stratification anywhere.
related_work.known_defects: Unidirectional (expansion-only) by construction, which CAL identifies as the reason it fails on over-estimated canvases; LLaDA-family-specific (LR-DLLM's appendix notes it is 'not easily transferable' to other backbones); its 'higher effective token ratio' efficiency metric measures non-pad fraction rather than any quality-per-FLOP quantity.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list=2508.00819 (v1 published 2025-08-01T17:56:07Z); OpenReview /notes/search confirmed venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference'; performance figures cross-read from CAL Table 2 where DAEDAL is the adapted baseline.

related_work.citation: "rho-EOS: Training-free Bidirectional Variable-Length Control for Masked Diffusion LLMs." arXiv:2601.22527.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-01-30; comment '11 pages, 6 figures, 6 tables'). No venue claim found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Uses the implicit density of EOS tokens during denoising as a sufficiency signal for bidirectional (expand AND contract) length adjustment in a single unified denoising pass, contrasting itself with two-stage expansion-only prior work. Evaluated on math and code. Another pre-cutoff entrant establishing that training-free bidirectional length control is a crowded axis.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Math/code generation rather than a length-stratified infilling audit; no oracle-length control, no gt_len binning, no DreamOn comparison.
related_work.known_defects: 'Comparable performance while substantially improving inference efficiency' is an efficiency-first framing that does not isolate where quality changes across length regimes; no per-case statistics; venue unverified.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list=2601.22527 (v1 published 2026-01-30T04:00:04Z); surfaced via Semantic Scholar citation graph of DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326 citations endpoint).

related_work.citation: "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2607.24763.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 dated 2026-06-04, comment 'updated version'). No venue claim found.
related_work.what_it_covers: The methodological template for the differentiated version of this candidate, in the adjacent remasking subfield. Shows that seven recent remasking papers evaluate under incompatible nominal step counts, metrics and temperatures; standardises ACTUAL NFE, enforces multi-metric reporting, and controls stochasticity. Headline findings: temperature explains most MAUVE variance, and compute-matched comparisons REVERSE several published strategy rankings.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Covers remasking strategies on OpenWebText/LM1B with MAUVE, not variable-length/canvas control on code infilling with pass@1. So the exact audit it validates as a genre — compute-matched re-ranking of a subfield's published claims — has not been applied to the variable-length-infilling literature at all. Directly supports our framing that DreamOn-vs-baseline needs actual-NFE matching.
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent and itself a protocol paper: its findings are about remasking, so transferring the 'compute-matching reverses rankings' result to length control is a hypothesis we would be testing, not importing. MAUWE/MAUVE-based quality metrics do not carry over to functional-correctness benchmarks.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list=2607.24763 (published 2026-06-04T22:21:08Z, comment 'updated version'); found via targeted arXiv full-text query for audit/reassess terms combined with diffusion language models.

related_work.citation: Marianne Arriola, Volodymyr Kuleshov. "Set Diffusion: Interpolating Token Orderings Between Autoregression and Diffusion for Fast and Flexible Decoding." arXiv:2607.01775.
related_work.venue_status: arXiv comment says 'ICML 2026'; NOT independently confirmed — OpenReview has no ICML.cc/2026/Conference venue record retrievable, so ICML 2026 acceptances cannot currently be verified through that channel. Treat the venue as arXiv-comment-only evidence.
related_work.what_it_covers: Factorises likelihood over flexible-position, flexible-length token SETS with a set-causal architecture supporting KV caching; claims better speed-quality tradeoffs than prior diffusion LMs and 'stronger infilling performance than block diffusion'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent. Infilling is one bullet among math/summarisation/unconditional generation; no oracle-length control, no gt_len stratification, no DreamOn comparison, no HumanEval-Infilling canvas sweep.

related_work.citation: "Beyond Masks: Efficient, Flexible Diffusion Language Models via Deletion-Insertion Processes" (DID). arXiv:2603.23507.
related_work.venue_status: arXiv comment says 'Accepted at ICLR 2026'; NOT independently confirmed on OpenReview in this pass. Treat as arXiv-comment-only.
related_work.what_it_covers: Replaces masking/unmasking with rigorously formulated token deletion and insertion as discrete diffusion processes, natively supporting variable length without pad tokens, with a claimed intrinsic self-correction from insertion. Score-based training objective solved by parallelised dynamic programming.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: A generative-modelling paper evaluated on fixed and variable-length language modelling settings, not a code-infilling audit; no oracle-length control, no gt_len stratification, no DreamOn comparison.
related_work.known_defects: Efficiency claims rest on eliminating MASK/PAD compute, an accounting choice that flatters deletion-insertion relative to masked diffusion unless total NFE and wall clock are both reported; 'without any hyperparameter tuning' is asserted rather than demonstrated against tuned baselines; venue not OpenReview-verified.
