feas.concrete_plan:
PILOT IS ALREADY DONE. I ran it today; below is what I measured, then what remains.

WHAT I RAN (read-only; all probes in /tmp, nothing written into the repo)
- Hole construction from the OFFICIAL span pool, /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/data/infilling/HumanEval-SingleLineInfilling.jsonl (1033 rows, 164 base tasks), NOT fresh AST punching. Reconstruct the file as row['prompt']+row['canonical_solution']+row['suffix'] (verified parseable 164/164), then blank k non-adjacent code lines.
- Diffusion arm: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B via diffusion_generate, oracle per-hole token length, steps = n_masks (1 token/step), T=0, top_p=0.95, alg=entropy. Local L20A.
- AR arm: models/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B native FIM sentinels [PRE]prefix[SUF]suffix[MID], holes filled sequentially left-to-right per InCoder Appendix B.2, greedy, 48 new tokens, truncate at first newline. On .73 via .venv_dream/bin/python.
- Grading: evalplus.eval.untrusted_check against evalplus.evaluate.get_groundtruth. No hand-rolled verifier.

*** BUG I HIT AND FIXED -- THIS IS RETRACTION #2's EXACT CLASS, DO NOT REPEAT IT ***
In SingleLineInfilling/HumanEval/N/L{k}, L{k} indexes lines WITHIN THE SOLUTION BODY, not the file. My first pilot treated k as a file line index, which put 379/379 holes INSIDE DOCSTRINGS. That version yielded a beautiful, entirely meaningless ladder (diffusion .975/.950/.975, flat) and was caught only by the mutated-gold null passing at 1.000/0.975/0.975. The correct hole line is row['prompt'].count('\n'). Any implementation MUST assert every hole line is outside the docstring.

CORRECTED RESULTS (evalplus-graded; diffusion n=60, AR n=40)
  k=1: diffusion .783 | AR-FIM .950 | AR-FIM-fair .950 | delta -0.167
  k=2: diffusion .850 | AR-FIM .875 | AR-FIM-fair .900 | delta -0.025
  k=4: diffusion .883 | AR-FIM .525 | AR-FIM-fair .600 | delta +0.358
  Interaction (delta@k4 - delta@k1) = +0.525, SE 0.109, z=4.80, p<1e-5 -- significant ALREADY at pilot n.
  AR-FIM-fair = my own fairness repair: later unfilled holes kept as 'pass  # TODO' so the FIM suffix stays syntactically valid instead of being deleted. The AR collapse SURVIVES it (.950->.600), so it is not merely suffix corruption.
  Cost, measured: diffusion cum_model_tokens (steps x canvas) 1255/2879/7659; AR tokens_fed 147/358/958, attended 2115/4247/10352.
  Diffusion EM-to-gold: .633/.792/.833 -- rises with k (the confound).

NULL CONTROLS on identical hole specs (n=60):
  gold refill    .983/.983/.983 (ceiling sanity)
  delete hole    .033/.017/.000, parseable 43/60 -> 21/60 -> 6/60
  mutated gold   .800/.433/.200  <- holes are load-bearing and increasingly so with k
  (On the buggy docstring holes these were .975-1.000 across the board. That contrast is the diagnostic.)

REMAINING STEPS
1. Reimplement the corrected construction as a committed script (e.g. scripts/build_kspan_infilling.py) emitting explicit hole specs {task_id, k, hole_line_numbers, gold_lines, total_masked_tokens}, with hard asserts: (a) every hole line is outside the docstring, (b) holes pairwise non-adjacent, (c) reconstructed file ast.parse-es, (d) n per cell logged. Freeze the spec file so every arm consumes byte-identical holes.
2. Scale to full n per cell: k=1 n=164, k=2 n=108, k=4 n=60 (measured caps). Add k=3 (n=84) -- it is free and makes the slope a 4-point ladder instead of 3.
3. Add the two missing arms: DreamOn-v0-7B via its native infilling_with_expansion (vendor/DreamOn/eval/generator.py:320, so no oracle length needed -- this is the honest length-elastic leg), and the third AR protocol (chat '// region 1' region markers) as an exact replication of arXiv:2508.10111's format, plus permuted hole order for the within-item paired order test.
4. Run the topology-vs-length control: hold total masked lines at 4 and vary k in {1,2,4} (1 hole of 4 lines / 2 of 2 / 4 of 1). I ran this on the buggy holes (flat .975 across all three); it must be rerun on corrected holes. This is what pre-empts 'isn't this just more masked tokens?'.
5. Decontamination leg (see risk): rerun the diffusion k-ladder on held-out code the model cannot have memorised, or on paraphrased/renamed variants, and report EM-to-gold per cell alongside pass@1.
6. Cost axis: reuse the existing ForwardCostTracker in scripts/generate_evalplus_ar.py rather than writing a new one; report pass@1 vs cumulative_model_tokens with per-cell truncation/abort rates disclosed separately.
7. RandomSpan anchor: patch the split name in vendor/DreamOn/eval/evaluate.py:95 (or bypass it), pip install human_eval_infilling or reimplement read_problems, and report RandomSpanInfilling (1640) + Light (164, at /tmp/RandomSpanInfillingLight.jsonl) both raw and post-processed with the stopping rule stated per family.

NODES: diffusion arms on LOCAL/.252 (wzc1, models/ present). AR arms on .73/.82/.104 (zwfy6, Qwen2.5-Coder-7B present, .venv_dream/bin/python works, evalplus 0.1.0.dev1 -- note the version differs from wzc1's 0.3.1, so grade all arms on ONE node or verify graders agree). .73 was fully idle (8x0MiB) when I used GPUs 0-2.

DO NOT DUPLICATE: .104 AR EvalPlus from-scratch baseline, .73 DreamOn infilling/FIM eval, .82 sampler audit, .252+LOCAL MBPP+ Large@1024. REUSE: .82's sampler audit fixes the T/top_p operating point (top_p 1.0->0.95 alone moved HumanEval +14.6 pts, so the k-ladder must pin it); .104's AR row gives the from-scratch reference that contextualises AR's infilling numbers; .73's DreamOn work de-risks the DreamOn arm's invocation.
feas.risk: MOST LIKELY CONFOUNDED RESULT (not null -- I already measured a z=4.80 interaction, so the null outcome is largely off the table): the headline "diffusion's advantage grows with k" is driven by MEMORISATION, not coordination. I measured diffusion's exact-match-to-gold rate rising monotonically with k: .633 -> .792 -> .833 at k=1/2/4. HumanEval canonical solutions are in every code pretraining corpus, and adding holes adds two-sided context that makes each remaining line more retrievable from memory. Under that reading, diffusion's pass@1 RISE with k (.783 -> .883) is not evidence of joint bidirectional filling at all -- it is a fixed-canvas model recalling lines it has seen, while the AR arm is penalised because sequential decoding must commit before seeing later holes. A reviewer who computes EM-to-gold (which no arm of the design as written reports) kills the paper in one line. Secondary confounding routes: (a) oracle per-hole length is a real advantage handed to diffusion -- when I used a fixed 12-token canvas instead, Dream-Coder fell out of infilling mode entirely and emitted chat scaffolding ("```python", "the the the problem:"), so the honest non-oracle diffusion arm needs DreamOn's expand/delete and its numbers will differ; (b) ceiling compression at k=1,2 (diffusion .783-.850, AR .875-.950 against a gold refill ceiling of .983) means most of the interaction slope lives in the single k=4 cell, which is also the smallest (n=60) -- one badly-specified k=4 item is worth 1.7 points; (c) the AR arm's k=4 parseable rate (27/40, and 32/40 after my fairness repair) means a third of the AR collapse is syntax breakage rather than wrong logic, so pass@1 alone conflates two mechanisms that must be reported separately.
feas.required_control:
CONTAMINATION-CONTROLLED HOLE-SENSITIVITY LADDER: report, per (k, arm) cell, THREE quantities on byte-identical frozen hole specs -- (1) pass@1, (2) exact-match-to-gold of the filled spans, (3) the mutated-gold null. This is one control with three legs because each leg blocks one of our three retractions, and I have already shown each leg fires.

Leg 2 (EM-to-gold) blocks the memorisation reading and is the one the candidate omits entirely: I measured diffusion EM rising .633/.792/.833 with k, so pass@1 gains that track EM gains are recall, not coordination. Ship the leg with a pre-registered rule: if the pass@1-vs-k slope is not significant after conditioning on EM (or after moving to held-out/paraphrased code), the "uncontested home turf" claim is withdrawn and the paper reports the k x family interaction for AR only.

Leg 3 (mutated-gold null: refill each hole with the gold line, one operator/identifier flipped, keeping it syntactically valid) blocks retraction #1 -- a grader that compares nothing. It must DEGRADE with k. Measured on correct holes: .800/.433/.200. Measured on my buggy docstring holes: 1.000/0.975/0.975 -- i.e. this null is precisely what caught my construction bug, because a null that passes means the holes are not load-bearing and the metric is measuring nothing.

Leg 1 plus a hard assert blocks retraction #2 -- a pipeline stage silently discarding its input. Assert that every hole line lies OUTSIDE the docstring (the L{k} index in SingleLineInfilling is body-relative, not file-relative; taking it as a file line put 379/379 of my holes in docstrings and produced a clean-looking flat ladder), that holes are pairwise non-adjacent, and that the reconstructed file parses. Also assert per-cell n and log truncation/abort counts separately from failures, so the k=4 cell's cost growth cannot silently drop its most expensive items the way retraction #3 did.

lens.title: Structural Constraints Are Free for Diffusion, Costly for AR: A Parse-Validity/Compute Frontier on Typed Generation
lens.claim: Enforcing hard structural validity (parseability, exact-length, schema conformance) costs a masked diffusion model far less quality-per-token than it costs an AR model, because diffusion can satisfy global constraints by iterative revision whereas AR must satisfy them prefix-locally. Operationally: at matched cumulative_model_tokens, constrained diffusion loses less pass@1 relative to its own unconstrained baseline than constrained AR loses relative to its own.
lens.why_now: This is where our existing, already-measured asset is decisive and nobody else has the instrument. We have a WORKING typed-AST decoder runtime (scaffold_coder/decoder_runtime.py) that makes structural validity a hard invariant by construction, and we have already measured its cost curve honestly (Medium: 13.98k tokens -> .177 HE+, 7.08k -> .354 MBPP+; vanilla scores ~.000/.008 at 19-22k tokens). Our surviving Pareto-segmentation claim IS a constraint-cost result that we have so far framed only as a cost result. The constrained-decoding-for-diffusion literature is now active but exclusively method-side and NON-code: DINGO (arXiv:2505.23061, 2025-05-29, pre-cutoff, regex/JSON, symbolic math), Constrained Decoding via Finite Automata (arXiv:2607.07026, 2026-07-08, JSON function calls on Dream-7B/LLaDA-8B), EPIC (arXiv:2606.00722), DIA (arXiv:2606.04535, ACL 2026, format-constrained reasoning on GSM8K/MATH), Continuous Diffusion Can Obey Formal Syntax (arXiv:2602.12468). Not one of them prices the constraint against an AR model on executable code at matched compute — they report constraint satisfaction and accuracy, never the paradigm-relative constraint TAX. The nearest code-structural work, AnCoder/AnchorTree (arXiv:2602.17688, 2026-02-05, AST-anchored diffusion), is soft prioritisation of salient tokens, not a hard-invariant runtime, and reports no AR constraint-tax comparison.
lens.experiment: Three-way frontier on HumanEval+/MBPP+ with our existing evalplus grading and cumulative_model_tokens: (A) scaffold runtime (hard AST validity by construction) at the capacity ladder we already have — Tiny/Small/Medium/Large, ALREADY MEASURED, zero new GPU cost; (B) unconstrained Dream-Coder-Instruct across NFE 16..1024 — ALREADY MEASURED; (C) NEW: AR arm with and without an equivalent grammar constraint, so the AR constraint tax is measured in the same unit. The new measurement is the AR pair plus a diffusion soft-constraint arm (logit masking to parseable continuations) so we have both hard and soft constraint mechanisms per paradigm. Primary metric: constraint tax = (unconstrained pass@1 - constrained pass@1) at matched tokens, per paradigm. Secondary: parse-validity rate, which we already track (unparseable-output falls 94%->1.8% over the NFE range, so the diffusion baseline curve is in hand). Optional non-code leg: JSON-schema conformant output, where DINGO/2607.07026 give published reference points to sanity-check our harness against.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE (this is the point — most of the experiment is already run): scaffold_coder/decoder_runtime.py full working runtime (from_function_header, unresolved_masks, commit_many, remask_leaves, rule_fixed_point, capacity_metrics, final_text); measured capacity ladder + NFE sweep + matched Plain-SFT control (HE+ .2195 / MBPP+ .2434) + flat-canvas cost accounting (685/604 tok per step); scripts/make_pareto_figures.py + figures/; evalplus 0.3.1; models/Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B. MISSING: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B for the AR arm (~15GB, on neither disk) — shared with candidates 1 and 4. jsonschema/lark/outlines are NOT installed in dllm-env (only tree_sitter is) so the grammar-constrained AR arm needs either a pip install (proxy works) or a hand-rolled parseability check via tree_sitter; peft is also absent from dllm-env but the wheel exists at wheels/peft-0.19.1-py3-none-any.whl with scripts/setup_peft019_overlay.sh (only relevant if we add a trained arm). MUST re-read process OR failure_process when aggregating (retraction 3: dropping budget-truncated cases understated scaffold Large cost by 2.85x/3.69x).
lens.kill_criterion: Killed if the constraint tax is statistically indistinguishable between paradigms at matched tokens — i.e. hard structural validity costs diffusion and AR the same, in which case 'structure is cheaper for diffusion' is false and our Pareto segmentation stays a pure cost result with no mechanistic reading. Killed also if the AR constrained arm simply beats scaffold outright at every budget on both benchmarks (then the low-cost segment we claim to own is not actually ours, which would additionally undercut the currently surviving claim — a genuinely important self-falsification worth running early). Note scaffold peaks at .177/.354, so this arm is a real risk, not a formality.
lens.builds_on: Our own surviving Pareto-segmentation result, reframed from a cost claim into a constraint-tax claim; and the constrained-diffusion-decoding line (DINGO arXiv:2505.23061 pre-cutoff; arXiv:2607.07026, 2606.00722, 2606.04535 concurrent). Defect repaired: that entire line reports constraint satisfaction and task accuracy but never the paradigm-relative cost of the constraint on executable code, so it cannot say whether structure is genuinely cheaper for diffusion — which is the field's main a-priori argument for the paradigm.

diff.sharpened_claim: The constraint tax is not a property of a generation paradigm but of the interaction between CONSTRAINT STRENGTH, paradigm, and token budget -- and it can be negative. We measure a constraint-strength ladder (L0 unconstrained, L1 prompt-only format request, L2 token-mask/grammar constrained decoding, L3 hard structural invariant by construction) crossed with paradigm (masked diffusion: Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B; AR: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) on executable code (HumanEval+/MBPP+, evalplus-graded), pricing every cell in cumulative_model_tokens rather than steps/NFE. Headline claim, already half-measured: in the LOW-BUDGET regime a hard structural invariant is a NEGATIVE tax for diffusion -- our L3 scaffold runtime reaches .177 HE+ / .354 MBPP+ at 13.98k/7.08k tokens where the L0 diffusion baseline scores ~.000/.008 at 19-22k tokens -- whereas in the HIGH-budget regime the same invariant is a large POSITIVE tax (.177 vs .707 at 512 steps). The decisive new measurement is whether AR shows the same sign flip: if a hard-invariant AR decoder also buys quality at low token budgets, "structure is cheaper for diffusion" is false and the honest result is a budget-indexed, paradigm-invariant law. We additionally supply the control the constrained-decoding literature omits (L1, from The Format Tax) and the control The Format Tax omits (a diffusion arm), so the prompt-side and decoder-side components of the tax are separated per paradigm.
diff.differentiation_statement: The constrained-decoding-for-diffusion line (DINGO, NeurIPS 2025; Muendler et al. CFG-diffusion 2025-08; LAVE 2026-01; EPIC and Dang & Ermon 2026, concurrent) is exclusively METHOD-side: each paper proposes a decoder that guarantees satisfaction of a regex/finite-automaton/CFG constraint and then reports (a) constraint-satisfaction rate, (b) downstream accuracy, and (c) wall-clock overhead RELATIVE TO ITS OWN UNCONSTRAINED DIFFUSION BASELINE. Not one of them pairs its constrained arm with a constrained AR arm at matched generation cost, so none can answer the field's central a-priori argument for the diffusion paradigm -- that global constraints are cheaper to satisfy by iterative revision than prefix-locally. Symmetrically, the constraint-tax measurement line (Let Me Speak Freely, EMNLP 2024; The Format Tax, 2026-04; The Constraint Tax for SLMs, 2026-05) does the paradigm-relative accounting we want but has ZERO diffusion arms and no executable-code task surface. Our work is the intersection nobody occupies: a constraint-STRENGTH ladder x paradigm x matched-cumulative-token grid on executable code, with a strength level (L3, hard structural validity as an invariant of a typed-AST decoder runtime, not a logit mask) that is strictly stronger than anything in either line -- AnCoder/AnchorTree and TreeDiff use the AST only as a soft prior over which tokens to resolve or corrupt first and cannot guarantee parseability, while all the CFG/FA papers constrain a flat token canvas. Our cost unit is also different and stricter: cumulative_model_tokens (prompt + canvas re-attended per step) rather than NFE or wall-clock, which is the only unit that lets a step-based diffusion decoder and a token-based AR decoder be placed on one axis. Finally, half the grid is already measured with an honest, audited accounting convention (including budget-truncated cases, which we previously got wrong by 2.85x/3.69x and corrected), so the marginal claim rests on one new arm rather than a from-scratch campaign.

related_work.citation: Tarun Suresh, Debangshu Banerjee, Shubham Ugare, Sasa Misailovic, Gagandeep Singh. DINGO: Constrained Inference for Diffusion LLMs. arXiv:2505.23061.
related_work.venue_status: NeurIPS 2025 poster. Verified via OpenReview API v2 notes/search (venueid=NeurIPS.cc/2025/Conference, venue='NeurIPS 2025 poster'; an earlier ICML 2025 R2-FM Workshop poster record also exists) and cross-checked on DBLP (NeurIPS 2025, Conference and Workshop Papers).
related_work.what_it_covers: Dynamic-programming constrained decoding for diffusion LLMs that is provably distribution-preserving and enforces user-specified regular expressions; up to 68 pp improvement over unconstrained inference on symbolic math and JSON generation benchmarks.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Regex-only (no CFG, no type system, no hard-invariant runtime). No executable-code task surface. No AR arm at all, hence no paradigm-relative accounting. Cost reported as algorithmic efficiency, not as a quality-vs-cumulative-token frontier.
related_work.known_defects: The 68 pp headline is measured against an unconstrained diffusion baseline that collapses on schema tasks, which flatters the constrained arm: it compares 'valid output' to 'no valid output' rather than isolating the answer-quality component -- exactly the confound The Constraint Tax (2605.26128) later shows matters (schema validity can go to 100% while answer accuracy falls). No prompt-only format-request control, so the decoder-side share of the effect is unidentified (the defect The Format Tax names as dominant). Distribution-preservation is proved w.r.t. the model's own factorised posterior, which is not the same as preserving task accuracy, yet accuracy gains are attributed to the constraint.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (id_list=2505.23061, v1 2025-05-29, cs.LG/cs.PL/cs.SE); OpenReview API v2 notes/search for venueid; DBLP publ API.

related_work.citation: Niels Muendler, Jasper Dekoninck, Martin Vechev. Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars. arXiv:2508.10111.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2025) as of check. DBLP publ API returns only 'CoRR 2025 | Informal and Other Publications'; no conference/journal record; arXiv abs page shows no venue comment. OpenReview search returned no submission record.
related_work.what_it_covers: First CFG-constrained decoding method for diffusion LLMs; reduces constrained decoding to additive infilling, then to CFG-vs-regular-language intersection emptiness; evaluated on C++ code infilling and JSON structured extraction. Reports near-perfect syntactic correctness while 'preserving or improving' functional correctness with practical overhead.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: This is the single most dangerous prior work for our claim's SIGN, because it already reports approximately zero-or-negative constraint tax for diffusion on code. But it does so (i) without an AR counterpart measured under an equivalent constraint, (ii) on C++ infilling rather than from-scratch HumanEval+/MBPP+ synthesis, (iii) at a single operating point rather than across a token budget, and (iv) at token-mask strength, not hard-invariant strength. So it establishes one cell of our grid, not the grid.
related_work.known_defects: 'Preserving or improving functional correctness' is asserted without a compute-matched comparison -- constrained decoding changes the effective number of model calls and the per-step candidate set, so the constrained and unconstrained arms are not priced in the same unit. Overhead is characterised as 'practical' rather than as a cost axis. No prompt-only control. Infilling task selection means the model is given most of the program, which minimises the space in which a syntax constraint can bind; the claim is unlikely to replicate on from-scratch synthesis where unparseable output rates are 10-90x higher.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + arXiv abs page (subjects cs.LG/cs.FL/cs.PL/cs.SE, no comments field); DBLP publ API venue lookup; OpenReview API v2 notes/search (no hit).

related_work.citation: Meihua Dang, Stefano Ermon. Constrained Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Efficient Inference over Finite Automata. arXiv:2607.07026.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2026). DBLP returns only 'CoRR 2026 | Informal and Other Publications'; no OpenReview submission record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Exact, tractable sampling from the constrained mean-field posterior under any finite-automaton constraint, viewing FAs as graphical models; log-depth sampling via arithmetic-circuit depth reduction. Evaluated on Dream-7B and LLaDA-8B across function calling (xLAM, BFCL), planning (Sudoku, Countdown), text-to-SQL (Spider), math (GSM-Symbolic). BFCL-Live greedy 63.9% -> 71.5%; stochastic 22.3% -> 69.0%; under 5% wall-clock overhead.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent, so it cannot preempt us, and it is the closest method-side work on our exact base model family (Dream-7B). Still no executable-code benchmark, no AR arm, no token-cost frontier -- overhead is wall-clock relative to its own unconstrained diffusion baseline only.
related_work.known_defects: The dramatic stochastic-sampling gain (22.3 -> 69.0) is a repair of a degenerate baseline ('the unconstrained baseline collapses'), which measures the fragility of unconstrained stochastic diffusion decoding rather than the value of the constraint; a temperature/top-p sweep control is absent, and we have independently measured that top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 alone moves HumanEval by +14.6 points, i.e. sampler hygiene can account for a large share of apparent method gains. Wall-clock overhead <5% is reported without matched output quality at matched token spend. Finite-automaton expressiveness excludes the type/AST constraints that actually bind on code.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-07-08) + arXiv abs page full abstract; DBLP publ API; OpenReview API v2 notes/search; also surfaced as a DINGO citer via Semantic Scholar citations endpoint.

related_work.citation: Hyundong Jin, Yo-Sub Han. EPIC: Efficient and Parallel Inference under CFG Constraints for Diffusion Language Models. arXiv:2606.00722.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2026). DBLP: 'CoRR 2026 | Informal and Other Publications'. No OpenReview record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Efficiency-focused CFG-constrained decoding for dLLMs: lexing memoization, Earley-style validation instead of DFA, relaxed compatible-subset selection for parallel commit. Up to 67.5% inference-time reduction and up to 90.5% overhead reduction vs prior CFG-constrained dLLM decoding, on three benchmarks with four models. Explicitly frames the problem as prior CFG methods 'diminishing one of the key advantages of diffusion over autoregressive models, namely parallel decoding'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: This paper comes closest to naming our question -- it says CFG constraints erode diffusion's paradigm advantage -- but treats that erosion purely as latency to be engineered away, never as a quality tax, and never measures the AR side. Concurrent, so no preemption.
related_work.known_defects: Optimises and reports SPEED (inference time, overhead) while the quality axis is not the headline; a decoder that commits multiple 'compatible' tokens per step under a relaxed subset criterion trades distributional fidelity for parallelism, and the paper's abstract does not report the accuracy cost of that relaxation against DINGO/LAVE-style exact methods. 'Three benchmarks, four models' unspecified in the abstract -- I could not verify whether any is executable code. No AR baseline, so the framing claim about diffusion's advantage over AR is argued rather than measured.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-05-30) + arXiv abs page full abstract; DBLP publ API; Semantic Scholar DINGO-citations list.

related_work.citation: Boyan Han, Yiwei Wang, Yi Song, Yujun Cai, Chi Zhang. Dynamic Infilling Anchors for Format-Constrained Generation in Diffusion Large Language Models (DIA). arXiv:2606.04535.
related_work.venue_status: ACL 2026 main conference per DBLP publ API ('ACL 2026 | Conference and Workshop Papers') and the arXiv comment ('Accepted to the 64th Annual Meeting of the ACL'). CAVEAT: OpenReview shows a same-titled record with venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Withdrawn_Submission, i.e. it was withdrawn from ICLR before the ACL acceptance; I could NOT locate an OpenReview ARR camera-ready record to satisfy the OpenReview-mandatory rule, so the ACL 2026 status rests on DBLP + author comment.
related_work.what_it_covers: Training-free dynamic estimation of end-anchor positions to set generation length before iterative infilling, so format constraints (parseable JSON, reasoning templates) are enforced without rigid fixed spans; zero-shot gains in format compliance and answer accuracy on GSM8K and MATH.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Non-code (math reasoning), no AR arm, no token-cost accounting. Its motivating observation -- that fixed-span anchors cause truncated reasoning or redundant content -- is precisely the capacity/budget-truncation failure mode we already measure in our scaffold Large arm (17 HE+ / 35 MBPP+ tasks hit model_call_budget), giving us a citable point of contact.
related_work.known_defects: Measures format compliance and accuracy but not cost, so 'avoiding the inefficiencies of fixed-span methods' is an efficiency claim without an efficiency metric. GSM8K/MATH format compliance is a weak proxy for structural validity because the constraint is a template, not a grammar -- there is no executable-correctness ground truth. No prompt-only control separating the format instruction from the anchor mechanism.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-06-03, comment states ACL 2026); DBLP publ API (ACL 2026); OpenReview API v2 notes/search (found ICLR 2026 Withdrawn_Submission record only).

related_work.citation: Anton Xue, Litu Rout, Constantine Caramanis, Sanjay Shakkottai. AnCoder: Anchored Code Generation via Discrete Diffusion Models (AnchorTree). arXiv:2602.17688.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2026). DBLP: 'AnCoder: Anchored Code Generation via Discrete Diffusion Models. | CoRR 2026 | Informal and Other Publications'. No OpenReview submission record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: AST-derived hierarchical priors used to PRIORITISE resolving syntactically/semantically salient tokens (keywords, identifiers) during discrete diffusion, establishing a structural scaffold that guides remaining generation; AnCoder model family presented as a parameter-efficient path to code generation.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Closest work to our L3 arm conceptually, but it is soft prioritisation, not a hard invariant: it cannot guarantee parseability, so it has no constraint to price and no tax to report. No AR constraint-tax comparison, no token-cost frontier.
related_work.known_defects: Abstract reports no numbers, no benchmark names, and no baseline identities -- the claim 'parameter-efficient path to high-quality code generation' is unfalsifiable as stated, and I could not verify which benchmarks or which unconstrained diffusion control were used. Because the AST prior enters at the denoising-order level, a decisive control is 'random salient-token ordering at matched schedule', which the abstract does not mention; without it the gain could be an ordering/curriculum effect rather than a structural one. Parameter-efficiency claims are not compute-matched in the abstract.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-02-05) + arXiv abs page full abstract; DBLP publ API; OpenReview API v2 notes/search (no hit); Semantic Scholar DINGO-citations list.

related_work.citation: Yiming Zeng, Jinghan Cao, Zexin Li, Yiming Chen, Tao Ren, Zhuochun Li, Dawei Xiang, Xidong Wu, Shangqian Gao, Tingting Yu. TreeDiff: AST-Guided Code Generation with Diffusion LLMs. arXiv:2508.01473.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2025). DBLP: 'CoRR 2025 | Informal and Other Publications'; v3 dated 2026-01-06; arXiv abs page shows no venue comment. No OpenReview record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Syntax-aware diffusion TRAINING: instead of random token masking, selectively mask tokens belonging to key AST nodes, so corruption aligns with code structure. Reports 13.3% relative improvement over random-masking training for code generation.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Attacks the same 'diffusion ignores code structure' premise from the training side rather than the decoding side. No hard validity guarantee, no AR comparison, no constraint tax, no token-cost accounting. Directly relevant to us because our scaffold_coder/corruption.py implements a structure-aware corruption schedule -- we should cite this as the training-side analogue and be explicit that our contribution is the runtime invariant plus the paradigm-relative pricing, not the corruption schedule.
related_work.known_defects: The 13.3% relative gain is measured against random masking only; there is no matched-compute control (structure-aware masking changes the effective difficulty and therefore the effective token budget per training step), and the abstract names no benchmark, no base model, and no absolute pass@1, so the number cannot be located on any published frontier. Relative-improvement-only reporting is exactly the accounting convention that CaRE (2607.24763) shows reverses several published diffusion rankings once actual NFE is controlled.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2025-08-02, v3 2026-01-06) + arXiv abs page (no comments); DBLP publ API.

related_work.citation: Yitong Zhang, Yongmin Li, Yuetong Liu, Jia Li, Xiaoran Jia, Zherui Li, Ge Li. Lookahead-then-Verify: Reliable Constrained Decoding for Diffusion LLMs under Context-Free Grammars (LAVE). arXiv:2602.00612.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2026). OpenReview shows venueid=OpenReview.net/Public_Article, venue='CoRR 2026'; DBLP: 'CoRR 2026 | Informal and Other Publications'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Exploits the dLLM property that all positions have distributions each forward pass to do lookahead verification, preventing intermediate outputs that cannot be completed into valid strings -- the reliability gap in prior dLLM constrained decoding. Targets source code and chemical expressions as CFG-defined languages.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Pure method-side reliability; no AR arm, no matched-token quality frontier, no executable pass@1 accounting reported in the abstract. Notably a same-group follow-up (Dgrammar) appears as an ACL ARR 2026 May submission, so this subfield is crowded on METHOD and empty on PARADIGM-RELATIVE COST.
related_work.known_defects: Lookahead-then-verify costs extra forward-pass information use per committed token, so 'reliability' is bought with compute that the abstract does not price against the unconstrained baseline in a common unit. 'Reliably generate syntactically valid outputs' is validity, not correctness -- the functional-correctness consequence of rejecting completions the model wanted is not isolated. No AR reference point for what the same CFG costs a left-to-right decoder.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-01-31, v2 2026-02-08); OpenReview API v2 notes/search (Public_Article / CoRR 2026); DBLP publ API.

related_work.citation: Jinwoo Kim, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Loris D'Antoni. Continuous Diffusion Models Can Obey Formal Syntax. arXiv:2602.12468.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv v1 2026-02-12, v2 2026-05-27; no venue comment on arXiv; no DBLP conference record surfaced; no OpenReview submission record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Training-free guidance for CONTINUOUS latent diffusion LMs: an analytic score for the probability that a latent decodes to a regex-accepted string, whose gradient steers sampling. Implemented as Diffinity on PLAID, evaluated on 180 regular-expression constraint tasks.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Different model class (continuous latent diffusion, PLAID-scale) than our masked discrete diffusion at 7B; regex not CFG/types; no code execution, no AR arm, no cost frontier. Useful mainly as evidence that the constrained-diffusion line is broad but uniformly method-side and non-executable.
related_work.known_defects: PLAID-scale continuous diffusion is far below 7B instruction-tuned code models, so nothing about the constraint's cost transfers to the regime where diffusion is actually competitive -- a scale-replication gap. 180 regex tasks measure satisfiability, not downstream task quality. Same first-author group as The Format Tax (D'Antoni, Berg-Kirkpatrick) yet the two papers do not connect guidance-side and prompt-side constraint costs, which is an opening.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-02-12, v2 2026-05-27); DBLP publ API and OpenReview API v2 searches returned no venue record.

related_work.citation: Ivan Yee Lee, Loris D'Antoni, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick. The Format Tax. arXiv:2604.03616.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2026). DBLP: 'The Format Tax. | CoRR 2026 | Informal and Other Publications'. No OpenReview record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: The most important pre-cutoff work for our framing. Across six open-weight models, four API models, four formats (JSON/XML/LaTeX/Markdown) and math/science/logic/writing tasks, structured-output requirements substantially degrade performance -- and crucially the DOMINANT cost enters at the PROMPT, not the decoder: format-requesting instructions alone cause most of the accuracy loss before any decoder constraint applies. Prescribes decoupling (freeform then reformat, or extended thinking). Notes recent closed-weight models show little format tax.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: ZERO diffusion arms. No executable-code task surface. No cost/compute axis at all (accuracy only). Its own headline decomposition -- prompt-side vs decoder-side share of the tax -- has never been run for a diffusion model, and its 'decouple reasoning from formatting' prescription is mechanically what a diffusion model does natively via iterative revision, which is a testable and unexercised prediction.
related_work.known_defects: Being AR/API-only, its central diagnosis is confounded with left-to-right generation: it cannot distinguish 'format instructions consume reasoning capacity' from 'format instructions force prefix-local commitment'. A masked-diffusion arm separates these, because a diffusion model can emit the wrapper and fill the payload in any order. Its two-pass remedy also costs roughly 2x tokens, which the paper does not price -- so 'decoupling recovers most lost accuracy' is not compute-matched, and our cumulative_model_tokens unit is exactly the instrument that would price it.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-04-04) + full abstract; DBLP publ API (CoRR 2026); OpenReview API v2 notes/search (no hit).

related_work.citation: Jaideep Ray. The Constraint Tax: Measuring Validity-Correctness Tradeoffs in Structured Outputs for Small Language Models. arXiv:2605.26128.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2026). DBLP: 'CoRR 2026 | Informal and Other Publications'. No OpenReview record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Owns the term 'constraint tax' as a measurement protocol isolating answer- and executable-accuracy loss caused by structured-output constraints at fixed model, task distribution, and problem instances. 15,000 generations on Qwen2.5-0.5B/1.5B and SmolLM2-1.7B: hard answer-only schema decoding raises schema validity 61.5% -> 100.0% but drops answer accuracy 19.7% -> 11.0% and raises wrong-but-valid outputs 49.5% -> 88.9%; a calendar tool-call task falls 91.5% -> 48.0% executable accuracy under hard schema at equal 100% validity. Recommends 'reason free, constrain late'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent (2026-05-20, after the 2026-05-07 cutoff), so it does not preempt us, but it does claim the NAME and the AR-side protocol -- we must cite it and adopt its instance-fixed design. It is sub-3B AR-only, JSON/tool-call only, no code synthesis benchmark, no diffusion arm, and no compute axis (fixed model, no budget sweep).
related_work.known_defects: Single-author, sub-3B, no compute matching, and the paradigm generality is untested: everything reported could be a small-model capacity artefact, which the paper itself half-concedes by probing 'the 3B boundary'. Directly contradicts Muendler et al.'s type-constrained AR result (compilation errors halved AND functional correctness up on HumanEval/MBPP at 7B-30B+), so the sign of the AR constraint tax is scale- and constraint-type-dependent and nobody has mapped that surface. Our 7B-vs-7B, code-execution, budget-swept design is the natural repair.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-05-20) + full abstract; DBLP publ API; Semantic Scholar DINGO-citations list (a sibling paper, Constraint Tax in Open-Weight LLMs arXiv:2606.25605, 2026-06-24, also concurrent, documents grammar-mask-induced tool-call suppression).

related_work.citation: Niels Muendler, Jingxuan He, Hao Wang, Koushik Sen, Dawn Song, Martin Vechev. Type-Constrained Code Generation with Language Models. arXiv:2504.09246.
related_work.venue_status: Published: Proc. ACM Program. Lang. (PACMPL) 2025, journal article, per DBLP publ API. Pre-cutoff and peer-reviewed.
related_work.what_it_covers: The strongest AR-side counter-evidence to our claim's stated direction. Type-constrained decoding via prefix automata plus search over inhabitable types, sound enforcement of well-typedness, formalised on a simply-typed language and extended to TypeScript. On HumanEval and MBPP it more than halves compilation errors AND significantly increases functional correctness across model sizes and families including 30B+ open-weight models, on synthesis, translation, and repair.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It is AR-only and TypeScript-only, with no token-cost accounting and no diffusion counterpart. But it means the AR constraint tax at automaton strength on code is plausibly NEGATIVE at 7B+, which is why our claim must be restated as strength- and budget-indexed rather than 'diffusion pays less'. It also gives us the AR L2 arm's expected sign for free, sharpening the kill criterion.
related_work.known_defects: No compute/token accounting: type-constrained decoding runs inhabitable-type search per step, so the reported quality gain is not priced -- our cumulative_model_tokens unit would place it on a frontier for the first time. TypeScript-only means the constraint mechanism does not transfer to our Python benchmarks without a re-implementation, and a Python type checker gives far weaker guarantees, so the constraint STRENGTH is not comparable across languages -- an under-acknowledged limitation. Functional-correctness gains are reported without separating 'fixed a real bug' from 'refused to emit an unparseable answer that would have scored 0 anyway'.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2025-04-12, v2 2025-05-08) + full abstract; DBLP publ API returns Proc. ACM Program. Lang. 2025 journal record.

related_work.citation: Zhi Rui Tam, Cheng-Kuang Wu, Yi-Lin Tsai, Chieh-Yen Lin, Hung-yi Lee, Yun-Nung Chen. Let Me Speak Freely? A Study on the Impact of Format Restrictions on Performance of Large Language Models. arXiv:2408.02442.
related_work.venue_status: EMNLP 2024, Conference and Workshop Papers, per DBLP publ API. Pre-cutoff and peer-reviewed.
related_work.what_it_covers: The originating format-restriction-degrades-reasoning result: LLMs under JSON/XML constraints lose reasoning ability, and stricter constraints cause greater degradation. Establishes the monotone strength-vs-degradation relationship our L0-L3 ladder generalises.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: AR-only, 2024-era models, no diffusion, no code execution, no compute accounting. Its monotone strength->degradation finding is the null hypothesis our L3 low-budget result violates (a hard invariant that IMPROVES quality at fixed budget), which is a clean way to state our contribution against a well-cited baseline.
related_work.known_defects: Conflates prompt-side and decoder-side constraint effects, which The Format Tax (2026-04) later shows are separable and prompt-dominated -- so the 2024 headline over-attributes to constrained decoding. No cost axis. Model generation is now dated and the 'stricter is worse' monotonicity is contradicted at 7B+ for type constraints on code (Muendler et al., PACMPL 2025), so the strength-degradation relation is not universal and its boundaries are unmapped.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2024-08-05, v3 2024-10-14); DBLP publ API (EMNLP 2024).

related_work.citation: Kanghee Park, Jiayu Wang, Taylor Berg-Kirkpatrick, Nadia Polikarpova, Loris D'Antoni. Grammar-Aligned Decoding (ASAp). arXiv:2405.21047.
related_work.venue_status: NeurIPS 2024 poster. Verified via OpenReview API v2 notes/search (venueid=NeurIPS.cc/2024/Conference, venue='NeurIPS 2024 poster') and DBLP (conf/NIPS/2024).
related_work.what_it_covers: The mechanistic explanation of WHY the AR constraint tax exists: greedy grammar-constrained decoding distorts the LLM distribution so outputs are grammatical but not proportional to the model's own likelihoods, hence low quality. Proposes adaptive sampling with approximate expected futures to restore the correctly conditioned distribution.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: AR-only, and the distortion argument is precisely the theoretical asymmetry our claim rests on: greedy prefix-local masking distorts because the AR model cannot see the future, whereas a diffusion model's per-step full-sequence distribution plus revision is in principle less prefix-myopic. Nobody has tested that asymmetry empirically at matched cost, and GAD-style expected-future correction has no diffusion counterpart.
related_work.known_defects: ASAp's correction requires repeated sampling to approximate expected futures, so the fix costs compute that the paper does not convert into a quality-per-token frontier -- the distortion is priced in likelihood terms, not budget terms. Evaluated on constraint-satisfaction/likelihood proxies rather than executable pass@1, so it never shows that undistorting the distribution recovers functional correctness on code. The distortion analysis is not carried over to any non-left-to-right model, which is the gap our diffusion arms fill.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2024-05-31, comment 'Accepted to NeurIPS 2024'); OpenReview API v2 notes/search venueid; DBLP publ API.

related_work.citation: Yash Shah, Abhijit Chakraborty, Vivek Gupta. CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models. arXiv:2607.24763.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv API published field 2026-06-04 (note: the 2607.* identifier is inconsistent with that date; I report the API-provided published field and flag the discrepancy). No DBLP record surfaced.
related_work.what_it_covers: Methodological ally: seven recent remasking papers evaluate under incompatible settings (nominal step counts, metrics, temperatures) making rankings incomparable. CaRE standardises ACTUAL NFE, enforces multi-metric reporting, controls stochasticity, across 7 remasking strategies x LLaDA-8B-Base/Dream-7B-Base x 4 stochasticity levels x 3 step budgets. Finds temperature explains most MAUVE variance and compute-matched comparison REVERSES several published rankings.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Validates our cost-accounting discipline from the outside and gives us a citable authority for why NFE/steps are not a legitimate cross-family unit. But it is open-domain LM (OpenWebText, LM1B, MAUVE), not code, not execution-graded, and has no AR arm and no constraint dimension -- so it standardises WITHIN masked diffusion, while we need a unit valid ACROSS paradigms, which is why we use cumulative_model_tokens rather than actual-NFE.
related_work.known_defects: Standardises on actual NFE, which is still a diffusion-internal unit and does not commensurate with AR token generation -- so CaRE cannot itself support any diffusion-vs-AR comparison, the very comparison the field most needs. MAUWE/MAUVE-style distributional metrics on OpenWebText/LM1B have no executable ground truth, so 'ranking reversals' are reversals in a proxy metric. Restricted to base models, so nothing is said about instruction-tuned code models where the practical claims are made.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and full abstract (published field 2026-06-04); DBLP publ API returned no record for the title.

related_work.citation: Jingyao Zhang, Tianlin Li, Xiaoyu Zhang, Qiang Hu, Bin Shi. Exploring the Power of Diffusion Large Language Models for Software Engineering: An Empirical Investigation. arXiv:2510.04605.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (CoRR 2025) per DBLP publ API; no conference venue. Previously audited in this project's own notes (TASK_SURFACE_LIT_GAPS.md).
related_work.what_it_covers: The only paper claiming diffusion > AR across the SE lifecycle (generation, defect detection, repair): 52,937 tasks, 7B dLLMs beat AR-LLMs by ~30% average accuracy, 113% on cross-file repair, with better latency. It is the closest thing to a paradigm-level empirical comparison on code and therefore the natural target for our accounting critique.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No constraint dimension at all, and no compute-matched cost unit -- 'superior efficiency and reduced latency' is asserted without a quality-per-token frontier. Leaves the entire constraint-tax question untouched while claiming paradigm superiority on code, which is exactly the overclaim our matched-token grid disciplines.
related_work.known_defects: Severe and independently verified in this project's audit: (i) compares commercial Mercury-Diffusion-7B against AR-Llama3-8B, a GENERAL model rather than a code model, with no Qwen2.5-Coder control -- a catastrophic confound that alone could produce the 30%/113% gaps; (ii) two garbled placeholder citations for its own PR/DDF1 metric definitions; (iii) cites LLaDA as arXiv:2309.12401, which is an astrophysics paper on assembly bias, i.e. a fabricated reference; (iv) CoRR-only, unreviewed. Our matched AR arm (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, same benchmark, same grader, same token unit) is the direct repair.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2025-10-06); DBLP publ API (CoRR 2025, no venue); project-internal audit recorded in /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/TASK_SURFACE_LIT_GAPS.md.

followup_openings.target_paper: The Format Tax (arXiv:2604.03616, 2026-04-04, pre-cutoff)
followup_openings.defect: Its central, most-cited decomposition -- that the format tax is dominated by the PROMPT (format-requesting instructions) rather than by the DECODER constraint -- is established entirely on autoregressive open-weight and API models. There is not a single diffusion arm. Because every model tested generates left-to-right, the paper cannot distinguish 'format instructions consume reasoning capacity' from 'format instructions force prefix-local commitment before the answer is known'. Its prescribed remedy (freeform-then-reformat, or extended thinking) roughly doubles token spend and is never priced.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run its exact prompt-vs-decoder decomposition on a masked diffusion model, adding the level it lacks (L3 hard invariant) and the axis it lacks (cumulative_model_tokens). A diffusion model can emit the structural wrapper and fill the payload in any order, so it natively implements 'decouple reasoning from formatting' inside one generation -- if the prompt-side tax shrinks or vanishes for diffusion while the decoder-side tax persists, the two mechanisms are separated for the first time, and the paper's remedy is shown to be a workaround for a specifically autoregressive defect. We also price its two-pass remedy against a single-pass diffusion arm at matched tokens.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This converts a purely negative measurement result into a mechanistic claim about why left-to-right generation pays for structure, and it gives the diffusion paradigm its first quantified, non-latency argument. It is also cheap: the format-tax protocol is prompt-level, needs no new training, and reuses our existing evalplus harness plus an added JSON-schema leg.

followup_openings.target_paper: Muendler, Dekoninck, Vechev, Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with CFGs (arXiv:2508.10111, 2025-08-13, pre-cutoff) and the whole constrained-diffusion line (DINGO NeurIPS 2025; LAVE; EPIC; Dang & Ermon)
followup_openings.defect: Every paper in this line measures its constrained arm against ITS OWN unconstrained diffusion baseline and reports satisfaction rate, accuracy, and wall-clock overhead. None pairs the constrained diffusion arm with a constrained AR arm under an equivalent constraint at matched generation cost. Consequently the line's implicit motivating premise -- that global/structural constraints suit diffusion better than AR -- is argued from architecture (EPIC even states CFG constraints erode diffusion's parallel-decoding advantage) but never measured. Additionally, 2508.10111's 'preserving or improving functional correctness' is obtained on C++ INFILLING, where most of the program is given and a syntax constraint has little room to bind.
followup_openings.our_fix: Build the missing 2x2-plus: {diffusion, AR} x {unconstrained, constrained} on from-scratch executable synthesis (HumanEval+/MBPP+, evalplus untrusted_check), every cell priced in cumulative_model_tokens, with constraint strength laddered L1/L2/L3 rather than treated as a single binary. Report the paradigm-relative tax delta with paired bootstrap CIs. Include the from-scratch regime the line avoids, where our own measurements show unparseable-output rates of 94% (HE+) and 89% (MBPP+) at low budgets -- i.e. the regime where a validity constraint can actually bind.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It supplies the one number the entire constrained-diffusion subfield needs but cannot produce from its own designs, and it does so on the benchmark and model family (Dream-7B) those papers already use, so the result is immediately legible to that community. It also turns a crowded method race into an evaluation-protocol contribution, which is much harder to scoop.

followup_openings.target_paper: The Constraint Tax for SLMs (arXiv:2605.26128, concurrent) vs Type-Constrained Code Generation (arXiv:2504.09246, PACMPL 2025, pre-cutoff)
followup_openings.defect: These two peer-adjacent results have OPPOSITE signs and nobody has reconciled them. Ray reports hard schema constraints dropping answer accuracy 19.7% -> 11.0% and executable tool-call accuracy 91.5% -> 48.0% on sub-3B AR models. Muendler et al. report type constraints halving compilation errors AND significantly raising functional correctness on HumanEval/MBPP at 7B-30B+. So the AR constraint tax flips sign somewhere in (model scale) x (constraint type: schema/regex vs type system) x (task: tool-call vs code synthesis), and that surface is entirely unmapped. Neither paper has a compute axis.
followup_openings.our_fix: Map the sign-flip surface with the two axes both papers omit: constraint STRENGTH as an ordered ladder (L1 prompt-only, L2 token-mask/grammar, L3 hard invariant by construction) and token BUDGET as a swept variable, holding model scale fixed at 7B and holding the grader fixed at evalplus execution. Our already-measured scaffold ladder gives the L3 diffusion column for free and shows the flip explicitly WITHIN one arm: L3 is a negative tax at low budget (.177/.354 at 13.98k/7.08k tokens vs ~.000/.008 for unconstrained diffusion at 19-22k) and a large positive tax at high budget (.177 vs .707). Then test whether hard-invariant AR flips at the same budget.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: 'Is the constraint tax positive or negative?' is currently answered inconsistently in the literature, and the honest resolution -- it depends on budget and strength, and it can be negative -- is a more robust and more publishable finding than any paradigm-superiority claim. It also directly de-risks our candidate: it survives even if the diffusion-vs-AR difference is null, because the budget-indexed sign flip is itself the result.

followup_openings.target_paper: Exploring the Power of Diffusion LLMs for Software Engineering (arXiv:2510.04605, 2025-10-06, pre-cutoff, CoRR-only)
followup_openings.defect: The only existing paradigm-level diffusion-beats-AR claim on code is built on comparing commercial Mercury-Diffusion-7B against AR-Llama3-8B -- a general model, not a code model -- with no Qwen2.5-Coder control, so the reported 30% average and 113% cross-file-repair gains are confounded with 'code model vs general model'. It also contains two garbled placeholder citations for its own metric definitions and cites LLaDA as an arXiv ID that is actually an astrophysics paper, i.e. a fabricated reference. It is unreviewed. Yet it is the paper a reviewer will cite at us as prior art for any diffusion-vs-AR code comparison.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the properly matched comparison it should have run: Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B (diffusion, code-specialised, adapted from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) against Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (AR, same lineage) on the same benchmarks with the same evalplus grader and the same cumulative_model_tokens unit, then add the constraint dimension it lacks entirely. Because the diffusion model is literally adapted from the AR model, the paradigm is close to the only free variable -- a control quality that paper cannot approach.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It pre-empts the obvious 'this was already shown' objection by demonstrating the prior claim rests on a lineage confound, and it makes our AR arm (already running on .104) do double duty: it is both our constraint-tax control and a correction of the field's headline paradigm result. Base-lineage matching is a control design reviewers immediately recognise as strong.

followup_openings.target_paper: AnCoder/AnchorTree (arXiv:2602.17688, 2026-02-05) and TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473, 2025-08-02), both pre-cutoff, both CoRR-only
followup_openings.defect: Both use the AST as a SOFT prior -- AnchorTree to prioritise resolving salient tokens at decode time, TreeDiff to bias which tokens get masked at train time -- and both therefore report relative improvements over a random-masking or unstructured baseline without any validity guarantee, without absolute pass@1 locatable on a published frontier, and without compute matching. AnCoder's abstract names no benchmark, no baseline, and no numbers at all. Neither has the decisive control: matched-schedule random salient-token ordering, which would separate a genuine structural effect from a decode-order/curriculum effect. Neither compares to AR under any constraint.
followup_openings.our_fix: Position our L3 as the hard-invariant upper end of the same axis they explore softly, and measure the axis as an axis: L2 soft AST prioritisation (reimplemented as logit masking to parseable continuations, plus a random-order matched control) versus L3 hard invariant by construction, both priced in cumulative_model_tokens, both graded by execution. This gives soft structural guidance its first compute-matched evaluation against a hard guarantee, and gives our runtime a principled place in a lineage rather than looking like an isolated engineering artefact. TreeDiff also becomes the training-side citation for our existing scaffold_coder/corruption.py schedule, which we should credit explicitly rather than have a reviewer discover.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts our biggest apparent liability -- 'someone already did AST-guided diffusion' -- into our clearest differentiation, because soft-prior work structurally cannot report a constraint tax (there is no constraint), and it adds a control (random-order matched schedule) that both target papers are missing and that a reviewer would demand of them.

followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, concurrent) and the accounting conventions of the whole masked-diffusion literature
followup_openings.defect: CaRE correctly shows that nominal step counts are not a valid unit and that compute-matched comparison reverses several published remasking rankings -- but it standardises on ACTUAL NFE, which is still a diffusion-internal quantity with no autoregressive analogue. So the field's newest evaluation-protocol paper still cannot support a diffusion-vs-AR comparison. Its metrics (MAUVE on OpenWebText/LM1B) have no executable ground truth, and it covers base models only.
followup_openings.our_fix: Adopt CaRE's discipline but replace its unit with cumulative_model_tokens (prompt + canvas re-attended per step, which we measure at 685 tok/step on HE+ and 604 on MBPP+ for a flat 512-token canvas), the one accounting convention that is well-defined for a step-based diffusion decoder, a variable-capacity structural runtime, and a token-by-token AR decoder simultaneously. Publish the unit as an explicit protocol contribution with our own two accounting retractions documented as worked examples: NFE is not a cross-family unit, and aggregating only naturally-terminating cases understated our scaffold Large cost by 2.85x (HE+) and 3.69x (MBPP+) because it silently dropped the most expensive, budget-truncated tasks. Enforce reading process OR failure_process in every aggregation.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A cross-paradigm cost unit is a reusable contribution that outlives any single result, and the two documented retractions make the protocol credible in a way an unforced methods section cannot -- they demonstrate the failure mode is real and easy to hit. It also hardens every other leg of this candidate against the exact criticism that sank our earlier refinement grid.

lens.title: Protocol Sensitivity Dominates Method Gains: A Compute-Aware Audit Protocol for Diffusion Code Evaluation
lens.claim: On code benchmarks, decoding-protocol choices that papers report as incidental (top_p, temperature, canvas length, block size, base-vs-chat prompting, step count) move pass@1 by more than the method deltas those papers claim, and the standard practice of holding nominal step count fixed while comparing across model families is not compute-matched. We provide the audit and a minimal reporting standard (cumulative model tokens + parse-validity + termination reason + failure_process inclusion), and we demonstrate at least one published code-model ranking that reverses under it.
lens.why_now: CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, 2026-06-04) proved exactly this for remasking strategies on OPEN-DOMAIN TEXT — standardising actual NFE 'reverses several published strategy rankings', and temperature explains most MAUVE variance across LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base on OpenWebText/LM1B. 'Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis' (arXiv:2606.19475, 2026-06-17) covers eight DLMs on eight benchmarks including coding but is a broad survey, not a protocol-sensitivity audit with a reversal demonstration. Neither does code with execution-based grading and cross-family cost units. We have independently measured a sensitivity of exactly the predicted magnitude: top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 moved HumanEval by +14.6 POINTS, larger than most published diffusion-LM method gains — and we have the three retractions that show precisely how these protocols fail (a did-not-raise verifier scoring empty solutions as passes; a 'restart' refinement policy that silently measured the base model instead of the method; and averaging that dropped budget-truncated cases and understated cost 2.85x/3.69x). Those are not embarrassments to hide, they are a taxonomy of failure modes with worked examples, which is what makes this a methods paper rather than a complaint.
lens.experiment: Fully factorial protocol sweep on HumanEval+/MBPP+ with evalplus untrusted_check: {temperature 0.1,0.2,0.6} x {top_p 0.95,1.0} x {steps 128,256,512} x {Dream-Coder-Instruct, Dream-Coder-Base with and without --add-bos-token/--base-continuation, DreamOn} — most cells are cheap and several already exist in runs/. Compute the variance decomposition: fraction of pass@1 variance attributable to protocol vs to model identity. Then the load-bearing deliverable: take one published cross-model code comparison, re-run it under (a) nominal-step matching as published and (b) cumulative-token matching, and show whether the ranking holds. Ship a reusable audit harness plus three worked failure-mode case studies from our own retracted runs (runs/*.BROKEN_VERIFIER are preserved on disk with the corrected numbers alongside — an unusually concrete provenance trail). Report NFE and cumulative_model_tokens and elapsed_seconds and peak_memory_gib per case, all of which our sidecar already emits.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE nearly everything: 30+ graded runs already on disk under runs/ (dream_instruct_heplus_nfe{16,32,64,128,256,512,1024}, matching mbppplus set, dream_coder_base_*, dreamon_*_r2, capacity ladder, schedule-only, plain-SFT control) with per-case metrics.rank*.jsonl carrying elapsed_seconds/peak_memory_gib/process; the preserved runs/*.BROKEN_VERIFIER pairs for the case studies; evalplus 0.3.1 as the single trusted grader; scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py already exposing --add-bos-token and --base-continuation (commit 3cef855); scripts/merge_evalplus_shards.py + compare_evalplus_runs.py; documented protocol notes in SAMPLER_RUNTIME.md, EVAL_HARNESS.md, UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md, DREAMON_BASELINE_AUDIT.md. Nothing missing for the diffusion-only audit; an AR reference row would want Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (absent both disks) but is optional here. Caveat to handle honestly: the unresolved Dream-Coder Base protocol reproduction (parse 4/16, not the targeted 8/16) must be reported as 'protocol not aligned', never as 'reproduction failed'.
lens.kill_criterion: Killed as a standalone contribution if protocol variance turns out SMALLER than method variance across the factorial (i.e. our +14.6-point top_p observation was an outlier specific to one configuration rather than a general sensitivity) — then it becomes an appendix to whichever of candidates 1-5 proceeds. Killed also if we cannot exhibit at least one concrete ranking reversal under token-matching, since 'protocols vary' without a reversal is a known-and-tolerated complaint rather than a finding; CaRE already set the bar by exhibiting reversals, and matching that bar on code with execution grading is the minimum. Third kill condition: if the published numbers we try to re-rank cannot be reproduced within noise under their own stated protocol, we cannot attribute a reversal to the accounting change.
lens.builds_on: CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763) — we port its compute-aware auditing thesis from open-domain text/MAUVE to executable code with pass@1 and cross-family token accounting, a setting CaRE explicitly does not cover; and arXiv:2606.19475 (Experimental Analysis), which surveys DLMs broadly but performs no protocol-sensitivity decomposition or reversal demonstration. Our distinctive asset is three documented, corrected, on-disk retractions as worked failure-mode case studies — a null-result-friendly contribution that is publishable whichever way the variance decomposition lands.

diff.differentiation_statement: No pre-cutoff paper makes this claim with this method in this setting, so nothing here disqualifies the candidate -- but the proposal as written is differentiated much more narrowly than it believes, and two of its three headline deliverables are already claimed. First, the parent it names, CaRE (concurrent, 2026-06-04), does not merely prove the thesis on open-domain text: its Table 11 already exhibits a compute-matched ranking reversal on HumanEval pass@1 (nominal-256 high_entropy 31.7 beats none 28.3, but at 3.4x the actual NFE; at matched NFE=437 none wins). The proposal's stated minimum bar -- "matching CaRE's bar on code with execution grading" -- is thus a delta on grading rigour, not on the existence of a code reversal. Second, and not cited in the proposal at all, dLLM (Zhou et al., arXiv 2026-02-26, PUBLISHED ACL 2026, pp. 78-88) is pre-cutoff, peer-reviewed, and states the sensitivity claim almost verbatim in Section 3.3 with a supporting two-panel sweep and a boxed Takeaway; and "Understanding Evaluation Illusion in dLLMs" (concurrent, 2026-06-28) already demonstrates on HumanEval and MBPP that decoding-method rankings flip under prompt template. Third, pre-cutoff arXiv:2510.18480 already published the critique of dLLM efficiency-evaluation practice, and arXiv:2502.17450 (ICPC 2025) already reported that top-p dominates temperature for code generation -- which is our +14.6-point observation's nearest prior. What genuinely remains ours is narrower and sharper: (a) every one of these works prices compute in NFE, nominal steps, or throughput, and NONE introduces a cross-family cost unit -- CaRE explicitly defends NFE-only in its appendix, and the Experimental Analysis paper computes a ~1200x TFLOPS gap between Dream and Qwen3-8B and then never connects it to its quality tables. Cumulative model tokens (prompt + canvas re-attended every step, hook-measured) applied to a three-way AR / flat-diffusion / variable-canvas-runtime comparison is unclaimed; (b) no prior work in this set apportions pass@1 variance between protocol factors and MODEL IDENTITY -- CaRE's ANOVA is within one model, dLLM's sweep is one-factor-at-a-time anchored at a per-model tuned optimum (a biased estimator that guarantees perturbations look like degradation), Evaluation Illusion has no decomposition; (c) no prior work runs code-specialised diffusion models on this question at all (all are LLaDA/Dream-Base; Dream-Coder and DreamOn are absent everywhere), nor grades with EvalPlus untrusted_check on full HumanEval+/MBPP+ rather than n=100 lm-eval subsamples; (d) the reporting standard we propose -- parse-validity, termination reason, and mandatory failure_process inclusion so budget-truncated cases cannot be silently dropped -- is nobody's, and our Retraction 3 (2.85x/3.69x cost understatement from dropping truncated cases) is the worked existence proof that its absence flatters methods; (e) our three preserved-on-disk retraction pairs (runs/*.BROKEN_VERIFIER alongside corrected numbers) are an unusually concrete provenance trail, and Speculative Refinement's Finding (4) -- "standard Python post-processing silently breaks code evaluation for non-AR generators" -- asserts one of our failure modes without quantifying it, which we can. One honest hazard the proposal must absorb: the reversal target it implies (arXiv:2510.04605, diffusion-beats-AR on SE) uses closed-weight Mercury, so its numbers cannot be reproduced under their own stated protocol, which trips the candidate's own third kill condition; the reversal must instead be staged against an open-weight, reproducible comparison. And a new confound has appeared -- arXiv:2608.04714 (2026-08-05) finds ~39% of observed benchmark variance is attributable to inference backend, so our factorial must pin and disclose the backend or our variance decomposition is itself confounded.

followup_openings.defect: The code leg is self-admittedly underpowered and cannot bear the weight placed on it. Authors state binomial uncertainty at n=100 is ~+/-4.7pp so the headline 32.0-vs-31.7 comparison 'is within sampling noise'; the +/-0.3 SEs are seed variance ONLY. Grading is lm-eval string matching on plain HumanEval, one model (LLaDA-8B-Base), 3 seeds. Separately, NFE-only accounting is internally inconsistent: the paper's own selling point is that '256 steps hides 128-513 forward passes', yet NFE still ignores that each diffusion pass re-attends the entire canvas, so it cannot price diffusion against AR or against a variable-canvas runtime -- and Appendix C defends this choice explicitly rather than acknowledging it as a limit.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run the compute-matched code leg at full strength: n=164 HumanEval+ and n=378 MBPP+ under EvalPlus untrusted_check with plus-tests, on code-specialised diffusion models CaRE never touched (Dream-Coder-Instruct/Base, DreamOn), with binomial CIs and paired-difference bootstrap per task rather than seed-only SEs. Then extend the cost axis from NFE to cumulative_model_tokens, hook-measured, and show that the SAME cells reorder differently under NFE-matching vs token-matching -- i.e. CaRE's own protocol point (nominal steps hide compute) recurses one level up: NFE hides attended compute. Our matched AR control (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, architecturally identical to Dream-Coder-Base: hidden 3584, 28 layers, 28/4 heads, intermediate 18944, vocab 152064, rope_theta 1e6) makes this the first three-way AR/diffusion/runtime cost-matched code comparison, and our own measurement (AR greedy 204/101 tokens_fed vs Dream nfe512 350,832/308,995) shows the two cost units disagree by ~1700x.
followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, concurrent 2026-06-04)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts the candidate from 'port CaRE to code' -- which CaRE partially did itself -- into 'CaRE's headline code result is underpowered and its chosen cost unit reproduces the very confound it names, one level up'. followup_openings.defect: The sensitivity claim rests on a biased estimator. Figure 5 anchors at 'Baseline denotes the best-performing setting' and perturbs one hyperparameter at a time (EOS suppression, cfg, Parallel@4, Temp@0), so every cell is guaranteed to degrade; the design cannot yield an unbiased magnitude for protocol sensitivity, cannot detect interactions (which is exactly where CaRE found eta^2=0.47), reports no seeds or CIs, and exhibits NO ranking reversal (zero occurrences of 'ranking' or 'reversal'). Deeper irony: the framework's stated goal is to 'faithfully reproduce the evaluation configurations used in prior work', which bakes each paper's favourable protocol into the harness rather than standardising across them -- preserving the incomparability the paper documents.
followup_openings.our_fix: Replace one-factor-at-a-time-off-an-optimum with a fully crossed factorial with no privileged cell ({T 0.1,0.2,0.6} x {top_p 0.95,1.0} x {steps 128,256,512} x model), and report a variance decomposition apportioning pass@1 variance to protocol factors vs model identity -- the quantity dLLM's Takeaway asserts but never estimates. Because dLLM is PUBLISHED at ACL 2026 and pre-cutoff, this is the citation that must be positioned against most carefully: our contribution is the unbiased factorial estimate plus the reversal, not the qualitative claim. Additionally, fix the harness-level defect by shipping a cumulative-token/parse-validity/termination sidecar as an lm-eval extension, so a standardised protocol becomes expressible rather than each paper's own protocol being faithfully reproduced.
followup_openings.target_paper: dLLM (arXiv:2602.22661; ACL 2026 pp. 78-88, PRE-CUTOFF and PUBLISHED)

followup_openings.defect: Attributes ranking instability to prompt template WITHOUT jointly controlling compute. A method that wins on template 3 may simply be consuming more actual NFE there -- the paper never standardises actual NFE the way CaRE does, so template effect and compute effect are confounded in exactly the manner CaRE warns about. Its 6 code templates are hand-authored 'with minor modifications to enhance template diversity', making the effect size partly a design choice; no CIs or seeds in the code tables; LLaDA-family only (no Dream, no Dream-Coder, no infilling model); lm-eval grading on plain HumanEval/MBPP.

Sample templates from those PUBLISHED protocols actually use (Dream-Coder, DreamOn, CoDA, DiffuCoder released harnesses) rather than hand-authoring diversity, so the estimate is of the variance a reader of the literature actually faces. Add the base-vs-chat prompting axis (our --add-bos-token / --base-continuation flags, commit 3cef855), which is the sharpest template variable for a base model and is absent from all prior work.
followup_openings.target_paper: Understanding Evaluation Illusion in dLLMs (arXiv:2606.29228, concurrent 2026-06-28)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Joint template x compute control is unclaimed by anyone, and it is the natural synthesis of the two closest concurrent works -- a reviewer sees immediately that each prior paper controlled one confound and missed the interaction.

followup_openings.defect: Explicitly footnotes that 'performance refers to system-level efficiency metrics rather than task-level or downstream accuracy' -- so it proves dLLM efficiency accounting is broken while never pairing it to a quality axis, leaving its AR-wins-on-throughput conclusion answerable by 'but the DLM was more accurate'. Its fairness convention forces AR and block-diffusion 'to continue until the target length is met even after an <eos> token is produced', a deliberate anti-early-stopping rule that inflates AR cost -- the exact mirror image of our own Retraction 3 (dropping budget-truncated cases understated scaffold Large's cost 2.85x/3.69x). Single inference framework (HF Transformers), GSM8K only, zero code benchmarks.

Then treat the termination convention as a first-class, reportable protocol choice rather than a hidden one: run BOTH conventions (honour EOS vs run-to-budget), show how much the cross-family ordering moves between them, and make 'termination reason' plus mandatory failure_process inclusion part of the minimal reporting standard -- with our two documented, opposite-signed accounting errors as the worked case studies proving neither convention is neutral.

Their 'rankings strictly consistent' is a direct, cheap falsification target -- if our factorial reverses a ranking on the temperature/top_p/canvas axes they never crossed, we have both the reversal the candidate needs AND a named prior claim to overturn, which is far more publishable than an unattached sensitivity number. followup_openings.defect: Reports four findings that overlap our failure-mode taxonomy but each as an uncontrolled by-product of evaluating its own method: (1) 'providing a syntactic scaffold lifts accuracy from near zero to over 20% without changing the model' with no ablation isolating it from SpecRef; (4) 'standard Python post-processing silently breaks code evaluation for non-AR generators' asserted without quantifying how many tasks flip; (3) log-likelihood vs generative scoring gives different rankings, shown on ONE model pair. Report all of it under the minimal standard (cumulative tokens + parse-validity + termination reason + failure_process inclusion).

Offensively: add backend as a factor on a cheap subset and report the diffusion-specific backend share on execution-graded code, extending their 39% AR result to the family where per-step whole-canvas re-attention makes backend effects plausibly larger. The HumanEval reversal therefore rests on a block-to-block contrast at n=100 -- our n=164/n=378 full EvalPlus sets with plus-tests are a strictly stronger instrument. (2) 3 seeds only, self-flagged as insufficient for marginal effects. (3) NFE-only accounting is internally inconsistent with their own claim that nominal steps hide 'a 4x range' -- NFE still ignores that each diffusion forward pass re-attends the whole canvas, so it cannot price diffusion against AR or against a variable-canvas runtime. (4) Interaction analysis limited to none vs high_entropy; other five strategies not re-evaluated at the stochastic headline config. (5) Cross-family (LLaDA vs Dream) comparisons are admitted to 'inherit small implementation differences'. (6) Deliverable-quality claim 'reverses several published strategy rankings' is asserted at the protocol-table level (Table 1) rather than by re-running each cited paper under its own stated protocol first -- exactly the third kill condition this candidate imposes on itself.

related_work.what_it_covers: The single closest work and the candidate's declared parent. Seven-point protocol: report actual NFE, multi-metric, external-evaluator PPL, control stochasticity, language filter, seeds. 7 remasking strategies x LLaDA-8B-Base + Dream-7B-Base x 4 stochasticity levels x 3 step budgets on OpenWebText/LM1B. Three-way ANOVA: temperature dominates MAUVE variance (eta^2=0.91), strategy x temperature interaction eta^2=0.47. Compute-matched reversals demonstrated. Leaderboard over 12 open-weight MDLMs. CRITICAL for this candidate: CaRE DOES include a HumanEval leg (Table 11, LLaDA-8B-Base, n=100, 3 seeds, via lm-eval) exhibiting a code ranking reversal: at nominal 256 steps high_entropy appears to beat none (31.7 vs 28.3 pass@1) but uses 3.4x more actual NFE; at matched NFE=437, none matches or exceeds all strategies. No variance decomposition of protocol vs MODEL IDENTITY (the ANOVA decomposes strategy x temperature x budget within one model).

related_work.citation: H. Peng, P. Liu, Z. Dong, D. Cheng, J. Li, Y. Tang, S. Wang, W. X. Zhao. "How Efficient Are Diffusion Language Models? A Critical Examination of Efficiency Evaluation Practices." arXiv:2510.18480v3.
