feas.risk: The most likely outcome is that the whole thing collapses into an errata note plus a tautology, and the collapse is already visible in data on disk. Three of the four load-bearing claims degrade under the checks I ran: (1) "bias grows with budget" is an arithmetic identity -- 147/147 resolved tasks are bit-identical across caps, so only the capped runs move, and they move because they run to the cap; (2) "the tail is intrinsic, not a budget artifact" is falsified -- 33/33 MBPP+ truncated tasks resolve at cap 4096 with nfe 1035-1077, so the cap was set 5% below a cliff and the "heavy tail" is manufactured by cap placement; (3) "truncated requests are SYSTEMATICALLY the most expensive" is false in 4 of 8 arms, where depth_capacity_exhausted terminates early and cheap and the bias flips sign. What survives -- the mechanism-dependent sign and the intra-family pairwise reversal -- is real and verified, but it is a within-one-runtime observation about two cap mechanisms in one decoder, and the natural reviewer response is "you mis-set your own cap, then measured the consequence." The second failure mode is confounding on the external leg: it is tempting to read the AR summarizer's identical `if row.get("process")` filter as the bias recurring, but AR never writes failure_process, so that filter drops only crashed rows and the bias does not actually recur there -- writing it up as a recurrence would be a fourth self-inflicted retraction of exactly the Retraction-2 shape (a pipeline stage that looks like it does the thing but does not). Third, the arm carrying the entire headline (scaffold Large) has already been removed from the frontier by Retraction 4, so even a correct accounting fix lands on a configuration nobody would deploy.
feas.required_control: THE IDENTITY-VS-EFFECT CONTROL, WITH A SATURATION LADDER. Before any bias-versus-budget number is reported, two assertions must be run and printed in the artifact: (A) DETERMINISM/DEGREES-OF-FREEDOM ASSERTION -- for every pair of arms differing only in the cap, verify task-by-task that the non-truncated subset has identical per-task cost, and report the count (I measured 147 identical / 0 differing for HE+ 512 vs 1024). If it is identical, then the bias ratio has exactly one free component (the truncated-set total) and any movement in it is definitional, not empirical; the paper must say so in those words rather than presenting it as a counter-intuitive finding. The bias ratio must be reported decomposed into (resolved-set total, truncated-set total, n_resolved, n_truncated) so a reader can see which component moved and why. (B) SATURATION LADDER -- no arm's truncation rate may be characterised as a "tail" until the cap has been raised until truncation reaches zero, or until it is shown not to reach zero within a stated multiple of the cap. runs/scaffold_large_mbppplus_budget4096_hit35 is exactly this control, and it falsifies the filed claim: 33/33 resolve at nfe 1035-1077. The HE+ twin does not exist and must be run before publication. Together these prevent the failure that maps onto all three prior retractions: Retraction 1 shipped a comparison that compared nothing, Retraction 2 shipped a stage that silently discarded its input, Retraction 3 shipped an average whose denominator dropped the expensive cases -- and the analogue here is shipping a ratio whose numerator moves only because we redefined the cap that generates it, on a tail we created by placing that cap below a cliff. The control is what distinguishes "budget-truncated requests are systematically expensive" from "we capped a bimodal cost distribution just below its second mode."

lens.title: The Canvas Is the Confound: Generation-Length Budget, Not Step Count, Sets the Quality-Compute Frontier of Masked Diffusion LMs
lens.claim: Published masked-diffusion quality-vs-compute curves are confounded by a fixed, oversized generation canvas L. Because per-step cost is T*(prompt+L), and because the tokens-committed-per-step ratio r=L/T is the real quality driver (not T), sweeping T at fixed L conflates two variables. Concretely: (i) reported 'step saturation' occurs exactly at r=1.0 (strictly sequential decoding), not at a property of the diffusion objective; (ii) right-sizing L to the task's actual output length shifts the entire cost axis left by ~1.9x on HumanEval+, changing which method owns which segment of the frontier; (iii) at matched r, cells with different (T,L) but equal r score within noise, so r is the sufficient statistic and T alone is not.
lens.why_now: We can already show this from our own data rather than assert it. Verified from raw runs/*/metrics.rank*.jsonl: every NFE cell (16..1024) has generated_tokens=512 pinned, so r=L/T = 32,16,8,4,2,1.0,0.5. Our headline 'saturates at 512, exactly 0.0 gain to 1024' is r=1.0 -> r=0.5: the model's BEST score (.707/.680) is its FULLY SEQUENTIAL score, and steps beyond that commit nothing. Meanwhile mean correct HE+ solution is ~191 tokens against the 512 canvas, so vanilla nfe512 cost drops 343,040 -> ~179,200 tok at L=192. That directly threatens our own surviving Pareto claim, which is exactly why it is worth publishing. The two concurrent audits leave this axis open: CaRE (arXiv 2607.24763, first public 2026-06-04) standardizes actual NFE, stochasticity and multi-metric reporting but holds generation length fixed; 'Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis' (2606.19475, 2026-06-17) varies denoising steps, context length, block size and unmasking strategy but not the response canvas as a cost variable. Both are within 3 months of today, hence concurrent, not preemptive.
lens.experiment: 2-D grid over (L, T) instead of the standard 1-D T sweep, on Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, HumanEval+ (n=164) and MBPP+ (n=378), evalplus.evaluate official grader, T=0.1/top_p=0.95 fixed. L in {128,192,256,384,512,768}, T in {32,64,128,256,512}, restricted to cells with r=L/T in [0.5,16] (~22 cells/benchmark). Report pass@1+ against BOTH cost units: nominal steps T (the field's unit) and cumulative model tokens T*(prompt+L) (the honest unit), using the proc() accessor that includes budget-truncated tasks (our Retraction-3 fix). Three analyses: (a) iso-r contrast -- do (T=256,L=256) and (T=512,L=512), both r=1.0, tie? (b) iso-cost contrast -- at a fixed token budget, is it better to spend on more steps or a bigger canvas? (c) refit our published Pareto figure with per-benchmark right-sized L and report whether the scaffold-vs-flat 'no crossover' claim survives. Replicate the (L,T) grid on DreamOn-v0-7B and on our Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B (whose runtime grows its canvas, so it is the natural contrast) plus one downloadable cross-family checkpoint (LLaDA-8B-Instruct or DiffuCoder-7B, both HTTP 200 on HF) so the finding is not single-family. Deliverable includes a drop-in reporting template: report (T, L, r, tokens) as a 4-tuple, never T alone.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, models/DreamOn-v0-7B, models/Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, data/evalplus/{humaneval,mbpp}_plus.jsonl, evalplus 0.3.1, scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py (already exposes --steps and --max-new-tokens as SEPARATE flags, so the 2-D grid needs no new code), scripts/make_pareto_figures.py with the fixed proc() accessor, 8x L20A idle-ish locally + .252/.73/.82/.104. MISSING: cross-family checkpoint download (LLaDA-8B-Instruct ~16GB or DiffuCoder-7B; both reachable via hy-proxy, 13T free on wzc1). RISK: L>512 needs a re-check that extract_python still truncates correctly; and the canvas for MBPP+ must be right-sized separately (its solutions are shorter).
lens.kill_criterion: Falsified if, at matched r, quality is NOT recovered by shrinking L -- i.e. if (T=256,L=256) scores materially below (T=512,L=512) (say >3 points on HE+ pass@1+, outside a paired bootstrap 95% CI). That would mean the oversized canvas is doing real work (extra bidirectional compute or scratch space), T is not substitutable, and the standard 1-D sweep is defensible. Also falsified if right-sizing L leaves our published Pareto segmentation qualitatively unchanged AND the iso-r cells do not tie, since then r is not the sufficient statistic and the paper has no mechanism.
lens.builds_on: Directly repairs OUR OWN published-internal NFE-saturation and token-cost Pareto claims (DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md sections 2 and 3b) -- the defect is that steps were swept at fixed canvas, so 'saturation at 512' is r=1.0 and the cost axis is inflated ~1.9x. Positions against CaRE (2607.24763, concurrent) which controls actual-NFE/stochasticity/metrics but not canvas; and against 'An Experimental Analysis' (2606.19475, concurrent) which varies steps/context/block-size but not response length as a cost variable. Distinct from VoidPadding (2606.17999) and Length Regularization (2602.07546), which propose METHODS to handle padding/length; we make length an EVALUATION-PROTOCOL confound and measure its effect on published rankings.

related_work.citation: Bertolani, Bucciarelli, Zini, Cornia, Baraldi. "Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis." arXiv:2606.19475v1 (17 Jun 2026), v2 22 Jun 2026.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv abs page shows no journal-ref and no comments field; CEUR-style author-block formatting in the HTML suggests a workshop submission but I could not verify any venue. OpenReview search returned no matching note.
related_work.what_it_covers: 8 DLMs x 8 benchmarks (incl. HumanEval, MBPP) with explicit quality-vs-efficiency framing. Two scaling figures directly adjacent to this candidate: Fig.1 sweeps generation length with ONE token denoised per step (i.e. an iso-r=1.0 line where T and L move together 1:1) and finds quality saturates/declines beyond 256-512 tokens; Fig.2 fixes generation length at N=1024 and sweeps denoising steps. It then states the conclusion verbatim: "suggesting that in the joint scaling experiment (Figure 1), it is the generation length rather than the step count that drives performance degradation." Also reports per-forward-pass and full-generation TFLOPS/VRAM per model.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Never runs a 2-D (L,T) grid: it runs one diagonal (r=1.0) plus one vertical (L=1024). Therefore cannot test iso-r equivalence, cannot separate L-as-cost from L-as-quality, and cannot state a sufficient-statistic claim. Reports cost only as TFLOPS per model (Table 3) and never converts the quality axis to a cumulative-token or FLOP cost axis, so it produces no quality-vs-cost frontier and never re-ranks any method under canvas control. No execution-graded pass@1+ (uses standard harness accuracy), no MBPP+/HumanEval+ plus-tests, no budget-truncation accounting, no right-sizing prescription, no reporting template.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The headline length-vs-step attribution rests on comparing two figures run under different protocols (r=1.0 diagonal vs L=1024 vertical) rather than a crossed design -- L and r are not orthogonalised, so "length drives degradation" is confounded with "r=1.0 is where the diagonal ends up". (2) Fig.2 reports "no clear saturation within the evaluated range" at L=1024, which is arithmetically expected because the range never reaches T=L; they do not note that the step axis is bounded by L. (3) Attributes decline at long L to "error accumulation" without testing the competing EOS-overflow mechanism that Rainbow Padding (ICLR 2026) had already established for instruction-tuned dLLMs. (4) GSM8K generation TFLOPS of 23,727 (Dream) vs 9.85 (Qwen3-4B) is a 2400x gap reported without noting it is almost entirely the padded canvas -- the exact accounting artefact this candidate is about, left uninterpreted.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page + full HTML (arxiv.org/html/2606.19475v2) fetched and grepped for 'generation length', 'sequence length', 'canvas', 'NFE', 'Pareto', 'budget'; OpenReview api2 /notes/search on the title.

related_work.citation: CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models. arXiv:2607.24763v1 (4 Jun 2026).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint under review (anonymous 4open.science artifact link in the paper implies double-blind submission). No OpenReview note found; no journal-ref.
related_work.what_it_covers: Seven-point evaluation protocol for MDLM remasking: report ACTUAL NFE (not nominal steps), multi-metric reporting (PPL+MAUVE), external-evaluator PPL, controlled stochasticity. 7 remasking strategies x LLaDA-8B-Base + Dream-7B-Base x 4 temperatures x 3 step budgets on OpenWebText/LM1B, plus HumanEval pass@1 and GSM8K. Shows compute-matched comparison REVERSES published strategy rankings (HumanEval: high_entropy 31.7 vs none 28.3 at nominal steps, but none wins at matched NFE=437). Crucially, it derives the r=1.0 arithmetic explicitly: for the no-remasking sampler, "each of the L=128 output positions is unmasked exactly once; the model therefore requires exactly 128 forward passes regardless of any nominal step count above 128."
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Holds L=128 fixed everywhere and explicitly relegates length to unstudied: "the three confounds we study are not exhaustive -- numerical precision, prompt format, and sequence length also matter but produce smaller measured effects." Never varies L, never prices cost as T*(prompt+L), never right-sizes, never treats the canvas as a ranking-relevant variable. Its ranking reversals are under NFE control, not canvas control.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The dismissal "sequence length ... produce[s] smaller measured effects" is asserted with zero supporting experiment and is directly contradicted by pre-existing published work: Rainbow Padding (ICLR 2026 Poster) shows max_length 512->1024 swings LLaDA MATH accuracy from 34.3 to 0.9 -- an effect far larger than CaRE's own headline 0.296 MAUVE interaction. This is a clean, citable, repairable defect. (2) Runs at L=128 with 256 nominal steps, i.e. r=0.5, so the entire study sits inside the regime where extra steps commit nothing for non-remasking samplers; CaRE states this arithmetic for `none` but does not draw the protocol consequence that its own step budgets are partly inert. (3) 3 seeds; the paper itself flags that marginal claims need >=5. (4) Cost accounting is forward passes only -- a forward pass at L=128 and one at L=1024 are counted identically, so "compute-matched" is not token-matched or FLOP-matched.

related_work.citation: Rottoli, Roy et al. "Predict-then-Diffuse: Adaptive Response Length for Compute-Budgeted Inference in Diffusion LLMs." arXiv:2605.04215v1 (5 May 2026); v3 31 Jul 2026.
related_work.venue_status: Accepted at IJCNN 2026 (International Joint Conference on Neural Networks), per arXiv comments field on v3. Not on OpenReview (IJCNN does not use it).
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest pre-cutoff work on the cost half of the candidate's claim. States the framing almost identically: "oversized response length results in computational waste on semantically meaningless padding tokens, while undersized response length causes output truncation." Derives an analytical per-block FLOP cost model FLOP_l = (6DF+8D^2)L + 4D*L^2, empirically validates it on LLaDA-8B (H100, T=128 fixed, L from 64 to 30k), then trains an Adaptive Response Length Predictor (AdaRLP) + safety margin to right-size L per query. Reports 99.34% FLOP reduction vs default fixed-L inference.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Runs ZERO quality experiments. Section IV-F is titled "Impact on Generation Quality" and says verbatim: "We rely on prior results on whether adaptive sizing affects generation quality," then reproduces LLaDA's canvas table (1024/512/256 -> GSM8K 70.3/70.8/70.0, HumanEval pass@1 35.4/32.9/32.9) from arXiv:2502.09992. Holds T=128 fixed and never sweeps T, so it cannot decompose steps from length or define a tokens-per-step ratio. It is a serving/FLOP paper on ShareGPT/Alpaca/Dolly/OpenOrca/ELI5 (mean response 96 tokens), not a benchmark-protocol paper: no HumanEval+/MBPP+, no execution grading, no method rankings, no re-analysis of anyone's published curve.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The 99.34% FLOP saving is unaccompanied by any first-party quality measurement -- it is borrowed from a 3-row appendix table in another paper on a different benchmark, and that borrowed table itself shows HumanEval pass@1 dropping 35.4 -> 32.9 when the canvas shrinks, i.e. the cited evidence partially contradicts "preserving output quality". (2) Cost model is FLOPs only; at T fixed it cannot express the T*(prompt+L) interaction, so the reported saving is a pure-L saving that says nothing about the achievable quality-at-fixed-budget. (3) Length predictor is trained on chat/instruction data with mean length 96 and evaluated on the same distribution -- untested on code, where the correct canvas is bimodal and where truncation is catastrophic rather than degrading. (4) No EOS-overflow control, so "shorter canvas is free" is confounded with "shorter canvas avoids EOS collapse".

related_work.what_it_covers: The pre-cutoff theoretical backbone of the candidate's claim (iii). Proves that for token error rate / perplexity, MDMs reach near-optimal quality in a number of sampling steps INDEPENDENT of sequence length L; but for sequence error rate (all-tokens-correct, the relevant metric for code and reasoning), the required sampling steps must scale AT LEAST LINEARLY with L, because SER "forces MDMs to sample only a small number of tokens per step." That is precisely 'the tokens-committed-per-step ratio bounds achievable quality, so T must track L'. Also notes each MDM step costs more than an AR step at equal architecture. Empirically corroborated on n-gram/HMM formal languages plus Dream-v0-Base-7B and LLaDA-8B-Base on GSM8K and MBPP against Qwen2.5-7B.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Worst-case theory over formal languages; the real-model experiments sweep decoding steps at a FIXED maximum answer length of 512 (MBPP) and never vary L, so the L axis is untouched empirically. No pass@1+/execution grading (accuracy only), no cumulative-token cost unit (uses relative efficiency vs an AR baseline), no protocol prescription, no re-ranking of competing dLLM methods, no instruction-tuned models, no code-specific canvas analysis.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Theory is worst-case over adversarial distributions; the linear-in-L step requirement need not bind for real code where much of the canvas is padding -- the paper does not test whether the binding constant is anywhere near 1 token/step on real tasks. (2) Its own empirics fix L=512 for MBPP and L per lm-eval defaults for GSM8K, so the length axis that its central theorem is about is never varied. (3) Explicitly disables EOS-based early stopping ("This configuration does not stop generation after encountering EOS ... but our results indicate that this behavior does not affect the overall conclusions") -- asserted, not shown, and it is exactly the knob that Rainbow Padding shows is decisive.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abs + full HTML (arxiv.org/html/2502.09622v2); grepped 'sequence length L', 'number of sampling steps', 'tokens per step', 'answer length', 'EOS', 'NeurIPS'. Venue confirmed on OpenReview api2 /notes/search.

related_work.citation: Rainbow Padding: Mitigating Early Termination in Instruction-Tuned Diffusion LLMs. arXiv:2510.03680v1 (4 Oct 2025).
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 (venue "ICLR 2026 Poster", venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference).
related_work.what_it_covers: Establishes, pre-cutoff and at a top venue, that the canvas size L is not a neutral cost knob for instruction-tuned dLLMs: it names <eos> overflow, shows accuracy COLLAPSES as max_length grows (LLaDA MATH 34.3 -> 0.9 at #Blocks=1; Dream-Base MATH 34.3 -> 0.0 and GSM8K 77.3 -> 9.1 with <eos> padding at max_length 1024), traces the cause to <eos> serving as both terminator and pad, and shows longer allocation yields SHORTER responses with higher <eos> fraction unmasked in the first 50% of steps. Reports both accuracy and realised res_length at max_length 512 vs 1024 on MATH/GSM8K/HumanEval.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Proposes a training-side METHOD (cyclic distinct pad tokens + 1-epoch LoRA) rather than an evaluation-protocol claim. Does not sweep denoising steps, does not define a tokens-per-step ratio, does not report any compute/cost axis (no NFE, no cumulative tokens, no FLOPs), does not re-rank competing decoding methods, and does not evaluate code with plus-tests or execution grading beyond vanilla HumanEval accuracy.
related_work.known_defects: (1) All length effects are reported at whatever step schedule the harness supplies, so 'longer canvas is worse' is not separated from 'longer canvas at the same T means larger r'. Since their Dream-Base 512-vs-1024 rows change L without a matched-r control, the reported degradation is length-and-ratio confounded -- a directly repairable gap. (2) MATH and GSM8K use randomly sampled >100-problem subsets for cost reasons, so the largest reported swings have wide binomial uncertainty and no CIs. (3) Quality is reported against L but never against cost, so the paper cannot say whether Rainbow Padding at L=1024 beats plain padding at L=256 per token spent.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abs + full HTML (arxiv.org/html/2510.03680v1) fetched; grepped 'allocated sequence length', 'max_length', '512', '1024', 'length robustness', 'HumanEval', 'NFE' (zero hits for NFE). Venue confirmed on OpenReview api2.

related_work.citation: VoidPadding: Let [VOID] Handle Padding in Masked Diffusion Language Models so that [EOS] Can Focus on Semantic Termination. arXiv:2606.17999v1 (16 Jun 2026), v2.
related_work.venue_status: Under review -- OpenReview api2 shows "ACL ARR 2026 August Submission" (venueid aclweb.org/ACL/ARR/2026/August/Submission) plus a CoRR 2026 Public_Article record. Not accepted anywhere yet.
related_work.what_it_covers: Opens with exactly the candidate's premise: "MDLMs generate text by denoising a preallocated masked response canvas, making response-length modeling central." Separates [VOID] padding from [EOS] termination, enabling learned early stopping AND adaptive canvas EXPANSION. On Dream-7B-Instruct reports +17.84 block-size-averaged four-task mean over the original model, +6.95 over RainbowPadding, while cutting decoding NFE 55.7%. So it is the concurrent state of the art on jointly improving quality and canvas cost, on the same model family as this candidate.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: A training/decoding METHOD, not an evaluation-protocol audit. Cost is reported as NFE reduction, not as cumulative model tokens T*(prompt+L), so the very quantity the candidate argues is the honest unit is still not reported. Does not run a crossed (L,T) grid, does not test iso-r equivalence, does not re-price or re-rank any third-party published curve, and does not address plus-test/execution-graded code frontiers.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Improvement is reported as a block-size-averaged mean over four tasks, which aggregates away the length x block-size interaction that is the actual object of study -- per-cell (L, block, NFE) numbers are needed to know where the gain lives. (2) 55.7% NFE reduction with adaptive expansion means realised L varies per sample, so NFE is no longer comparable across arms without token-level accounting; the paper does not supply it. (3) Baseline is RainbowPadding at its own defaults rather than at matched cost, so the +6.95 is not compute-matched.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abs + version history; OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned both the ARR August 2026 submission record and the CoRR record.

related_work.citation: Peng, Liu, Dong, Cheng, Li, Tang, Wang, Zhao. "How Efficient Are Diffusion Language Models? A Critical Examination of Efficiency Evaluation Practices." arXiv:2510.18480v1 (21 Oct 2025), v2 10 Nov 2025.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint / technical report. OpenReview api2 returns only a CoRR 2025 Public_Article record (venueid OpenReview.net/Public_Article), i.e. no peer-reviewed venue. Self-described as a technical report in the text.
related_work.what_it_covers: The pre-cutoff paper that names the candidate's confound by name: among "three major issues in existing research on acceleration and evaluation of DLMs" the first is Evaluation Scope -- "Prior evaluations often compare DLMs and AR models in limited conditions, such as single instance inference or fixed generation length." It then sweeps generation length over {64,128,256,512,1024,2048} x {0-shot, 5-shot} x batch size for LLaDA-8B-Instruct vs LLaMA-3.1-8B vs Fast-dLLM, builds a throughput model as FLOPs/s x FLOPs/token, and shows AR > block diffusion > DLM on throughput everywhere. Also notes LLaDA "achieves optimal performance when the number of sampling steps matches the output length, making each decoding step effectively generate about one token" -- i.e. r=1.0 as the operating point.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Explicitly scoped to system efficiency only, with a footnote: "performance refers to system-level efficiency metrics rather than task-level or downstream accuracy." So it measures cost across L and never measures quality across L. No pass@1, no accuracy, no quality-compute frontier, no method ranking on quality, no per-task right-sizing, and no cumulative-token unit (uses tokens/sec throughput).
related_work.known_defects: This is the single best follow-up target in the set: it establishes fixed-generation-length as an evaluation defect and then measures ONLY the cost side, leaving the quality side -- which is what determines published rankings -- entirely unmeasured. It also forces AR baselines to keep generating past <eos> to the target length "to ensure a fair comparison of throughput", which is fair for throughput but makes its numbers unusable for any quality-at-matched-cost statement. Third, being throughput-based, its conclusions are hardware- and implementation-bound (HF Transformers, no vLLM), which it acknowledges but cannot fix.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abs; full HTML fetched via arxiv.org/html/2510.18480 (the v2-specific URL returned a 7.7KB stub, the unversioned URL returned the full 186KB document) and grepped for 'generation length', 'output length', 'fixed', 'issues', 'throughput', 'EOS'. OpenReview api2 /notes/search for venue.

related_work.citation: DiffuCoder: Understanding and Improving Masked Diffusion Models for Code Generation. arXiv:2506.20639v1 (25 Jun 2025), v2.
related_work.venue_status: Venue unverified; treat as preprint. No journal-ref on arXiv; OpenReview search returned no matching note.
related_work.what_it_covers: The reference code-dLLM analysis and a competing MECHANISM for why r=1.0 wins. Defines local/global AR-ness metrics, shows adapted dLLMs (Dream, DiffuCoder -- both initialised from AR checkpoints, as is this candidate's Dream-Coder) inherit strong left-to-right bias, and identifies an 'entropy sink': the position immediately right of the prefix gets disproportionate confidence. Runs its whole decoding analysis at sequence length = diffusion timesteps = 512, i.e. r=1.0, and notes the model decides pad tokens (hence effective length) early in the trajectory.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Never varies L or T as a 2-D grid (fixes both at 512), no cost axis, no protocol claim. Critically, it never tests whether AR-ness explains the r=1.0 optimum -- which is the alternative hypothesis this candidate must rule out.
related_work.known_defects: AR-ness is measured only at r=1.0 (L=T=512), so the reported 'dLLMs are quasi-AR' finding is partly an artefact of running the sampler in its strictly-sequential regime; AR-ness at r=8 or r=16 is never reported. That circularity is a clean opening: if adapted dLLMs are quasi-AR, then 'best quality occurs at r=1.0' is a statement about AR-adapted initialisation, not about masked diffusion, and it should NOT replicate on a from-scratch dLLM.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abs + full HTML (arxiv.org/html/2506.20639v2) fetched; grepped 'generation length', 'AR-ness', 'entropy sink', 'decoding steps', '512', 'parallel'.

related_work.citation: DreamOn: Diffusion Language Models For Code Infilling Beyond Fixed-size Canvas. arXiv:2602.01326v1 (1 Feb 2026).
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 (venue "ICLR 2026 Poster", venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference); arXiv comments field also reads "ICLR 2026".
related_work.what_it_covers: Pre-cutoff, top-venue statement that fixed canvas size is a first-order problem: "This constraint severely degrades code infilling performance when the predefined mask size mismatches the ideal completion length." Adds two length-control states so the model expands/contracts its own canvas; built on Dream-Coder-7B and DiffuCoder-7B; matches oracle-length performance on HumanEval-Infilling and SantaCoder-FIM.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Scoped to INFILLING with a known hole, not to from-scratch generation, and framed as a capability fix, not an evaluation-protocol confound. Reports quality vs oracle length, not quality vs compute; no step sweep, no r, no cumulative-token cost, no re-ranking of published curves, no HumanEval+/MBPP+ plus-tests.
related_work.known_defects: Its central comparison is against an oracle-length upper bound, which measures 'did we find the right L' but not 'what did finding it cost' -- expansion/contraction changes NFE per sample and the paper does not report a matched-cost frontier. Also, because it is infilling-specialised, the L-mismatch penalty it documents may be far larger than in open-ended generation; that scope limit is untested and is exactly the regime this candidate operates in.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abs + comments field; OpenReview api2 /notes/search confirmed ICLR 2026 Poster.

related_work.citation: Improving Variable-Length Generation in Diffusion Language Models via Length Regularization (LR-DLLM). arXiv:2602.07546v1 (7 Feb 2026).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. No journal-ref; OpenReview search returned no matching note.
related_work.what_it_covers: Pre-cutoff formal statement that the fixed canvas biases the model's own confidence estimates: "naively comparing confidence across mask lengths becomes systematically biased, leading to under-generation or redundant continuations." related_work.citation: rho-EOS: Training-free Bidirectional Variable-Length Control for Masked Diffusion LLMs. arXiv:2601.22527v1 (30 Jan 2026), v2 7 Feb 2026.

related_work.citation: Pynadath, Shi, Zhang. "Generative Frontiers: Why Evaluation Matters for Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2604.02718v1 (3 Apr 2026).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint / technical note (self-described "technical note"; accompanying blog post). No journal-ref, no OpenReview note.
related_work.what_it_covers: The pre-cutoff dLLM evaluation-methodology note that CaRE positions against. Argues generative perplexity alone is uninformative, decomposes generative PPL and entropy as two components of a KL to a reference distribution, and proposes 'generative frontiers' (quality-diversity curves parameterised by temperature) as the principled comparison object.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Entirely at GPT-2-small scale on unconditional generation; the frontier is parameterised by temperature, not by compute, and generation length never appears as an axis. No task benchmarks, no code, no cost unit, no canvas.
related_work.known_defects: Establishes 'evaluate on a frontier, not a point' as the field's methodological norm and then instantiates the frontier over a stochasticity knob only -- leaving the compute knob (and within it, the L-vs-T decomposition) unparameterised. related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abs (fetched via id_list); also cross-referenced as reference [24] in CaRE's bibliography.

diff.differentiation_statement: No pre-2026-05-07 paper makes this candidate's claim with this method in this setting, so it survives -- but the honest positioning is much narrower than the proposal assumes, and two of the proposal's stated gaps are factually wrong and must be fixed before submission. First correction: the proposal asserts that "Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis" (2606.19475) "varies denoising steps, context length, block size and unmasking strategy but not the response canvas as a cost variable." It does vary the response canvas, and it already prints the conclusion "it is the generation length rather than the step count that drives performance degradation." Second correction: the proposal treats the r=1.0 saturation and the r-sufficiency claim as new. LLaDA's own Appendix B.4 (Feb 2025) runs an iso-r sweep at r=2 over L in {256,512,1024} and finds near-invariance, Appendix B.6 runs a fixed-L=1024 step sweep and finds monotone gain up to T=L, the NeurIPS 2025 theory paper (2502.09622) proves sequence-error-rate quality requires T to scale linearly in L, and CaRE (2607.24763) states the arithmetic outright -- for a non-remasking sampler, L output positions unmask exactly once, so forward passes are pinned at L regardless of nominal steps above L. Claim (i) is therefore a tautology of the sampler, not a discovery, and claim (iii) has a published theoretical backbone. What genuinely remains ours, and is defensible to a reviewer, is the conjunction of four things nobody has assembled: (a) a fully crossed (L,T) grid -- prior work runs only the r=1.0 diagonal (2606.19475 Fig.1, DiffuCoder at L=T=512) or a single vertical at fixed L (2606.19475 Fig.2 at 1024, LLaDA B.6 at 1024, Predict-then-Diffuse at T=128, CaRE at L=128) -- so we are the first to orthogonalise L and r rather than infer their separate effects by comparing two differently-configured figures; (b) the quality side of the canvas confound on execution-graded code, where the closest pre-cutoff paper, Predict-then-Diffuse (IJCNN 2026, first public 5 May 2026, two days before cutoff), explicitly declines to measure quality at all -- "We rely on prior results on whether adaptive sizing affects generation quality" -- and the closest cost-side audit, 2510.18480, footnotes itself out of quality entirely; (c) reporting the frontier in cumulative model tokens T*(prompt+L) with budget-truncated tasks included, rather than in nominal steps, forward passes, or throughput, which is the only unit under which a canvas change is visible as a cost change and which no paper in this set uses; and (d) demonstrating that canvas control CHANGES METHOD RANKINGS -- CaRE reverses rankings under NFE control and 2606.19475 does not re-rank at all, so ranking reversal under canvas control is unclaimed. Finally, we hold a control no one else can run: the candidate's own published Pareto segmentation is the first casualty, which converts the paper from a critique of others into a self-refutation with a matched Plain-SFT baseline and an EvalPlus-graded verifier already in place.

followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, concurrent, 2026-06-04)
followup_openings.defect: CaRE dismisses the canvas in one sentence of its limitations -- "prompt format and sequence length also matter but produce smaller measured effects" -- with zero supporting experiment, while holding L=128 fixed across its entire 12-model, 7-strategy, 4-temperature study. The dismissal is contradicted by a pre-existing ICLR 2026 paper: Rainbow Padding shows max_length 512->1024 moves LLaDA MATH accuracy from 34.3 to 0.9, an effect an order of magnitude larger than CaRE's own headline finding (a 0.296 MAUVE shift, p=0.020).
followup_openings.our_fix: Add L as a fourth CaRE-style confound and measure its effect size against their three (compute, metric, stochasticity) in the same units. Run their protocol at L in {128,256,512} and report whether the remasking-strategy ranking reversal they attribute to actual-NFE control survives canvas variation, and whether eta^2 for L exceeds their eta^2=0.91 for temperature. Also note the structural consequence they missed: at L=128 with 256 nominal steps they are running at r=0.5, so for the `none` strategy roughly half their nominal step budget is provably inert -- their own Table 3 arithmetic says so.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Turns a one-line hand-wave in the field's would-be standard protocol into a measured, ordered effect-size table, and either promotes canvas to a first-class CaRE confound or legitimately retires the concern. Either outcome is publishable, and it makes our contribution additive to the emerging standard rather than competing with it.

followup_openings.target_paper: Predict-then-Diffuse (arXiv:2605.04215, IJCNN 2026, first public 2026-05-05, PRE-CUTOFF)
followup_openings.defect: Claims 99.34% FLOP reduction from right-sizing L while "maintaining quality of output", but runs zero first-party quality experiments -- Section IV-F outsources the entire quality question to a 3-row table copied from the LLaDA paper. That borrowed table partially contradicts the claim: HumanEval pass@1 falls 35.4 -> 32.9 when the canvas shrinks 1024 -> 512. It also fixes T=128 throughout, so it cannot express the T-L interaction, and its length predictor is trained and tested on chat data (mean response 96 tokens), never on code, where truncation is catastrophic rather than merely degrading.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the missing quality leg on their own terms: measure pass@1+ (EvalPlus untrusted_check, HumanEval+ n=164, MBPP+ n=378) as a function of right-sized L, sweeping T rather than pinning it at 128, and report both nominal-T and cumulative-token cost. Then test their implicit assumption directly -- is the FLOP saving free, or does it buy back quality (via avoided EOS overflow) or lose quality (via truncation)? On code, add a first-party per-task oracle-length reference so the truncation risk their safety margin is designed for is actually quantified in the regime where it bites.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the closest pre-cutoff work and the most likely reviewer objection to our whole direction. Repairing its explicit self-declared gap converts it from a threat into our strongest citation: they established the cost model and the FLOP saving, we establish what it costs in quality and on which task family. It also forces us to reckon with the possibility -- visible already in their borrowed table -- that our own ~1.9x cost-axis shift is not free.

followup_openings.target_paper: Rainbow Padding (ICLR 2026 Poster, arXiv:2510.03680) and VoidPadding (arXiv:2606.17999, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Both establish that canvas size L changes quality through EOS overflow, but neither ever holds r=L/T fixed while varying L. Their 512-vs-1024 comparisons change L at whatever step schedule the harness supplies, so 'longer canvas is worse' is inseparable from 'longer canvas at the same T means larger r'. Neither reports any compute axis at all (Rainbow Padding's full text contains zero occurrences of NFE), so neither can say whether Rainbow Padding at L=1024 beats plain padding at L=256 per token spent.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the 2x2 that separates the two mechanisms: {L small, L large} x {r matched, r free} x {padding as shipped, Rainbow/Void-adapted}. If iso-r cells tie within a paired bootstrap CI once EOS overflow is controlled, canvas is purely a cost variable and the field's fix is a reporting change; if they do not tie, the canvas is doing real work and our own kill criterion fires. Then place both padding schemes on a single cumulative-token frontier -- the compute-matched comparison neither paper reports.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the confound most likely to sink the candidate as written, and it is also its best mechanism story. The literature currently has two disjoint accounts of the same knob -- canvas as wasted FLOPs (Predict-then-Diffuse, 2510.18480) and canvas as EOS collapse (Rainbow Padding, VoidPadding) -- and nobody has shown they are two different things being conflated in one hyperparameter. Disentangling them is a cleaner, more defensible contribution than 'steps were the wrong axis'.

followup_openings.target_paper: LLaDA (arXiv:2502.09992) Appendix B.4/B.6 and the field's inherited protocol
followup_openings.defect: The canonical dLLM paper runs its length ablation with steps pinned to L/2 -- iso-r=2 by construction -- and then reports the conclusion as "the final results are insensitive to this length hyperparameter." That is an iso-r invariance result mis-stated as an L invariance result, and the field inherited it. The same paper's Table 8 then quietly assigns different per-benchmark answer lengths (GSM8K 256, HumanEval 512, MBPP 512, MMLU-pro 256), contradicting the insensitivity claim it just made. Neither ablation reports any cost, so the L=1024/65.9 GSM8K cell is presented as strictly better than the L=256/62.5 cell despite costing roughly 4x the tokens.
followup_openings.our_fix: Restate the ablation properly on a crossed grid and price it: show that LLaDA's own numbers, replotted against cumulative tokens, put L=256 on the frontier and L=1024 off it, and that the 'insensitivity' is an iso-r artefact. Then test whether the invariance is a property of masked diffusion or of AR-adapted initialisation -- DiffuCoder shows Dream/DiffuCoder inherit strong AR-ness and measures it only at r=1.0, so run the iso-r test on an AR-adapted model (Dream-Coder, DiffuCoder) versus a from-scratch model (LLaDA-8B-Instruct). If r=1.0 optimality holds only for AR-adapted checkpoints, then 'best quality is fully sequential quality' is a statement about initialisation, not about the diffusion objective, and that is a sharper and more surprising finding than the protocol claim.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Repairing a mis-stated ablation in the field's most-cited dLLM paper is inherently citable, and the AR-adapted-vs-from-scratch interaction is the one cell in this literature that no paper in the related work occupies. It also supplies a cross-family replication that answers the single-family objection our proposal already anticipates, and it gives the paper a mechanism (initialisation-inherited AR-ness) rather than only an accounting correction.

followup_openings.target_paper: How Efficient Are Diffusion Language Models? (arXiv:2510.18480, pre-cutoff)
followup_openings.defect: Names fixed generation length as evaluation-scope defect #1 and then sweeps L in {64..2048} measuring throughput only, with an explicit footnote that "performance refers to system-level efficiency metrics rather than task-level or downstream accuracy." It also forces AR baselines to keep generating past <eos> to hit the target length -- defensible for throughput, but it makes every number unusable for any quality-at-matched-cost statement.
followup_openings.our_fix: Complete their study on the axis they excluded: same L grid, same models, quality on the y-axis and cumulative model tokens on the x-axis, with the AR baseline allowed to stop at <eos> (the setting that matters for quality) reported alongside their forced-length setting (the setting that matters for throughput). Report the gap between the two accounting conventions explicitly -- it is the size of the mispricing the field is carrying.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This paper already legitimised 'fixed generation length is an evaluation defect' pre-cutoff, which is a gift: we do not have to argue the premise, only supply the half they declared out of scope. Pairing our token-cost frontier with their throughput frontier also produces the practically useful statement -- whether the cheapest cell in tokens is also the fastest cell in wall-clock -- that neither paper alone can make.

diff.sharpened_claim: The response canvas L is two variables wearing one name, and the field's 1-D step sweep at fixed oversized L conflates them: L is simultaneously the dominant term in per-step cost T*(prompt+L) and the trigger for EOS-overflow quality collapse. We disentangle them with the first fully crossed (L,T) grid on execution-graded code -- L in {128,192,256,384,512,768} x T in {32..512} restricted to r=L/T in [0.5,16], Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B and DreamOn-v0-7B and Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B plus one cross-family checkpoint, HumanEval+ (n=164) and MBPP+ (n=378) under the official EvalPlus grader, each cell crossed with padding-as-shipped versus a Rainbow/Void-adapted arm so the EOS mechanism is controlled rather than absorbed. Prior work has established the pieces separately and never crossed them: LLaDA's Appendix B.4 tested length only at iso-r=2 and mis-reported the resulting invariance as L-invariance; the NeurIPS 2025 theory paper proved sequence-error-rate quality forces T to scale linearly in L; CaRE derived that a non-remasking sampler is pinned at L forward passes regardless of nominal steps, then dismissed length as a small effect without measuring it; Predict-then-Diffuse (IJCNN 2026) right-sized L for a 99.34% FLOP saving while explicitly declining to measure quality; Rainbow Padding (ICLR 2026) showed L wrecks quality without reporting any compute axis. Our contribution is the crossed measurement plus its consequence: reported in cumulative model tokens with budget-truncated tasks included, right-sizing L moves the HumanEval+ cost axis by roughly 1.9x and REORDERS which method owns which frontier segment -- the first casualty being our own published scaffold-versus-flat "no crossover" segmentation, which we re-fit and report honestly. Secondary and potentially the more surprising result: if iso-r equivalence holds for AR-initialised checkpoints (Dream-Coder, DiffuCoder, whose inherited left-to-right bias DiffuCoder measured only at r=1.0) but fails for a from-scratch dLLM, then "best quality is fully sequential quality" is a fact about AR adaptation rather than about the diffusion objective. Deliverable is a reporting template -- report (T, L, r, cumulative tokens) as a 4-tuple, never T alone -- plus a re-priced replot of the published curves this convention distorts.

Measured on runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus_r2 raw outputs: mean 101.3 prose tokens (median 98, p90 199) before the first ```; tokens needed to reach the CLOSE of the code block: HE+ mean 290, p90 418, p99 495. At L=192 only 21.7% of HE+ tasks would still contain a closed code block. The mean-191-token figure measures the EXTRACTED solution, not the canvas the model needs. This is exactly Retraction 3's error class (averaging over a quantity that omits the expensive/long tail) reappearing in the proposal's own headline number.

Positioning's stated gap (a) -- "we are the first to orthogonalise L and r" -- is the only surviving novelty, and it survives into a NULL.
