feas.risk:
The most likely outcome is not a null -- it is a CONFIRMED-AND-SCOOPED result, which is worse, and I have already produced it. The 27-cell grid will show quality monotone increasing in L along the iso-r diagonal and roughly flat in T above r=1.0. That is verbatim 2606.19475's published sentence ("it is the generation length rather than the step count that drives performance degradation"), first public 2026-06-17. We would spend 291 GPU-hours to produce a crossed design whose conclusion a concurrent preprint already printed from an uncrossed one, and whose arithmetic half CaRE already derived. A reviewer who knows either paper reads our contribution as "they orthogonalised two variables and got the answer everyone had already inferred," and orthogonalisation-as-contribution does not carry a main-conference paper.

The second, subtler risk is a confound that would make even the surviving Step-2 leg uninterpretable: L is not one intervention. Changing --max-new-tokens changes (a) the number of mask positions the model must fill, (b) the attention span every step sees, AND (c) the schedule, because timesteps = linspace(1, eps, T+1) is fixed but number_transfer_tokens = int(num_mask_token * (1 - s/t)) scales with num_mask_token = L. So L=256/T=256 and L=512/T=512 do not merely differ in canvas -- they differ in tokens-committed-per-step at every step index (max_commit 2 in both, but the commit trajectory and the count of zero-commit steps differ: 1 inert step at L=256/T=256 vs 1 at L=512/T=512, but 129 at L=128/T=256). Any "canvas effect" I report is a compound of canvas size, attention span, and realised schedule. The measured .506-vs-.360 gap between native L=256 and truncated-to-256 proves the compound is real and large. Without decomposing it, "right-sizing L costs 20 points" is a true but mechanistically empty statement -- and mechanistically empty length claims are exactly what we criticise Rainbow Padding and 2606.19475 for.

Third risk, specific to this project's history: n=164 with no seeds. The three native cells I ran are single-seed. A 0.201 spread is safe, but the .707-vs-.689 comparison (L=512 vs L=384, 3 tasks of 164) is inside noise -- and a seed-variance run is live on GPUs 0-4 right now precisely because we have never measured it. Any claim finer than ~5 points on HE+ is currently unsupportable, and the proposal's kill threshold is 3 points.
feas.required_control:
MANDATORY: the native-vs-truncated canvas control, run on every L before any L is called "right-sized."

For each candidate canvas L, produce TWO numbers on the same tasks: (i) a NATIVE run with --max-new-tokens L, and (ii) the L=512 trajectory post-hoc truncated to its first L tokens and re-extracted with the same extract_python. Report both, always, side by side.

Why this is the control that prevents our fourth retraction. Each prior retraction was a pipeline stage that silently substituted a different quantity for the one being measured: Retraction 1 substituted "did not raise" for "returned the right value"; Retraction 2 substituted a Dream-Coder generation for the scaffold draft it claimed to refine; Retraction 3 substituted the cheap subset for the full cost distribution. The analogous substitution here is treating "how many tokens the answer occupies" as "how big the canvas must be" -- and then reporting a cost saving computed from the former while quality is set by the latter. I already caught it live: at L=256 the truncated number is .360 and the native number is .506, a 14.6-point gap on identical tasks with identical grading. Either number alone tells a confident, publishable, wrong story. Truncation-only understates what a smaller canvas can do (it discards the model's ability to re-plan into a smaller space) and would have made us claim right-sizing is catastrophic; native-only hides that the extra canvas was functioning as scratch space and would have made us claim r is sufficient. Only the pair identifies the mechanism.

Two supporting controls, both cheap and both non-optional:
1. ZERO-COMMIT-STEP LEDGER. For every reported cell, log the schedule-derived count of steps where number_transfer_tokens == 0, computed from (L, T, eps) by re-running the generation_utils.py:406-440 arithmetic, and assert it against the realised commit count. This makes "we swept T" auditable: at L=128/T=1024, 898 of 1024 steps commit nothing, and any cost reported in nominal T for that cell is fiction. This is the direct analogue of the Retraction-3 proc() fix, applied to the step axis instead of the cost axis.
2. RIGHT-SIZING TARGET MUST BE THE p99 OF CODE-BLOCK-CLOSE, NOT THE MEAN OF THE EXTRACTED SOLUTION. Measured on our own runs: HE+ needs 290 tokens at the mean, 418 at p90, 495 at p99 to reach a closed code fence; the extracted solution averages 194. Any L chosen from the 194 figure truncates the tail, and the tail is where the hard tasks live -- the same "dropped the expensive tasks" failure as Retraction 3. Report the coverage fraction (share of tasks whose code block still closes within L) next to every pass@1+ so a truncation-driven score can never be mistaken for a capability-driven one.

lens.title: Sampler Choice Dominates Method Choice: A Variance Decomposition of Diffusion-LM Code Benchmarks
lens.claim: For open masked-diffusion code LMs, the variance in pass@1 attributable to decoding-protocol nuisance factors (temperature, top_p, unmasking algorithm, canvas length, prompt/chat wrapper, answer-extraction rule) is comparable to or larger than the variance attributable to model identity -- so a majority of published head-to-head diffusion-LM comparisons at fixed protocol are not resolving their method's effect. We further claim the nuisance factors INTERACT with model identity (non-additive), meaning no single 'standardized protocol' rescues the comparison; only per-model protocol tuning with a reported search budget does.
lens.why_now: We measured a 14.6-point HumanEval swing that we attributed to top_p alone -- larger than most published diffusion-LM method deltas. But auditing our own runs shows that claim is itself confounded: runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus.r1 vs _r2 straddle commit 97595c8, which ALSO rewrote the prompt path, and the raw outputs differ in kind (r1 emits a bare fenced code block, r2 emits a prose preamble then code). So the honest version of our own most striking number is unknown, and that is precisely the field's disease in miniature. A properly crossed design turns an anecdote into a variance-components result. CaRE (concurrent, 2026-06-04) shows temperature explains most MAUVE variance and that compute-matched comparison reverses several published rankings, but it is scoped to remasking strategies on open-ended text (OpenWebText/LM1B, MAUVE) on Base models; nobody has done the variance decomposition on executable code pass@1 with instruct checkpoints, where the answer-extraction rule is an additional and rarely-reported nuisance factor.
lens.experiment: Fully crossed factorial with model identity as one factor: models {Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, DreamOn-v0-7B, Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, + LLaDA-8B-Instruct or DiffuCoder-7B} x temperature {0.0,0.1,0.2,0.4} x top_p {0.9,0.95,1.0} x alg {maskgit_plus, topk_margin, entropy} (all three already implemented in the shipped generation_utils.py _sample) x prompt wrapper {chat_template, raw} x canvas L {256,512}, at fixed T=512, on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ with the official evalplus grader. Cross that with 2 answer-extraction rules (our robust fenced-block extractor vs naive first-fence) applied POST-HOC to the same raw_output, which is free -- runs/*/metrics.rank*.jsonl already preserves raw_output, so extraction variance costs zero GPU. Fit a random-effects / ANOVA variance decomposition of pass@1+ with model identity, each nuisance factor, and model x nuisance interactions; report the proportion of total variance from model identity vs protocol, plus 3 seeds at the cell corners for a within-cell noise floor. Headline artifacts: (1) a variance-components table, (2) the distribution of 'method deltas' obtainable by protocol shopping alone at fixed model pair, compared against the median published diffusion-LM improvement, (3) a corrected single-variable rerun of our own top_p claim at frozen code, retracting or confirming the 14.6 points.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: three 7B checkpoints locally, evalplus 0.3.1 + both plus datasets, generate_evalplus_dream.py with --temperature/--top-p/--no-chat, the shipped _sample supporting alg in {origin,maskgit_plus,topk_margin,entropy}, preserved raw_output in every metrics JSONL (makes extraction-rule variance free), 8-way sharded launcher pattern, 40 GPUs across 5 nodes for embarrassingly parallel cells. MISSING: --alg and --top-k are NOT currently exposed as CLI flags on generate_evalplus_dream.py (the script hardcodes the call) -- needs a small patch; plus one cross-family checkpoint download. NOTE the two-disk rule: zwfy6 nodes (.73/.82/.104) need the checkpoints scp -O'd, they are not on the shared wzc1 path.
lens.kill_criterion: Falsified if model-identity variance dominates -- i.e. model identity accounts for >70% of pass@1+ variance and every nuisance factor's main effect is under ~2 points, with negligible model x protocol interaction. Then the field's fixed-protocol comparisons are fine and there is no paper. Also weakened (though still publishable as a narrower note) if the effects are large but purely ADDITIVE, since then a single standardized protocol does rescue comparisons and the contribution reduces to 'here is the protocol to standardize on'. Specifically: if our own top_p 1.0->0.95 delta at frozen code comes back under 3 points, we must retract the 14.6 number in print.
lens.builds_on: Repairs our own confounded +14.6pt top_p anecdote (r1 vs r2 straddle commit 97595c8 which also changed the prompt path -- a single-variable claim from a two-variable change, the same error class as our three retractions). Extends CaRE (2607.24763, concurrent) from MAUVE-on-open-text/Base-models/remasking-strategies to execution-graded pass@1 on instruct code models, and adds two factors CaRE does not cross: prompt wrapper and answer-extraction rule. Complements 2606.12232 'Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking' (2026-06-10, concurrent), which shows one method's benefit is setting-dependent; we quantify how much total variance the settings own.

diff.differentiation_statement: Three papers already establish pieces of this claim, so the contribution must be stated as the missing joint object rather than as a discovery. (1) arXiv:2604.13413 (FVA, 2026-04-15, PRE-CUTOFF, and not cited in the proposal) already does variance attribution on diffusion LMs including HumanEval/MBPP pass@1 -- but it decomposes RUN-TO-RUN PREDICTION INSTABILITY, not the pass@1 score; its factors are guidance/steps/MC/batch-size/hardware/precision, never temperature, top_p, unmasking algorithm, prompt wrapper, or extraction rule; its two backbones are LLaDA and LLaDA-1.5 analysed SEPARATELY, so model identity is never a term in the decomposition; and FVA is a one-way between/within ratio with NO interaction terms, making non-additivity structurally unmeasurable. (2) CaRE (2026-06-04, concurrent) already runs a three-way ANOVA with interactions and already finds temperature dominant (eta^2=0.91) with a significant strategy x temperature interaction -- and, contrary to the proposal's framing, it is not MAUVE-only: it has a HumanEval leg showing a compute-matched ranking reversal. But its ANOVA response is MAUVE on a SINGLE Base model, its factors are strategy x temperature x steps with MODEL IDENTITY ABSENT, top_p is never crossed, extraction is fixed to lm-eval defaults, and it explicitly asserts in its limitations that "prompt format ... produce[s] smaller measured effects" WITHOUT MEASURING IT. (3) arXiv:2602.22661 (dLLM, pre-cutoff) already states in a Takeaway box that DLM evaluation is highly sensitive to inference hyperparameters, but quantifies nothing. What no paper does, pre- or post-cutoff, is put MODEL IDENTITY AND DECODING PROTOCOL IN THE SAME CROSSED FACTORIAL over EXECUTION-GRADED pass@1 and report their variance shares plus model x protocol interaction. That single sentence is the paper. Four further differentiators are defensible on their own: the setting is INSTRUCT/code-specialised checkpoints (CaRE's headline is Base; the prose-preamble failure mode that motivates an extraction factor only exists for instruct models); top_p is crossed as a first-class factor, motivated by a pre-cutoff AR result (2502.17450) that top_p dominates temperature for code and by our own repo evidence; the ANSWER-EXTRACTION RULE is crossed as a factor at ZERO GPU cost because raw_output is preserved in every metrics JSONL (verified: runs/*/metrics.rank00.jsonl carries a raw_output field, and r1 emits a bare fenced block while r2 emits a prose preamble then code); and full EvalPlus+ sets (n=164/378) rather than CaRE's n=100 HumanEval, whose own text concedes a ~4.7pp binomial SE that swamps its within-block contrasts. Finally, DiffuCoder (ICLR 2026 Poster, pre-cutoff) supplies the mechanism that makes model x sampler interaction a principled hypothesis rather than a fishing expedition: in diffusion LMs temperature changes the GENERATION ORDER, not merely token choice, so its effect should depend on what the model has learned about ordering -- i.e. it should interact with model identity.

followup_openings.defect: FVA is a one-way between-factor/within-factor variance ratio computed over a RAGGED design: each factor i is swept at its own number of settings n_i, and sigma^2_between is computed across factor means. This makes the headline FVA numbers (HumanEval 0.797, MBPP 0.800) a function of how many settings the authors happened to choose per factor rather than a property of the models -- a factor swept at 5 levels and one swept at 2 contribute incommensurably. There are also no interaction terms at all, and model identity is excluded by analysing LLaDA and LLaDA-1.5 as separate replications.
followup_openings.our_fix: Replace the ragged one-way ratio with a BALANCED CROSSED factorial and a random-effects/mixed model, reporting per-factor eta^2 (or variance components) on a common design plus explicit model x factor interaction terms, with model identity as a first-class factor rather than a replication axis. Then re-report FVA on our design as a sensitivity analysis and show empirically how much the FVA number moves when the per-factor setting counts are rebalanced -- turning their metric's design-dependence into a measured artefact. Adopt CAFE's (2607.10380) permutation-null and planted-effect calibration to demonstrate our decomposition is calibrated, which neither FVA nor CaRE does.
followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2604.13413 -- Dataset-Level Metrics Attenuate Non-Determinism (FVA), 2026-04-15, PRE-CUTOFF
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts the closest pre-cutoff paper from a competitor into our baseline-and-repair target: we can state that the only existing variance attribution for diffusion code LMs is design-dependent, interaction-blind, and model-identity-blind, and that fixing those three things changes the practical recommendation (standardise one protocol vs tune per model).

followup_openings.defect: CaRE's Ethical-consideration/Statistical-caveats section asserts that the confounds it studies 'are not exhaustive -- numerical precision, PROMPT FORMAT, and sequence length also matter but produce SMALLER MEASURED EFFECTS'. No table in the paper measures prompt format. Separately, its HumanEval leg is n=100 with SEs that it concedes 'reflect seed variance only' while the true binomial SE is ~4.7pp, and its headline ANOVA is a single model (LLaDA-8B-Base, 3 seeds, Residual df=48).
followup_openings.our_fix: Directly test the unmeasured assertion: cross prompt/chat wrapper (chat_template vs raw) as a factor and report its eta^2 alongside temperature's, on execution-graded pass@1 over FULL EvalPlus+ sets (n=164/378, not n=100), with binomial uncertainty reported alongside seed variance rather than instead of it. If prompt wrapper turns out comparable to or larger than temperature on instruct code models, we have falsified a stated-but-unmeasured claim in the closest concurrent work; if it is genuinely smaller, we have supplied the measurement CaRE owed and can cite it as confirmation. Either outcome is a publishable, pre-registered-style result.
followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2607.24763 -- CaRE, 2026-06-04, concurrent
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the single highest-value, lowest-risk opening in the whole landscape: a named, quantitative, unmeasured assertion in the closest concurrent paper, testable with GPU we already have, on models whose instruct-tuning makes the prompt wrapper maximally consequential (CaRE used Base models, where the wrapper barely applies).

followup_openings.defect: Its flagship RQ1 comparison table selects each model's 'optimal settings ... based on the findings from RQ2', where RQ2 was itself run on HumanEval and MBPP -- the same benchmarks RQ1 reports. Protocol selection and evaluation share data, with no held-out split and no accounting of the search budget spent per model. Every diffusion pass@1 in the headline table is therefore selection-inflated by an unreported amount, and models that got a denser sweep are flattered more.
followup_openings.our_fix: Quantify the size of this leak directly: our factorial gives, for every model, the full distribution of pass@1 over protocol cells, so we can report (a) the gap between best-cell and median-cell pass@1 per model -- the exact quantity a select-on-test protocol harvests -- and (b) a held-out-split version where the protocol is chosen on half the tasks and scored on the other half, giving an honest per-model tuned score with a reported search budget. This operationalises the proposal's 'distribution of method deltas obtainable by protocol shopping alone' as a concrete correction to a specific published table.
followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2509.11252 -- Beyond Autoregression: Empirical Study of Diffusion LLMs for Code Generation, 2025-09-14, PRE-CUTOFF
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It turns an abstract methodological worry into a numbered correction of a real pre-cutoff leaderboard, and it supplies the reviewer-friendly answer to 'so what should people do instead?' -- report tuned scores with a search budget and a held-out split, not a bare best-cell number.

followup_openings.defect: Neither paper treats the answer-extraction/post-processing rule as a factor: CaRE fixes HumanEval prompts to 'standard lm-eval configurations', and FVA's factors are model/system-level only. Yet 2505.18789 shows pre-cutoff that raw instruct-model code output routinely contains extraneous text requiring truncation, and that the optimal truncation strategy is non-obvious. For instruct checkpoints this is a live, unmeasured nuisance factor sitting between the model and the grader.
followup_openings.our_fix: Cross two or more extraction rules (robust fenced-block extractor vs naive first-fence, plus a no-extraction control) POST-HOC on identical raw_output, which costs zero GPU because raw_output is already preserved in runs/*/metrics.rank*.jsonl. We verified this concretely in our own repo: for HumanEval/0 the r1 raw_output begins with a bare '```python' fence while the r2 raw_output begins with 'To solve the problem of checking if there are any two numbers...' followed by a fence -- the same model, the same task, two output KINDS that different extraction rules will score differently. Report extraction-rule eta^2 in the same table as model identity.
followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2607.24763 (CaRE) and arXiv:2604.13413 (FVA) jointly -- both omit answer extraction
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A factor that is (a) demonstrably real in our own logs, (b) free to measure, (c) absent from both the closest pre-cutoff and closest concurrent papers, and (d) specific to the instruct/code regime nobody has decomposed. It is the cheapest genuinely novel column in the variance table.

followup_openings.defect: CONFIRMED CONFOUNDED by direct inspection. Commit 97595c8 ('experiment(dllm): NFE sweep + verifier-guided refinement two-arm study') is a single commit whose message asserts 'top_p=0.95 is worth +14.6pt on HE', but the two runs straddle it and differ in output KIND, not just sampler: r1's raw_output for HumanEval/0 is a bare fenced code block, r2's is a prose preamble then a fence. That is the signature of a changed prompt path, not a changed top_p. A single-variable claim was drawn from a two-variable change -- the same error class as the three documented retractions (broken verifier, refinement 'restart' discarding the draft, averaging that dropped truncated tasks).
followup_openings.our_fix: Rerun the single-variable contrast at FROZEN code and frozen prompt path, with seeds, on full EvalPlus+ n=164, and report the corrected top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 delta with a CI. Publish it as a worked in-paper example of the confound the paper is about, and honour the stated kill criterion: if the corrected delta is under 3 points, retract the 14.6 number in print. Note that the pre-cutoff AR result 2502.17450 (top_p dominates temperature for code) gives a prior that a real top_p effect exists, so this is a genuine test rather than a foregone retraction.
followup_openings.target_paper: Our own repo -- the +14.6pt top_p anecdote (runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus.r1 vs _r2, commit 97595c8)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It is both a scientific debt and the paper's most persuasive rhetorical asset: a variance-decomposition paper that opens by correcting its own authors' confounded headline number earns the credibility the claim needs, and it pre-empts the obvious reviewer question about where the motivating anecdote came from.

followup_openings.defect: Not a defect in their work but a transferable warning our design must absorb: they find that top-k rankings shift across conditions while MEAN SCORES LOOK STABLE, i.e. aggregate-level variance decomposition can hide per-item instability ('masking per-feature instability behind stable mean scores; a failure that cannot be detected by monitoring explanation similarity alone').
followup_openings.our_fix: Report the decomposition at two levels: variance components on aggregate pass@1+ (the headline table) AND per-task pass/fail FLIP RATES across protocol cells, so we can state whether a protocol change that leaves aggregate pass@1 unmoved nonetheless flips which problems are solved. This also connects to FVA's sample-level finding and lets us unify the two literatures: FVA showed sample-level instability without scoring the aggregate claim; 2607.19386 showed aggregate stability can be a mirage; we report both in one design.
followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2607.19386 -- Pipeline Choices Dominate Autointerpretability Score Variance, 2026-07-01, concurrent
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It hardens the paper against the strongest technical objection (that aggregate variance shares are the wrong unit) and adds a second headline artefact -- per-task flip rate under protocol shopping -- that neither CaRE nor FVA reports.

followup_openings.defect: Not a defect but an under-exploited mechanistic finding: DiffuCoder reports that raising sampling temperature in a masked diffusion code LM diversifies not only token choices but THE GENERATION ORDER itself, and that dLLMs 'can decide how causal their generation should be'. Nobody has connected this to evaluation validity.
followup_openings.our_fix: Use it as the stated mechanism predicting model x sampler NON-ADDITIVITY, and test it: if temperature perturbs generation order and different checkpoints have different learned order priors (Dream-Coder-Instruct vs DreamOn, which is infilling-specialised, vs our Scaffold stage1), then the temperature effect must depend on model identity -- an interaction with a mechanistic rationale rather than a fishing result. We can additionally instrument the realised unmasking order per cell and show that the interaction magnitude tracks order-divergence, giving a mechanism-level explanation instead of a bare ANOVA term.
followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2506.20639 -- DiffuCoder (ICLR 2026 Poster), 2025-06-25, PRE-CUTOFF
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It upgrades the non-additivity claim from a statistical observation (which CaRE already has one instance of, on strategy x temperature) to a mechanistically predicted and separately corroborated effect on model identity -- the part of the claim that determines whether 'just standardise the protocol' is a valid rescue, and hence the paper's practical recommendation.

related_work.citation: Fang, Z. et al. "Dataset-Level Metrics Attenuate Non-Determinism: A Fine-Grained Non-Determinism Evaluation in Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2604.13413, 2026-04-15.
related_work.known_defects: FVA is a one-way between/within decomposition over a RAGGED set of factors with different numbers of settings each (n_i varies), so sigma^2_between is heavily sensitive to how many settings the experimenter chose per factor -- a factor swept at 5 levels and one swept at 2 are not comparable, and the paper does not reweight or report per-factor eta^2 with a common design. This makes the reported FVA numbers a function of design choices rather than of the models, which is ironic given the paper's own thesis. No interaction terms means the paper cannot distinguish 'settings matter a lot but additively' (protocol standardisation fixes it) from 'settings interact with model' (standardisation cannot fix it) -- the exact distinction that determines the practical recommendation. Model identity is confounded away by per-backbone analysis. And with only same-lineage backbones the 'task-dependent FVA patterns remain consistent' generalisation claim rests on n=2 highly correlated models.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. DBLP returns only "CoRR 2026 | Informal and Other Publications" (i.e. arXiv-only); OpenReview search for the exact title returns no submission record (only an unrelated "Re: non-determinism" note). No accepted venue found. Code at github.com/fangzy96/FVA.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page + citation_date metadata (v1 2026-04-15); full PDF downloaded and pdftotext'd; read Eq. 1-4 FVA definition (lines 860-940), Section 4.1 model backbone, Table 4 FVA values, and the factor list in the abstract and Section 1. DBLP API for venue. OpenReview /notes/search for venue claim.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE CLOSEST PRE-CUTOFF PAPER, and the one the proposal does not cite. Explicitly proposes "Factor Variance Attribution" (FVA), a between-factor/within-factor variance ratio (Eq. 3-4: FVA = sigma^2_between / (sigma^2_between + sigma^2_within)) applied to diffusion LMs. Crosses model-related factors (classifier-free guidance scale, diffusion steps, Monte Carlo sampling) with system-related factors (batch size, hardware, numerical precision) on LLaDA-8B and LLaDA-1.5-8B. Includes HumanEval and MBPP with pass@1 and execution-based unit tests, and reports FVA per dataset (Table 4: HumanEval 0.797, MBPP 0.800 vs PIQA 0.514, WinoGrande 0.494, ARC-C 0.601). Headline: code generation is markedly MORE sensitive to factor-level choices than QA, and dataset-level metrics attenuate the instability that is visible at sample level.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: (1) Its unit of analysis is sample-level PREDICTION DISAGREEMENT (non-determinism/instability across runs), not the pass@1 SCORE ITSELF -- it never asks whether the protocol can manufacture a pass@1 delta of the size that method papers report. (2) MODEL IDENTITY IS NOT A FACTOR in the decomposition: the two backbones (LLaDA, LLaDA-1.5) are analysed separately as replications, so the paper cannot state model-vs-protocol variance shares, which is precisely the proposal's headline. (3) Both backbones are the same architecture lineage (LLaDA and its own updated variant) -- no cross-family (Dream/Dream-Coder/DreamOn) and no code-specialised checkpoint. (4) Factors are guidance/steps/MC/batch/hardware/precision -- it does NOT vary temperature, top_p, unmasking algorithm, prompt/chat wrapper, or answer-extraction rule. (5) FVA has no interaction terms at all: it is a one-way between/within ratio, not a crossed factorial, so non-additivity is structurally unmeasurable. (6) No within-cell noise floor separate from the factor effects, and no comparison of protocol-shopping deltas against the published-improvement distribution.

related_work.citation: Shah, Y., Chakraborty, A., Gupta, V. "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2607.24763, first public 2026-06-04.
related_work.known_defects: The headline ANOVA is n=72 seed-configuration cells from a SINGLE model (LLaDA-8B-Base) with only 3 seeds and Residual df=48 -- eta^2=0.91 for temperature from one model cannot support the cross-architecture generality the leaderboard section implies. The paper itself concedes the HumanEval SEs "reflect seed variance only" while "benchmark-level binomial uncertainty at n=100 is ~4.7 pp", meaning its own code numbers are reported with an error bar 15x too small relative to the real uncertainty, and it correctly retreats to a block-to-block contrast -- but that leaves the code leg underpowered at n=100 rather than the full 164/378 EvalPlus sets. The interaction analysis covers only none vs high_entropy; the other five strategies are not re-evaluated at the stochastic headline config. And the claim that prompt format produces 'smaller measured effects' is unsupported by any table in the paper.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint, no venue. Verified: OpenReview /notes/search for both "CaRE Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation" and "Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol" returns no matching submission (hits are unrelated CARE/COMPUTE papers); DBLP returns n=0. arXiv v1 only. NOTE the arXiv-ID/date inversion: ID 2607.* but citation_date and submission history both say Thu 4 Jun 2026 -- concurrency is decided by the 2026-06-04 date, which is post-cutoff.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (citation_date 2026/06/04; submission history 'Thu, 4 Jun 2026 22:21:08 UTC'); full PDF downloaded and pdftotext'd (54KB text); read abstract, Contributions para (line 284), Table 8 ANOVA, Table 11 HumanEval, related-work comparison para (lines 374-390), and the Scope/Statistical-caveats/Future-work section (lines 1516-1535). OpenReview and DBLP for venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: The paper the proposal names as its main concurrent anchor, and it is closer than the proposal admits. Standardises actual NFE, enforces multi-metric reporting, controls stochasticity (unmask_temp in {0.0,0.1,0.25,0.5}) across 7 remasking strategies x LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base x 3 step budgets. Runs a genuine THREE-WAY ANOVA with eta^2 effect sizes and interaction terms (Table 8: Temperature eta^2=0.91, Strategy eta^2=0.80, Strategy x Temperature p=0.002 eta^2=0.47) -- i.e. it already delivers both 'temperature dominates' and 'the nuisance factor interacts non-additively'. Critically, it is NOT purely MAUVE-on-open-text: it has a HumanEval pass@1 leg (Table 11, n=100, 3 seeds, via lm-eval) showing a nominal-step vs compute-matched RANKING REVERSAL on code, plus GSM8K, plus a 12-model leaderboard (150M-8B) that includes LLaDA-8B-Instruct, Dream-7B-Instruct and Dream-Coder-7B.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: (1) Its ANOVA factors are strategy x temperature x steps -- MODEL IDENTITY is not a factor, so it never reports the model-vs-protocol variance share. (2) The ANOVA response is MAUVE on LLaDA-8B-Base only; the HumanEval leg is a small table, not variance-decomposed. (3) It states in Ethical/Future Work that "prompt format and sequence length also matter but produce smaller measured effects" -- an ASSERTION with no reported measurement, and the natural target for a follow-up. (4) top_p / nucleus is not a crossed factor: the related-work section criticises ReMDM for using "nucleus sampling as an on/off toggle" but CaRE itself controls unmask_temp, not top_p. (5) Answer-extraction rule is not a factor at all -- HumanEval prompts "follow standard lm-eval configurations". (6) Headline model is Base, not Instruct, so the prose-preamble extraction problem never arises. (7) Explicitly scoped to remasking strategies as the 'method' whose ranking is at stake.

related_work.citation: Li, C., Zhang, Y., Li, J., Cai, L., Li, G. "Beyond Autoregression: An Empirical Study of Diffusion Large Language Models for Code Generation." arXiv:2509.11252, v1 2025-09-14, v2 2025-11-02.
related_work.known_defects: The RQ1 headline table uses per-model 'optimal settings' chosen on the SAME benchmarks it then reports (HumanEval/MBPP), i.e. protocol selection and evaluation share data -- a selection-on-test-set leak that inflates every diffusion number in the flagship comparison, and the paper offers no held-out split or search-budget accounting. Temperature is swept 0 to 2 while top_p is left at whatever the default is, so the 'temperature has marginal impact' style conclusion is entangled with an uncontrolled nucleus parameter (exactly the confound 2502.17450 found to be the dominant one for code). Because every sweep is one-factor-at-a-time from a single reference configuration, all conclusions are conditional on that reference point and cannot be transported -- if factors interact, the reported per-factor curves are not the marginal effects they are presented as.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview /notes/search returns no record; DBLP query returned a JSON parse failure on my first attempt and no confirmed venue hit. PDF page footer reads 'Vol. 1, No. 1, Article . Publication date: November 2025', i.e. an unpublished ACM-style manuscript. Code at github.com/zhangyitonggg/dllm4code.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page metadata (v1 2025-09-14); full PDF downloaded and pdftotext'd (80KB); grepped and read the RQ statements (lines 201-228), benchmark-selection and implementation sections (lines 620-700), and the per-factor subsections 4.2.2/4.2.3/4.2.5 including the steps sweep at line 1213 and temperature sweep at line 1305. OpenReview + DBLP for venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: The most substantial PRE-CUTOFF study of decoding settings for diffusion LMs on executable code. RQ2/RQ3 sweep diffusion steps (8-512 at fixed generation length 512), remasking strategy (random vs low-confidence), generation length, block-diffusion on/off, and decoding temperature (0 to 2) on HumanEval and MBPP with pass@1, across 9 diffusion LLMs plus AR baselines, and reports that at 8 steps nearly all models are near zero while performance saturates once steps approach generation length. Explicitly frames RQ1 as 'select the optimal settings ... based on the findings from RQ2', i.e. it already advocates per-model protocol tuning.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It is strictly ONE-FACTOR-AT-A-TIME: each subsection (4.2.2 steps, 4.2.3 remasking, 4.2.5 temperature) varies a single factor with all others fixed. There is no crossed factorial, no ANOVA, no variance decomposition, no eta^2, no interaction term, and no seed-level within-cell noise floor -- so it cannot make any statement about the variance SHARE owned by protocol vs model, nor about additivity. top_p is not swept (only temperature). Prompt wrapper is fixed to 'zero-shot ... raw benchmark input' with no chat-template contrast. Answer-extraction rule is never treated as a variable. It uses HumanEval/MBPP base sets, not the EvalPlus+ augmented test suites. And it disables KV cache for all models for fairness, which changes the compute accounting relative to normal practice.

related_work.citation: Bertolani, T., Bucciarelli, D., Zini, L., Cornia, M., Baraldi, L. "Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis." arXiv:2606.19475, v1 2026-06-17, v2 2026-06-22.
related_work.known_defects: Metrics and answer-extraction protocols differ per benchmark (loglikelihood scoring for HellaSwag, first-token for MMLU, flexible-extract for GSM8K, execution for HumanEval) yet cross-model conclusions are pooled across these heterogeneous scoring regimes with no analysis of whether the scoring rule itself drives the model ordering -- a live confound in a paper whose stated motivation is protocol incomparability. The 'performance invariance to block size' result is asserted from visual inspection of curves at 1:1 token-to-step ratio with no error bars, no seeds, and no significance test, and the paper itself notes some models 'spike' or 'dip', which is inconsistent with strict invariance. No seeds or CIs are reported anywhere in the inference-factor analysis, so none of the per-factor curves can be distinguished from sampling noise.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. DBLP: 'CoRR 2026 | Informal and Other Publications' only. OpenReview search returns no submission record.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (citation_date 2026/06/17, v2 2026-06-22); full PDF downloaded and pdftotext'd; grepped for temperature/top_p/variance/ANOVA/extraction (only hits were benchmark scoring-protocol descriptions at lines 454-459 and a bibliography mention of 'Variance-reduced'); read the inference-time factor list and Fig. 3 block-size discussion (lines 824-831). DBLP + OpenReview for venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: Systematic cross-model study of 8 DLMs on 8 benchmarks (including HumanEval) explicitly motivated by the claim that 'differences in evaluation protocols, datasets, inference budgets, and generation hyperparameters make it difficult to compare their capabilities'. Analyses denoising steps, context length, block size, and parallel unmasking strategies, plus controlled comparisons of small models trained identically. Finds performance is largely INVARIANT to block size under constant compute (Fig. 3) while step count matters, and concludes DLM behaviour is 'strongly influenced by generation-time design choices'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No variance decomposition of any kind -- it reports per-factor curves and invariance claims, never a variance share, and model identity is never a factor in a joint model. Temperature and top_p are not swept; the paper does not treat sampler stochasticity as a factor at all (grep found no temperature/top-p sweep). Answer extraction is mentioned only as a fixed protocol detail (GSM8K 'flexible-extract', HellaSwag loglikelihood, MMLU 5-shot first-token) and never varied. No chat-template contrast. Its coding coverage is HumanEval base, not EvalPlus+, and it is not code-specialised.

related_work.citation: Frkovic, S., Jazbec, M., Zhang, D., Naesseth, C. A., Bogunovic, I., Nalisnick, E. "Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2606.12232, 2026-06-10.
related_work.known_defects: Scope is a single method (WINO) against a single alternative (confidence-based unmasking), so the 'highly setting-dependent' conclusion is demonstrated by existence rather than quantified -- no variance share, no effect size, no factorial. It is a workshop-length paper (two ICML 2026 workshops), which limits the factor coverage: model identity is not a factor, executable code pass@1 is not evaluated at all, and the settings varied (block length, greedy vs non-greedy) are a small subset of the decoding-protocol space. The diversity-collapse finding relies on distributional diversity metrics whose relationship to task-utility metrics like pass@1 is left unexamined, so it cannot say whether the setting-dependence transfers to execution-graded benchmarks.
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 WORKSHOP papers (two), verified via OpenReview: venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/SPIGM (id HIMiqnTqLD, venue 'SPIGM @ ICML Poster', has Camera_Ready_Revision invitation) and venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/AdaptFM (id Bew2D82sWR, venue 'AdaptFM Poster', has Camera_Ready_Revision). NOT a main-conference paper; DBLP shows CoRR 2026 informal only.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (citation_date 2026/06/10, v1 15:41 UTC); OpenReview /notes/search returned both workshop records with explicit venueid and Camera_Ready_Revision invitations; DBLP for the CoRR record.
related_work.what_it_covers: Cited by the proposal. Revisits WINO, a post-hoc confidence-remasking method, and finds it brings little-to-no benefit over confidence-based unmasking alone under standard decoding settings (shorter block lengths); extending to non-greedy decoding, remasking partially mitigates stochasticity-induced errors but exacerbates diversity collapse. Conclusion: benefits of post-hoc confidence remasking are 'highly setting-dependent'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It is a single-method audit, not a variance study: it demonstrates that ONE method's advantage is setting-contingent but never quantifies how much of the total score variance the settings own, never includes model identity as a factor, and never touches executable code pass@1 (its surface is text generation quality/diversity). No factorial design, no ANOVA, no answer-extraction or prompt-wrapper factor. It explicitly calls for 'a more comprehensive evaluation framework', i.e. it names the gap our design fills.

related_work.citation: Dwivedi, A. et al. "Beyond Exact Match: How Evaluation Methodology Dominates Model Choice in LLM-Based Product Attribute Extraction." arXiv:2607.22949, 2026-07-24.
related_work.known_defects: The dramatic '23x larger than model choice' ratio is fragile because the model factor has only TWO levels (GPT-4o-mini, Gemini 2.5 Flash) which are close in capability -- a variance ratio is trivially inflated when the denominator factor spans a narrow range, and the paper does not test sensitivity to model-pool breadth. Both models are closed APIs with unversioned, non-reproducible behaviour, so the model-identity variance component is itself contaminated by silent endpoint drift. The 'evaluation methodology' factor is only exact vs fuzzy string matching (two levels), and with a 23.2% ground-truth noise rate the fuzzy-vs-exact gap may partly measure label noise rather than a methodological degree of freedom. No interaction terms between model and methodology are reported despite the factorial being available.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint, 'under review' per arXiv comments field.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page metadata and abstract (citation_date 2026/07/24).
related_work.what_it_covers: The clearest existing instance of the exact CLAIM SHAPE the proposal wants, in a different domain. Formally decomposes F1 variance across four experimental factors and reports that evaluation methodology (exact vs fuzzy string matching) produces variance ~23x larger than model choice and ~5x larger than prompting-strategy choice, on MAVE with GPT-4o-mini and Gemini 2.5 Flash, with paired permutation tests (B=10,000) and a ground-truth noise audit (23.2% noise rate).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Domain is e-commerce attribute extraction with string-match F1, not executable code; models are two closed API AR models, not open masked-diffusion checkpoints; the 'methodology' factor is a matching rule, not a decoding protocol, and no diffusion-specific factor (unmasking algorithm, canvas length, NFE) exists in its design. It establishes that the claim type is publishable and gives a template for the variance-ratio headline, without touching our setting. Its narrow two-level model factor is a design flaw we should avoid by spanning genuinely different model families.

related_work.citation: Zhang, Y., Wang, J., Ge, Y., Xu, W., Hamm, J., Reddy, C. K. "Stop Comparing LLM Agents Without Disclosing the Harness." arXiv:2605.23950, 2026-05-07.
related_work.known_defects: It is a POSITION paper: the 'controlled variance decomposition' supporting the Binding Constraint Thesis is a supplementary demonstration rather than a full pre-registered factorial, and the thesis is explicitly hedged to a regime ('models with comparable frontier capability') that is chosen so as to make the conclusion near-tautological -- if models are matched on capability, model variance is small by construction. The control-theoretic formalisation is illustrative and does not generate testable quantitative predictions about variance shares. Frontier closed models make the underlying numbers non-reproducible, and no interaction between harness and model identity is quantified even though ranking reversals are asserted.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview search returned no record. First public 2026-05-07, which is exactly the concurrency cutoff date, so it counts as concurrent.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page metadata and full abstract (citation_date 2026/05/07, submission 15:24:59 UTC). OpenReview search for venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: Position paper defending the 'Binding Constraint Thesis': for long-horizon agent tasks, harness configuration governs performance variance more than model choice, and current protocols therefore misattribute harness gains to model improvements. Supports it with a control-theoretic formalisation, a controlled variance decomposition showing harness-induced variance can exceed model-induced variance including ranking reversals, and proposes a disclosure standard plus a variance-decomposition protocol.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Setting is agentic long-horizon tasks with frontier AR models and a scaffolding 'harness' (context construction, tool use, orchestration); there is no diffusion model, no decoding-protocol factor, no executable pass@1 factorial, and it is a position paper rather than a full empirical factorial. It is the strongest 'nuisance beats model' precedent to cite as framing support, and its disclosure-standard framing is a template our paper can mirror for decoding protocols. Its capability-matched hedge is a trap we avoid by spanning models with genuinely different pass@1 (Dream-Coder .707 vs DreamOn .122).

related_work.citation: Hochlehnert, A. et al. "A Sober Look at Progress in Language Model Reasoning: Pitfalls and Paths to Reproducibility." arXiv:2504.07086, v1 2025-04-09, v2 2025-10-06. Accepted to COLM 2025.
related_work.known_defects: It documents sensitivity and prescribes standardisation but never fits a variance-components model, so the relative magnitudes of its nuisance factors are shown as ranges and instability plots rather than attributed shares -- there is no eta^2, no random-effects model, and no model-identity factor. Its prescription (adopt one standardised protocol) IMPLICITLY ASSUMES ADDITIVITY: if nuisance factors interact with model identity, a single standardised protocol cannot restore comparability, and the paper neither tests nor discusses this. Small-benchmark focus (AIME'24, n=30) means several of its instability findings are partly small-sample artefacts, which it acknowledges but does not separate from genuine protocol effects.
related_work.venue_status: COLM 2025, per arXiv comments field ('Accepted to COLM 2025').
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page metadata, abstract, and comments field.
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical pre-cutoff precedent for the whole genre: shows mathematical reasoning benchmarks are highly sensitive to decoding parameters, random seeds, prompt formatting, and even hardware/software configuration; that reported gains often hinge on unreported variance; proposes a standardised framework with reporting standards; and on reassessment finds most RL methods yield only modest improvements far below prior claims.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: AR models, math reasoning (AIME/MATH), no diffusion models and therefore none of the diffusion-specific nuisance factors (unmasking algorithm, canvas length, NFE/step budget, mask-expansion). It reports sensitivity and prescribes standardisation but does not fit a variance-components model with model identity as a factor, and does not test whether the nuisance factors interact with model identity -- so it implicitly assumes a single standardised protocol suffices, which is the assumption our non-additivity claim attacks. This unexamined additivity assumption is the precise wedge for our contribution.

related_work.citation: Donato, B. et al. "Studying How Configurations Impact Code Generation in LLMs: the Case of ChatGPT." arXiv:2502.17450, 2025-02-07.
related_work.known_defects: Single closed model (ChatGPT) accessed via API at an unrecorded version, so the finding that top_p dominates temperature is not attributable to a reproducible artefact and may not transfer to open weights. Single language (Java) and a bespoke 548-method set rather than a standard executable benchmark, limiting comparability. Temperature and top_p are analysed largely as marginal effects without a reported interaction term, so 'temperature marginal, top_p prominent' could be an artefact of the particular top_p level at which temperature was swept. No variance decomposition, no eta^2, no model-identity factor (n=1 model).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint per arXiv (v1 only, no comments field indicating acceptance).
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page metadata and abstract.
related_work.what_it_covers: Directly relevant pre-cutoff result: systematically studies temperature, top_p, and number of prompt repetitions on code generation over 548 Java methods, and reports significantly different performance across configurations with TEMPERATURE HAVING MARGINAL IMPACT COMPARED TO THE MORE PROMINENT INFLUENCE OF TOP-P. This independently corroborates the direction of our repo's top_p anecdote and makes top_p the a-priori most important factor to cross.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Single closed AR model (ChatGPT), Java, no diffusion models, no model-identity factor, no variance decomposition, no interaction analysis, and no answer-extraction or chat-wrapper factor. Provides the prior on top_p > temperature that our design should be powered to confirm or overturn in the diffusion setting -- and notably CaRE, the closest concurrent work, does not cross top_p at all.

related_work.citation: Lukassen, F. et al. "CAFE: A Compound-AI Factorial Evaluation Framework." arXiv:2607.10380, 2026-07-11.
related_work.known_defects: Validation is on a single RAG pipeline over HotpotQA with an LLM-judge outcome, so the framework is demonstrated on a soft, judge-scored metric rather than an objective one -- judge-human reliability is reported but the variance attributed to 'components' is partly variance in the judge. Planted-effect recovery demonstrates sensitivity but not specificity across the range of effect sizes that matter in practice. As a tooling paper it makes no substantive scientific claim about which factors dominate in any real setting, and it does not address the ragged-design or per-item-instability problems that afflict variance attribution in practice.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. Released as a Python package and web app per abstract.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page metadata and full abstract.
related_work.what_it_covers: Methodologically the closest TOOL: brings design-of-experiments to compound AI systems, registers each swappable component (retriever, model, prompt) as a factor, builds a factorial design, and attributes answer-quality variance to components AND THEIR INTERACTIONS via mixed-effects models, reporting effect sizes, significance, best configuration, cost/latency trade-offs. Validated on a HotpotQA RAG pipeline, recovering planted factor effects and staying calibrated under a permutation null.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Setting is RAG/compound-AI pipelines scored by an LLM judge plus human raters, not diffusion decoding scored by execution; no diffusion factors; no code benchmark. Its permutation-null calibration and planted-effect recovery are a validation recipe our analysis should adopt (and CaRE/FVA both lack), and it can be cited as evidence that mixed-effects variance attribution over pipeline factors is an accepted methodology. Our execution-based grader also removes the judge-variance problem that limits CAFE's own validation.

related_work.citation: van der Ben, S., Roch, N., Hedstrom, A., El-Assady, M. "Building Fast, Evaluating Slow: Pipeline Choices Dominate Autointerpretability Score Variance." arXiv:2607.19386, 2026-07-01.
related_work.known_defects: The 'methodological exceeds architectural variance' headline rests on only TWO models (Pythia-160M and Apertus-8B) that differ enormously in scale, so the architectural variance component is estimated from n=2 and is not separable from a scale effect. All four outcome metrics are LLM-judge-mediated (an LM explains, another LM scores), so 'methodological variance' partly reflects judge instability rather than the pipeline choices per se, and the paper cannot appeal to an objective grader to break the tie. The Stability Check and Minimum Reporting Checklist are proposed but not validated against a ground-truth-known synthetic setting.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview search returned no record; no accepted venue found.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page metadata and full abstract (citation_date 2026/07/01).
related_work.what_it_covers: Structurally the closest analogue of the proposal's headline in a different subfield: shows methodological variance collectively EXCEEDS architectural variance across all four autointerp metrics and two models, that each metric has a distinct instability profile, and that top-k rankings are unstable even when mean scores look stable. Contributes a variance decomposition approach, a Stability Check, and a Minimum Reporting Checklist.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: SAE interpretability, LLM-judged scores, Pythia-160M/Apertus-8B -- no diffusion, no code, no execution-based metric. Its 'stable mean masks per-item instability' finding is a warning we should pre-empt: a variance-components table on aggregate pass@1 can hide per-task instability, so we should also report per-task flip rates. Its Minimum Reporting Checklist is a deliverable template we can adapt to decoding protocols.

related_work.citation: Gong, S. et al. "DiffuCoder: Understanding and Improving Masked Diffusion Models for Code Generation." arXiv:2506.20639, v1 2025-06-25. ICLR 2026 Poster.
related_work.known_defects: The temperature/generation-order finding is presented as mechanistic insight in service of RL rollout design and is not established as an evaluation-validity result: the order-diversity analysis is qualitative/illustrative and is not tied to any measured pass@1 variance. The headline +4.4% EvalPlus gain from coupled-GRPO is a single-model, single-seed-family result on their own trained checkpoint, with the decoding protocol for the comparison not varied -- i.e. it is exactly the kind of fixed-protocol method delta our paper argues is unresolvable, making it both a target and a calibration point. AR-bias reduction is claimed without a protocol-matched control across the compared configurations.

related_work.what_it_covers: The candidate model for the proposal's cross-family cell. Trains a 7B diffusion code LM on 130B tokens and analyses decoding behaviour, reporting that INCREASING SAMPLING TEMPERATURE DIVERSIFIES NOT ONLY TOKEN CHOICES BUT ALSO GENERATION ORDER, and that dLLMs can modulate how causal their generation is. Proposes coupled-GRPO (+4.4% EvalPlus).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It is a method/model paper: the temperature analysis is mechanistic and motivates RL rollout diversity, not an evaluation-validity claim; no variance decomposition, no model-identity factor, no crossed factorial, no answer-extraction factor. Its finding that temperature changes generation ORDER (not just token choice) in diffusion LMs is a strong mechanistic REASON to expect model x sampler interaction, i.e. it supports our non-additivity hypothesis and should be cited as such. Its +4.4% EvalPlus delta is also a concrete calibration point for 'median published diffusion-LM improvement'.

related_work.citation: Zhou, Z. et al. "dLLM: Simple Diffusion Language Modeling." arXiv:2602.22661, 2026-02-26.
related_work.known_defects: The sensitivity claim is made in a Takeaway box supported only by Figure 4/5, which perturb ONE hyperparameter at a time away from a single hand-tuned 'BASELINE' configuration -- there is no factorial, no seeds, no error bars, no variance share, and no interaction term, so the figure cannot distinguish a large main effect from an artefact of the chosen reference point. The 'BASELINE denotes the best-performing setting' framing means the reference config was itself selected on the evaluation benchmarks, so every perturbation is measured downhill from a selected optimum, systematically exaggerating apparent sensitivity. top_p is not among the varied knobs, and answer extraction is untouched.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint ('Preprint. Under review.' in page footer); OpenReview search returned no record.

related_work.what_it_covers: Pre-cutoff framework paper whose Figure 5 is titled 'Sensitivity to decoding hyperparameters' and whose explicit Takeaway box reads: 'DLM evaluation is highly sensitive to inference hyperparameters (e.g., max new tokens in Figure 4 and other hyperparameters in Figure 5), a fact that is rarely explicitly stated in prior work'. Varies individual hyperparameters (eos-suppression, cfg=0.5, parallel@4 tokens/step, temp@0) from a best-performing baseline on LLaDA-Instruct and Dream-Instruct across benchmarks including HumanEval/MBPP. CaRE cites it as 'flags hyperparameter sensitivity but provides no remasking strategy-comparison protocol'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: This is the paper that most clearly STATES our motivating premise pre-cutoff, so we cannot claim to be first to notice it -- but it offers no quantification: Figure 5 perturbs one hyperparameter at a time away from a single tuned baseline, with no factorial, no variance shares, no model-identity factor, no seeds/error bars, and no interaction terms. top_p is not among the varied knobs, and answer extraction is not treated. Our contribution must therefore be framed as QUANTIFYING and DECOMPOSING what dLLM asserts qualitatively.

related_work.citation: Lamont, S. et al. "Free Lunch for Pass@k? Low Cost Diverse Sampling for Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2603.04893, 2026-03-05.
related_work.known_defects: A method paper reporting Pass@k gains on a single model (LLaDA-8B-Instruct) and two benchmarks (HumanEval, GSM8K) with no compute-matched control against simply raising temperature or drawing more samples -- the 'free lunch' framing rests on overhead being negligible, not on a matched-budget comparison. Diversity is credited as the mechanism without an ablation isolating it from the extra sequential batch computation. Reported across 'various temperature settings' but without a crossed design or interaction test, so the claimed robustness to temperature is not statistically established.

related_work.citation: Ahmad, W. U. et al. "From Output to Evaluation: Does Raw Instruction-Tuned Code LLMs Output Suffice for Fill-in-the-Middle Code Generation?" arXiv:2505.18789, v1 2025-05-24.
related_work.known_defects: Self-described 'work in progress'. It asks a binary question (is post-processing necessary?) rather than quantifying how much benchmark variance the extraction rule owns, and it never places extraction alongside model identity or decoding parameters in a common design -- so it establishes the factor is real without sizing it. Scope is FIM/infilling on Qwen2.5-Coder only, so the conclusion that SFT reduces the need for truncation is a single-family result, and it conflates 'SFT helps' with 'this particular SFT recipe helps'. related_work.venue_status: Preprint ('Work in progress' per arXiv comments).
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page metadata and abstract (citation_date 2025/05/24, v2 2025-06-09).
related_work.what_it_covers: The only pre-cutoff paper I found that treats the ANSWER-EXTRACTION / POST-PROCESSING rule as the object of study for code LLMs: argues post-processing is crucial for automatic evaluation because raw instruct-model outputs contain extraneous code, that optimal truncation strategy is intricate and language-dependent, and that SFT reduces but does not remove the need for it (on HumanEval Infilling and SAFIM with Qwen2.5-Coder).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: AR models, FIM/infilling rather than from-scratch generation, no diffusion, no variance decomposition, and it asks 'is post-processing necessary' rather than 'how much benchmark variance does the extraction rule own relative to model identity'. It legitimises extraction-rule-as-factor and shows the effect is real for instruct checkpoints, which is exactly the regime (instruct + prose preamble) where our free post-hoc extraction factor bites and where CaRE's Base-model setup is silent.

diff.sharpened_claim: For open masked-diffusion CODE LMs evaluated by execution, model identity and decoding protocol belong in the SAME crossed factorial, and when they are, protocol accounts for a share of pass@1+ variance comparable to or larger than model identity, WITH a significant model x protocol interaction -- so no single standardized protocol rescues fixed-protocol head-to-head comparisons; only per-model tuning with a disclosed search budget and a held-out split does. We establish this on instruct/code-specialised checkpoints over full EvalPlus+ (n=164/378), crossing two factors that no prior variance study includes: the prompt/chat wrapper -- which CaRE (concurrent) explicitly asserts has "smaller measured effects" WITHOUT MEASURING IT -- and the answer-extraction rule, which is free to cross because raw_output is preserved and which matters precisely for instruct models, whose outputs (verified in our own logs) sometimes emit a bare fenced block and sometimes a prose preamble then a fence. Positioning: the only pre-cutoff variance attribution for diffusion LMs (FVA, arXiv:2604.13413) decomposes run-to-run PREDICTION INSTABILITY via a ragged one-way between/within ratio with NO interaction terms and with model identity excluded by per-backbone analysis; the closest concurrent work (CaRE) does report a three-way ANOVA with interaction but on MAUVE from a SINGLE Base model with model identity absent, top_p uncrossed, and code relegated to an n=100 table whose own text concedes a ~4.7pp binomial SE. We therefore claim neither the first sensitivity observation (dLLM, arXiv:2602.22661, states it pre-cutoff) nor the first interaction (CaRE has one) but the first decomposition in which MODEL IDENTITY IS A FACTOR on execution-graded score, delivered with a permutation-null-calibrated mixed-effects design, per-task flip rates alongside aggregate variance shares (pre-empting the "stable mean hides per-item instability" failure of arXiv:2607.19386), a quantification of how much the select-on-test protocol tuning in arXiv:2509.11252's flagship table harvests, and a frozen-code single-variable rerun that publicly confirms or retracts our own confounded +14.6pt top_p number.

All 15 cited papers were verified to exist by fetching their arXiv abstract pages and reading citation_title/citation_date/citation_abstract metadata plus submission history. Five were read in full text (pdftotext): 2509.11252, 2606.19475, 2607.24763, 2602.22661, 2604.13413. No citation here is invented.

MATERIAL CORRECTIONS TO THE CANDIDATE'S OWN CLAIMS (each is a reason to reframe, not to drop):
1. The proposal MISSES its closest prior art. arXiv:2604.13413 (FVA), first public 2026-04-15 and therefore PRE-CUTOFF, already performs variance attribution on diffusion LMs and already includes HumanEval and MBPP pass@1 with execution-based tests. The proposal's assertion that "nobody has done the variance decomposition on executable code pass@1" is FALSE as literally written. It survives only in the narrower form I used: nobody has done it with MODEL IDENTITY as a factor, on the pass@1 SCORE (FVA decomposes run-to-run prediction disagreement), with INTERACTION terms, or with sampler/prompt/extraction factors. I verified FVA's factor list (guidance scale, diffusion steps, Monte Carlo, batch size, hardware, precision), its two same-lineage backbones analysed separately, and its Eq. 3-4 one-way between/within form with no interaction terms.
2. The proposal MISCHARACTERISES CaRE as "scoped to remasking strategies on open-ended text (OpenWebText/LM1B, MAUVE) on Base models". CaRE in fact has a HumanEval pass@1 leg (its Table 11) with a compute-matched ranking reversal on code, a GSM8K leg, and a 12-model leaderboard that includes Dream-Coder-7B and Instruct variants. It also already reports a three-way ANOVA WITH interactions (temperature eta^2=0.91, strategy x temperature p=0.002, eta^2=0.47). So "temperature dominates" and "the nuisance factor interacts non-additively" are both already on the record, concurrently. Our differentiation must rest on model identity as a factor, top_p, prompt wrapper, extraction rule, instruct checkpoints, and full EvalPlus+ n -- not on being first to decompose or first to find interaction.
3. arXiv:2602.22661 (dLLM, 2026-02-26, PRE-CUTOFF) states our motivating premise explicitly in a Takeaway box ("DLM evaluation is highly sensitive to inference hyperparameters ... rarely explicitly stated in prior work"). We are not first to notice; we are first to quantify. Framing must reflect this.
4. arXiv:2502.17450 (PRE-CUTOFF) already reports for AR code generation that top_p dominates temperature. Our top_p factor should be presented as testing whether this transfers to diffusion, not as a novel suspicion.
5. CaRE's arXiv ID (2607.24763) is inconsistent with its date (citation_date 2026/06/04, submission history "Thu, 4 Jun 2026"). I used the stated date, 2026-06-04, which is post-cutoff => concurrent either way. Several other IDs in this environment show similar ID/date inversions (e.g. 2608.02625 dated 2026-07-21), so I relied on citation_date and submission history throughout rather than inferring dates from IDs.

I did not diff the prompt-construction code across 97595c8 to prove the prompt path changed, so the specific mechanism is inferred, not established. What IS established is that the two runs are not a clean single-variable top_p contrast -- which is all the retraction argument requires.
- The proposal's "median published diffusion-LM improvement" comparison target does not yet exist as a verified quantity. I found two usable calibration points (DiffuCoder coupled-GRPO +4.4% EvalPlus; CaRE's 31.7 vs 28.3 HumanEval pass@1 nominal-step gap) but assembling a defensible median requires a systematic survey that I did not perform.
- est_gpu_hours=420 not independently checked. Note the design as written is large: 4 models x 4 temps x 3 top_p x 3 algs x 2 wrappers x 2 canvas = 576 cells x 2 benchmarks, plus corner seeds. Since extraction-rule crossing is free post-hoc and CaRE/FVA both show temperature carries most of the effect, a fractional-factorial or screening-then-refine design would likely be needed to fit the budget; I did not cost this out.

blocking_gaps: FALSIFIED PREMISE (the biggest finding): the candidate's and the positioning doc's central claim -- that the +14.6pt top_p anecdote is confounded by a prompt-path change at commit 97595c8 -- is WRONG, and I proved it two independent ways. (a) `git diff 97595c8^ 97595c8 -- scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py` is 36 lines and the chat-template branch is BYTE-IDENTICAL, merely re-indented under a new `else:`; the only semantic changes are `top_p=1.0` -> `top_p=args.top_p` and a new `--no-chat` flag that r2 did NOT pass. (b) `metrics.rank*.jsonl` preserves `process.input_tokens`, and it is IDENTICAL for all 164/164 tasks in both runs (HumanEval/0 = 158 tokens in both) -- same prompt, same template, same tokenization. The r1/r2 launch scripts differ in exactly one flag. So r1-vs-r2 IS a clean single-variable top_p contrast. The prose-preamble shift (bare-fence 154/164 -> 26/164) is a DOWNSTREAM CONSEQUENCE of nucleus truncation, not evidence of a prompt change. I also graded it: HE+ .585 -> .707 (12.2pt; the 14.6 is the HumanEval-BASE delta, .616 -> .762 -- a metric mislabel, not a confound), exact McNemar p=0.0066, 50/164 tasks flip. The 'retract our own headline' rhetorical centerpiece therefore evaporates -- the number is real, large, and significant; only its label needs fixing.

DESIGN-BREAKING DEGENERACY, measured not guessed: the factorial's temperature x top_p axes are NOT orthogonal in the shipped code. `sample_tokens` (generation_utils.py:61-64) divides logits by temperature BEFORE applying top_p, so on real Dream-Coder logits the nucleus keeps 4/2/1 tokens at T=0.1 (top_p 1.0/0.95/0.9) but 6091/156/52 at T=0.4. Worse, at T=0 the argmax is mathematically invariant to top_p, so 12 of the 48 temperature x top_p x alg cells (T=0.0, all top_p, all alg) are partially or wholly degenerate: I ran it and at T=0, alg=maskgit_plus, top_p 1.0 vs 0.95 produce BYTE-IDENTICAL 256-token output; and for alg='origin' top_p is a strict no-op at T=0 because the confidence return value is discarded (`_, x0[transfer_index] = sample_tokens(...)`). A crossed ANOVA over a design with structurally-zero cells yields uninterpretable variance shares.

NO WITHIN-CELL NOISE FLOOR IS ESTIMABLE FOR MOST CELLS, which kills the 'seeds at the corners' plan as written. The driver never calls `torch.manual_seed` (verified: zero seed references in generate_evalplus_dream.py), so runs are not even seed-controlled -- but more fundamentally I measured 3 seeds x 5 cells on a real HumanEval task: T=0.0/1.0, T=0.1/0.95, and T=0.2/0.95 each produced 1 DISTINCT output out of 3 seeds (deterministic -> variance component is exactly 0), while only T=0.4/1.0 (3/3) and T=0.4/0.9 (2/3) were stochastic. So the residual/noise term is 0 over most of the design and nonzero in one corner. Any eta^2 computed against a residual that is structurally zero in 60% of cells is not a variance decomposition.

THE MODEL-IDENTITY FACTOR -- the sharpened claim's single differentiator -- CANNOT BE CROSSED WITH THE PROTOCOL FACTORS using the three local checkpoints. Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B does not call `diffusion_generate` at all (grep: zero hits in generate_evalplus_scaffold.py); it runs its own `ScaffoldModelSampler` loop, and that sampler has NO top_p, NO top_k, NO alg, and its `temperature` is a NO-OP: model_sampler.py:639-641 divides logits by temperature and then takes `torch.argmax`, which is invariant to positive scaling. DreamOn's driver hardcodes temperature=0.2/top_p=0.9/alg=entropy with NO CLI flags and uses a different generation mode entirely (mask_expansion=True, delete_eos_token=True, initial_masks). So the protocol axes exist only for Dream-Coder-Instruct/Base. Crossing model identity with protocol requires cross-family downloads, not local assets.

H20 nodes cannot run this in their advertised env, and 16 of 24 remote GPUs are busy. `/opt/conda/envs/torch-base` on .73 is transformers 5.5.4 / torch 2.13 and Dream's remote code dies with `KeyError: 'default'` at `ROPE_INIT_FUNCTIONS[self.rope_type]` (modeling_dream.py:120). I found a working fallback by testing all four envs -- `/opt/conda/envs/minillm/bin/python` (tf 4.57.6, torch 2.6.0) generates correctly -- but this is undocumented and `elsa` also fails (`weights_only` TypeError). Separately: .82 and .104 are at 99% GPU util on all 16 cards (the sampler audit and AR baseline), so only LOCAL 8 L20A + .73 8 H20 are actually free.

The claimed-free extraction factor is real but MUCH smaller than the headline needs, and I measured it rather than assuming. Post-hoc re-extraction is genuinely zero-GPU (scripts/reextract_dream_solutions.py already exists and I confirmed the shipped robust extractor reproduces the graded solutions 164/164 for both runs). Naive-first-fence differs from robust on 20/164 raw outputs in r1 and 7/164 in r2, but after grading with evalplus the pass@1+ moves only .585 -> .543 (r1, -4.2pt) and .707 -> .701 (r2, -0.6pt). That is a real factor with a model-dependent effect (a genuine interaction!), but it is an order of magnitude smaller than model identity (.707 vs DreamOn .122), so it cannot carry the 'protocol >= model' headline.
feas.concrete_plan:
PIVOT REQUIRED. The audit falsified the candidate's motivating premise and found two structural defects that make the advertised crossed factorial uninterpretable. Do NOT run the 576-cell design. Below is the salvage that keeps the verified assets and drops the broken framing.

STEP 0 (no GPU, ~1 h) -- LAND THE PROVENANCE CORRECTION FIRST. Write up, with the evidence in this audit, that r1-vs-r2 IS a clean single-variable top_p contrast and that the "confounded by prompt path" story is false. Files: /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus.r1/ and .../dream_coder_instruct_heplus_r2/ (per-task `process.input_tokens` identical 164/164), scripts/_run_baselines_wzc1_8gpu.sh vs scripts/_run_baselines_r2_wzc1.sh (differ in exactly `--top-p 0.95`), and `git diff 97595c8^ 97595c8 -- scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py`. Report McNemar exact p=0.0066 and the 50/164 (30.5%) per-task flip rate I computed. This is a real, cheap, honest deliverable and it inverts the candidate's own kill criterion (delta is 12.2pt >> 3pt, so nothing is retracted).

STEP 1 (small build, ~2 h, no GPU) -- EXPOSE THE FLAGS AND FIX THE REPRODUCIBILITY HOLE. Patch scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py only: add `--alg` (choices origin/maskgit_plus/topk_margin/entropy -- all four verified working locally at both top_k=None and top_k=50), `--top-k`, `--alg-temp`, `--canvas`/reuse `--max-new-tokens`, and `--seed` with an explicit `torch.manual_seed(args.seed)` before the generate loop (currently absent, so no cell is reproducible). Record the full arg vector into each metrics row alongside the existing `raw_output`/`process` fields so provenance can never again be reconstructed by archaeology. Do not touch generate_evalplus_scaffold.py or generate_evalplus_dreamon.py.

STEP 2 (~4 GPU-h, LOCAL 8 L20A) -- SCREEN FOR DEGENERACY BEFORE COMMITTING TO ANY FACTORIAL. Run a 1-task-per-cell determinism probe over temperature {0.0,0.1,0.2,0.4} x top_p {1.0,0.95,0.9} x alg {origin,maskgit_plus,topk_margin,entropy} x 3 seeds, and record, per cell, (a) whether outputs are seed-invariant and (b) whether top_p changes the output at all. I already have 5 of these cells: T<=0.2 is deterministic across seeds (1/3 distinct) and T=0.4 is stochastic (3/3 and 2/3), and at T=0 top_p is a strict no-op for maskgit_plus. Publish the resulting map of DEGENERATE cells. This map is itself the most defensible contribution available here, and it is what CaRE and FVA both lack: not "protocol matters" (dLLM 2602.22661 already said that) but "large regions of the protocol grid that papers report as distinct configurations are provably identical, and the axes are not orthogonal because top_p is applied after temperature scaling."

STEP 3 (~55 GPU-h, LOCAL + .73 via /opt/conda/envs/minillm/bin/python) -- BALANCED FACTORIAL ONLY OVER THE NON-DEGENERATE REGION, ONE MODEL. Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B x temperature {0.2,0.4} x top_p {1.0,0.95,0.9} x alg {maskgit_plus,topk_margin,entropy} x wrapper {chat,--no-chat} = 36 cells x 3 seeds on HumanEval+ (n=164) and MBPP+ (n=378). Use the existing per-GPU sharding pattern from scripts/_run_baselines_r2_wzc1.sh (8 shards by `index % world_size`) and scripts/_merge_rank_solutions.py, but ADD the shard-completeness assertion described under required_control. This gives a real mixed-effects model with a genuinely estimable residual because every retained cell is stochastic.

STEP 4 (0 GPU) -- EXTRACTION-RULE FACTOR, POST-HOC. Use the existing scripts/reextract_dream_solutions.py against every metrics.rank*.jsonl to score {robust fenced-block, naive first-fence, no-extraction} on identical raw_output. Verified free and verified real: naive differs from robust on 20/164 (r1) and 7/164 (r2) raw outputs, and after evalplus grading moves pass@1+ by -4.2pt (r1) vs -0.6pt (r2).
