STEP 5 (optional, ~1 h download + 176 GPU-h) -- ONLY IF THE MODEL-IDENTITY FACTOR IS STILL WANTED. Download apple/DiffuCoder-7B-Instruct (14.2 GiB) and/or GSAI-ML/LLaDA-8B-Instruct (14.9 GiB); both verified reachable through http_proxy=http://hy-proxy.woa.com:3128 (HTTP 200 + safetensors manifests confirmed), and 13 T is free on the wzc1 share. Then replicate Step 3's grid on the new checkpoint to get a 2-level model factor. Be explicit that a 2-level model factor is the exact design flaw the positioning doc criticises in FVA (n=2 same-lineage) and 2607.22949 (n=2 close-capability), so the model-vs-protocol variance RATIO must not be reported as a headline. Do NOT try to include Scaffold or DreamOn in this factorial -- their samplers have no top_p/top_k/alg and Scaffold's temperature is an argmax no-op.

REUSE, DO NOT DUPLICATE: the .82 sampler/decoding audit is already occupying that exact ground -- coordinate before launching Step 3 or the two efforts will collide. The .104 AR baseline supplies the cross-family reference point, and the existing runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe{16..1024} sweep already provides the steps/NFE axis, so steps stays FIXED at 512 in this design.
feas.risk: The most likely outcome is a CONFOUNDED-BY-DEGENERACY result mistaken for a finding. Because top_p is applied AFTER temperature scaling (generation_utils.py:61-64) and the argmax is scale-invariant at T=0, a large fraction of the 576 advertised cells are either byte-identical to a sibling cell or have a structurally zero residual -- I measured both. Fit an ANOVA over that grid and temperature gets a large confident-looking eta^2 while everything else goes to ~0, not because protocol dominates model identity but because temperature is the only axis that changes the effective nucleus width (4/2/1 tokens kept at T=0.1 vs 6091/156/52 at T=0.4) and the only one that switches determinism on. That reproduces CaRE's eta^2=0.91 as an artefact of the implementation rather than a property of the models -- the same error class as the three retractions: a statistic computed over a design whose cells do not mean what the column headers say. The second failure is aggregation: model identity spans .707 (Dream-Coder-Instruct) to .122 (DreamOn) largely because DreamOn is an infilling model measured off its home turf, so any "model identity" variance share is dominated by a task-mismatch artefact and "protocol >= model" can be manufactured or destroyed by choosing which checkpoints enter the pool, with no principled stopping rule. Third and most mundane: the 8-way merge silently drops missing ranks, so one crashed shard yields a quietly wrong pass@1 for a single cell, which surfaces as an inflated interaction term rather than an obvious error.
feas.required_control:
A CELL-VALIDITY PRE-REGISTER, asserted mechanically before any variance component is computed. Concretely, three assertions that must all pass per cell or the cell is excluded and reported as excluded:

(1) NON-DEGENERACY ASSERTION (prevents the analogue of the 'restart' stage that silently discarded its input -- here, a factor level that silently changes nothing). For every pair of cells differing in exactly one factor level, hash the concatenated raw_output. If two cells that the design calls distinct produce identical hashes, that factor level is a no-op in that region and the cell pair is flagged, not averaged. I have already demonstrated this fires: T=0.0/maskgit_plus at top_p 1.0 vs 0.95 gives byte-identical 256-token output, and alg='origin' discards the confidence value entirely so top_p cannot affect ordering at T=0.

(2) ESTIMABLE-RESIDUAL ASSERTION (prevents the analogue of the cost-average that dropped the expensive tasks -- here, computing eta^2 against a residual that is structurally zero for most cells). Require >=3 seeds per retained cell AND require the within-cell output set to contain >=2 distinct outputs. Cells that are deterministic have a zero noise floor and MUST be excluded from any eta^2 denominator rather than silently contributing zero residual. Measured: T=0.0/1.0, T=0.1/0.95 and T=0.2/0.95 all give 1 distinct output across 3 seeds; only T=0.4 cells are stochastic.

(3) SHARD-COMPLETENESS ASSERTION (prevents the analogue of the verifier that compared nothing -- here, a cell graded on a silently truncated sample set). scripts/_merge_rank_solutions.py de-duplicates by task_id and prints a count but never checks it, so a crashed shard yields a short solutions.jsonl that evalplus will happily grade. Assert merged row count == 164 (HumanEval+) or 378 (MBPP+) and assert the task_id set equals the benchmark's, and hard-fail the cell otherwise. Note runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus.r1/ literally contains a solutions.PARTIAL_21of164.jsonl artefact, so this failure mode has already occurred in this repo.

And one provenance control that is specific to how this candidate went wrong: every metrics row must carry the complete resolved argument vector and the git commit hash. This audit could only settle the r1-vs-r2 question because `process.input_tokens` happened to be preserved and let me prove the prompts were identical 164/164; that was luck, not design. Without recorded arg vectors, the next single-vs-two-variable dispute will again be adjudicated by reading git diffs, which is precisely how the false 'prompt path changed' inference entered the positioning doc in the first place.

lens.title: A Negative Result: Bidirectional Context Does Not Buy Repair. Verifier-Localized Canvas Remasking Fails to Beat Regenerate-From-Scratch at Matched Token Cost
lens.claim: The single structural affordance that masked diffusion has and AR does not -- editing arbitrary already-committed positions with full bidirectional context -- does not yield a usable self-repair mechanism on code at matched compute. Specifically, canvas-level remasking of verifier-localized failing spans, re-diffused in place with the rest of the draft intact, does NOT outperform discarding the draft and regenerating from the prompt at equal cumulative model tokens. We predict the mechanism, not just the outcome: the model's conditional distribution given a mostly-correct-but-wrong canvas is sharply peaked on re-committing the SAME wrong tokens (measured as token-level agreement between pre- and post-remask commits), so the surviving draft acts as a self-confirming prior rather than as useful context.
lens.why_now: This is the field's most-cited qualitative argument for diffusion LMs and it is nearly always asserted rather than measured at matched cost. Our own two refinement arms both failed to test it and were retracted: 'restart' discards the draft (so the grid measured Dream-Coder-Instruct, not repair -- each tier's hidden-pass rate on its own routed set matched the tiny run's on the same tasks to within -0.008..-0.023), and 'remask' only splices truncated text back into the PROMPT rather than remasking the canvas. So we have already paid for the wrong experiment twice and know exactly what the right one is. Feasibility is now confirmed by code inspection: the shipped generation_utils.py _sample exposes generation_tokens_hook_func, called both before the loop and after every step with the full canvas x, and the mask is recomputed each iteration as (x == mask_token_id) -- so writing mask_token_id into chosen positions mid-trajectory is genuine in-place canvas remasking, no model surgery required. A credible negative result here is more useful to the field than another method that quietly measures the wrong thing.
lens.experiment: Four arms at MATCHED cumulative model tokens (proc() accessor, budget-truncated tasks included), Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, HumanEval+ and MBPP+, evalplus untrusted_check as the verifier (with expected-value comparison -- the fix from Retraction 1). Arm A regenerate-from-prompt (our corrected 'restart' upper-ish baseline). Arm B canvas remask, verifier-localized: map the failing traceback/assert to token spans in the canvas, write mask_token_id there via generation_tokens_hook_func, re-diffuse in place. Arm C canvas remask, random spans of identical token count -- the control that separates 'localization is informative' from 'any perturbation helps'. Arm D oracle localization using hidden tests, to bound how much better any localizer could do. Critically, every arm must be compared against the flat upper bound of simply spending the same tokens on Dream-Coder nfe512 directly (HE+ .707 / MBPP+ .680); our best retracted grid number was .624, i.e. below just handing the task to the model once. Mechanism measurement: token-level agreement between pre-remask and post-remask commits in the remasked span, and per-position confidence before vs after, to test the self-confirming-prior explanation. Sweep remask fraction {10,25,50%} and rounds {1,2}. Also run Arm B/C on Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, where typed subtree collapse gives a structurally principled span (the never-implemented 'Arm C' from our own TODO), so the negative result is tested with the most favourable localizer we can build.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: Dream-Coder-Instruct + Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, evalplus grader with the FIXED untrusted_check verifier (commit 67a7a01), scripts/refine_verifier_guided.py harness with --dataset, generation_tokens_hook_func already in the shipped model code (verified), scaffold_coder/decoder_runtime.py exposing remask_leaf/remask_leaves/backtrack_structural_subtree/completed_structural_subtrees for the typed-span variant, cumulative-model-token accounting incl. failure_process. MISSING: the traceback->canvas-token-span localizer (nontrivial: needs char offsets from the failing test mapped through the tokenizer back onto canvas positions); and refine_verifier_guided.py currently does prompt-text splicing, so its remask path must be rewritten to drive the hook. Both are contained code work, no training.
lens.kill_criterion: This candidate is DESIGNED to survive either outcome, but the negative claim is falsified if Arm B beats Arm A by more than ~3 points pass@1+ at matched cumulative model tokens on BOTH benchmarks with a paired bootstrap 95% CI excluding zero, AND beats the flat nfe512 upper bound -- that flips it into a positive method paper. The paper collapses entirely (no publishable claim either way) only if Arm B, Arm C and Arm D are mutually indistinguishable AND all three sit at the Arm A level, since then we cannot distinguish 'repair does not work' from 'our localizer is broken' -- Arm D exists precisely to prevent that ambiguity, so this is the outcome to watch for.
lens.builds_on: Repairs our own Retraction 2 (the 'restart' policy discarded the scaffold draft, so the 4x2 refinement grid measured Dream-Coder-Instruct rather than structural revision, killing two headline findings) and Retraction 1 (verifier never compared return values). Distinguished from training-free confidence-based revision work -- WINO-style post-hoc remasking, CORE (2602.04096, pre-cutoff, context-brittleness probing), and 2606.12232's re-evaluation of confidence remasking -- because our remask trigger is an EXECUTION verifier localizing a failure, not a model-internal confidence signal, and our comparator is regenerate-from-scratch at matched token cost rather than compute-matched confidence baselines. Also distinct from DreamOn (2602.01326) and CAL (2602.00476), which address infilling LENGTH, not verifier-driven repair.

related_work.citation: "Stop the Flip-Flop: Context-Preserving Verification for Fast Revocable Diffusion Decoding" (COVER), arXiv:2602.06161
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 (regular). Verified via OpenReview api2 notes/search: venueid=ICML.cc/2026/Conference, venue='ICML 2026 regular'.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest pre-cutoff work to our mechanism claim. Defines and quantifies 'flip-flop oscillations': a canvas position is remasked and then re-unmasked to EXACTLY THE SAME TOKEN. Reports ~99% of Saber's ReMask operations and ~90% of WINO's are ineffective in this sense, across datasets, on Dream-Ins-7B and LLaDA-Ins-8B, HumanEval/MBPP/GSM8K/MATH500. Also argues explicit remasking weakens the conditioning context for other positions. Proposes COVER (KV-cache-override leave-one-out verification with diagonal self-leakage correction) to avoid ineffective remasks.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Trigger is entirely model-internal (confidence/stability scores). Never tests whether an EXTERNAL execution verifier -- strictly more information than any confidence signal -- escapes the flip-flop. Frames flip-flop as an EFFICIENCY bug to engineer around, never as evidence that repair-by-remasking is capability-limited. No regenerate-from-scratch arm at matched cost. No oracle-localization upper bound. Code is only a benchmark, never the source of the remask signal.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The 99%/90% ineffective-remask statistics are computed only for baselines COVER wants to beat, and only under model-internal triggers -- so the paper cannot distinguish 'remasking is a weak repair primitive' from 'these particular selectors are bad', exactly the confound our Arm D (oracle localization) breaks. (2) The framing flatters COVER: if flip-flops persist even under good localization, its contribution is avoiding a useless action rather than enabling a useful one, and the correct baseline becomes 'spend the budget on a fresh sample' -- an arm they never run. (3) Cost is reported as decoding steps and relative speed, not cumulative model tokens, so their revision budget is not commensurable with a resample budget.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-02-05, v2 2026-05-28); full v2 HTML fetched via corporate proxy and grepped -- the 99%/90% figures and the 'remasked and later restored unchanged' definition are verbatim. Venue verified on OpenReview.

related_work.citation: Zhai, Mollah, Wang, Shah, "CoRe/CORE: Context-Robust Remasking for Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2602.04096
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 (regular). Verified via OpenReview: venueid=ICML.cc/2026/Conference, Submission6230 with Camera_Ready_Revision.
related_work.what_it_covers: Training-free inference-time remasking on LLaDA-8B-Base. Selects revision targets by probing sensitivity to masked-context perturbations ('context-brittle' tokens) rather than static confidence. HumanEval 12.20->17.07 and MBPP 15.60->24.80 greedy pass@1 at N=128, L=512. Crucially ships the control our Arm C proposes: compute-matched 'Random Remask' and 'Margin Remask' at identical revision settings (E=8, m=32) and identical forward passes, both yielding negligible gains (HumanEval 13.41/13.41, MBPP 16.60/17.40). Also reports confidence-based remasking (ReMDM-conf) can DEGRADE code performance.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No arm spending the same compute regenerating from the prompt, so 'CoRe beats compute-matched revision baselines' does not license 'revision beats resampling'. Trigger is model-internal; no execution verifier. Base (non-instruct) LLaDA only, few-shot, greedy, N=128/L=512 -- a heavily compute-constrained regime far from a saturated code model. No oracle localizer, so the localization ceiling is unknown. No pre/post-remask token-agreement measurement.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The missing regenerate-from-scratch arm is a live reviewer objection to their central claim; supplying it is a clean follow-up. (2) 'Up to +9.2% on MBPP' is a max over cells and the framing does not disclose the base is a 15.60 pass@1 model -- gains this size exist only far below the model's ceiling and are unlikely to replicate on a code-specialised instruct model already at .68 MBPP+. (3) Their Random Remask control already establishes the negative half of our Arm C on LLaDA-8B-Base, so we must cite it rather than claim that control as novel. (4) Greedy-only, no sampler-sensitivity control -- material given our measurement that top_p 1.0->0.95 moved HumanEval by 14.6 points.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-02-04, v3 2026-03-13); full v3 HTML fetched via proxy, tables and the 'compute-matched controls' passages read directly. Venue verified on OpenReview.

related_work.citation: "Prism: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Hierarchical Search and Self-Verification for Discrete Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2602.01842
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026. Verified via OpenReview (venueid=ICML.cc/2026/Conference, 'ICML 2026 regular'); arXiv comment also states 'Accepted to ICML 2026'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Closest pre-cutoff work combining a verifier + partial remasking + code + explicit compute accounting. 'Local branching with partial remasking' preserves high-confidence tokens as a logic skeleton and remasks low-confidence positions to explore alternative implementations; Self-Verified Feedback replaces external verifiers with self-evaluation prompts. HumanEval/MBPP/GSM8K/MATH500 on LLaDA-8B-Instruct, Dream-7B-Instruct, LLaDA-2.0-mini, reporting NFE alongside accuracy.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Verifier is the model judging itself, not program execution. Remask targets are confidence-selected, not failure-localized. Comparator is best-of-N, never 'spend the same budget on one fresh trajectory'. No pre/post-remask token-agreement measurement. No oracle-localization bound.
related_work.known_defects: (1) NFE as the cross-arm cost unit is the exact accounting error this project retracted (Retraction 3): NFE ignores how many canvas tokens are re-attended per evaluation, pricing a 512-canvas branch and a short branch identically. (2) Their own Table 1 shows HumanEval 54.88@512 NFE -> 77.44@2048 NFE for plain best-of-4, i.e. headline gains sit where simply spending compute on the base model moves 22 points; remasking's contribution is never isolated from width scaling. (3) 'Preserving high-confidence tokens' is uncontrolled -- no arm randomises the preserved skeleton, so the claim that the skeleton is informative is untested.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-02-02, v3 2026-05-05); full v3 HTML fetched via proxy, Table 1 NFE/accuracy rows read directly. Venue verified on OpenReview.

related_work.citation: Singh, Verbruggen, Le, Gulwani, "Diffusion is a code repair operator and generator", arXiv:2508.11110
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (cs.SE, 12 pages). No journal_ref or venue on the arXiv abs page; OpenReview returns only a DBLP CoRR 2025 shell. Verified by fetching the abs page via proxy.
related_work.what_it_covers: Clearest pre-cutoff statement of the underlying idea: take a broken code snippet, ADD NOISE to it, and resume the diffusion process -- corrupt-and-re-denoise as a last-mile repair operator. Python, Excel and PowerShell, plus a second use generating last-mile-repair training pairs.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Code diffusion models over latent representations, not a masked-diffusion LLM with an explicit [MASK] canvas; noise is added globally/by schedule rather than localized to a verifier-identified span. Targets last-mile syntactic/near-converged breakage, not semantically wrong-but-runnable programs. No matched-cumulative-token comparison against regenerating from the prompt, no EvalPlus-graded pass@1+, no measurement of whether the model re-commits the same tokens.
related_work.known_defects: (1) 'Last-mile' selects the easiest possible repair regime -- snippets already near the model's fixed point -- so the positive result does not transfer to failures needing a semantic change, which is exactly what a unit-test failure identifies. (2) No matched-cost baseline of any kind, so 'diffusion is a repair operator' is never compared to 'just sample again'. (3) Excel/PowerShell programs are very short, conflating repair capability with sequence length.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API + arXiv abs page fetched via proxy (authors, date, subjects, absence of journal_ref confirmed). OpenReview search returned only the DBLP CoRR shell.

related_work.citation: "Try Again, Don't Look Back: Blind Resampling Outperforms Self-Repair in Small Code Models", arXiv:2607.26117
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. No OpenReview record under this title (an unrelated ICML 2026 paper, 'Anchoring Self-Play for Code Repair', surfaced instead). arXiv comment links a GitHub repo with pre-registrations and run traces.
related_work.what_it_covers: The autoregressive twin of our claim, including the mechanism. Placebo-controlled MATCHED-BUDGET comparison on MBPP+ at 1.5B/3B/7B of blind resampling, a content-free failure notice, genuine execution feedback, and feedback+self-reflection. Blind resampling is strongest below 7B and statistically tied at 7B while using 2.5-5.5x fewer tokens; conditioning on the model's own failed attempt costs 6.1 points at 1.5B (p=0.006); execution feedback adds nothing measurable over the placebo. Attributes this to ANCHORING: shown its previous attempt, the model reproduces a near-identical program in 33-68% of retries vs 2-14% under blind resampling. Rules out context-length and cross-task-retrieval explanations, replicates on a second family and at full precision; penalty magnitude predicted by baseline quality alone (r=0.96).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Entirely autoregressive and prompt-mediated: the failed program is SHOWN to the model in context. It therefore cannot separate 'harm from exposure to the wrong tokens' from 'harm from conditioning on the surviving correct context'. Canvas remasking is the only mechanism that dissociates these, because the wrong tokens are deleted rather than displayed. No diffusion, no in-place editing, no bidirectional context.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Concurrent, so it does not preempt us -- but it means a standalone diffusion negative result reads as 'the AR finding again', which is why the exposure-vs-conditioning framing is the version to write. (2) Their anchoring measure is 'near-identical program' at program level; ours is token-level agreement inside a specific remasked span, strictly finer and testable position-by-position. (3) The r=0.96 baseline-quality scaling law is fit over six configurations of 0.5-7B models with baselines far below Dream-Coder-Instruct's .680 MBPP+, so it makes a specific extrapolated prediction at our operating point that they cannot test and we can.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-07-28, abstract read in full). OpenReview searched for the title and for 'Blind Resampling Outperforms Self-Repair' -- no matching submission; treated as preprint.

related_work.citation: "Falsification, Not Exposure: An Internally Preregistered Placebo-Controlled Decomposition of Self-Repair Feedback in Frozen Small Code Models", arXiv:2606.31511
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (39 pages). No OpenReview record found. Self-describes as 'the third stage of a falsification-centered measurement program', apparently the same programme as 2607.26117.
related_work.what_it_covers: Placebo-controlled, matched-output-budget decomposition of the self-repair feedback packet on HumanEval+/MBPP+ with three 0.5B-1.5B frozen models. Introduces the design detail we should copy: restricting to 290 'dead task-cell units' (no best-of-8 candidate passing the public tier) rather than diluting over all tasks. Blind resampling beats bare-code retry by +18 net unlocks (Holm p=0.0021); code-plus-facts beats bare code by +18 and a generic-bullet placebo by +15; code-plus-facts and blind resampling TIE at 26 unlocks each.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Autoregressive, prompt-mediated, 0.5-1.5B only. No diffusion, no canvas, no in-place span editing. Does not test whether structured/localized feedback helps when the failing span is deleted rather than shown.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Model scale 0.5-1.5B; the tie at that scale says little about a 7B code-specialised model at .68 MBPP+. (2) 'Net unlocks' on a dead-task subset is a good denominator but is not pass@1+, so it is not directly comparable to published EvalPlus numbers -- a dual-denominator report would be stronger. (3) Concurrent, so it neither preempts nor is repairable by us; cite as convergent evidence and borrow the dead-task denominator.

related_work.citation: "Revise, Don't Freeze: Sampler-Matched Training for Self-Correcting Masked Diffusion Language Models" (D3IM + SCOPE), arXiv:2606.01026
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (8 pages, 2 figures, 10 tables). OpenReview title search returned nothing.
related_work.what_it_covers: Names and diagnoses our proposed mechanism explicitly: 'preservation bias -- the model tends to reproduce its own wrong committed tokens rather than correct them.' Proposes D3IM, a parameter-free corrector-style sampler permitting direct visible-to-visible revision, and SCOPE, a light post-training procedure simulating D3IM's sampling. LLaDA-8B at 64 steps: +15.3 HumanEval (29.3%), +10.4 MBPP (30.8%).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent, and its remedy is TRAINING (SCOPE post-training), whereas our question is whether the training-free affordance works at all. Trigger is sampler-internal, not an execution verifier. No matched-cumulative-token regenerate-from-prompt comparator; no code-specialised model; operating point (29.3% HumanEval) far below ceiling.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Preservation bias is asserted as a model-side obstacle but never measured as token-level pre/post agreement on identified-wrong spans, so it stays a story rather than a measurement -- our Arm B/C/D agreement measurement is the missing instrument. (2) The +15.3/+10.4 gains are at 64 denoising steps, an aggressively under-stepped regime; the paper does not show they survive where the base model is saturated (our own nfe512->1024 measurement shows exactly zero headroom there). (3) SCOPE changes weights, so comparing to 'original LLaDA-8B with standard unmasking' confounds sampler and training.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-05-31, abstract read in full). OpenReview title search returned no record.

related_work.citation: "Detect, Remask, Repair: Diffusion Editing for Faithful Summarization of Evolving Contexts", arXiv:2606.12807
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (Columbia University authors per HTML). OpenReview title search returned no record.
related_work.what_it_covers: Structurally the same pipeline as our Arm B in a different domain: detect unsupported spans, remask them in a masked diffusion LM, repair in place, explicitly contrasting FULL REGENERATION, which they note 'discards the previous draft'. Baselines: AR Draft (LLaMA-3-8B), Full Regeneration, and DCR (AR detect-critique-refine). Repair models LLaDA-Steering / LLaDA-1step / LLaDA-1step-Distill. Cost as NFE and wall-clock; paired bootstrap over examples with 10,000 resamples for AlignScore.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Summarization faithfulness, not code; verifier is an AlignScore/NLI-style judge with no ground truth. Cost is 'additional refinement cost' (NFE, seconds), NOT matched cumulative model tokens against the regeneration arm -- so 'controllable alternative to full rewriting' is a speed/preservation argument, not an equal-budget quality argument. No random-span control, no oracle-localization bound, no pre/post token-agreement measurement.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The comparison to Full Regeneration is not budget-matched: repair cost is reported as an increment while regeneration pays full price, structurally flattering repair. (2) Minimal-change preservation is part of their objective, so the metric rewards not changing things -- partly measuring the very self-confirming behaviour we treat as the failure mode. (3) StreamSum is synthetic, making span localizability far easier than real traceback-to-span mapping. All three are directly repairable in the code setting where execution gives an unambiguous verifier.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-06-11); full HTML fetched via proxy -- baseline list, cost-accounting sentence, and the 'full regeneration discards the previous draft' framing read verbatim. OpenReview title search returned no record.

related_work.citation: "Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2606.12232
related_work.venue_status: Workshop-only, verified on OpenReview: venueid=ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/SPIGM ('SPIGM @ ICML Poster') AND venueid=ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/AdaptFM ('AdaptFM Poster'), both with Camera_Ready_Revision. No main-conference record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Re-evaluates WINO post-hoc confidence remasking and finds that under standard decoding settings (shorter block lengths) it brings little-to-no benefit over confidence-based unmasking alone; under non-greedy decoding it partially mitigates stochasticity-induced errors while worsening diversity collapse. Concludes benefits are highly setting-dependent.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Confidence remasking only; no external/execution verifier, no code-repair task, no regenerate-from-scratch comparator, no localization oracle. Workshop-scale evaluation.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Only one representative method (WINO) is audited, so the negative conclusion may be WINO-specific. (2) Being workshop-only and confidence-specific, it leaves the strong version -- that no localizer, however good, rescues remasking -- entirely unclaimed, which is precisely the space our Arm D occupies.

related_work.citation: "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2607.24763
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview searches returned only the two workshop records of 2606.12232 and the NeurIPS 2025 ReMDM paper; no CaRE venue record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Directly attacks the evaluation problem our protocol addresses: seven recent remasking papers evaluate under incompatible settings, so their strategy rankings are incomparable. CaRE standardizes ACTUAL NFE, enforces multi-metric reporting, controls stochasticity; applied to 7 remasking strategies x LLaDA-8B-Base/Dream-7B-Base x 4 stochasticity levels x 3 step budgets on OpenWebText and LM1B, plus a 12-model leaderboard (150M-8B). Finds temperature explains most MAUVE variance and that compute-matched comparison REVERSES several published rankings.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Open-domain text (OpenWebText, LM1B) with MAUVE/likelihood metrics -- no execution-graded code task, so no failure localization and no pass/fail verifier. Cost unit is NFE, not cumulative model tokens. Base models only. No regenerate-from-scratch arm.
related_work.known_defects: (1) NFE is the wrong invariant when arms differ in canvas occupancy: two methods at equal NFE can differ severalfold in tokens re-attended -- exactly the class of accounting error this project retracted. A token-level accounting standard is a strict improvement and can be demonstrated on their own strategy set. (2) MAUVE/GenPPL on OpenWebText cannot adjudicate 'did the repair fix the bug', so the protocol is untested on the metric that matters for repair claims. (3) Base-model-only means the leaderboard says nothing about instruct/code-specialised checkpoints where saturation changes the sign of extra compute.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-06-04, abstract read in full). OpenReview title/keyword searches found no venue record; treated as preprint.

related_work.citation: "OSCAR: Orchestrated Self-verification and Cross-path Refinement", arXiv:2604.01624
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview record exists only as venueid=OpenReview.net/Public_Article, venue='CoRR 2026' -- a preprint shell, not a conference acceptance.
related_work.what_it_covers: Formulates 'commitment uncertainty localization' for dLLMs: N parallel denoising chains with randomized reveal orders, cross-chain Shannon entropy to detect unreliable commitments, then TARGETED REMASKING conditioned on retrieved evidence. Introduces trajectory-level assessments including a cross-chain divergence-at-hallucination metric. LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B on TriviaQA, HotpotQA, RAGTruth, CommonsenseQA; ablations claim localization and correction contribute complementary gains.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Factuality/hallucination, not code correctness; localizer is model-internal cross-chain entropy, not an execution verifier; correction is conditioned on RETRIEVED EVIDENCE, so new external information enters at repair time. No oracle localizer, no matched-cumulative-token regenerate arm, no code benchmarks.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Because repair injects retrieved evidence, the design cannot attribute gains to the remasking affordance versus the new information -- the ablation separates localization from correction but not correction from retrieval. (2) N parallel chains at 4/8/16 multiplies compute; gains are not reported against simply drawing N samples and voting at matched cost. (3) Claims dLLMs have 'an inherent capacity to identify factual uncertainty not present in AR models' without an AR baseline given equivalent N-sample entropy access.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-04-02, abstract read in full). OpenReview: only a Public_Article/CoRR 2026 shell, so preprint.

related_work.citation: "Don't Settle Too Early: Self-Reflective Remasking for Diffusion Language Models" (RemeDi), arXiv:2509.23653
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster. Verified on OpenReview: venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, venue='ICLR 2026 Poster'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Makes remasking a first-class trained mechanism: jointly predicts token distributions and per-token confidence, remasks low-quality tokens, trained via SFT plus RL over full trajectories. Claims SOTA among open-source DLMs on multiple datasets.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Requires training; trigger is a learned internal confidence head, not an execution verifier. No code-repair-at-matched-token-cost comparison; no regenerate-from-prompt arm; no oracle localization bound.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Because remasking ability is trained in, RemeDi cannot answer whether the affordance is usable in the shipped training-free checkpoints everyone deploys -- our regime. (2) SFT+RL confounds 'remasking helps' with 'more training helps'; there is no control trained identically without the remask objective. (3) 'SOTA among open-source DLMs' is a leaderboard claim, not a matched-compute claim.

related_work.citation: "Wide-In, Narrow-Out: Revokable Decoding for Efficient and Effective DLLMs" (WINO), arXiv:2507.18578
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster. Verified on OpenReview: venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, 'ICLR 2026 Poster' (also NeurIPS 2025 ER Workshop Spotlight, plus a DBLP CoRR 2025 shell).
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical training-free revokable-decoding baseline: aggressively draft many tokens, verify with bidirectional global context, re-mask unreliable ones for later refinement. LLaDA/MMaDA; GSM8K 6x speedup with +2.58 accuracy.

related_work.citation: "Remask, Don't Replace: Token-to-Mask Refinement in Diffusion Large Language Models", arXiv:2604.18738 (supersedes withdrawn arXiv:2605.26436, 'Targeted Remasking')
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview title search returned only RemeDi, no venue record for this paper. The earlier 2605.26436 carries an explicit withdrawal comment redirecting to 2604.18738.
related_work.what_it_covers: Argues the repair PRIMITIVE matters: LLaDA2.1's Token-to-Token editing overwrites suspect committed tokens, which under polluted context can propagate the error; Token-to-Mask (T2M) instead resets them to [MASK] so mask-filling re-predicts from cleaner context. Training-free drop-in. +13.33 on AIME 2025, +8.56 on CMATH. The superseded version reports 12 benchmarks including coding, and that T2M repairs 59.4% of 'last-mile token corruption' cases on CMATH.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Detection is probability/trigger/temporal-difference based, never execution-based. Math-dominant; code cells are not execution-localized. No regenerate-from-scratch-at-matched-cost arm. No agreement measurement between pre- and post-remask commits.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The theoretical claim that remasking 'purifies context' and converts systematic errors back to native mask noise is asserted, not measured against the counter-hypothesis that the surviving context re-imposes the same token -- exactly what COVER's flip-flop data suggests. (2) Headline gains are on AIME/CMATH where a single final-answer token dominates the metric ('last-mile token corruption'), the most favourable case for span-local repair; generalisation to multi-line program semantics is untested. (3) Version churn (an earlier version withdrawn as superseded) means the 12-benchmark coding numbers should be re-derived, not cited from the withdrawn draft.

related_work.citation: "BackPlay: Head-Only Look-Back Self-Correction for Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2601.06428
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview search surfaced a different title ('Teach Diffusion Language Models to Learn from Their Own Mistakes', venueid=OpenReview.net/Public_Article, CoRR 2026), so no verified conference venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: Frozen-backbone self-correction: trains only a lightweight correction head on a finetuned DLM, using errors from the same frozen generator so the head's training distribution matches deployment. 'Look-back Correction' injects predictions from earlier corrupted denoising states into later richer contexts. At inference, periodically revisits earlier tokens via selective remasking and regeneration. Reports improved speed-quality tradeoff on math and code under multi-token decoding.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Needs training (a head); signal is learned, not execution-based; framed as mitigating parallel-decoding error accumulation, not repairing a semantically wrong finished program. No matched-token regenerate arm.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Gains are demonstrated under 'aggressive multi-token decoding', a deliberately degraded operating point -- the improvement may be recovering self-inflicted damage rather than adding capability, and there is no arm at the model's own best quality. (2) A trained corrector cannot separate 'bidirectional editing is useful' from 'an extra learned module is useful'; the missing control is the same head trained without the remask/look-back structure.

related_work.citation: "Speculative Refinement: A Hybrid Autoregressive Diffusion Decoding Strategy and Its Behavior Across Benchmarks", arXiv:2606.27474
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview title search returned no record.
related_work.what_it_covers: Warm-starts a masked diffusion LM from an AR draft via entropy-guided selective masking -- i.e. remask-and-re-diffuse an existing draft -- across HumanEval, MBPP, GSM8K, BBH, ARC-C, HellaSwag under three evaluation protocols. Four findings bear on our design: (1) code benchmarks conflate structural discovery with logical correctness -- a syntactic scaffold lifts accuracy from near zero to over 20% with no model change; (2) a 'refinement tension' where multi-stage correction DEGRADES already-correct tokens; (3) log-likelihood and generative evaluation rank the same model pair differently; (4) standard Python post-processing silently breaks code evaluation for non-AR generators.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Masking is entropy-guided, not verifier-localized; the draft comes from a different (AR) model, so it is not self-repair; no matched-cumulative-token regenerate arm; refinement tension is qualitative rather than a token-level agreement/degradation rate.
related_work.known_defects: (1) 'Refinement tension' is exactly half of our mechanism claim (repair damages what was right) but is left as a phenomenon without an instrument or a control separating it from sampler noise. (2) Its finding (4) -- post-processing silently breaking non-AR code eval -- is an unquantified warning; our own measured unparseable-output rate falling 94%->1.8% across the NFE sweep shows this confound is large and budget-dependent. (3) Concurrent, so convergent evidence rather than something we repair.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-06-25, abstract read in full). OpenReview title search returned no record.

related_work.citation: Olausson, Inala, Wang, Gao, Solar-Lezama, "Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?", arXiv:2306.09896
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2024 poster. Verified on OpenReview: venueid=ICLR.cc/2024/Conference, venue='ICLR 2024 poster'.
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical prior negative-leaning result on cost-accounted self-repair: on HumanEval and APPS with Code Llama, GPT-3.5 and GPT-4, once the cost of carrying out repair is taken into account, gains are often modest, vary a lot across data subsets, and are sometimes absent. related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Autoregressive, prompt-mediated repair with natural-language self-critique; no diffusion, no canvas, no in-place span editing, no execution-localized token spans. Its 'stronger feedback helps' result identifies FEEDBACK as the bottleneck; it never holds feedback quality at oracle while varying the edit mechanism.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Cost accounting is AR token-count based, and 'matched' is approximate rather than a paired equal-budget design with CIs. (2) Its diagnosis (bad self-critique is the bottleneck) is now in tension with concurrent AR results (2607.26117: execution feedback adds nothing over a content-free placebo), so the field still has not isolated feedback quality from edit mechanism -- exactly what our Arm B vs Arm D vs Arm A triangle does. (3) API models, so unreproducible weights.

related_work.citation: "Locally Confident, Globally Stuck: The Quality-Exploration Dilemma in Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2604.00375

diff.differentiation_statement: No paper before 2026-05-07 asks whether an EXECUTION verifier's failure localization, used to remask spans of a masked-diffusion canvas in place, beats discarding the draft and regenerating from the prompt at matched CUMULATIVE MODEL TOKENS. The remasking literature is uniformly triggered by model-internal signals -- confidence (WINO, ReMDM, 2606.12232), context-brittleness (CoRe, ICML 2026), cross-chain entropy (OSCAR), learned quality heads (RemeDi, BackPlay), or self-evaluation prompts (Prism, ICML 2026) -- and its comparators are other remasking selectors or best-of-N, never "spend the identical token budget on a fresh sample." The two papers that do run that comparator, and that report our exact mechanism (a model shown its failed attempt reproduces a near-identical program in 33-68% of retries), are autoregressive, prompt-mediated, at 0.5-7B, and both first public after the concurrency cutoff (arXiv:2607.26117, 2026-07-28; arXiv:2606.31511, 2026-06-30). That gap is not cosmetic, and it is what makes the experiment decisive rather than confirmatory: in AR self-repair the wrong tokens are SHOWN to the model in context, so "anchoring" cannot be separated from "exposure." Canvas remasking is the only mechanism that dissociates them, because the failing tokens are literally deleted and replaced by [MASK] while the surrounding draft is preserved. If the model re-commits the same wrong tokens even when they have been erased, the harm lives in the surviving correct context acting as a self-confirming prior, not in exposure to the failure -- a claim no existing paper is positioned to make. Second, we hold the localizer at ORACLE (Arm D, hidden tests), bounding how much any localizer could achieve; every existing remasking paper varies the selector and therefore cannot distinguish "remasking is a weak primitive" from "this selector is bad." Third, our cost unit is cumulative model tokens including budget-truncated tasks, not NFE or decoding steps; CaRE (concurrent) standardizes NFE, but NFE prices a 512-token canvas and a short canvas identically, and our own retracted result understated a method's cost by 2.85-3.69x through exactly this error class. Fourth, the setting is a code-SPECIALISED instruct model at the top of its curve (Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B, HumanEval+ .707 / MBPP+ .680, with a measured zero gain from nfe512 to nfe1024), whereas the remasking literature operates on LLaDA/Dream base checkpoints at 12-33% pass@1 where large gains are cheaply available; a saturated ceiling makes "beats just handing the task to the model once" a crisp falsifiable bar rather than rhetoric. Fifth, the Scaffold-v0 typed-AST variant gives a structurally principled span (subtree collapse) that no published localizer can express.

followup_openings.target_paper: "Stop the Flip-Flop: Context-Preserving Verification for Fast Revocable Diffusion Decoding" (COVER), arXiv:2602.06161, ICML 2026
followup_openings.defect: COVER measures that ~99% of Saber's and ~90% of WINO's ReMask operations are 'ineffective' -- the position is remasked then re-unmasked to exactly the same token -- but treats this purely as an efficiency bug (wasted revision budget, weakened drafting context) to engineer around with better seed selection. Because every trigger it studies is model-internal confidence/stability, the paper cannot distinguish 'remasking is a weak repair primitive' from 'these selectors pick the wrong positions'. It also never runs an arm that spends the revision budget on a fresh sample instead.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run the flip-flop measurement with the trigger replaced by information COVER cannot access: an execution verifier's failure localization (Arm B) and, decisively, an oracle localizer from hidden tests (Arm D). Report token-level agreement between pre- and post-remask commits inside the remasked span, plus per-position confidence before vs after. If the ineffective-remask rate stays high even under ORACLE localization, the flip-flop is a property of the conditional distribution given a mostly-correct canvas, not of selector quality -- which reframes COVER's contribution as avoiding a useless action rather than enabling a useful one, and installs 'resample at matched cumulative tokens' (our Arm A) as the correct baseline for the whole revocable-decoding line. Add the random-span control (Arm C) at identical remasked token count to price the perturbation itself.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This converts our negative result from 'one more selector did not work' into a claim about the limit of the entire localization axis, anchored to a pre-cutoff ICML measurement the field already accepts. It is also the cheapest framing: COVER supplies the metric definition and the baseline numbers, so our contribution is the trigger upgrade and the missing comparator, not new instrumentation.

followup_openings.target_paper: "CoRe/CORE: Context-Robust Remasking for Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2602.04096, ICML 2026
followup_openings.defect: CoRe's fairness argument rests on two compute-matched controls -- Random Remask and Margin Remask -- both alternative model-internal selectors. There is no arm spending the same forward passes regenerating from the prompt. So 'CoRe outperforms compute-matched baselines' establishes only that CoRe is the best REVISION policy, not that revision is worth doing. Additionally the operating point is LLaDA-8B-Base at HumanEval 12.20 / MBPP 15.60 pass@1 under N=128, L=512 greedy, far below any code model's ceiling, with no sampler-sensitivity control.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the missing arm in their own setting: add regenerate-from-prompt at matched cumulative model tokens to the HumanEval/MBPP comparison and report the joint frontier. Then replicate on a saturated code-specialised instruct model (Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B at .707/.680) to test whether the +9.2 MBPP gain is a property of context-brittleness detection or of a low baseline -- their own data plus our measured nfe512->nfe1024 zero-gain result predicts the latter. Include a sampler control (top_p 1.0 vs 0.95), since we measured a 14.6-point HumanEval swing from that knob alone, larger than their headline effect.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It repairs a specific, nameable hole in an ICML 2026 paper's central claim using an arm we must run anyway, and turns the 'does this replicate at another scale/family?' reviewer question into our result rather than our vulnerability. Note honestly that their Random Remask control already establishes the negative half of our Arm C on LLaDA-8B-Base -- so Arm C must be cited as replication-and-extension, not a novel control.

followup_openings.target_paper: "Prism: Efficient Test-Time Scaling ... for Discrete Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2602.01842, ICML 2026 (and "CaRE", arXiv:2607.24763, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Prism prices everything in NFE and CaRE proposes standardizing 'actual NFE' as the field-wide compute invariant. NFE is not comparable across arms whose canvases differ in occupancy: one function evaluation over a 512-token canvas re-attends far more tokens than one over a short canvas, so two arms at equal NFE can differ severalfold in real compute. Prism's headline is further confounded because its own Table 1 shows plain best-of-4 moving HumanEval 54.88@512 NFE -> 77.44@2048 NFE, i.e. most available gain is width scaling, and its 'preserve high-confidence tokens as a logic skeleton' step has no randomised-skeleton control.
followup_openings.our_fix: Publish the accounting itself as a contribution: cumulative-model-token accounting including budget-truncated tasks (read via proc() OR failure_process), applied to a matched four-arm design, and demonstrate on a shared benchmark that NFE-matched and token-matched rankings disagree. This project has already been burned by exactly this: a cost was understated 2.85x (HumanEval+) and 3.69x (MBPP+) by silently dropping the most expensive, budget-truncated tasks. Add the randomised-skeleton control Prism lacks (our Arm C generalises to it).
followup_openings.why_it_matters: CaRE is concurrent, so we are not scooped on the protocol concern; we can position as an independent, execution-graded instantiation of it that additionally shows NFE is the wrong invariant. A protocol result travels further than a single negative finding and is defensible even if all four arms tie.

followup_openings.target_paper: "Try Again, Don't Look Back: Blind Resampling Outperforms Self-Repair in Small Code Models", arXiv:2607.26117 (concurrent) and "Falsification, Not Exposure", arXiv:2606.31511 (concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Both are prompt-mediated and autoregressive: the failed program sits in the context window. They therefore cannot separate the two candidate causes of the anchoring penalty -- being EXPOSED to the wrong tokens versus being CONDITIONED on the surviving correct context. 2607.26117 tries to localize this (retrieved solutions to other tasks change nothing, bounding the effect to self-conditioning rather than context length), but the wrong tokens remain visible in every condition. Both are also 0.5-7B with baselines well below our operating point, and 2607.26117's anchoring-cost scaling law (magnitude predicted by baseline quality alone, r=0.96) is fit entirely in that low-baseline range.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the one experiment that dissociates exposure from conditioning: canvas remasking DELETES the wrong tokens (writes mask_token_id) while preserving the rest of the draft. Measure program-level near-identity (their unit) AND token-level agreement inside the remasked span (finer). Two clean outcomes: if anchoring survives deletion, the AR papers' 'do not look back' prescription is insufficient because the harm is in the surviving context, not exposure -- a strictly stronger, more general claim than theirs. If anchoring vanishes, diffusion has a real repair affordance AR lacks and the candidate flips to a positive method paper. Separately, use Dream-Coder-Instruct at .707/.680 to test their r=0.96 baseline-quality extrapolation at a point they could not reach.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Concurrency means these papers cite as convergent evidence, not prior art, and their existence raises rather than lowers our value: they establish the phenomenon on the AR side, and we own the only architecture that can decompose it. This reframing -- exposure vs conditioning, adjudicated by the one mechanism that can delete rather than display -- is the sharpest sentence available for the paper and is nobody's yet.

followup_openings.target_paper: "Detect, Remask, Repair: Diffusion Editing for Faithful Summarization of Evolving Contexts", arXiv:2606.12807 (concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Structurally the same pipeline as our Arm B (detect span, remask, repair in place, contrast with full regeneration) but the comparison is not budget-matched: repair cost is reported as an INCREMENT ('repair time reports additional refinement cost') while Full Regeneration pays full price -- a convention that structurally flatters repair. The verifier is an AlignScore/NLI-style judge with no ground truth, and minimal-change preservation is part of the objective, so the metric partly rewards the very not-changing-things behaviour we treat as the failure mode. StreamSum is synthetic, making span localization far easier than real traceback-to-span mapping. No random-span control and no oracle-localization bound.
followup_openings.our_fix: Port the design to a domain with an unambiguous verifier (program execution, EvalPlus untrusted_check with expected-value comparison), price both arms in the SAME unit (cumulative model tokens, truncated tasks included) so the increment convention cannot flatter repair, and add the two controls they lack: random spans at identical token count, and oracle localization. Report success as pass/fail rather than a similarity metric gameable by preservation.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It demonstrates the negative result is not domain-specific hand-waving but the outcome of removing three specific advantages the summarization instantiation grants itself. It also inoculates us against 'but localized diffusion repair works in summarization' by naming exactly which design choices do the work.

followup_openings.target_paper: "Speculative Refinement...", arXiv:2606.27474 (concurrent), plus our own measured unparseable-output rate
followup_openings.defect: 2606.27474 reports, without quantification, that 'standard Python post-processing silently breaks code evaluation for non-AR generators', and separately that code benchmarks conflate structural discovery with logical correctness -- a syntactic scaffold alone lifts accuracy from near zero to over 20% with no model change. Our own NFE sweep independently shows unparseable-output rate falling 94%->1.8% (HumanEval+) and 89%->1.6% (MBPP+) across the budget range. Together these mean any diffusion repair result measured across differing token budgets is partly an EXTRACTION artifact, and no remasking paper audits this.
followup_openings.our_fix: Ship a mandatory extraction audit as part of the protocol: report, per arm and per budget, the parse-failure rate and pass@1+ under at least two extraction policies, so a reviewer can see how much of any arm difference is code-extraction rather than code-correctness. Because our four arms differ in canvas state and token spend, this is not optional hygiene -- it is a confound that can manufacture or erase the entire effect. Additionally report the headline on the CONDITIONAL set (tasks failing at nfe512) with an explicit dead-task denominator, following 2606.31511's 290-dead-unit design, alongside full-set pass@1+; averaging a repair effect over 164 tasks of which ~71% already pass dilutes it roughly 3x.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the difference between a negative result reviewers believe and one they suspect. Given this project's three retractions all stemmed from measurement conventions (a verifier ignoring return values, a policy discarding the object of study, an average dropping the expensive tasks), pre-committing the extraction audit and the conditional denominator is the cheapest available insurance and is itself citable methodology.

followup_openings.target_paper: "DreamOn: Diffusion Language Models For Code Infilling Beyond Fixed-size Canvas", arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026
followup_openings.defect: Not a competitor but an unaddressed threat to our claim's validity. DreamOn establishes that a fixed-size canvas materially degrades infilling when hole size mismatches ideal completion length. Our Arm B remasks N positions and re-diffuses in place, which is length-PRESERVING: a repair needing more (or fewer) tokens than the failing span is unreachable by construction. A reviewer can then attribute our negative result to canvas geometry rather than repair capability.
followup_openings.our_fix: Add a length-elastic variant of Arm B using DreamOn-v0-7B's expansion/contraction states (or, more cheaply, sweep the remasked span to be strictly larger than the localized failing span -- the {10,25,50%} fraction sweep partially does this, so state explicitly that the largest fraction over-provisions length relative to every localized span). Report whether the repair-vs-regenerate gap narrows as the span is over-provisioned. This also finally evaluates DreamOn on a task adjacent to its home turf, addressing our self-diagnosed failure of never testing it on infilling-like settings.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It closes the single most likely reviewer objection to a negative result, using an asset already on disk. If the gap does NOT narrow with over-provisioned spans, the negative claim becomes much harder to dismiss; if it does narrow, we have found a real and publishable boundary condition instead of a null.

diff.sharpened_claim: In masked diffusion code models, in-place canvas remasking of an execution-verifier-localized failing span does not beat discarding the draft and regenerating from the prompt at matched cumulative model tokens -- and it fails for a reason invariant to localizer quality. We hold the localizer at oracle (hidden tests) to bound what any localizer could achieve, and measure token-level agreement between pre- and post-remask commits inside the remasked span: the model re-commits the same wrong tokens at a high rate even when those tokens have been DELETED and replaced by [MASK], not merely shown. This is the decisive experiment that the concurrent autoregressive results (arXiv:2607.26117, 2026-07-28; arXiv:2606.31511, 2026-06-30) structurally cannot run, because in prompt-mediated self-repair the failed attempt is always visible: canvas remasking is the only mechanism that dissociates "harm from exposure to the wrong tokens" from "harm from conditioning on the surviving correct context." If anchoring survives deletion, the anchoring penalty is a property of the conditional distribution given a mostly-correct canvas -- a self-confirming prior -- and "do not look back" is an insufficient prescription. This also completes two pre-cutoff ICML 2026 papers on their own terms: COVER (arXiv:2602.06161) measured that 90-99% of remask operations restore the identical token but framed it as a wasted-budget efficiency bug under model-internal triggers, and CoRe (arXiv:2602.04096) compute-matched its remasking only against other remasking selectors, never against regenerating from the prompt. We supply the missing arm and the missing oracle bound, in a code-specialised instruct model at its saturated ceiling (Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B, HumanEval+ .707 / MBPP+ .680 with exactly zero gain from nfe512 to nfe1024) rather than at the 12-33% pass@1 operating points where the remasking literature harvests its gains, priced in cumulative model tokens including budget-truncated tasks rather than NFE, with a pre-committed code-extraction audit and a dead-task conditional denominator reported alongside full-set pass@1+.

feas.risk: The most likely outcome is a CONFOUNDED null that reads as a methods failure, not a finding -- and it is confounded three ways at once, all of which I confirmed empirically rather than predicted. (1) Arm B's localizer hits the gold bug line 1.8% of the time (155/164 failures are bare AssertionError naming the test line, not the code), so any Arm B null is "our localizer is chance" and the paper cannot claim anything about repair. (2) Arm B is length-preserving while 100% of the model's own failing drafts need a length change (mean +13.6 tokens) and the oracle span covers 63.6% of the draft -- so a null is attributable to canvas geometry and span non-locality, exactly the DreamOn objection, and "remask 50%" is no longer localized repair but disguised regeneration, collapsing Arm B into Arm A and making the comparison vacuous. (3) The stated mechanism is already false: agreement is 0.298-0.362, not "sharply peaked," and oracle-localized remask repairs 70% of length-preserving injected bugs. So the paper would ship a null whose stated explanation its own instrument contradicts. The second, subtler risk is a Retraction-6 of the exact Retraction-4 shape: proving "regenerate beats repair" strictly WITHIN the diffusion family while a matched AR model does prompt-mediated repair better and 1719-3062x cheaper in tokens_fed, so the whole comparison sits inside a family that AR already dominates -- which is the failure mode this project has now committed twice (R4 from-scratch, R5 infilling) and which the candidate's framing sentence ("the single structural affordance AR does not have") reasserts despite R5 having measured the suffix-context gain at +.231 for AR vs +.299 for diffusion.
feas.required_control:
A PRE-REGISTERED LOCALIZER-AND-REACHABILITY GATE, run and reported BEFORE any arm is compared, with the paper's claim conditioned on it. Concretely, three numbers per benchmark, published as Table 1 whatever they say: (a) localizer accuracy at three levels -- traceback (measured 1.8% gold-line hit), SBFL/Ochiai (upper bound for a deployable localizer; its harness currently HANGS and must be subprocess-timeout-bounded first), and oracle-from-hidden-tests; (b) span geometry on the ACTUAL arm inputs -- oracle span as a fraction of the draft (measured 63.6% on own drafts vs 6.7% on injected HumanEvalPack bugs) and the fraction of repairs reachable without a length change (measured 44.5% on HumanEvalPack, 0% on own drafts); (c) token-level agreement inside the deleted span with the full-canvas-remask arm as its own control (measured 0.298 / 0.362).

Why this is the control that prevents a fourth retraction of the same shape: all three prior retractions were an instrument that silently did not measure the thing it was named for -- a verifier that compared nothing, a "refine" stage that discarded its input, a cost average that dropped the expensive tasks. The analogous failure here is a "verifier-localized remask" arm whose localizer is chance and whose edit operator cannot express the needed repair, producing a clean-looking null that is actually an instrument reporting on itself. (a) proves the localizer localizes, (b) proves the operator can reach the answer, (c) proves the mechanism story before it is asserted. Each is cheap (minutes to ~2 CPU-hours; I produced all three in about 25 GPU-minutes on one idle L20A) and each independently kills the experiment early rather than after the budget is spent. Crucially the gate must be binding: if (a) is at chance and (b) is ~0% reachable, the honest paper is the gate itself -- "execution verifiers cannot localize semantic failures, and saturated code-model failures are not span-local" -- and the four arms become supporting evidence, not the headline. Pair it with the accounting discipline already in the repo: cumulative tokens_fed AND attended_context_sum via proc()/failure_process including budget-truncated tasks, plus a parse-failure/extraction audit per arm and per budget (our own unparseable rate moves 94%->1.8% across the NFE range, large enough to manufacture or erase the whole effect), and both dead-task and full-set denominators (45/48 HE+, 115/121 MBPP+).

lens.title: Attributing the Win: How Much of Open Diffusion-LM Quality Is the Diffusion Objective, and How Much Is the Autoregressive Checkpoint Underneath?
lens.claim: For the open 7B masked-diffusion code models the field benchmarks, most measurable capability is inherited from the autoregressive checkpoint they were adapted from rather than produced by the diffusion objective, and the adaptation is better described as acquiring a decoding interface than acquiring capability. Testable form: (i) the diffusion model's quality ceiling is reached at its FULLY SEQUENTIAL operating point (r=L/T=1.0), so it buys no quality from parallelism, only from a left-to-right-equivalent schedule; (ii) at matched parameters and matched sequential token budget, the AR ancestor matches or beats it on pass@1; (iii) what the diffusion model uniquely gains is order flexibility (infilling, order-robust output formats), which standard from-scratch code benchmarks never measure.
lens.why_now: Nearly every headline diffusion-LM number comes from teacher-initialised adaptation of an AR checkpoint, which muddies what the objective buys -- and we can now show one half of the argument from data already on disk. Dream-Coder's own config.json records an AR-lineage RL provenance path and it is adapted from Qwen2.5-Coder-7B; and our verified NFE grid shows its best HE+/MBPP+ (.707/.680) occurs exactly at r=1.0, with r=0.5 adding precisely 0.0. A 'parallel' model peaking at its sequential setting is the cleanest possible statement of the elephant. A matched AR baseline is also already in flight on .104, which is the control 30+ of our diffusion evals never had. Prior work brackets but does not close this: 2603.22075 (2026-03-23, PRE-cutoff) is a controlled AR-vs-MDLM comparison but only at 50M tokens on TinyStories with diversity/fluency metrics, not 7B code pass@1; 2410.17891 established AR->diffusion adaptation as a method without auditing attribution; 2601.13228 (2026-01-19) and 2601.15165 'The Flexibility Trap' (2026-01-21) argue AR can match or that arbitrary order hurts reasoning, but neither decomposes an ADAPTED checkpoint's quality into inherited vs objective-acquired.
lens.experiment: Three-way matched comparison plus a capability-vs-interface decomposition. Models: Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B and Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B (diffusion, adapted) vs Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct (the AR ancestor family, HF HTTP 200 verified) vs DreamOn-v0-7B. Leg 1 (sequential-ceiling): confirm across models that pass@1+ peaks at r=1.0 and that r<1 adds nothing, on HE+ and MBPP+ -- if the diffusion advantage is parallelism, this should not hold. Leg 2 (matched-budget head-to-head): AR at N generated tokens vs diffusion at T=L=N (r=1.0), compared on pass@1+ AND on honest cost -- AR pays sum over t of (prompt+t) with KV caching, diffusion pays T*(prompt+L) with no reusable cache, which is the accounting that decides whether 'parallel decoding = speed' survives; report both token counts and wall-clock on identical hardware. Leg 3 (where diffusion actually wins): evaluate all models on DreamOn's home turf and on order-flexible surfaces we have never touched -- HumanEval-Infilling / single-line and multi-line FIM, and an answer-before-reasoning output-order stress condition -- where AR must commit prematurely. The prediction is a clean dissociation: AR wins or ties from-scratch generation at matched budget, diffusion wins infilling and order-robustness. Leg 4 (interface not capability): probe whether the adapted model's inherited knowledge is intact but only reachable through the diffusion decoding interface, by comparing its likelihood-based scoring against the AR ancestor's on the same code corpus.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: both Dream-Coder checkpoints, DreamOn-v0-7B, Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, Qwen3 family locally, evalplus + both plus datasets, vendor/Dream-Coder with the official base eval scripts (vendor/Dream-Coder/base/eval_code_base.sh and lm_eval/models/diffllm.py) plus our new --add-bos-token/--base-continuation flags from commit 3cef855, and a matched AR baseline already running on .104. MISSING: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct download (verified reachable, ~15GB); HumanEval-Infilling / FIM harness does not exist in this repo and must be built; and the Base-protocol reproduction is still NOT aligned (our Base HE .085 vs paper .665, 16-task smoke passed only 4/16 parse) -- Leg 1/4 on Base are BLOCKED until that is fixed, which is a real risk to the 'adapted' half of the story. HONEST LIMITATION: we cannot pretrain a 7B masked-diffusion model from scratch, so we can bound attribution by matched comparison and interface probing but cannot fully isolate the objective; the strongest from-scratch leg would need a small-scale (<=1B) matched pair, which our 40 GPUs could do but only at a scale reviewers may discount.
lens.kill_criterion: Falsified if the diffusion models beat the parameter-matched AR ancestor on from-scratch HE+/MBPP+ at matched sequential token budget AND at matched wall-clock -- then adaptation adds real capability and the attribution story dies. Also falsified on Leg 1 if any model's quality keeps improving at r<1 (more steps than canvas positions), since that would mean iterative refinement beyond one-token-per-step does buy quality and 'peaks when sequential' is wrong. Leg 3 is falsified if diffusion does NOT win infilling/order-flexible surfaces, which would leave the paradigm with no measured advantage at all -- a stronger but riskier negative. If Base protocol alignment cannot be fixed, downgrade to Instruct-only and the ceiling drops.
lens.builds_on: Fixes our own self-diagnosed scoping failure of running ZERO autoregressive baselines and evaluating only AR's home turf. Extends 2603.22075 (pre-cutoff, the one genuinely prior controlled AR-vs-MDLM comparison) from 50M-token TinyStories with diversity metrics to 7B execution-graded code with honest KV-cache-aware cost accounting -- their setting cannot speak to adapted 7B checkpoints. Positions against 2601.13228 (AR rivals diffusion at any-order) and 2601.15165 (arbitrary order can hurt), both of which argue about capability but neither of which decomposes an adapted checkpoint's score into inherited vs objective-acquired, nor reports the r=1.0 sequential-ceiling diagnostic.

diff.sharpened_claim: For the open 7B masked-diffusion CODE models the field actually benchmarks, we quantify — rather than assert — how much of execution-graded capability is attributable to the autoregressive ancestor versus the diffusion objective, using the one comparison the literature has never run: Dream-Coder-7B (Base and Instruct) against its own architecture-identical AR ancestor lineage (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B), on EvalPlus pass@1+, under a joint (sequential-token-budget x KV-cache-aware wall-clock) accounting that is comparable across families. Three sharpened sub-claims, each of which repairs a specific defect in existing work: (1) SEQUENTIAL-CEILING, DISENTANGLED FROM SAMPLER: Dream-Coder's HE+/MBPP+ ceiling is reached at T=L (one commit per position) and is not improved by T>L, but we show this is a property of the no-revocation sampler, not of the paradigm — we run the T>L arm WITH remasking/revocation enabled as the control that 2510.19990 and 2601.15593 never separated, so "extra denoising compute buys nothing" is stated only where it survives that control. (2) LINEAGE-PAIRED ATTRIBUTION: at matched parameters and matched sequential token budget the AR ancestor matches or beats the adapted diffusion model on from-scratch code pass@1+, and — the part no prior paper reports — the residual gap is decomposed into an INTERFACE component (recoverable by changing decoding schedule) and a CAPABILITY component (irrecoverable), measured behaviourally, not just representationally as in 2603.07475. (3) COST HONESTY ACROSS FAMILIES: the accounting convention decides the headline. AR pays sum_t (prompt + t) with a reusable KV cache; the diffusion model pays T*(prompt + L) with no reusable cache. We report both, plus wall-clock on identical hardware, and show that any "parallel decoding = speed" claim for these checkpoints is an artefact of counting NFE instead of attended tokens — extending CaRE's within-MDLM NFE standardisation across the AR/diffusion family boundary, which CaRE explicitly does not do.

related_work.citation: Wang et al. (?), "Parallelism and Generation Order in Masked Diffusion Language Models: Limits Today, Potential Tomorrow", arXiv:2601.15593
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v2 2026-04-11). Verified: OpenReview title search returns NO record; DBLP/OpenReview title query for this exact title returns nothing; only arXiv listing exists. No venue claim to check.
related_work.what_it_covers: The single closest paper on the quality side of Leg 1/Leg 2. Eight mainstream MDLMs up to 100B on 58 benchmarks (incl. HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench). Introduces Average Finalization Parallelism (AFP) and Kendall's tau over decoding trajectories. Headline: MDLMs still lag comparably sized AR models; Sec 4.2 'More Parallelism, Lower Accuracy'; peak-precision configs use block size 4 and decode only the top-confidence token per step (i.e. effectively sequential); Sec 4.3 explains it via a Conditional-Total-Correlation lower bound on the factorisation error. Argues for Generate-then-Edit.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No lineage pairing: it compares MDLMs against DIFFERENT-lineage AR models (e.g. Qwen3-next-80B, Qwen2.5-7B-instruct vs LLaDA/Dream/Trado), so 'MDLMs lag AR' conflates the objective with pretraining data, tokenizer, recipe and RL. No adapted-vs-ancestor decomposition. Code numbers are lm-eval-style, not execution-graded pass@1+ on EvalPlus. No wall-clock or KV-cache-aware token accounting — parallelism is measured as AFP (a decoding-trajectory statistic), never converted into attended-token or latency cost. No infilling/FIM leg.
related_work.known_defects: (a) Cross-lineage confound is the big one: the AR reference models are not the ancestors of the diffusion models, so no attribution is possible from their design. (b) AFP is a descriptive statistic of the sampler, not of the model — a confidence-threshold change moves AFP without touching weights, so 'MDLMs adapt their parallelism' is partly a sampler property. (c) The 58-benchmark sweep uses each model's own default decoding, so sampler/temperature/block-size are uncontrolled across rows — exactly the confound CaRE (2607.24763) shows reverses rankings. (d) The CTC bound is a floor on parallel-block error but is never measured, so the theory-to-experiment link is qualitative.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (published 2026-01-22, v2 2026-04-11); full HTML of v2 read for Sec 4.2/4.3, AFP definition and Table 8 model list; OpenReview api2 notes/search returned no matching record.

related_work.citation: (authors n.v.), "A Comparative analysis of Layer-wise Representational Capacity in AR and Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2603.07475
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v4 2026-08-02, comment says 'v4: improving writing and adding Qwen2.5-Instruct results'). Verified: OpenReview api2 title search returns no matching record; no venue claimed in metadata.
related_work.what_it_covers: The closest prior work to our Leg 4, and it uses EXACTLY our three-way design: native AR (Qwen2.5), native dLLM (LLaDA), AR-initialised dLLM (Dream-7B, initialised from Qwen2.5), explicitly 'to isolate whether observed representational properties arise from the diffusion objective itself or are inherited from AR initialization.' Finds diffusion objectives give more global representations, early-layer redundancy, reduced recency bias; and states 'AR-initialized dLLMs retain AR-like dynamics despite diffusion training, revealing persistent initialization bias.' Uses layer-skipping as an intervention: native dLLMs absorb 18.75% FLOPs cut retaining >90%; AR-initialised dLLM ~78% retention at 2-layer skip; native AR ~63%.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Purely representational + a skipping intervention. It never converts 'persistent initialization bias' into a quantity of task capability: no matched-budget pass@1 head-to-head, no execution-graded code metric attributed to inherited vs acquired, no likelihood-scoring comparison against the ancestor on a code corpus, no cost accounting, no infilling. It also uses Dream-7B (general), not Dream-Coder, so the code-specialised post-training (SFT + RLVR) that the field actually benchmarks is untouched.
related_work.known_defects: (a) Cosine similarity across layers is a weak construct for 'representational capacity' — it is scale- and basis-sensitive and does not identify what information is present; a linear/logit-lens probe or activation patching would. (b) Layer-skipping robustness is confounded with residual-stream norm growth and with the fact that diffusion inference does T forward passes, so a skipped layer's error can be re-corrected across steps while AR's cannot — the intervention is not matched across paradigms, which undercuts 'diffusion objectives induce depth redundancy'. (c) Qwen2.5 is the ancestor of Dream but the paper does not exploit the pairing quantitatively (no per-layer ancestor-vs-descendant delta on matched inputs). (d) v4 (2026-08-02) is still adding baseline results, i.e. the comparison set was incomplete for ~5 months.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-03-08, v4 2026-08-02) + full HTML of v4 read for the three-family design statement, initialization-bias claim, and skipping retention numbers; OpenReview api2 search: no record.

related_work.citation: (authors n.v.), "Don't Retrain, Align: Adapting Autoregressive LMs to Diffusion LMs via Representation Alignment" (REPR-ALIGN), arXiv:2605.06885
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (code at github.com/pengzhangzhi/Open-dLLM). Verified: OpenReview api2 title search returns no matching record. First public 2026-05-07T19:35Z, i.e. ON the cutoff date -> concurrent by the stated rule.
related_work.what_it_covers: CONCURRENT but conceptually the nearest statement of our thesis: it hypothesises that 'much of the semantic structure learned by AR pretraining can transfer across generation orders, and thus DLM training should be viewed as relearning the decoding path rather than relearning language representations,' then operationalises it as a per-layer cosine alignment of the DLM's hidden states to a frozen AR model of identical architecture, getting up to 4x training acceleration, strongest in low-data regimes.

related_work.citation: Tang et al., "Is Your Diffusion Sampler Actually Correct? A Sampler-Centric Evaluation of Discrete Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2602.19619
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026. VERIFIED via OpenReview api2: venue='ICML 2026 regular', venueid='ICML.cc/2026/Conference' (plus a CoRR 2026 record). v2 2026-05-27.
related_work.what_it_covers: The theoretical pre-cutoff statement of our sequential ceiling. Builds an oracle framework replacing the learned denoiser with an exact HMM posterior, isolating sampler-induced from denoiser error, and shows 'few-step discrete diffusion samplers are not distributionally correct even under an oracle denoiser, with transition-level mismatch that vanishes only as the number of steps approaches the sequence length.'
