related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Oracle/synthetic Markov-chain setting only. Never touched a real 7B model, never an execution-graded task, no code, no AR ancestor, no wall-clock. So the prediction 'quality peaks only at T=L' is derived but never tested on the checkpoints the field benchmarks — which is precisely the empirical slot our Leg 1 fills.
related_work.known_defects: (a) Ground-truth HMM chains have far weaker long-range token dependence than code, so the quantitative rate at which mismatch vanishes will not transfer; the direction should, the magnitude will not. (b) Distributional correctness is not task correctness — a sampler can be distributionally wrong and still pass unit tests, which their metric set (NLL/GenPPL/MAUVE) cannot see, and they say as much. (c) No treatment of remasking/revocable samplers, where T>L is meaningful; their T->L limit is defined for irrevocable unmasking only.

related_work.citation: (authors n.v.), "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2607.24763
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (comment: 'updated version'). Verified: OpenReview api2 title search returns no CaRE record (returns the different paper 2606.12232 at ICML 2026 workshops). Concurrent.
related_work.what_it_covers: CONCURRENT, and the closest existing work on the cost-accounting axis. Audits 7 remasking strategies on LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base by standardising ACTUAL NFE, enforcing multi-metric reporting and controlling stochasticity, across 4 stochasticity levels and 3 step budgets. (b) MAUVE/GenPPL on OpenWebText cannot detect functional correctness, so 'preserved quality' claims do not transfer to code. (c) Concurrent — we should adopt and extend their protocol and cite it as the precedent for our accounting, which is a strength, not a conflict.

related_work.citation: Gong et al., "DiffuCoder: Understanding and Improving Masked Diffusion Models for Code Generation", arXiv:2506.20639

related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical prior audit of decoding behaviour for 7B diffusion CODE models, and it pre-empts parts of Leg 1's descriptive layer. (c) 'Matches oracle performance achieved with ground-truth length' is the paper's own ceiling, implying the remaining gap to AR is not a length problem. related_work.citation: (authors n.v.), "Thinking Out of Order: When Output Order Stops Reflecting Reasoning Order in Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2601.22035
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. Verified: OpenReview api2 returns only a CoRR 2026 / OpenReview.net/Public_Article record for this title — no conference venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: This PRE-EMPTS Leg 3's 'answer-before-reasoning output-order stress condition' almost exactly, pre-cutoff. Introduces ReasonOrderQA with controlled difficulty and order-level evaluation, plus GSM8K/Math500. When prompts demand answer-before-reasoning, AR models drop up to 67% relative while MDLMs drop <=14% — the property they name 'order robustness'. Mechanism: MDLMs stabilise easy tokens (reasoning steps) earlier than hard ones (final answers). Also identifies failure conditions where the advantage weakens.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Math/QA only — no code, no execution grading, no EvalPlus. No cost accounting (the order-robustness win is quality-only). No lineage-matched ancestor pairing, so it cannot say whether order robustness is objective-acquired or a decoding-schedule artefact. No sequential-ceiling / step sweep.
related_work.known_defects: (a) 'Order robustness' is measured as a relative drop from CoT ordering, so a model with a lower CoT baseline can look more robust by construction — a floor effect that needs an absolute-accuracy control. (b) The AR models are not the diffusion models' ancestors, so architecture, data and instruct-tuning are confounded. (c) ReasonOrderQA is self-introduced and unreplicated. (d) The mechanism (easy-before-hard stabilisation) is a confidence-ordering statement about the sampler, and no revocable-sampler control is reported. IMPLICATION FOR US: our answer-before-reasoning condition must be framed as a code-domain replication + cost extension of this result, not as a new dissociation.

related_work.citation: (authors n.v.), "Autoregressive vs. Masked Diffusion Language Models: A Controlled Comparison", arXiv:2603.22075
related_work.venue_status: Preprint, v1 only. Verified: OpenReview api2 title search returns no record; no venue in arXiv metadata. (The candidate's characterisation of this paper is accurate.)
related_work.what_it_covers: The one genuinely prior controlled AR-vs-MDLM comparison. Identical data (50M tokens TinyStories), identical compute (20k steps, bs 32, seq 512), identical hardware (one H100), isolating the paradigm. Findings: comparable throughput (~50K tok/s, MDLM +4.7% wall-clock); AR converges faster and overfits by step 14k while MDLM is still improving at 20k; a diversity-fluency trade-off (AR fluent but repetitive, 99.8% of samples share an opening).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: 50M tokens, TinyStories, from-scratch pairs, distributional metrics. It cannot speak to (i) 7B scale, (ii) execution-graded code, (iii) ADAPTED checkpoints — its models are both trained from scratch, so the inherited-vs-acquired question is definitionally absent, (iv) KV-cache-aware inference accounting (its wall-clock is TRAINING throughput).
related_work.known_defects: (a) Single seed per arm, single scale, single dataset — the convergence/overfitting claim is one training curve pair. (b) TinyStories has near-trivial long-range dependence, which is exactly the regime where the parallel-factorisation penalty is smallest, so it is the most favourable possible setting for MDLM and generalises poorly upward. (c) '+4.7% wall-clock' is training-side; inference cost, the axis that matters for the parallelism claim, is not measured. (d) Diversity measured by opening-token statistics and MAUVE-like proxies, not by any correctness criterion.

related_work.citation: Gong et al., "Scaling Diffusion Language Models via Adaptation from Autoregressive Models" (DiffuGPT / DiffuLLaMA), arXiv:2410.17891
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2025 Poster. VERIFIED via OpenReview api2: venue='ICLR 2025 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2025/Conference' (plus CoRR 2024). v3 2025-05-31.
related_work.what_it_covers: Establishes AR->diffusion adaptation as the method the whole field now uses (127M-7B, GPT2 and LLaMA), with the objective-connection argument and a continual-pretraining recipe, plus systematic evaluation on LM, reasoning and commonsense benchmarks. It is the reason the attribution question exists.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: By design it argues adaptation WORKS; it never audits how much of the resulting score is inherited. No ancestor-vs-descendant matched-budget head-to-head as an attribution measurement, no sequential-ceiling diagnostic, no code execution grading, no KV-aware cost accounting, no infilling-vs-from-scratch dissociation.
related_work.known_defects: (a) The paper's own framing ('lack fair comparison on language modeling benchmarks') is a fairness complaint it only partially answers — the adapted models are compared to AR models on likelihood-ish benchmarks where the diffusion ELBO is a bound, not an exact likelihood, so cross-family perplexity comparisons are apples-to-oranges. (b) Adaptation-token budget is not amortised into any reported cost, so 'scaling via adaptation' hides the ancestor's entire pretraining bill. (c) Downstream gains are not decomposed against the ancestor at matched decode budget — the single cleanest control, and the gap our Leg 2 fills.

related_work.citation: (authors n.v.), "Answer First, Reason Later: Commitment Order in Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2608.05687 (under review as 'Premature Commitment in Diffusion Language Models', ACL ARR 2026 August)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint + ACL ARR 2026 August Submission. VERIFIED via OpenReview api2: a note titled 'Premature Commitment in Diffusion Language Models' with venue='ACL ARR 2026 August Submission', venueid='aclweb.org/ACL/ARR/2026/August/Submission'. Under review, not accepted. Concurrent (first public one day before our date).
related_work.what_it_covers: CONCURRENT and mechanistically overlapping with Leg 1. Logs every commitment during LLaDA-8B decoding on GSM8K: unconstrained decoding commits the final answer at 15-24% of the trajectory with half the reasoning region still masked, collapsing to answer-only output on up to 90% of problems as the canvas grows. Shows the cause is reachability, not EOS beliefs; a 2x2 prompt-decoder design gives a CoT x ordered-commitment interaction of +34.8pp [26.8, 42.8]; replicates on Dream-7B and MATH-500. Frontier-gated commitment recovers 0.528->0.852 while preserving up to 4x parallel decoding, and the optimal window 'flips from w=1 at full refinement to unconstrained at 8 tokens/step'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Math reasoning; no code execution grading; no AR ancestor; no cross-family cost accounting; no attribution decomposition. Note their w=1-at-full-refinement result is an independent, concurrent instance of 'the ceiling sits at the sequential operating point' — so our version must be quantitatively distinct (code, ancestor-paired, cost-accounted), not merely directional.
related_work.known_defects: (a) Under review, not yet peer-accepted. (b) The 4x-parallel-preservation claim is in tokens/step, not KV-aware attended tokens or wall-clock. (c) Frontier-gating is a sampler constraint, so 'causally recovers the gap' shows the pathology is decoding-side but does not separate objective from initialisation. (d) Concurrent — cite as convergent evidence.

related_work.citation: Ni et al. (?), "Diffusion Language Models are Super Data Learners", arXiv:2511.03276; and Prabhudesai et al. (?), "Diffusion Beats Autoregressive in Data-Constrained Settings", arXiv:2507.15857
related_work.venue_status: 2507.15857: NeurIPS 2025 poster — VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 (venue='NeurIPS 2025 poster', venueid='NeurIPS.cc/2025/Conference'; also a SPIGM@NeurIPS workshop record and CoRR 2025). 2511.03276 (2025-11-05): preprint, no OpenReview record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: The strongest COUNTER-EVIDENCE to our thesis and the paper a reviewer will raise first. Under strictly controlled pretraining, DLMs surpass AR models when unique data is limited and training runs for more epochs (a 'Crossover'), attributed to any-order modelling, super-dense compute from iterative bidirectional denoising, and built-in MC augmentation. A 1.7B DLM on ~1.5T-token compute over 10B unique Python tokens overtakes a strictly-matched AR coder; a 1B DLM exceeds 56% HellaSwag / 33% MMLU from 1B tokens.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Both are FROM-SCRATCH, data-constrained, <=1.7B, and their code result is validation-loss/benchmark-style rather than a matched-decode-budget execution-graded head-to-head. Neither speaks to an ADAPTED 7B checkpoint at inference, nor to the sequential-ceiling diagnostic, nor to KV-aware inference cost. So they show the OBJECTIVE can buy real capability in a data-bound training regime, which is fully compatible with our claim that the released 7B adapted checkpoints, in the compute-bound regime they were made in, do not exhibit that gain at inference.
related_work.known_defects: (a) The regime is data-constrained multi-epoch training — the opposite of the setting Dream-Coder was produced in — so extrapolating 'the objective buys capability' to adapted 7B checkpoints is unlicensed. (b) 'Super-dense compute' means the DLM sees vastly more effective FLOPs per unique token; the crossover is therefore partly a compute-accounting artefact, which is our exact methodological complaint in a different guise. (c) 1.7B ceiling. NOTE FOR US: we must state this scope boundary explicitly or a reviewer will read our claim as contradicted.

related_work.citation: Wang et al. (?), "Diffusion LLMs Can Do Faster-Than-AR Inference via Discrete Diffusion Forcing" (D2F), arXiv:2508.09192

diff.differentiation_statement: Every ingredient of this candidate has a precedent, but no paper — pre- or post-cutoff — assembles them into a lineage-paired, execution-graded, cost-honest attribution of an ADAPTED 7B code diffusion model, and that is precisely the composite a reviewer will accept as new. The sequential ceiling is known qualitatively (2510.19990, pre-cutoff, on LLaDA/math+code), theoretically under an oracle denoiser (2602.19619, ICML 2026, synthetic HMMs, mismatch vanishing only as steps approach sequence length), and descriptively as a parallelism-accuracy monotone across 58 benchmarks (2601.15593, preprint). The persistent influence of AR initialisation is known representationally (2603.07475 states outright that AR-initialised dLLMs retain AR-like dynamics, 'persistent initialization bias'), and the interface-not-capability reading is asserted as a design hypothesis by two concurrent works (2605.06885 on 2026-05-07, 2607.26504). What none of them does is convert any of this into a number attached to a benchmark score. Concretely, ours differs on four axes simultaneously: (i) LINEAGE PAIRING AS AN ATTRIBUTION INSTRUMENT — 2601.15593's headline 'MDLMs lag comparably sized AR models' is confounded because its AR references (Qwen3-next-80B, Qwen2.5-7B-instruct) are not the ancestors of the diffusion models it tests, so its gap mixes objective with data, tokenizer, recipe and RL; we run Dream-Coder-7B against the AR lineage it was actually adapted from at identical architecture (28 layers, hidden 3584, 28 heads / 4 KV heads, vocab 152064 — verified in the local checkpoint's config.json, whose _name_or_path also records the diffusion-RL provenance path), which turns a leaderboard gap into an attributable delta. (ii) EXECUTION GRADING WHERE PRIOR AUDITS USED DISTRIBUTIONAL METRICS — CaRE (concurrent) standardises compute within the MDLM family on OpenWebText/LM1B with MAUVE; 2603.22075 (the one genuinely prior controlled AR-vs-MDLM comparison) uses 50M TinyStories tokens with diversity/fluency; we use evalplus untrusted_check pass@1+ on HumanEval+/MBPP+, where a metric cannot be gamed by fluency. (iii) CROSS-FAMILY COST ACCOUNTING THAT NOBODY HAS PUBLISHED — CaRE explicitly stops at NFE standardisation inside one family; DiffuCoder's '2x speedup from halving timesteps' is a step-count claim; D2F concedes pre-cutoff that no open dLLM beats a same-size AR model on speed and then buys its own 2.5x by reintroducing block-causal attention and a KV cache. We report attended tokens under both conventions (AR: sum_t (prompt+t) with cache reuse; diffusion: T*(prompt+L) with none) alongside wall-clock on identical hardware, which is the accounting that decides whether the paradigm's efficiency claim survives at all. (iv) A SAMPLER CONTROL THE SEQUENTIAL-CEILING LITERATURE OMITS — our own grid shows nfe512 == nfe1024 exactly (.707/.680 both), but with an irrevocable-unmasking sampler T>L is definitionally wasted compute; we therefore run the T>L arm with revocable/remasking decoding enabled, so 'more denoising buys nothing' is asserted only where it survives the control that 2602.19619's oracle result formally does not cover and that 2601.15593 and 2510.19990 never separated from their samplers. We must also concede scope publicly: 2507.15857 (NeurIPS 2025) and 2511.03276 show the diffusion objective DOES buy capability in data-constrained from-scratch training at <=1.7B, so our claim is explicitly indexed to compute-bound, adapted, 7B, inference-time — which is the regime the field's leaderboards actually report.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2601.15593, "Parallelism and Generation Order in Masked Diffusion Language Models: Limits Today, Potential Tomorrow" (2026-01-22, preprint)
followup_openings.defect: Its headline — MDLMs lag comparably sized AR models because parallel factorisation weakens inter-token dependencies — is derived from CROSS-LINEAGE comparisons: the AR references (Qwen3-next-80B, Qwen2.5-7B-instruct, Qwen3-8B) are not the ancestors of the MDLMs tested (LLaDA, Dream, Trado, OpenPangu). The measured gap therefore conflates the diffusion objective with different pretraining data, tokenizer, post-training and RL. Separately, each of the 58 benchmarks is run at each model's own default decoding, so sampler, temperature and block size vary across rows — the exact confound CaRE (2607.24763) shows reverses published rankings.
followup_openings.our_fix: Replace the cross-lineage gap with an ancestor-paired delta: Dream-Coder-7B (Base and Instruct) vs the AR lineage it was adapted from, at identical architecture and matched sequential token budget, with decoding held fixed (temperature, top_p, block size, revocability) across arms and swept as an explicit factor rather than inherited from defaults. Report pass@1+ on HumanEval+/MBPP+ so the metric is execution-graded. This converts 'diffusion lags AR' into 'X points of the adapted model's score are attributable to the ancestor, Y to the objective, Z to the decoding schedule'.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It is the difference between a leaderboard observation and a causal attribution. A reviewer can dismiss 'MDLMs lag AR' as a recipe artefact; an ancestor-paired delta at fixed decoding cannot be dismissed that way, and it retroactively tells the field how to read every adapted-checkpoint number it has published.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2607.24763, CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol (2026-06-04, CONCURRENT)
followup_openings.defect: CaRE correctly identifies that MDLM evaluations conflate algorithmic gains with hidden compute and stochasticity choices, and standardises ACTUAL NFE — but NFE is the wrong unit the moment you cross the AR/diffusion family boundary. One diffusion function evaluation attends prompt+L tokens with no reusable cache; one AR step attends prompt+t with a KV cache. Equating them systematically flatters diffusion. CaRE also never leaves distributional metrics (MAUVE on OpenWebText/LM1B), so nothing in it can detect functional correctness.
followup_openings.our_fix: Extend CaRE's protocol across the family boundary with a KV-cache-aware attended-token unit plus wall-clock on identical hardware, and re-do the comparison on execution-graded code. Publish the same quality number under three accounting conventions (NFE, attended tokens, wall-clock) and show which published orderings flip. This is exactly the error class we already retracted internally (using NFE as a cross-family cost unit), so we can state the failure mode from experience.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Cost accounting is the load-bearing axis of the whole 'diffusion is faster' literature and it is currently un-standardised across families. A protocol that survives family-crossing, with a table of which claims flip, is a reusable contribution independent of whether our attribution thesis holds — and it is the leg with the least existing coverage.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2602.19619, Is Your Diffusion Sampler Actually Correct? (ICML 2026); and arXiv:2510.19990, No Compute Left Behind (2025-10-22)
followup_openings.defect: 2602.19619 proves that few-step samplers are distributionally incorrect even under an ORACLE denoiser, with mismatch vanishing only as steps approach sequence length — but only in a synthetic HMM setting with weak long-range dependence, and only for irrevocable unmasking; it never tests a real 7B model or any correctness-based metric, and explicitly notes NLL/GenPPL/MAUVE gains do not imply correct sampling. 2510.19990 asserts the behavioural counterpart (any-order underperforms or ties left-to-right on math/code) but on LLaDA-8B, a from-scratch model with no AR ancestor, using its own default samplers with no factorial control.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the empirical instantiation neither of them can: a full r = L/T sweep on 7B ADAPTED code models with execution-graded pass@1+, crossed with revocability (irrevocable vs remasking/revocable) and stochasticity, so the T->L convergence prediction is tested where it matters and the T>L arm is not trivially wasted. Our existing grid already brackets it (nfe64 .018/.029 -> nfe256 .555/.545 -> nfe512 .707/.680 -> nfe1024 identical), and unparseable-output rate falling 94%->1.8% across that range gives an independent diagnostic of what the extra steps actually buy: parseability, not logic.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It closes an explicit theory-to-practice gap in an ICML 2026 paper with a measurement on the checkpoints the field benchmarks, and the parseability-vs-correctness decomposition is a genuinely new lens: it reframes 'more steps improve quality' as 'more steps improve syntactic completion', which is an interface story, not a capability story — directly serving the sharpened claim.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2603.07475, Layer-wise Representational Capacity in AR and Diffusion LLMs (2026-03-08, preprint, still adding baselines in v4 on 2026-08-02)
followup_openings.defect: It has the right three-family design (native AR Qwen2.5 / native dLLM LLaDA / AR-initialised Dream-7B) and states the right conclusion ('persistent initialization bias'), but its evidence is layer-wise cosine similarity plus layer-skipping — a weak construct for 'representational capacity' that never quantifies how much TASK capability is inherited. Worse, its central intervention is not matched across paradigms: diffusion inference makes T forward passes, so a skipped layer's error can be re-corrected across denoising steps while AR gets one shot. That alone can explain 'diffusion tolerates skipping, AR collapses' without any objective-induced depth redundancy. It also uses Dream-7B, not Dream-Coder, so the code post-training the field benchmarks is untested.
followup_openings.our_fix: Convert the representational claim into a behavioural one on the code models: per-layer ancestor-vs-descendant deltas on matched inputs, plus likelihood-based scoring of the adapted model against its ancestor on a held-out code corpus, and — the decisive control — repeat the layer-skipping intervention at MATCHED forward-pass count (diffusion restricted to T=1 vs AR's single pass, and AR given T repeated refinement passes) so re-correction is not silently credited to the objective.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: The matched-forward-pass control is a clean, cheap falsification of a published mechanism claim, and it feeds our Leg 4 directly: if the ancestor's knowledge is intact but only reachable through the diffusion interface, that is measurable as a likelihood/probe gap that closes under schedule changes, which is a far stronger statement than a cosine-similarity trend.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2602.01326, DreamOn (ICLR 2026 Poster, 2026-02-01)
followup_openings.defect: It reports infilling QUALITY only, with zero compute or NFE accounting (a gap we independently verified in our own repo audit). And read carefully, its own numbers do not show a diffusion win: HumanEval-Infilling single-line 92.1 vs Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 92.6, SantaCoder-FIM 79.0 vs 79.8 — ties or losses — with a win only on multi-line (63.8 vs 58.7), and only after an additional training intervention on top of Dream-Coder. Coverage is Python-only, with no RandomSpanInfilling and no multi-span.
followup_openings.our_fix: Do NOT claim Leg 3's infilling win; re-frame it as the cost-accounted and regime-extended version: same HumanEval-Infilling / FIM surfaces under our attended-token + wall-clock accounting (does a length-elastic diffusion infiller attend more tokens per completion than an AR FIM model?), extended to multi-span and random-span infilling where AR's single left-to-right pass must be invoked repeatedly and diffusion's bidirectional edit should have a real structural edge.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the honest correction of our own proposal's weakest leg: as written, Leg 3 would have been scooped by a pre-cutoff ICLR 2026 poster. Reframed as cost-accounted multi-span infilling, it becomes the one surface where a genuine diffusion advantage might survive an honest cost audit — which is the strongest possible ending for an otherwise deflationary paper.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2601.22035, Thinking Out of Order (2026-01-29, preprint)
followup_openings.defect: Its 'order robustness' metric is a RELATIVE drop from CoT ordering, so a model with a weaker CoT baseline can appear more robust purely by a floor effect — no absolute-accuracy control is reported. The AR comparators are not the diffusion models' ancestors, so architecture, data and instruct-tuning are confounded. The mechanism (easy tokens stabilise before hard ones) is a property of the confidence-ordering sampler, with no revocable-sampler control. And it is math/QA only, with no cost accounting.
followup_openings.our_fix: Replicate answer-before-reasoning in the CODE domain with (a) absolute pass@1+ reported alongside relative drop to kill the floor effect, (b) the ancestor-paired comparator so order robustness can be attributed rather than merely observed, and (c) cost accounting, since order robustness bought at 10x attended tokens is not obviously a win. Frame explicitly as replication-plus-repair of a pre-cutoff result, not as a new dissociation.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts a leg that would otherwise read as scooped into a targeted methodological repair with a domain extension, and the absolute-vs-relative control is the kind of finding reviewers remember because it can invert a published headline.

followup_openings.target_paper: Our own proposal, skeptic-4 (internal defects to fix before running)
followup_openings.defect: Three self-inflicted risks. (1) The Base-protocol reproduction is NOT aligned (our Base HE .085 vs paper .665; a 16-task smoke passed only 4/16 parse), which means the 'adapted' half of the story is currently unmeasurable on Base — and an unreproduced baseline is exactly the failure mode that produced our three prior retractions. (2) Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is not on either disk, so the single most important control does not exist yet. (3) The claim text says the ceiling is at 'r=L/T=1.0, so it buys no quality from parallelism', but our data shows two distinct things — r>1 (T<L, genuinely parallel) HURTS, and r<1 (T>L, over-refinement) adds exactly 0.0 under an irrevocable sampler where extra steps are definitionally wasted. Conflating those weakens the argument and invites a one-line reviewer rebuttal.
followup_openings.our_fix: Gate the paper on three preconditions in order: fix Base-protocol alignment (or downgrade to Instruct-only and say so in the abstract); download Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and verify the lineage claim from weights/config rather than prose — note the local config.json's _name_or_path records only the diffusion-RL provenance path and does NOT name Qwen, so the ancestry rests on the Dream-Coder paper plus exact architectural identity (28L / 3584 / 28 heads / 4 KV / vocab 152064); and split the r-axis into two separately-stated claims with the revocable-sampler arm run for the r<1 side. Pre-register the kill criteria before the AR baseline on .104 reports.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: The paper's entire value is being the audit that other papers failed to be. A single unreproduced baseline or a conflated axis would make it the fourth retraction rather than the corrective, and the r-axis conflation is the first thing a reviewer who knows the remasking literature will attack.

Concretely: after Step 2 makes wall-clock same-hardware, the table will read "AR is 70x-3000x cheaper in tokens-fed, ~7x faster in wall-clock, and 18 points WORSE on HE+ / 3 points worse on MBPP+" -- i.e. neither family dominates, there is no crossover, and the honest headline is a two-segment Pareto. That is word-for-word the claim structure that was already retracted three weeks of work ago ("structural runtime and flat diffusion own different segments of the frontier"), retracted precisely because a Pareto split is not a contribution when the sides trade off on axes reviewers weigh differently. And the cost half is not news to experts: D2F (2508.09192, pre-cutoff) already concedes in print that "none of the existing open-source dLLMs have achieved superior inference speed over AR LLMs of similar size". So the deflationary result is unsurprising and the attribution result is unavailable -- claim (ii) is refuted at the natural operating point (Dream .707 > Qwen .524 on HE+), and it can only be rescued by cost-matching, which starves diffusion to nfe16/32 where it scores exactly .000/.008. Rescuing the claim by choosing the budget that makes it true is itself the confound. Secondary null risk: Step 3's revocable sampler recovers nothing at T>L (the plausible outcome, since 2606.12232 already reports confidence-based remasking as a null), leaving Step 0's int()-truncation artifact as the only novel finding -- true, cheap, and probably a workshop-sized observation rather than a main-conference paper.
feas.required_control: EFFECTIVE-STEP (COMMITTED-POSITION) ACCOUNTING, ASSERTED PER ARM -- the control against "an arm that appears to run more compute while performing no computation". This is the exact analogue of the three prior retractions: Retraction 1 was a verifier that compared nothing, Retraction 2 was a stage that silently discarded its input, Retraction 3 was an average that dropped the expensive tasks. Here the failure mode is an arm that bills 1024 forward passes while committing tokens on only 510 of them. Implement three assertions, and refuse to publish any step-count claim that fails them: (1) INSTRUMENT: log number_transfer_tokens (generation_utils.py:439) for every step of every task, emit it into the metrics row alongside the existing nfe/generated_tokens/input_tokens fields, and report no_op_step_fraction per arm. (2) ASSERT: sum over steps of committed positions == L exactly, for every task; and require no_op_step_fraction < 0.02 for any arm advertised as "more denoising compute" -- the released nfe1024 arm fails at 0.502 and must therefore be reported as an int()-truncation artifact, never as evidence about the paradigm. (3) DISTINGUISHABILITY: before comparing any two arms, hash their solutions pairwise and assert they are not near-identical. nfe512 vs nfe1024 is 163/164 byte-identical on HE+ with zero pass-flips; a comparison of two arms that emitted the same bytes is not a comparison. Extend the same distinguishability check to the cost axis by keeping the existing ForwardCostTracker cross-check (measured forward-hook counts vs closed-form prediction, currently reporting measured_matches_analytic:true / inconsistent_task_ids:[] over 1084 task-runs) as a hard gate rather than a diagnostic -- and additionally forbid NFE from appearing as a cross-family denominator anywhere in the paper, since one diffusion NFE attends prompt+L with no reusable cache while one AR step attends prompt+t with a cache.

lens.title: What Does a Shipped Diffusion LM Actually Do? Commit-Order Telemetry as a Required Reporting Artifact for Code Generation
lens.claim: The decoding behaviour of shipped open diffusion code LMs is not what their marketing or their benchmark protocol implies, and the discrepancy is measurable and consequential: (i) effective parallelism (mean tokens genuinely committed per step) is far below the nominal L/T at the operating points people report, so 'steps' systematically overstates parallelism; (ii) commit order carries a strong left-to-right bias on code that strengthens as you coarsen the analysis granularity, making any reported 'block size' partly an artifact of the measuring ruler; (iii) commit-time confidence predicts correctness for syntax but not for semantics, so confidence-based schedulers optimize the wrong objective on code. We claim this telemetry changes conclusions, not just decorates them: two models with identical pass@1 can have opposite commit profiles and hence opposite responses to a parallel-decoding speedup.
lens.why_now: Our own instrumentation already shows the field's cost unit is broken in this exact way -- NFE cells at T=1024 have r=L/T=0.5, i.e. HALF the steps cannot commit anything, yet they are reported as 1024 'steps' of compute and priced at 686,080 tokens. If nominal steps can be 2x the ceiling of useful commits, effective parallelism must be reported. This is a strict follow-up opening on a concurrent paper: 'Neither Parallel Nor Sequential: How DiffusionGemma Actually Commits Tokens' (2606.14620, first public 2026-06-12, therefore concurrent) established the granularity-artifact and regime-dependence findings on a SINGLE proprietary-lineage MoE model (DiffusionGemma 26B) over a 686-prompt probe suite, with confidence-vs-correctness measured on math reasoning and factual recall. It does not cover code, does not cover the open 7B checkpoints the field actually benchmarks, does not connect commit telemetry to execution-graded pass@1, and does not cross the canvas-length axis. Feasibility is verified: generation_utils.py _sample exposes generation_tokens_hook_func before the loop and after every step, plus generation_logits_hook_func, and can return full per-step histories (output_history), so per-position commit step and confidence are recordable without touching model weights.
lens.experiment: Instrument the accept step of every checkpoint we have and log, per position: commit step index, confidence at commit, and whether that position's final token survived. Models: Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B, DreamOn-v0-7B, Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, plus one cross-family checkpoint (LLaDA-8B-Instruct or DiffuCoder-7B) so this is not single-model like the concurrent DiffusionGemma study. Surfaces: HumanEval+ and MBPP+ (executable, so telemetry can be regressed against ground-truth correctness), crossed with the (L,T) axis from skeptic-1 so we can show effective parallelism as a function of BOTH. Metrics: (1) effective tokens-committed-per-step vs nominal L/T, exposing wasted steps at r<1; (2) a left-to-right commit-order statistic computed at multiple granularities (token, 4-token, 16-token, line) to replicate-or-refute the granularity artifact on code specifically, where indentation and block structure give a strong prior the concurrent paper's JSON/math regimes lack; (3) AUC of commit confidence for predicting per-token survival, split by syntactic vs semantic failure using our existing syntax-error decomposition (HE+ syntax errors fall 93.9% -> 1.8% across the sweep, giving a clean split); (4) the decision-relevant test: pick two checkpoints matched on pass@1+ and show their commit profiles differ, then apply an identical parallel-decoding speedup to both and show the quality loss differs -- telemetry predicts speedup tolerance where pass@1 does not. Ship the logger and a per-model commit-profile card as the reusable artifact.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: four 7B checkpoints locally, verified hook points (generation_tokens_hook_func / generation_logits_hook_func / output_history) in the shipped generation_utils.py, evalplus for ground-truth per-task correctness, our existing syntax-vs-semantic failure decomposition and the per-step parseability instrumentation already built into the scaffold sampler (SAMPLER_RUNTIME.md records parseability of a placeholder-completed program after every step), 40 GPUs. MISSING: per-position telemetry logging for the Dream path is not written yet (the scaffold runtime has it, the flat path does not); one cross-family checkpoint download; and storage discipline -- full histories for 164+378 tasks x ~22 (L,T) cells x 5 models is large, so log commit events rather than full canvas snapshots (wzc1 has 13T free but is at 90% use).
lens.kill_criterion: Falsified if effective tokens-per-step tracks nominal L/T closely (within ~15%) at all reported operating points -- then 'steps' is an honest parallelism unit and point (i) dies. Point (ii) is falsified if the left-to-right commit statistic is granularity-INVARIANT on code, contradicting the concurrent DiffusionGemma finding and removing the ruler artifact. Point (iii) is falsified if commit confidence has similar AUC for syntactic and semantic survival. The paper loses its teeth if, additionally, pass@1-matched models turn out to have indistinguishable commit profiles AND identical speedup tolerance, since the whole 'telemetry changes conclusions' framing rests on that dissociation -- in that case this degrades to a measurement note rather than a required-reporting argument.
lens.builds_on: Direct follow-up on 'Neither Parallel Nor Sequential' (2606.14620, 2026-06-12, CONCURRENT so not preempting): we vary the axes it holds fixed -- open 7B checkpoints instead of one 26B MoE, executable code instead of math/JSON/factual probes so telemetry can be validated against ground-truth correctness, and the canvas-length axis it does not cross. Complements 2606.00997 (2026-05-31, concurrent) which shows confidence-first reveal orders are near-left-to-right on LLaDA content tokens and proposes reporting confidence variance; we add the execution-grounded syntactic-vs-semantic split and the speedup-tolerance dissociation. Also grounded in our own finding that T=1024 cells have r=0.5, i.e. nominal steps exceeding the useful-commit ceiling by 2x.

related_work.citation: Zhong et al., "Parallelism and Generation Order in Masked Diffusion Language Models: Limits Today, Potential Tomorrow", arXiv:2601.15593 (v1 2026-01-22, v2 2026-04-11)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv listing shows no journal-ref/comments; OpenReview api2 search for the exact title returns no matching note (only unrelated hits), so no verified 2026 venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE MOST DANGEROUS PRE-CUTOFF PAPER for points (i) and (ii). Defines Average Finalization Parallelism AFP = n / T_eff where T_eff = |{t : some position commits at step t}| -- i.e. EXACTLY 'effective tokens genuinely committed per step', with steps that commit nothing excluded by construction. Also adopts Kendall's tau between position index i and finalization step c_i as the left-to-right commit statistic. Evaluates 8 mainstream MDLMs up to 100B (LLaDA, Trado, SDAR, LLaDA2-flash, openPangu-7B-Diffusion) over 58 benchmarks explicitly INCLUDING a code group (HumanEval, MBPP, MultiPL-E, CruxEval-O, LiveCodeBench, BigCodeBench, Spider, CodeForces, SciCode, Aider). Reports AFP and tau split by correct vs incorrect samples: 'correct samples consistently exhibit higher AFP than incorrect ones'; 'High AFP in Code and Agent domains suggests MDLMs effectively capture structural parallelism'; localized tau 'plunges' at semantic pivots and code-to-comment transitions; repetitive/entropy-collapse outputs show AFP 5-7x normal with near-zero tau. Reports AFP alongside TPS as a 'hardware-agnostic speed metric'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Only two analysis granularities (intra-chunk vs inter-chunk), not a systematic bin-size ruler sweep, so it never frames block size as a measuring artifact. Deep analysis is concentrated on ONE model (LLaDA2-flash 100B); the 8-model table reports accuracy + block size, not per-model commit profiles. Correctness linkage is SAMPLE-level (correct vs incorrect trace) not TOKEN-level survival, and never split by syntactic vs semantic failure. Does not cross the canvas-length x step-budget (L,T) plane -- block size is a fixed per-model config, not a swept axis. Does not include Dream-Coder, Dream-Coder-Base, DreamOn, or DiffuCoder -- the open 7B code checkpoints the code-generation literature actually benchmarks. Never reports the T_eff / T_nominal ratio as an accounting-honesty claim even though its own metric computes T_eff.
related_work.known_defects: AFP is presented as a speed metric, not as an indictment of 'steps' as a reported unit -- the paper computes T_eff but never contrasts it with the T that papers report, so the accounting argument is left on the table. Sample-level 'correct samples have higher AFP' is confounded: repetitive/collapsed outputs are excluded into a separate bucket precisely because they distort statistics, and short correct answers vs long incorrect ramblings differ in length, so the AFP-correctness association may be a length artifact with no length control shown. The 100B deep-dive model is a different family from the 7B/8B checkpoints the field benchmarks, so 'MDLMs are adaptive' generalizes on n=1. Kendall's tau is used without a tie-aware correction, yet the paper's own finding is that models commit in large simultaneous batches -- massive ties -- so tau is computed on a statistic whose ties it does not handle (the concurrent DiffusionGemma paper explicitly uses tau_b for this reason).

related_work.citation: Gong et al. (Apple), "DiffuCoder: Understanding and Improving Masked Diffusion Models for Code Generation", arXiv:2506.20639 (v1 2025-06-25); ICLR 2026 Poster
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 /notes/search, which returns the exact title with venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference' (plus a CoRR 2025 DBLP record).
related_work.what_it_covers: THE MOST DANGEROUS PRE-CUTOFF PAPER for point (ii). Introduces local AR-ness@k and global AR-ness@k -- both explicitly SWEPT over k, i.e. a multi-granularity left-to-right commit statistic -- and measures them on zero-shot HumanEval (code) and 8-shot GSM8K (math) for LLaDA (from scratch), Dream, and DiffuCoder, at seq len = timesteps = 512 under low-confidence remasking. Reports exactly the granularity structure the candidate proposes to test: 'Local AR-ness decays as k grows'; 'Global AR-ness is non-decreasing with k'. Finds code has lower mean and higher variance in global AR-ness than math. Documents the 'entropy sink': positions immediately right of the prefix receive disproportionately high confidence, which is the mechanistic cause of residual AR-ness under confidence-based decoding. Shows temperature 0.2 -> 1.2 substantially lowers AR-ness (the same sampler-sensitivity axis this project independently measured at top_p 1.0 -> 0.95). Tracks AR-ness drift across adaptation pretraining / mid-training / SFT / RL stages. Shows post-GRPO models degrade less at 0.5x steps, i.e. links reduced AR-ness to greater parallel-speedup tolerance.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: AR-ness is measured on generated sequences only, never regressed against per-token ground-truth survival or execution outcome; there is no AUC of commit confidence for predicting whether a position's token survives, and no syntactic-vs-semantic decomposition of the failures. Granularity is swept over k in the AR-ness definitions but never over LINGUISTIC units (4-token / 16-token / line), so indentation- and block-structure priors specific to Python are never isolated. No canvas-length axis: L = T = 512 fixed throughout. Its speedup-tolerance observation is within-model before/after RL, not a between-model pass@1-matched dissociation. Does not instrument Dream-Coder-Instruct, Dream-Coder-Base, or DreamOn.
related_work.known_defects: The AR-ness metrics are ratio statistics over decoding steps with no tie handling, and the paper's own default config sets timesteps = sequence length (one token per step), which mechanically inflates AR-ness relative to genuinely parallel operating points -- so the headline 'adapted dLLMs have stronger AR-ness' is partly a decode-config artifact rather than a property of the weights. AR-ness vs performance is reported as a co-movement across training stages (700B tokens: AR-ness up, performance down) with no intervention holding one fixed, so the causal reading is unsupported. The temperature-lowers-AR-ness finding is confounded with the well-documented quality drop at high temperature, and no compute-matched or quality-matched control is shown. Entropy sink is offered as a hypothesis with an explicit admission that 'its underlying cause requires further analysis and verification'.

related_work.citation: Asaria, Salomone & Gandhi (Transformer Lab), "Neither Parallel Nor Sequential: How DiffusionGemma Actually Commits Tokens", arXiv:2606.14620 (v1 2026-06-12)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint, cs.LG. arXiv shows no comments and no journal-ref; single version v1 (12 Jun 2026 16:45:11 UTC).
related_work.what_it_covers: The candidate's stated follow-up target -- CONFIRMED to exist exactly as described. Inference-only interpretability study of google/diffusiongemma-26B-A4B-it (25.2B total / 3.8B active MoE on Gemma 4), instrumenting EntropyBoundSampler.accept_canvas to record per-accept-call which canvas positions commit and their per-position entropy. 686-prompt six-regime probe suite; strengthening run of 5 seeds x 20 prompts/regime with prompt-clustered bootstrap. Findings: partial, granularity-dependent left-to-right commit bias, not clean block-autoregression; tie-aware Kendall tau_b ~0.43-0.60 at token level for prose/code/math/factual, rising smoothly with analysis bin size so 'block size' is a ruler artifact rather than architecture; large simultaneous commit batches leave within-batch order genuinely undefined; JSON is approximately order-independent (CI [-0.086, -0.00]); commit confidence predicts correctness on GSM8K math (AUROC 0.749, clustered CI [0.602, 0.879]) but carries no signal on factual recall (CI [0.383, 0.544]); aggressive entropy-bounded early stopping well inside the step budget; accuracy matches the AR Gemma-4 26B-A4B sibling. Documents a methodology checklist: trailing-EOS padding, within-regime confounding, commit non-monotonicity, block-size sensitivity, large commit-batch ties, Simpson's-paradox pooling.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: CRITICAL CORRECTION to the candidate's framing: the paper DOES include a code regime and DOES report tau_b for code -- what it does not do is GRADE it. Its own limitations list an explicit item titled 'Unscored code regimes', so telemetry is never validated against execution-graded correctness anywhere; the confidence-correctness AUROC exists only for math and factual recall. Also listed as limitations by the authors themselves: 'Single GPU, single checkpoint, small constrained regimes' and 'AR contrast is on accuracy only, and underpowered'. Canvas is fixed at the shipped 256-token config, so the (L,T) plane is never crossed. Effective-vs-nominal parallelism accounting is not the paper's argument. No between-model comparison at all -- n=1 checkpoint -- so no pass@1-matched commit-profile dissociation and no speedup-tolerance test.
related_work.known_defects: n=1 checkpoint of a proprietary-lineage MoE, so every claim is a single-model observation; the authors concede this. Only 20 prompts per regime for the strengthening run -- the confidence-correctness AUROCs have CIs so wide (math [0.602, 0.879]) that the math-vs-factual dissociation rests on barely-separated intervals. Correctness scoring is restricted to the regimes with automatable answers, which excludes precisely the regime (code) where an execution oracle is cheapest and most trustworthy. The granularity/bin-size sweep is an analysis-side sweep on one decode config, so it cannot separate 'the ruler is arbitrary' from 'this model's shipped block schedule happens to sit at 16'. Accuracy contrast with the AR sibling is self-described as underpowered.

related_work.citation: Zhu et al., "ParallelBench: Understanding the Trade-offs of Parallel Decoding in Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2510.04767 (v1 2025-10-06); ICLR 2026 Poster
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 /notes/search returning the exact title with venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference'.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE MAIN PRE-CUTOFF THREAT TO POINT (iv). Information-theoretic analysis of parallel decoding plus a purpose-built benchmark. Core claims that overlap the candidate's decision-relevance framing: 'evaluations on standard benchmarks (e.g. math and coding) are not sufficient to capture the quality degradation caused by parallel decoding'; dLLMs under parallel decoding suffer dramatic real-world quality degradation; and 'current parallel decoding strategies struggle to adapt their degree of parallelism based on task difficulty, thus failing to achieve meaningful speedup without compromising quality'. Systematically analyzes both dLLMs and AR LLMs on synthetic list operations plus the ParallelBench tasks.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The unit of analysis is the TASK/benchmark, not the CHECKPOINT: it argues standard benchmarks hide parallel-decoding damage, and answers with a new benchmark. It never asks whether two checkpoints with equal pass@1 differ in speedup tolerance, and never proposes any per-model decoding telemetry as the predictor. No commit-order logging, no commit-time confidence, no per-position survival, no granularity sweep. Diagnosis is distributional/information-theoretic (conditional independence + token dependency strength), not measured from a shipped sampler's accept step. Does not touch the open 7B code checkpoints as instrumented subjects.
related_work.known_defects: The headline degradation evidence leans on analytically tractable synthetic list operations chosen to be adversarial to parallel decoding ('trivial for humans and autoregressive LLMs yet exceptionally challenging for dLLMs'), so the effect size is by construction near worst-case and does not calibrate how much damage occurs at the operating points people actually report on HumanEval/MBPP. Prescribes a new benchmark rather than a reporting artifact computable on existing runs, so it cannot retroactively audit the published NFE/steps numbers it criticises. Offers no mechanism-level predictor of which model will tolerate a given parallelism setting.

related_work.citation: Chakraborty et al., "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2607.24763 (v1 2026-06-04)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv comments field says only 'updated version'; no journal-ref. Note the 2607 identifier with a 4 Jun 2026 v1 timestamp -- submission history confirms v1 = Thu, 4 Jun 2026 22:21:08 UTC, which is after the 2026-05-07 cutoff either way.
related_work.what_it_covers: The closest existing instance of the candidate's 'required reporting artifact' framing applied to dLLM compute accounting. Argues seven recent remasking papers evaluate under incompatible settings -- 'varying nominal step counts, metrics, and sampling temperatures without jointly controlling these factors' -- rendering rankings incomparable. Proposes standardizing the ACTUAL number of function evaluations (as distinct from nominal steps), enforcing multi-metric reporting, and explicitly controlling stochasticity. Applied to 7 remasking strategies x LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base x 4 stochasticity levels x 3 step budgets. Headline: temperature explains most MAUVE variance, and 'compute-matched comparisons reverse several published strategy rankings'. Ships a leaderboard over 12 open-weight MDLMs (150M-8B).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Standardizes compute on the INPUT side (actual NFE, temperature, step budget) but never measures the OUTPUT side of the same ledger -- how many tokens actually commit per step, or how many steps commit nothing. Surfaces are OpenWebText and LM1B with MAUVE/likelihood metrics: no executable task, no pass@1, no per-token correctness oracle, so nothing links compute accounting to graded output quality. No commit-order or commit-confidence telemetry at all. Its 'reversal of published rankings' is about remasking strategies, not about model checkpoints or parallel-decoding speedup tolerance.
related_work.known_defects: MAUVE on OpenWebText/LM1B is a distributional-similarity proxy, and the paper's own strongest result is that temperature explains the majority of MAUVE variance -- which is closer to a warning that the metric is dominated by a nuisance parameter than a validated construct for ranking remasking strategies. Key effect (high-entropy remasking reducing MAUVE by 0.296) is reported at a single step budget and single unmask_temp with p=0.020, i.e. one cell of a large grid with no multiplicity correction stated in the abstract. The 12-model leaderboard is used to claim the interaction 'holds across architectures and scales' without per-model CIs.

related_work.citation: "Answer First, Reason Later: Commitment Order in Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2608.05687 (v1 2026-08-06)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv v1 dated 2026-08-06, i.e. one day before this assessment; no comments, no journal-ref.
related_work.what_it_covers: Extremely close in method and in the 'telemetry changes conclusions' framing, but published yesterday and therefore strongly concurrent. Logs EVERY commitment during decoding of LLaDA-8B on GSM8K. Finds pure decoding commits the final answer at 15-24% of the trajectory while half the reasoning region is still masked, and collapses to answer-only output on up to 90% of problems AS THE CANVAS GROWS -- i.e. it crosses the canvas-length axis, which the candidate asserts is uncrossed. Rules out EOS pressure as the cause in favour of reachability. 2x2 prompt-decoder design with a +34.8pp interaction (95% CI [26.8, 42.8]) decomposed into collapse and order channels, replicated on Dream-7B and MATH-500. Then a single-knob frontier-gated commitment intervention recovers 0.528 -> 0.852 while preserving up to 4x parallel decoding, with an optimal window that flips from w=1 to unconstrained across the frontier. Explicitly reframes existing window samplers as the minimal fix for a pathology they were not designed for.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Reasoning-only surface: GSM8K and MATH-500, with correctness as final-answer exact match, not execution. No code, no EvalPlus, no syntactic-vs-semantic decomposition. No per-position commit-confidence AUC for token survival. Its cross-model work (Dream-7B) is a replication of the same pathology, not a pass@1-matched commit-profile dissociation. Does not include Dream-Coder, Dream-Coder-Base, DreamOn, or DiffuCoder.
related_work.known_defects: The canvas-growth collapse finding is entangled with the well-documented EOS/padding pathology of MDLM canvases (cf. VoidPadding/RainbowPadding), and the paper's EOS-pressure control is on decoder-side pressure rather than on padding convention, so an alternative explanation via padding-token training remains live. The headline recovery (0.528 -> 0.852) is a single intervention on one model-task pair, and the '4x parallel decoding preserved' claim is a nominal-parallelism statement with no reported effective-commits-per-step. Optimal-window flip is characterized on a measured frontier without seed variance reported in the abstract.

related_work.citation: Lin Yao, "Decoding in Order-Agnostic Language Models: Chain-Rule Deviation and Uniform Spreading", arXiv:2606.00997 (v1 2026-05-31)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv v1 Sun, 31 May 2026 04:25:36 UTC; no comments, no journal-ref; single author.
related_work.what_it_covers: Confirms the candidate's second cited concurrent anchor. On LLaDA-2.1: (1) learned conditionals are not exact factorizations of a coherent joint -- changing only the reveal order shifts target log-likelihood by up to 0.49 nats/token, so likelihood mixes content difficulty with path-dependent artifacts; (2) confidence-first decoding, though nominally order-agnostic, produces reveal orders CLOSE TO LEFT-TO-RIGHT on content tokens; (3) a uniform-spreading theorem showing target recoverability is maximized when per-step confidence is spread uniformly at fixed total likelihood, motivating Var(log q_t) as a path diagnostic. Across C4 and four downstream benchmarks, low variance separates structured paths from random ordering and is associated with correctness. Concludes by advocating joint reporting of mean confidence AND confidence variance -- a reporting-standard recommendation adjacent to the candidate's.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Metrics are likelihood/recoverability-based, not execution-graded; correctness enters only as an association with downstream benchmark scores, not as a per-token survival oracle. No syntactic-vs-semantic split. No effective-vs-nominal step accounting. No granularity sweep of the L2R statistic. Single model family (LLaDA-2.1); no code checkpoints. No speedup-tolerance dissociation.
related_work.known_defects: The uniform-spreading result is a theorem about recoverability at FIXED total likelihood -- a condition that decoding paths do not satisfy in practice, so the empirical Var(log q_t) diagnostic inherits an assumption the experiments never verify. 'Variance is consistently associated with downstream correctness' is an association across paths with no intervention and no control for output length, and the paper's own first finding (order changes likelihood by 0.49 nats/token) means the likelihood-derived diagnostic is measured in the very units it shows to be path-contaminated. Single-author, single-model-family, preprint with no venue check available.

related_work.citation: "Measuring Temporal Linguistic Emergence in Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2604.23235 (v1 2026-04-25)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv v1 2026-04-25; no comments, no journal-ref.
related_work.what_it_covers: PRE-CUTOFF partial precedent for point (iii). Three independent 32-step runs of LLaDA-8B-Base on masked WikiText-103, 1000 probe-training / 200 held-out sequences, deriving four temporal measurements from saved trajectories: token commitment; linear recoverability of POS, coarse semantic category, and token identity; confidence and entropy dynamics; and sensitivity under mid-trajectory re-masking. Directly relevant finding: 'uncertainty remains higher for tokens that ultimately resolve incorrectly even though late confidence becomes less calibrated' -- i.e. token-level commit-time confidence does carry signal about eventual per-position correctness. Also finds content categories stabilize earlier than function-heavy categories (a syntax-vs-content ordering result), coarse labels recovered earlier than lexical identity, and perturbation sensitivity peaking mid-trajectory and being overwhelmingly local to perturbed positions.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Surface is masked WikiText-103 language modelling, not an executable task, so 'correctness' means token reconstruction against the original text, not program semantics; there is no pass@1, no execution oracle, no syntax-error vs wrong-answer decomposition. Only 32 steps, one canvas configuration, one model, base (not instruct). No AUC reported for confidence-as-survival-predictor. No L2R order statistic and no granularity sweep. No cross-model comparison.
related_work.known_defects: n=1 checkpoint, n=3 seeds, 200 held-out evaluation sequences -- small enough that the paper hedges every claim with 'in this LLaDA+WikiText setting' and 'under our measurements'. The POS/semantic recoverability results come from linear probes whose ceiling is set by the probe, so 'coarse labels are recovered earlier than lexical identity' partly reflects the easier probe task rather than the model's trajectory. Confidence-vs-eventual-correctness is reported qualitatively (uncertainty 'remains higher') with no discrimination metric, so it cannot be compared against or combined with AUROC-based results elsewhere.

related_work.citation: Peng et al., "How Efficient Are Diffusion Language Models? A Critical Examination of Efficiency Evaluation Practices", arXiv:2510.18480 (v1 2025-10-21; v2 withdrawn; v3 2025-11-10)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv submission history shows v1 2025-10-21, v2 2025-10-30 WITHDRAWN (1 KB), v3 2025-11-10; no journal-ref; OpenReview search surfaced no venue note.
related_work.what_it_covers: PRE-CUTOFF precedent for the general 'dLLM efficiency reporting is broken' argument. diff.differentiation_statement: Nothing pre-cutoff makes this paper's claim with this method in this setting, so the direction survives -- but two of its four legs are already occupied by pre-cutoff work and must be demoted from findings to calibration. Leg (i), "effective parallelism is far below nominal L/T", is essentially the AFP = n/T_eff metric of arXiv:2601.15593 (2026-01-22), whose T_eff already counts only steps at which something commits, and the wasted-compute observation is stated verbatim and venue-backed in FOCUS (ICML 2026, first public 2026-01-30). Leg (ii), "the left-to-right commit statistic strengthens as you coarsen the ruler, on code", is DiffuCoder's local/global AR-ness@k sweep measured on HumanEval with Dream and LLaDA (ICLR 2026 Poster, first public 2025-06-25), which reports exactly the monotone-in-k structure the candidate proposes to discover, with the entropy sink as its mechanism. What remains genuinely unoccupied is the execution-grounded half. No paper -- pre-cutoff or concurrent -- regresses per-position commit telemetry against an EXECUTION oracle: the concurrent DiffusionGemma study measures a code regime but lists "Unscored code regimes" among its own limitations, so its confidence-correctness AUROCs exist only for math (0.749) and factual recall (chance), never for code; the concurrent Answer-First study crosses the canvas axis but on GSM8K/MATH-500 final-answer exact match; the pre-cutoff WikiText trajectory study finds token-level uncertainty tracks eventual correctness but against text reconstruction, not program semantics. And no paper anywhere performs the decision-relevant test: take two checkpoints matched on pass@1, show their commit profiles differ, apply an identical parallel-decoding speedup, and show the quality loss differs. ParallelBench (ICLR 2026 Poster, pre-cutoff) is the closest and it argues the complementary point -- that standard math/code benchmarks fail to expose parallel-decoding damage -- but its unit of analysis is the task, answered with a new benchmark, never the checkpoint, and it proposes no telemetry-based predictor of speedup tolerance. So our differentiation is: an execution-graded commit-telemetry study on the open 7B code checkpoints the code-generation literature actually benchmarks (Dream-Coder-Instruct, Dream-Coder-Base, DreamOn, plus DiffuCoder as a deliberate cross-family replication of the very model whose AR-ness metric we are extending), where evalplus untrusted_check supplies per-task ground truth, our existing syntax-error decomposition (93.9% -> 1.8% across the NFE sweep) supplies a clean syntactic/semantic split of per-token survival, and the (L,T) plane is crossed rather than fixed at one shipped config.

followup_openings.target_paper: Asaria, Salomone & Gandhi, "Neither Parallel Nor Sequential: How DiffusionGemma Actually Commits Tokens", arXiv:2606.14620 (2026-06-12, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: The paper's own limitations section contains an item titled "Unscored code regimes": a code regime IS in the six-regime probe suite and IS assigned a Kendall tau_b, but it is never graded, so the confidence-vs-correctness analysis runs only on math (AUROC 0.749, CI [0.602, 0.879]) and factual recall (CI [0.383, 0.544] = chance). The central methodological claim -- that commit telemetry is decision-relevant -- is therefore validated on the two regimes where an answer oracle happened to be cheap, and left unvalidated on the one regime where the oracle is strongest and cheapest of all. The authors additionally concede "Single GPU, single checkpoint" and "AR contrast is on accuracy only, and underpowered".
followup_openings.our_fix: Score the code regime. Instrument the accept step of Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B, Dream-Coder-Base-7B, DreamOn-v0-7B and Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, log per position (commit step, commit confidence, whether the final token survived), and compute the confidence-as-survival AUROC against evalplus untrusted_check on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ -- an execution oracle, not an answer-string match. Then do what a math/factual split cannot: partition survival by SYNTACTIC vs SEMANTIC failure using the syntax-error decomposition we already measured (unparseable-output rate falls 93.9% -> 1.8% on HE+ and 89% -> 1.6% on MBPP+ across the NFE sweep), giving a within-regime dissociation that is graded by a compiler and an interpreter rather than by regime membership.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts their strongest and widest-CI claim (confidence tracks correctness on math, not on facts) from a between-regime comparison with barely-separated intervals into a within-task, execution-graded, syntax-vs-semantics contrast on the surface practitioners deploy. If confidence predicts syntactic survival but not semantic survival, then every confidence-based scheduler on code is optimizing parseability while being scored on correctness -- a concrete, actionable indictment their setup structurally cannot deliver.

followup_openings.target_paper: Zhong et al., "Parallelism and Generation Order in Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2601.15593 (2026-01-22, PRE-CUTOFF -- this is the leg-(i) blocker)
followup_openings.defect: The paper computes T_eff = |{t : some position commits at step t}| in order to form AFP = n/T_eff, and then never reports T_eff / T_nominal. It therefore holds the exact quantity needed to indict 'steps' as a reported cost unit and declines to make the argument, presenting AFP instead as a hardware-agnostic SPEED metric alongside TPS. Separately, its sample-level claim that 'correct samples consistently exhibit higher AFP than incorrect ones' has no length control, while the paper itself quarantines repetitive outputs precisely because they distort AFP -- so the correctness association may be a length/degeneracy artifact. And it computes Kendall's tau without tie correction while simultaneously finding that models commit in large simultaneous batches.
followup_openings.our_fix: Report the ratio they left unreported. Publish T_eff / T_nominal per (model, L, T) cell as the headline accounting number, anchored on our own measured case where a 512-token canvas at T=1024 caps useful commits at r = L/T = 0.5, so at most half the nominal steps can commit anything -- corroborated by our independently measured exactly-zero pass@1 gain from T=512 to T=1024 on both HE+ and MBPP+. Cross the (L,T) plane instead of using each model's single shipped block config. Use tie-aware tau_b (as the concurrent DiffusionGemma study does) since our own scaffold runtime commits in batches. Add the length control they omit: condition the AFP-correctness association on output length and on degeneracy, rather than excluding degenerate traces into a separate bucket.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Leg (i) cannot be a finding after AFP, but it can be a correction: their metric's denominator silently absorbs the wasted steps that the field reports and prices, and no one has published the ratio. Adding tie-awareness and a length control also repairs the two statistical soft spots in the pre-cutoff paper that our own data are unusually well placed to expose, since we have both a batch-committing runtime and a measured degeneracy channel.

followup_openings.target_paper: Gong et al., "DiffuCoder", arXiv:2506.20639 (2025-06-25, ICLR 2026 Poster, PRE-CUTOFF -- this is the leg-(ii) blocker)
followup_openings.defect: Local and global AR-ness@k are swept over k, but k indexes TOKEN offsets and mask-position ranks -- never linguistic units. The paper therefore establishes that the L2R statistic is granularity-dependent on code without ever testing whether the dependence is driven by Python's indentation and block structure, which is the specific prior the candidate wants to isolate. Worse, all AR-ness numbers are measured at timesteps = sequence length = 512, i.e. one token per step, a configuration that mechanically inflates AR-ness; so 'adapted dLLMs have stronger AR-ness' is partly an artifact of the decode config rather than a property of the weights, and no compute-matched control is shown. AR-ness is also never linked to per-token survival, and the entropy sink is offered with an explicit admission that its cause 'requires further analysis and verification'.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run the k-sweep with LINGUISTIC granularities -- token, 4-token, 16-token, and physical source line -- so indentation and block boundaries become the binning unit, and report whether the granularity gradient is carried by structural boundaries or is scale-free. Break their decode-config confound by measuring AR-ness across the (L,T) plane rather than only at T = L, which separates 'this model is AR-ish' from 'one-token-per-step forces AR-ish measurements'. Instrument DiffuCoder-7B itself alongside the Dream-Coder family so the extension is a same-model replication plus an axis change rather than a competing measurement. Then connect AR-ness to survival: test whether out-of-order commits are disproportionately the ones that get overwritten or that end up in failing programs.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the honest route past the strongest pre-cutoff blocker. Their k-sweep already predicts our leg (ii) will replicate, which the candidate's own kill criterion does not acknowledge -- so re-deriving it would produce nothing. Re-binning by source structure and breaking the T = L confound turns a foregone replication into two new results, one of which (is the ruler artifact structural or scale-free?) directly adjudicates the concurrent DiffusionGemma claim that block size is a property of the measuring instrument.

followup_openings.target_paper: Zhu et al., "ParallelBench", arXiv:2510.04767 (2025-10-06, ICLR 2026 Poster, PRE-CUTOFF)
followup_openings.defect: It establishes that standard math and code benchmarks fail to expose parallel-decoding degradation, and answers with a new benchmark. The unit of analysis is the task, never the checkpoint: it offers no per-model measurement that predicts which checkpoint will tolerate a given parallelism setting, and its degradation evidence leans on synthetic list operations deliberately chosen to be adversarial to parallel decoding, so the effect size does not calibrate the damage at the operating points people actually report on HumanEval/MBPP. Being a new benchmark, it also cannot retroactively audit the published steps/NFE numbers it criticises.
followup_openings.our_fix: Move the unit of analysis from task to checkpoint and supply the missing predictor. Select two checkpoints matched on pass@1+ (our measured ladder makes this feasible -- scaffold Medium sits at .177/.354 while the plain-SFT control reaches .2195/.2434 on HE+/MBPP+, and the NFE sweep provides multiple additional matched cells), show their commit profiles differ, then apply an IDENTICAL parallel-decoding speedup to both and show the quality loss differs. The claim becomes: commit telemetry predicts speedup tolerance where pass@1 does not -- computable on existing runs, on real benchmarks, at reported operating points, without a new benchmark.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the leg with no prior art at all, pre-cutoff or concurrent, and it is the only leg that earns the paper's 'required reporting' framing. ParallelBench says the benchmark is blind; we say the metric is blind and hand back a per-model artifact that fixes it. It also supplies the falsifiable core the candidate's own kill criterion identifies as load-bearing, so the paper's headline should be built here rather than on legs (i) and (ii).

followup_openings.target_paper: Chakraborty et al., "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol", arXiv:2607.24763 (2026-06-04, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: CaRE standardizes the INPUT side of the compute ledger -- actual NFE, temperature, step budget -- and shows compute-matched comparison reverses published rankings. But it never measures the OUTPUT side: no tokens-committed-per-step, no count of steps that commit nothing. Its surfaces are OpenWebText and LM1B scored by MAUVE, and its own headline is that temperature explains the majority of MAUVE variance, i.e. the ranking metric is dominated by a nuisance parameter and is never validated against graded task success.
followup_openings.our_fix: Complete the ledger and ground the metric. Pair their input-side NFE standardization with our output-side T_eff / T_nominal and effective-commits-per-step, and score on executable tasks where pass@1+ from evalplus replaces MAUVE, so 'compute-matched' claims are validated against a correctness oracle rather than a distributional proxy. Our sampler-sensitivity measurement (top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 moved HumanEval by +14.6 points, larger than most published diffusion-LM method gains) independently corroborates their stochasticity-control thesis on an execution-graded surface they never touch, which is a citable convergence rather than a competing claim.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: CaRE is the closest existing instance of the candidate's 'required reporting artifact' framing, so the paper must either subsume or complement it. Complementing is cleanly available: they fixed what goes in, we report what comes out, and we replace a metric they themselves show is temperature-dominated with execution grading.

followup_openings.target_paper: "Answer First, Reason Later: Commitment Order in Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2608.05687 (2026-08-06, concurrent -- appeared one day before this assessment)
followup_openings.defect: Crosses the canvas-length axis and logs every commitment, but only on reasoning: GSM8K and MATH-500 with final-answer exact match. Its canvas-growth collapse finding is entangled with the well-documented MDLM EOS/padding pathology -- its EOS control is on decoder-side pressure, not on padding convention -- leaving a padding-training explanation live. Its '4x parallel decoding preserved' is a nominal-parallelism statement with no effective-commits-per-step reported, and its cross-model work on Dream-7B replicates the pathology rather than testing between-model dissociation.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the same canvas axis on executable code with per-position survival, where 'collapse' is not answer-only truncation but a compilable-yet-wrong or unparseable program, and where the failure mode is graded rather than string-matched. Report effective commits per step alongside their nominal speedup factor, which is exactly the accounting they omit. Use DreamOn -- a variable-length / mask-expansion model -- as a padding-convention control the reasoning setting lacks, which is the discriminating test between their reachability explanation and the padding explanation.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is concurrent and therefore non-preempting, but it is the nearest neighbour in both method and framing, so the paper must state the axis change explicitly. Doing so also converts a threat into a contribution: our DreamOn arm adjudicates a confound their design cannot address, and our effective-parallelism number closes the gap in their speedup claim.
