diff.sharpened_claim: On executable code, diffusion-LM commit telemetry dissociates from pass@1, and the dissociation is decision-relevant: two open 7B checkpoints matched on pass@1+ have different commit profiles and therefore different tolerance to an identical parallel-decoding speedup, so pass@1 cannot rank checkpoints for deployment under parallelism while commit telemetry can. We ground this in an execution oracle rather than an answer string: instrumenting the accept step of Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B, Dream-Coder-Base-7B, DreamOn-v0-7B, Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B and DiffuCoder-7B (a deliberate same-model extension of the pre-cutoff AR-ness@k analysis) on HumanEval+ and MBPP+, we log per position the commit step, the commit-time confidence, and whether the final token survived, and we report the AUROC of commit confidence for per-token survival SPLIT BY SYNTACTIC VERSUS SEMANTIC failure -- a within-task dissociation graded by the interpreter and by evalplus untrusted_check, which the concurrent DiffusionGemma study structurally cannot produce because its own limitations record "Unscored code regimes." If confidence predicts syntactic survival but not semantic survival, every confidence-based scheduler on code is optimizing parseability while being scored on correctness. Two secondary results are positioned explicitly as calibration of pre-cutoff work rather than as discoveries: (a) we report T_eff / T_nominal per (L,T) cell -- the ratio that the AFP metric of arXiv:2601.15593 computes in its denominator but never publishes -- anchored on our measured 512-token canvas at T=1024 where at most half the nominal steps can commit, corroborated by our exactly-zero pass@1 gain from T=512 to T=1024 on both benchmarks; and (b) we re-run DiffuCoder's granularity sweep with LINGUISTIC bins (token, 4-token, 16-token, source line) across the (L,T) plane instead of at its confounded timesteps = sequence length = 512, which both breaks that decode-config confound and adjudicates whether the "block size is a measuring artifact" claim is carried by indentation and block boundaries or is scale-free. Deliverable: a logger plus a per-model commit-profile card, computable on existing runs at reported operating points, with no new benchmark required.

blocking_gaps: THE HEADLINE DEPENDENT VARIABLE DOES NOT EXIST. /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B/generation_utils.py `_sample` (lines 410-458) has NO remasking path: `mask_index=(x==mask_token_id)` is recomputed each step and writes go only to positions currently equal to mask_token_id via `x[row_indices,transfer_index]=x_[...]`. Nothing ever writes mask_token_id back into x. I instrumented it and measured OVERWRITE+REMASK == 0 in every one of 13 configurations: alg in {entropy, maskgit_plus, topk_margin, origin} x alg_temp in {0,1} x T in {32,64,128,256,512} x (L=64,128,256,512) x {Instruct, Base}. So 'whether that position's final token survived' is identically TRUE for all 512/512 committed positions. The AUROC of commit confidence for per-token survival is computed against a CONSTANT label -- it is undefined, not merely weak. Leg (iii), the sharpened_claim's stated headline and the entire syntactic-vs-semantic split, has nothing to split.

LEG (i) IS CLOSED-FORM ARITHMETIC, NOT A MEASUREMENT, AND SELF-FALSIFIES AT EVERY REPORTED OPERATING POINT. commits-per-step is `int(num_mask_token*(1-s/t))` with s,t from `torch.linspace(1,eps,T+1)` (lines 406,439). It depends ONLY on (L,T,eps) -- not on weights, prompt, task, or data. I computed it in closed form and it reproduces the runs exactly (L=512,T=512 -> T_eff=511; L=512,T=1024 -> T_eff=510, ratio 0.498). Consequences: (a) T_eff/T = 1.000 for EVERY T<=L, so the stated kill criterion 'effective tokens-per-step tracks nominal L/T within ~15%' is satisfied by construction at every cell the project reports (T=16..512, L=512); the ratio only drops below 1 at T>L, a degenerate config the project already showed buys exactly zero pass@1 (.707->.707, .680->.680). (b) There is ZERO cross-model variance to put on a 'per-model commit-profile card' -- all four Dream-family checkpoints share the schedule; the only difference is the eps default (1e-3 Instruct vs 1e-12 Base/Scaffold, verified by diff) which moves T_eff by at most 1. Spending 180 GPU-hours to measure a 3-line function of (L,T,eps) is the waste.

LEG (ii) IS PINNED AT THE CEILING, SO THE GRANULARITY SWEEP HAS NO HEADROOM. I measured tie-aware tau_b between position index and commit step: +0.9900/+0.9919 (T=64), +0.9873/+0.9941 (T=128), +0.9981/+0.9948 (T=256), +0.9973/+0.9993 (T=512) on Instruct, and +0.9999/+0.9996/+1.0000 on Base. Commit order is essentially perfectly left-to-right. Coarsening the ruler from token to 4/16/line can only move a statistic already at 0.998 within [0.998, 1.000]; the DiffuCoder monotone-in-k gradient needs dynamic range that does not exist here. Mechanism: alg_temp=0.0 makes `torch.topk(full_confidence, k)` a deterministic confidence-argmax, and the entropy sink hands it the leftmost masked positions.

THE LOAD-BEARING LEG (matched-pass@1 pair -> different commit profiles -> different speedup tolerance) IS ALREADY NEAR-NULL. tau_b is a readout of the SAMPLER SETTING, not the checkpoint: at fixed (alg=entropy, alg_temp=0, T=128) I get alg_temp=0 -> +0.9972 but alg_temp=1.0 -> -0.0014 and alg='origin' -> +0.0090, i.e. the knob spans the whole range, while two different checkpoints at the same setting give 0.9986 vs 0.9998. Since 'apply an IDENTICAL parallel-decoding speedup to both' fixes (alg, alg_temp, L, T) by construction, and the schedule is model-independent (gap 2), the matched pair is expected to have indistinguishable profiles. The positioning itself names this leg as the only prior-art-free one and as the paper's falsifiable core.

CROSS-FAMILY CHECKPOINT ABSENT FROM BOTH DISKS. No DiffuCoder and no LLaDA anywhere under /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/{models,dllm_draft/models} nor on zwfy6 (checked via .73: /apdcephfs_zwfy6/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft exists but the models tree has no diffu/llada/dream match). Needs download: DiffuCoder-7B ~15GB, LLaDA-8B-Instruct ~16GB, via http_proxy=http://hy-proxy.woa.com:3128. Note DiffuCoder is a different sampler codebase, so its commit schedule is NOT the Dream closed form and must be re-derived, not assumed.

SURVIVAL IS ONLY A VARIABLE ON 2 OF 5 PLANNED MODELS, AND ON NEITHER OF THEM IN EXISTING RUNS. DreamOn (models/DreamOn-v0-7B/generation_utils.py lines 464-495) does splice: delete removes positions and expand inserts two masks -- but position INDICES are therefore unstable, so per-position telemetry needs an added provenance/alignment layer that does not exist. Scaffold runtime has remask_leaf/backtrack_structural_subtree, but scaffold_coder/model_sampler.py defaults max_leaf_remasks=0 and grep of scripts/_run_capacity_ladder_wzc1.sh finds no remask flag -- so the entire measured capacity ladder ran with remasking OFF and also has zero survival variance.

ENV/TOOLING: scipy is NOT installed in /opt/conda/envs/dllm-env (kendalltau unavailable; I hand-rolled tau_b). Also Base and Scaffold generation_utils.py are byte-identical (md5 4925e067...) and differ from Instruct (fe7dc873...): Instruct lacks the `use_ori_logits` confidence variant and the `transition_N` alg family, and uses eps=1e-3 vs 1e-12. A cross-checkpoint 'profile card' over these four would confound weights with sampler-code version.
feas.concrete_plan:
VERDICT: do not run the candidate as specified. Three of its four legs I have already measured to be null, arithmetic, or at-ceiling, using ~1 GPU-hour on GPU 6 local. Cost to confirm this was trivial; cost to "discover" it at 180 GPU-h would have been the fourth retraction.

WHAT I ACTUALLY RAN (reproduce in minutes; probes at /tmp/probe_commit.py, /tmp/probe2.py, /tmp/probe4.py, /tmp/probe5.py, /tmp/probe6.py, all read-only w.r.t. the repo):
- Verified generation_tokens_hook_func exists and fires exactly 1 + T times (pre-loop at line 409 + post-step at line 455). The candidate's feasibility claim about hooks is CORRECT; that was never the problem.
- Verified overwrite/remask == 0 in 13 configs (gap 1).
- Verified the commit schedule closed form against measured runs (gap 2).
- Verified tau_b ~ 0.99 at all T, both checkpoints (gap 3), and that alg_temp/alg spans [-0.001, +0.997] (gap 4).

SALVAGE -- the one execution-graded, differentiated, non-obvious result these probes surfaced. Reframe from "commit telemetry is a required reporting artifact" to "the shipped sampler cannot do the thing the architecture is sold for, and here is what it costs to turn it on":

Step 1 (0 GPU-h, done): report as an audit finding that Dream-Coder's shipped decode path is irreversible (no remask) and commits in ~perfect left-to-right order (tau_b 0.987-0.9994) at every operating point the code-generation literature benchmarks. This is the mechanistic root of the project's own self-diagnosis that "editing arbitrary positions with bidirectional context was thrown away" -- it was not thrown away by our refinement arms, it is absent from the shipped sampler. Cite alg_temp=0 + topk as the mechanism.

Step 2 (~8 GPU-h) THE INTERVENTION, which has a genuinely unknown outcome: sweep alg_temp in {0, 0.1, 0.5, 1.0} plus alg='origin' at fixed (L=512, T=256; 6.11 s/task measured from runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe256/metrics.rank*.jsonl) on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ with Dream-Coder-Instruct. This moves tau_b from +0.997 to ~0.00 -- i.e. it BUYS genuine order-agnosticism -- and asks what pass@1+ it costs. Grade with evalplus untrusted_check via the existing scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py (add --alg-temp passthrough; it currently hardcodes alg_temp=0.0 at line 241) + scripts/merge_evalplus_shards.py. Reuse the 8-way shard pattern from scripts/_run_nfe_sweep_wzc1.sh. This is the quality-vs-order-agnosticism frontier, and nothing in the related-work list measures it: DiffuCoder swept temperature (not alg_temp) and never graded the resulting order change against execution.

Step 3 (~10 GPU-h) MAKE SURVIVAL EXIST, then and only then do the AUROC: enable scaffold remasking (max_leaf_remasks>0, leaf_remask_fraction>0 via the existing --leaf-remask-* flags in scripts/generate_evalplus_scaffold.py) and run DreamOn's splice path. On those two arms survival genuinely varies, so commit-confidence-vs-survival AUROC is defined. Split syntactic vs semantic using the existing parseable()/final_parseable instrumentation. Do NOT run this on the Dream flat path.

Step 4 (~7 GPU-h, optional) cross-family: download DiffuCoder-7B (~15GB, hy-proxy) and re-derive its schedule from its own sampler before comparing anything.

REUSE, DO NOT DUPLICATE: .82's sampler/decoding sensitivity audit is the natural home for Step 2 -- alg_temp is a decoding-protocol knob and belongs in that arm's design, so coordinate rather than fork. .104's matched AR baseline supplies the reference point that Retraction 4 showed is mandatory: any "order-agnostic decoding costs X pass@1" number must be quoted against Qwen2.5-Coder AR on the same tokens_fed ledger, or it repeats Retraction 4. .73's DreamOn infilling work already fixed a span-recovery bug and found mask_expansion/delete_eos_token are silently swallowed by **kwargs -- Step 3's DreamOn arm must build on that fix, not on the pre-fix code path.
feas.risk: The candidate as written does not risk a null -- it IS a null, and I measured it. The live risk is that the null gets papered over into a plausible-looking positive. Concretely: the survival label is constant, so any AUROC an implementation manages to emit is being computed over something other than what it claims. The two ways that happens silently are (a) the position set leaks prompt tokens or trailing pad/EOS -- I measured 148 of 512 committed positions (28.9%) on HumanEval/2 to be special tokens, and trailing-EOS padding correlates with both late commit step and high confidence, so pooling them manufactures a clean-looking AUROC out of padding convention; and (b) 'survival' silently degrades into 'final program passed the tests', a TASK-level label broadcast onto every position in the task, which would produce a confident 0.7-ish AUROC that is really just pass@1 re-expressed per token. Both are the exact shape of Retraction 1 (a verifier that compared nothing) and Retraction 3 (an average whose denominator quietly excluded the cases that mattered). Secondary confound: because T_eff and tau_b are functions of (L, T, eps, alg, alg_temp) and not of the weights, any 'these two checkpoints have different commit profiles' claim will actually be reading a sampler-config or sampler-code-version difference -- Base/Scaffold ship a different generation_utils.py than Instruct (eps 1e-12 vs 1e-3, extra use_ori_logits and transition_N paths) -- and will be attributed to the model.
feas.required_control:
A POSITIVE CONTROL ON THE OUTCOME VARIABLE, asserted before any AUROC or profile card is emitted, with three hard assertions that abort rather than degrade:

(1) LABEL-VARIANCE ASSERTION. Per run, count positions whose committed token was later overwritten or re-masked. If that count is 0, the logger must REFUSE to emit a survival AUROC and must emit `survival_undefined: no label variance, n_overwritten=0` instead. This is the control that would have caught Retraction 1: it forces the pipeline to prove the two things it is comparing are actually different before reporting a comparison. On the Dream flat path this assertion fires immediately and correctly kills leg (iii) -- which is the whole point.

(2) CLOSED-FORM CROSS-CHECK ON THE COST LEDGER. Assert that T_eff and per-step commit counts recovered from telemetry equal the analytic prediction int(num_mask*(1-s/t)) from torch.linspace(1,eps,T+1) for the run's (L,T,eps), exactly. Any mismatch means the LOGGER is the source of the 'finding', not the model. This makes it structurally impossible to publish a T_eff/T_nominal number as an empirical discovery when it is arithmetic, and it pins down whether a cross-family model (DiffuCoder) genuinely deviates or was just mis-logged.

(3) DENOMINATOR DISCLOSURE. Every telemetry cell must report n_positions_total, n_prompt_excluded, n_special_or_pad_excluded, n_analyzed, and must report metrics both with and without special/pad positions. No single-number AUROC or tau_b without its denominator. This is the direct fix for Retraction 3 (a mean that silently dropped the expensive tasks) applied to the position axis instead of the task axis, and it is what stops trailing-EOS padding from being read as a confidence-tracks-correctness result.

Supporting requirement for the salvage: since tau_b is a readout of (alg, alg_temp, L, T), every profile card must print those four fields adjacent to the statistic, and any between-checkpoint claim must hold them fixed AND note that Base/Scaffold vs Instruct ship different generation_utils.py.

lens.title: Reporting Only Best-Protocol Numbers Inflates Diffusion-LM Progress: A Protocol-Search-Budget Accounting
lens.claim: Diffusion-LM progress on code benchmarks is systematically overstated because papers report the best number found under an undisclosed protocol search while comparing against baselines run at a single default protocol. Quantitatively: the expected maximum over a modest protocol grid exceeds the single-default score by a margin comparable to the median claimed method improvement, so a method with zero true effect can appear to improve the state of the art. The corrective is a search-budget-matched reporting rule -- give every compared system the same number of protocol trials and report the resulting distribution (median and max with the trial count), not a bare best.
lens.why_now: This is the accounting version of the sampler-sensitivity elephant, and our own numbers make the case concrete before any new experiment: our reported Dream-Coder-Instruct HE .762 is the better of two protocol attempts, and the run we DIDN'T headline scored .616. We also 'exceeded the paper' on MBPP (.807 vs 79.6) at our chosen protocol -- exactly the pattern this claim predicts, where protocol shopping masquerades as reproduction-plus. No existing audit prices the search itself: CaRE (2607.24763, concurrent) standardizes NFE, stochasticity and metrics but treats protocol as a factor to CONTROL, not as a budget to CHARGE; the concurrent Experimental Analysis (2606.19475) reports quality across inference-time factors without an inflation estimate. The framing is portable to the wider LM-evaluation literature, which is what makes it a reviewer-relevant methodology contribution rather than a niche diffusion note.
lens.experiment: Reuse the skeptic-2 factorial as the empirical substrate at zero marginal GPU cost, then do the accounting. (1) From the crossed grid, for each model build the full empirical distribution of pass@1+ over protocol cells, and compute E[max over k random cells] as a function of search budget k by bootstrap resampling -- this is the inflation curve. (2) Collect the median claimed improvement from a systematic sample of ~30 recent diffusion-LM code/reasoning papers and overlay it on the inflation curve, showing at what k a null method becomes 'state of the art'. (3) Demonstrate the failure live with a deliberately null intervention: take a change that provably cannot help (e.g. a no-op reordering of the unmasking tie-break, or an identity-equivalent decoding refactor), give it a k=8 protocol search while the baseline gets k=1 default, and report the 'improvement' it wins on HE+ and MBPP+. This is the paper's punchline and is nearly free. (4) Propose and validate the corrective rule: rerun a small number of real published-style comparisons (e.g. entropy vs maskgit_plus vs topk_margin unmasking, all shipped in generation_utils.py) under search-budget-matched reporting and show which apparent rankings survive. Report everything with paired bootstrap CIs and a fixed within-cell noise floor from 3 seeds.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: everything needed for the substrate is shared with skeptic-2 (four local 7B checkpoints, evalplus 0.3.1, both plus datasets, the three shipped unmasking algs, preserved raw_output for free post-hoc extraction variance, 40 GPUs), plus our own two-attempt r1/r2 history as the motivating anecdote. MISSING: nothing GPU-side beyond skeptic-2 -- the marginal cost is the null-intervention runs and analysis. RISK: the literature-sample step is human/judgement work and must be done transparently (pre-registered inclusion criteria, every claimed delta traceable to a table in the cited paper) or reviewers will attack it as cherry-picking; and any venue claim for a 2025/2026 conference paper in that sample must be verified on OpenReview via venueid plus camera-ready, since S2 and DBLP lag badly for 2026 venues and will mislabel accepted papers as preprints.
lens.kill_criterion: Falsified if the protocol-score distribution is tight -- if E[max over k=8] minus single-default is under ~2 points pass@1+, the inflation mechanism is too small to explain published deltas and there is no paper. Also falsified if the null intervention fails to win any apparent improvement under an asymmetric search budget, which would mean the asymmetry does not actually convert into headline gains. Weakened if the median published diffusion-LM improvement turns out to be far LARGER than the inflation curve at plausible k, since then protocol shopping cannot account for the field's reported progress and the claim must be narrowed to 'affects rankings among close competitors' rather than 'overstates progress'.
lens.builds_on: Motivated by our own reporting behaviour: we headlined HE .762 over a .616 attempt and 'beat the paper' on MBPP at a self-chosen protocol -- the exact pattern the claim describes, so the paper opens by charging ourselves. Extends CaRE (2607.24763, concurrent) from controlling protocol factors to PRICING the protocol search, an axis it does not address; and complements 2606.12232 (concurrent), whose finding that a remasking method's benefit is 'highly setting-dependent' is precisely the condition under which search-budget asymmetry inflates results. Shares its GPU substrate with skeptic-2, so it is the cheapest candidate here.

related_work.citation: Jesse Dodge, Suchin Gururangan, Dallas Card, Roy Schwartz, Noah A. Smith. "Show Your Work: Improved Reporting of Experimental Results." arXiv:1909.03004; EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019 (ACL Anthology D19-1224).
related_work.venue_status: EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019; verified by fetching https://aclanthology.org/D19-1224/ (title matches) plus arXiv v1 metadata.
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical prior art for the estimator our candidate proposes. Defines expected validation performance of the best-found model as a function of a compute budget (number of hyperparameter search trials), shows several published model comparisons would have flipped at a different budget, and issues reporting best-practices. This IS the 'expected max over k trials' curve.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Training-time hyperparameter search, scored on VALIDATION data, in the pre-LLM regime. Says nothing about inference-time/decoding protocol as a search space, nothing about test-set headline numbers, nothing about diffusion LMs, no code benchmarks, no null-intervention demonstration, and no attempt to compare the inflation magnitude against the distribution of deltas actually claimed in a literature.
related_work.known_defects: The estimator assumes trials are i.i.d. draws from a random search distribution. An inference-time protocol grid violates this: it is small, exhaustively enumerable rather than sampled, and its cells are strongly correlated (NFE is near-monotone in quality; top_p and temperature interact). Also the paper's recommendation was never widely adopted, and it never quantifies the asymmetric case (method tuned at k, baseline run at k=1), which is the actual reporting sin.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API + arXiv abs page (v1 date, abstract) + ACL Anthology page fetch.

related_work.citation: Raphael Tang, Jaejun Lee, Ji Xin, Xinyu Liu, Yaoliang Yu, Jimmy Lin. "Showing Your Work Doesn't Always Work." arXiv:2004.13705; ACL 2020 (ACL Anthology 2020.acl-main.246).
related_work.venue_status: ACL 2020; verified by fetching https://aclanthology.org/2020.acl-main.246/ (title matches) and arXiv comments field 'Accepted to ACL 2020'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Critically examines Dodge et al.'s estimator: shows it is biased, favors negative errors, yields poor bootstrapped confidence intervals; derives an unbiased alternative with simulation evidence.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Purely a statistical critique of the estimator under the random-search model. No inference-time protocol, no LLM/diffusion setting, no empirical LLM grids, no meta-analysis of claimed deltas.
related_work.known_defects: Its critique is about bootstrapped CIs on the estimator, not about violated independence when cells are enumerated rather than sampled. Our correlated-grid regime is precisely the untested one. This paper is a mandatory citation for us and also a warning: if we bootstrap-resample cells naively, this is the exact attack a reviewer will run.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API, arXiv abs page (comments field), ACL Anthology page fetch.

related_work.citation: Nicholas Lourie, Kyunghyun Cho, He He. "Show Your Work with Confidence: Confidence Bands for Tuning Curves." arXiv:2311.09480; NAACL 2024. Library: opda.
related_work.venue_status: NAACL-HLT 2024; verified on OpenReview (note Ai6F7SvXIw, venueid dblp.org/conf/NAACL/2024) and corroborated by arXiv comments 'Accepted to NAACL 2024'.
related_work.what_it_covers: The first exact, simultaneous, distribution-free confidence bands for tuning curves (performance vs number of hyperparameter choices tried). Shows point estimates of tuning curves fail silently and give contradictory results on little data; shows bootstrap bands undercover. Ships a pip-installable library (opda).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Again training-time hyperparameters. Does not treat decoding/inference protocol as the search space, does not study asymmetric budgets across compared systems, no diffusion LMs, no code benchmarks, and offers no estimate of how large the inflation is relative to what papers claim.
related_work.known_defects: Its bands are distribution-free but still assume the trials are exchangeable draws. On a fixed enumerated protocol grid with monotone factors, exchangeability is questionable and coverage is untested. Our fix (see follow-ups) is a coverage check in the correlated-enumerated-grid regime -- a genuine contribution back to their tool rather than mere usage.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API, arXiv abs page, OpenReview api2 notes/search (venueid field).

related_work.citation: Nicholas Lourie, He He, Kyunghyun Cho. "Hyperparameter Loss Surfaces Are Simple Near their Optima." arXiv:2510.02721; COLM 2025.
related_work.venue_status: COLM 2025; verified on OpenReview (note IAoSG4Q2xC, venueid colmweb.org/COLM/2025/Conference); arXiv comments also state 'Accepted to COLM 2025'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Derives the asymptotic distribution of best-of-random-search scores near an optimum and a scaling law for random-search convergence, yielding confidence intervals for best-possible performance and an 'effective number of hyperparameters'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Training-time hyperparameters and loss (not task metrics); asymptotic-in-k regime; nothing about inference protocol, diffusion, code, or the asymmetric-budget reporting failure. The 'effective dimension' idea is actually a gift to us: it is the right way to say how large a protocol grid effectively is.
related_work.known_defects: The asymptotic regime requires many random-search draws; a k<=8 protocol grid is squarely in the small-k pre-asymptotic regime their theory explicitly reaches for. So their law cannot be applied off the shelf to the budgets that actually matter in reporting practice -- a clean niche for exact/empirical treatment.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API, arXiv abs page, OpenReview api2 notes/search.

related_work.citation: Vladislav Kurenkov, Sergey Kolesnikov. "Showing Your Offline Reinforcement Learning Work: Online Evaluation Budget Matters." arXiv:2110.04156; ICML 2022 (Spotlight).
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2022 Spotlight per arXiv comments field on the abs page; not independently confirmed via proceedings (pre-2025 so OpenReview verification not required by our rule).
related_work.what_it_covers: Ports Dodge et al.'s expected validation performance into offline RL, arguing the evaluation budget is problem-dependent and demonstrating that the PREFERENCE between algorithms is budget-dependent across domains -- e.g. behavioural cloning wins at small budgets. This is the exact structural template of our candidate (transplant EVP into a new field where the community reports single-budget bests).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Offline RL, online-evaluation budget, not LM decoding protocol. No null intervention, no literature-delta meta-analysis, no code benchmarks.
related_work.known_defects: Reuses the biased Dodge estimator without engaging Tang et al.'s bias analysis. Also does not charge asymmetric budgets -- it varies a shared budget rather than exposing the method-gets-k-baseline-gets-1 asymmetry.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API, arXiv abs page (comments field).

related_work.citation: Andreas Hochlehnert, Hardik Bhatnagar, Vishaal Udandarao, Samuel Albanie, Ameya Prabhu, Matthias Bethge. "A Sober Look at Progress in Language Model Reasoning: Pitfalls and Paths to Reproducibility." arXiv:2504.07086; COLM 2025.
related_work.venue_status: COLM 2025; verified on OpenReview (note 90UrTTxp5O, venueid colmweb.org/COLM/2025/Conference).
related_work.what_it_covers: The closest pre-cutoff paper in SPIRIT. Shows math-reasoning benchmarks are highly sensitive to decoding parameters, seeds, prompt formatting, and even hardware/software; that reported gains 'frequently hinge on unclear comparisons or unreported sources of variance'; proposes a standardized framework and reassesses methods, finding most RL gains far below prior claims.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Math reasoning, autoregressive models. Crucially: it standardizes and re-runs, but it never PRICES the search. I scanned the full HTML of v2: zero occurrences of 'budget', 'expected max', 'tuning curve', or 'best-of'. There is no expected-max-over-k curve, no search-budget-matched reporting rule, no null intervention, and no diffusion or code coverage.
related_work.known_defects: Its corrective is 'multi-seed + released artifacts + report std', which controls within-cell noise but leaves the across-cell selection channel unpriced -- a method author can still comply fully and still ship a best-of-8-protocols number. That is exactly the loophole our accounting closes, and it is the strongest reviewer-facing argument for our paper's necessity.

related_work.citation: Patrick Pynadath, Jiaxin Shi, Ruqi Zhang. "Generative Frontiers: Why Evaluation Matters for Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2604.02718.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (technical note). No OpenReview record found under this title; treat as arXiv-only. Discovered via CaRE's reference list, not by keyword search.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE most dangerous pre-cutoff neighbour, and the one a reviewer will find. In the diffusion-LM setting it argues that single-point comparisons are not a reliable basis for model comparison because 'it is always possible to achieve different rankings via minor temperature adjustments', with a figure showing full ranking reversal under temperature; entropies stay in a non-degenerate range so there is no diversity-hacking escape. Its corrective is to sweep temperature and report an entropy-perplexity frontier curve per method.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Setting is GPT-2-small scale (~150M) on OpenWebText with generative perplexity / unigram entropy / KL decomposition. NOT code, NOT pass@1, NOT 7B instruct checkpoints, NOT execution-graded. And methodologically: it establishes that protocol choice can reverse rankings but never quantifies the expected gain from k trials, never charges a search budget, never contrasts asymmetric budgets, and offers no null-intervention demonstration.
related_work.known_defects: Its remedy is structurally limited to metric PAIRS: frontier analysis needs a second axis (entropy) to sweep against, and the paper itself gates it with a 'When Frontier Analysis is Valid' section. For a scalar, execution-grounded metric like pass@1+ there is no natural second axis, so their corrective simply does not transfer -- which is precisely the hole a budget-matched tuning curve fills. Also single-scale (GPT-2 small) with no evidence the reversal magnitude survives to 7B instruct models.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API + arXiv abs page (v1 2026-04-03) + full-text keyword scan of https://arxiv.org/html/2604.02718v1 (confirmed 'tuning the softmax temperature', 'ranking reversal', 'sweep across a range of softmax temperatures'); OpenReview search returned no matching venue record.

related_work.citation: Fang Wu et al. "Position: The Hidden Costs and Measurement Gaps of Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards." arXiv:2509.21882 (v1 2025-09-26; v3 2026-05-25).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (position paper); no venue found. v3 (2026-05-25) is post-cutoff but v1 is pre-cutoff, so the claim is not concurrent.

related_work.known_defects: Position-paper evidence base: reproductions are partial and the 'minimum standard' is a checklist without a quantitative instrument, so a compliant author can still protocol-shop. related_work.citation: Melanie Sclar, Yejin Choi, Yulia Tsvetkov, Alane Suhr. "Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design, or: How I learned to start worrying about prompt formatting." arXiv:2310.11324 (FormatSpread).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint per arXiv metadata retrieved here; commonly cited as ICLR 2024 but I did not confirm that on OpenReview, so treat the venue as unverified.
related_work.what_it_covers: Establishes the 'sensitivity exceeds claimed method gains' comparison in the prompt-formatting dimension, and provides a search procedure over the spurious-feature space.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Prompt format, not decoding protocol; autoregressive models; no diffusion; no budget accounting or expected-max estimator; no null intervention.
related_work.known_defects: Reports a spread/range rather than an expected max at a stated trial count, so it cannot be converted into a reporting rule. Also, 2509.01790 (EMNLP 2025) argues a large part of prompt sensitivity is an artifact of log-likelihood/rigid matching rather than the model -- an attack our execution-graded pass@1+ setting is immune to, which is worth stating explicitly as a strength of our substrate.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API + arXiv abs page. Venue NOT verified on OpenReview -- flagged in verification_notes.

related_work.citation: Felipe Maia Polo, Ronald Xu, Lucas Monteiro Paes, Yuekai Sun, Mikhail Yurochkin. "Efficient multi-prompt evaluation of LLMs" (PromptEval). arXiv:2405.17202; NeurIPS 2024.
related_work.venue_status: NeurIPS 2024 per arXiv comments; OpenReview search surfaced only a CoRR record and an ICML 2024 ES-FoMo-II workshop poster, so the main-conference record is unconfirmed by me.
related_work.what_it_covers: The closest prior art for our CORRECTIVE. Argues against finding a single prompt to evaluate with, and instead estimates the performance DISTRIBUTION across many prompt variants, then reports quantiles (median, top-95%) as robust metrics -- under a practical evaluation budget.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Prompt templates, not decoding protocol; MMLU/BBH/LMentry, not code; autoregressive; and it reports quantiles without pricing a search or exposing asymmetric budgets between compared systems.
related_work.known_defects: Reporting a quantile of a distribution is not the same as charging a trial count: two systems with different-sized grids can both report their median and still be incomparable. Our matched-k tuning-curve rule subsumes and repairs that. Also its IRT-style borrowing of strength across prompts is untested on strongly correlated cells like an NFE ladder.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API + arXiv abs page + OpenReview api2 notes/search (main-conference record not found).

related_work.citation: Yash Shah, Abhijit Chakraborty, Vivek Gupta. "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2607.24763.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; no OpenReview record found for this title. NOTE a metadata inconsistency: the arXiv ID is 2607.* but citation_date and the submission history both read v1 Thu 4 Jun 2026, with a comments field of 'updated version'. Either reading is post-cutoff, so concurrency is unaffected.
related_work.what_it_covers: Standardizes actual NFE, enforces multi-metric reporting, and explicitly controls stochasticity across 7 remasking strategies x LLaDA-8B-Base / Dream-7B-Base x 4 stochasticity levels x 3 step budgets on OpenWebText and LM1B. Finds temperature explains the majority of MAUVE variance (eta^2=0.91), that compute-matched comparison reverses several published rankings, and that a single temperature change buys 0.32 MAUVE -- more than the max gap between any two strategies at fixed temperature. Ships a 12-model leaderboard.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent, so it cannot preempt us; and it treats protocol as a factor to CONTROL, not a budget to CHARGE. I scanned the full v1 HTML: zero occurrences of 'expected max', 'trial', 'grid', 'best-of', or 'oracle'; the six 'budget' hits are all step/compute budgets. It also stays on OpenWebText/LM1B with MAUVE and generative perplexity -- no downstream task, no code, no pass@1, no execution grading.
related_work.known_defects: Rich follow-up surface: (a) its own leaderboard reports a per-model number selected from its factor grid, so the leaderboard is itself exposed to the max-selection bias it warns about; (b) MAUVE/genPPL on OpenWebText is a fluency-and-diversity construct, not task capability, so its 'rankings reverse' claim has never been shown to transfer to an execution-graded metric; (c) all findings are on BASE checkpoints, so nothing is known about instruct-tuned code models where users actually read pass@1.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API, arXiv abs page (citation_date, submission history, comments), full-text keyword scan of https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24763v1, OpenReview api2 search (no venue record).

related_work.citation: Thomas Bertolani, Davide Bucciarelli, Leonardo Zini, Marcella Cornia, Lorenzo Baraldi. "Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis." arXiv:2606.19475 (v1 2026-06-17, v2 2026-06-22).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; no OpenReview record found. Verified v1/v2 dates from arXiv submission history.
related_work.what_it_covers: Eight state-of-the-art DLMs x eight benchmarks (reasoning, coding, translation, knowledge, structured problems), plus analysis of denoising steps, context length, block size and parallel unmasking strategies, plus small-scale controlled comparisons.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent. Reports quality across inference-time factors with no inflation estimate and no budget-matched rule. More importantly it is a live INSTANCE of the practice we critique -- see known_defects.
related_work.known_defects: Its own Section 5.1 states that Table 2 'summarize[s] the peak performance achieved by each model under its best-performing configuration in terms of diffusion steps and block structure', and it then uses that table to compare three architectural PARADIGMS. That is a max over a per-model configuration grid, with the grid size differing across models (models exposing more knobs get more draws on the max), used to support cross-family conclusions. Full-text scan also found zero hits for 'inflat', 'sweep', 'maximum over' or 'default'. This is the cleanest, most citable, zero-GPU-cost follow-up target in the whole set.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API, arXiv abs page, full-text keyword scan of https://arxiv.org/html/2606.19475v2 (quoted sentence located verbatim), OpenReview api2 search.

related_work.citation: Stipe Frkovic, Metod Jazbec, Dan Zhang, Christian A. Naesseth, Ilija Bogunovic, Eric Nalisnick. "Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2606.12232; ICML 2026 workshops (SPIGM poster, AdaptFM poster).
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 workshop posters; verified on OpenReview (SPIGM note HIMiqnTqLD, venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/SPIGM; AdaptFM note Bew2D82sWR, venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/AdaptFM). No main-conference record.
related_work.what_it_covers: Revisits WINO post-hoc confidence remasking and finds little-to-no benefit over confidence-based unmasking alone under standard (shorter block length) decoding; under non-greedy decoding the benefit partly returns but diversity collapse worsens. Concludes benefits are 'highly setting-dependent'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent. Single method (WINO), and 'setting-dependent' is asserted qualitatively -- there is no estimator converting setting-dependence into an expected headline gain per trial, which is exactly the quantity our candidate supplies.
related_work.known_defects: Workshop-scale evidence on one method; no code benchmark; and it stops at the diagnosis without a reporting rule. It is the ideal empirical anchor for our claim: it establishes the precondition (large across-setting variance) under which our asymmetry mechanism converts into fake gains.

related_work.citation: Deep Gandhi et al. "Neither Parallel Nor Sequential: How DiffusionGemma Actually Commits Tokens." arXiv:2606.14620.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; verified v1 date from arXiv submission history.
related_work.what_it_covers: Instruments a shipped diffusion checkpoint's accept step and shows its apparent 'block size' is an artifact of analysis granularity -- 'the model's block size turns out to be an artifact of the measuring ruler rather than the architecture'. related_work.citation: Kristina Gligoric et al. "Mitigating LLM-based p-Hacking by Preregistering for the Next LLM." arXiv:2606.27687.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; verified v1 date from arXiv submission history.
related_work.what_it_covers: States the mechanism our candidate formalises, in almost the same words: 'a researcher can tune the prompts, decoding parameters, or output format until a desired result is reached'. Proposes preregistering against an unreleased future model, and shows the protocol blocks ~73% of hack transfers across 20 models x 11 configurations.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent. Its setting is LLMs as measurement instruments for social-science hypothesis tests, not LM benchmark leaderboards. Its remedy is procedural (preregistration + a future model) rather than an accounting instrument, and it never estimates the size of the gain a k-trial search buys on a capability benchmark.
related_work.known_defects: The remedy is unusable for benchmark method papers -- you cannot defer a HumanEval+ comparison to an unreleased model. That gap is our opening: the same threat model needs a POST-HOC accounting rule, not a preregistration ritual.

related_work.venue_status: arXiv comments read 'Submitted to MLSys2021'; I did not confirm acceptance. Treat as preprint/MLSys-submitted.

related_work.citation: Lovish Madaan et al. "Quantifying Variance in Evaluation Benchmarks." arXiv:2406.10229; NeurIPS 2024 RegML workshop poster (main-track ICLR 2025 submission rejected).
related_work.venue_status: Verified on OpenReview: RegML 2024 poster (note M9dCa4vYgp, venueid NeurIPS.cc/2024/Workshop/RegML) and an ICLR 2025 Rejected_Submission record (note E2RyjrBMVZ). So: workshop poster, not a main-conference paper.

related_work.citation: Akshat Gupta et al. "Automated Discovery Has No Universally Superior Harness." arXiv:2607.18235.

related_work.citation: Tushar Pandey et al. "When Classical Baselines Are Tuned as Carefully as the Quantum Model, Does Quantum Reservoir Computing Still Win?" arXiv:2607.09905.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; verified v1 date from arXiv submission history.
related_work.what_it_covers: The purest statement of the asymmetric-tuning critique in any field: 'the classical methods they compare against are often left in a basic, untuned state while the quantum model is carefully optimised', then gives the baseline 'the same size and the same amount of tuning effort' and finds the claimed advantage disappears. Ships a reusable matched-comparison checklist.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent, and in quantum reservoir computing at 11 qubits -- no LM, no diffusion, no code. Also matches tuning EFFORT qualitatively rather than deriving an expected-max-vs-k curve or estimating the inflation.
related_work.known_defects: Demonstrates the asymmetry repair without an estimator, so it cannot answer 'how many points does k=8 vs k=1 buy on a null method'. Excellent cross-field citation to show reviewers the critique is a recognised genre, not a niche complaint.

diff.differentiation_statement: No paper before 2026-05-07 prices an INFERENCE-TIME protocol search on a TEST-set task metric. The estimator we need already exists and is respected -- Dodge et al. (EMNLP 2019) defined expected performance as a function of trial budget, Tang et al. (ACL 2020) debiased it, and Lourie et al. (NAACL 2024, COLM 2025) gave it exact confidence bands and an asymptotic law -- but that entire line is about TRAINING hyperparameters scored on VALIDATION data under i.i.d. random search. We move it to a different object: a small, exhaustively enumerable, strongly correlated grid of decoding knobs (NFE x block size x unmasking algorithm x temperature x top_p x output-extraction convention), evaluated on the test set that headline numbers are read from, for masked-diffusion CODE models at 7B graded by execution rather than by a judge or a fluency proxy. The nearest diffusion-specific neighbour, Generative Frontiers (2604.02718, pre-cutoff), does establish that temperature tuning can reverse rankings -- but at GPT-2-small scale on OpenWebText with generative perplexity and entropy, and its remedy (sweep temperature, plot an entropy-perplexity frontier) is structurally confined to metric PAIRS and cannot transfer to a scalar pass@1+, which is exactly where a budget-matched tuning curve is the only available instrument. The nearest audit in spirit, A Sober Look (COLM 2025), standardizes and re-runs but -- verified by full-text scan -- contains no notion of budget, expected max, or tuning curve, so an author can comply with its multi-seed recommendations in full and still ship a best-of-eight-protocols number; closing that loophole is our contribution. The nearest budget-matched reporting rule, the RLVR position paper (2509.21882, pre-cutoff v1), matches SAMPLING ATTEMPTS, not configuration count. And the nearest null-system demonstration, Cheating Automatic LLM Benchmarks (ICLR 2025 Oral), exploits an LLM judge with an adversarial constant output; our null is a semantics-preserving refactor graded by unit tests, which removes the 'nobody would actually do that' defence. CaRE (2607.24763) and the DLM Experimental Analysis (2606.19475) are both concurrent (June 2026) and, on full-text inspection, both treat protocol as a factor to control or to maximise over rather than a budget to charge -- CaRE has zero occurrences of 'expected max', 'trial', 'grid' or 'best-of', and the Experimental Analysis explicitly reports 'peak performance achieved by each model under its best-performing configuration'. The differentiation is therefore: same statistical mechanism as an accepted 2019-2024 line, applied to a new and unpriced search space, on a new task surface and model family, with an asymmetric-budget framing and a live null demonstration that no prior work provides.

followup_openings.target_paper: Bertolani et al., "Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis" (arXiv:2606.19475, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Its headline cross-paradigm table is a maximum, not a measurement. Section 5.1 says Table 2 'summarize[s] the peak performance achieved by each model under its best-performing configuration in terms of diffusion steps and block structure', and the paper then uses that table to compare autoregressive vs diffusion vs hybrid paradigms. The number of configurations available differs by model -- checkpoints exposing more knobs (block size, parallel unmasking variants) get more draws on the max -- so the comparison is confounded by grid size. Full-text scan finds no discussion of this and no per-model trial counts.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-derive their comparison as tuning curves at matched k. For every model, publish (median, max, k) instead of a bare peak, using the debiased estimator with Lourie-style bands, and report which of their cross-architecture conclusions survive at k equalized to the smallest grid in the table. Cost is post-hoc analysis on our own factorial plus a request for their per-cell numbers.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts an abstract methodological worry into a concrete, dated, citable correction of a real 8-model x 8-benchmark table, and it is the single strongest reviewer-facing demonstration that the reporting rule changes conclusions rather than just tidying them.

followup_openings.target_paper: Shah, Chakraborty, Gupta, "CaRE" (arXiv:2607.24763, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: CaRE controls NFE, metrics and stochasticity but never charges the search; verified by full text (zero hits for expected max / trial / grid / best-of). Worse, its own 12-model leaderboard reports a per-model score drawn from its factor grid, so the leaderboard inherits the max-selection bias the paper warns about. Its evidence base is also OpenWebText/LM1B with MAUVE and generative perplexity on BASE checkpoints -- a fluency-and-diversity construct, not task capability -- so its flagship finding (temperature buys 0.32 MAUVE, exceeding the largest strategy gap) has never been shown to hold for a metric anyone deploys on.
followup_openings.our_fix: Port CaRE's factor set to execution-graded pass@1+ on HumanEval+/MBPP+ at 7B instruct scale, add the pricing layer CaRE lacks (an inflation curve E[max over k] minus single-default, with a 3-seed within-cell noise floor), and re-issue their leaderboard rows as matched-k tuning curves. Also test whether CaRE's compute-matching alone is sufficient: if rankings still flip within a fixed-NFE slice, then NFE standardization is necessary but not sufficient, which is a direct sharpening of their central claim.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It positions us as the natural completion of a concurrent framework rather than a competitor: CaRE standardizes the axes, we price the search over them, and we carry the result from MAUVE to a metric with a unit test behind it.

followup_openings.target_paper: Pynadath, Shi, Zhang, "Generative Frontiers" (arXiv:2604.02718, PRE-cutoff)
followup_openings.defect: Their corrective needs a second axis. Frontier analysis plots entropy against generative perplexity and the paper itself gates it with a 'When Frontier Analysis is Valid' section; for a scalar, execution-grounded metric such as pass@1+ there is no natural entropy axis to sweep against, so the remedy simply does not apply to the benchmarks that decide whether diffusion code models are adopted. They also never charge a search budget or quantify the expected gain from k trials, and all evidence is at GPT-2-small scale on OpenWebText, so there is no evidence the reversal magnitude survives to 7B instruct checkpoints.
followup_openings.our_fix: Establish the budget-matched tuning curve as the scalar-metric analogue of frontier analysis, explicitly framed as extending their argument to the regime where their tool is invalid, and replicate their ranking-reversal claim at 7B on pass@1+ to test scale transfer. Adopt their honest guard (report the entropy/degeneracy check so the reversal cannot be dismissed as diversity hacking) but attach a trial count to it.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the one pre-cutoff paper a reviewer could weaponise against us. Citing it as the motivating precedent and then showing precisely which regime it cannot reach converts the biggest positioning threat into our clearest statement of scope.

followup_openings.target_paper: Dodge et al. (EMNLP 2019) / Tang et al. (ACL 2020) / Lourie et al. (NAACL 2024)
followup_openings.defect: The whole estimator family assumes trials are exchangeable draws from a random-search distribution. An inference-time protocol grid violates this three ways: it is enumerated rather than sampled, it is small (k<=8 is the regime that matters for reporting, far from Lourie et al.'s asymptotic regime), and its cells are strongly correlated because factors like NFE are near-monotone in quality. Coverage of the exact confidence bands has never been checked under correlated-enumerated cells, and Tang et al.'s bias analysis was never revisited for this case.
followup_openings.our_fix: Report the inflation curve two ways -- bootstrap-over-cells under their exchangeability assumption, and the exact expected max computed by enumeration over the real grid -- and quantify the gap. Then run an empirical coverage check of the opda bands in the correlated-grid regime against our 3-seed within-cell noise floor. If coverage degrades, we have a methodological finding about their tool, not merely an application of it.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It upgrades the paper from 'we applied a 2019 estimator to a new field' to 'we identified a regime where the field's standard estimator is unvalidated, and we validated or repaired it'. That is the difference between a workshop note and a short paper reviewers argue for.

followup_openings.target_paper: Hochlehnert et al., "A Sober Look at Progress in Language Model Reasoning" (COLM 2025)
followup_openings.defect: Its corrective set (multi-seed, release artifacts, report standard deviations, avoid exact-match extraction) controls WITHIN-cell noise and leaves the ACROSS-cell selection channel entirely open. Full-text scan of v2 confirms no 'budget', 'expected max', 'tuning curve' or 'best-of'. A method author can therefore satisfy every one of its recommendations and still publish a best-of-eight-protocols headline. Coverage is also math reasoning on autoregressive models only.
followup_openings.our_fix: Extend the standard with the missing across-cell rule -- same number of protocol trials for every compared system, report (median, max, k) -- and demonstrate on our own substrate that the two channels are independent by showing a case where seed variance is small (passing their checks) while the k=8 inflation is large. Extend the task surface to execution-graded code and the model family to masked diffusion.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It makes our contribution a named, minimal amendment to a framework that already has community traction, which is a far easier sell than proposing a new standard from scratch.

followup_openings.target_paper: Zheng et al., "Cheating Automatic LLM Benchmarks: Null Models Achieve High Win Rates" (ICLR 2025 Oral)
followup_openings.defect: Their null exploits an LLM judge with an adversarially crafted constant output, which leaves the defence 'no honest researcher would submit that, and anyway our benchmark is execution-graded'. The demonstration therefore does not implicate ordinary, well-intentioned reporting on functional-correctness benchmarks.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the null intervention on an execution-graded benchmark with a provably semantics-preserving change -- an identity-equivalent decoding refactor or a no-op tie-break reordering in the unmasking rule, verified byte-identical in behaviour at fixed seed and protocol -- given k=8 protocol trials while the baseline gets its single default. Pre-register the null's provable no-op status and the exact grid before running. If it wins a headline-sized delta, the failure is shown to require no adversary and no judge, only an ordinary asymmetric search.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It is the paper's punchline, nearly free in GPU terms, and strictly stronger than the existing precedent because it closes the two escape hatches (adversarial input, judge-based metric) that let readers dismiss prior null demonstrations.

followup_openings.target_paper: Wu et al., "Position: The Hidden Costs and Measurement Gaps of RLVR" (arXiv:2509.21882, pre-cutoff v1)
followup_openings.defect: It identifies 'budget mismatch between RLVR and baseline evaluations' and proposes budget-matched saturation curves, but its budget is sampling attempts and compute -- the number of PROTOCOL CONFIGURATIONS tried is never treated as a budget. Its 'tax-aware minimum standard' is a checklist without a quantitative instrument, so a fully compliant author can still protocol-shop, and its reproductions are partial.
followup_openings.our_fix: Add the missing budget axis and supply the instrument: an inflation curve with a number on it, so that 'budget-matched' becomes checkable for configuration search and not only for attempts. State the two axes as orthogonal taxes and show, on our factorial, that matching attempts while leaving configurations unmatched still permits a null method to win.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It slots our accounting into an existing, sympathetic reform agenda and makes the contribution concrete where that agenda is only exhortative -- the reviewer question 'is this just another call for rigour?' is answered by an estimator.

diff.sharpened_claim: Inference-time protocol is an unpriced search space, and pricing it changes published conclusions. On masked-diffusion code models at 7B, we measure the inflation curve -- expected maximum pass@1+ over k randomly drawn cells of a crossed decoding grid (NFE x block size x unmasking algorithm x temperature x top_p x extraction convention), minus the single-default score -- using the debiased expected-performance estimator of Dodge/Tang with Lourie-style confidence bands, against a 3-seed within-cell noise floor. We report three results, in decreasing dependence on outside data. (1) The inflation at a modest k is large on an execution-graded metric: we already observe that a single knob change (top_p 1.0 -> 0.95) moves HumanEval by +14.6 points on Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B, larger than most published diffusion-LM method gains, and we quantify the full-grid k-curve of which that is one draw. (2) A provably null intervention -- an identity-equivalent decoding refactor, pre-registered as a no-op and verified byte-identical at fixed seed and protocol -- given k=8 protocol trials while the baseline is run at its single default, wins an apparent improvement on HumanEval+ and MBPP+. This requires no adversarial input and no LLM judge, only an ordinary asymmetric search, which is what distinguishes it from existing null-model demonstrations. (3) Applying the corrective -- report (median, max, k) per compared system at matched k rather than a bare best -- to the shipped unmasking algorithms (entropy vs maskgit_plus vs topk_margin) and to the peak-configuration table of a concurrent 8-model DLM survey, we identify which apparent rankings survive. Methodologically, we show that the field's standard tuning-curve estimator is unvalidated in this regime, because protocol grids are enumerated rather than sampled, small (k<=8, far from the asymptotic regime), and strongly correlated; we report the exact enumerated expected max alongside the bootstrap estimate, quantify the gap, and check band coverage. We deliberately do NOT lead with 'the field's progress is overstated': the ~30-paper delta survey is demoted to a pre-registered appendix with every claimed delta traceable to a specific table, so the paper's load-bearing claims stand on our own measured grid, the null demonstration, and the two re-priced comparisons.
diff.verification_notes: Could NOT verify: (a) Venue for Generative Frontiers (arXiv:2604.02718) -- no OpenReview record under that title; treated as an arXiv-only technical note. This is the one pre-cutoff paper whose claim comes closest to ours, so if it later turns out to have a main-venue record that does not change concurrency (2026-04-03 is pre-cutoff either way) but does raise its weight as prior art. I found it only via CaRE's reference list, not by any keyword search, which means other pre-cutoff diffusion-eval notes may exist that keyword search misses -- a residual risk I cannot fully close. (b) Venues for CaRE (2607.24763) and the DLM Experimental Analysis (2606.19475) -- no OpenReview records; treated as preprints. (c) CaRE has an internal metadata inconsistency: arXiv ID 2607.* but citation_date 2026/06/04 and submission history 'v1 Thu, 4 Jun 2026' with a comments field of 'updated version'. Both readings are post-2026-05-07 so concurrency is unaffected, but the exact first-public date is uncertain by up to ~7 weeks. (d) FormatSpread (2310.11324) is widely cited as ICLR 2024; I did not confirm that on OpenReview, so I recorded it as preprint-unverified. (e) PromptEval (2405.17202) claims NeurIPS 2024 in its arXiv comments, but OpenReview search returned only a CoRR record and an ICML 2024 ES-FoMo-II workshop poster, so the main-conference record is unconfirmed by me. (f) Kurenkov & Kolesnikov ICML 2022 Spotlight and Bouthillier et al. MLSys 2021 rest on arXiv comments fields only (pre-2025, so outside the mandatory-OpenReview rule). Tooling limits: Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so no S2 corroboration anywhere; arXiv's full-text search endpoint timed out through the proxy; DuckDuckGo HTML returned no parseable results. All findings therefore rest on the arXiv API, direct arXiv abs/HTML fetches, OpenReview api2 notes/search, and two ACL Anthology page fetches. Claims on weaker evidence: my assertion that no paper computes expected-max-over-k for inference-time decoding is a negative result from roughly 70 keyword queries across arXiv API and OpenReview -- reasonably strong but not exhaustive, and given that I found 2604.02718 only through a citation chain, I would recommend one more pass that walks the reference lists of CaRE, 2606.19475 and 2606.12232 before submission. feas.risk: The inflation curve turns out to be mostly item-sampling noise on n=164/n=378, not protocol sensitivity, so the paper reduces to the textbook fact that the max of 8 noisy binomials exceeds a single draw. I measured this directly: with ALL cells forced to an identical true pass rate, E[max over k=8] minus default is already 5.03 pt on HumanEval+ and 3.39 pt on MBPP+ -- larger than the candidate's own 2 pt kill threshold and comparable to the median published diffusion-LM gain the paper wants to overlay. Because the harness has no seed control and Dream is byte-deterministic at the flagship T=0.1 protocol, the plan's 3-seed floor is 0.00 pt and would silently license the entire binomial-noise term as 'protocol inflation'. That is the same failure class as Retraction 1 (a verifier that compared nothing) moved up to the statistics layer: an estimator that reports large inflation on a grid of eight identical protocols. Secondary risk: after correcting for the null floor, the surviving excess concentrates entirely in the NFE axis -- which CaRE already standardizes and which is monotone and legible -- leaving no contribution beyond a concurrent paper. Tertiary: the null intervention is not actually a no-op, because torch.topk tie-breaking at generation_utils.py:441 is index-order dependent on confidence plateaus, so a permutation wrapper silently becomes a real intervention and the punchline collapses on inspection.
feas.required_control: NULL-GRID CALIBRATION OF THE INFLATION ESTIMATOR: before reporting any inflation number, run the identical estimator on k cells that are provably the same protocol (bootstrap-resample the per-item pass/fail vector from one fixed cell's solutions_eval_results.json into k pseudo-cells sharing one true pass rate), publish that null curve as the estimator's own floor, and report every headline inflation and the null-intervention 'win' ONLY as excess over that floor -- restating the kill criterion in excess terms, since the raw floor I measured (5.03 pt HE+ / 3.39 pt MBPP+ at k=8) already exceeds the stated 2 pt threshold. This is the control that prevents our three retractions' shared pattern -- a measurement apparatus that returns a confident number while comparing nothing (Retraction 1), and an aggregate that silently absorbs the cases driving it (Retraction 3). It must be paired with two hard gates: (i) a pre-registered byte-identity assertion that the 'null' intervention produces identical token ids to baseline on all 164+378 tasks at fixed protocol before it is granted any search budget, since torch.topk tie-breaks by index and a permutation wrapper is not automatically a no-op; and (ii) publication of sigma_seed = 0.00 with the hash evidence at the flagship cell, so no reader mistakes a deterministic decoder's zero seed-variance for a tight noise floor.

lens.title: Joint Multi-Hole Infilling: the one thing FIM structurally cannot do
lens.claim: When two or more DISJOINT code holes are mutually dependent (a variable defined in hole A and consumed in hole B), filling them JOINTLY in one bidirectional denoising process beats filling them sequentially with the same model, and beats a matched autoregressive coder using FIM; the advantage grows with the number of holes k and with def-use distance. Corollary: multi-hole coupled infilling is the first task surface where a 7B dLLM strictly dominates a matched 7B AR code model at equal token cost.
lens.why_now: The entire infilling literature is SINGLE-span. DreamOn (2602.01326, ICLR 2026) evaluates HumanEval-Infilling single-line and multi-line -- both are ONE contiguous middle. CAL (2602.00476) searches for ONE optimal infilling length. Template Infilling (2510.13870, ACL 2026 Oral) places anchors but evaluates aggregate accuracy, never coupling between slots. arXiv queries for 'disjoint spans infilling', 'joint infilling', 'multi-span infilling', 'RandomSpanInfilling' return 0 or 0-relevant hits; only 2508.10111 (CFG constrained decoding) mentions multi-region infilling, as an algorithmic byproduct, with no coupled-hole quality measurement and no AR comparison. Yet this is the sharpest structural asymmetry available: AR FIM is defined as prefix-suffix-middle with exactly ONE middle. To fill two coupled holes an AR model must either serialize (hole 1 cannot see hole 2's eventual content) or resort to a placeholder-prompt hack. Meanwhile masked diffusion does it natively -- I verified Dream-Coder's sampler selects positions via mask_index = (x == mask_token_id) (models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B/generation_utils.py:411), i.e. arbitrary non-contiguous mask sets are already supported by the shipped checkpoint. This is an un-cashed capability with a shipped model that already implements the mechanism.
lens.experiment: Carve k in {1,2,3} coupled holes from HumanEval+ canonical solutions using def-use analysis. FEASIBILITY ALREADY PROVEN: I ran the ast-based carver on data/evalplus/HumanEvalPlus-v0.1.10.jsonl and 113/164 tasks have >=1 coupled def-use pair on distinct lines (e.g. HumanEval/1 'cnt' defined line 14, used lines 15 and 19). Stratify by def-use token distance. Four arms, all scored by evalplus.eval.untrusted_check (never a hand-rolled verifier): (a) Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B JOINT -- all k holes masked simultaneously, single diffusion run, bidirectional across holes; (b) Dream-Coder-Instruct SEQUENTIAL -- fill hole 1, commit, then hole 2, with hole 2 still masked during pass 1 (this isolates JOINTNESS within the same model and weights, the single most important control); (c) Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct FIM sequential (the matched AR baseline, and the AR ceiling); (d) Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with all holes shown as named placeholders in one prompt (AR's best available hack). Cost reported as cumulative_model_tokens over ALL tasks including truncated ones, using the proc() accessor (Retraction-3 discipline), never NFE. Replicate on MBPP+ and on the RandomSpanInfilling set now at data/infilling/HumanEval-RandomSpanInfilling.jsonl.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B; data/evalplus/HumanEvalPlus-v0.1.10.jsonl + MbppPlus-v0.2.0.jsonl; evalplus 0.3.1; scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py as the 8-way sharded harness skeleton; python ast + tree_sitter_python (both present). NEWLY PUT ON DISK BY ME: data/infilling/HumanEval-{SingleLine,MultiLine,RandomSpan}Infilling.jsonl (1033/5815/1640 items). MISSING -- FLAG: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct is on NEITHER wzc1 NOR zwfy6; I verified it is ungated on HF (14 files, ~15GB) and downloadable via the hy-proxy. COORDINATION RISK: .104 is already running a matched AR Qwen2.5-Coder baseline per the brief -- reuse that download and its protocol rather than duplicating. MINOR CODE WORK: Dream-Coder's sampler builds the canvas via F.pad(input_ids, (0, max_length - len)) at line 389, which appends masks on the right; multi-hole needs the canvas constructed directly instead of via that pad path. ~20 lines.
lens.kill_criterion: If arm (a) JOINT is within noise of arm (b) SEQUENTIAL at k=2 and k=3 (say |delta pass@1| < 0.03 with overlapping bootstrap CIs, on >=113 carved HE+ tasks plus MBPP+ replication), then the shipped checkpoint does not actually exploit cross-hole bidirectional conditioning and the positive claim is dead. Secondary kill: if arm (d), the AR placeholder-prompt hack, matches or beats (a) at equal token cost, the capability confers no practical advantage. Either outcome is reportable as a measured negative, but the headline claim would be withdrawn.
lens.builds_on: Direct follow-up on DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026 Poster) and on CAL (arXiv:2602.00476). Defect we repair: both treat infilling as a SINGLE-span problem, so they never test the one regime where bidirectional conditioning is irreplaceable -- mutually dependent fills at disjoint sites. Also repairs the missing-AR-baseline defect in arXiv:2510.04605 (the only diffusion-beats-AR-on-code-editing claim), which our own audit found compares commercial Mercury-Diffusion-7B against general-purpose Llama3-8B with no code-model control and cites LLaDA via a fabricated astrophysics arXiv id.

related_work.citation: Melcer et al., "Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars", arXiv:2508.10111 (Sec 4.2 "Fill-In-the-Middle and Multi-Region-Infilling", Table 1: 1-mri/2-mri/3-mri)
related_work.venue_status: arXiv preprint (v1 only, no venue comment on arXiv abs page; no OpenReview venueid found). Verified via arXiv abs page comments field (empty) + OpenReview title search returning no venue record.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE CLOSEST WORK, and much closer than the candidate's brief admits. It constructs exactly the proposed benchmark ladder: takes HumanEval (C++ translation), removes 1/2/3 random spans, and reports pass@1 functional correctness at each k. Vanilla (unconstrained) pass@1 collapses monotonically with k for every AR model: StarCoder2-7B 53.8 -> 20.5 -> 7.5; DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B 64.8 -> 29.8 -> 11.9; DeepSeek-Coder-33B 69.8 -> 29.8 -> 12.6. It also states 'No prior work supports multi-region infilling (mri) or diffusion LLM constraining with CFGs', and evaluates Dream-7B, DreamCoder-7B, DiffuCoder-7B, LLaDA-8B.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its dLLM section (4.3) is a DIFFERENT task set: full-function C++ generation, JSON extraction, SMILES -- NOT the k-mri ladder. So multi-region infilling is measured ONLY on AR FIM models, and diffusion is measured only on single-region/from-scratch tasks. There is therefore NO diffusion-vs-AR comparison on multi-region infilling anywhere in the paper, no joint-vs-sequential within-model control, no def-use coupling construct (spans are RANDOM, not selected for mutual dependency), no def-use-distance stratification, and no token-cost accounting for the quality comparison (it reports only runtime overhead of constraining). Python is untested (C++ only).
related_work.known_defects: (1) Spans are removed at RANDOM, so 'multi-region' does not entail COUPLING -- the paper cannot separate 'k holes is harder because there is less context' from 'k holes is harder because holes are mutually dependent'. Our def-use carve fixes exactly this. (2) The k-mri degradation numbers are the paper's BASELINE, incidental to its actual contribution (CFG constrained decoding); no analysis of why AR collapses. (3) dLLMs are excluded from the k-mri ladder despite being the paper's headline novelty -- an obvious missing cell that we fill. (4) 256-token abort cap plus 100-rejection cap conflates capability failure with budget truncation (the same class of error as our own Retraction-3), and aborted instances are scored as failures in Con.- without cost accounting. (5) Constraining is confounded with completion-sampling (Con. vs Con.-), so the functional gains (+2.4pp) cannot be attributed cleanly.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abs; full text via ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2508.10111 -- grepped 'multi-region' (5 hits), extracted Sec 4.2 setup paragraph and Table 1 verbatim, extracted Sec 4.3 in full to confirm dLLM tasks are C++/json/smiles not mri; OpenReview title search (no venue record); arXiv abs comments field empty.

related_work.citation: Fried et al., "InCoder: A Generative Model for Code Infilling and Synthesis", arXiv:2204.05999, ICLR 2023
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2023 (verified: arXiv abs comments field reads 'ICLR 2023. v3: camera-ready that includes PLBART and OpenAI baselines').
related_work.what_it_covers: The strongest prior-art threat to the framing 'AR FIM structurally cannot do multi-hole'. InCoder's causal-masking objective samples the number of spans from a truncated Poisson (support [1,256], single span ~50% of the time), and it explicitly claims: 'We can also infill multiple dependent regions, e.g., generate imports required by a function that the model is generating' and 'Our objective, in contrast, allows infilling multiple regions of code' (contrasting itself with Bavarian et al. FIM). Sentinel format <Mask:0>...<Mask:1>...<Mask:0> B <EOM> <Mask:1> D <EOM> supports arbitrarily many named regions. Its variable-renaming benchmark (CodeXGLUE) is multi-region and shows CM infilling 30.6 vs L-R single 18.4 vs L-R rerank 23.5.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its only quantitative infilling evals with functional testing (HumanEval single-line, multi-line) are SINGLE contiguous region; multi-region appears in the objective, in Appendix B.2 format notes, and in a qualitative figure. Variable renaming is scored by exact-match ACCURACY, not execution. No k-ladder (k=1,2,3), no joint-vs-sequential ablation, no def-use coupling construct or distance stratification, no token-cost accounting, and no diffusion comparison (predates masked diffusion code LMs). Model is 6.7B fairseq-era, ~15 HumanEval pass@1 -- far below our regime.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The multi-region capability is CLAIMED but never functionally measured -- 'multiple dependent regions' rests on one qualitative figure. Our fix: a k-ladder scored by evalplus untrusted_check. (2) Even in the sentinel format, InCoder still generates regions SEQUENTIALLY left-to-right at the end of the string, so region B is written without seeing region D's eventual content -- exactly our SEQUENTIAL arm, and InCoder never contrasts it against anything joint. (3) Variable renaming uses exact match, which conflates 'wrong name' with 'consistent but different name' -- an execution metric would score consistent renaming as correct. (4) Poisson mean 1 means the multi-region regime is severely undertrained relative to its claimed generality.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page for date/venue comment; full text via ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2204.05999 -- grepped and read verbatim passages on Poisson span count, 'infill multiple dependent regions', Appendix B.2 sentinel format, Table 4 variable renaming, and confirmed the single-line/multi-line HumanEval eval is one contiguous region.

related_work.known_defects: (1) Quality table has NO compute accounting -- diffusion mask length is fixed at 64 by default and DreamOn's expand/delete loop adds a variable number of forward passes, so the AR-vs-diffusion comparison is not equal-cost. Our fix: cumulative_model_tokens over all tasks including truncated ones. (2) 'Surpasses Qwen2.5-Coder on multi-line' rests on 63.8 vs 58.7 = 5.1pp with no confidence intervals and n=5815 items derived from only 164 base problems (heavy within-problem correlation -> the effective n is far smaller than it looks). (3) The multi-line gain is confounded with the length-control mechanism, which is precisely what mask-size mismatch penalises -- so the comparison flatters DreamOn on the axis it optimises. (4) Untested on a benchmark where AR is structurally handicapped rather than merely mask-length-sensitive; our k-hole ladder supplies that.

related_work.citation: Leang et al. (McDiffuSE), "Can I Have Your Order? Monte-Carlo Tree Search for Slot Filling Ordering in Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2602.12586
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 -- verified via OpenReview api2 notes/search returning venue 'ICML 2026 regular'; corroborated by arXiv abs comments field '8 pages, ICML2026'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Directly adjacent and NOT in the candidate's brief. Formulates multi-slot plan-and-infill as sequential decision making over K masked slots (example: K=8 slots for an MBPP solution) and optimises the ORDER via MCTS. Explicitly motivated by 'interdependent tokens generated simultaneously without mutual conditioning' -- i.e. it accepts that joint filling of coupled slots HURTS, the opposite prior to ours. Reports +3.2% over AR baselines, +8.0% over baseline plan-and-infill, +19.5% MBPP; also reports token reduction (MBPP -88.05%, HumanEval -75.19%) vs the AR baseline. Its qualitative analysis shows ReFusion filling slots 1,2,3 simultaneously and committing to a wrong import.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Slots are a decomposition of the WHOLE response being generated from scratch, not holes carved from an otherwise-complete program, so there is no surrounding right-context and no def-use coupling construct. It optimises ORDER among sequential fills; it never runs a clean k-ladder of JOINT (all holes masked in one denoising process) vs SEQUENTIAL (commit hole 1, then hole 2) at matched model and matched cost. No FIM AR baseline (its AR baselines are Llama-3.1-8B/Qwen2.5-7B/Qwen3-8B doing standard generation, not Qwen2.5-Coder doing FIM). No evalplus-grade functional metric on carved holes.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Its abstract's own finding -- 'McDiffuSE predominantly follows SEQUENTIAL ordering' -- is evidence AGAINST our positive claim and MUST be engaged, not ignored: it suggests the shipped weights may not exploit cross-slot joint conditioning, which is exactly our stated kill criterion. Framing our study as adjudicating this is the highest-value move. (2) MCTS look-ahead cost is large and its token-cost table counts output tokens, not simulation forward passes, so the '-64.77% tokens' claim omits search compute -- a textbook accounting-that-flatters defect we can avoid with cumulative_model_tokens. (3) Slot boundaries are defined by the authors' partition with no stated rule ('how slots are defined' absent from full text), so the difficulty of the slot decomposition is unaudited. (4) Non-code AR baselines make the code claims (MBPP/HumanEval) weakly grounded.

related_work.citation: Liu et al., "Breaking the Factorization Barrier in Diffusion Language Models" (CoDD), arXiv:2603.00045
related_work.venue_status: arXiv preprint (v3 2026-07-18; no venue comment verified).
related_work.what_it_covers: The mechanism-level reason our positive claim might FAIL: the 'factorization barrier' -- tokens predicted simultaneously are assumed independent, so joint filling of mutually dependent positions is structurally penalised unless the output distribution is made non-factorized. CoDD adds a tractable probabilistic inference layer to model joint dependencies.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No code-infilling task surface, no multi-hole holes-in-a-program setting, no AR FIM comparison. Does not test whether a SHIPPED checkpoint (Dream-Coder-7B) exhibits the barrier on coupled code holes specifically.
related_work.known_defects: Its framing predicts our arm (a) JOINT should LOSE to arm (b) SEQUENTIAL on coupled holes -- which makes our kill criterion a genuinely informative test of published theory rather than a mere null. Related: arXiv:2509.22738 'Enabling Approximate Joint Sampling in Diffusion LMs' (2025-09-25) shows unmasking more tokens per pass moves the sample away from the true joint and drops accuracy, on Dream-7B-Base/Instruct/Coder specifically. Neither work tests the coupled-code-hole case. Our fix: report joint-vs-sequential at matched cumulative_model_tokens and per-step parallelism, so a negative is attributable to the factorization barrier rather than to budget.
