related_work.citation: Du et al., "GLM: General Language Model Pretraining with Autoregressive Blank Infilling", arXiv:2103.10360 (ACL 2022); Aghajanyan et al., "CM3: A Causal Masked Multimodal Model of the Internet", arXiv:2201.07520
related_work.venue_status: GLM: ACL 2022 (widely known; arXiv v2 2021). CM3: arXiv preprint 2022-01-19. Venue for CM3 not verified in this session.
related_work.what_it_covers: The ancestral multi-blank AR lineage. GLM pretrains on autoregressive blank infilling with 2D positional encodings and explicitly allows an ARBITRARY ORDER to predict multiple spans. CM3's causal masking (which InCoder adopts) masks several spans and regenerates them at the end of the string with bidirectional context.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Pretraining-objective papers: no code-execution benchmark, no coupled def-use holes, no k-ladder with pass@1, no cost accounting, no diffusion comparison. Their 'arbitrary order over multiple spans' is a training-time property, never evaluated as a coupled-fill CAPABILITY.
related_work.known_defects: Their existence forbids the strong claim 'multi-hole is something only diffusion can do' -- the honest claim is about JOINT (all holes visible to each other in one denoising process) versus SERIALISED multi-span filling, which is what every one of these AR objectives actually does. This is a framing repair we must make before submission, and it is also what makes arm (b) the load-bearing control.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list fetch for both (titles, v1 dates, abstracts). GLM's ACL 2022 venue is asserted from general knowledge, NOT verified in this session -- see verification_notes.

diff.differentiation_statement: No paper before 2026-05-07 measures, with an execution-based metric, whether a masked diffusion code LM benefits from filling MUTUALLY DEPENDENT holes JOINTLY rather than SEQUENTIALLY, at matched model, matched weights, and matched token cost. Four bodies of work bracket this gap without closing it. (1) Melcer et al. (2508.10111) builds precisely the k-in-{1,2,3}-region HumanEval infilling ladder we propose and shows AR pass@1 collapsing monotonically with k (DeepSeek-Coder-33B: 69.8 -> 29.8 -> 12.6), but its regions are RANDOM rather than def-use-coupled, and -- decisively -- it runs the k-mri ladder only on AR FIM models, while its diffusion section evaluates full C++/JSON/SMILES generation instead; so the diffusion-vs-AR cell on multi-region infilling is empty in the very paper that named the task. (2) InCoder (ICLR 2023) and the GLM/CM3 lineage do support multi-region infilling in the OBJECTIVE and even claim 'multiple dependent regions', but their only functionally graded infilling evals are single contiguous spans, their multi-region evidence is a qualitative figure plus an exact-match renaming benchmark, and their generation is still serialised region-by-region -- i.e. they instantiate our SEQUENTIAL control and never contrast it with anything joint. (3) DreamOn (ICLR 2026 Poster) and CAL are strictly single-middle: a full-text grep of DreamOn for 'multi-span', 'disjoint', 'multiple spans' returns zero hits, and 'multi-line' denotes one contiguous multi-line middle. (4) McDiffuSE (ICML 2026) does operate on K masked slots but optimises the ORDER of sequential fills, on slots that partition a from-scratch response rather than holes carved from a complete program, with no FIM AR baseline. The single genuinely close result -- 'multi-site editing: diffusion 84% vs AR 32%' -- is an anonymous ACL ARR 2026 May submission first public 2026-05-21, i.e. CONCURRENT under the 2026-05-07 cutoff; and it differs in three reviewable ways regardless: a 1.5B MDLM backbone versus our 7B shipped Dream-Coder checkpoint, exact-match rather than execution grading, and diffusion-vs-AR rather than the within-model joint-vs-sequential control that is the only design able to isolate jointness from model identity. Our contribution is that control plus a coupling construct (def-use pairs carved by AST analysis, 113/164 HumanEval+ tasks verified feasible), stratification by def-use distance, and Retraction-3-compliant cumulative_model_tokens accounting including truncated tasks. One framing repair is mandatory: because GLM/CM3/InCoder do serialise multiple spans and A3 (2601.13228) adapts AR to any-order any-subset prediction, the claim cannot be 'AR structurally cannot do multi-hole'; it must be 'standard FIM prompting admits exactly one middle, so multi-hole forces AR to serialise or to hack a placeholder prompt, and we measure what that costs'.

followup_openings.target_paper: Melcer et al., Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with CFGs, arXiv:2508.10111 (Sec 4.2 / Table 1)
followup_openings.defect: The paper builds the k-in-{1,2,3} multi-region-infilling ladder on HumanEval and shows AR pass@1 collapsing with k, but (a) removes spans at RANDOM so multi-region never entails COUPLING, (b) evaluates the ladder only on AR FIM models while its diffusion section switches to full C++/JSON/SMILES generation, leaving the diffusion-vs-AR mri cell empty, (c) caps generation at 256 tokens / 100 rejections and scores aborts as failures with no cost accounting -- conflating capability failure with budget truncation, and (d) tests C++ only.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the same k in {1,2,3} ladder but with holes selected by def-use analysis so coupling is the manipulated variable, add a RANDOM-span control at matched k and matched total masked-token count to separate 'less context' from 'mutual dependency', put Dream-Coder-7B on the ladder (the cell they left empty), grade with evalplus untrusted_check, replicate in Python on HumanEval+ and MBPP+, and report cumulative_model_tokens over ALL tasks including budget-truncated ones via the proc()/failure_process accessor.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This converts our study from 'a new benchmark' into 'the missing row of an existing published table', which is far easier for a reviewer to accept and gives us their five AR models as free comparison points. Their random-span numbers also become our control arm, so the coupled-vs-random contrast is the paper's cleanest single figure and directly answers the obvious 'is it coupling or just less context?' objection.

followup_openings.target_paper: Anonymous, Discrete Diffusion Models for Code (ACL ARR 2026 May, forum Ni6xxPzBlz) -- CONCURRENT, first public 2026-05-21
followup_openings.defect: Its headline complementarity claim -- multi-site editing diffusion 84% vs AR 32% -- is scored by EXACT MATCH (so a functionally correct edit using a different identifier scores zero), uses a 1.5B Qwen2.5-Coder MDLM backbone, compares diffusion-vs-AR rather than joint-vs-sequential (so jointness is confounded with paradigm), and prices a 16/48-candidate sampling pipeline against single-shot AR without equal-token normalisation.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run the multi-site regime at 7B on a shipped checkpoint, replace exact match with evalplus untrusted_check, add the within-model JOINT-vs-SEQUENTIAL arm that isolates jointness at identical weights, and normalise all arms by cumulative_model_tokens so candidate-sampling arms cannot buy quality with unaccounted compute.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Because it is concurrent it does not preempt us, but it does something better: it makes our result a scale-and-metric generalisation test of a live claim. If 84-vs-32 survives at 7B under execution grading we corroborate and sharpen it; if it collapses (plausible, since the AR ceiling at 7B is much higher -- Qwen2.5-Coder-7B hits 92.6 on HumanEval-Infilling single-line per DreamOn) we have a replication-failure result with a clear mechanism. Either way the within-model control is ours alone and is the thing a reviewer will say the concurrent paper was missing.

followup_openings.target_paper: Leang et al. (McDiffuSE), ICML 2026, arXiv:2602.12586
followup_openings.defect: It concludes that 'McDiffuSE predominantly follows SEQUENTIAL ordering' while non-sequential fills are only occasionally essential -- an explicit prior AGAINST joint filling helping -- yet it never runs the clean adjudicating experiment (all-holes-joint vs strictly-sequential at matched model and matched cost). Its token-efficiency table counts output tokens while omitting MCTS simulation forward passes, so the -64.77% token claim flatters the method. Slot boundaries come from an unstated authorial partition.
followup_openings.our_fix: Make our arm (a)-vs-(b) contrast the direct adjudication of their observation, on holes with a MECHANICALLY DEFINED coupling criterion (AST def-use) rather than hand-chosen slots, and report all search/denoising forward passes inside cumulative_model_tokens so no arm hides compute. Stratifying by def-use distance turns their binary observation into a curve: predict where sequential order suffices and where jointness is required.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the strongest available framing. Instead of asserting a positive claim that a published ICML paper's analysis casts doubt on, we position the study as resolving a live disagreement between two published priors -- McDiffuSE and the factorization-barrier line (CoDD 2603.00045, approximate-joint-sampling 2509.22738) predict joint filling LOSES; Dream-Coder's own motivation predicts it WINS. A measured answer either way is publishable, which makes the kill criterion a result rather than a dead end.

followup_openings.target_paper: DreamOn, arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026 Poster
followup_openings.defect: Its main quality table (Table 1) carries NO compute accounting: diffusion mask length is fixed at 64 by default and the expand/delete loop adds a variable number of forward passes (its own ablation shows steps swinging 122.8 -> 52.4), so 'DreamOn surpasses Qwen2.5-Coder on multi-line' (63.8 vs 58.7, 5.1pp) is neither equal-cost nor accompanied by confidence intervals -- and the 5815 multi-line items derive from only 164 base problems, so within-problem correlation makes the effective n far smaller than reported.
followup_openings.our_fix: Report every arm at matched cumulative_model_tokens with bootstrap CIs clustered BY BASE PROBLEM rather than by carved item (this correlation trap applies to our own 113-task carve too), and add a cost-matched re-analysis of the single-hole regime so our multi-hole numbers sit on the same axis as theirs.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It repairs the accounting of our declared parent work while establishing the cost convention our own headline needs. It also inoculates us against the exact error we already retracted three times (NFE as a cross-family unit; dropping truncated tasks), and clustered CIs are the difference between a defensible k-ladder and 5815 pseudo-replicates.

followup_openings.defect: InCoder claims 'our objective allows infilling multiple regions' and 'multiple dependent regions', but the claim is never functionally measured: its execution-graded infilling evals are single contiguous spans, multi-region appears only in Appendix B.2 format notes and a qualitative figure, and its multi-region variable-renaming benchmark is scored by exact-match ACCURACY -- which marks a consistently renamed, functionally correct program wrong. Training samples span count from a Poisson with mean 1, so the multi-region regime is undertrained relative to the generality claimed.
followup_openings.our_fix: Give the 14-year-old multi-region claim its first execution-graded test on a modern coder, and reframe variable-consistency as a functional task (rename at 2-3 coupled sites; pass only if tests pass), which is exactly what def-use-coupled holes measure. Cite InCoder's sentinel format as the historical instantiation of our SEQUENTIAL arm.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It supplies the framing repair our claim urgently needs -- multi-span AR infilling has existed since 2022, so the contribution must be JOINT vs SERIALISED, not 'only diffusion can' -- and it hands us a well-cited ICLR paper whose central unmeasured claim we are the first to test. That is a cleaner reviewer story than novelty-by-absence.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2510.04605 (Diffusion LLMs for SE) and arXiv:2601.13228 (A3: AR rivals diffusion at any-order)
followup_openings.defect: 2510.04605 is the only pre-existing broad 'diffusion beats AR on SE' claim and it compares commercial Mercury-Diffusion-7B against general-purpose AR Llama3-8B with no code-model control (plus a fabricated LLaDA citation pointing at an astrophysics paper). Symmetrically, A3 argues AR matches diffusion at any-order generation but demonstrates it only on story infilling and QA -- never on code with execution grading -- and needs an extra adaptation-training stage its diffusion baselines do not get.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the matched 7B code-model AR control both papers lack: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with native FIM (sequential) plus the placeholder-prompt hack, execution-graded, equal token cost. Add Self-Infilling (ICML 2024, 2311.17972) as a non-monotonic AR arm so the AR ceiling is not artificially low, and treat A3-style any-order AR as the acknowledged stronger-AR caveat (an optional fifth arm if compute allows).
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It makes ours the first fair 7B code-model-to-code-model comparison on a coupled-edit surface, which is the load-bearing control missing from BOTH the pro-diffusion and pro-AR sides of this argument. Concretely: adding Self-Infilling is what stops a reviewer from dismissing arm (d) as a strawman, and it is cheap since it needs the same Qwen2.5-Coder download already being fetched on .104 -- coordinate with that agent rather than re-downloading, since the model is confirmed absent from BOTH wzc1 and zwfy6.

diff.sharpened_claim: On code holes that are MUTUALLY DEPENDENT by def-use analysis, we measure -- for the first time with an execution-based metric and at matched token cost -- whether filling k holes JOINTLY in one bidirectional denoising pass beats filling them SEQUENTIALLY with identical weights, thereby supplying the diffusion row that arXiv:2508.10111 left empty in its own 1/2/3-region HumanEval infilling ladder. Three design choices carry the paper regardless of the sign of the result. First, the within-model joint-vs-sequential control isolates JOINTNESS from model identity, which no prior work does: the concurrent ACL ARR 2026 May submission's 'multi-site editing: diffusion 84% vs AR 32%' confounds the two, and InCoder/GLM/CM3 only ever instantiate the sequential side. Second, a def-use-coupled arm versus a random-span arm at matched k and matched masked-token count separates 'coupling' from 'less surrounding context' -- the confound that makes 2508.10111's monotone AR collapse (DeepSeek-Coder-33B 69.8 -> 29.8 -> 12.6 across k=1,2,3) uninterpretable as a coupling result. Third, all arms are priced in cumulative_model_tokens over ALL tasks including budget-truncated ones, so no arm buys quality with unaccounted forward passes. We adjudicate a live published disagreement rather than assert a novel capability: Dream-Coder's own motivation (simultaneously modify signatures and update call sites) predicts joint filling wins, while McDiffuSE (ICML 2026, finding that optimal slot orders are 'predominantly sequential') and the factorization-barrier line (CoDD arXiv:2603.00045; approximate-joint-sampling arXiv:2509.22738, measured on Dream-Coder itself) predict it loses because simultaneously predicted tokens are modelled as independent. We report the crossover in def-use distance at which jointness starts to matter, and the AR side is a genuine ceiling -- Qwen2.5-Coder-7B FIM sequential, its placeholder-prompt variant, AND Self-Infilling (ICML 2024) non-monotonic decoding -- so the framing is the defensible one: standard FIM admits exactly one middle, forcing AR to serialise or hack, and we measure what that costs rather than claiming AR structurally cannot.

blocking_gaps: KILL CRITERION IS BELOW DETECTION LIMIT. I ran the pilot myself (GPU2, T=0, alg=entropy, steps=n_masks, 40 def-use-carved HE+ tasks, k=2, splice roundtrip asserted): JOINT and SEQUENTIAL produced BYTE-IDENTICAL fills on 27/40 = 67.5% of tasks. Identical fills are forced-concordant pairs, so only ~32.5% of items can flip at all. McNemar MDE on n=113 is ~0.105 pass@1 (~0.096 MBPP+ k=2, ~0.116/0.119 at k=3) -- the stated |delta|<0.03 threshold is 3.5x BELOW what n=113 can resolve. As specified the experiment cannot distinguish its hypothesis from its null; 'within noise' would be a property of the sample size, not of the model.

'JOINT' AS SPECIFIED IS ALREADY SEQUENTIAL INTERNALLY. models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B/generation_utils.py:437 computes number_transfer_tokens = int(num_mask_token * (1 - s/t)). I traced commits per step via generation_tokens_hook_func: at steps==n_masks the mask-count trace is [9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2,0] = ONE position committed per forward pass. Multi-position commits only appear at steps<n_masks (steps=4 -> [9,7,5,3,0]; steps=2 -> [9,5,0]). So the factorization barrier is exercised by the STEPS axis, not by the masking layout. Masking two holes at steps=s1+s2 buys bidirectional VISIBILITY (which arm b also largely has) but zero simultaneous prediction -- which is precisely the mechanism CoDD/2509.22738 predict should hurt. The experiment as written manipulates the wrong variable.

THE ANNOUNCED COROLLARY IS ALREADY FALSIFIED ON DISK, AT k=1. /apdcephfs_zwfy6/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft_104/outputs/infilling_single_line/ holds 6 arms x n=1033 with grader_self_test.trustworthy=true: qwen_fim (AR native FIM) .7638 @ 239 tokens_fed/task BEATS dream_fim .7115 @ 2035 and dreamon_oracle .7590 @ 5827. Suffix-visibility gain is +.299 for diffusion vs +.231 for AR -- comparable, so bidirectional context is a property of the TASK FRAMING, not a diffusion monopoly. This is logged as Retraction 5 in /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md. 'First task surface where a 7B dLLM strictly dominates a matched 7B AR coder at equal token cost' begins 5.2 points and 8.5x cost behind at k=1.

SEQUENTIAL ARM AS BRIEFED CONFOUNDS JOINTNESS WITH DENOISING SCHEDULE. My own first pilot pass hit this: running the same canvas at steps=s1 to get hole1 then re-running for hole2 gives arm (b) a different per-step transfer fraction AND a different total NFE than arm (a). A difference would be unattributable. The clean control requires generation_tokens_hook_func (verified a real public kwarg at generation_utils.py:305) to force-remask hole2 at EVERY step of pass 1 -- I verified this works: 'hole2 still masked after pass1: True' with hole1 fully resolved. The brief does not mention the hook and budgets ~20 lines for canvas construction only.

feas.concrete_plan:
GO, but as a REFRAMED study. The candidate's variable (masking layout) is inert on this checkpoint; the live variable is per-step COMMIT PARALLELISM. Reuse the k=1 rung already on disk instead of re-running it.

STEP 0 (CPU, ~1h) -- Pin the grader, kill the version skew.
Run everything on LOCAL /opt/conda/envs/dllm-env/bin/python (evalplus 0.3.1). Do NOT grade on .73/.104 .venv_dream (0.1.0.dev1). If .73 GPUs are used for generation, ship solutions.jsonl back to wzc1 and grade on LOCAL only. Record evalplus.__version__ in every score.json.

STEP 1 (CPU, ~3h) -- Build the carver as a standalone, auditable artifact.
New file /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/scripts/carve_coupled_holes.py. Use python ast (tree_sitter not needed; ast parsed 164/164 HE+ and 378/378 MBPP+ with zero failures). Emit, per item: task_id, k, hole line indices, the coupling variable, def-use token distance, pre/between/post segments, per-hole oracle token counts, and a RANDOM-span twin at matched k and matched total masked-token count. VERIFIED YIELD (I ran this): HE+ k>=2 113/164, k>=3 93/164; MBPP+ k>=2 136/378, k>=3 88/378. Assert pre+m1+between+m2+post == prompt+canonical_solution for every emitted item (my pilot asserted this and it held). Token-boundary drift on separately-encoded splices measured 0/260 on HE+, so segment-wise encoding is safe -- but re-assert per item.

STEP 2 (~30 min GPU) -- Reframe the arms around the axis that actually moves.
Verified sampler fact: generation_utils.py:437 commits exactly ONE position per step when steps==n_masks. So run a PARALLELISM LADDER, not a layout contrast:
  (a1) joint canvas, steps = s1+s2  -> 1 commit/step (bidirectional visibility, zero simultaneity)
  (a2) joint canvas, steps = (s1+s2)/2 -> 2 commits/step
  (a3) joint canvas, steps = (s1+s2)/4 -> ~4 commits/step
  (b)  CLEAN sequential: force-remask hole2 at every step of pass 1 via generation_tokens_hook_func (verified working), commit hole1, then a second pass for hole2 with matched per-step transfer fraction and reported total NFE.
  (c)  qwen_fim sequential -- REUSE the existing k=1 protocol in /apdcephfs_zwfy6/.../dllm_draft_104/scripts/generate_infilling.py run_qwen(use_suffix=True); extend to k holes by serialising two FIM calls.
  (d)  qwen placeholder-prompt, all holes named in one prompt.
  (e)  Self-Infilling (2311.17972) non-monotonic AR -- only if (a2)/(a3) show signal; otherwise cite as unrun.
Register ForwardCostTracker (scripts/generate_evalplus_ar.py:108) on every arm so tokens_fed and attended_context_sum are measured identically across families, as the k=1 run already did.

STEP 3 (~2 GPU-h) -- Power gate BEFORE the full run. This is the decision point.
On the 113 HE+ k=2 items, run (a1) vs (b) and (a3) vs (b) and count DISCORDANT pairs (one passes, other fails). My pilot predicts ~32.5% eligible-to-differ, i.e. ~37 discordant at best, MDE ~0.105. GATE: if discordant pairs < 25 for (a3) vs (b), the experiment is underpowered by construction -> STOP and write the mechanism note (Step 6) instead of the k-ladder. Do not proceed to MBPP+ or k=3 on hope.

STEP 4 (~6 GPU-h, only if Step 3 gate passes) -- Full ladder.
k in {2,3} x {coupled, random-twin} x 5 arms on HE+ (113/93) and MBPP+ (136/88). Node: .73 is fully idle (8x H20, verified 0% util) and sees the harness on the same zwfy6 disk; LOCAL GPUs 2,4,6,7 are free. Use the existing 8-way sharding pattern (CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=$g RANK=$g LOCAL_RANK=0) and the shard-count assertion from _run_ar_baseline_104.sh. Splice k=1 in from the run already on disk (regraded under 0.3.1) rather than re-running 1033 items.

STEP 5 (CPU) -- Analysis with the right unit.
Bootstrap CIs CLUSTERED BY BASE HumanEval/MBPP PROBLEM, not by carved item -- carved items from one problem are not independent. Report McNemar on paired items for (a*) vs (b). Report cumulative_model_tokens over ALL items including budget-truncated ones via the proc()/failure_process accessor (Retraction-3 discipline). Primary figure: pass@1 vs commits-per-step, coupled overlaid on random-twin.

STEP 6 -- The fallback deliverable, which is worth writing either way.
'On a shipped 7B masked-diffusion code LM, joint multi-hole filling is byte-identical to sequential filling on 67.5% of def-use-coupled HumanEval+ holes, because the sampler commits one position per step at the default schedule. The factorization barrier (CoDD 2603.00045, 2509.22738) is a function of commit parallelism, not of mask layout; and the parallelism that would exercise it monotonically degrades quality.' Combined with the on-disk k=1 result (qwen_fim .7638 @ 239 tok vs dream_fim .7115 @ 2035 tok) this adjudicates McDiffuSE's 'predominantly sequential' observation with a mechanism, and supplies the diffusion row 2508.10111 left empty. Frame as capability-audit, not capability-discovery.

FRAMING REPAIRS THAT ARE NOT OPTIONAL: drop 'the one thing FIM structurally cannot do' (GLM/CM3/InCoder serialise multi-span; A3 adapts AR to any-order). Drop the 'first surface where a 7B dLLM strictly dominates matched AR' corollary outright -- it is already falsified at k=1 on our own disk.
feas.risk: The overwhelmingly likely outcome is a NULL THAT IS UNINTERPRETABLE UNDER THE STATED DESIGN, and I have already measured why. JOINT and SEQUENTIAL produce byte-identical fills on 27/40 = 67.5% of def-use-carved k=2 HE+ tasks, so pass@1 must be near-identical; and the stated kill threshold (0.03) sits 3.5x below the n=113 McNemar MDE (~0.105). The trap is that this null has TWO indistinguishable causes under the briefed protocol: (i) the shipped checkpoint genuinely cannot exploit cross-hole conditioning (the reportable finding), or (ii) the protocol never asked it to, because at steps==n_masks the sampler commits exactly one position per forward pass (verified trace [9,8,7,6,5,4,3,2,0]) -- so 'joint' and 'sequential' differ only in whether hole 2's masks are visible, not in whether any two positions are ever predicted simultaneously. Publishing (i) when the cause is (ii) is EXACTLY the Retraction-2 failure mode -- a pipeline stage that silently does not do the thing its name claims, so the measurement is of something other than the advertised construct. The commit-parallelism ladder in Step 2 is what makes the null attributable. Secondary confound: 'coupled holes are harder' will be partly 'coupled holes are longer / carry more tokens' unless the random-span twin is matched on total masked tokens, not merely on k. Third: because the identical-fill rate is so high, any small observed delta will be driven by a handful of discordant items and will not survive base-problem-clustered CIs -- so an unclustered 'significant' result would be a pseudo-replication artifact of the same kind that inflates DreamOn's n=5815.
feas.required_control:
FILL-IDENTITY AND COMMIT-PARALLELISM INSTRUMENTATION, LOGGED PER ITEM, AS A PRECONDITION FOR REPORTING ANY pass@1 COMPARISON.

For every task and every arm pair, persist to metrics.jsonl: (1) the exact decoded string of each hole; (2) a boolean fills_identical across the arm pair; (3) the full per-step mask-count trace captured via generation_tokens_hook_func, from which commits_per_step is derived; (4) an assertion that in the clean-sequential arm hole 2 was masked at EVERY step of pass 1 (I verified this returns True) and that hole 1 was fully resolved before pass 2 began; (5) the splice roundtrip assertion pre+m1+between+m2+post == prompt+canonical_solution.

Then enforce two hard gates before any headline number is written:
GATE A -- if fills_identical rate exceeds 50%, the arms are not manipulating the model's behaviour and pass@1 MUST NOT be reported as evidence about jointness. Report the identity rate itself as the finding.
GATE B -- if commits_per_step == 1 for the arm labelled JOINT, that arm MUST NOT be described as joint, simultaneous, or parallel anywhere in the paper. It is bidirectional-visibility-with-sequential-commit.

This is the direct analogue of the control the three retractions lacked. Retraction 1 shipped a verifier that compared nothing; Retraction 2 shipped a 'refine' stage that discarded its own input; Retraction 3 shipped a cost average that dropped the expensive tasks. Each was a component whose NAME asserted a behaviour nobody instrumented. Here the component at risk is the word 'joint' itself: an arm named JOINT that commits one token per step and returns byte-identical output to the SEQUENTIAL arm is a stage silently discarding its input, and pass@1 alone cannot detect it -- only the fill-identity rate and the per-step commit trace can. Additionally, pin evalplus to a single version (0.3.1, LOCAL) for every graded number and record it in each score.json, since the k=1 rung being reused was graded under 0.1.0.dev1 on the other disk.

lens.title: Per-Region Length Elasticity: a code-level structural limit in DreamOn's sampler
lens.claim: DreamOn's length-control mechanism is architecturally restricted to a single contiguous mask region, so it cannot allocate length independently across multiple holes; a segment-scoped expand/delete state recovers per-hole oracle-length performance on multi-span infilling, where stock DreamOn degrades. Secondary claim: DreamOn's reported infilling parity with AR models does not survive a compute-matched accounting, because its paper reports no NFE or token cost at all.
lens.why_now: I read DreamOn's shipped sampler and found the limit in code, not by speculation: models/DreamOn-v0-7B/generation_utils.py:318-330 computes prefix_len = mask_token_indices[0] and start_gen_len = num_mask_tokens, i.e. it takes the FIRST mask index as the region start and the TOTAL mask count as that one region's length. The window bookkeeping at line 399 (current_window_length = input_ids.shape[1] - start_gen_len + num_generation_tokens) and the expand/delete index arithmetic at lines 465-494 all operate on that single span. With two disjoint holes the length accounting is simply wrong. Separately, per our own verified audit notes (TASK_SURFACE_LIT_GAPS.md), DreamOn's paper reports NO compute/NFE accounting and never evaluated RandomSpanInfilling or multi-span -- and I now have RandomSpanInfilling (1640 items) on disk. Length control is also live: 2602.07546 (length regularization) and 2603.06123 ('natively length-aware') both work on single-region length, and 2603.23507 (deletion-insertion) changes the process wholesale. Nobody has made length elastic PER REGION. Our own project already learned the hard way that [expand] tokens never fire without sampler-matched training (64-step leaf-only training and expand bonuses 1/2/4 all gave 0 expands), so we know exactly what the training-side pitfall is.
lens.experiment: Three stages, each gated on the previous. (i) REPRODUCTION GATE: run DreamOn-v0-7B on data/infilling/HumanEval-SingleLineInfilling.jsonl and confirm our harness lands near the published 92.1 single-line number; if we cannot reproduce, stop and fix the harness before claiming anything (this is the discipline that Dream-Coder-Base cost us). (ii) MISSING-AXIS RUN: RandomSpanInfilling (subsample 500) and MultiLine, with cumulative_model_tokens reported alongside pass rate, plus Qwen2.5-Coder-7B FIM at matched token cost -- this alone fills two acknowledged holes in an ICLR 2026 paper. (iii) MECHANISM: implement segment-scoped length state (per-hole expand_budget, per-hole delete accounting, window length computed per segment) and evaluate on 2-hole carved tasks from the capability-1 carver against (a) stock DreamOn on the same 2-hole inputs, (b) fixed canvas at per-hole ORACLE length (the upper bound), (c) CAL-style calibrated adaptive length search applied per hole (2602.00476 is the training-free length-search competitor and must be a baseline, not just a citation).
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: models/DreamOn-v0-7B with its full generation_utils.py (mask_expansion + delete_eos_token path already exercised by scripts/generate_evalplus_dreamon.py); vendor/DreamOn/eval/{eval_humaneval_infilling.sh,generator.py,configs/eval_infill.yaml} = the authors' own harness for protocol fidelity; data/infilling/*.jsonl (I downloaded these); scaffold_coder/training/scaffold_sft_trainer.py + corruption.py for the sampler-matched training stage; idle B200-class GPUs (LOCAL 8xL20A, .252 8xB200). MISSING -- FLAG: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B for the AR arm (same download as capability-1). RISK: stage (iii) likely needs light SFT, because our own logs show expand tokens never activate from inference changes alone -- budget for a short sampler-matched fine-tune on the DreamOn checkpoint, which also finally spends our idle training capacity.
lens.kill_criterion: Stage (iii) dies if stock DreamOn on 2-hole inputs already reaches per-hole oracle-length quality (arm (a) within 0.03 of arm (b)) -- that would mean the single-region bookkeeping is benign in practice and the code-level limit has no behavioural consequence. Stage (ii) dies as a contribution if DreamOn's single-line parity with Qwen2.5-Coder survives token-cost matching with margin, i.e. there is no hidden compute subsidy to expose. Stage (i) is a hard gate: failure to reproduce single-line within a few points means we report a reproduction failure and do not build on top.
lens.builds_on: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026 Poster). Two defects we repair, one verified in their released code (single-contiguous-region length state at generation_utils.py:318-330), one in their evaluation (no compute/NFE accounting anywhere, and RandomSpanInfilling untested). Positions against CAL (2602.00476) and length regularization (2602.07546), both single-region.

diff.sharpened_claim: DreamOn's length-control state is GLOBAL, not per-region, and I verified the three specific places this bites in its shipped sampler (models/DreamOn-v0-7B/generation_utils.py): (a) prefix_len = mask_token_indices[0] (L318-326) is only the FIRST hole's start, so max_gen_len = max_length - prefix_len (L381), the loop bound (L397) and the default expand_budget = max_gen_len*2 (L384) are all computed against a phantom single region; (b) expand_budget is ONE global counter decremented at L488, with no per-hole allocation, so one hole can starve the others; (c) most severely, the deletion-broadcast `pad_delete_to_right` (L449-462) finds the FIRST [delete] index and fills EVERY mask at or after it with [delete] -- so with two disjoint holes, a contraction decided in hole 1 annihilates hole 2. That broadcast is not an incidental flag: it is the mechanism DreamOn's paper credits with cutting inference from 122.8 to 52.4 steps (Fig. 4), and the authors' own harness turns it ON (vendor/DreamOn/eval/configs/eval_infill.yaml: pad_eos_to_right: true), so the published 92.1 uses the multi-hole-unsafe path. Our contribution is therefore a targeted repair plus the benchmark cell that the multi-region literature left empty: (1) transplant the 1-MRI/2-MRI/3-MRI protocol of arXiv:2508.10111 -- which DEFINED multi-region infilling but benchmarked it on AR models only, and ran diffusion LMs exclusively on non-MRI whole-function tasks -- onto DreamOn-v0-7B, filling the DLM x MRI cell absent from their own paper; (2) attribute the degradation with a 2x2 of {broadcast on/off} x {1 hole / k holes}, so the finding is "the efficiency mechanism is multi-region-unsafe", not the weaker "multi-region is harder"; (3) restore per-hole oracle-length quality with a segment-scoped expand/delete state (per-hole expand budget, hole-local delete broadcast, per-segment window); (4) price everything in cumulative_model_tokens rather than NFE, because DreamOn reports generation STEPS only inside its broadcast ablation and never in the headline table where it claims parity with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (92.1 vs 92.6), and steps are not a cross-family unit when a diffusion step re-attends a full canvas and an AR step is KV-cached.
diff.differentiation_statement: No prior work makes length elastic PER REGION in a diffusion code LM, and the two closest papers miss on orthogonal axes. On the task surface, arXiv:2508.10111 (2025-08-13) is the closest: it explicitly defines Multi-Region Infilling, builds 1/2/3-MRI datasets from C++ HumanEval by removing multiple random spans, and documents catastrophic degradation with more regions (StarCoder2-7B functional 53.8 -> 20.5 -> 7.5). But it evaluates MRI ONLY on autoregressive models (StarCoder2, CodeGemma, DeepSeek-Coder 1.3/6.7/33B); its diffusion-LM section runs LLaDA/Dream/DreamCoder/DiffuCoder on whole-function C++, JSON and SMILES generation -- never on MRI -- and its remedy is a context-free-grammar constraint on token identity, which is orthogonal to how many tokens each region gets. It cites DreamOn only as a blog post and never touches length allocation. On the mechanism, DDOT (arXiv:2506.13579, EMNLP 2025 Main) is the closest: it jointly denoises token values and continuous positions so infilled spans can move and change length, and its "-Random" settings do place 1-6 independently-sized blanks. But DDOT is a 90M-non-embedding-parameter SEDD model evaluated with BLEU/NIST/METEOR/success-rate on One-Billion-Word, Yelp and CodeParrot -- no execution-based correctness, no HumanEval-Infilling, and by its own numbers it nearly collapses on code (CodeParrot success rate 1.01 / 3.53). Its mechanism (continuous position diffusion, requiring retraining from a SEDD checkpoint) is not transferable to DreamOn's discrete [expand]/[delete] sentinel state on a 7B pretrained coder. Everything else in the live length-control literature is single-region or whole-sequence by construction: CAL (2602.00476) searches one length for one "contiguous span of 2 to 8 tokens"; LR-DLLM (2602.07546) regularizes one canvas length; "Natively Length-Aware" (2603.06123) crops the whole context window for short chat/reasoning replies; rho-EOS (2601.22527) does bidirectional length control for one generation region; DID (2603.23507) replaces masking wholesale with a deletion-insertion process. Our setting is a 7B pretrained masked-diffusion CODE model, our unit of analysis is per-hole length allocation, our metric is executed pass@1 with cumulative_model_tokens, and our evidence is a defect verified in released code rather than a conjectured limitation. Separately, note that our three on-disk HumanEval-Infilling files (SingleLine 1033, MultiLine 5815, RandomSpan 1640) are ALL single-contiguous-hole by construction -- their only fields are prompt/canonical_solution/suffix -- so "multi-line" means multiple lines of ONE span. That is direct evidence that no paper in the DreamOn lineage has ever put this model on multiple disjoint holes.

related_work.citation: Wu et al., DreamOn: Diffusion Language Models For Code Infilling Beyond Fixed-size Canvas, arXiv:2602.01326; ICLR 2026 Poster

NOTE first public date is NOT the arXiv v1 (2026-02-01): the HKUNLP blog https://hkunlp.github.io/blog/2025/dreamon carries 2025-07-15 and the HF repo Dream-org/DreamOn-v0-7B has createdAt 2025-07-15T05:20:02Z; Stable-DiffCoder and arXiv:2508.10111 both cite it as a 2025 blog.
related_work.what_it_covers: The paper we build on. Adds [expand] and [delete] sentinel tokens to a masked diffusion LM so the canvas grows/shrinks, with no architecture change. Evaluated on HumanEval-Infilling single-line and multi-line plus SantaCoder-FIM (Python), across initial mask lengths 4/8/16/32/64. DreamCoder-7B 55.5 -> 92.1 single-line, 43.2 -> 63.8 multi-line, 59.3 -> 79.0 SantaCoder; claims parity with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B (92.6 / 58.7 / 79.8) and near-oracle-length performance. Ablates w/o Expand and w/o Delete, and a static vs dynamic-inverse merge scheduler.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Every evaluated benchmark is a SINGLE contiguous hole. No multi-region / multi-span / multiple-disjoint-hole setting anywhere. No RandomSpanInfilling subset. Python-only. No cross-family cost column next to the AR-parity claim. Its own Limitations section flags only (i) code-only scope, (ii) heuristic training/inference, (iii) the single [expand]->2-mask factor -- it never notices that its length state is global rather than per-region.
related_work.known_defects: CORRECTION TO OUR OWN PRIOR NOTE: DreamOn is NOT free of compute accounting -- Figure 4 reports average generation steps and the text says broadcasting cuts total inference steps from 122.8 to 52.4 at mask length 64. But the accounting appears ONLY inside the broadcasting ablation on multi-line, never in Table 1 where the AR-parity claim lives, and 'steps' is not comparable across families (a diffusion step re-attends the whole canvas; an AR step is KV-cached). So the real defect is 'no cross-family-comparable cost for the headline parity claim', not 'no accounting at all'. Code-level defects verified by reading models/DreamOn-v0-7B/generation_utils.py: prefix_len = mask_token_indices[0] (L318-326) takes only the first hole's index and feeds max_gen_len/loop-bound/default-expand_budget (L381,384,397); expand_budget is a single global counter (L488) with no per-hole allocation; pad_delete_to_right (L449-462) locates the FIRST [delete] and overwrites EVERY mask at or after it, so on 2 holes a contraction in hole 1 destroys hole 2 -- and that broadcast is exactly the mechanism credited with the 122.8->52.4 speedup, and is ON in the authors' own harness (vendor/DreamOn/eval/configs/eval_infill.yaml pad_eos_to_right: true). Extra reproducibility hazard: delete_token_id == eos_token_id == bos_token_id == 151643 (generation_config.json; generation_utils.py L109 assigns delete_token_id from the eos_token_id kwarg), and L395 pads the canvas with eos_token_id, i.e. with the DELETE token; the vendor harness also encodes the suffix with add_eos=True, planting a delete token inside the sequence.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (published 2026-02-01T16:46:34Z v1); OpenReview api2 /notes/search (forum EQTPmqukiU, venueid + Camera_Ready_Revision invitation); HKUNLP blog HTML date 2025-07-15; HuggingFace api /api/models/Dream-org/DreamOn-v0-7B createdAt; full PDF read via pdftotext (setup L405-470, oracle table L465-540, steps L595-640, limitations L675-700); direct read of the on-disk generation_utils.py, generation_config.json, config.json, and vendor/DreamOn/eval/{generator.py,configs/eval_infill.yaml,eval_humaneval_infilling.sh}.

related_work.citation: Melcer-style constrained decoding line -- 'Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars', arXiv:2508.10111
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT / CoRR only. Semantic Scholar returns publicationVenue 'arXiv.org', DBLP key journals/corr/abs-2508-10111 with venue 'CoRR 2025'. OpenReview title search returned no note, so no conference venue is verifiable. DBLP also lists a 2026 CoRR follow-up, 'Lookahead-then-Verify: Reliable Constrained Decoding for Diffusion LLMs under Context-Free Grammars'.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest work on our task surface. Explicitly introduces and names Multi-Region Infilling (MRI) as generalising FIM to multiple fixed snippets interleaved by infilling regions, motivated by 'infilling multiple function bodies'. Builds 1-MRI/2-MRI/3-MRI datasets (159/156/143 samples) from the C++ translation of HumanEval by removing 1-3 random spans. Documents severe degradation with more regions: StarCoder2-7B syntax 88.2/55.4/24.5 and functional 53.8/20.5/7.5 for 1/2/3-MRI; same trend across five AR models 1.3B-33B. Fixes syntax with a CFG intersection-emptiness algorithm; reports runtime overhead growing from 67% (1-MRI) to 205% (3-MRI).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The MRI experiments are AR-ONLY (StarCoder2 7B, CodeGemma 7B, DeepSeek-Coder 1.3/6.7/33B). Its separate diffusion-LM section (LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B, DreamCoder-7B, DiffuCoder-7B, all at 32 steps / 256 tokens) runs whole-function C++, JSON-Schema and SMILES generation -- never MRI. So the DLM x MRI cell is empty in their own paper. DreamOn is cited only as a 2025 blog and never evaluated. Length allocation is never discussed: their remedy constrains WHICH tokens are legal, not HOW MANY each region gets, and their DLM runs use a fixed 256-token canvas.
related_work.known_defects: Grammar constraints raise syntactic correctness enormously (+31.5 pp at 3-MRI) but functional correctness barely moves (+2.4 pp average; 3-MRI DeepSeek-33B 12.6 -> 15.4), which their own text concedes -- strong evidence that the residual multi-region failure is a length/content-allocation problem their method cannot reach, i.e. exactly our slot. Functional correctness is measured on C++-translated HumanEval with a hand-written partial C++ CFG that rejects 5 human reference solutions for containing multi-line comments or helper functions, so the denominator is a filtered subset. DLM runs use 32 steps at temperature 0.2 with no step or NFE sweep in the main text, and no diffusion-vs-AR cost matching.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API + full PDF via pdftotext (abstract, sec 4.1 setup, Table 1 MRI results, sec 4.3 DLM models/tasks, references L673-680); Semantic Scholar graph API paper record (publicationVenue arXiv.org, publicationDate 2025-08-13); DBLP publ search API (CoRR 2025 + the 2026 follow-up); OpenReview title search (no hit).

related_work.citation: CAL -- 'Diffusion LMs Can Approximate Optimal Infilling Lengths Implicitly', arXiv:2602.00476
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT. arXiv v1 2026-01-31, no v2. Semantic Scholar reports 0 citations. No OpenReview note found under this title; a likely sibling, 'Training-Free Length Discovery for Diffusion Language Model Infilling', exists as an ICLR 2026 DeLTa Workshop Poster (see separate entry).
related_work.what_it_covers: The training-free length-search competitor the candidate correctly names as a required baseline. Identifies an 'Oracle Peak' in first-step denoising confidence near the ground-truth length plus a systematic 'Length Bias' that obscures it, calibrates the bias with a fitted double-exponential, and runs a bidirectional hill-climbing search over candidate lengths that terminates after D non-improving steps. Reports up to +8.5/+9.9% ROUGE-L in text infilling and gains over chat-based adaptive methods on HumanEval-Infilling with LLaDA-8B-Base/Instruct. Also quantifies how much oracle length alone buys.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Single-region by construction: the task is formalised as one middle segment M of length L between prefix and suffix, and the reported code setting is a 'contiguous span of 2 to 8 tokens'. There is no notion of allocating a separate length to each of several holes, no joint search over a length vector, and no discussion of how the search's combinatorics change when k regions must be sized simultaneously. Zero citations means nobody has extended it to multi-region.
related_work.known_defects: The search's cost is asserted rather than measured -- the text says only that because it reuses a single forward pass for first-step logits 'the additional inference overhead is modest', with no NFE or wall-clock table for the hill-climbing trajectory. That is a soft-accounting flaw of the same family as DreamOn's. Also, extending it naively to k holes is exponential in k unless the search is factorised, so its own framing hides a scaling problem we can expose by running it per-hole and reporting the true forward-pass count.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; full PDF via pdftotext (abstract, sec 2 infilling task formulation, sec 3 phenomena, sec 4 bidirectional search algorithm, sec 5 code-infilling setup incl. the '2 to 8 tokens' span, Table 1 oracle-length comparison); Semantic Scholar citations endpoint returned 0 citing papers.

related_work.citation: LR-DLLM -- 'Improving Variable-Length Generation in Diffusion Language Models via Length Regularization', arXiv:2602.07546
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT. arXiv v1 only. OpenReview title search returned no matching note (only unrelated length-generalization papers), so no venue is verifiable.
related_work.what_it_covers: One of the two length-control papers the candidate names. Shows that naively comparing confidence across mask lengths is systematically biased by an intrinsic length-induced bias, causing under-generation or redundant continuations, and proposes a length-regularization training scheme so variable-length inference becomes reliable. Cites DreamOn.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Operates on a single canvas length for completion/infilling. No per-region decomposition; nothing about several holes competing for a shared budget.
related_work.known_defects: Diagnoses the same confidence/length-bias pathology as CAL from a training-side rather than search-side angle, but neither paper tests whether the bias is per-region separable -- i.e. whether calibrated confidence for hole i is contaminated by the mask count of hole j. That separability question is directly testable in our setting and neither paper poses it.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (published 2026-02-07T13:48:19Z) and abstract; Semantic Scholar citation list of DreamOn confirms it cites DreamOn; OpenReview title search (no hit).

related_work.citation: 'Diffusion Language Models Are Natively Length-Aware', arXiv:2603.06123
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT. arXiv v1 only; OpenReview title search returned no note.
related_work.what_it_covers: The second length paper the candidate names. Argues the latent prompt representation already encodes required output length, and proposes a zero-shot mechanism that dynamically crops the context window so short responses stop wasting denoising compute. Targets reasoning and chat, where most responses are short.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: This is whole-sequence length awareness for a single free-running generation, not per-region allocation, and not infilling. The prompt-level length predictor has no way to emit a length per hole because there is no hole structure in its formulation.
related_work.known_defects: The 'natively length-aware' framing is evidenced on short-response chat/reasoning; the latent-length-predictability claim is untested for bidirectional infilling where the constraint comes from BOTH sides, and untested for a length VECTOR. If prompt latents predict one scalar length, whether they predict k lengths is an open and cheap question -- a probe we could run as a side finding.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (published 2026-03-06T10:30:13Z) and abstract.

related_work.citation: DID -- 'Beyond Masks: Efficient, Flexible Diffusion Language Models via Deletion-Insertion Processes', arXiv:2603.23507
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT. arXiv v1 only; no OpenReview note found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Rigorously formulates token deletion and insertion as discrete diffusion processes, replacing masking/unmasking entirely, eliminating compute spent on non-informative [MASK] and [PAD] tokens. The candidate correctly characterises it as changing the process wholesale.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Because length changes are intrinsic to the process rather than bolted on via sentinel tokens, DID sidesteps rather than solves the per-region budget question -- and it is not a 7B pretrained code model, so it cannot be dropped into HumanEval-Infilling. It gives no MRI/multi-hole evaluation.
related_work.known_defects: Efficiency gains are argued from removing MASK/PAD compute, which is an architectural accounting argument; whether that survives a matched wall-clock or matched-token comparison against a masked model on code infilling is untested. Also a different-backbone confound for anyone trying to attribute quality differences to the process rather than the checkpoint.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (published 2026-03-04T12:53:17Z) and abstract.

related_work.citation: rho-EOS -- 'Training-free Bidirectional Variable-Length Control for Masked Diffusion LLMs', arXiv:2601.22527
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT (v2 dated 7 Feb 2026 on the PDF banner). No OpenReview note found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Uses the implicit density of EOS tokens during denoising as a signal of generation sufficiency, giving training-free BIDIRECTIONAL length adjustment (grow and shrink) in a single stage. Explicitly criticises prior two-stage approaches for requiring separate length-adjustment and mask-insertion phases and for supporting only unidirectional expansion. Cites DreamOn.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Scoped to one generation region for long-chain reasoning and hybrid short/long thinking; not infilling, not code, and no multi-region structure. Its EOS-density signal is global over the generated span, so it inherits exactly the cross-hole contamination problem we are attacking -- a first EOS-density signal cannot say WHICH hole is over-long.
related_work.known_defects: Its own critique of two-stage/unidirectional methods is the strongest external endorsement that the DreamOn-style expand/delete state is a heuristic worth repairing; but rho-EOS itself never asks whether a global sufficiency signal can be localised, which is our exact question. Its reliance on EOS is also fragile in a tokenizer where DreamOn already overloads EOS as the delete sentinel (both 151643).
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; PDF first page via pdftotext (abstract + intro framing of the two-stage/unidirectional critique); Semantic Scholar DreamOn citation list confirms it cites DreamOn.

related_work.citation: DDOT -- 'Flexible-length Text Infilling for Discrete Diffusion Models', arXiv:2506.13579; EMNLP 2025 Main
related_work.venue_status: EMNLP 2025 Main -- OpenReview note (search hit) shows venue 'EMNLP 2025 Main', venueid OpenReview.net/Archive; arXiv v2 comment states 'Major edit of methodology section. Matches EMNLP camera-ready version'.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest prior art on our mechanism, and it was NOT in the candidate's radar. Jointly denoises discrete token values and CONTINUOUS token positions with sample-level optimal-transport position coupling, so infilled spans can move and change length without oracle positional data. Its '-Random' evaluation settings use examples with 1 to 6 keywords that must be infilled while preserving relative order -- i.e. genuinely MULTIPLE blanks, each with independently flexible length. Also has a Block setting with one contiguous span of 0 to L/2 tokens. Benchmarks: One-Billion-Word, Yelp, and the Python subset of CodeParrot.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Scale and surface. DDOT is a 90M-non-embedding-parameter SEDD-based model, not a 7B pretrained diffusion coder. Metrics are BLEU2/4, NIST2/4, METEOR and success rate -- no execution-based functional correctness, no HumanEval-Infilling, no pass@1. Its mechanism requires retraining from a SEDD checkpoint with added position-prediction modules, so it cannot be transplanted onto DreamOn's discrete [expand]/[delete] sentinel state. It never touches code infilling as a functional-correctness task and never diagnoses an existing 7B sampler.
related_work.known_defects: Its own numbers show the multi-blank flexible-length claim does NOT carry to code: CodeParrot-Block success rate 1.01 and CodeParrot-Random 3.53 for DDOT-R, versus 16.9 and ~0 for the LC/PoP baselines -- i.e. essentially nothing works on code under this protocol, yet the abstract advertises performance on par with SOTA non-autoregressive models. The paper also concedes that in benchmarks with six or fewer keywords fixed-position baselines remain competitive, and that One-Billion-Word/Yelp '-Random' settings over-index on an artifact. So the natural follow-up is exactly ours: re-test per-region length elasticity at 7B with executed pass@1 instead of BLEU, where their positive result is weakest.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (published 2025-06-16, v2); arXiv abs page Comments field ('Matches EMNLP camera-ready version'); OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned the note with venue 'EMNLP 2025 Main'; full PDF via pdftotext (abstract, sec 4 approach incl. prompt/response/pad partition and OT coupling, sec 5.1 datasets with the 1-6 keyword and block-masking definitions, Table 1 examples, main results table with CodeParrot-Block/Random SR).

related_work.citation: Anonymous ACL ARR 2026 May submission, 'Discrete Diffusion Models for Code: Bidirectional Infilling and Hybrid Autoregressive-Diffusion Pipelines' (OpenReview Ni6xxPzBlz)
related_work.venue_status: UNDER REVIEW / anonymous. OpenReview venueid aclweb.org/ACL/ARR/2026/May/Submission, venue 'ACL ARR 2026 May Submission', cdate 1779385876157 = 2026-05-21, pdate None. Invitations include Preprint_Post_Submission. No arXiv id found for it. CONCURRENT: first public 2026-05-21 is after the 2026-05-07 cutoff.
related_work.what_it_covers: The single closest concurrent result: an MDLM on a Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B backbone, claiming two complementary regimes -- MULTI-SITE EDITING where diffusion reaches 84% exact match vs 32% for AR, and standard infilling where AR (68.3% execution accuracy) beats diffusion (54.3%). Adds a hybrid multi-candidate pipeline with execution filtering plus MBR consensus (90.2% execution accuracy on single-line infilling at 16 candidates), execution-guided iterative re-masking of failing regions, and an oracle analysis showing AR and diffusion fail on largely disjoint subsets.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Multi-site EDITING scored by exact match is not multi-region INFILLING scored by executed pass@1, and nothing in it concerns per-region length allocation: an edit task supplies the site, so the length question is not raised. Backbone is 1.5B, not 7B, and it is a from-scratch MDLM adaptation rather than a diagnosis of DreamOn's shipped sampler. Its headline numbers come from 16-48 candidate samples with execution filtering, a very different compute regime from single-sample decoding.
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent and unpublished, so it cannot preempt us, but it is the paper a reviewer will raise. Its strongest claim (84% vs 32% on multi-site) is exact-match on a self-constructed edit set with no compute matching against the 16/48-candidate pipelines it compares to, and 'execution accuracy' at 16-48 candidates is a pass@k dressed as pass@1 from a cost standpoint. Our per-hole length result is orthogonal and would strengthen rather than duplicate it; we should cite it as concurrent and, if it appears, position our segment-scoped length state as the missing length axis of their multi-site claim.
related_work.verified_how: OpenReview api2 /notes/search (title, keywords, full abstract, venueid, cdate); timestamp converted to 2026-05-21T17:51:16Z; arXiv title/keyword searches found no corresponding preprint.

related_work.citation: CaRE: 'Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models', arXiv:2607.24763
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT (arXiv v1, cs.AI, banner 4 Jun 2026). CONCURRENT: after the 2026-05-07 cutoff.
related_work.what_it_covers: Independent, concurrent validation of our accounting critique as a general disease. Finds that seven recent remasking papers evaluate under incompatible settings, rendering their rankings incomparable, and proposes standardising ACTUAL NFE, multi-metric reporting and stochasticity. Applied to 7 remasking strategies across LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base at 4 stochasticity levels and 3 step budgets, it finds temperature explains most of the MAUVE variance.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It standardises NFE within the diffusion family and on OpenWebText/LM1B language modelling -- not cross-family diffusion-vs-AR accounting, and not infilling or code. It therefore does not price DreamOn's parity claim against Qwen2.5-Coder, which needs a unit valid across a KV-cached AR decoder and a full-canvas denoiser.
related_work.known_defects: Standardising on NFE is itself the accounting convention our own project already retracted as invalid across families (NFE hides that a diffusion step re-attends the whole canvas). We can cite CaRE as agreeing that dLLM evaluation is compute-confounded, while differentiating by reporting cumulative_model_tokens, which is comparable across AR and diffusion. That is a genuine methodological improvement over a concurrent protocol paper.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; PDF first page via pdftotext (abstract with the seven-papers claim, NFE standardisation, model/step/stochasticity grid).

related_work.citation: dLLM-Var: 'Diffusion LLM with Native Variable Generation Lengths: Let [EOS] Lead the Way', arXiv:2510.24605
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT (arXiv v1, banner 28 Oct 2025; PDF header dated 2025-10-29, EPIC Lab SJTU).
related_work.what_it_covers: Trains a dLLM to predict [EOS] accurately so it can natively infer in a block-diffusion manner while keeping full bidirectional attention, reporting 30.1x speedup over traditional dLLM inference and 2.4x over block diffusion. Cites DreamOn. Establishes that the pre-DreamOn-arXiv length-control literature was already active in 2025.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Whole-response length for generation/reasoning, not infilling and not per-region. [EOS]-led termination is inherently a single right-edge signal, so it has no representation for k interior holes.
related_work.known_defects: Headline speedups are relative to a fixed-long-canvas baseline, which is the easiest possible comparator; there is no matched-quality-at-matched-token-cost curve. Same accounting weakness we intend to fix. Its relevance to us is mainly chronological -- it shows length control was live well before DreamOn's arXiv date, which supports using 2025-07-15 as DreamOn's true first public date.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API + PDF first page via pdftotext; appears in the Semantic Scholar citation list of DreamOn.

related_work.citation: Shen et al., Blank Language Models, arXiv:2002.03079
related_work.venue_status: PREPRINT record verified via arXiv (v2). I did NOT verify its conference venue and did not read the paper in this session -- see verification_notes.
related_work.what_it_covers: The pre-diffusion precedent for filling MULTIPLE blanks whose individual lengths are not given in advance, by iteratively expanding blanks. Conceptually the oldest statement of the per-region length problem we are attacking, and the honest ancestor a reviewer may cite to say 'multi-blank variable length is old'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Small-scale text LM, not masked diffusion, not a 7B code model, no execution-based code metrics, and no compute accounting against modern AR coders. It also predates the whole fixed-canvas diffusion framing, so it does not speak to the sampler-level defect we found.
related_work.known_defects: Not assessed -- I only confirmed its existence, title and date via the arXiv API and did not read it. Before citing it as THE multi-blank precedent, read it and confirm that blank lengths are genuinely independent per blank rather than governed by a single global insertion budget.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API search all:"blank language model" returned 2002.03079v2, published 2020-02-08. Full text NOT read.

followup_openings.target_paper: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026 Poster; first public 2025-07-15)
followup_openings.defect: The length-control state is global, not per-region, and the worst offender is the very mechanism the paper credits for its efficiency. models/DreamOn-v0-7B/generation_utils.py L449-462 (pad_delete_to_right) finds the FIRST [delete] index and overwrites EVERY remaining mask at or after it with [delete]; with two disjoint holes a contraction decided in hole 1 annihilates hole 2. The paper attributes the 122.8 -> 52.4 step reduction to exactly this deletion broadcast, and the authors' own harness enables it (vendor/DreamOn/eval/configs/eval_infill.yaml: pad_eos_to_right: true), so the published 92.1 single-line number is produced by the multi-hole-unsafe path. Compounding it: expand_budget is one global counter (L488) with no per-hole allocation, so one hole can starve the others; and prefix_len = mask_token_indices[0] (L318-326) is only the first hole's start, inflating max_gen_len, the loop bound and the default expand budget (L381/384/397). Nobody has ever run this model on multiple disjoint holes -- all three HumanEval-Infilling files on disk (SingleLine 1033, MultiLine 5815, RandomSpan 1640) carry only prompt/canonical_solution/suffix, i.e. exactly ONE contiguous hole, so 'multi-line' means multiple lines of one span.
followup_openings.our_fix: Segment-scoped length state: per-hole expand_budget, hole-local delete broadcast (clip the fill to the current segment's boundaries instead of to end-of-sequence), and window length computed per segment. Attribute the effect with a 2x2 of {broadcast ON / OFF} x {1 hole / k holes} so the finding is 'the efficiency mechanism is multi-region-unsafe' rather than the weaker 'multi-region is harder'. Because broadcast-OFF is the HF default while broadcast-ON is the authors' evaluated setting, this 2x2 also isolates whether the defect is behavioural or benign, which is precisely the candidate's own kill criterion -- and it makes the kill test cheap and decisive.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts a speculative architectural claim into a code-verified defect in the efficiency mechanism of an ICLR 2026 paper, on a task surface (multi-region infilling) that a separate paper already argued matters for real editing workflows. A reviewer can check the eight lines of source themselves.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2508.10111, 'Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars' (CoRR 2025-08-13)
followup_openings.defect: It DEFINES Multi-Region Infilling, builds 1/2/3-MRI datasets from C++ HumanEval, and shows AR models collapsing as regions increase (StarCoder2-7B functional 53.8 -> 20.5 -> 7.5). But it benchmarks MRI on AR models ONLY; its diffusion-LM section runs LLaDA/Dream/DreamCoder/DiffuCoder on whole-function C++, JSON and SMILES generation and never on MRI. The DLM x MRI cell is empty in its own paper. It cites DreamOn only as a blog and never evaluates it. And its remedy is orthogonal to ours: grammar constraints govern WHICH tokens are legal, not HOW MANY each region gets -- which is why its syntax gains are huge (+31.5 pp at 3-MRI) while functional gains are tiny (+2.4 pp average), an admission in its own results that the residual multi-region failure is an allocation problem it cannot reach.
followup_openings.our_fix: Fill the empty cell: run DreamOn-v0-7B (and a Dream-Coder-Instruct control) on the 1/2/3-MRI protocol, in Python rather than their C++ translation so we can use evalplus untrusted_check for executed pass@1 instead of a hand-written partial C++ CFG that rejects 5 human reference solutions. Then show that segment-scoped length state closes the multi-region gap that grammar constraints demonstrably could not, and report both under matched cumulative_model_tokens. Optionally stack our fix on their constraint to show the two are additive rather than competing.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the strongest single framing available: we are not inventing a task, we are filling a cell that an existing multi-region paper left blank, and we explain its most conspicuous negative result (syntax fixed, function not) with a mechanism it lacked.

followup_openings.target_paper: DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326) -- cost accounting for the AR-parity claim
followup_openings.defect: Our own prior note that DreamOn 'reports NO compute/NFE accounting at all' is WRONG and must be corrected before we build on it: Figure 4 reports average generation steps and the text states broadcasting cuts total inference steps from 122.8 to 52.4 at mask length 64. The real, narrower defect is that this accounting appears ONLY inside the broadcasting ablation on the multi-line subset, and never in Table 1 where the headline parity claim lives (DreamCoder+DreamOn 92.1 vs Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 92.6 single-line; 63.8 vs 58.7 multi-line). Worse, 'steps' is not a valid cross-family unit -- a diffusion step re-attends the entire canvas while an AR step is KV-cached -- which is exactly the NFE-as-cross-family-unit error our own project already retracted.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run the parity comparison with cumulative_model_tokens (prompt + canvas re-attended per step, summed over steps) for DreamOn and true decode tokens for Qwen2.5-Coder-7B FIM, at matched token cost, on single-line, multi-line and RandomSpan. State the corrected premise explicitly in the paper so a reviewer holding the PDF cannot catch us overclaiming; the contribution is 'parity is unpriced in a comparable unit', not 'unmeasured'. Also report the broadcast's step savings against its multi-region correctness cost, turning their Figure 4 into a quality-compute tradeoff rather than a free win.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A precise, checkable accounting critique survives review; an overstated one ('reports nothing') dies on the first reviewer who opens Figure 4 and takes the rest of the paper down with it. This is the same failure mode as our three retractions.

followup_openings.target_paper: CAL (arXiv:2602.00476) and LR-DLLM (arXiv:2602.07546)
followup_openings.defect: Both are single-region by construction -- CAL formalises the task as one middle segment M of length L and reports code results on a 'contiguous span of 2 to 8 tokens'. Neither asks whether the calibrated-confidence length signal is separable across regions, i.e. whether the Oracle Peak for hole i survives when hole j's mask count also varies. CAL's search cost is asserted, not measured: the text says overhead is 'modest' because it reuses one forward pass for first-step logits, with no NFE or wall-clock table for the hill-climbing trajectory. Extended naively to k holes, a per-length hill climb becomes a search over a length VECTOR -- combinatorics the paper never confronts. CAL has 0 citations, so nobody has done this.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run CAL per-hole as a first-class baseline (as the candidate proposes) but ALSO measure its true forward-pass count and token cost, so the training-free comparator is priced rather than assumed cheap. Add a cheap diagnostic that stands alone even if our mechanism fails: sweep hole j's initial mask count and check whether hole i's calibrated-confidence Oracle Peak shifts. A positive result means the length signal is cross-contaminated and the whole training-free-search family needs factorising; a null means per-hole CAL is a strong training-free alternative to our SFT, which is still a publishable comparison.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It gives the mechanism stage a second, cheaper deliverable that is independent of whether our segment-scoped state trains successfully -- valuable given our own logs show [expand] tokens never fire without sampler-matched training (64-step leaf-only training and expand bonuses 1/2/4 all yielded 0 expands).

followup_openings.target_paper: DDOT (arXiv:2506.13579, EMNLP 2025 Main)
followup_openings.defect: This is the real closest prior art on per-region length elasticity and was absent from the candidate's positioning -- it must be cited. Its '-Random' settings place 1-6 independently-sized blanks and it jointly diffuses continuous positions so spans can move and resize. But the claim does not survive contact with code by its own numbers: CodeParrot-Block success rate 1.01 and CodeParrot-Random 3.53 for DDOT-R, versus 16.9 for the LC baseline on Block. It is a 90M-non-embedding-parameter SEDD model scored with BLEU/NIST/METEOR/success-rate, never with executed pass@1, never on HumanEval-Infilling. The paper also concedes fixed-position baselines stay competitive at six or fewer keywords and that the '-Random' settings over-index on an artifact.
followup_openings.our_fix: Cite DDOT as the flexible-position/flexible-length precedent and differentiate on four explicit axes -- scale (7B pretrained coder vs 90M SEDD), mechanism (discrete [expand]/[delete] sentinels on a shipped checkpoint vs continuous position diffusion requiring retraining), metric (executed pass@1 + cumulative_model_tokens vs BLEU/SR), and surface (HumanEval-Infilling MRI vs One-Billion-Word/Yelp/CodeParrot). Frame our result as the first test of per-region length elasticity at 7B under execution-based correctness, which is exactly the regime where DDOT's own evidence is weakest.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Failing to cite DDOT is the single most likely way this paper gets desk-rejected for missing the closest work; citing it with these four axes converts the nearest threat into the cleanest statement of our delta, and points at the regime where its positive claim is known to break.

followup_openings.target_paper: DreamOn released artifacts (models/DreamOn-v0-7B vs vendor/DreamOn/eval) -- reproducibility
followup_openings.defect: The HF checkpoint's defaults do not reproduce the paper. generation_config.json ships pad_delete_to_right: false, temperature: 0.0, top_p: null, mask_token_id: null, while the authors' own harness runs pad_eos_to_right: true, temperature 0.2 (0.1 in eval_infill.yaml), top_p 0.9, alg entropy, steps 256, and sweeps min_gen_len over 4/8/16/32/64. Anyone following the HF card alone will miss the 92.1. There is also a token-identity hazard: delete_token_id == eos_token_id == bos_token_id == 151643 (generation_utils.py L109 assigns delete_token_id from the eos_token_id kwarg), L395 pads the canvas with eos_token_id -- i.e. with the DELETE token -- and vendor/DreamOn/eval/generator.py encodes the suffix with add_eos=True, planting a delete sentinel inside the sequence. Given our own measured sampler sensitivity (top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 moved HumanEval by 14.6 points, larger than most published diffusion-LM method gains), any of these silently degrades a reproduction.
followup_openings.our_fix: Make Stage (i) a published reproduction note, not just an internal gate: report single-line pass@1 under HF defaults vs authors'-harness settings side by side, name the exact deltas, and document the EOS/BOS/delete collision. Pin every sampler knob in our own runs and report them in a settings table. This also protects the headline: a 2-hole degradation measured under mis-set defaults would be an artifact, not a mechanism, which is the same class of error as our three retractions (verifier that counted 'did not raise' as pass, refinement 'restart' that discarded the draft, averaging that silently dropped truncated tasks).
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It is a free, GPU-cheap contribution that makes the mechanism claim credible, and it protects us from the specific failure mode this project has already committed three times -- measuring the wrong thing and only noticing after the result was written up.

diff.verification_notes:
Claims I could NOT verify, and claims resting on weak evidence:

(1) VENUE GAPS. No conference venue is verifiable for arXiv:2508.10111 (the multi-region-infilling paper): Semantic Scholar returns publicationVenue "arXiv.org", DBLP lists it as CoRR 2025, and an OpenReview title search returned no note. It may be under review or at a venue OpenReview does not index. DBLP does show a 2026 CoRR follow-up ("Lookahead-then-Verify: Reliable Constrained Decoding for Diffusion LLMs under Context-Free Grammars") that I did not read. Likewise no venue found for CAL (2602.00476), LR-DLLM (2602.07546), 2603.06123, 2603.23507, 2601.22527, 2510.24605, or CaRE (2607.24763) -- all listed as preprint above. Per project rule I treated OpenReview as authoritative and did not upgrade any of these on Semantic Scholar's word.

(2) OPENREVIEW API LIMITATION. api2.openreview.net /notes?id= and ?forum= both returned HTTP 403 in this environment; only /notes/search worked. So I have venue/venueid/cdate for the OpenReview items but could not retrieve the abstract of "Training-Free Length Discovery for Diffusion Language Model Infilling" (Hl8w6DC9VY, ICLR 2026 DeLTa Workshop Poster, cdate 2026-01-30). Its relationship to CAL (arXiv v1 dated 2026-01-31, one day later, same topic and framing) is UNRESOLVED -- they may be the same work. Resolve before writing related work; citing both as independent would be an error.

(3) NOT READ. Blank Language Models (2002.03079) -- I confirmed only title and date via the arXiv API. Its per-blank-independent-length property is asserted from title/abstract-level familiarity, NOT from reading the paper. Verify before citing it as the multi-blank precedent. Edit Flows (2506.09018) -- the PDF download was corrupt ("Couldn't find trailer dictionary"), so its infilling/code coverage is unverified and I have deliberately excluded it from related_work rather than guess. Also not read: Insertion Transformer (1902.03249), Levenshtein Transformer (1905.11006), LoFlexMDM (2602.18695), Stable-DiffCoder (2601.15892, which I only grepped and which cites DreamOn as a 2025 blog), ME-DLM (2605.09603, grepped only; concurrent at 2026-05-10 and appears to be whole-response edit refinement, not multi-region infilling).

(4) DATE SCHEME. This environment's arXiv IDs are future-dated relative to my training data (2602.x = 2026-02 etc.). I did not assume this -- I confirmed every date from the arXiv API <published> field, and cross-checked the two that matter most. DreamOn's FIRST PUBLIC DATE is 2025-07-15, not the 2026-02-01 arXiv v1: the HKUNLP blog HTML carries July 15, 2025, the HF repo Dream-org/DreamOn-v0-7B has createdAt 2025-07-15T05:20:02Z, and both arXiv:2508.10111 and Stable-DiffCoder cite it as a 2025 blog. Either date is comfortably pre-cutoff, so concurrency is unaffected, but the paper must not describe DreamOn as a Feb-2026 work.

(5) CORRECTION TO THE CANDIDATE'S OWN PREMISE. The candidate's secondary claim -- "DreamOn's paper reports no NFE or token cost at all" -- is FALSE and is repeated from our internal TASK_SURFACE_LIT_GAPS.md, which is therefore also wrong on this point and should be amended. DreamOn Figure 4 reports average generation steps and the text states broadcasting reduces total inference steps from 122.8 to 52.4 at mask length 64. The defensible version is narrower: steps are reported only inside the broadcasting ablation on the multi-line subset, never alongside the Table 1 AR-parity claim, and steps are not a cross-family cost unit. I have restated the claim accordingly in sharpened_claim; do not ship the original wording.

(6) SEVERITY CALIBRATION ON THE CODE CLAIM. The candidate says that with two holes "the length accounting is simply wrong". I read the arithmetic and this is stronger than what the code supports for the window bookkeeping specifically: current_window_length = input_ids.shape[1] - start_gen_len + num_generation_tokens (L399) stays globally self-consistent for TOTAL mask count across holes, because start_gen_len is the total. The genuinely behavioural defects are (a) the single global expand_budget with no per-hole allocation, (b) the pad_delete_to_right broadcast that crosses hole boundaries, and (c) prefix_len being only the first hole's index, whose effect is a loosened iteration/expansion budget (via max_gen_len at L381 -> L384/L397) rather than a hard error. Claiming a total-length miscount would be falsified by anyone instrumenting the loop. The precise version is in sharpened_claim.

(7) EMPTY-SEARCH EVIDENCE (absence, not proof). Zero arXiv hits for: "multi-span infilling" (only an unrelated 2022 scaling-laws paper), "RandomSpanInfilling", "random span infilling"+HumanEval, "multi-region infilling" (sole hit = 2508.10111), abs "multiple regions"+infilling+code, abs "per-segment"+length, abs "each masked region", abs "multiple holes"/"multi-hole" (all physics), abs "length prediction"+diffusion LM+infilling, abs "multi-site"+diffusion+code. Two queries died on HTTP 429 and were retried; one ("multiple blanks"+infilling) failed permanently after 5 attempts and was NOT recovered -- that is the one residual gap in coverage, and it points at exactly the Blank-LM literature I also did not read (see 3). Absence of hits is weak evidence, and terminology in this area is unstable ("blank", "hole", "region", "span", "segment", "site" are all in use), so treat the "nobody has done per-region" claim as well-supported but not proven.

(8) NOTHING WAS RUN ON GPU. All quality/cost numbers cited from other papers are as-reported by those papers; I verified none empirically. The reproduction gate in Stage (i) remains genuinely unretired, and per item (6) of followup_openings there is a real risk that HF-default sampler settings will miss the published 92.1.
