feas.concrete_plan:
STAGE 0 -- DEDUP + BUILD (no GPU, ~2h). (0a) BEFORE ANYTHING: the task brief says .73 is already running "DreamOn infilling/FIM eval + a unidirectional control". That IS Stage (i)/(ii) of this candidate. SSH .73 (sshpass -f configs/password_h20_853573.txt, omit -p) and read its run dir + logs; if it is already doing SingleLine, take its output as the reproduction gate and skip to Stage 2. Do not launch a duplicate. (0b) With http_proxy=http://hy-proxy.woa.com:3128, install into /opt/conda/envs/dllm-env: `human-eval-infilling` (gives the official evaluate_infilling_functional_correctness -- this is the ONLY acceptable grader; do not hand-roll) and `omegaconf` (unblocks vendor/DreamOn/eval/evaluate.py). (0c) Write the instrumentation module that every later stage imports: a forward_pre_hook copied from the tracker in /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/scripts/generate_evalplus_ar.py (lines ~27-64, 277) emitting forward_calls and cum_model_tokens = sum of input_ids width per call. NEVER use len(output.history) as NFE -- I measured 160 vs 224 at H=32.

STAGE 1 -- REPRODUCTION GATE, and publish it as a settings table (8 GPU-h). Run SingleLine (all 1033, data/infilling/HumanEval-SingleLineInfilling.jsonl) on models/DreamOn-v0-7B via 8-way sharding, copying the shard/merge/coverage-assert skeleton of scripts/_run_ar_baseline_104.sh (its `n_shards -ne NG -> FATAL` block is the right pattern) and the per-rank loop of scripts/generate_evalplus_dreamon.py -- but FIX that script's two bugs first (it silently drops mask_expansion/delete_eos_token, and it never passes pad_delete_to_right). Sweep min_gen_len in {4,8,16,32,64} to match vendor/DreamOn/eval/eval_humaneval_infilling.sh. Run TWO cells, and report both: (A) HF-card defaults from models/DreamOn-v0-7B/generation_config.json (temperature 0.0, top_p null, pad_delete_to_right false); (B) authors' harness settings from vendor/DreamOn/eval/configs/eval_infill.yaml + eval_humaneval_infilling.sh (temperature 0.2, top_p 0.9, alg entropy, alg_temp 0.0, pad_delete_to_right/pad_eos_to_right TRUE). Note max_new_tokens is NOT "new tokens": generation_utils.py:200 sets max_length = max_new_tokens + input_ids_length - num_mask_tokens, and max_gen_len = max_length - prefix_len (L381) where prefix_len is the FIRST mask index -- so pass it deliberately. If neither cell lands near 92.1, STOP and report a reproduction failure; also state which code path (HF _sample vs vendor batch_generate_with_expand_as_token) the number came from, since I verified they order delete/expand oppositely.

STAGE 2 -- THE 2x2 ATTRIBUTION, WHICH IS THE REAL PAPER, AND WHICH I HAVE ALREADY SEEN FIRE (10 GPU-h). Build the k-hole carver (it does not exist) from the single-hole files: split canonical_solution into k disjoint spans, record each span's TRUE token length as the per-hole ORACLE (this is arm (b)) and its (prefix, gap-text, suffix) layout. Then run {broadcast ON, OFF} x {1 hole, 2 holes, 3 holes} x min_gen_len {4,32}. My smoke on an L20A already shows the effect is real and LARGER than the paper's own figure: at 2 holes/H=32, broadcast=0 gave forward_calls=236 / cum_model_tokens=36108 / masks_remaining_at_exit=2, while broadcast=1 gave forward_calls=35 / cum_model_tokens=5355 / masks_remaining_at_exit=30 -- a 6.7x step cut (vs the paper's 122.8->52.4 = 2.3x) purchased by annihilating 30 of 64 mask slots. At 1 hole, ON and OFF were byte-identical. That is the 2x2 in miniature. Report pass@1 (official grader) AND cum_model_tokens AND, mandatorily, the sampler-state counters from Stage 0c.

STAGE 3 -- MISSING-AXIS RUN (12 GPU-h). RandomSpan (subsample 500 of 1640) + MultiLine (subsample 500 of 5815), single-hole, priced in cum_model_tokens, versus Qwen2.5-Coder-7B FIM at matched token cost. The AR arm must run on .104 (the only disk copy: /apdcephfs_zwfy6/.../dllm_draft_104/models/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, 15G) using its <|fim_prefix|>/<|fim_suffix|>/<|fim_middle|> tokens (151659/151661/151660 exist in DreamOn's added_tokens.json too, so the tokenizers agree) -- wait for the AR EvalPlus baseline to free those 8 GPUs, and reuse its report.json as the matched-capacity anchor. My timing on real rows at min_gen_len=4: SingleLine 1.4 s/item / 11 forwards / 4385 cum_tok; MultiLine 1.5 s / 35 fwd / 12015 tok; RandomSpan 1.7 s / 18 fwd / 6473 tok -- cost scales with min_gen_len, and H=32 items ran 236 forwards, so budget by min_gen_len not by item count.

STAGE 4 -- DEFER. Segment-scoped length state + sampler-matched SFT. Do NOT gate the paper on this: it needs an FSDP/verl/hydra/flash-attn env build that does not exist in dllm-env, and our own logs already show [expand] never fires without sampler-matched training. Ship Stages 1-3 (reproduction note + broadcast-unsafety attribution + priced parity) as the unit; add CAL-per-hole as the training-free comparator ONLY with its true forward-pass count measured and a hard cap, since per-hole hill-climbing is exponential in k.
feas.risk: The broadcast defect is CONDITIONAL on a [delete] firing inside hole 1, and on items where it does not fire, stock DreamOn already equals the per-hole oracle exactly -- so the likeliest outcome is a bimodal population that reads as a length finding but is really a truncation rate. I measured both halves of this on one L20A. Firing case, 2 holes/H=32: broadcast ON cut forward_calls 236->35 but left masks_remaining_at_exit=30 (of 64). NON-firing case, a 2-hole task whose holes genuinely want different lengths (hole1 = a loop variable, hole2 = an expression): at H=16 and H=32 stock DreamOn allocated hole1=1 token (' x') and hole2=3 tokens ('x * k') -- CORRECTLY per-hole, with broadcast ON and OFF producing IDENTICAL forward counts (54/54 and 66/66) and IDENTICAL text. That is the candidate's own kill criterion (arm (a) within 0.03 of arm (b)) firing at the smoke level. So the headline risk is: aggregate 2-hole pass@1 drops, we attribute it to "global length state", and a reviewer decomposes it into "N% of items exit with unresolved <|mask|> tokens and therefore fail to parse" -- a bug report, not a mechanism. Worse, that failure mode is INDISTINGUISHABLE from the unparseable-output confound this project already characterised (94%->1.8% across the NFE sweep) unless parse failure is separated from length error. Secondary risk: because pad_delete_to_right was never actually being passed, a careless 2x2 silently runs OFF/OFF and produces a null with no error message.
feas.required_control: A SAMPLER-STATE ASSERTION HARNESS that makes every arm prove it is the arm it claims to be, emitted per item and hard-failing the run. Required fields: n_expand_fired, n_delete_fired, n_broadcast_events (count of times the pad_delete_to_right block actually rewrote >=1 slot), masks_remaining_at_exit, realized_length_per_hole, oracle_length_per_hole, forward_calls, cum_model_tokens, final_parseable, plus the resolved generation_config dict as actually seen inside _sample. Four assertions, any of which aborts: (1) in every broadcast-ON arm, n_broadcast_events > 0 on a nonzero fraction of items -- this catches the defect I PROVED is live, that DreamGenerationConfig silently swallows unknown kwargs (my probe: "SILENTLY DROPPED kwargs: {'mask_expansion': True, 'delete_eos_token': True, 'steps': 256}") so an arm can be mislabelled with no error, exactly retraction #2's silently-discarded-input; (2) broadcast-ON and broadcast-OFF outputs must NOT be byte-identical on more than a declared fraction of items, so the 2x2 cannot collapse to a 1x1 and be written up as an effect (at 1 hole they ARE identical, which is the correct null and must be shown as such); (3) items with masks_remaining_at_exit > 0 are reported as a SEPARATE truncation column and are never silently folded into the length-allocation claim -- this is what stops a truncation rate from being published as per-region length elasticity, and it is retraction #3's class (a statistic that quietly drops or absorbs the pathological subpopulation, here in the opposite direction); (4) NFE/cost comes ONLY from the forward_pre_hook count, never from len(output.history), which I measured to overstate forward passes by up to 40% (224 vs 160) and which scripts/generate_evalplus_dreamon.py currently records as "nfe". And the grader is the installed official human-eval-infilling evaluate_infilling_functional_correctness -- no hand-written exec()/assert runner, because evalplus.untrusted_check structurally cannot grade these rows and improvising one is retraction #1 verbatim.

lens.title: Execution-Localized Remasking: grounding revision in test failures instead of model confidence
lens.claim: Choosing WHICH committed tokens to remask from execution evidence -- the failing test's traceback line and the variables it implicates -- beats confidence-based remasking and beats random-span remasking at matched token cost on code repair; and unlike confidence-based remasking, its advantage survives compute-matched evaluation.
lens.why_now: There is a large and fast-growing remasking literature (I enumerated 30+ papers: WINO-style post-hoc, NAVIRA 2606.06031, CORE 2602.04096, STaRR 2601.04205, Saber 2510.18165, T2M 2605.26436, anchor-token 2606.16847, and more) and essentially ALL of it selects remask positions from MODEL-INTERNAL signals -- confidence, entropy, temporal difference, attention, anchors. Two 2026 papers show that family is in trouble: 2606.12232 finds post-hoc confidence remasking gives little-to-no benefit over confidence-based unmasking alone under standard block lengths, and CaRE (2607.24763) finds compute-matched comparison REVERSES several published strategy rankings. Meanwhile the signal that actually correlates with correctness has never been used: arXiv 'test failure' AND 'remask' = 0 hits; 'execution-guided' AND 'diffusion' = 0 hits; 'diffusion' AND 'traceback' = 0 relevant hits. We are unusually well placed: we have a retraction-hardened verifier (evalplus.eval.untrusted_check, whose visible-pass rate we validated to EXACTLY match evalplus base pass@1 at three independent points) and we already have Dream-Coder nfe256 drafts on disk in runs/. This also repairs our own two retracted refinement arms -- Arm A (restart) discarded the draft entirely and so measured Dream-Coder rather than refinement, and Arm B (remask) was a prompt-text splice rather than a canvas operation.
lens.experiment: Take existing Dream-Coder-Instruct nfe256 drafts (runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe256, runs/dream_instruct_mbppplus_nfe256 -- already on disk, 131/164 parse, 33 syntax errors). For each draft failing visible tests: execute, parse the traceback for the offending line, extract the identifiers implicated at that line, map both to token spans on the canvas, remask ONLY those spans, and re-diffuse with all other committed tokens frozen -- a genuine canvas-level operation. Five arms, all at MATCHED cumulative_model_tokens: (a) execution-localized remask; (b) lowest-confidence-k remask, k set to the same token count (this is the published SOTA family and, per 2606.12232, expected weak); (c) random-span remask, same token count (the control the literature omits); (d) full regeneration from the prompt at the same total token budget (the upper-bound control we learned to demand after Retraction 2 -- any pipeline that fails to beat 'just hand the task to Dream-Coder at nfe512', HE+ .707 / MBPP+ .680, has no value); (e) no-refine baseline. Report newly_lost alongside rescued, and report the visible-pass-but-hidden-fail count per arm, since our own grid showed real false-passes (HE+ medium 5, MBPP+ large 23). Cost accounting includes budget-truncated tasks via the proc() accessor.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: scripts/refine_verifier_guided.py with the FIXED verifier (commit 67a7a01, now calling evalplus.eval.untrusted_check with expected-value comparison); Dream-Coder nfe256/nfe512 drafts across 8 shards in runs/; scaffold_coder/decoder_runtime.py exposing remask_leaf, remask_leaves, backtrack_structural_subtree, completed_structural_subtrees for the structural variant; the models. NEEDS WRITING: traceback-line-to-token-span mapper (ast + tree_sitter_python, both installed) and a true canvas-level remask hook in the Dream sampler -- the existing 'remask' policy is only a prompt-text splice and must not be reused. NOTE: libcst is MISSING but ast + tree_sitter_python suffice. No new model downloads, no training.
lens.kill_criterion: If arm (a) is not better than max(arm (b), arm (c)) by more than bootstrap noise at matched token cost on BOTH HE+ and MBPP+, execution grounding adds nothing over cheap heuristics and the claim dies. Hard second gate: if no arm exceeds arm (d) (equal-token full regeneration) or the Dream-Coder nfe512 direct-run upper bound, the entire refine-the-draft framing is worthless regardless of which localization signal wins -- this is exactly the trap our Retraction 2 fell into and it must be checked before any number is written down.
lens.builds_on: Positions against the confidence-remasking family and its two 2026 critiques (2606.12232 null result; CaRE 2607.24763 compute-matched ranking reversals). Nearest neighbours, all concurrent (first public on/after 2026-05-07) and none using execution: Detect-Remask-Repair (2606.12807, 2026-06-11) does localized remasking but for summary faithfulness with a claim-support detector; CDC (2605.16829, 2026-05-16) is the closest -- it picks regions via STATIC program analysis, training-free, targeting security/syntax constraint satisfaction rather than test-driven repair; OSCAR (2604.01624) and Prism (2602.01842) are self-verification/search. Also repairs our own retracted Arm A/Arm B refinement design.

diff.sharpened_claim: Under a strictly compute-matched protocol that prices EVERY model forward pass (base denoiser AND any auxiliary scorer/surrogate) in one currency, remask-position selection grounded in HARD execution evidence -- the failing test's traceback line and the identifiers it implicates, mapped to canvas token spans -- beats (a) lowest-confidence-k remasking, (b) random-span remasking at matched token count, and (c) a learned soft correctness-surrogate saliency signal in the style of CDC/GradGuide, on Python EvalPlus (HumanEval+/MBPP+) with Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B. Two second-order claims carry the paper even if the primary ordering is null: (i) the entire refine-the-draft family is worthless unless it beats equal-token full regeneration and the Dream-Coder nfe512 direct-run ceiling (HE+ .707 / MBPP+ .680), which we report as a hard gate rather than omit; and (ii) a soft surrogate whose per-step forward/backward is charged to the budget may lose to a free exact oracle call, i.e. published "localized editing is token-efficient" claims are partly an artefact of not pricing the localizer.

related_work.citation: Lize Shao, Michael Cardei, Zichen Xie, Ferdinando Fioretto, Wenxi Wang. "Constrained Code Generation with Discrete Diffusion." arXiv:2605.16829v1.
related_work.venue_status: preprint (arXiv v1 only, cs.CL, CC BY 4.0). Verified: arXiv API returns single v1 with no journal_ref and no venue comment; OpenReview api2 title search returns no submission record for this exact title (nearest hits are the unrelated 'Constrained Language Generation with Discrete Diffusion Models' CoRR 2025 and 'Constrained Discrete Diffusion' NeurIPS 2025 poster).
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest prior work. Training-free neurosymbolic framework (CDC) that injects program-level constraints into the reverse denoising process of diffusion code models. Two operators: (1) GradGuide targets functional correctness -- trains a Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B surrogate on CodeContest pairs labeled by real execution (1[compiles] x test-pass-ratio), takes the gradient of predicted violation w.r.t. soft token embeddings, adds base-denoiser entropy/confidence terms, picks top-k saliency positions, expands them to syntactic neighborhoods, then in Mode B REMASKS those committed spans and re-denoises. Explicitly notes the trigger predicate 'can be an exact oracle when available, such as compilation, unit-test execution, or static analysis.' (2) MDFI targets security via static Code Property Graph analysis + localized remasking/insertion. Backbones include Dream-Coder-7B, DiffuCoder-7B, Dream-7B. Reports pass@1/pass@10 on HumanEval-X C++ (164) and MBPP-C++ (397); Dream-Coder 34.1->65.2 HE-X, 27.7->59.2 MBPP. Includes a random-editing ablation (matches vanilla), a token-cost comparison vs AR+reprompt, and a corrector-behavior table (improvement rate / Imp-vs-Reg / net / constructive ratio).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: (1) Never actually uses a real test-execution trace to select spans -- localization is always the differentiable surrogate gradient; the exact oracle is mentioned only as an optional boolean TRIGGER, never as the LOCALIZATION signal, and no traceback/variable-implication mapping exists anywhere in the paper. (2) All functional-correctness experiments are C++ (HumanEval-X C++, MBPP-C++), not Python EvalPlus; no EvalPlus/HumanEval+/MBPP+ anywhere (string 'EvalPlus' count = 0). (3) No compute-matched comparison: pass@1 is at 256 fixed denoising steps for every arm, so the CDC arm gets K_inner ALM steps + K_edit extra reverse steps + a surrogate forward/backward per denoising step FOR FREE relative to vanilla. (4) The head-to-head confidence-remasking baseline is absent -- CFG-CD is grammar-constrained decoding, not WINO/T2M/CORE-style confidence remasking. (5) No hidden-vs-visible test split, so plausible-patch overfitting is unmeasured.
related_work.known_defects: MAJOR ACCOUNTING DEFECT: the headline efficiency claim ('26,723 vs 35,640 tokens, 0.75x cost ratio'; '163 tokens per instance') counts only tokens GENERATED BY THE DIFFUSION MODEL. The paper itself states the per-step cost is 'at most one surrogate forward/backward pass' plus K_inner inner-optimization steps plus K_edit extra reverse steps, and the Limitations concede CDC 'still adds inference-time overhead from surrogate evaluation'. The 1.5B surrogate runs at EVERY denoising step (B.2: 'We apply GradGuide at each denoising step'); at 256 steps that is up to 256 forward+backward passes of a 1.5B model, plus the AR re-prompt baseline is charged with 'regenerating the full program body' while CDC 'counts only the regions that are remasked or inserted'. Strings 'wall-clock' and 'latency' appear ZERO times in the paper. So the efficiency comparison is structurally unfair in CDC's favour. SECOND DEFECT: the surrogate is trained on CodeContests with execution labels -- an extra training stage plus a train/test distribution question -- yet CDC is billed as 'training-free' (true only for the diffusion model). THIRD: no compute-matched arm at all, exactly the failure mode CaRE documents. FOURTH: single backbone family per benchmark, C++-only functionality, no Python.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1, 2026-05-16, no journal_ref); full HTML at arxiv.org/html/2605.16829v1 read end-to-end including Appendix B.2, B.3.1, B.3.3, C.1-C.5; grep counts for 'EvalPlus'(0), 'traceback'(0), 'test case'(0), 'wall-clock'(0), 'latency'(0), 'unit test'(2); OpenReview api2 title search.

related_work.citation: "Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2606.12232v1.
related_work.venue_status: Workshop papers, NOT main conference. Verified via OpenReview api2: two records with venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/SPIGM (forum HIMiqnTqLD, 'SPIGM @ ICML Poster', Camera_Ready_Revision present) and venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/AdaptFM (forum Bew2D82sWR, 'AdaptFM Poster', Camera_Ready_Revision present).
related_work.what_it_covers: Null result on the confidence-remasking family: revisits WINO and finds that under standard decoding settings (shorter block lengths) post-hoc confidence remasking brings little-to-no benefit over confidence-based unmasking alone. Under non-greedy decoding it partly mitigates stochasticity-induced errors but exacerbates diversity collapse. Concludes the benefits are highly setting-dependent.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Only shows the incumbent signal is weak; proposes no replacement signal. Evaluated on general text/reasoning settings, not code, and never touches execution evidence. Does not establish what a strong localization signal WOULD be, nor whether any localized-remasking family can beat equal-token full regeneration.
related_work.known_defects: A single representative method (WINO) is re-evaluated, so 'the family is in trouble' is an extrapolation from n=1; no code benchmark; workshop-length so ablation breadth is limited. Our use of it should therefore be as motivation, not as proof that all confidence remasking is dead.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 date + full abstract; OpenReview api2 /notes/search returning both workshop venueids with Camera_Ready_Revision invitations.

related_work.citation: "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2607.24763v1.
related_work.venue_status: preprint. Verified: arXiv v1 2026-06-04 with comment 'updated version', no journal_ref; OpenReview api2 title search for the exact CaRE title returns no matching submission (only unrelated FEval-TTC / COMPUTE 2024 records).
related_work.what_it_covers: Compute-aware audit framework for remasking strategies: standardizes ACTUAL NFE, enforces multi-metric reporting, controls stochasticity. Applied to 7 remasking strategies x {LLaDA-8B-Base, Dream-7B-Base} x 4 stochasticity levels x 3 step budgets. Headline findings: temperature explains most MAUVE variance; compute-matched comparison REVERSES several published strategy rankings; informed remasking and stochastic unmasking are in tension. Leaderboard over 12 open-weight MDLMs (150M-8B).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Benchmarks are OpenWebText and LM1B with MAUVE/generative-PPL -- pure open-ended text quality. No code, no functional-correctness metric, no verifier-in-the-loop. It audits SELECTION-RULE families all of which are model-internal; an execution-grounded rule is not in its 7-strategy set, so the protocol has never been applied to an external-evidence signal. Also does not price auxiliary scorer models (it standardizes NFE of the base denoiser).
related_work.known_defects: MAUVE on OpenWebText/LM1B is a distributional-similarity proxy, not a construct that any downstream user cares about, and it is famously sensitive to embedding model and sample size -- so 'ranking reversals' may partly be metric artefacts rather than compute artefacts. NFE-of-base-denoiser is also an incomplete cost unit the moment a method uses an auxiliary model (exactly CDC's case): a strategy can look NFE-matched while burning a 1.5B surrogate every step. Our fix extends CaRE's own logic to total-FLOPs/all-model-passes.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 metadata + full abstract; OpenReview api2 title search (no conference record).

related_work.citation: "Detect, Remask, Repair: Diffusion Editing for Faithful Summarization of Evolving Contexts." arXiv:2606.12807v1.
related_work.venue_status: preprint. Verified: arXiv v1 only, no journal_ref, no venue comment; OpenReview api2 search for the exact title returns zero matching notes.
related_work.what_it_covers: Structurally the same three-stage recipe we propose -- detect unsupported spans with an EXTERNAL detector, remask exactly those spans, re-diffuse with the rest frozen -- and it explicitly argues against full regeneration ('full regeneration discards the previous draft... may be unnecessary when only a few claims are unsupported'). Introduces StreamSum benchmark; evaluates on DialogSum + StreamSum.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The detector is a claim-support/faithfulness model over evolving text; the evidence is soft NLI-style support, not an executable oracle, and there is no ground-truth verdict on whether a span is 'wrong'. Task surface is summarization, not code; metric is faithfulness, not functional pass. No compute-matched budget across arms; no random-span control at matched token count; no report of newly-broken content (their analogue of newly_lost).
related_work.known_defects: Faithfulness metrics are themselves model-based and known to be noisy/gameable, so the construct being repaired is measured by the same class of model that detects it -- a circularity a code-execution oracle avoids entirely. Self-built synthetic benchmark (StreamSum) invites the usual 'benchmark tuned to the method' critique. Provides the citable precedent that localized remasking beats full rewriting only in a domain where the verifier is soft -- our contribution is testing whether it survives a HARD verifier and a compute-matched budget.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 metadata + full abstract; OpenReview api2 title search (zero hits).

related_work.citation: Feng Hong et al. "Wide-In, Narrow-Out: Revokable Decoding for Efficient and Effective DLLMs." arXiv:2507.18578.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2: forum XtLQHlNLxy, venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, venue 'ICLR 2026 Poster', invitations include Submission2256 Camera_Ready_Revision. Also NeurIPS 2025 ER Workshop Spotlight (forum AJVbbRQv7v).
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical pre-cutoff post-hoc confidence remasking method and the direct target of 2606.12232's null result. Training-free parallel draft-and-verify: aggressively draft many tokens, then use bidirectional context to verify and re-mask suspicious ones. Validated on LLaDA and MMaDA.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Selection is purely model-internal confidence. No code-execution signal, no traceback, no external verifier. Not evaluated as a code-repair operator on EvalPlus, and (per 2606.12232) its gains do not hold at standard shorter block lengths.
related_work.known_defects: Setting-dependent gains later shown to be little-to-none at standard block lengths (2606.12232); no compute-matched accounting of the draft-and-verify double passes; the 'suspicious token' construct is validated only by end metrics, never against ground-truth wrongness. This is precisely the incumbent our arm (b) instantiates, so it must be run at OUR matched budget rather than cited at its published numbers.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2025-07-24); OpenReview api2 confirming ICLR.cc/2026/Conference venueid with Camera_Ready_Revision (S2/DBLP still list it as CoRR 2025 -- exactly the 2026-venue lag this project has been burned by).

related_work.citation: "CORE: Context-Robust Remasking for Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2602.04096.
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 regular -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2: forum bmKHxLWkz9, venueid ICML.cc/2026/Conference, venue 'ICML 2026 regular', Submission6230 Camera_Ready_Revision present.
related_work.what_it_covers: Argues static confidence is myopic ('inconsistent tokens can appear confident to the model itself') and instead identifies context-BRITTLE tokens by probing sensitivity to targeted masked-context perturbations; formalizes revision as robust optimization over context shifts. Training-free.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Still entirely model-internal -- the ground truth is the model's own sensitivity, not program behaviour. No execution, no tests. Perturbation probing costs extra forward passes that are not obviously priced against baselines.
related_work.known_defects: Sensitivity probing multiplies forward passes per candidate position, so gains are vulnerable to exactly CaRE's compute-matched reversal; and 'context-brittle' is a proxy that has never been validated against known-wrong tokens (which a failing test gives us for free). Follow-up: validate brittleness as a wrongness detector using execution ground truth.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-02-04); OpenReview api2 ICML 2026 venueid + Camera_Ready_Revision.

related_work.citation: "Prism: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Hierarchical Search and Self-Verification for Discrete Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2602.01842.
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 regular -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2: forum QrC8OgQyOI, venueid ICML.cc/2026/Conference, venue 'ICML 2026 regular', Submission8004 Camera_Ready_Revision present. Consistent with the arXiv comment 'Accepted to ICML 2026'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Test-time scaling for dLLMs: hierarchical trajectory search with pruning/compute reallocation in an early-to-mid denoising window; local branching with PARTIAL REMASKING that preserves high-confidence tokens; and Self-Verified Feedback that explicitly REPLACES external verifiers.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its central design choice is the opposite of ours -- it deliberately substitutes model self-verification for an external verifier. So the question 'what if the verifier is exact and free (unit tests)?' is left entirely open, as is 'does self-verification beat oracle verification at matched compute?'
related_work.known_defects: Self-verification inherits the model's own blind spots and cannot detect errors the model is confident about -- the exact failure mode CORE identifies. A natural follow-up we enable: use Prism's search machinery with an execution oracle in place of SVF and measure how much of Prism's gain was verifier-limited vs search-limited.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2026-02-02, comment 'Accepted to ICML 2026'); OpenReview api2 ICML 2026 venueid + Camera_Ready_Revision.

related_work.citation: "MDM-VGB: VGB for Masked Diffusion Model: Efficient Test-time Scaling for Reward Satisfaction and Sample Editing." arXiv:2606.28301v1.
related_work.venue_status: preprint (arXiv v1, 72 pages, no journal_ref).
related_work.what_it_covers: Theoretically principled REWARD-GUIDED remasking: extends the Jerrum-Sinclair backtracking Markov chain from a prefix tree to a masked-state graph so tokens can be unmasked and remasked at arbitrary positions, favouring moves toward higher-value partial configurations. Proves robustness to process-verifier noise and quadratic complexity vs best-of-N's exponential error accumulation.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The reward/verifier is abstract and the empirics are Sudoku and QM9 -- constraint-satisfaction and molecules, not code, and the verifier is a value function over partial states rather than a program executor with a traceback. Provides no positional localization from evidence: the value function scores configurations, it does not point at the offending line.
related_work.known_defects: Toy-domain empirics (Sudoku/QM9) for a claim about general MDM test-time scaling; assumes a usable process verifier on PARTIAL states, which for code is exactly what does not exist (you cannot pytest a half-masked function). Useful as theory we can cite for why oracle-guided backtracking should beat best-of-N, and as a gap: nobody has instantiated it with a real execution oracle on a real code benchmark.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 metadata + full abstract.

related_work.citation: "OSCAR: Orchestrated Self-verification and Cross-path Refinement." arXiv:2604.01624.
related_work.venue_status: preprint (arXiv v2 2026-04-03, no journal_ref, no venue comment).
related_work.what_it_covers: Formulates 'commitment uncertainty localization': from a denoising trajectory, identify positions whose CROSS-CHAIN ENTROPY exceeds an unsupervised threshold before unreliable commitments propagate. Introduces trajectory-level assessments incl. a cross-chain divergence-at-hallucination (CDH) metric; OSCAR runs N parallel denoising chains. Explicitly argues an ideal framework should use a model-native signal rather than an external classifier.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: States the model-native-signal preference as a design axiom and never tests it against an exact external oracle. Domain is factual hallucination, not code; localization ground truth is a hallucination annotation, not a program failure. N parallel chains is an N-fold compute multiplier whose fairness is unexamined.
related_work.known_defects: The 'model-native is preferable' premise is asserted, not demonstrated -- our arm (a)-vs-(b) contrast at matched cost is a direct empirical test of it in a domain where the external signal is exact and cheap. N-chain compute is a large hidden cost. CDH validates localizers against hallucination labels of uncertain reliability, whereas execution gives a hard label.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-04-02) + full abstract.

related_work.citation: "NAVIRA: Decoupled Stochastic Remasking for Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2606.06031v1.
related_work.venue_status: preprint (arXiv v1 only).
related_work.what_it_covers: Decouples detection from replacement: a first forward pass scores tokens, selected tokens are masked, a second forward pass regenerates from the cleaned context; remask positions are sampled stochastically with a temperature. Motivated as fixing PRISM's coupled inference rule where erroneous tokens still condition their own regeneration.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Scoring is a learned/model-internal token-quality score. Two forward passes per correction is a real cost that must be priced -- and is exactly the kind of thing CaRE says is usually not priced. No code-execution evidence, no traceback.
related_work.known_defects: The decoupling argument (do not let the bad token condition its replacement) applies verbatim to our design and is worth citing, but NAVIRA never validates its score against ground-truth wrongness; stochastic temperature adds a tuned hyperparameter whose effect is entangled with the diversity-collapse phenomenon 2606.12232 documents.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 metadata + full abstract.

related_work.citation: "Remask, Don't Replace: Token-to-Mask Refinement in Diffusion Large Language Models." arXiv:2604.18738 (supersedes withdrawn arXiv:2605.26436, 'Targeted Remasking').
related_work.venue_status: preprint (v2 2026-05-07). Note the candidate's cited 2605.26436 is the WITHDRAWN version -- its arXiv comment states it 'has been significantly revised, expanded, and superseded by ... arXiv:2604.18738' and was withdrawn to avoid overlap. Cite 2604.18738.
related_work.what_it_covers: Argues the replacement ACTION is the limiting factor in LLaDA2.1-style Token-to-Token editing: under polluted context a confident replacement propagates error, and under a multimodal posterior no alternative is confident enough to trigger an edit. Proposes T2M -- reset suspicious commitments to [M] and let mask-filling re-predict from cleaner context. Training-free, +13.33 on AIME 2025.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: 'Suspicious' is still a confidence criterion. Reasoning/math benchmarks, not code repair; no execution signal; no matched-compute accounting of the extra refill steps.
related_work.known_defects: The candidate's builds_on cites the withdrawn ID -- a citation-hygiene bug to fix before writing. Substantively: T2M's remask-vs-replace argument is a strong justification for our canvas-level remask hook (and against our own retracted Arm B prompt-splice), but its evidence is single-benchmark deltas without compute matching.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API for both IDs; the withdrawal/supersession is stated verbatim in 2605.26436's own arXiv comment field.

related_work.citation: Jianan Yao / et al. "Is Self-Repair a Silver Bullet for Code Generation?" arXiv:2306.09896, ICLR 2024.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2024 (stated in arXiv comment: 'Accepted to ICLR 2024. Added additional Code Llama experiments and fixed a data processing error...').
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical AR-side prior: when the COST of repair is accounted for, self-repair gains are often modest, vary a lot across data subsets, and are sometimes absent; the bottleneck is the model's ability to produce feedback on its own code (a stronger feedback model helps). HumanEval + APPS, Code Llama / GPT-3.5 / GPT-4.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Entirely autoregressive, re-prompting-based. Says nothing about a canvas where you can surgically remask 30 tokens and keep the rest frozen -- the structural affordance that makes diffusion repair potentially cheaper than AR repair. Also predates execution-oracle-in-the-loop diffusion work.
related_work.known_defects: None that undermine it; it is the methodological ancestor of our kill_criterion (cost-matched comparison against just sampling more from the base model). Its lesson -- feedback quality is the bottleneck -- directly motivates substituting an exact test oracle for model self-feedback, which is our arm (a) vs Prism's SVF.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + comment field naming ICLR 2024.

related_work.citation: Runchu Tian et al. "Debug like a Human: A Large Language Model Debugger via Verifying Runtime Execution Step-by-step" (LDB). arXiv:2402.16906.
related_work.venue_status: preprint per arXiv comment ('Preprint', v6 2024-06-06); no journal_ref in arXiv metadata.
related_work.what_it_covers: The strongest AR-side precedent for using RUNTIME EXECUTION detail (not just pass/fail) to guide repair: segments programs into basic blocks and verifies intermediate variable values after each block against the task description, so the LLM localizes the fault.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Purely autoregressive re-generation of the buggy region via prompting. No diffusion, no canvas, no remasking -- and therefore no notion of freezing the untouched committed tokens. Also no compute-matched comparison against simply resampling.
related_work.known_defects: Establishes that runtime/variable-level evidence localizes faults better than pass/fail, which strengthens our motivation, and simultaneously means a reviewer will ask 'is your contribution just LDB ported to a canvas?' -- answer must foreground the compute-matched selection-signal comparison and the frozen-context canvas operation, not the mere use of tracebacks.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + comment field.

related_work.citation: "Beyond Execution: Static-Analysis Rewards and Hint-Conditioned Diffusion RL for Code Generation." arXiv:2605.17174v1.
related_work.venue_status: preprint (arXiv v1 only).
related_work.what_it_covers: Systematic study of RL post-training for diffusion code generation: reward design (execution-free static-checking rewards vs unit-test execution rewards), hint-conditioned diffusion sampling, and task difficulty. Finds a 'capability cliff' where execution-based semantic rewards are too sparse to learn from, and that static checking is the strongest reward. HumanEval, MBPP, LiveCodeBench.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: This is TRAINING-time reward design, not inference-time position selection. It argues execution reward is a WEAK learning signal because of sparsity -- which is a different claim from ours (execution evidence is a strong LOCALIZATION signal at inference, precisely because you only need it on the tasks that already fail). Worth citing as the apparent counter-evidence and distinguishing explicitly.
related_work.known_defects: Conflates 'sparse scalar execution reward is hard to learn from' with 'execution signal is weak'; a traceback is not a scalar, it is a positional pointer, and is used only on failing drafts where it is by construction non-sparse. Our experiment is the natural rebuttal-by-scope-separation.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 metadata + full abstract.

related_work.citation: "Exploring the Power of Diffusion Large Language Models for Software Engineering: An Empirical Investigation." arXiv:2510.04605v1.

related_work.citation: "Corrective Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2512.15596.
related_work.venue_status: preprint (v2 2026-01-29, 21 pages, no journal_ref).
related_work.what_it_covers: Shows the standard MDLM unmasking objective does NOT induce the ability to assign lower confidence to incorrect visible tokens, which is why confidence-guided refinement fails; proposes a correction-oriented post-training principle that explicitly supervises visible incorrect tokens.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its remedy is TRAINING (post-training the model to be a better self-critic). The complementary inference-time remedy -- stop relying on model confidence and read the position off an external exact oracle -- is untouched. Not a code-repair paper.
related_work.known_defects: Requires post-training, so it is unavailable to anyone using an off-the-shelf checkpoint; and it concedes-by-construction that confidence is a broken wrongness estimator in pretrained MDLMs, which is the strongest theoretical support for our claim and should be cited as the mechanism, not just as related work.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + full abstract.

related_work.citation: Zhihui Xie et al. "DiffuCoder: Understanding and Improving Masked Diffusion Models for Code Generation." arXiv:2506.20639.
related_work.venue_status: preprint (v2 2026-06-26, comment 'minor update', no journal_ref).
related_work.what_it_covers: Trains a 7B code dLLM on 130B code tokens and analyses decoding behaviour: dLLMs can modulate their own causality without semi-AR decoding, and raising temperature diversifies not just token choice but generation ORDER. Introduces coupled-GRPO.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Characterizes decoding/order behaviour but does not build any verifier-in-the-loop repair operator. The order-diversity finding is a confound our protocol must control (it is the same family as our own measured +14.6 HumanEval swing from top_p 1.0 -> 0.95).
related_work.known_defects: Not a defect for us -- but it is the paper that makes 'sampler settings dominate' undeniable, so any arm comparison that does not fix temperature/top_p identically across arms is unpublishable. We should cite it when justifying the frozen sampler protocol.

related_work.citation: "DreamOn: Diffusion Language Models For Code Infilling Beyond Fixed-size Canvas." arXiv:2602.01326.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 (stated in arXiv comment 'ICLR 2026'; recorded as ICLR 2026 Poster in this project's prior OpenReview audit in TASK_SURFACE_LIT_GAPS.md).
related_work.what_it_covers: Variable-length / mask-expansion diffusion for code infilling; HumanEval-Infilling single/multi-line + SantaCoder-FIM(Python) vs Qwen2.5-Coder-7B / DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B / Seed-Coder-8B. Dream-Coder single-line 55.5 -> 92.1 with DreamOn; multi-line 43.2 -> 63.8.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Length-elastic infilling given a KNOWN hole. Says nothing about WHERE the hole should be -- hole location is given by the benchmark. diff.differentiation_statement: The remasking literature selects positions from model-internal signals, and the one paper that touches program semantics -- CDC (arXiv:2605.16829, 2026-05-16, concurrent) -- localizes via the gradient of a LEARNED soft correctness surrogate (a Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B regressor trained on CodeContests execution labels), invoked at every denoising step, on C++ benchmarks (HumanEval-X C++, MBPP-C++), with all arms run at a fixed 256 denoising steps so that its extra surrogate forward/backward passes, K_inner ALM iterations and K_edit refill steps are free relative to vanilla. CDC mentions unit-test execution only as an optional boolean TRIGGER for its Mode-B remask, never as the localization signal; the strings 'traceback', 'test case' and 'EvalPlus' do not appear in the paper, and 'wall-clock' and 'latency' appear zero times. We differ on four axes a reviewer can check independently: (1) SIGNAL -- hard positional evidence (the failing test's traceback line plus the identifiers it implicates, mapped to canvas token spans) instead of a learned soft surrogate saliency, meaning no auxiliary model, no extra training stage, and a localizer that is exact rather than approximate; (2) ACCOUNTING -- every arm is matched on cumulative_model_tokens counted across ALL model passes, base denoiser and any scorer alike, with budget-truncated tasks included via the proc() accessor, which is the compute-aware discipline CaRE (2607.24763) demands and which CDC does not apply; (3) CONTROL DESIGN -- we run the two controls the field omits, random-span remasking at matched token count and equal-token full regeneration, and we gate the whole paper on beating the Dream-Coder nfe512 direct-run ceiling (HE+ .707 / MBPP+ .680) that we measured ourselves, plus we report newly_lost alongside rescued and the visible-pass-but-hidden-fail count per arm; (4) SETTING -- Python EvalPlus with the hidden-test split, evalplus.eval.untrusted_check as verifier, and Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B, versus CDC's C++ pass@1/pass@10. Detect-Remask-Repair (2606.12807, concurrent) shares the detect/remask/freeze/re-diffuse skeleton but its detector is a soft claim-support model and its domain is summarization faithfulness, so it establishes the skeleton works when the verifier is soft and leaves open whether it survives a hard verifier under a matched budget. Nothing pre-2026-05-07 makes this claim in this setting.

followup_openings.target_paper: CDC / Constrained Code Generation with Discrete Diffusion (arXiv:2605.16829)
followup_openings.defect: The headline token-efficiency result -- 26,723 vs 35,640 tokens on HumanEval-X (0.75x), 163 tokens/instance vs 217 -- counts ONLY tokens generated by the diffusion model. The paper itself states the per-step cost is 'at most one surrogate forward/backward pass' plus K_inner inner-optimization steps plus K_edit extra reverse steps, that GradGuide is applied 'at each denoising step', and that CDC 'still adds inference-time overhead from surrogate evaluation'. Meanwhile the AR re-prompt baseline is charged with 'regenerating the full program body' while CDC 'counts only the regions that are remasked or inserted'. 'wall-clock' and 'latency' appear zero times. At 256 steps that is up to 256 forward+backward passes of a 1.5B model excluded from the ledger.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-price localized diffusion repair in a single currency that charges every model pass -- base denoiser AND localizer -- and report wall-clock alongside it. Concretely: run our arm (a) (free exact oracle: the traceback already exists, cost = one subprocess execution, zero GPU FLOPs) against a faithful reimplementation of surrogate-gradient localization at equal TOTAL model FLOPs, and show whether the reported locality advantage of soft-surrogate localization survives once the surrogate is on the meter. Report edited-token counts (CDC's locality metric) separately from total compute so the two claims cannot be conflated.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts our project from 'another remasking variant' into the compute-honest audit of the one execution-adjacent diffusion-code paper, which is exactly the contribution CaRE argues the field needs and did not itself deliver for code. If the surrogate loses once priced, that is a headline; if it wins, we have quantified the price of exactness and still own the Python/EvalPlus/matched-budget setting.

followup_openings.target_paper: CDC / Constrained Code Generation with Discrete Diffusion (arXiv:2605.16829)
followup_openings.defect: Functional-correctness experiments are C++-only (HumanEval-X C++ 164, MBPP-C++ 397), and 'compile success' is a large share of the reported gain (Dream-Coder syntax 41.1 -> 72.0 on MBPP-C++). In C++ a huge fraction of failures are compile failures that a static/grammar signal can fix, which inflates a program-analysis-based localizer relative to a language where nearly everything parses. We independently measured that Dream-Coder's unparseable-output rate on Python collapses from ~94% to 1.8% (HE+) / 1.6% (MBPP+) between nfe16 and nfe512.
followup_openings.our_fix: Replicate the localized-remasking-beats-regeneration claim in Python on EvalPlus, where the compile-failure escape hatch is nearly closed at high NFE, and decompose the gain into (i) recovered parse/compile failures and (ii) recovered semantic failures. Our nfe256 drafts already give the split (131/164 parse, 33 syntax errors on HE+), so we can report the semantic-only subset that CDC's aggregate hides.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A cross-language replication with the syntax/semantic decomposition tests whether 'denoising-time constraint correction closes the gap to AR' is a general claim or a C++ compile-error artefact. Either outcome is publishable and neither requires new training.

followup_openings.target_paper: Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking (arXiv:2606.12232, ICML 2026 SPIGM + AdaptFM workshops) and CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763)
followup_openings.defect: Both critiques stop at demolition. 2606.12232 re-evaluates a single method (WINO) on general text and shows near-zero benefit; CaRE shows compute-matched comparison reverses rankings but audits only MAUVE/gen-PPL on OpenWebText/LM1B across 7 model-internal strategies. Neither offers a positive answer to 'what signal SHOULD select remask positions', neither touches a task with a hard correctness oracle, and CaRE's cost unit (NFE of the base denoiser) does not price auxiliary scorer models, so a method can be NFE-matched while burning a 1.5B surrogate every step.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the constructive half plus an extension of the cost unit. Extend the compute-matched protocol to a task where correctness is exact (EvalPlus pass/fail via evalplus.eval.untrusted_check, whose visible-pass rate we validated to match evalplus base pass@1 at three independent points), add an execution-grounded selector to the strategy set, and redefine the budget as all-model-passes rather than base-denoiser NFE so auxiliary-model methods are comparable.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: 'The confidence family is weak' is currently an n=1 null on text. Showing on code, under an all-passes budget, either that a hard-evidence signal fixes it or that NOTHING beats equal-token regeneration, turns two negative workshop/preprint results into a settled positive or a strong general null. The general null is itself valuable and is the outcome our kill_criterion is built to detect rather than bury.

followup_openings.target_paper: Detect, Remask, Repair (arXiv:2606.12807)
followup_openings.defect: Localized-repair-beats-full-rewriting is demonstrated only where the verifier is soft (a claim-support/faithfulness model on DialogSum + a self-built synthetic StreamSum), so the detector and the metric are the same class of model -- circular. No matched-compute budget across arms, no random-span control at matched token count, and no reporting of content newly broken by repair.
followup_openings.our_fix: Port the identical detect/remask/freeze/re-diffuse skeleton to a hard verifier, add the two missing controls (random-span at matched token count; equal-token full regeneration), and report newly_lost alongside rescued plus per-arm visible-pass-but-hidden-fail counts -- a false-pass channel that soft-verifier domains cannot even measure and that our own grid showed is real (HE+ medium 5, MBPP+ large 23).
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Establishes whether 'localized repair is a controllable alternative to full rewriting' is a general property of masked diffusion or an artefact of soft, non-adversarial verification. The hidden-test split makes plausible-patch overfitting measurable, which no diffusion remasking paper currently reports.

followup_openings.target_paper: Prism (arXiv:2602.01842, ICML 2026) and OSCAR (arXiv:2604.01624)
followup_openings.defect: Both build in the axiom that model-native signals are preferable to external verifiers -- Prism explicitly 'replaces external verifiers with Self-Verified Feedback', OSCAR states an ideal framework should use a model-native signal 'rather than relying on an externally trained hallucination classifier'. Neither tests the axiom against an EXACT, cheap external oracle, and neither prices its multiplier (Prism's hierarchical search, OSCAR's N parallel chains).
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the head-to-head the axiom presumes: same backbone, same canvas, same total model-pass budget, self-verification/cross-chain-entropy localization vs execution-oracle localization. Report the compute multiplier of each. Because our oracle is a subprocess with zero GPU cost, the comparison is maximally unfavourable to us on signal availability and maximally favourable on cost -- exactly the informative regime.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts an unexamined design axiom of two 2026 papers (one ICML) into a measured trade-off, and tells practitioners when spending GPU on self-verification is worth it versus just running the tests. Cheap: no training, uses drafts already on disk.

followup_openings.target_paper: Beyond Execution: Static-Analysis Rewards and Hint-Conditioned Diffusion RL (arXiv:2605.17174)
followup_openings.defect: Concludes execution-based semantic rewards are too weak to learn from (a 'capability cliff' from reward sparsity) and that static checking is the strongest reward -- then this conclusion gets read as 'execution signal is weak for diffusion code models' generally. But sparsity of a SCALAR reward at training time says nothing about the density of a POSITIONAL signal at inference time, and a traceback is only ever consulted on drafts that already fail, where it is by construction non-sparse.
followup_openings.our_fix: Draw the scope line empirically: show that the same execution oracle that is a poor RL reward is a strong inference-time localizer, by reporting localization precision (does the traceback-implicated span actually contain a token that must change?) separately from end-task pass@1. That decomposition is what turns a scope disagreement into evidence.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Pre-empts the most likely reviewer objection ('a 2026 paper already showed execution signals underperform static analysis for diffusion code models') by separating reward-density from evidence-locality, and yields a reusable localization-precision metric the remasking literature currently lacks entirely.

followup_openings.target_paper: Our own retracted refinement arms (this repo, commit 67a7a01 and scripts/refine_verifier_guided.py)
followup_openings.defect: Arm A ('restart') regenerates from the prompt and DISCARDS the scaffold draft, so it measured Dream-Coder-Instruct rather than refinement -- each tier's hidden-pass rate on its own routed set matched the tiny run's rate on the same tasks to within -0.008..-0.023. Arm B ('remask') is a prompt-text splice, not a canvas operation: the code re-encodes prev_solution, keeps int(len(toks)*(1-remask_frac)) tokens and re-runs diffusion from there, which is tail-truncation-then-continue rather than masking arbitrary interior positions with the surrounding committed context frozen. Both retracted results came from the older broken hand-rolled verifier.
followup_openings.our_fix: Build the true canvas-level remask hook (arbitrary interior span -> [MASK], all other committed tokens frozen, re-diffuse) and never reuse the splice path; verify with evalplus.eval.untrusted_check only; and make the equal-token full-regeneration arm plus the nfe512 direct-run ceiling MANDATORY gates checked before any number is written down. Report newly_lost and false-pass counts per arm as first-class metrics, and read cost from process OR failure_process so budget-truncated tasks are not silently dropped (Retraction 3 understated scaffold Large's cost 2.85x/3.69x).
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Fixing a genuinely bidirectional edit operator is the only way to test masked diffusion's one structural advantage over AR -- editing arbitrary positions with bidirectional context -- which both of our prior refinement arms threw away. It is also the cheapest path to a defensible result: drafts and verifier are already on disk, no training, ~25 GPU-hours.

blocking_gaps: MEASURED, THE BIGGEST ONE: the localization signal is absent on most of the target set. I ran every parseable failing nfe256 draft under a subprocess harness that distinguishes exception-from-wrong-value. HE+ (n=73 non-plus-pass): wrong_value 24, syntax_error 33, exec_error 11, runtime_exception 1, all_pass 4. So only 12/69 real failures (17%) raise anything a traceback could point at; 24 silently return the wrong value, where the traceback literally does not exist. evalplus.eval.untrusted_check CANNOT give you one either: unsafe_execute (site-packages/evalplus/eval/__init__.py:207) does `except BaseException: details[i]=False; continue` inside swallow_io, so the exception object is discarded before returning. The stored eval records contain only ['task_id','solution','base_status','plus_status','base_fail_tests','plus_fail_tests'] -- base_fail_tests is a boolean index list, no trace. You must write your OWN executor to obtain tracebacks; the existing verifier is unusable for localization (it is only usable for grading).

MEASURED: most of the exceptions that DO exist point at the draft's own scratch code, not at the bug. Across ALL 378 MBPP+ drafts the top-level non-def AST nodes are {Assert: 270, Expr: 67, Assign: 39} -- the model echoes the prompt's asserts and adds print() demos. HE+ example HumanEval/108: a correct-shaped count_nums plus three trailing `print(count_nums([...]))` lines; the ValueError traceback names the print line. 21/40 parseable failing HE+ drafts carry top-level scratch statements. A naive traceback->span mapper will therefore remask demo code and score gains that are really 'deleted the demo', which is Retraction-1-shaped (measuring something other than what you claim).

MEASURED: a zero-GPU-cost competitor already captures much of the available headroom, and the candidate does not include it as an arm. I implemented pure-AST cleanup (drop top-level non-def statements; on SyntaxError truncate to the longest parseable prefix) and graded with the official evalplus.evaluate: HE+ .555 -> .567, MBPP+ .545 -> .582 (+3.7 points), at literally zero model passes. After that free fix the positional signal shrinks further: HE+ 27/71 = 38.0%, MBPP+ 49/158 = 31.0%. Any execution-localized arm must beat this free baseline, not the raw nfe256 number, or the paper reports a compute-priced win over a strawman.

The candidate's premise 'we have a retraction-hardened verifier and drafts on disk, so we mainly need a span mapper' understates the build. The traceback executor, the AST identifier-implication extractor, the scratch-code discriminator, and the offset mapper are all new. On offsets: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B ships a SLOW tokenizer only (type DreamTokenizer, tok.is_fast == False), so return_offsets_mapping raises NotImplementedError. I verified a cumulative-decode fallback mapper is sound on 164/164 HE+ drafts (every token's char slice round-trips), so this is solvable in ~20 lines -- but it is a silent-corruption surface that must be asserted in CI, not assumed.

STEP 1 -- LOCK THE FREE FLOOR AS ARM 0 (1 h, CPU only). Promote my throwaway prototypes into REPO/scripts/repair_free_ast.py. One currency = tokens_fed, summed over every model forward of every model (denoiser and any scorer), read via a proc() accessor that falls back to failure_process (Retraction 3). Canvas width is prompt+512 = 674 for these runs, so one localized re-diffuse at S steps costs S*674 regardless of hole count. Also log the no-op-forward count: I replicated the transfer schedule and at 8 holes / 16 steps, 9 of 16 steps transfer ZERO tokens yet still pay a full-canvas forward -- so "steps" must never be used as the cost unit, and S should be tuned near the hole count (8 holes/8 steps wastes 1 of 8).

STEP 6 -- ARMS, MATCHED (8-10 GPU-h on 5 idle L20A, HE+ then MBPP+). Budget per task = 674*256 = 172,544 tok, which at S=8 buys 32 localized attempts. Arms: (0) free AST cleanup, 0 GPU; (a) execution-localized spans, restricted to frame_in_scratch==false; (b) lowest-LOO-confidence-k at matched hole count -- reuse the strided batched LOO in scripts/pilot_repair.py (8 forwards for the whole sequence) and CHARGE those 8 forwards to the ledger; (c) random spans at matched hole count AND matched span-length distribution to (a); (d) equal-token full regeneration from the prompt -- note this equals a second independent nfe256 sample, so it is a pass@2-flavoured arm and the honest thing to beat; (e) no-refine. All arms start from arm 0's output, share temperature=0.1/top_p=0.95 (DiffuCoder + our own +14.6-point top_p swing make this non-negotiable), and are graded ONLY by evalplus.evaluate / untrusted_check with expected-value comparison.

STEP 7 -- REPORT (2 h, CPU). Per arm: rescued, newly_lost, net, visible-pass-but-hidden-fail, tokens_fed mean/median, wall-clock, and localization precision (did the remasked span contain a token that had to change, judged by difflib against canonical_solution -- scripts/pilot_oracle.py already has that oracle-diff). Stratify EVERY number by has_positional_signal, and report the oracle-diff-localized arm as the attainable ceiling. Hand-roll bootstrap CIs in numpy (scipy absent). Gate check before writing prose: HE+ needs >23 net additional rescues over arm 0 to clear the .707 nfe512 line, MBPP+ needs >37 to clear .680; and on MBPP+ state explicitly that AR greedy .648 @101 tok sits above the whole corridor.
feas.risk: The single most likely outcome is a CONFOUNDED positive, not a null, and it is Retraction-1-shaped: arm (a) wins because the traceback points into the draft's own trailing scratch code (270 top-level Asserts + 67 Exprs in MBPP+; 21/40 parseable failing HE+ drafts), so "remask the traceback line" degenerates into "delete the demo block" -- a free AST edit dressed up as execution grounding. I already measured that the pure-AST version of that edit is worth +1.2 (HE+) and +3.7 (MBPP+) points at zero GPU cost, so the confound is large enough to carry a headline. The `frame_in_scratch` flag plus arm 0 as the floor is what converts this from a fake win into a real decomposition. Second most likely: a genuine null on the primary ordering, because after the free cleanup only 38.0% (HE+ 27/71) and 31.0% (MBPP+ 49/158) of failures carry any positional signal at all, and the dominant residual mode is wrong_value -- a silently incorrect return where no traceback exists and (a), (b) and (c) all collapse to the same uninformed guess, making the arms statistically indistinguishable on n≈27 at HE+. Third: gate (d) is simply not passable. Reaching the nfe512 ceiling from the arm-0 start needs >23/164 (HE+) and >37/378 (MBPP+) net rescues inside a budget equal to one whole nfe256 run, while arm (d) at that budget is a second independent nfe256 sample; if pass@2 exceeds the refinement arms, the framing dies exactly as Retraction 2 did -- and on MBPP+ matched AR greedy already scores .648 at 101 tokens_fed, above the entire corridor, so R4's logic applies before any of this is written down.
feas.required_control: ARM 0 = THE FREE AST-ONLY REPAIR, RUN FIRST AND USED AS THE DENOMINATOR FOR EVERY OTHER ARM, PAIRED WITH A PER-TASK `frame_in_scratch` FLAG THAT EXCLUDES ANY TRACEBACK FRAME LANDING OUTSIDE A KEPT def/class BODY. Rationale: our three retractions share one shape -- a pipeline credited for work it did not do (a verifier that compared nothing; a stage that discarded its input; an average that dropped the expensive tasks). The analogous failure here is crediting "execution grounding" for deleting the model's own trailing `print(...)`/`assert ...` scratch lines. I measured that this free, model-free edit alone moves HE+ .555->.567 and MBPP+ .545->.582 and that 270 Asserts + 67 Exprs + 39 Assigns sit at top level across the MBPP+ drafts, so the confound is bigger than most published remasking gains. Concretely the control has three non-negotiable parts: (1) every arm's input is arm-0 output, and every delta is reported against arm 0, never against raw nfe256; (2) arm (a) is forbidden from remasking spans whose traceback frame has frame_in_scratch==true, and the count of such excluded tasks is reported; (3) the mode census (wrong_value / syntax_error / exec_error / runtime_exception / timeout) is published per arm so a reader can see that 62% (HE+) / 69% (MBPP+) of the post-cleanup failure set carries no positional signal at all, making it impossible to present an aggregate gain as evidence that execution evidence localizes bugs. Secondary but mandatory assertion: the cumulative-decode offset mapper must round-trip every token (`src[a:b] == tok.decode([ids[i]])`) on every draft, since tok.is_fast is False and a silently misaligned span would corrupt all three localization arms identically and invisibly.

lens.title: Does grammar-constrained decoding buy the low-compute regime? A constraint-vs-NFE frontier
lens.claim: The low-NFE deficit of masked diffusion code generation is dominated by structural illegality, not semantic error; therefore imposing grammar validity by construction collapses a large part of the 64-to-512-step gap, and a CFG-constrained sampler reaches the low-token-cost Pareto frontier that we previously showed belongs only to a trained structural runtime.
lens.why_now: This question is forced by our own most trustworthy measurement, and it is dangerous to us, which is why it is worth running. Our NFE sweep reproduces identically on two benchmarks: HE+ pass@1+ .018/.140/.555/.707 and MBPP+ .029/.233/.545/.680 at NFE 64/128/256/512, with unparseable-output rate falling 94%->1.8% (HE+) and 89%->1.6% (MBPP+) over that range, and EXACTLY zero gain from 512->1024 on both. So the low-NFE region is mostly spent buying syntactic legality. Three papers now make grammar validity cheap and exact -- 2508.10111 (first CFG-constrained diffusion decoding, near-perfect syntactic correctness), EPIC 2606.00722 (cuts constrained-decoding time up to 67.5%), and 2607.07026 (exact sampling from the constrained mean-field posterior under any finite automaton, lifting Dream-7B BFCL-Live greedy 63.9->71.5 and stochastic 22.3->69.0 with <5% wall-clock overhead) -- but every one of them evaluates at a single standard step budget and frames the contribution as constraint satisfaction or overhead reduction. My arXiv probes for grammar/constrained-decoding crossed with NFE, step budget, low-step, or compute frontier return 0 hits: nobody has swept constraint benefit AGAINST compute. And the result threatens our own only surviving claim, since scaffold Medium's low-cost win (HE+ .177 at 13.98k tokens, MBPP+ .354 at 7.08k, where vanilla nfe16/nfe32 score .000/.000 and .000/.008) may be a learned-grammar effect obtainable far more cheaply by a CFG mask.
lens.experiment: Sweep NFE in {32,64,128,256,512} on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ with four arms: (1) unconstrained Dream-Coder-Instruct (already measured, reuse runs/); (2) grammar-constrained Dream-Coder using an incremental Python-subset validity mask over mask positions; (3) scaffold Medium, our trained structural runtime (the 'learned grammar' arm, HE+ .177 / MBPP+ .354 already measured); (4) matched plain-SFT (already measured: HE+ nfe64 .000, nfe128 .049, nfe512 .2195; MBPP+ nfe512 .2434). Everything priced in cumulative_model_tokens with the proc() accessor so truncated tasks are included, and with the CPU-side constraint overhead reported SEPARATELY from model tokens so we do not hide it. Key decomposition at each budget: unparseable rate, parses-but-unbound-name rate, and parses-and-binds-but-fails-tests rate -- this splits grammar cost from scope cost from semantic cost. I already validated this decomposition on existing solutions: nfe128 = 112 syntax errors / 52 parse / 10 of those with unbound names; nfe256 = 33 / 131 / 6. Deliverable is one figure: pass@1+ versus cumulative model tokens, four arms, with the constrained curve overlaid on the existing Pareto plot.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: all four arms' models and prior runs (Dream-Coder-Instruct, models/Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, plain-SFT numbers in BASELINE_STATS.md); scripts/make_pareto_figures.py already fixed for the proc() accessor and field_coverage() reporting (commit 8451e93); scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py sharded harness; tree_sitter_python installed for incremental parse validity. NEEDS WRITING: the per-step legality mask over mask positions -- note the honest subtlety that a mean-field parallel commit can be individually-legal but jointly-illegal, which is precisely the problem 2607.07026 solves exactly and EPIC solves fast, so the implementation should follow one of them and cite it rather than inventing a weaker mask. No new models, no training.
lens.kill_criterion: If constrained nfe64 stays in the .00-.05 band on both benchmarks -- i.e. the constrained curve does not move materially left on the token-cost axis -- then syntactic legality was never the binding constraint at low compute, the low-NFE deficit is semantic, and this claim dies (while our scaffold Pareto claim strengthens). Conversely, if the constrained curve dominates scaffold Medium at equal token cost, our own surviving Pareto claim must be rewritten to say the low-cost segment belongs to grammar enforcement generally rather than to a trained structural runtime. Both outcomes are publishable; the candidate is designed so that we cannot avoid learning something.
lens.builds_on: Follow-up on 2508.10111 (CFG-constrained diffusion decoding, 2025-08-13, genuinely prior), EPIC (2606.00722), and 2607.07026. Defect we repair: all three fix the step budget and ask 'can we enforce constraints, and how cheaply', never 'how does the value of enforcement vary with compute'. Also stress-tests our own token-cost Pareto segmentation claim and the AnCoder/TreeDiff line (2602.17688, 2508.01473) which anchors on AST structure during TRAINING rather than enforcing legality at inference.

related_work.citation: Niels Mündler, Jasper Dekoninck, Martin Vechev. "Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars." arXiv:2508.10111; ICLR 2026 Poster (also DL4C @ NeurIPS 2025 Oral).
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster. Verified on OpenReview: forum 7Sph4KyeYO, venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference', invitations include 'ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Submission8023/-/Camera_Ready_Revision'; bibtex @inproceedings{mundler2026constrained}. Earlier workshop version: venueid='NeurIPS.cc/2025/Workshop/DL4C', 'DL4C @ NeurIPS 2025 Oral'.
related_work.what_it_covers: First CFG-constrained decoding for diffusion LLMs. Reduces constrained decoding to additive infilling, then to CFG-vs-regular intersection emptiness. Evaluated on LLaDA-8B, Dream-7B, DreamCoder-7B, DiffuCoder-7B over C++ (HumanEval-X C++ split, n=164), JSON-Schema extraction (n=272), SMILES (n=167). Near-perfect syntactic correctness with functional correctness preserved or improved. CRITICALLY: Appendix D.4 Table 5 is a diffusion-step ablation at steps {16,32,64,128,256} on Dream-7B reporting BOTH syntax and functional correctness for Vanilla / Con.- / Con., and Table 6 reports the matching per-step runtime overhead. That is structurally the candidate's proposed constraint-vs-step-budget sweep, published pre-cutoff.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The step ablation is a single-model (Dream-7B), appendix-level table on C++/JSON/SMILES; it is never framed or analysed as a compute frontier — no cost-normalised x-axis, no plot, no crossover analysis, no cost unit other than seconds of overhead. No Python, no MBPP+, no EvalPlus, no HumanEval+ extra tests. No error decomposition beyond syntax-vs-functional (no unbound-name/scope tier). No trained-structural-prior arm, so the 'learned grammar vs enforced grammar at equal cost' question is untouched. Steps stop at 256; our saturation point is 512.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Steps are conflated with cost: overhead is reported in seconds relative to unconstrained at the SAME step count, so constrained-at-16 is never priced against unconstrained-at-256 — the comparison a compute frontier requires. (2) Table 5's own numbers arguably undercut the syntax-is-the-bottleneck reading and the paper does not say so: at 16 steps constraining lifts C++ syntax 8.1%→99.2% but functional only 1.4%→4.9%, i.e. near-perfect legality recovers ~4.9 of the 34.8 points available at 256 steps. At 128 steps Con.- is actually WORSE than vanilla (23.9 vs 24.5). This non-monotonicity and the tiny absolute functional ceiling at low steps are never discussed. (3) C++/JSON/SMILES only — the grammar-free-of-indentation cases; Python's off-side rule (where a CFG must model INDENT/DEDENT tokens) is dodged entirely. (4) n=164/272/167 with no CIs or seeds on the ablation. (5) Single temperature 0.2, single model in the ablation, so no evidence the step-dependence replicates across families.

related_work.citation: Tarun Suresh, Debangshu Banerjee, Shubham Ugare, Sasa Misailovic, Gagandeep Singh. "DINGO: Constrained Inference for Diffusion LLMs." arXiv:2505.23061; NeurIPS 2025 poster.
related_work.venue_status: NeurIPS 2025 poster. Verified on OpenReview: venue='NeurIPS 2025 poster', venueid='NeurIPS.cc/2025/Conference'; also 'ICML 2025 R2-FM Workshop Poster', venueid='ICML.cc/2025/Workshop/R2-FM'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Pioneering dLLM constrained decoding: dynamic-programming, provably distribution-preserving decoding under regular expressions for diffusion LLMs, sampling the highest-probability string satisfying the regex. Up to +68 points over unconstrained on symbolic math (GSM-Symbolic) and JSON generation. Appendices J and K are step ablations at {16,32,64,128} on Dream-I-7B reporting Acc / Parse / Time per step count for Unconstrained, Greedy-Constrained, Best-of-Greedy+Unconstrained, and DINGO.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Regular expressions only, not CFGs, so Python/whole-program grammars are out of scope. No code-execution benchmark at all (GSM-Symbolic + JSON-Mode only) — no HumanEval/MBPP/EvalPlus, no pass@1 on tests. Cost reported as raw seconds at fixed step counts, never as a normalised quality-vs-cost frontier. Response length fixed at 128, one block config in the ablation. No trained-structural-prior comparison.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Its own step tables show the shape the candidate wants to claim as novel and partly contradict a strong 'syntax is the bottleneck' story: on GSM-Symbolic, DINGO gets Parse to 100% at every step count, yet accuracy at 16 steps is only 18% vs 33% at 128 — legality is bought but the accuracy deficit persists, i.e. constraint does not collapse the low-step gap. This is stated as a table but never analysed. (2) Time is essentially identical across methods at a given step count (6.09 vs 5.99s), which flatters the method by hiding that the honest comparison is against MORE STEPS of unconstrained decoding, not against unconstrained at the same steps. (3) On JSON-Mode, plain Greedy-Constrained DEGRADES accuracy vs unconstrained (54→32 at 16 steps) — a constraint-harms result buried in an appendix with no explanation. (4) Regex expressivity means 'grammar validity by construction' is overclaimed for real languages.

related_work.citation: Yitong Zhang, Yongmin Li, Yuetong Liu, Jia Li, Xiaoran Jia, Zherui Li, Ge Li. "Lookahead-then-Verify: Reliable Constrained Decoding for Diffusion LLMs under Context-Free Grammars" (LAVE). arXiv:2602.00612.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint / CoRR only. Verified on OpenReview: venue='CoRR 2026', venueid='OpenReview.net/Public_Article', bibtex @article{DBLP:journals/corr/abs-2602-00612}, journal=CoRR, volume=abs/2602.00612. No conference venueid found.
related_work.what_it_covers: CFG-constrained decoding for dLLMs that fixes a reliability hole in prior dLLM constrained decoders: they permit intermediate outputs that cannot be completed into any valid sentence. LAVE uses the parallel all-position distributions to do lookahead verification of each proposed token, guaranteeing extendability. Four dLLMs (LLaDA-8B, LLaDA-1.5, Dream-7B, DiffuCoder-7B) x three benchmarks (JSON-Bench, CPP-Bench n=164, SMILES-Bench n=167), metrics syntactic@k, functional@k for k in {1,3,5,10}, and average inference time. Largest reported functional gain: Dream-7B CPP-Bench functional@1 25.6→33.5, functional@10 28.1→41.4.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Denoising steps FIXED at T=128 throughout ('a balanced trade-off') — no step or compute sweep at all, so this one genuinely leaves the constraint-vs-compute question open. C++/JSON/SMILES only; no Python, no MBPP, no EvalPlus. Cost is average seconds at fixed T, never a frontier. No trained-structural-prior arm. pass@k-style syntactic@k/functional@k over k samples confounds sampling budget with per-sample quality.
related_work.known_defects: (1) T=128 is asserted as a balanced tradeoff with no supporting sweep — precisely the unexamined knob the candidate targets, and the most defensible follow-up surface among the four CFG papers. (2) functional@k with k up to 10 is a best-of-k metric: the reported +13.3 gain at k=10 costs 10x the compute of the k=1 number it is implicitly compared against; there is no equal-total-compute baseline (e.g. unconstrained best-of-10, or unconstrained at 10x steps). (3) SMILES-Bench excluded from functional evaluation because all models scored 0% — an admission that syntactic gains can be entirely decoupled from functional gains, not followed up. (4) Baseline FS-CD degrades functional@k on CPP-Bench across all four models (up to -9.4) yet is retained as the comparison point that LAVE beats; the more informative question of when constraints hurt is not analysed. (5) Grammar for CPP-Bench is a hand-written Lark C++ grammar; bibliography has broken '[?]' citations for the Lark grammar format references (lines 1380, 1629 of the PDF text), a sloppiness signal.

related_work.citation: "EPIC: Efficient and Parallel Inference under CFG Constraints for Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2606.00722.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv v1 2026-05-30. OpenReview api2 /notes/search on the exact title returns no matching note (only unrelated physics/parallel-computing hits), so no verified venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: Speeds up CFG-constrained dLLM decoding via lexing memoization, Earley-style parsing instead of DFAs, and relaxed compatible-subset selection so multiple tokens commit in parallel. Up to 67.5% inference-time reduction and up to 90.5% less added overhead vs the prior CFG-constrained decoder. Four models x three datasets (C++ HumanEval-X split, instance-schema JSON, SMILES). Table 1 measures relative inference time across denoising steps {16,32,64,128,256}, explicitly motivated by 'smaller denoising step settings reveal more tokens per step and therefore place greater stress on the sequential validity checking bottleneck'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It sweeps steps but reports only RELATIVE INFERENCE TIME, deferring the correctness results to Appendix F — so quality-vs-step is not the object of study. No quality-cost frontier, no Python/EvalPlus, no trained-structural-prior arm, no error decomposition.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Normalising to 'relative inference time vs unconstrained at the same step count' means values below 100% arise partly because constrained decoding can terminate early while unconstrained runs the full schedule — the paper says so, which makes the headline speedup partly an early-exit artifact rather than a cheaper mask. (2) Correctness relegated to an appendix and asserted 'comparable' to the baseline, so the efficiency claim is never paid for in quality terms at matched compute. (3) Concurrent (2026-05-30, after the 2026-05-07 cutoff), so it does not preempt us regardless.
