feas.risk:
Most likely null-or-confounded outcome, in order of probability:

(1) THE FROM-SCRATCH ARM IS NEAR-TAUTOLOGICAL AND WILL READ AS A NULL FOR THE WRONG REASON. On HE+/MBPP+ from-scratch there is no real suffix -- every position to the right of a mask is either another mask or trailing pad. 2601.15593 already measured Kendall's tau > 0.8 on code for MDLMs, i.e. this model commits nearly left-to-right on code anyway. So "causal-canvas costs ~0 on from-scratch" is close to a restatement of a published behavioural fact, and a reviewer can say the model had almost nothing to lose because it was already decoding monotonically. The finding only becomes non-trivial if the commit-order statistics move while pass@1+ does not (proving order and directional conditioning are decoupled, which is the real repair to 2601.15593's unlicensed inference), or if the infilling contrast is large. Budget the analysis around that contrast, not around the from-scratch delta.

(2) THE INFILLING ARM GETS CONFOUNDED BY THE 0.817 PLUS-CEILING AND BY HOLE LENGTH. My w-sweep already shows the effect is strongly item-dependent (HumanEval/1/L8 is exact even at w=0; HumanEval/0/L0 collapses at w=0). Short holes in highly-constrained syntactic positions are recoverable from the prefix alone, so the mean delta over holes is really a mixture over hole difficulty. If hole length is not stratified, "right context matters on infilling" could be entirely carried by long holes, and a mean would hide it. Worse, plus-test failures from the dataset's ORIGINAL-HumanEval canonical provenance (22/120 in my sample) will be silently attributed to the ablation.

(3) THE KERNEL-DISPATCH ARTIFACT EATS A SMALL TRUE EFFECT. I measured 93.4% argmax agreement at CAN=512 and 17% of solutions changing text from a pure kernel switch. pass@1+ did not move on n=24 (0 flips), but if the true w=128-vs-full effect is a couple of points, an uncontrolled kernel-path change of that magnitude is the same order as the signal. This is exactly the retraction pattern: a pipeline difference that is not the independent variable moving the number.

(4) MULTILINE SUBSAMPLING + CLUSTERING TURNS A REAL EFFECT INTO A NON-SIGNIFICANT ONE. Only 164 independent clusters exist across all three infilling files. Cluster-bootstrap CIs on 164 clusters are ~2.5-6x wider than naive item CIs. An honest analysis may simply lack power on MultiLine after subsampling, so the differentiating arm returns "trending but not significant" -- which is a null produced by the statistics, not the biology.
feas.required_control:
THE IDENTITY CONTROL (mandatory, must run and be reported before any w-sweep number is believed):

Run the ENTIRE pipeline with a right-context window that is information-theoretically IDENTICAL to no intervention -- a dense 4-D all-True bool mask, or equivalently scoped(w=N) -- and verify it reproduces the unmodified control. Report the resulting |delta pass@1+| as the measured confound floor next to every real delta, and declare any effect smaller than it uninterpretable.

Why this specific control: the three prior retractions were (a) a verifier that compared nothing, (b) a pipeline stage that silently discarded its input, (c) a cost average that dropped the expensive tasks. The analogue here is a pipeline that silently changes something OTHER than the independent variable. I already caught it live: passing any tensor mask moves SDPA off flash onto the mem-efficient kernel (modeling_dream.py:428 + generation_utils.py:404's `"full"` STRING sentinel), which at realistic sequence length perturbs logits by 7.5-9.6, flips 6.6% of mask-position argmaxes, and rewrote 4/24 = 17% of solutions with ZERO information removed. Without this control, "w=128 costs 1.5 points" is unfalsifiable -- it could be entirely kernel numerics. I measured 0/24 pass-fail flips and delta pass@1+ = 0.0000 on a small probe, so the floor looks low, but it must be established at full n, per surface, per canvas length, and REPORTED -- not assumed from my n=24.

Operationally this means: never use `attention_mask="full"` as the w=full arm. Every arm including the control passes a dense 4-D mask, so the only thing varying across arms is which entries are False. Also assert per run that scoped(w=N) equals the dense all-True mask elementwise (I verified this identity holds), and that scoped(w=N) logits match dense all-True to 0.0 (verified).

Second, subordinate guard against the retraction-3 pattern specifically: persist the per-item plus/base CEILING map from step 1 and the `failure_process` rows for budget-truncated / non-terminating items, and report both the all-items and ceiling-restricted deltas. Never let the mean silently drop the items that failed or ran long.

lens.title: Wall-Clock Reckoning: Every dLLM Efficiency Ranking Flips When You Stop Counting Steps
lens.claim: NFE, FLOPs, and cumulative-token accounting are all non-monotone in wall-clock latency for masked-diffusion LMs, and the substitution is not a constant rescaling: it reorders the quality-compute Pareto frontier. Concretely, a method that owns the frontier under token-cost accounting can occupy ZERO frontier points under wall-clock on the same hardware, same harness, same samples. We predict this reordering is systematic (not a quirk of one method) because per-step token count and per-step latency decouple whenever a method trades canvas size for step count.
lens.why_now: CaRE (2607.24763, first public 2026-06-04) is the field's flagship remasking-audit paper and it standardizes on *actual NFE*; it reports that compute-matched comparison already reverses several published rankings. ParallelBench (2510.04767, ICLR 2026), 'Diffusion LMs: An Experimental Analysis' (2606.19475), and the non-determinism audit (2604.13413) likewise all anchor on NFE. Abstract-level keyword check on all four: 'NFE' present, 'wall-clock'/'latency'/'throughput'/'seconds' absent. So the audit literature has converged on a step-count unit precisely while the acceleration literature (Fast-dLLM 27.6x, dInfer 10x, dLLM-Cache 9.1x FLOPs, SureLock 30-50% FLOPs, Mercury 1109 tok/s, Seed Diffusion 2146 tok/s) sells latency. Nobody has shown the two units disagree about ORDERING. We can, from data already on disk.
lens.experiment: Zero new GPU compute for the headline: `elapsed_seconds` and `peak_memory_gib` are already logged per task in all 60 run dirs (verified: scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py:266-267 does torch.cuda.synchronize then perf_counter; generate_evalplus_scaffold.py:286 the same; both on the same 8x L20A, same 8-shard layout, same night). Recomputed frontier, ALREADY MEASURED: HE+ (n=164) under token-cost, scaffold Medium owns 13.98k tok @ .177 and vanilla scores .000 below 22k tok; under WALL-CLOCK the ordering is vanilla nfe16 1.20s/.000, nfe64 2.19s/.018, nfe128 3.50s/.140, nfe256 6.11s/.555, scaffold Tiny 8.46s/.000, vanilla nfe512 11.31s/.707, scaffold Small 16.35s/.043, scaffold Medium 19.38s/.177, scaffold Large 54.62s/.177 -- the structural runtime holds ZERO frontier points, and vanilla nfe256 already beats scaffold Medium 3x faster AND 3x better. MBPP+ (n=378) is the honest counter-case: scaffold Medium survives at 5.38s/.354 vs vanilla nfe256 5.63s/.545, i.e. it keeps exactly ONE frontier point by a 0.25s margin. So the reversal is benchmark-dependent, which is itself the finding. Then three additions: (a) hardware-portability leg -- rerun the 11 HE+ configs on H20 (.73) and B200 (.252) to test whether the reordering is hardware-specific; the token-cost curve is hardware-invariant by construction while the wall-clock curve is not, and if the crossing point MOVES across three GPU classes that is a second, sharper claim; (b) a batched leg (batch 1 vs 8 vs 32) since flat diffusion's fixed-shape canvas batches trivially while variable-length structural decoding does not -- this should widen the gap and is the regime every acceleration paper actually deploys in; (c) apply the same three-unit re-scoring (NFE / tokens / seconds) to 2-3 published open-source remasking or caching methods on Dream-Coder to show the reordering is not specific to our own method. Report all three units side by side for every cell, plus per-shard timing spread (measured: vanilla shard means 11.2-11.5s, tight; scaffold 14.1-25.7s, and scaffold mean 19.38s vs median 10.93s -- a heavy right tail that token-cost accounting hides entirely).

For leg (a) need Dream-Coder-7B + Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B staged to zwfy6 for the H20 replication (Scaffold is 29GB; it originated on .82 so likely still there -- MUST ls both disks, do not trust the ledger). MISSING: no batched-inference path in either generator (both are batch-1 loops; the scaffold sampler is structurally batch-1 per UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md item 7) -- leg (b) needs new code for the vanilla side only, and the honest report for the scaffold side is 'cannot batch', which is itself a result. MISSING: Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is on neither disk (confirmed), so no matched-AR wall-clock anchor unless downloaded.
lens.kill_criterion: Falsified if, across all three cost units and all three GPU classes, the Pareto frontier membership set is identical (i.e. the unit is a monotone reparameterization in practice). Also killed as a *general* claim if the reordering is confined to our own scaffold runtime and does NOT reproduce on any published third-party method re-scored in all three units -- in that case it degrades to a single-system erratum, not a protocol finding. Weakened (workshop-only) if the crossing survives only at batch 1: the HE+ reversal is large (scaffold Medium 19.38s/.177 vs vanilla nfe256 6.11s/.555) but MBPP+ retains a frontier point by 0.25s, which is inside plausible scheduler noise, so we must report the MBPP+ margin as null rather than as support.
lens.builds_on: CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for MDLMs (arXiv:2607.24763, first public 2026-06-04). CaRE's claim: standardizing *actual NFE* plus multi-metric reporting plus explicit stochasticity control makes remasking claims comparable, and doing so already reverses several published rankings. The defect we repair: CaRE fixes the wrong invariant. NFE is a count of denoising steps, and the cost of a step is not constant across methods -- we measured 685 tok/step for flat diffusion on HE+ vs ~181 tok/call for a structural runtime, a 3.8x per-step cost difference that NFE-matching declares equal by fiat. Worse, our own token-cost fix is ALSO wrong as a proxy for the thing efficiency papers sell (latency), because it ignores kernel efficiency, fixed-shape batching, and per-task tail latency. We therefore repair CaRE by promoting wall-clock to a first-class reported unit and demonstrating that CaRE's own headline mechanism -- 'compute-matched comparison reverses rankings' -- applies recursively to CaRE's chosen definition of compute. This is a friendly, constructive extension of CaRE rather than a refutation, and it is also self-critical: it retracts/qualifies our own token-cost Pareto claim, which is the strongest possible evidence that we are not unit-shopping for a favorable answer. Secondary targets whose speedup numbers are stated in a unit different from the one they optimize: Fast-dLLM (2505.22618), dLLM-Cache (2506.06295, ICML 2026), dInfer (2510.08666), SureLock (2602.06412, ICLR 2026).

diff.sharpened_claim: For masked-diffusion LMs, step-count accounting (NFE) and token-cost accounting are not monotone reparameterizations of wall-clock latency ACROSS decoder families, and the substitution reorders quality-compute Pareto frontier MEMBERSHIP -- not merely rescales it. We isolate the mechanism: NFE-vs-latency proportionality (which CaRE explicitly assumes in its Appendix C -- "because per-step forward passes dominate MDLM runtime, NFE differences translate to proportional latency differences on matched hardware") holds WITHIN a fixed-shape flat-canvas family, where we measure it empirically (Dream-Coder HE+ nfe16/64/128/256/512 -> 1.20/2.19/3.50/6.11/11.31 s, near-linear), and BREAKS across families whenever a method trades canvas size for step count. Concretely, on the same 8x L20A, same harness, same 164/378 samples, same night: under cumulative-token accounting a structural typed-AST runtime owns three HumanEval+ frontier points (Tiny 2.73k tok, Small 9.73k, Medium 13.98k tok @ .177) while flat diffusion scores .000 below 22k tokens; under WALL-CLOCK the SAME runtime holds ZERO frontier points, and flat diffusion nfe256 dominates it 3x faster AND 3x better (6.11 s/.545 vs 19.38 s/.177). We report the honest counter-case rather than suppressing it: on MBPP+ the structural runtime retains exactly ONE frontier point by a 0.25 s margin (5.38 s/.354 vs nfe256 5.63 s/.545), scored as null. We further show wall-clock exposes distributional pathology that both step-count and token-count accounting are blind to by construction: the structural runtime's HE+ mean 19.38 s vs median 10.93 s (max 124.84 s), per-shard means spanning 14.13-25.66 s versus flat diffusion's tight 10.95-11.50 s -- a heavy right tail invisible in any hardware-invariant unit. This is a self-retracting extension: it qualifies our own previously-claimed token-cost Pareto result.
diff.differentiation_statement: The closest work splits into two camps and neither makes our claim. (1) The dLLM audit camp -- CaRE (2607.24763, 2026-06-04, concurrent), "Diffusion LMs: An Experimental Analysis" (2606.19475, concurrent), ParallelBench (2510.04767, ICLR 2026 Poster, pre-cutoff), and the non-determinism audit (2604.13413, pre-cutoff) -- all anchor on NFE/step counts. We verified this in FULL TEXT, not abstracts: 2606.19475 has NFE x25 and wall-clock/throughput/tokens-per-second/seconds x0; ParallelBench (via ar5iv) has NFE x20, wall-clock x0, throughput x0, seconds x0; CaRE has NFE x52 and mentions wall-clock only in an appendix titled "Why we use NFE and not wall-clock time", where it asserts the exact proportionality premise we falsify. None measures whether the unit substitution changes frontier MEMBERSHIP. (2) The acceleration/serving camp -- Fast-dLLM (2505.22618), dLLM-Cache (2506.06295, ICML 2026), dInfer (2510.08666), SureLock (2602.06412, ICLR 2026), BlockServe (2607.08930), dLLM-Serve (2512.17077) -- reports latency/throughput/FLOPs as the headline, but each optimises one system and never re-scores a cross-family quality-compute frontier in multiple units to test for reordering. The genuinely closest item is the IJCAI-ECAI 2026 survey "Accelerating Masked Diffusion LLMs" (2607.12829, 2026-07-14, concurrent), which states in prose that "step counts alone can be especially misleading" and proposes a latency-decomposition framework -- but full-text scan shows Pareto x0, reorder x0, reversal x0, HumanEval x0, frontier x4 (all prescriptive), and ZERO own measurements (we-measure/we-benchmark/we-run/H100/A100 all x0). It is a taxonomy that ASSERTS the hazard; we EXHIBIT it as a measured frontier-membership reversal with a named mechanism and a reported null -- exactly the empirical complement a survey cannot supply, and concurrent regardless. Separately, we found an ICLR 2026 review thread (Submission25294, forum wNAUAPfceN) where a reviewer raised precisely this critique; the authors' latency table (AR 512 steps 2.28s; MDLM 128/256/512 steps -> 2.26/4.56/9.16s) shows near-proportional scaling WITHIN one flat-canvas family, which CORROBORATES rather than preempts us, since our claim is that proportionality holds within a family and fails across families. Finally, the general-ML precedents "The Efficiency Misnomer" (2110.12894, 2021) and "Efficiency Pentathlon" (2307.09701, 2023) established that cost indicators can contradict each other; we owe them citations and inherit their framing, but neither touches diffusion LMs, neither identifies the canvas-size-vs-step-count decoupling mechanism specific to masked diffusion, and neither demonstrates a Pareto-membership reversal on a modern 7B code-generation frontier. Our differentiators a reviewer will accept: the dLLM setting and its specific mechanism; frontier MEMBERSHIP (not correlation) as the outcome variable; three units reported per cell for every configuration; a hardware-portability leg across three GPU classes testing whether the crossing point MOVES (token-cost is hardware-invariant by construction, wall-clock is not); a batching leg in the regime acceleration papers actually deploy; and the fact that the paper retracts our own prior token-cost claim, which is the strongest available evidence against unit-shopping.

All 7 audited strategies are flat-canvas, so the design cannot surface the failure mode. MAUVE/diversity on OpenWebText does not measure task utility. NFE ignores kernel efficiency, batching shape, and per-task tail latency. Single hardware class, so hardware-sensitivity of any conclusion is untested.

related_work.citation: D. Gwak, et al. "Accelerating Masked Diffusion Large Language Models: A Survey of Efficient Inference Techniques." arXiv:2607.12829. Accepted at IJCAI-ECAI 2026 (Survey Track).
related_work.venue_status: IJCAI-ECAI 2026 Survey Track (per arXiv comments field); arXiv v1 2026-07-14; no OpenReview record expected for IJCAI
related_work.what_it_covers: THE CLOSEST WORK. Explicitly argues 'parallel generation alone does not guarantee practical speedups' and that 'rigorous comparisons remain difficult, as end-to-end latency stems from intricate trade-offs between algorithmic, architectural, and system-level factors that are often conflated in existing benchmarks.' Introduces a unified latency-decomposition framework, categorizes acceleration along three axes, gives reproducible-benchmarking guidelines. Section 7.3 'Common Pitfalls for Interpreting Speedups' warns that 'step counts alone can be especially misleading' when multi-pass decoding hides forward passes, and recommends reporting a small matched-quality frontier.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: A taxonomy plus prescriptions with NO original measurements. Full-text census: Pareto x0, reorder x0, reversal x0, HumanEval x0, 'we measure'/'we benchmark'/'we run'/'we evaluate' x0, H100/A100 x0. It asserts step counts CAN mislead; it never demonstrates a case where substituting the unit changes which configurations are ON the frontier, never quantifies magnitude, never tests hardware-portability of a crossing point, never reports a null. Its pitfall mechanism is multi-pass decoding inflating N_fwd WITHIN a family -- not the cross-family canvas-size-vs-step-count decoupling we isolate.
related_work.known_defects: Zero empirical content behind the central warning, so the field has no calibration for effect size or whether it ever flips a published conclusion; the prescriptions are unfalsifiable as stated. The pitfall taxonomy omits (a) per-step canvas-size heterogeneity across decoder families, (b) tail-latency distributions (mean-vs-median divergence), (c) batching-shape asymmetry between fixed-shape and variable-length decoders, (d) hardware-class dependence of a crossing point. Being concurrent AND measurement-free makes it the ideal citation partner rather than a blocker.

related_work.venue_status: preprint (arXiv v1 2025-12-18, v2 2026-01-14); no venue in comments
related_work.what_it_covers: Production dLLM serving system addressing a 'memory footprint crisis' from monolithic logit tensors and severe resource oscillation between compute-bound Refresh and bandwidth-bound Reuse phases. Reports 1.61-1.81x throughput on RTX 4090, 1.60-1.74x on L40S, and ~4x tail-latency reduction under heavy contention.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Best available evidence that dLLM cost is bandwidth- and memory-shape-dependent rather than step-count-dependent -- and it reports results on TWO different GPU classes with DIFFERENT multipliers, indirect support for our hypothesis that a wall-clock crossing point MOVES with hardware. But it makes no evaluation-protocol claim, presents no quality axis, and does not test frontier membership.
related_work.known_defects: Throughput/tail-latency only with no quality axis at all, so it cannot speak to quality-compute trade-offs; consumer plus mid-range server GPUs only (4090, L40S), so scaling to datacenter-class parts is unverified; the phase-oscillation mechanism it identifies is exactly what NFE cannot represent, yet the paper does not confront the audit literature. Supports our leg (a) design and our peak_memory_gib reporting.

related_work.citation: C. Vicentino. "Autoregressive vs. Masked Diffusion Language Models: A Controlled Comparison." arXiv:2603.22075.
related_work.venue_status: preprint (arXiv v1 2026-03-23); comments '10 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Code and checkpoints at ...'; no venue
related_work.what_it_covers: The only pre-cutoff AR-vs-MDLM comparison found that reports wall-clock: identical data (50M TinyStories tokens), identical compute budget (20k steps, bs 32, seqlen 512), identical hardware (H100 80GB), isolating the generation paradigm as sole variable. Finds comparable TRAINING throughput (~50K tok/s) with MDLM needing 4.7% more wall-clock; different convergence regimes; a diversity-fluency trade-off.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its wall-clock accounting concerns TRAINING, not inference decoding, and the setting is a tiny TinyStories-scale model rather than a 7B code LM. Does not construct an inference quality-compute frontier, does not vary the cost unit, does not test reordering. Closest in spirit (same-hardware controlled comparison with time reported) but disjoint in claim and scale.
related_work.known_defects: 50M tokens on TinyStories, single seed, single hardware class -- conclusions about relative cost are unlikely to survive to 7B-scale inference where canvas re-attention dominates; training-time equivalence says nothing about inference-time ranking; diversity metrics (Distinct-n, Self-BLEU) are not task utility. Useful as the citation showing controlled same-hardware timing is accepted practice in this comparison genre.

followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for MDLMs (arXiv:2607.24763, 2026-06-04, CONCURRENT)
followup_openings.defect: CaRE's entire protocol rests on an unmeasured proportionality premise, stated verbatim in its Appendix C ('Why we use NFE and not wall-clock time'): 'Because per-step forward passes dominate MDLM runtime, NFE differences translate to proportional latency differences on matched hardware.' It is asserted, never validated, and its own experimental design cannot test it -- all 7 audited strategies are flat fixed-shape canvas decoders, for which the premise happens to hold. NFE also declares equal any two methods with the same step count regardless of per-step canvas size, which we measure to differ by ~3.8x (685 tok/step for flat diffusion on HE+ vs ~181 tok/call for a structural runtime).
followup_openings.our_fix: Validate the premise where CaRE could not: report NFE, cumulative model tokens, AND measured wall-clock for every cell, spanning both a flat-canvas family and a variable-shape structural decoder on identical hardware/harness/samples. We confirm near-proportionality WITHIN the flat family (already measured: nfe16/64/128/256/512 -> 1.20/2.19/3.50/6.11/11.31 s on HE+) and show it fails ACROSS families, flipping frontier membership (structural runtime 3/3 token-cost frontier points -> 0 wall-clock points on HE+). Then apply CaRE's own headline mechanism recursively: 'compute-matched comparison reverses rankings' applies to CaRE's chosen definition of compute. Strengthen with a cross-hardware leg (L20A / H20 / B200) testing whether the crossing point MOVES -- token-cost is hardware-invariant by construction, wall-clock is not, so a moving crossing is a second, sharper claim.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: CaRE is positioning itself as the field's standard remasking-audit protocol. If its cost unit is adopted with an unvalidated proportionality assumption, every future remasking ranking inherits a blind spot for exactly the methods that trade canvas size for step count -- including caching (dLLM-Cache: cheaper steps, same NFE) and dynamic sparsity (SureLock: same NFE, 30-50% algorithmic FLOPs), both invisible under NFE by construction. Repairing the unit before the standard hardens is high-leverage, and the framing is friendly rather than adversarial: CaRE's diagnosis is right, its invariant is one level too shallow.

followup_openings.target_paper: Accelerating Masked Diffusion LLMs: A Survey (arXiv:2607.12829, IJCAI-ECAI 2026 Survey Track, 2026-07-14, CONCURRENT)
followup_openings.defect: The survey asserts the hazard with zero measurements. Full-text census: Pareto x0, reorder x0, reversal x0, HumanEval x0, 'we measure'/'we benchmark'/'we run'/'we evaluate' x0, H100/A100 x0. Its Section 7.3 pitfall list is also mechanistically incomplete: it covers hidden multi-pass compute inflating N_fwd and mismatched operating points, but omits (a) per-step canvas-size heterogeneity ACROSS decoder families, (b) tail-latency distributions, (c) batching-shape asymmetry between fixed-shape and variable-length decoders, (d) hardware-class dependence of a crossing point. Its prescriptions ('make T, G_t, N_fwd explicit') are unfalsifiable as stated because no magnitude is ever attached.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the missing empirical instantiation and extend the pitfall taxonomy with the four omitted mechanisms, each backed by data already on disk or a cheap planned leg: (a) cross-family canvas decoupling, quantified as a frontier-membership reversal; (b) tail latency, quantified as HE+ mean 19.38s vs median 10.93s vs max 124.84s and per-shard means 14.13-25.66s versus flat diffusion's tight 10.95-11.50s; (c) batching, via a batch 1/8/32 leg where the honest scaffold-side result is 'structurally cannot batch' (per UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md item 7) -- itself a result; (d) hardware, via the three-GPU-class replication. Adopt the survey's latency-decomposition vocabulary so the two papers compose rather than compete.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A survey can prescribe but cannot demonstrate; a demonstration gives the prescription teeth and a magnitude the community can calibrate against. Because the survey is concurrent AND measurement-free, this is the ideal complement-not-conflict relationship: cite it as independent confirmation that the field recognizes the hazard, then supply the missing existence proof. It is also the strongest answer to a reviewer who says 'everyone already knows step counts can mislead' -- yes, and the paper that says so loudest has no numbers.

followup_openings.target_paper: SureLock (arXiv:2602.06412, ICLR 2026 Poster) and dLLM-Cache (arXiv:2506.06295, ICML 2026)
followup_openings.defect: Both report units that flatter them AND are invisible to the audit literature simultaneously. SureLock's headline is 30-50% reduction in ALGORITHMIC FLOPs -- a modelled quantity -- achieved by skipping query projections and FFN for a dynamically shrinking set of unlocked positions; irregular, ragged, shrinking active sets are exactly the pattern that fails to convert to wall-clock on dense GPU kernels (gather/scatter overhead, ragged shapes, kernel-launch cost), so the figure is plausibly an upper bound on realized speedup. dLLM-Cache likewise makes steps cheaper while leaving NFE unchanged. Both therefore score as ZERO improvement under CaRE-style NFE-matching and as large improvements under their own unit -- a flat contradiction between the field's two dominant accounting conventions that neither literature acknowledges.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-score both on Dream-Coder in all three units (NFE / cumulative tokens / measured seconds), same harness, same samples, at batch 1/8/32 and across three GPU classes, reporting the realized-to-algorithmic conversion ratio for SureLock's FLOPs claim and the input-dependent cost variance for dLLM-Cache's hit rate. This directly discharges our own kill criterion: the reordering must reproduce on published THIRD-PARTY methods, not just on our in-house structural runtime, or it degrades to a single-system erratum rather than a protocol finding.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the leg that decides whether the paper is a protocol contribution or an erratum, so it should be executed FIRST, not last. It also yields an independently valuable artifact -- the first table where a set of published dLLM acceleration methods is priced simultaneously in the acceleration literature's unit and the audit literature's unit -- demonstrating concretely that the two communities are not measuring the same thing. Both targets are pre-cutoff and accepted at top venues, so a well-aimed re-scoring is high-visibility.

followup_openings.target_paper: Dataset-Level Metrics Attenuate Non-Determinism (arXiv:2604.13413, 2026-04-15) and Diffusion LMs: An Experimental Analysis (arXiv:2606.19475, 2026-06-17, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: 2604.13413 proves dataset-level aggregation attenuates variation that matters, then applies the insight only to QUALITY -- it treats batch size as a nuisance source of output nondeterminism rather than a regime that changes cost rankings, and never reports latency. 2606.19475 advertises that it 'explicitly consider[s] both generation quality and computational efficiency' across 8 DLMs and 8 benchmarks, but operationalizes efficiency purely as NFE (census: NFE x25; wall-clock, throughput, tokens-per-second, seconds, runtime, TPS all x0). So the broadest dLLM comparison to date cannot tell a practitioner which of its 8 models is actually fastest, and the paper that established aggregation-hides-variance never turned that lens on cost.
followup_openings.our_fix: Complete both generalizations in one move: report per-sample cost DISTRIBUTIONS, not just means, in all three units. We already have the evidence this is not pedantry -- the structural runtime's HE+ mean (19.38s) exceeds its median (10.93s) by 1.8x with a 124.84s max, and per-shard means span 14.13-25.66s versus flat diffusion's 10.95-11.50s. A heavy right tail is invisible in any hardware-invariant unit by construction, and it is precisely what BlockServe (2607.08930) independently documents as 'convergence heterogeneity' causing stragglers in batched serving. Pair mean-vs-median-vs-tail reporting with the batch 1/8/32 leg so the tail's serving consequence is measured, not inferred.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts a metrology complaint into a deployment-relevant claim with an independent corroborating citation, and extends the contribution from 'the unit is wrong' to 'the summary STATISTIC is also wrong' -- two orthogonal accounting defects instead of one, both cheap to establish from data already on disk. It also inoculates against the obvious objection that the 0.25s MBPP+ margin is scheduler noise: with full distributions reported, noise and signal are separable, and MBPP+ can be honestly scored as null.

followup_openings.target_paper: Fast-dLLM (arXiv:2505.22618) / dInfer (arXiv:2510.08666) / dLLM-Serve (arXiv:2512.17077) -- the acceleration camp's cross-paper comparability
followup_openings.defect: dInfer reports ~10x over Fast-dLLM at similar quality, at FIXED algorithm class and FIXED NFE, purely from framework engineering; dLLM-Serve reports 1.60-1.81x with DIFFERENT multipliers on RTX 4090 versus L40S. Together these establish that implementation quality and hardware class each move latency by more than the algorithmic differences the audit papers are trying to rank -- which makes any NFE-based cross-paper ranking non-identifiable. Neither camp states this: the acceleration papers do not draw the methodological conclusion, and the audit papers (CaRE, 2606.19475, ParallelBench) do not cite it as a threat to their chosen unit. Headline numbers are also picked at flattering operating points (dInfer: batch size 1 on an 8xH800 node) with no quality-compute frontier.
followup_openings.our_fix: Make implementation quality and hardware class explicit confounds in the protocol, then neutralize them by construction: one harness, one sample set, three units per cell, three GPU classes, three batch sizes. This is what licenses attributing our reordering to ACCOUNTING rather than to engineering -- the single most likely reviewer objection. The cross-hardware leg is the sharp test: token-cost curves are hardware-invariant by construction, so if the wall-clock crossing point MOVES across L20A/H20/B200, hardware-invariance is revealed as a bug rather than a feature of the unit, and 'which method is on the frontier' becomes a hardware-dependent question the field currently reports as absolute.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This upgrades the paper from 'unit A disagrees with unit B on our system' to 'the field's efficiency rankings are not identifiable across labs, and here is the minimum reporting standard that fixes it' -- a protocol contribution with main-conference reach. It also gives the paper a constructive deliverable (a three-unit, three-hardware, three-batch reporting template) rather than only a negative result, and directly repairs the gap between a literature that SELLS latency and a literature that RANKS by steps.

HONEST ASSESSMENT OF EVIDENCE STRENGTH. The strongest claim I can support from verified sources: no paper found makes this claim, and the four audit papers demonstrably anchor on step counts (full-text confirmed). The weakest link in the candidate's framing is "nobody has shown the two units disagree about ORDERING" -- the concurrent IJCAI-ECAI survey 2607.12829 states in prose that step counts "can be especially misleading" and that two decoders with the same T can differ substantially in wall-clock, and an ICLR 2026 reviewer already demanded exactly this analysis. So the IDEA is in the air and must not be claimed as unrecognized; what is missing, and what we uniquely supply, is the MEASUREMENT of frontier-membership reversal plus the mechanism, the hardware-portability test, and a reported null. The paper must be framed as "first demonstration and quantification", never as "first observation". Recommendation is pursue-as-followup rather than pursue-as-is precisely because that reframing is required, and because the third-party re-scoring leg (SureLock / dLLM-Cache / Fast-dLLM) should be promoted to the critical path since it alone separates a protocol finding from a single-system erratum.

blocking_gaps: FATAL, MEASURED BY ME TODAY: the HE+ wall-clock reversal is a one-line kernel-warmup artifact, not the claimed canvas/step-decoupling mechanism. On an idle L20A I measured Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B forward at L=210: median 12.2 ms, mean 621.6 ms, bimodal (either ~12 ms or ~1500-2400 ms), uncorrelated with call index (r=-0.10) or allocated memory (r=-0.07). Direct test: sweep 30 DISTINCT lengths L=400..429 -> mean 1834 ms; immediately repeat the SAME 30 lengths -> mean 13.1 ms. First-touch penalty per never-before-seen (1,L) shape = 1821 ms. cuDNN/SDPA autotune+JIT per shape, no torch.compile or cudnn.benchmark anywhere in the repo (grep of scaffold_coder/*.py and scripts/generate_evalplus_*.py returns nothing). The structural runtime grows its canvas ~1 token per model call, so EVERY call is a new shape and pays 1.82 s; flat diffusion has ONE fixed shape (prompt+512) per task and amortizes a single warmup over 16-1024 steps. Predicted penalty alone is <=26.7/85.8/116.6/190.0 s for Tiny/Small/Medium/Large vs measured 8.46/16.35/19.38/54.62 s -- i.e. warmup upper-bounds EXCEED the entire measured runtime. The 'mechanism' the paper claims to isolate (per-step canvas cost, 685 vs ~181 tok/call) is NOT what is being measured; both models are bit-identical in cost at matched shape (12.2/12.1/18.5/20.9 ms at L=256/512/900/1200 -- I benchmarked Dream-Coder and Scaffold side by side and they are the same to <2%). Publishing the current HE+ table would be Retraction #4: a cost metric that measures harness warmup and is reported as an architectural property.

The 'zero new GPU compute for the headline' premise is false because the timing instrumentation is ASYMMETRIC between the two families being compared. scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py:266 calls torch.cuda.synchronize(device) before stopping the clock; scripts/generate_evalplus_scaffold.py:286 and :291 do NOT synchronize at all (verified by grep: scaffold has reset_peak_memory_stats at 239 and perf_counter at 240/286/291, and zero synchronize calls). generate_evalplus_dreamon.py:163 and generate_evalplus_ar.py:432 DO synchronize. So the one arm that loses under wall-clock is the only arm whose timer is unsynchronized. It happens to be ~96% GPU-bound with internal syncs (I measured GPU forward = 182.5 s of 189.5 s wall over 8 HE+ tasks, CPU/Python only 3.7%), so the numbers are approximately rescuable -- but 'same harness' is not true as written and a reviewer who greps will find it.

Provenance defect confirmed and worse than the positioning states: runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe512/ contains ZERO metrics records (I counted). The 11.31 s nfe512 anchor comes from runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus_r2. That directory is NOT a clean same-config replicate: runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus.r1 is the SAME nominal config (steps 512, T=0.1, top_p=0.95 per scripts/_run_baselines_r2_wzc1.sh vs _run_baselines_wzc1_8gpu.sh) yet means 9.37 s vs 11.31 s -- a 21% same-config wall-clock spread, with peak_memory_gib also differing (15.74 vs 17.19 GiB, so r1 ran without the --top-p/--no-chat code path). 21% >> the 0.25 s (4.6%) MBPP+ margin the paper wants to score, and comparable to gaps it wants to call reversals. MBPP+ r1/r2 shows the same pattern (9.61 vs 10.57 s).

Leg (b) batching is not a small build and is asymmetrically impossible, which destroys it as a comparison rather than yielding a clean 'cannot batch' result. Neither generator has any batch dimension (grep 'batch' over both files returns NOTHING -- both are strictly batch-1 per-task loops). Worse, batching is exactly the axis where the shape-warmup artifact explodes: variable-length structural decoding produces a new (B,L) shape every step, so a batched scaffold arm would pay MORE autotune, and any measured 'gap widening' would again be warmup, not architecture.

Leg (a) hardware portability is blocked on staging, not just present/absent. There is no /apdcephfs_zwfy6/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/models at all, and df shows only ONE apdcephfs mount on this host (dop-fuse on /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610, 90% full, 13T free). But Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B (29 GB) is NOT on zwfy6 and must be scp -O'd cross-disk before any H20 replication.
