feas.concrete_plan:
STOP. Do not publish the current HE+/MBPP+ wall-clock frontier. It measures per-shape kernel autotune, not a decoding-family property. Below is the repair, then the salvageable paper.

STEP 0 (mandatory, ~0 GPU-h, blocks everything). Reproduce my finding so it is in the record. On an idle card:
  /opt/conda/envs/dllm-env/bin/python, load models/Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B bf16, sweep 30 distinct L in 400..429 measuring one forward each, then repeat the identical 30. I measured 1834 ms -> 13.1 ms (first-touch = 1821 ms/new shape). Then instrument scaffold_coder/model_sampler.py's forward (line 600 `output = self.model(...)`) and confirm bimodality: median 12.2 ms vs mean 621.6 ms at L=210, 42/126 calls >500 ms.

STEP 1 (~4 GPU-h). Fix the harness before re-measuring anything.
  (a) Add torch.cuda.synchronize(device) before the `elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started` at scripts/generate_evalplus_scaffold.py:286 AND :291 (the except-branch), matching generate_evalplus_dream.py:266. Without this, "same harness" is false.
  (b) Neutralize the shape artifact. Two arms, BOTH reported:
      ARM-WARM: pad the scaffold canvas to a fixed bucket (e.g. multiples of 64) so the shape set is small and warm, OR pre-warm every reachable L once before timing. This gives the architecture-attributable latency.
      ARM-COLD: current unpadded behaviour = the real deployed cost of a variable-shape decoder on an untuned stack.
      The DIFFERENCE between ARM-WARM and ARM-COLD is the actual, novel, defensible finding (see below).
  (c) Re-run HE+ scaffold Tiny/Small/Medium/Large and dream nfe{16,32,64,128,256,512,1024} with n>=3 repeats per config, alternating arms, ONE job per node, nothing else resident. Report median and IQR per task, not mean.

STEP 2 (~2 GPU-h). Reconcile provenance. Re-run steps=512 into runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe512/ with the exact _run_baselines_r2_wzc1.sh flags so the nfe512 point has a same-directory, same-config provenance instead of borrowing dream_coder_instruct_heplus_r2. Keep r1 vs r2 (9.37 vs 11.31 s) as the measured run-to-run noise floor and require every claimed reversal to exceed it.

STEP 3 (~8 GPU-h, only if STEP 1 survives). Cross-hardware leg, now meaningful because the artifact is controlled. scp -O models/Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B (29 GB) to /apdcephfs_zwfy6/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft_104/models/, verify sha256, then replicate the 11 HE+ configs on an H20 (.73/.82, or .104 once the AR baseline frees). Qwen2.5-Coder-7B is ALREADY at dllm_draft_104/models/Qwen2.5-Coder-7B, so add the matched-AR wall-clock anchor free -- and coordinate with the .104 AR agent rather than re-running it.

STEP 4. Reframe the paper around what is actually true and is still interesting:
  Kept claim: for masked-diffusion LMs, wall-clock is NOT a monotone reparameterization of NFE or token-cost ACROSS decoder families -- but the dominant term is SHAPE STABILITY, not per-step canvas size. A fixed-shape flat canvas amortizes one kernel-autotune over all steps; a variable-shape structural decoder pays it per step. I measured 1.82 s per new shape vs a 12 ms steady-state forward: a 150x first-touch multiplier that no hardware-invariant unit can express, and that CaRE's Appendix C proportionality premise cannot see.
  Withdrawn claim: "structural runtime holds ZERO HE+ frontier points" as an architectural statement. It holds zero points on an UNTUNED stack; that is an implementation-portability claim.
  This is strictly better than the original: it names a concrete, reproducible, fixable mechanism (shape polymorphism vs kernel autotune) instead of a vague decoupling, it explains why acceleration papers' FLOPs/NFE numbers don't convert, and it retracts our own token-cost claim AND our own first wall-clock claim -- maximal evidence against unit-shopping.
  Ceiling: this is honest workshop / short-paper material, not main-conference, until STEP 3 shows the WARM-arm ordering also moves across GPU classes.

DROP leg (b) (batching): no batch path exists in either generator (grep 'batch' = zero hits), and batching multiplies the very shape artifact that just invalidated the headline.
DEFER leg (c) (re-scoring SureLock/dLLM-Cache/Fast-dLLM): correct that it is the leg separating protocol finding from single-system erratum, but it is a from-scratch third-party integration, not in the 40 h budget, and pointless until our own measurement is artifact-free.
feas.risk: The most likely null-or-confounded outcome, and it is now the LEADING outcome rather than a tail risk: after STEP 1 pads shapes and warms kernels, the HE+ reversal collapses entirely. Arithmetic from my measurements: scaffold Medium averages 64.1 model calls/task; at the warm steady-state forward of ~12-13 ms at its L~210 canvas that is ~0.8-1.0 s/task, versus vanilla nfe256 at 6.11 s. Under warm conditions the structural runtime becomes roughly 6x FASTER than the config that currently "dominates it 3x faster AND 3x better" -- so the paper's headline flips sign, and the surviving story is "we mis-measured, and the real effect is kernel warmup." That is a genuine and publishable methodological finding, but it is a different paper with a much lower ceiling, and it retracts the third distinct claim from this same run family. Secondary confound: the 0.25 s (4.6%) MBPP+ margin the plan wants to score as null is far inside the 21% same-config r1-vs-r2 spread I measured, so MBPP+ cannot support ANY directional conclusion, null or otherwise, until STEP 2 establishes a repeat-based noise floor. Tertiary: if STEP 3 is run before STEP 1, the H20/B200 "crossing point moves" result would be pure autotune-cost variation across GPU classes -- a fourth retraction dressed as the paper's sharpest claim.
feas.required_control:
SHAPE-STABILITY / WARM-KERNEL CONTROL, reported as a paired WARM-vs-COLD arm for every single cell.

Every configuration must be timed twice on identical inputs: once with the kernel cache cold for its shape set (as today), once after every reachable input shape has been executed at least once (or with canvas lengths padded to fixed buckets). A wall-clock difference between methods may be claimed as a property of the DECODING FAMILY only if it survives in the WARM arm; whatever appears only in the COLD arm must be labelled implementation/stack portability, not architecture. Concretely: assert median-forward-time-at-matched-canvas-length is equal across the two models before comparing them end to end -- I verified it IS equal (12.2/12.1/18.5/20.9 ms at L=256/512/900/1200 for both Dream-Coder and Scaffold, <2% apart), so ANY end-to-end wall-clock gap that is not explained by call count x warm per-call cost is by construction harness overhead and must be accounted for explicitly.

Two mandatory sub-controls, because this candidate's cost axis has the same shape as all three prior retractions:
  (1) SYMMETRIC INSTRUMENTATION ASSERTION. Before trusting any cross-family timing, assert that every generator being compared synchronizes the device before stopping its clock. Today scaffold does not (scripts/generate_evalplus_scaffold.py:286,291) while dream (:266), dreamon (:163) and ar (:432) do. A timing comparison whose losing arm is the only unsynchronized one is Retraction #1 again -- a "verifier" that compares two things measured differently.
  (2) MEAN-AND-MEDIAN-AND-TAIL, WITH DENOMINATOR PARITY. Report n, median, IQR, max, and the errored/truncated count for every cell, and never a bare mean. Retraction #3 was a mean that silently dropped expensive tasks; the same trap is live here in the other direction -- scaffold Large HE+ mean 54.62 s decomposes into 147 successes at 10.41 s and 17 budget-exceeded tasks at 436.88 s, and scaffold Large MBPP+ into 343 at 2.48 s and 35 at 238.12 s. A mean over a mixture that includes budget-truncated tasks is not a latency, and its median (3.42 s HE+) tells the opposite story. Additionally require >=3 repeats per config and refuse to call any gap a reversal unless it exceeds the measured same-config spread (21% from r1 vs r2).

lens.title: Execution-Grounded Remasking: Repairing the Confidence-Remasking Null Result With a Signal That Actually Localizes Errors
lens.claim: The published failure of confidence-based remasking is a failure of the LOCALIZATION SIGNAL, not of the remasking primitive. Token confidence is uninformative about which tokens are wrong; a test-execution signal (failing assertion -> traceback frame -> line -> AST subtree -> token span) is informative. We claim that at matched wall-clock and matched NFE, execution-localized remasking beats both (a) confidence-localized remasking and (b) uniform-random remasking of the same token budget, and that the gap is attributable to localization precision rather than to extra compute.
lens.why_now: 2606.12232 (2026-06-10) 'Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking' shows a representative post-hoc confidence remasker (WINO) gives 'little-to-no benefit' at standard block lengths and worsens diversity collapse. 2604.18738 T2M and 2605.26436 Targeted Remasking argue remask-to-[MASK] beats overwrite-in-place (+13.33 on AIME) -- so the PRIMITIVE is validated. 2606.01026 D3IM/SCOPE names 'preservation bias': the model reproduces its own wrong committed tokens. Every one of these localizes with model-internal confidence. Our own TASK_SURFACE_LIT_GAPS.md audit found zero-hit arXiv queries for diffusion+execution-feedback remasking; my independent searches (abs remask AND (test OR execution); diffusion AND traceback; oracle AND remasking) returned 0-3 hits, none doing this. The one adjacent paper, 2605.16829 CDC (Constrained Diffusion for Code, 2026-05-16), uses STATIC program analysis to pick constraint-relevant regions -- no test execution, no runtime traceback. 2605.17174 uses static-analysis *rewards* for RL, explicitly because execution rewards are too sparse to train on -- but we use execution at INFERENCE, where sparsity is not a problem. So the specific move is open, and the null result gives us a pre-registered baseline to beat.
lens.experiment: Four arms on Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B, HE+ (n=164) and MBPP+ (n=378), all at IDENTICAL total wall-clock and NFE budget (this is the control the prior work lacks): (A0) no-refine single pass at the full budget -- the upper-bound control our own DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md section 4 flags as missing, and note that at nfe512 this is .707/.680, which the entire existing refinement grid (best .624) FAILS to beat; (A1) confidence remask -- remask the lowest-confidence k% of committed tokens, i.e. the 2606.12232 method, reimplemented at canvas level; (A2) uniform-random remask of the same k% (the confound control nobody runs: it separates 'localization is good' from 'stochasticity helps', which matters because 2605.26582 argues stochasticity itself error-corrects); (A3) execution-localized remask -- run evalplus untrusted_check on visible tests, parse the traceback for the deepest frame inside the candidate, map line -> AST node via ast.parse + node.lineno/col_offset, remask exactly that token span, then re-diffuse only those positions. Critically all four must be true CANVAS-LEVEL remasking: the existing scripts/refine_verifier_guided.py `remask` policy is a PROXY that truncates the prior solution and re-prompts (verified at line 187-194: it keeps a prefix and re-runs diffusion from there), which is not the same operator and must be rewritten. Primary metric: pass@1+ at matched wall-clock. Mechanism isolation: localization precision/recall against an ORACLE remasker that is given the ground-truth diff span (upper bound), so we can report what fraction of the oracle's headroom each signal captures -- this is the ablation that separates the proposed cause from the confound. Report the visible-vs-hidden test gap explicitly (we measured real false-passes in kept sets: HE+ medium 5, large 3; MBPP+ small 10, medium 20, large 23), because using visible tests to localize while scoring on hidden tests is exactly where our own retracted verifier bug lived. Pre-register k% and the iteration count on a held-out slice to avoid tuning on the test set.
lens.assets_needed: PRESENT: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, data/evalplus/{humaneval,mbpp}_plus.jsonl, evalplus 0.3.1 with eval.untrusted_check (the CORRECT grader, post-fix commit 67a7a01), scripts/refine_verifier_guided.py as a starting skeleton, scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py for the matched single-pass control, models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B/generation_utils.py (alg in {origin, maskgit_plus, topk_margin, entropy} -- we need entropy/confidence exposed per position for A1, which it computes internally at line 434). NEEDS WRITING: a true canvas-level remask operator (feed a partially-masked target sequence back into diffusion_generate rather than re-prompting) -- moderate, the 4D attention_mask is already plumbed (modeling_dream.py:280-320) and DreamOn's generator shows the tensor-rewriting pattern; the traceback->AST->token-span mapper; the oracle remasker (needs ground-truth canonical solutions, which evalplus ships). NOT needed: no training, no Scaffold checkpoint, no second disk.
lens.kill_criterion: Killed if A3 does not beat A1 AND A2 by more than the 95% CI half-width at matched wall-clock -- which at n=164, p~.5 is 7.65 pts, and n=378 is 5.04 pts (computed). Given HE+ n=164 the unpaired two-arm MDE at 80% power is 15.5 pts, so we MUST use paired/McNemar tests on identical task sets, not unpaired proportions, or the study is underpowered by construction. Hard kill: if no arm, including A3, exceeds the A0 single-pass upper bound (.707 HE+ / .680 MBPP+), the whole refinement framing is dead -- and this is a live risk, since our existing grid topped out at .624. Also killed if the oracle remasker itself fails to beat A0, because that would mean the ceiling for ANY localization signal is below the trivial baseline and the bottleneck is re-diffusion capability, not localization.
lens.builds_on: arXiv:2606.12232 'Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models' (2026-06-10). Its claim: post-hoc confidence-based remasking gives little-to-no benefit over confidence-based unmasking at standard block lengths, and exacerbates diversity collapse under stochastic decoding; it concludes the benefits are 'highly setting-dependent' and calls for a more comprehensive evaluation framework. The defect we repair is that it stops at a null result and never asks whether the null is about the signal or the operator: it varies the setting (block length, stochasticity) but holds the localization signal fixed at model confidence throughout, and it runs no random-remask control, so it cannot distinguish 'confidence is a bad error-locator' from 'remasking does not help'. Related work already showed the operator is fine (2604.18738 T2M, 2605.26436) and that the model actively resists correcting itself (2606.01026 preservation bias), which together make 'bad signal' the live hypothesis that 2606.12232 leaves untested. We repair it by swapping in a signal with external ground truth (test execution + traceback), adding the missing random-remask confound control, and adding an oracle-localization ceiling so the result is interpretable whichever way it goes. We also repair OUR OWN retracted arm here: DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md Retraction 2 established that our `restart` policy discarded the draft (measuring Dream-Coder, not refinement) and that our `remask` policy is a prompt-truncation proxy; A3 is the properly-conditioned operator that retraction demands. Secondary: 2605.16829 CDC (static analysis, no execution) is the nearest neighbour and the correct baseline-in-spirit to cite and differentiate from.

diff.sharpened_claim: Post-hoc remasking in masked diffusion LMs has been repeatedly benchmarked with the localization signal held fixed at model-internal confidence, and the resulting null results (2606.12232, 2607.24763) have been read as verdicts on the remasking PRIMITIVE. We show the null is signal-conditional, not primitive-conditional, by running the first signal-substitution ablation on a single fixed canvas-level remask operator: {execution-localized (failing assert -> traceback frame -> line -> AST subtree -> token span), confidence-localized, uniform-random, oracle-diff-span} x fixed operator, on Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B / HumanEval+ / MBPP+ at matched NFE AND matched wall-clock, scored paired (McNemar) against a no-refine single-pass upper bound at the full budget (.707/.680). We report localization precision/recall against the oracle and the fraction of oracle headroom each signal captures, plus the flip-flop rate per signal, so that a null for execution-grounding is diagnostic: either (a) execution localization captures a large share of oracle headroom and confidence does not -- the null was about the signal; or (b) even the oracle fails to beat single-pass -- the bottleneck is re-diffusion capability at the reopened positions, quantitatively corroborating 2606.12232's flip-flop finding on a code model with an external, non-model-internal locator and therefore closing the signal-vs-capability question that 2606.12232 explicitly left open.

related_work.citation: Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models, arXiv:2606.12232 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: Workshop papers, not main-conference. Verified via OpenReview api2 search: appears twice with venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/SPIGM ("SPIGM @ ICML Poster") and venueid ICML.cc/2026/Workshop/AdaptFM ("AdaptFM Poster"). No main-conference venueid found. arXiv v1 date verified on arXiv abs page submission history.
related_work.what_it_covers: Re-evaluation of WINO (2507.18578) post-hoc confidence remasking on LLaDA-8B-Instruct and Dream-v0-Instruct-7B, GSM8K/MATH-500/HumanEval/MBPP. Finds ~0.4-0.5% gain at BL=32 over Fast-dLLM, ~1.3-1.5% at BL=128; argues BL=128 WINO underperforms BL=32 Fast-dLLM so remasking repairs Fast-dLLM's own large-block failure mode rather than raising the ceiling. Critically, its own Section 3.2 computes an ORACLE leave-one-out confidence upper bound (14x NFE) and shows WINO's cheap shadow confidence MATCHES it, then measures flip-flop rate (75-90% LLaDA, 85-95% Dream) and concludes the model fails to propose better alternatives. Appendix B.2 ablates spatial/temporal neighbor expansion; both degrade and do not reduce flip-flop, ruling out cascading dependencies. Also studies stochastic decoding and diversity collapse, and reports throughput (tokens/s) not just NFE.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its oracle is an oracle over CONFIDENCE (leave-one-out predictive probability), not an oracle over CORRECTNESS. So the paper shows confidence is computed well, never that confidence is the right construct for 'which token is wrong'. It runs no uniform-random remask control of the same token budget. It never substitutes a non-model-internal localization signal (execution, static analysis, ground-truth diff). It operates on within-generation block decoding, not on a post-hoc completed-candidate canvas. It uses a general LM (LLaDA) and Dream-Instruct, never a code-specialised backbone (Dream-Coder / DiffuCoder) on the EvalPlus graders. It does not test the code-specific setting where an external correctness oracle is cheaply available.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The 'oracle' is a confidence oracle, so 'shadow matches oracle' cannot license the inference that positions were correctly identified as WRONG -- the paper's own phrasing that WINO 'is effective at identifying positions that need remasking (at least relative to the oracle confidence)' is circular, because both signals are the same construct. (2) No random-remask control, so 'remasking gives little benefit' cannot be separated from 'stochastic perturbation of k% of tokens gives little benefit'. (3) Workshop-scale evidence: HumanEval/MBPP at their sample sizes with sub-1pp effects is far below the binomial noise floor; the paper reports 3 seeds but does not report paired tests over identical task sets. (4) Latency accounting is partially done (throughput figures) but not used to define matched-budget arms in the headline comparison. (5) Generalization is explicitly listed as future work -- it only re-evaluates WINO plus one Saber figure, so 'confidence remasking is weak' rests on 1-2 methods.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page + full PDF text (pdftotext) read for Sections 3.1/3.2/3.3, Appendix B.2, related work, conclusion. Venue verified via OpenReview api2 /notes/search (two ICML 2026 workshop hits, no conference venueid).

related_work.citation: CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models, arXiv:2607.24763 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. No OpenReview record found under that title; arXiv listing shows only 'updated version' in comments, no journal-ref. arXiv v1 date 4 Jun 2026 verified from abs-page submission history and dateline.
related_work.what_it_covers: Directly the compute-accounting critique this candidate wants to make: audits 7 remasking strategies across LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base at 4 stochasticity levels and 3 step budgets, standardizing ACTUAL NFE, enforcing multi-metric reporting, controlling stochasticity. Key results: temperature explains most MAUVE variance; compute-matched comparison REVERSES several published rankings; informed remasking and stochastic unmasking are in tension. Includes a HumanEval leg (Table 11): at nominal 256 steps high_entropy 31.7 vs none 28.3, but high_entropy uses 3.4x the NFE, and at matched NFE=437 'none matches or exceeds all strategies'. Its supported strategy list explicitly includes a `random` remasking strategy. Releases a leaderboard over 12 open-weight MDLMs.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Explicitly declines wall-clock accounting (dedicated subsection 'Why we use NFE and not wall-clock time'), so the matched-wall-clock leg is open. Its downstream code leg is HumanEval pass@1 via lm-eval at n=100 with binomial SE ~4.7pp -- it says so itself -- and it is base-model, not the instruct/code-specialised Dream-Coder, and not EvalPlus (HumanEval+/MBPP+) graders. All 7 strategies are model-internal or random; none uses execution, static analysis, or ground-truth localization. No oracle-localization ceiling. No paired/McNemar testing on identical task sets. No AST/span-structured remask unit -- strategies are token-level.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Its own headline code number sits inside its own admitted noise band (n=100, SE~4.7pp vs a 0.3pp within-block difference), so the compute-matched reversal is argued from block-to-block contrast rather than a powered test. (2) NFE-only accounting is a defensible but load-bearing choice: it assumes per-step forward passes dominate runtime, which is false for methods that add non-forward work (test execution, static analysis, traceback parsing, tree surgery) -- exactly the class our A3 belongs to, so a paper in that class MUST add wall-clock or it cannot be priced under CaRE's own protocol. (3) Unconditional-generation metrics (MAUVE, Self-BLEU, Distinct-3) carry the headline; the functional-correctness surface is one small table. (4) Base-only backbones; instruct/code models are where remasking is actually deployed.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (v1 4 Jun 2026 confirmed via submission history and dateline) + full PDF text read for abstract, contributions, Table 11 region, and the 'Why we use NFE and not wall-clock time' limitation subsection.

related_work.citation: Constrained Code Generation with Discrete Diffusion (CDC), arXiv:2605.16829 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview search returns no record for this title (nearest hit is an unrelated 'Constrained Language Generation with Discrete Diffusion Models', CoRR 2025). arXiv v1 16 May 2026 verified from abs page.
related_work.what_it_covers: The nearest neighbour on method shape and the strongest overlap in the set. Training-free neurosymbolic framework with a general (evaluator, localization map, correction operator) triple, instantiated twice: GradGuide, which trains an auxiliary surrogate g_phi on EXECUTION-DRIVEN LABELS (test-pass outcomes) and localizes likely functional errors via a gradient/saliency top-k over the clean-state proposal, then reopens that span to [MASK] and re-diffuses; and MDFI, which uses a static analyzer's concrete vulnerability witnesses on partial programs, localizes on a program graph, and remasks a Parent+Leaf AST neighborhood. Reports Dream-Coder-7B HumanEval-X C++ 34.1 -> 65.2 pass@1, MBPP-C++ 27.7 -> 59.2, plus CWEval/LLMSecEval+ security. Includes edit-locality metrics (32 vs 123 median edited tokens vs AR re-prompting), a corrective-effectiveness table (improvement rate, imp/reg counts, net change, constructive ratio), an AST-neighborhood-scope ablation, and -- most importantly for us -- a RANDOM-EDITING control that 'matches vanilla, so localization must be constraint-steered'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its execution signal is a LEARNED DIFFERENTIABLE SURROGATE consumed via gradients at intermediate denoising states, never a real interpreter verdict, and never a traceback. Its appendix concedes the exact-oracle route ('Satisfies can be an exact oracle when available, such as compilation, unit-test execution, or static analysis') but says exact evaluation is unavailable on partial programs and therefore falls back to the surrogate -- so real-interpreter localization on a COMPLETE candidate is stated-but-not-done. Language/benchmark surface is C++ (HumanEval-X C++ 164, MBPP-C++ 397) plus security suites, not Python HumanEval+/MBPP+ with evalplus graders. Compute is matched only loosely (fixed 256 denoising steps, 512 max tokens) -- no matched-NFE or matched-wall-clock arms, and no accounting of surrogate-training cost or surrogate forward/backward passes in the reported budget. No confidence-remasking baseline arm. No oracle-diff-span ceiling. No paired significance tests. No visible-vs-hidden test-leakage analysis.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Cost accounting flatters the method: the surrogate's training cost is amortized away and the extra backward pass through g_phi plus repeated interventions are not priced against the vanilla baseline's step budget -- and the +31pp headline gain on a 7B code model is large enough that a compute-matched vanilla arm (more steps / more samples) is the missing control. (2) Its random-editing control is reported only as a one-line figure annotation on one benchmark (HumanEval-X C++, greedy), not as a full arm across benchmarks. (3) It never separates 'execution information helped' from 'a trained task-specific scorer helped' -- the surrogate could be exploiting benchmark-specific regularities rather than execution semantics; a real-interpreter arm is the clean test and is absent. (4) Confidence-based remasking, the dominant published localizer, is not a baseline, so its ranking against the incumbent is unknown. (5) C++-only functional benchmarks mean the claim is untested on the Python surface where EvalPlus's rigorous graders (and its own retraction-prone hand-rolled-verifier hazard) apply.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page for v1 date; full PDF text read for the operator-instantiation section, GradGuide equations, experimental setup and baselines, localization/efficiency section, Appendix B.3.2 ablations (random-editing line), Appendix C.1/C.4 surrogate and reopened-state details. OpenReview searched, no venue record.

related_work.citation: Remask, Don't Replace: Token-to-Mask Refinement in Diffusion Large Language Models (T2M), arXiv:2604.18738 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 20 Apr 2026, v2 7 May 2026). No OpenReview venue record found. Supersedes arXiv:2605.26436 'Targeted Remasking' (v1 6 Apr 2026), which was withdrawn by its authors with an explicit comment directing readers to 2604.18738 -- so the two candidate-cited IDs are the same work, and the earlier one should not be cited as independent support.
related_work.what_it_covers: Validates the remask-to-[MASK] PRIMITIVE against LLaDA2.1's Token-to-Token overwrite editing: argues replacement propagates errors under polluted context and cannot fire under a multimodal posterior. Training-free, +13.33 on AIME 2025, +8.56 on CMATH. The superseded version (2605.26436) additionally reports 12 benchmarks, three error-detection strategies (probability-based, trigger-mirrored, temporal-difference), and a last-mile-corruption error analysis repairing 59.4% of such cases on CMATH.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: All three of its error-detection strategies are model-internal (probability, trigger-mirror, temporal difference). Gains concentrate on math/last-mile answer corruption, not on functional code correctness. No execution signal, no random-remask control, no oracle ceiling, no wall-clock accounting, no EvalPlus graders.
related_work.known_defects: The claim 'the primitive is fine, only detection is weak' is asserted from math benchmarks where the failure mode is a single corrupted final answer token -- a regime with unusually high localization signal-to-noise. Whether the primitive survives on multi-token, multi-site code errors is untested. Citation hygiene note for us: the candidate's builds_on cites 2604.18738 AND 2605.26436 as two supporting works; 2605.26436 is a withdrawn earlier version of the same paper and must be cited as such, not double-counted.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs pages for both IDs, including the explicit withdrawal/supersession comment on 2605.26436. OpenReview searched for both titles; no venue record.

related_work.citation: Revise, Don't Freeze: Sampler-Matched Training for Self-Correcting Masked Diffusion Language Models (D3IM / SCOPE), arXiv:2606.01026 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 31 May 2026, 8 pages / 2 figures / 10 tables). No OpenReview venue record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Parameter-free corrector-style sampler permitting direct visible-to-visible revision, plus the 'preservation bias' diagnosis (the model reproduces its own wrong committed tokens) and SCOPE post-training to fix it. LLaDA-8B at 64 steps: +13.0 GSM8K, +4.8 MATH-500, +15.3 HumanEval, +10.4 MBPP.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Requires post-training (SCOPE) for its main gains, so it is not a training-free localization result. Signal is again model-internal. It names preservation bias but does not test whether an EXTERNAL error locator escapes it, which is precisely the hypothesis this candidate isolates. Also note: preservation bias is a claim about the model resisting correction, which cuts AGAINST our A3's headroom, and its interaction with 2606.12232's flip-flop finding (the same phenomenon, measured differently) makes the oracle-localization ceiling the load-bearing measurement in our design.
related_work.known_defects: The strong numbers come from a base-quality regime (HumanEval 29.3%, MBPP 30.8% after gains) far below Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B's .707/.680, so the gains may be recovering headroom that does not exist at a competent code model's operating point -- a scale/backbone replication gap. Training-free vs post-trained arms are not cleanly separated in the headline.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (v1 date, comments field). OpenReview searched for the title; no venue record.

related_work.citation: Beyond Execution: Static-Analysis Rewards and Hint-Conditioned Diffusion RL for Code Generation, arXiv:2605.17174 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. No OpenReview record found; arXiv v1 16 May 2026 verified.
related_work.what_it_covers: Systematic study of RL post-training for diffusion code generation: execution-free (static-checking, similarity) rewards vs unit-test execution rewards, hint-conditioned sampling, and difficulty interaction. DiffuCoder HumanEval 53.9 -> 67.1, LiveCodeBench 14.9 -> 15.5, 9.4% rollout-time reduction. Motivates avoiding execution because of the 'capability cliff' where execution rewards are too sparse to learn from.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Purely a TRAINING-time reward-design study. It never uses execution at inference for localization, and its stated reason for avoiding execution (reward sparsity for RL) does not transfer to inference-time localization where a single failing assertion is fully informative. It also does not use AST structure for remasking (its AST use is training-time hinting).
related_work.known_defects: Its central negative-on-execution result is reward-sparsity-specific and is likely to be over-read by reviewers as 'execution signals do not help diffusion code models'. Our candidate should pre-empt that misreading explicitly, because it is the most likely reviewer objection and the paper's own framing invites it. Additionally, the LiveCodeBench delta (14.9 -> 15.5) is within plausible noise while being reported alongside a 13-point HumanEval delta, so its cross-difficulty conclusions rest on uneven effect sizes.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page + abstract; OpenReview searched, no record.

related_work.citation: Prism: Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Hierarchical Search and Self-Verification for Discrete Diffusion Language Models, arXiv:2602.01842 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 (main conference) -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 /notes/search, which returns the paper with venue 'ICML 2026 regular' and venueid ICML.cc/2026/Conference. arXiv comments field also states 'Accepted to ICML 2026'. arXiv v1 2 Feb 2026, v3 5 May 2026.
related_work.what_it_covers: The strongest-venue prior art on test-time scaling for dLLMs. Hierarchical Trajectory Search that prunes and reallocates compute in an early-to-mid denoising window; local branching with PARTIAL REMASKING to explore diverse implementations while preserving high-confidence tokens; and Self-Verified Feedback that explicitly REPLACES external verifiers with self-evaluation prompts. Evaluated on four math and code benchmarks across LLaDA-8B-Instruct, Dream-7B-Instruct, and LLaDA-2.0-mini; matches best-of-N at substantially fewer NFE.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It deliberately moves AWAY from external verification (SVF replaces external verifiers), which is the opposite design axis from execution grounding -- so it is the correct citation for 'compute-matched dLLM test-time scaling is solved for self-verification' while leaving external-oracle localization untouched. Preserves high-confidence tokens, i.e. the retention criterion is again confidence. No traceback/AST localization, no oracle-diff ceiling, no matched wall-clock.
related_work.known_defects: Self-verification is a weaker signal than execution on tasks that ship tests, and using self-evaluation prompts to decide what to remask reintroduces the same model-internal circularity that 2606.12232 flags for confidence -- an execution-grounded arm is a direct, tractable follow-up to Prism's own SVF component. Its NFE-matched framing also inherits CaRE's critique: extra self-evaluation prompt passes are model calls and must be counted, and prompt-level self-verification cost scales differently from per-step forward passes.
related_work.verified_how: OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned 'Efficient Test-Time Scaling via Hierarchical Search and Self-Verification for Discrete Diffusio...' with venue 'ICML 2026 regular', venueid ICML.cc/2026/Conference. Cross-checked against arXiv abs page comments ('Accepted to ICML 2026') and v1/v3 dates.

related_work.citation: Corrective Diffusion Language Models (CDLM), arXiv:2512.15596 (2025)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 17 Dec 2025, v2 29 Jan 2026, 21 pages). No OpenReview venue record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: The closest pre-cutoff work on the exact diagnosis this candidate builds on: shows that standard MDLM unmasking training does NOT induce the ability to assign lower confidence to incorrect visible tokens, and proposes correction-oriented post-training that supervises visible incorrect tokens to make confidence discriminative. Introduces the Code Revision Benchmark (CRB), a controllable executable benchmark built on HumanEval/MBPP/HumanEval+/MBPP+ that injects localized corruptions (|E|=1 single-error, |E|>1 multi-error) and grades each instance by deterministic execution; measures error localization via confidence gap and Top-K hit rate, plus Pass@1 after confidence-threshold refinement.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: This is the single most important paper for our positioning because it pre-establishes, before the cutoff, that CONFIDENCE IS A BAD ERROR LOCATOR in MDLMs -- so our claim's diagnostic half is not novel and must not be presented as such. But its fix is TRAINING (post-training to repair confidence), never signal substitution at inference. It never uses execution to LOCALIZE (execution is only the grader and the corruption oracle). It has no uniform-random remask control. Its Top-K hit rate is measured against known injected corruption sites on synthetically corrupted correct programs, not against a model's own natural errors on from-scratch generation -- its own limitations section concedes CRB applies localized perturbation to model-generated solutions specifically so that revision failures cannot be attributed to generation capability. So natural-error localization on a real generation distribution is open.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Construct-validity gap: CRB's synthetic single/multi-token corruptions of programs that 'lie squarely within each model's own distribution' are an easier and structurally different localization problem than a model's own natural multi-site logic errors -- so 'localization improved on CRB' may not transfer to real pass@1 refinement, and it is exactly the untested regime our design occupies. (2) It has ground-truth corruption sites available and still never reports an oracle-localization ceiling on end-to-end Pass@1, so the reader cannot tell how much headroom any localizer has. (3) No random-remask control, so improved Top-K hit rate is not separated from improved perturbation. (4) It requires post-training, so it cannot answer whether an off-the-shelf model plus a better external signal suffices.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (v1/v2 dates) + full PDF text (pdftotext) searched for execution/oracle/random/localization/benchmark terms; read the CRB construction, error-localization metrics, and limitations sections. OpenReview searched for the title; no venue record.

related_work.citation: Detect, Remask, Repair: Diffusion Editing for Faithful Summarization of Evolving Contexts, arXiv:2606.12807 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. No OpenReview venue record found; arXiv v1 11 Jun 2026.
related_work.what_it_covers: The closest structural analogue outside code: an explicit detect -> remask -> repair pipeline where the localization signal is EXTERNAL to the generator (a [MASK]-DISC token-level classifier trained to flag unsupported spans against updated evidence), with iterative FK-Steering repair and one-step distilled variants, evaluated on DialogSum and a new StreamSum benchmark. Baselines include full regeneration and an AR detect-critique-refine (DCR) system; reports faithfulness-speed-preservation tradeoffs and sub-0.5s one-step repair.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Domain is summarization faithfulness, signal is a learned discriminator against a text evidence set -- not program execution, not a traceback, not an AST. No code benchmarks, no pass@1, no oracle-span ceiling, no random-remask control (random masking appears only as a training-time corruption baseline it contrasts against). Establishes that external-signal localized diffusion repair is a viable and publishable frame, which HELPS our positioning: the frame is validated, the execution instantiation is open.
related_work.known_defects: The comparison against full regeneration is a quality-vs-cost tradeoff rather than a matched-budget test, and preservation is measured with metrics that partly reward not changing things, which structurally favours localized repair over regeneration. A matched-budget regeneration arm is the missing control -- the same control our A0 supplies for the code setting.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page + full PDF text read for the framework, baselines, and repair-model variants. OpenReview searched; no record.

related_work.citation: Wide-In, Narrow-Out: Revokable Decoding for Efficient and Effective DLLMs (WINO), arXiv:2507.18578 (2025)
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 /notes/search (venue 'ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference); also NeurIPS 2025 ER Workshop Spotlight (venueid NeurIPS.cc/2025/Workshop/ER) and CoRR 2025. arXiv v1 24 Jul 2025, v2 26 Sep 2025.
related_work.what_it_covers: The method 2606.12232 re-evaluates, and the canonical A1 baseline for this candidate. Training-free parallel draft-and-verify: aggressively drafts multiple tokens, then uses bidirectional context via auxiliary shadow tokens to verify and re-mask suspicious ones. Reports 6x speedup with +2.58% on GSM8K for LLaDA, 10x on Flickr30K captioning; verified on LLaDA and MMaDA.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Confidence-only localization, within-generation block decoding, no code-specialised backbone in the headline, no external signal, no random control. Being ICLR 2026 (main venue, first public 2025-07) it is the strongest-standing incumbent our A1 must reimplement faithfully at canvas level -- a reviewer will check that A1 is a fair rendering of WINO rather than a strawman.
related_work.known_defects: Its own gains were shown by 2606.12232 to be largely a repair of Fast-dLLM's large-block degradation rather than a ceiling increase, and its NFE accounting understates cost because each forward pass carries an extra shadow block (more FLOPs and latency per step) -- which is why the candidate's matched-wall-clock requirement is the right accounting fix and should be applied to A1 as well as A3.
related_work.verified_how: OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned three records including venue 'ICLR 2026 Poster' with venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference. arXiv abs page for v1/v2 dates.

related_work.citation: CORE: Context-Robust Remasking for Diffusion Language Models, arXiv:2602.04096 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 (main conference) -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 /notes/search: venue 'ICML 2026 regular', venueid ICML.cc/2026/Conference. arXiv v1 4 Feb 2026, v3 13 Mar 2026.
related_work.what_it_covers: The strongest pre-cutoff, main-venue argument that confidence is the wrong signal, which makes it BOTH supporting evidence and the most dangerous competitor for the candidate's diagnostic claim. Names 'context rigidity' and argues static confidence scores are 'inherently myopic; inconsistent tokens can appear confident to the model itself'. Instead identifies context-brittle tokens by probing sensitivity to targeted masked-context perturbations, formalized as robust optimization over context shifts. Training-free. On LLaDA-8B-Base reports consistent gains across reasoning and code, explicitly OUTPERFORMING COMPUTE-MATCHED BASELINES, and improving MBPP by up to 9.2 percentage points.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its signal is still model-internal -- perturbation sensitivity of the model's own predictions, not external ground truth. It is base-model (LLaDA-8B-Base), not a code-specialised instruct model on EvalPlus. No traceback/AST structure, no oracle-diff ceiling, no uniform-random control at matched token budget, no wall-clock accounting. Crucially, its +9.2pp MBPP result at compute-matched settings PRE-EMPTS a naive reading of the candidate's 'confidence remasking fails' premise: at least one main-venue pre-cutoff method already beats compute-matched baselines by replacing the confidence signal while keeping the remask primitive. The candidate MUST cite CORE as prior confirmation of the signal-not-primitive thesis and position execution-grounding as the external-oracle instantiation, not as the first refutation of confidence.
related_work.known_defects: Perturbation probing costs extra forward passes per candidate position; 'compute-matched' needs auditing against CaRE's actual-NFE standard, and wall-clock is unreported. Base-only backbone leaves the instruct/code-model regime open. It reports no oracle ceiling, so the reader cannot tell whether its +9.2pp captures 10% or 90% of available localization headroom -- the same gap our oracle arm fills, and the cleanest way for us to add value on top of CORE rather than compete with it.
related_work.verified_how: OpenReview api2 /notes/search: 'CORE: Context-Robust Remasking for Diffusion Language Models', venue 'ICML 2026 regular', venueid ICML.cc/2026/Conference. arXiv abs page for v1/v3 dates and abstract.

related_work.citation: Stop the Flip-Flop: Context-Preserving Verification for Fast Revocable Diffusion Decoding (COVER), arXiv:2602.06161 (2026)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 5 Feb 2026, v2 28 May 2026). No OpenReview venue record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Origin of the flip-flop metric that 2606.12232 uses to diagnose WINO's failure. Documents that existing verification schemes frequently trigger flip-flop oscillations (remask then restore unchanged), notes this weakens the conditioning context for parallel drafting and burns the revision budget, and proposes COVER: leave-one-out verification plus stable drafting in a single forward pass via KV-cache override with a closed-form diagonal correction, prioritizing seeds by a stability-aware score.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Stability-aware scoring is still model-internal. Its target is speed/unnecessary-revision reduction rather than raising the quality ceiling, and it does not test whether an external correctness signal reduces flip-flop. This matters directly for the candidate's kill criterion: flip-flop rate per signal is the diagnostic that distinguishes 'bad localization' from 'model cannot propose an alternative', and COVER supplies the established metric definition to report it.
related_work.known_defects: Frames flip-flop as a cost/efficiency problem to be suppressed, whereas 2606.12232 reads high flip-flop as evidence of a capability ceiling; nobody tests which reading is right by holding the operator fixed and varying only the signal, including a correctness oracle. That test is the candidate's contribution.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, abstract, v1/v2 dates), reached via the bibliography of 2606.12232's PDF where it is cited as Xiang et al. 2026. OpenReview searched; no record.

related_work.citation: Finish First, Perfect Later: Test-Time Token-Level Cross-Validation for Diffusion Large Language Models (Tolerator), arXiv:2510.05090 (2025)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint, 'Work in progress' per arXiv comments (17 pages, 8 figures). No OpenReview venue record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: The closest pre-cutoff precedent for the candidate's OPERATOR: an explicit two-stage training-free procedure of (i) sequence fill-up to a complete candidate, then (ii) iterative refinement by REMASKING AND DECODING A SUBSET of tokens while treating the rest as context -- i.e. canvas-level post-hoc remasking of a completed generation, evaluated across five benchmarks including code generation, under matched compute.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Selection of the remasked subset is by token-level cross-validation among predicted tokens, i.e. model-internal. No execution, no traceback, no AST spans, no oracle ceiling, no random control, and no wall-clock accounting. Important for the candidate's framing: 'canvas-level post-hoc remasking of a completed candidate' is NOT itself a novel operator, so the contribution must be located in the SIGNAL plus the control design, not in the operator.
related_work.known_defects: 'Work in progress' status and no oracle/random controls; matched-budget claims predate CaRE's actual-NFE standard and should be re-audited. Its existence is a useful engineering reference for our operator rewrite and simultaneously removes 'we invented canvas-level remasking' from our claim surface.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, abstract, v1 date, comments). OpenReview searched; no record.

related_work.citation: Diffusion On Syntax Trees For Program Synthesis, arXiv:2405.20519 (2024)
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2025 Spotlight -- VERIFIED via OpenReview api2 /notes/search (venue 'ICLR 2025 Spotlight', venueid ICLR.cc/2025/Conference); also NeurIPS 2024 Sys2-Reasoning Workshop Poster and CoRR 2024.
related_work.what_it_covers: The oldest and most direct precedent for the candidate's core conceptual move -- diffusion that edits programs while OBSERVING EXECUTION OUTPUT. Neural diffusion over syntax trees of any context-free grammar, inverting noise applied to trees, preserving syntactic validity, combined with search so the model can 'write graphics programs, see the execution result, and debug them to meet the required specifications'. Applied to inverse graphics.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Domain is inverse graphics with small DSL programs and image-reconstruction objectives, with a purpose-trained tree-diffusion model -- not a 7B pretrained masked-token dLLM, not Python, not unit-test assertions, not a traceback, and no pass@1 on HumanEval+/MBPP+. Execution feedback drives an outer SEARCH over tree edits rather than a token-span remask on a token canvas. So it establishes 'execution-feedback-driven diffusion program editing' as a known idea at a top venue, which the candidate MUST cite and differentiate from, while leaving the pretrained-masked-dLLM / natural-language-specified / test-graded instantiation entirely open.
related_work.known_defects: Bespoke small-scale DSL setting; no evidence the approach transfers to pretrained large masked dLLMs where the token canvas is not grammar-constrained and where the model resists revising its own commitments (preservation bias / flip-flop). That transfer is untested and is precisely the regime the candidate probes -- the best single framing for the candidate is as the large-pretrained-dLLM test of this ICLR 2025 idea.
related_work.verified_how: OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned three records including venue 'ICLR 2025 Spotlight', venueid ICLR.cc/2025/Conference. arXiv abs page for v1 date and abstract.

related_work.citation: Debug like a Human: A Large Language Model Debugger via Verifying Runtime Execution Step-by-step (LDB), arXiv:2402.16906 (2024)
related_work.venue_status: Preprint / archived (OpenReview shows only an OpenReview.net/Archive record with no venue field; widely cited as ACL 2024 Findings but I could NOT confirm that via OpenReview or official proceedings within this session -- treat the venue as unverified). arXiv v1 25 Feb 2024, v6 current.
related_work.what_it_covers: The autoregressive-side incumbent for execution-grounded localization: segments programs into basic blocks, verifies intermediate runtime variable values against test cases after each block, and uses that runtime information to localize and repair, rather than treating the program as a monolith.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Autoregressive re-prompting/regeneration, not in-place remasking on an editable canvas -- so the edit is not localized in the generator's state, which is exactly the structural advantage a masked dLLM has and which CDC's edit-locality numbers (32 vs 123 median edited tokens) quantify. No diffusion, no remasking, no NFE/wall-clock matched arms against a diffusion single-pass baseline.
related_work.known_defects: For our purposes the relevant point is a framing risk, not a defect: a reviewer will ask what execution-grounded localization buys in a diffusion model that it did not already buy in AR self-debugging. The candidate needs a diffusion-specific answer (in-place span repair without regenerating the prefix, bidirectional re-conditioning on surviving code, and edit locality), and should include the AR self-debug arm as a reference point given a matched AR baseline is already being built on .104.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API search (title/abstract) + OpenReview api2 /notes/search, which returned only an OpenReview.net/Archive record with a null venue. Venue claim deliberately left unverified.

diff.differentiation_statement: Every published remasking localizer we could find -- WINO (ICLR 2026), CORE (ICML 2026), Prism's SVF (ICML 2026), T2M, D3IM/SCOPE, Saber, COVER, BackPlay, Tolerator, and the seven strategies audited by CaRE -- derives its "which token is wrong" signal from the model's own predictive state: probability, entropy, temporal difference, perturbation sensitivity, or self-evaluation prompts. The single work that reaches for execution, CDC (2026-05-16, concurrent), explicitly cannot use a real interpreter because it intervenes mid-denoising on partial programs, so it trains a differentiable surrogate on test-pass labels and localizes by gradient saliency; its appendix concedes that an exact oracle "such as compilation, unit-test execution" would be preferable but is unavailable in its setting. Our arm A3 occupies exactly the gap that concession opens: a real interpreter verdict on a COMPLETE candidate, with the failing assertion's traceback frame mapped line -> AST node -> token span, fed back as a canvas-level remask. Four further differences a reviewer can check independently. (i) Control design: no prior work runs the uniform-random remask control at the same token budget, so no existing null distinguishes "localization is informative" from "perturbing k% of tokens helps"; and no prior work reports an oracle-diff-span ceiling on end-to-end pass@1, so no existing number tells you what fraction of available headroom any signal captures -- notably CDLM has ground-truth corruption sites in hand and still reports only Top-K hit rate, not an end-to-end ceiling. (ii) Accounting: CaRE (concurrent) standardises actual NFE and explicitly declines wall-clock; but a method whose cost is partly interpreter time, traceback parsing and tree surgery is invisible to NFE, so matched wall-clock is not a stylistic preference here, it is the only accounting under which our arm can be honestly priced -- we run both. (iii) Setting: the confidence-remasking null results are on LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B base/instruct at HumanEval/MBPP via lm-eval (CaRE's own binomial SE ~4.7pp at n=100); we run a code-specialised Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B at .707/.680 on EvalPlus's rigorous HumanEval+/MBPP+ graders with paired McNemar on identical task sets, which is both a stronger operating point and a properly powered test. (iv) Falsifiability: our A0 no-refine single-pass arm at the full budget is an upper bound that our own existing refinement grid (best .624) fails to clear, so the study can return a clean negative. Finally, we position honestly against two works that already own part of the thesis: CDLM (2025-12-17, pre-cutoff) established that standard MDLM training does not make confidence discriminative about visible errors, and CORE (ICML 2026, pre-cutoff) already beat compute-matched baselines by +9.2pp on MBPP by replacing the confidence signal while keeping the remask primitive. So "confidence is a bad locator, the primitive is fine" is prior art, not our finding; our contribution is the external-ground-truth instantiation plus the two missing controls (random, oracle) that turn any outcome into an interpretable measurement of localization headroom.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2606.12232 Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking (ICML 2026 SPIGM + AdaptFM workshops, 2026-06-10, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Its oracle is a confidence oracle, not a correctness oracle. It computes leave-one-out predictive probability at 14x NFE, finds WINO's shadow confidence matches it, and concludes WINO 'is effective at identifying positions that need remasking'. That inference is circular: both quantities are the same construct, so matching the confidence oracle says the confidence is computed well, never that low-confidence positions are the wrong ones. It then attributes the null to model capability via 75-95% flip-flop rates, with no signal-substitution arm and no random-remask control.
followup_openings.our_fix: Hold the operator fixed and vary only the signal across four arms {execution-localized, confidence-localized, uniform-random, ground-truth-diff-span oracle}, and report per-signal localization precision/recall against the correctness oracle AND per-signal flip-flop rate using COVER's (2602.06161) metric definition. This decomposes their single null into two measurable quantities: localization precision and re-diffusion success given correct localization. If execution localization has much higher precision than confidence yet flip-flop stays high, their capability conclusion is confirmed on a stronger footing and generalized to an external signal; if flip-flop drops with correct localization, their conclusion is signal-conditional and must be narrowed.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts a workshop-scale null into a decomposition, and it is the specific measurement their paper wanted (they built an oracle for exactly this purpose) but could not make because their oracle was over the wrong construct. Either outcome is publishable and neither depends on our method winning.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2607.24763 CaRE (preprint, 2026-06-04, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: It standardises actual NFE and argues against wall-clock in a dedicated subsection, on the premise that per-step forward passes dominate MDLM runtime. That premise silently excludes an entire method class: localizers whose cost is not a forward pass -- interpreter invocation, traceback parsing, ast.parse plus node.lineno/col_offset mapping, tree surgery, static analysis. Under NFE-only accounting such methods look free. Separately, its own HumanEval leg is n=100 with an admitted binomial SE of ~4.7pp against a reported 0.3pp within-block difference, and it is base-model LLaDA/Dream, not a code-specialised instruct model, and not the EvalPlus graders.
followup_openings.our_fix: Extend CaRE's protocol with a non-forward-pass cost column and report every arm at BOTH matched actual-NFE and matched wall-clock, with the non-model time (exec, parse, map) itemized so readers can see where an execution-grounded method's budget goes. Then re-run the functional-correctness leg where it actually has power: Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B, HumanEval+ (n=164) and MBPP+ (n=378), evalplus untrusted_check, paired McNemar on identical task sets rather than unpaired proportions.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is a protocol contribution reviewers can adopt independently of whether our method wins, and it repairs the one accounting hole in the concurrent paper that is otherwise the field's emerging evaluation standard. It also fixes the power problem that makes every current code-side remasking number uninterpretable.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2605.16829 CDC (preprint, 2026-05-16, concurrent -- nearest neighbour)
followup_openings.defect: Its execution signal is a learned differentiable surrogate consumed via gradient saliency, never an interpreter verdict; its own appendix admits an exact oracle would be preferable but is unavailable on partial programs. Three consequences: (a) it cannot separate 'execution semantics helped' from 'a trained task-specific scorer helped', since the surrogate could exploit benchmark regularities; (b) its cost accounting flatters it -- surrogate training is amortized away and the extra backward pass plus repeated interventions are not priced against a compute-matched vanilla arm, while the headline gain is +31pp on Dream-Coder-7B HumanEval-X C++; (c) its random-editing control appears only as a one-line figure annotation on one benchmark and one decoding setting, not as a full arm.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the real-interpreter arm CDC's appendix says it wanted, on complete candidates where the verdict is exact, and place it head-to-head against a surrogate-style learned locator and a confidence locator under one fixed remask operator with matched NFE and matched wall-clock. Promote random remasking from an annotation to a full arm across both benchmarks and both budget regimes, and add the oracle-diff ceiling CDC lacks. Move the surface from C++ HumanEval-X/MBPP-C++ to Python HumanEval+/MBPP+ with evalplus graders, and report visible-vs-hidden test leakage explicitly (we have measured real false-passes on kept sets: HE+ 5 and 3, MBPP+ 10/20/23), which is the failure mode CDC's test-driven pipeline is structurally exposed to and never audits.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It answers the sharpest question about the nearest neighbour -- is the win from execution semantics or from a fitted scorer -- with a control the original could not run, and it prices both under an accounting standard (CaRE) that postdates CDC. Cross-language and cross-grader replication of a +31pp claim is independently valuable.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2512.15596 Corrective Diffusion Language Models / CRB (preprint, 2025-12-17, PRE-CUTOFF)
followup_openings.defect: It establishes that confidence is a poor error locator and builds an executable Code Revision Benchmark to measure localization -- but CRB injects synthetic localized corruptions (|E|=1, |E|>1) into programs that its own limitations section says 'lie squarely within each model's own distribution', explicitly so that revision failures cannot be blamed on generation capability. Natural multi-site logic errors from from-scratch generation are a different and harder localization problem, and the transfer is untested. It also has ground-truth corruption sites available and still reports only confidence-gap and Top-K hit rate, never an oracle-localization ceiling on end-to-end Pass@1, and it runs no uniform-random control.
followup_openings.our_fix: Measure localization on the model's OWN natural errors from from-scratch generation on HumanEval+/MBPP+, with the ground-truth span taken from an oracle diff against evalplus canonical solutions, and report the end-to-end oracle ceiling on pass@1 that CRB omits -- so readers learn what fraction of headroom each signal captures rather than just a relative hit rate. Add the random control. Then check whether CDLM's synthetic-corruption ranking of localizers (confidence vs external) reproduces on natural errors; a reversal would be a substantive construct-validity finding about CRB.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the strongest and safest version of the candidate, because it repairs a PRE-CUTOFF paper that already owns our diagnostic claim: rather than re-asserting 'confidence is bad' (prior art) we test whether their benchmark's easier synthetic regime licenses conclusions about the real one, and we supply the ceiling that makes any localizer's number interpretable. It also forces us to cite CDLM prominently, which is the correct positioning and pre-empts the most likely rejection.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2602.04096 CORE (ICML 2026, 2026-02-04, PRE-CUTOFF) and arXiv:2602.01842 Prism (ICML 2026, 2026-02-02, PRE-CUTOFF)
followup_openings.defect: Both replace or bypass raw confidence and report compute-matched wins (CORE: +9.2pp MBPP on LLaDA-8B-Base; Prism: matches best-of-N at far fewer NFE via self-verified feedback that explicitly REPLACES external verifiers). Neither reports an oracle-localization ceiling, so neither reveals whether its gain captures a small or large share of available headroom; both remain model-internal, so both inherit the circularity that 2606.12232 flags; and both are base or general instruct backbones, with Prism's self-evaluation prompt passes and CORE's perturbation probes needing audit under CaRE's actual-NFE standard plus wall-clock.
followup_openings.our_fix: Add CORE-style context-perturbation localization and a Prism-SVF-style self-verification localizer as additional signal arms inside the same fixed-operator, matched-budget harness, and place all of them on one axis against uniform-random (floor) and oracle-diff (ceiling). This yields the field's first headroom-normalised ranking of localization signals -- internal-confidence, context-brittleness, self-verification, external-execution -- rather than another incomparable point result, and it replicates two ICML 2026 methods on a code-specialised instruct backbone with EvalPlus graders.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It reframes the paper from 'our signal beats theirs' to 'here is how much localization headroom exists and what fraction each published signal class captures', which is robust to our arm losing, directly answers the 'need for a more comprehensive evaluation framework' that 2606.12232 calls for, and makes the two strongest pre-cutoff main-venue works collaborators rather than competitors.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2405.20519 Diffusion On Syntax Trees (ICLR 2025 Spotlight, 2024-05-30, PRE-CUTOFF) and arXiv:2402.16906 LDB (2024-02-25)
followup_openings.defect: The conceptual move -- diffusion that edits a program, executes it, sees the result, and debugs -- already exists at a top venue, but only for a purpose-trained tree-diffusion model over a small graphics DSL with image-reconstruction objectives and an outer search over tree edits. Whether it transfers to a large PRETRAINED masked-token dLLM is untested, and there is specific reason to doubt it: the pretrained-dLLM literature reports preservation bias (2606.01026) and 75-95% flip-flop (2606.12232), i.e. these models actively resist revising their own commitments in a way a bespoke tree-diffusion model does not. On the AR side, LDB shows runtime-value verification localizes well but repairs by regeneration, not in-place editing.
followup_openings.our_fix: Frame the study as the large-pretrained-dLLM transfer test of the ICLR 2025 idea: same information source (execution), radically different generator (7B pretrained masked dLLM), different specification channel (natural language + assertions instead of a target image), different grader (evalplus), and a token canvas that is not grammar-constrained. Include an AR execution-guided self-debug reference arm -- cheap, since a matched Qwen2.5-Coder AR baseline is already being built on .104 -- and report edit locality (tokens changed, spans touched) alongside pass@1, using CDC's locality metrics, so the diffusion-specific claim is in-place span repair without prefix regeneration rather than a vague appeal to bidirectionality.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It pre-empts the two most likely reviewer objections at once ('syntax-tree diffusion already did execution feedback' and 'AR self-debugging already localizes with tracebacks') by making the transfer and the AR comparison explicit measurements rather than hand-waves, and it gives the paper a defensible mechanism claim tied to a number (edit locality) instead of an architectural intuition.

diff.verification_notes: Could NOT verify, and the candidate's framing must change accordingly. (1) The candidate's premise that "every one of these localizes with model-internal confidence" and that the signal-vs-primitive question is untested is NOT accurate: CDLM (arXiv:2512.15596, v1 2025-12-17, PRE-CUTOFF) already argues standard MDLM training fails to make confidence discriminative about visible errors and builds an executable Code Revision Benchmark to measure error localization; and CORE (arXiv:2602.04096, ICML 2026 verified via OpenReview, v1 2026-02-04, PRE-CUTOFF) already replaces confidence with context-perturbation sensitivity while keeping the remask primitive and reports beating compute-matched baselines by up to +9.2pp on MBPP. So "the null is about the signal, not the primitive" is pre-cutoff prior art. This does not warrant dropping the candidate (neither uses execution, neither runs a random control, neither reports an end-to-end oracle ceiling, neither is on a code-specialised instruct model with EvalPlus), but the claim must be restated as an external-ground-truth instantiation plus missing-controls repair, not as a novel diagnosis. (2) The candidate cites 2604.18738 (T2M) and 2605.26436 (Targeted Remasking) as two supporting works; 2605.26436 was WITHDRAWN by its own authors with a comment stating it is superseded by 2604.18738. They are one work and must not be double-counted. (3) Also missed by the candidate and pre-cutoff at a top venue: arXiv:2405.20519 Diffusion On Syntax Trees (ICLR 2025 Spotlight, verified via OpenReview) already does diffusion program editing with execution feedback, in an inverse-graphics DSL setting -- it does not preempt the pretrained-masked-dLLM instantiation but it must be cited. (4) The candidate's "why_now" asserts 2606.12232 "runs no random-remask control" -- confirmed correct from the PDF -- but its claim that the paper "holds the localization signal fixed at model confidence throughout" needs one nuance I verified: the paper DOES compute an oracle leave-one-out confidence upper bound (§3.2, Fig 2) and a spatial/temporal neighbour-expansion ablation (App B.2). Our differentiation must therefore be precise: their oracle is over CONFIDENCE, not over CORRECTNESS. (5) CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, concurrent) partially preempts the compute-accounting contribution: it already standardises ACTUAL NFE across 7 remasking strategies including a `random` strategy, and already reports a nominal-vs-compute-matched reversal on HumanEval. blocking_gaps: THE HEADLINE CLAIM IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE, MEASURED. I ran the execution signal on the real r2 solutions. HE+ (n=164): 48 failures, 45 parseable; when executed on base_input, 38/45 raise NO EXCEPTION AT ALL (silent wrong answer) — only 6/45 produce a traceback frame inside the candidate. So A3's traceback->AST->span chain FIRES ON 6/164 = 3.66% OF TASKS. Even repairing all 6 gives +3.66 pts. The candidate's own kill criterion demands beating A1 AND A2 by >7.65 pts (HE+) / >5.04 (MBPP+). The study is pre-killed by its own threshold before a single arm is run.

MBPP+'s APPARENT SIGNAL IS A SELF-ASSERT ARTIFACT — this is retraction-2 shaped. MBPP+ shows 40/115 localizable frames, which looks workable, but 37 of those 40 are AssertionError, and 98/115 failing solutions contain the model's OWN self-written `assert` lines (e.g. Mbpp/103 ends `assert eulerian_num(3, 1) == 4`). The 'failing assertion' A3 would localize is the model's own test code, not the bug. I measured the zero-model-call baseline: deleting those asserts flips 41/115 to base-pass (+10.85 pts of apparent free gain). An execution-localized remasker would bank that and report it as localization working. Genuine non-assert localizable failures: 3/115 = +0.79 pts max.

THE DESIGNATED CEILING ARM IS NOT AN ORACLE — it fails its own construct-validity test. `oracle-diff-span` (difflib vs evalplus canonical_solution, exactly as specified) covers a MEDIAN 89.6% of solution tokens on HE+ failures; 0% of failures have a <=10% span, 89% have >80%. I ran it: oracle-diff remask repairs 0/45, and random remask at the same budget also 0/45. Then the control that settles it: median diff span is 89.2% on PASSING solutions vs 89.6% on FAILING — separation +0.4 pts. The diff measures STYLISTIC divergence from the reference, not error location, so it cannot bound localization headroom. The kill criterion 'killed if the oracle fails to beat A0' is therefore already satisfied by an invalid instrument.

FIXED-SPAN REMASK CANNOT EXPRESS THE FIX. 45/45 (100%) of HE+ failing candidates differ in LENGTH from the canonical solution, median +137 tokens. A same-length span remask cannot reach a correct program for any of them. Length-elastic repair is the operator that could — and DreamOn is already being evaluated on .73.

evalplus 0.3.1 `untrusted_check` RETURNS NO TRACEBACK. Verified signature: `-> Tuple[str, np.ndarray]`, i.e. (status_string, per-input boolean array). It executes in a separate `multiprocessing.Process` and communicates via `Array('b',...)`; the exception is consumed inside `unsafe_execute` and never crosses the process boundary. Wrong-answer failures assert inside evalplus's own harness, not in candidate code. A3 needs a bespoke instrumented runner (I wrote a throwaway one for this audit) — the assets_needed line implies the grader supplies this, and it does not.

THE 'NEEDS WRITING' LIST IS STALE — the canvas-level remask operator already exists and works. `scripts/pilot_oracle.py`, `pilot_repair.py`, `pilot_mut_k1.py`, `pilot_mech.py`, `pilot_typed.py`, `test_remask.py`, `test_localize.py`, `test_batchloo.py`, `test_multiregion.py` (all untracked, `git status` shows `??`, mtime today 12:01) already implement true canvas-level remask, strided batched leave-one-out confidence, oracle-diff holes, and random controls. feas.concrete_plan:
DO NOT RUN THE FOUR-ARM STUDY AS SPECIFIED. Its kill criterion is met before launch and its ceiling arm is an invalid instrument (evidence above, all measured this session). Two of my probes also produced the paper's actual finding, so the pivot is nearly done rather than speculative.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENTS ALREADY ESTABLISH (the reframed contribution):
The signal-vs-capability question 2606.12232 left open is ANSWERABLE and I answered half of it in ~1 GPU-hour. Capability is FINE; localizability is the binding constraint.
  (a) Operator capability, perfect localization, injected single-token semantic bugs (`>`->`<` etc., each verified to actually break the task): repaired 24/25 (96%) at k=1, 25/25 (100%) at k=2, 25/25 (100%) at k=4. No preservation bias, no flip-flop ceiling, at a code-specialised backbone. This CONTRADICTS the capability reading of 2606.12232's 85-95% flip-flop and D3IM's preservation bias.
  (b) Natural errors are not span-localizable AT ALL: 0/45 HE+ and 0/115 MBPP+ natural failures have a <=10% oracle-diff span; median 89.6%; passing-vs-failing separation +0.4 pts; 100% length mismatch (median +137 tok).
  => Conclusion: post-hoc remasking works beautifully on LOCALIZED corruption and is inapplicable to natural from-scratch failures, because natural failures are whole-program divergences, not repairable spans. This is precisely the construct-validity gap the positioning already flagged in CDLM/CRB (arXiv:2512.15596) — CRB INJECTS localized corruptions, and my (a) shows why that regime is easy and my (b) shows why it does not transfer. That is a real finding about a pre-cutoff paper, and it is robust to our method not winning.
