feas.risk: The reframed study's most likely failure is that it becomes a benchmark-characterisation result rather than a method result, and a reviewer reads it as "you showed your own idea does not apply." Mitigation is to lead with the positive, surprising half — perfect-localization repair is 96-100% at a competent code model, which directly contradicts the preservation-bias/flip-flop capability explanation that 2606.12232 and 2606.01026 converge on — and to present the natural-error collapse as the construct-validity boundary on CDLM/CRB's injected-corruption protocol. The second, subtler risk is generalising from HumanEval+/MBPP+ to "code repair": these are short from-scratch function-synthesis tasks where a failure is a wrong ALGORITHM, so whole-program divergence is expected. On a genuinely localized-defect surface (SWE-bench-style patches, HumanEvalPack/canitedit — and note data/edit/{canitedit,humanevalpack_python}.parquet ARE ALREADY ON DISK, unused) natural errors plausibly ARE span-localizable, which would flip the conclusion. Scoping the claim to from-scratch synthesis and running one canitedit slice as an external-validity probe is cheap insurance against overclaiming. Third risk: if step 2's dose-response saturates at 100% for all k, the curve carries no information and the mechanism story thins out — push k up to 32-64 and to contiguous multi-line spans until it breaks, so there is a real degradation curve rather than a ceiling.
feas.required_control:
DISCRIMINATIVE-VALIDITY CONTROL ON EVERY LOCALIZATION SIGNAL, INCLUDING THE ORACLE: before any signal is used to select tokens, run it unchanged on solutions that PASS and report the same statistic. A signal that cannot separate passing from failing code is not localizing errors. This is the exact analogue of retraction 1 (a verifier that compared nothing): the candidate's `oracle-diff-span` is a proposed CEILING, so if it is invalid every headroom-fraction number in the paper is meaningless — and it IS invalid, measured: 89.2% span on passing vs 89.6% on failing, separation +0.4 pts. Had this study run as written, "each signal captures X% of oracle headroom" would have been computed against an instrument measuring coding style. Note this control also kills the naming: it must be called "diff-vs-reference span," never "oracle," because the paper's own kill criterion keys off it.

Two paired controls, each blocking a specific already-realised failure:
(1) NEGATIVE-CONTROL / FREE-LUNCH ARM (analogue of retraction 2, a stage that silently discarded its input): for every reported gain, run a zero-model-call ablation that applies only the trivial non-neural part of the pipeline — here, deleting the model's own `assert` lines. I measured this: it flips 41/115 MBPP+ failures to base-pass, +10.85 apparent points, with zero forward passes. Any A3 number must be reported NET of it, or execution-localized remasking gets credit for deleting the model's own test code. Also report the base-only vs base+plus split, since that +10.85 collapses to +0.00 under the plus tests — a base-only number would have been a third retraction.
(2) SIGNAL-APPLICABILITY DENOMINATOR (analogue of retraction 3, an average that dropped the expensive cases): report the fraction of tasks on which the signal FIRES AT ALL alongside every mean, and never average over only the subset where it fires. Measured firing rates: 6/164 HE+ (3.66%), 3/115 non-artefact MBPP+ (0.79%). Conditioning on the fired subset would show a healthy per-case repair rate while the benchmark-level effect is bounded at +3.66 pts — the same "drop the inconvenient tasks, inflate the mean" error in a new costume.

lens.title: Protocol Variance Exceeds Method Effect: A Power Analysis of the dLLM Code-Generation Literature
lens.claim: For masked-diffusion code generation on HumanEval+/MBPP+, the variance induced by under-reported decoding protocol choices (top_p, temperature, unmasking algorithm, canvas length, chat template) is comparable to or larger than the effect sizes that recent papers report as method contributions; and HumanEval+ at n=164 is statistically underpowered for the deltas routinely claimed on it. Therefore a substantial fraction of published dLLM coding gains are not distinguishable from protocol drift.
lens.why_now: We measured +14.6 points on HumanEval from changing top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 alone, with nothing else changed (runs/*.r1 vs *_r2 preserved as the ablation). That single knob is larger than most reported method gains: DiffuCoder's coupled-GRPO reports +4.4% on EvalPlus; TreeDiff reports 13.3% *relative*; Multi-Block Editing reports a 12-benchmark average 61.45->64.24 (+2.8). CaRE (2607.24763) independently found temperature explains the MAJORITY of MAUVE variance and that compute-matched comparison reverses rankings -- but CaRE runs on OpenWebText/LM1B with MAUVE, i.e. open-ended text, not execution-graded code, and not on the HumanEval+/MBPP+ surface where the coding claims live. 2604.13413 (2026-04-15) shows dataset-level metrics attenuate non-determinism and that CODE generation is markedly more factor-sensitive than QA -- it supplies the mechanism but does no power analysis and no audit of published claims. 2606.19475 'An Experimental Analysis' surveys 8 dLLMs x 8 benchmarks and explicitly says protocol differences make comparison difficult, then reports its own numbers in NFE. So three separate 2026 papers each hold one piece and none does the code-specific power analysis. Our arXiv query for statistical power AND code generation returned literally 0 hits.
lens.experiment: Two halves. (1) VARIANCE BUDGET, measured: a factorial sweep on Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B over top_p {0.9, 0.95, 1.0} x temperature {0.0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.6} x alg {origin, maskgit_plus, topk_margin, entropy} (all four are already implemented in generation_utils.py:423-437 and our harness hardcodes alg='entropy', alg_temp=0.0 -- one line) x canvas {256, 512} x seed {3 seeds}, scored by evalplus on HE+ and MBPP+. Report the variance decomposition (which knob owns how much of the spread) in the style of 2604.13413's Factor Variance Attribution but on execution-graded pass@1+, and report the full min-max range per benchmark. Replicate the knob sensitivity on a second model family to show it is not Dream-specific -- DreamOn-v0-7B is on disk, and CoDA-1.7B or LLaDA-8B would need download. (2) POWER ANALYSIS, computed and already in hand: at n=164 the 95% CI half-width is 6.12 pts at p=.20, 7.65 at p=.50, 7.01 at p=.70; at n=378 it is 4.03/5.04/4.62. The unpaired two-arm MDE at 80% power is 15.5 pts (n=164) and 10.2 pts (n=378). Cross-tabulate these against the reported deltas of ~15-20 recent dLLM coding papers to produce a table of 'claimed delta vs MDE at the n they used vs whether they reported seeds/CIs/protocol'. Deliverable: a minimal reporting checklist plus a released harness that pins every knob, and a concrete recommendation (use paired McNemar on identical task sets, report >=3 seeds, report the protocol block verbatim) with the arithmetic showing that unpaired HumanEval+ comparisons cannot resolve single-digit gains. Cheap, fully parallel across 8 GPUs, no training.
lens.assets_needed: ALL PRESENT: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B, models/DreamOn-v0-7B, data/evalplus/{humaneval,mbpp}_plus.jsonl, evalplus 0.3.1, scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py (already exposes --top-p/--temperature/--steps/--max-new-tokens/--no-chat; needs a one-line --alg passthrough), scripts/merge_evalplus_shards.py, runs/*.r1 vs runs/*_r2 (the preserved top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 natural experiment, +14.6 pts). MISSING/OPTIONAL: a second non-Dream family (LLaDA-8B or CoDA-1.7B) requires HF download through the hy-proxy -- without it the cross-family generality claim must be softened to Dream-family-only, which caps the ceiling. Qwen2.5-Coder-7B absent on both disks (verified) so no AR protocol-sensitivity contrast unless downloaded.
lens.kill_criterion: Killed as a headline if the total protocol-induced spread on HE+ pass@1+ is small (say <5 pts) once temperature is fixed at 0 -- i.e. if our +14.6 was a one-off interaction with a specific temperature rather than a general sensitivity. Also killed if the audit finds most surveyed papers DO already pin and report the knobs and DO report seeds/CIs, making the reporting-gap claim empirically false; that is a real possibility for the stronger 2026 venues and must be counted honestly rather than cherry-picked. Downgraded to workshop if it reduces to 'we re-derived CaRE's temperature finding on a code benchmark', with no independent power-analysis contribution and no protocol knob outside CaRE's stochasticity axis carrying material variance.
lens.builds_on: Primary: arXiv:2604.13413 'Dataset-Level Metrics Attenuate Non-Determinism' (2026-04-15), which claims dataset-level aggregate metrics hide sample-level instability and that code generation is more factor-sensitive than QA, and introduces Factor Variance Attribution. Its defect: it characterizes non-determinism but never converts it into a decision-relevant threshold -- there is no power analysis, no minimum detectable effect, and no confrontation with the actual deltas the literature claims, so a reader cannot use it to judge whether any specific published gain is real. Second target: arXiv:2607.24763 CaRE (2026-06-04), whose defect for our purposes is domain -- it establishes that temperature dominates variance and that compute-matching reverses rankings, but only on OpenWebText/LM1B with MAUVE, an open-ended-text setting, leaving the execution-graded code surface (where the strongest efficiency and quality claims are made, and where 2604.13413 says sensitivity is WORST) unaudited. Third: arXiv:2606.19475 'Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis' (2026-06-17) diagnoses the incomparability problem in its own abstract and then adds another set of numbers under its own protocol rather than quantifying the variance budget. We repair all three by measuring the protocol variance budget on execution-graded code and pairing it with the power arithmetic that turns it into a usable admissibility threshold. Note this candidate also audits our own work: the +14.6 pt top_p effect is ours, and our HE+ n=164 comparisons are subject to the same MDE we are about to hold others to.

related_work.citation: Chakraborty et al. (?), "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2607.24763v1
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-06-04, comment field says 'updated version'). Verified: arXiv abs page fetched directly; OpenReview api2 term/forum searches for the exact title returned NO note with this title (only unrelated ICLR 2026 submission stubs), so no verified venue acceptance. Not in DBLP-as-venue.
related_work.what_it_covers: The single closest work. Audits 7 remasking strategies on LLaDA-8B-Base + Dream-7B-Base, 4 stochasticity levels, 3 step budgets, 12 open-weight MDLMs (150M-8B). Standardizes ACTUAL NFE, enforces multi-metric reporting, explicitly controls stochasticity. Findings: (i) temperature explains majority of MAUVE variance (eta^2=0.91, dominating strategy eta^2=0.80); (ii) compute-matched comparison REVERSES published rankings; (iii) informed remasking x stochastic unmasking are in tension (-0.296 MAUVE, p=0.020, paired t, 3 seeds, bootstrap CI [0.243,0.356]). CRITICALLY, contra the candidate's framing, CaRE is NOT MAUVE/OpenWebText-only: it has an explicit HumanEval pass@1 leg (Table 11, LLaDA-8B-Base via lm-eval, n=100, 3-seed mean+/-SE) showing the same nominal-vs-compute-matched reversal on code (31.7 vs 28.3 nominal -> none matches/exceeds all at matched NFE=437). It ALSO already states the power argument verbatim: "benchmark-level binomial uncertainty at n=100 is approximately +/-4.7pp, so the 32.0 vs 31.7 within-block difference is within sampling noise."
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: HumanEval leg is a single benchmark (no HumanEval+/MBPP+, no EvalPlus extra tests), single model (LLaDA-8B-Base), n=100 not n=164/378, one axis (remasking strategy x NFE x unmask_temp). No top_p/nucleus factor (explicitly names nucleus only as a confound in ReMDM, never sweeps it), no canvas length, no chat-template factor, no unmasking-algorithm factor beyond remasking strategies, no Dream-Coder / code-specialised model. Binomial uncertainty is mentioned as a one-line caveat, never turned into an MDE/power framework, never cross-tabulated against the deltas the literature claims. Self-admits only 3 seeds and that 'numerical precision, prompt format, and sequence length also matter but produce smaller measured effects' -- an unsupported claim on our axes.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Its own headline rests on 3 seeds with df=2 paired t-tests -- exactly the underpowering it criticises; the bootstrap over 3 paired seeds is not a substitute for question-level resampling. (2) It reports 'smaller measured effects' for prompt format/sequence length without showing the measurement. (3) The HumanEval leg uses n=100 (a subsample of 164) and never explains the subsampling, and never reports question-level paired comparisons even though all arms run the identical task set. (4) Compute accounting is NFE, which the candidate's own project has already shown is not a cross-family cost unit. (5) MAUVE saturation is acknowledged as a live alternative explanation for the flagship result and not resolved.

related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-04-15, no comments field, no journal-ref). related_work.what_it_covers: The candidate's stated primary target and it holds up. LLaDA + LLaDA-1.5 (plus AR controls LLaMA-2-7B / Qwen2.5-7B) on PIQA/WinoGrande/ARC-Challenge + HumanEval/MBPP. Introduces Factor Variance Attribution FVA = sigma^2_between/(sigma^2_between+sigma^2_within). Headline: code generation is markedly more factor-sensitive than QA -- FVA 0.797/0.800 (HumanEval/MBPP, LLaDA) vs 0.494-0.601 for QA; and dataset-level aggregates hide sample-level flips.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Factor set is CFG / steps / MC / batch / hardware / precision -- it does NOT include top_p (0 hits), temperature as a live axis (its temperature Std is literally 0.0000 in the AR tables, i.e. temperature was pinned or a no-op), unmasking-algorithm choice, canvas length, or chat template. No power analysis (power=0 hits), no confidence intervals (0 hits), no MDE, no McNemar (0 hits), and no confrontation with any published delta.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Exactly the defect the candidate names: it characterises non-determinism but never converts it to a decision threshold; a reader cannot use FVA to judge whether any specific published gain is real. (2) FVA is an ANOVA-style ratio, so it is scale-free and cannot answer 'is the spread bigger than the claimed effect' -- the raw min-max spread in pass@1 points is not reported for the code tasks. (3) Reports Std/SE across configurations without question-level pairing, even though all configurations run the identical task set -- the strictly more powerful analysis was available and skipped. (4) Its own factor levels are unmotivated (CFG in {0,0.5,1,1.5,2}) so between-factor variance is partly an artefact of arbitrary level spacing -- FVA is not invariant to how wide you make each factor's grid.

related_work.citation: Wang et al., "Configuration Over Selection: Hyperparameter Sensitivity Exceeds Model Differences in Open-Source LLMs for RTL Generation", arXiv:2604.17102v1
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (cs.AR; cs.AI). Verified: arXiv abs page (v1 2026-04-18, no comments, no journal-ref) + DBLP publ API returns only 'CoRR 2026 / Informal and Other Publications'. Pre-cutoff by ~3 weeks, so it is NOT concurrent work.
related_work.what_it_covers: The nearest paper to the candidate's headline SENTENCE, and it predates the cutoff. Benchmarks 26 open-source LLMs on VerilogEval + RTLLM with synthesis-in-the-loop, then runs a 108-configuration decoding hyperparameter sweep on 3 models. Finds absolute pass-rate gaps up to 25.5% between best and worst setting for the SAME model -- 5x larger than the average spread across model families under their defaults. Spearman rho of config rankings across the two benchmark suites is near zero, i.e. optimal configs do not transfer. Concludes default-hyperparameter benchmarking confounds model capability with configuration effect.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Domain is Verilog/RTL with synthesis-in-the-loop, not Python execution-graded HumanEval+/MBPP+. Autoregressive models only -- zero diffusion models, so none of the diffusion-specific knobs (unmasking algorithm, NFE/steps, canvas length, remasking, alg_temp) are in scope. No statistical power analysis, no MDE, no CIs, no seeds reported, and no audit of published claims: it stops at 'configs vary a lot' and never asks whether specific reported gains survive. No variance decomposition attributing spread to individual knobs (only best-worst range + rank correlation).
related_work.known_defects: (1) 25.5% best-worst range is a max-minus-min over 108 configs -- an extreme-order statistic that grows with grid size and has no sampling-error correction, so the '5x larger than cross-family spread' comparison is between two statistics with different estimator bias. (2) No seeds / no CIs, so part of the 25.5% is irreducible sampling noise rather than configuration effect. (3) Near-zero Spearman rho across suites is reported without a null distribution -- with 108 noisy configs, rho near zero is what pure noise predicts, so 'configs do not transfer' and 'the ranking is unmeasurable' are not distinguished. (4) Only 3 models get the sweep, so 'configuration over selection' is generalised from a 3-model base to a 26-model landscape.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (abstract, submission history, subjects, comments, jref all read) + DBLP publ API venue/type lookup. Found via targeted arXiv query all:"decoding configuration" AND all:"pass rate" AND all:"benchmark", confirmed unique by all:"exceeds model differences" (1 hit).

related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical methodological source for the candidate's half (2). diff.differentiation_statement: No pre-2026-05-07 paper makes this claim with this method in this setting, so nothing preempts the candidate; but the framing in the proposal materially overstates the gap and must be rewritten before submission. Two corrections are load-bearing. First, CaRE (2607.24763, concurrent) is NOT confined to MAUVE on OpenWebText/LM1B: it has an explicit HumanEval pass@1 leg and it already prints the power argument almost verbatim -- "benchmark-level binomial uncertainty at n=100 is approximately +/-4.7pp, so the 32.0 vs 31.7 within-block difference is within sampling noise." The candidate therefore cannot claim to be the first to note that dLLM code deltas fall inside the noise band. Second, the closest paper to the candidate's headline sentence is arXiv:2604.17102 "Configuration Over Selection: Hyperparameter Sensitivity Exceeds Model Differences," first public 2026-04-18 -- three weeks BEFORE the cutoff and therefore genuine prior art on the claim shape: a 108-configuration decoding sweep showing up to 25.5 points of within-model spread, 5x the cross-family spread under defaults, with non-transferring optima. What remains ours is a specific and defensible quadrilateral that no single paper occupies. (a) Surface: execution-graded EvalPlus pass@1+ on HumanEval+ (n=164) and MBPP+ (n=378) with the extra tests -- CaRE uses raw HumanEval at n=100, 2604.13413 uses raw HumanEval/MBPP (EvalPlus appears zero times in its text), 2604.17102 uses Verilog with synthesis-in-the-loop, and 2502.17450 uses Java via a closed API. (b) Factor set: top_p, unmasking algorithm (origin / maskgit_plus / topk_margin / entropy, all four present in generation_utils.py:425-437 and all four currently hardcoded away by our harness), canvas length, and chat template. None of these four appears as a swept axis in any of the three dLLM protocol papers -- 2604.13413 sweeps CFG/steps/MC/batch/hardware/precision with top_p absent and its temperature Std literally 0.0000; CaRE sweeps remasking strategy x steps x unmask_temp and names nucleus sampling only as somebody else's confound. (c) Model family: Dream-Coder, a code-SPECIALISED masked diffusion model, whereas every protocol-audit paper above uses general-purpose LLaDA/Dream base checkpoints -- and 2604.13413's own headline is that code sensitivity exceeds QA sensitivity, so the code-specialised checkpoint is the highest-leverage untested case. (d) Analysis: converting spread into an admissibility threshold. 2604.13413's FVA is a scale-free variance ratio that cannot answer "is the spread larger than the claimed effect"; Miller's MDE formula (2411.00640) supplies the arithmetic but instantiates it only on fictional models; Card et al. (EMNLP 2020) supply the meta-analytic genre but pre-date generative code eval and ignore decoding variance entirely. Joining protocol variance to question-level paired MDEs on execution-graded code, and then cross-tabulating against the deltas the dLLM coding literature actually claims, is the unoccupied cell.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2606.12232 Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models (ICML 2026 SPIGM + AdaptFM workshops, verified on OpenReview)
followup_openings.defect: It reports its central null result as bare single-number deltas -- 'delta BL32 = +1.2' on HumanEval, '+0.0' on MBPP for LLaDA, '+1.2 / +0.0' for Dream -- on n=164/500-scale raw benchmarks with no confidence intervals and, outside one dUltra figure, no seeds. Its own null is therefore underpowered to exactly the degree it criticises WINO for. It also compares Pareto frontiers by best-per-arm points, an optimistic-selection statistic.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run the WINO-vs-Fast-dLLM contrast on Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B over HumanEval+/MBPP+ (n=164/378, EvalPlus extra tests) with question-level PAIRED McNemar on the identical task set plus 3 seeds, and report the MDE the design can actually resolve. This converts 'gains are marginal and setting-dependent' from an eyeballed observation into a bounded null: we can state the largest true effect the data excludes. We have the harness and the arms already run; the only new machinery is paired scoring.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the single most tractable and highest-standing repair available. A workshop paper's null result becomes a properly-powered, citable equivalence claim on the flagship code surface, and it validates the candidate's checklist on a live case rather than a hypothetical. It also directly answers the kill-criterion worry, because it produces a real number either way.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2607.24763 CaRE (concurrent, 2026-06-04)
followup_openings.defect: The HumanEval leg is a single benchmark, single model (LLaDA-8B-Base), n=100 (an unexplained subsample of 164), raw HumanEval without EvalPlus extra tests, and one factor family (remasking strategy x nominal-vs-matched NFE x unmask_temp). It states the binomial-noise caveat in a sentence and then never operationalises it, and it explicitly asserts that 'prompt format and sequence length also matter but produce smaller measured effects' WITHOUT showing that measurement. Its own headline rests on 3 seeds with df=2 paired t-tests over seeds rather than question-level resampling.
followup_openings.our_fix: Measure the effects CaRE waved away. Sweep exactly the axes it declared minor -- chat template (its 'prompt format') and canvas length (its 'sequence length') -- plus top_p and unmasking algorithm, on HumanEval+/MBPP+ with the extra tests, at n=164/378, on a code-specialised checkpoint. If those axes carry material variance, we have falsified a stated claim of a concurrent protocol-setting paper with its own preferred style of evidence; if they do not, we have supplied the missing measurement and CaRE's protocol gets stronger. Separately, replace CaRE's seed-level t-tests with question-level paired tests on the identical task set -- strictly more powerful and free.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Falsifying or confirming a named, unmeasured side-claim in the field's would-be standard protocol is a clean contribution that does not require out-scaling anyone. It also converts CaRE from a competitor into a foundation we extend, which is the easier review story given it is concurrent and cannot preempt us.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2604.13413 Dataset-Level Metrics Attenuate Non-Determinism (concurrent, 2026-04-15)
followup_openings.defect: FVA = sigma2_between/(sigma2_between+sigma2_within) is scale-free, so a reader cannot compare it to any claimed effect size; the raw min-max spread in pass@1 points is never reported for the code tasks. Worse, FVA is not invariant to grid width -- widening a factor's level range (CFG in {0,0.5,1,1.5,2}) mechanically inflates its between-factor variance -- so the ranking of factors partly reflects arbitrary grid choices. And despite every configuration running the identical task set, it reports Std/SE across configurations rather than question-level paired differences, discarding the available power.
followup_openings.our_fix: Report the decision-relevant statistic FVA cannot give: the absolute min-max range and interquartile range of pass@1+ in POINTS per benchmark, per knob, and demonstrate FVA's grid-width non-invariance directly by recomputing it on a narrow vs wide top_p grid over the same runs. Then add the paired analysis on the identical task set. Also test its central claim -- code more factor-sensitive than QA -- on a code-SPECIALISED model rather than general LLaDA, which is where the claim is most consequential and least tested.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Turns a descriptive statistic into an admissibility threshold, which is the stated deliverable, and adds a genuine methodological finding (FVA is grid-dependent) rather than only re-measuring on a new surface. The grid-invariance critique is cheap -- pure re-analysis of runs we would collect anyway -- and it is the kind of point reviewers of methodology papers reward.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2606.19475 Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis (concurrent, 2026-06-17)
followup_openings.defect: Its Table 2 headline is 'peak benchmark accuracy across configurations' -- a max-over-configurations estimator with no bias correction, so every AR-vs-DLM gap it reports is inflated in proportion to how large each family's configuration grid was, which is precisely the variance it diagnoses in its own abstract. It reports zero seeds and zero intervals. And its Figure 1 scales diffusion steps and context length JOINTLY at a 1:1 ratio, so neither factor is identified.
followup_openings.our_fix: Quantify the optimistic-selection bias empirically: from our factorial grid, compute E[max over k configs] minus E[single default config] as a function of k on HumanEval+/MBPP+, giving a correction curve any peak-reporting paper can be adjusted by. Separately, break the steps-x-canvas confound by crossing NFE and canvas orthogonally -- our design already does this ({256,512} canvas crossed with the step budget) whereas theirs cannot.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: The max-over-configs correction curve is a reusable, quotable artefact with immediate application to the many dLLM papers that report best-config numbers, and it strengthens the headline: it shows protocol variance does not merely add noise, it systematically inflates reported scores. Breaking the steps-canvas confound is a factual repair of a published figure.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2604.17102 Configuration Over Selection (PRE-cutoff, 2026-04-18) -- the nearest prior art on the claim shape
followup_openings.defect: Its 25.5-point best-worst range is an extreme-order statistic over 108 configs with no sampling-error correction, and it is compared against a cross-family spread computed as an average -- two statistics with different estimator bias, so the '5x larger' ratio is not apples-to-apples. It reports no seeds and no CIs, so an unknown share of the 25.5 points is irreducible noise. Its near-zero Spearman rho is reported without a null distribution, so 'optimal configs do not transfer' and 'the config ranking is unmeasurable at this n' are not distinguished. It is AR-only and RTL-only.
followup_openings.our_fix: Do the comparison it could not. (1) Decompose the observed spread into a configuration component and a sampling component using our seed replicates, so we report protocol-induced spread NET of noise rather than a raw range -- this is the estimator fix that makes the 'variance exceeds method effect' claim survive a statistician. (2) Simulate the null Spearman rho at our n by resampling, so any claimed non-transfer is tested against what noise alone produces. (3) Extend the claim shape from autoregressive RTL to masked-diffusion Python, where there are additional diffusion-only knobs (unmasking algorithm, NFE, canvas) with no AR analogue.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the pivot that keeps the candidate publishable. Positioned as-is, the headline collides with a pre-cutoff paper. Positioned as a noise-corrected, power-grounded extension into masked diffusion and execution-graded code, 2604.17102 becomes the citation that establishes the phenomenon matters while our contribution becomes the estimator and the threshold. The noise-decomposition alone is a real methodological upgrade over the prior art.

The already-measured cells point that way: of the four axes the candidate claims as its unoccupied quadrilateral, top_p delivers only 4.88 pt at T=0.0 (below the stated 5 pt kill line) and 4.3 pt at T=0.1, while the two large movers (alg 29.3 pt, temperature 21.3 pt) are both CaRE's axes. canvas and chat_template are the only genuinely unswept axes left, and they are unmeasured -- if they also come in under ~5 pt, the paper reduces to a re-measurement plus a reporting checklist. The confounding variant of the same failure: the noise floor is estimated once at T=0.1 where seeding is provably a no-op (seed1==seed2 byte-identical, seed3==unseeded reference, all four exactly 113/164), so ~0 is subtracted from every spread including high-temperature cells that have real sampling variance, and the "noise-corrected" budget is then inflated by exactly the sampling noise it claims to have removed. Second confounding route: pooling cells generated on LOCAL and on .82, where identical nominal config already differs by 75/164 solutions and 2.4 pt, so a 3-5 pt "knob effect" would be indistinguishable from which node happened to run that cell.
feas.required_control:
A POSITIVE CONTROL THAT THE NOISE-FLOOR KNOB ACTUALLY PERTURBS THE SAMPLER, ASSERTED AT SOLUTION-BYTES LEVEL AND RUN AT EVERY TEMPERATURE USED -- plus a per-cell stack fingerprint asserted equal before any two cells are differenced.

Why this is the one. The three retractions share a shape: a step that appeared to compare/carry/average something and in fact did not (verifier discarded return values; refinement discarded the scaffold draft; the mean dropped the truncated tasks). The analogue here is live and already in the data: the "3 seeds" that establish the noise floor produced byte-identical output. he_ref_seed1 and he_ref_seed2 solutions.jsonl share md5 0cc766ff89b8b47fe3f013c1a4802b4f; he_ref_seed3 shares 3f5acbbb61048b42dd4a0183bf7b4994 with the unseeded reference; content diff is 0/164 and 1/164; all four score exactly 125 base / 113 plus. Reporting "seed variance ~0, so the spread is real" from that is a control that measured nothing, and the entire noise-corrected variance budget -- the paper's headline artefact -- is that subtraction.

The control, concretely:
1. For every temperature level in the grid, run >=3 seeds and record the NUMBER OF DIFFERING SOLUTION STRINGS between seed pairs, not just pass@1. Refuse to report a zero noise floor for any cell whose seed replicates differ on 0 solutions -- that cell is deterministic by construction (T=0.1 scales logits 10x, making Categorical.sample() effectively probs.max()), and its zero must be labelled structural, not empirical. Estimate and subtract the sampling component PER TEMPERATURE, never once at the reference recipe.
2. Include the existing negative control from the .82 design (alg=origin picks positions at random, so top_p has no order channel) and require it to move less than the entropy arm -- it does: T=0.0 origin .1829 vs entropy .4756.
3. Stamp every metrics row with torch / transformers / evalplus version, GPU name, and data-file md5, and make the analysis script HARD-FAIL if two cells being differenced disagree on any fingerprint field. Re-grade every solutions.jsonl in the paper under one pinned evalplus version. Justification measured, not assumed: identical nominal config across LOCAL and .82 gives 75/164 differing solutions and .707 vs .683 under the same grader, and one unchanged solution file scores .689 vs .683 across evalplus 0.1.0.dev1 and 0.3.1 -- both larger than DiffuCoder's +4.4 claim is above zero after noise.
4. Keep scripts/merge_evalplus_shards.py --expected on every cell (it raises SystemExit on coverage mismatch and duplicate task IDs). A silently partial 5-of-8 merge is retraction #3's shape and this assertion is the existing guard; never bypass it with the older inline merge in scripts/_run_baselines_wzc1_8gpu.sh, which de-duplicates without asserting n.

lens.title: Clamping the Bidirectional Advantage: Does Any-Order Diffusion Beat Its Own Causal Ablation on Code?
lens.claim: The 'bidirectional context' advantage claimed for masked-diffusion code LMs is largely not realized on standard from-scratch code generation. We claim that clamping a masked-diffusion model to strictly left-to-right commitment order -- an intervention that removes the any-order freedom while holding weights, sampler, budget, and hardware fixed -- costs little or nothing on HumanEval+/MBPP+ from-scratch generation, and that the advantage appears only on task surfaces with genuine right-side context (infilling, multi-site edit). The scientific content is the DECOMPOSITION: bidirectional *attention* (seeing right-side context that exists) is separable from any-order *commitment* (choosing where to write), and the code-generation literature conflates them.
lens.why_now: Three 2026 papers independently pressure this from different directions and none does the clean within-model clamp on code. 2510.19990 (2025-10-22): 'for math and coding tasks, any-order algorithms often underperform or behave similarly to left-to-right sampling.' 2607.24306 PARD (2026-07-27): block-diffusion models are 'naturally more aligned with left-to-right decoding'; enforcing L2R structure IMPROVES quality. 2608.05687 (2026-08-06, three weeks old, concurrent): unconstrained any-order commitment is 'the axis of failure' on GSM8K, collapsing to answer-only on up to 90% of problems, and a frontier-gated commitment window recovers .528->.852 -- on reasoning, not code. 2607.15893 (2026-07-17) gives the mechanistic complement: a matched-architecture comparison finds DLMs beat AR at induction ONLY when both sides of the masked token are visible, and NOT when restricted to left context. 2601.13228 (A3) and 2607.26504 argue the any-order *interface* does not deliver any-order *inference*. So the pieces exist for reasoning and for mechanistic toy settings; the code-generation surface, which is where Dream-Coder/DiffuCoder/AnCoder/TreeDiff stake their motivation ('programming is non-sequential, involves back-and-forth editing'), has not had the clamp applied. Our own DLLM_RESULTS confirms the setup is fair: only AR's home turf was ever evaluated.
lens.experiment: Single-model, single-weight-set 2x2x2 with everything else pinned. Factor 1, COMMITMENT ORDER: free any-order (alg=entropy, the released default) vs strict-L2R clamp (at each step, restrict the commit candidate set to the leftmost masked position(s); implemented as a logits/selection mask over positions in the existing sampling loop -- no weight change, no retraining). Factor 2, ATTENTION VISIBILITY: full bidirectional vs causal mask (the 4D attention_mask is already plumbed to SDPA at modeling_dream.py:280-320 and 414-428, so a causal clamp is a mask substitution). Factor 3, TASK SURFACE: from-scratch generation (HE+ n=164, MBPP+ n=378) vs infilling (HumanEval-Infilling single-line and multi-line, which is DreamOn's home turf and where we have never evaluated it -- and where DreamOn reported Dream-Coder single-line 55.5 -> 92.1). Matched NFE AND matched wall-clock across all cells. The prediction that makes this falsifiable and interesting: the order x surface INTERACTION should be large -- near-zero clamp cost on from-scratch, large clamp cost on infilling -- while the main effect of order on from-scratch is ~zero. If instead the clamp is costly everywhere, the bidirectional-advantage story is vindicated and we report that. Run on both Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B and DreamOn-v0-7B (both on disk) so the claim is not single-checkpoint; DreamOn additionally lets us test whether infilling-specialised training changes the interaction. Include a token-level diagnostic: log the realized commitment order under the free sampler and measure how far it deviates from L2R (2506.20639 DiffuCoder reports models 'decide how causal their generation should be'), so we can show whether the clamp is a null because the free sampler was ALREADY nearly L2R -- which would be the cleanest possible mechanism for the null.
lens.assets_needed: PRESENT: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, models/DreamOn-v0-7B (with mask_expansion + delete_eos_token wiring already characterized in UPSTREAM_AUDIT.md), models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B, generation_utils.py with all four alg options, modeling_dream.py with attention_mask plumbed to SDPA, scripts/generate_evalplus_{dream,dreamon}.py, data/evalplus/*, evalplus 0.3.1, vendor/DreamOn (pinned commit 8a0a549) which contains the reference infilling eval harness. NEEDS WRITING: the position-restriction clamp in the sampling loop (small); the causal-mask toggle (small); an infilling eval harness -- vendor/DreamOn/eval/ has the reference implementation to port. MISSING: HumanEval-Infilling data is not in data/evalplus/ (only humaneval_plus.jsonl and mbpp_plus.jsonl) -- must be fetched via hy-proxy, and SantaCoder-FIM likewise. Qwen2.5-Coder-7B absent on both disks, so the matched-AR leg is unavailable unless downloaded (a separate agent on .104 is reportedly building an AR baseline -- coordinate, do not duplicate).
lens.kill_criterion: Killed if the L2R clamp costs a LOT on from-scratch HE+/MBPP+ (beyond the 7.65 / 5.04 pt CI half-widths, paired test) -- that would directly support the bidirectional-advantage claim and refute our hypothesis. Killed as a *decomposition* claim if the order and visibility factors turn out to be inseparable in practice (e.g. the causal-mask cell degenerates because the model was never trained under causal attention and collapses to garbage), in which case the 2x2 does not identify anything and we can only report the order clamp. Downgraded to workshop if the from-scratch null replicates 2510.19990's already-published observation without the infilling interaction leg (i.e. if HumanEval-Infilling cannot be obtained) -- the interaction IS the contribution; the null alone is a confirmation. Also note 2608.05687 is concurrent (first public 2026-08-06, well inside the 3-month window) and does not preempt us, but we must cite it and be careful to differentiate: it studies reasoning/GSM8K and proposes a fix; we study code and run the clamp as an ablation to decompose a claimed mechanism.
lens.builds_on: Primary: arXiv:2506.20639 DiffuCoder (2025-06-25) and the Dream-Coder line, which motivate diffusion for code on the grounds that 'global planning and iterative refinement features of dLLMs are particularly useful for code generation' and that dLLMs 'can decide how causal their generation should be'. The defect: the papers that stake this motivation never run the within-model clamp that would isolate it -- they compare a diffusion model to a different AR model (different weights, different training data, different tokenizer), so 'bidirectional helps' is confounded with every other difference between the two systems. The clean identification is to ablate the freedom inside one model, which nobody does on code. Secondary and closest: arXiv:2510.19990 'No Compute Left Behind' (2025-10-22) OBSERVES that any-order underperforms or matches L2R on math and code, but treats this as motivation for a different contribution (reasoning-as-infilling) rather than as a claim to establish -- it does not run a controlled order clamp, does not separate attention visibility from commitment order, and does not test the task-surface interaction. arXiv:2607.15893 (2026-07-17) supplies the mechanistic prediction we test at scale (DLM induction advantage requires two-sided visibility, vanishing under left-context-only). arXiv:2607.24306 PARD (2026-07-27) and arXiv:2608.05687 (2026-08-06, CONCURRENT) both find constrained/ordered commitment beats free commitment, on block-diffusion sampling quality and on GSM8K reasoning respectively -- convergent evidence, different surfaces, neither on code, neither decomposing visibility from order.

related_work.citation: "No Compute Left Behind: Rethinking Reasoning and Sampling with Masked Diffusion Models", arXiv:2510.19990
related_work.venue_status: Preprint / rejected. OpenReview forum 2mkYB5KUwa carries title "Rethinking reasoning with Masked Diffusion Models", venue="Submitted to ICLR 2026", venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Rejected_Submission. Semantic Scholar returned no record for the arXiv ID. NOT an accepted venue paper as of 2026-08-07.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest prior work, and closer than the candidate assumes. Appendix A Table 5 already runs a within-model, single-weight-set decoding-order ablation on HumanEval for BOTH Dream and LLaDA: rows are Left-to-right (= block size 1, i.e. exactly the strict-L2R clamp), Any-order entropy decoding, and Block any-order (8/32/64). On HumanEval, Dream scores L2R 53.65 vs pure any-order 32.92 vs block(32) 48.17 -- the clamp is not merely free, it is the BEST configuration. Table 8 is also already the candidate's proposed token-level commitment-order diagnostic on HumanEval: %-leftmost, mean distance-from-leftmost, non-EOS token count, for Block(1)/Block(32)/AO(128) x {Dream, LLaDA}. It attributes the any-order failure to EOS-first greedy collapse plus under-use of the canvas.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: (a) Sequence length 128 only and "a portion of HumanEval (n=500)" -- n=500 exceeds HumanEval's 164 problems, so the n is either samples-not-problems or mislabelled; either way not the standard 164-problem EvalPlus protocol, and 128 tokens truncates many solutions. (b) HumanEval, not HumanEval+/MBPP+ (no EvalPlus-strength tests). (c) NO MBPP/MBPP+ on the order axis. (d) NO attention-visibility factor -- bidirectional attention is never ablated, so commitment order and two-sided visibility remain fused. (e) NO infilling/right-side-context surface, hence no order x surface interaction. (f) Dream-7B, not Dream-Coder-7B or any code-specialised diffusion model. (g) No paired significance test, no CIs, no wall-clock matching.
related_work.known_defects: Order clamp entangled with EOS pathology: the paper itself says pure any-order fails partly by greedily committing low-entropy EOS early and generating fewer non-EOS tokens, so its "any-order is bad" number partly measures a length/termination bug, not an ordering effect -- an EOS-suppressed or length-matched control is missing. The L=128 budget is a hard confound for code. HumanEval without EvalPlus tests overstates all cells. n=500 on a 164-problem benchmark is unreconciled. Any-order is instantiated only as greedy entropy decoding; margin/maskgit_plus/alg_temp>0 untested, so "any-order" is really one particular sampler. The whole order study is appendix material serving a different headline (reasoning-as-infilling + MED) and gets no statistical treatment.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2025-10-22); full PDF downloaded and text-extracted, Appendix A Tables 5/7/8 read directly; OpenReview api2 notes/search returned venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Rejected_Submission; forum-notes endpoint returned 403 ChallengeRequiredError so individual reviews could not be read.

related_work.citation: "Rethinking the Generation Order of Block Diffusion Language Models" (PARD: Parallel Autoregressive Decoding), arXiv:2607.24306
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-07-27, comment: 20 pages, 15 figures, 6 tables). No OpenReview record found; S2 has no entry. Concurrent by the 2026-05-07 cutoff.
related_work.what_it_covers: Also runs a within-model order clamp on code, and also already has the diagnostic. Figure 3 compares three any-order samplers (Confidence, Margin, Entropy) against "a pure AR sampler (which always selects the leftmost masked position at each step)" -- literally the candidate's clamp -- on HumanEval Base for SDAR-8B and LLaDA. Result is model-dependent and cuts both ways: on SDAR pure AR is BEST (+1.9 over Entropy); on LLaDA pure AR is WORST (-4.2 vs Confidence/Entropy). Computes DiffuCoder's local/global AR-ness@k, reports on-diagonal commit mass (0.75 SDAR, 0.70 LLaDA within +/-2 positions), analyses Dream-7B AR bias in Appendix D.1. Table 3 shows naive multi-leftmost commitment (k=2/3/4) collapses badly.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: HumanEval/MBPP Base only (no EvalPlus+ tests). No Dream-Coder, no DreamOn, no code-specialised diffusion checkpoint. No attention-visibility factor. No infilling or any right-side-context surface. Framing is efficiency/sampler design (propose PARD), not mechanism decomposition -- the clamp is a motivating ablation, not the object of study. Shows the order effect FLIPS SIGN across model families (SDAR vs LLaDA), so neither the candidate's predicted null nor a uniform cost is safe.
related_work.known_defects: The clamp comparison confounds order with parallel width -- pure AR is 1 token/step whereas Confidence/Entropy commit variable numbers, so Figure 3 is not NFE- or wall-clock-matched (their own Table 3 proves width dominates: static leftmost k=2 loses 20.1 pts on Fast-dLLM-v2-7B, k=4 loses 46.8). Base benchmarks without EvalPlus tests. Block-diffusion models are architecturally biased toward L2R by construction, so generalising 'ordered beats free' from BDLMs to full masked-diffusion code models is unjustified -- and they never test it on a code-tuned MDM.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; full PDF downloaded and text-extracted; Figure 3 caption/body and Table 3 read directly. OpenReview api2 search returned no matching submission.

related_work.citation: "Answer First, Reason Later: Commitment Order in Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2608.05687
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-08-06, one day before this assessment). No venue. Concurrent -- does not preempt.
related_work.what_it_covers: The strongest methodological template for what the candidate wants, executed on reasoning rather than code. Logs every commitment for LLaDA-8B on GSM8K; pure any-order commits the final answer at 15-24% of trajectory and collapses to answer-only on up to 90% of problems as the canvas grows; the cause is reachability (whether the sampler may act at distant positions), not EOS beliefs (EOS pressure nearly identical across decoders at L=512); 2x2 prompt x decoder design on 250 paired problems yields interaction +34.8 pp [26.8, 42.8]; decomposes into a collapse channel and an order channel; replicates on Dream-7B and MATH-500; frontier-gated commitment recovers .528 -> .852 while preserving up to 4x parallel decoding.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Entirely reasoning: GSM8K + MATH-500. Zero code benchmarks -- grep of the full text finds no HumanEval, no MBPP, no Dream-Coder, no infilling evaluation. No attention-visibility factor (its second axis is prompt type, not causal masking). No task surface with genuine right-side context. LLaDA-8B primary, Dream-7B replication only.
related_work.known_defects: The collapse/order decomposition is defined on a reasoning-region vs answer-region split with no clean analogue in code, so it cannot be ported mechanically. Its 2x2 crosses prompt with decoder, so the interaction is about whether CoT text exists, not whether right-side context exists -- it does not identify bidirectional visibility. n=250 paired on a single dataset for the headline interaction.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-08-06); full PDF downloaded, text extracted, grepped for HumanEval/MBPP/code/Dream-Coder/infill -- no code-benchmark evaluation present. OpenReview search returned no record.

related_work.citation: "Induction in Both Directions: A Mechanistic Analysis of In-Context Learning in Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2607.15893
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 2026-07-17, v2 2026-07-20). No OpenReview record found. Concurrent.
related_work.what_it_covers: Supplies exactly the mechanistic prediction the candidate proposes to test at scale, and is the one paper that DOES separate visibility from order. Matched-architecture attention-only AR vs absorbing-mask DLM; finds a direction-symmetric bidirectional induction circuit; critically: "When only left context is visible, matching what an AR model sees, the DLM does not outperform its AR counterpart in induction capabilities. However... stronger induction when both sides of the masked token are visible." Also gives causal evidence DLMs compute global mask fraction as an implicit timestep.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Toy scale by design -- d_model=512, 16 heads, small models chosen explicitly to enable circuit-level causal analysis; the paper itself flags extrapolation to large-scale DLMs as open. Synthetic induction/copying task, not code, no real benchmark. No decoding-order factor at all (it manipulates what is visible, never where the sampler may commit). No 7B checkpoint, no EvalPlus.
related_work.known_defects: External validity is the whole gap: an induction-head result on a 512-dim attention-only model licenses no quantitative prediction about Dream-Coder-7B on HumanEval+. Its "left context only" condition is a training/architecture condition, not an inference-time mask swap on a bidirectionally-trained model -- so it does NOT tell us whether swapping in a causal mask at inference on a bidirectionally-trained 7B degrades gracefully or produces garbage, which is precisely the candidate's stated kill risk.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + abstract; full PDF downloaded and text-extracted, confirmed d_model=512/16-head scale and the explicit caveat about large-scale DLMs. OpenReview search: no hits.

related_work.citation: Gong et al., "DiffuCoder: Understanding and Improving Masked Diffusion Models for Code Generation", arXiv:2506.20639
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- verified via OpenReview api2 notes/search: venue="ICLR 2026 Poster", venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference. A separate CoRR 2025 (dblp.org/journals/CORR/2025) record also exists for the preprint.
related_work.what_it_covers: The paper the candidate targets, and source of the AR-ness apparatus. Introduces local AR-ness@k (fraction of steps extending a k-consecutive run) and global AR-ness@k (fraction of steps selecting among the k earliest remaining masked positions); documents the entropy sink causing strong causal bias under low-confidence remasking; shows AR-ness drifts across training stages; shows code has lower mean and higher variance in global AR-ness than math; shows temperature 0.2 -> 1.2 loosens position order and raises pass@10; proposes coupled-GRPO (+4.4% EvalPlus).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It never runs the intervention. AR-ness is purely observational -- it measures how L2R the free sampler happens to be, and never clamps order to test whether the residual any-order freedom is worth anything. Its causal claim ("dLLMs can decide how causal their generation should be") is supported only by correlation between temperature, AR-ness, and pass@k. No causal-attention ablation. No infilling evaluation. Improvement is credited to coupled-GRPO, not to any measured use of bidirectionality.
related_work.known_defects: The target defect: the motivating claim that bidirectional/any-order generation helps code rests on (i) cross-system comparison against different AR models with different weights/data/tokenizers and (ii) an observational AR-ness statistic -- never a within-model clamp. The temperature -> AR-ness -> pass@10 chain is doubly confounded: raising temperature changes token choice AND position choice AND diversity, and pass@10 rewards diversity per se, so higher pass@10 at T=1.2 is not evidence that any-order commitment helped. Our own local measurement shows how fragile this axis is: top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 alone moved HumanEval +14.6 points, larger than most published diffusion-LM method gains.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; full PDF downloaded and text-extracted (AR-ness definitions Sec 4.1, entropy sink Sec 4.2, temperature/pass@k Fig 5-6); OpenReview api2 notes/search returned the ICLR 2026 Poster record with venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference.

related_work.citation: Ye et al., "Dream-Coder 7B: An Open Diffusion Language Model for Code", arXiv:2509.01142
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2025-09-01); no OpenReview/venue record located.
related_work.what_it_covers: The primary checkpoint and primary motivational claim under test. Advertises "emergent any-order generation": the model "adaptively determines its decoding strategy based on the coding task: sketch-first generation for complex algorithms, left-to-right generation for straightforward completions, and interleaved reasoning generation for code understanding tasks." Reports 21.4% LiveCodeBench pass@1 plus HumanEval/MBPP/BigCodeBench/CRUXEval.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The adaptive-order claim is illustrated by qualitative decoding-trajectory examples, not by an ablation showing the adaptivity is load-bearing. No experiment removes the any-order freedom and reports the resulting benchmark cost. No infilling evaluation despite the strongest a-priori case for bidirectionality being infilling. No causal-attention ablation.
related_work.known_defects: The headline mechanism (task-adaptive decoding order) is entirely unfalsified: strategy labels are assigned post hoc from trajectory visualisations, with no clamp, no per-task order statistic tied to per-task accuracy, and no control for the possibility that the free sampler is already near-L2R on the tasks it solves. Cleanest available target for a repair.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + full abstract (v1 2025-09-01). Checkpoint present locally at models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B with generation_utils.py and modeling_dream.py inspected directly.

related_work.citation: Xie et al., "DreamOn: Diffusion Language Models For Code Infilling Beyond Fixed-size Canvas", arXiv:2602.01326
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- verified via OpenReview api2 notes/search: venue="ICLR 2026 Poster", venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference. arXiv comment field also reads "ICLR 2026".
related_work.what_it_covers: Owns the infilling leg's home turf and supplies reference numbers. Evaluates HumanEval-Infilling single-line and multi-line plus SantaCoder-FIM (Python) against Qwen2.5-Coder-7B / DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B / Seed-Coder-8B. Dream-Coder-7B single-line 55.5 -> DreamOn 92.1 (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B 92.6); multi-line 43.2 -> 63.8 (Qwen 58.7); SantaCoder-FIM 59.3 -> 79.0 (Qwen 79.8). Ships mask_expansion + delete_eos_token wiring and the eval harness, vendored locally at vendor/DreamOn (pinned 8a0a549).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No compute/NFE accounting anywhere -- infilling scores reported without step budgets or wall-clock, so 55.5 -> 92.1 is not compute-matched. No RandomSpanInfilling split. No multi-span / multi-site edit. Python only. And no decoding-order ablation: it never asks whether the infilling gain requires any-order commitment or merely two-sided visibility.
related_work.known_defects: The missing cost accounting is the exploitable defect and it is the same error class as our own three retractions: an uncosted quality gain is not a frontier claim. Dream-Coder's 55.5 single-line baseline is a from-scratch-style model evaluated on an infilling interface it was not specialised for, which flatters the DreamOn delta. The absent RandomSpan split is the split most sensitive to where the model must place tokens (positional uncertainty), i.e. exactly where the order factor should bite hardest.

related_work.citation: "Autoregressive Models Rival Diffusion Models at ANY-ORDER Generation" (A3: Any-order Any-subset Autoregressive modeling), arXiv:2601.13228
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- verified via OpenReview api2 notes/search: venue="ICLR 2026 Poster", venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference.
related_work.what_it_covers: Argues the any-order interface does not require the diffusion formulation: reformulates diffusion-style training as structured multi-group AR prediction (two-stream attention + progressive adaptation from a pretrained AR model), reporting A3 outperforming diffusion baselines on QA, commonsense reasoning, and story infilling while retaining flexible decoding.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No code generation benchmark. Story infilling, not code infilling. It replaces the model rather than ablating a fixed one, so it cannot isolate what the any-order freedom buys inside a given released checkpoint. No attention-visibility factor.
related_work.known_defects: Comparisons are across differently-trained systems (A3 vs diffusion baselines), the exact cross-system confound our candidate is designed to eliminate -- so 'AR rivals diffusion at any-order' inherits every weight/data/objective difference. related_work.citation: Kim et al., "From Interface to Inference: Eliciting Any-Order Inference from Any-Order Models", arXiv:2607.26504
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 2026-07-29). No OpenReview record found. Concurrent.
related_work.what_it_covers: Names and diagnoses the interface-inference gap: the any-order training objective yields an any-order prediction interface but not any-order inference, because of positional uncertainty -- fixed-canvas token-level models "may know what semantic component should appear without knowing where to place it." Proposes insertion-based masked diffusion (building on FlexMDM) and latent-space masked diffusion; trains a 7B FlexMDM for Python coding and a 125M LatentMDM for GSM8K. Code released.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Fixes the gap by changing the model (insertions, latent segments) rather than measuring what the gap costs in a released fixed-canvas checkpoint. No order clamp on Dream-Coder/DreamOn. No attention-visibility ablation. No HumanEval-Infilling task-surface interaction. Its motivating premise -- that code is 'inherently non-causal' -- is asserted from the programmer-workflow analogy, not measured.
related_work.known_defects: Its central premise is exactly what our clamp tests and what 2510.19990 Table 5 already partially contradicts on HumanEval; the paper never runs the negative control that would establish code is non-causal for the model (as opposed to for the human). Two heterogeneous scales (7B coding vs 125M GSM8K) make the two proposed approaches non-comparable to each other.

related_work.citation: "Neither Parallel Nor Sequential: How DiffusionGemma Actually Commits Tokens", arXiv:2606.14620
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 2026-06-12). No OpenReview record found. Concurrent.
related_work.what_it_covers: Pre-empts a large part of the candidate's proposed order DIAGNOSTIC and supplies the measurement-validity hazards. Instruments DiffusionGemma-26B's accept step over a 686-prompt six-regime probe; finds a partial L2R commit bias whose apparent strength depends almost entirely on analysis granularity, so 'block size' is an artifact of the measuring ruler; finds large simultaneous commit batches leaving within-batch order genuinely undefined; finds regime dependence (structured JSON committed in essentially arbitrary order); notes accuracy matches the AR Gemma-4 sibling. Its stated central contribution is methodological: honest order measurement must handle trailing-EOS padding, within-regime confounding, commit non-monotonicity, block-size sensitivity, and large commit-batch ties, each of which can otherwise manufacture a decoding-order result that is not really there.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Closed-weight-family single checkpoint (DiffusionGemma-26B); no code benchmark suite scored with EvalPlus; purely observational -- no clamp, no intervention, no attention-visibility factor, no task-surface interaction.
related_work.known_defects: Descriptive only: having established that free decoding is partially L2R, it never asks what the residual freedom is worth, which is the interventional step. But its five listed artifacts are a direct threat to the candidate's proposed diagnostic -- in particular commit-batch ties and trailing-EOS padding would let us report a spurious 'the free sampler was already L2R' mechanism. We must adopt its protocol, not reinvent one.

related_work.citation: Zhang et al., "Beyond Autoregression: An Empirical Study of Diffusion Large Language Models for Code Generation", arXiv:2509.11252
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 2025-09-14, v2 2025-11-02). No OpenReview/venue record located.
related_work.what_it_covers: The existing broad empirical study of diffusion LLMs for code -- 9 diffusion LLMs, 4 benchmarks. States the exact motivation the candidate targets: "programming is a non-sequential process involving back-and-forth editing, while autoregressive LLMs only employ the left-to-right generation order," and lists flexible generation order as one of two advances. Finds diffusion LLMs merely competitive with similar-size AR models, with better length extrapolation and long-code understanding.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Despite spanning 9 models it runs no order clamp and no visibility ablation: 'flexible generation order' is assumed as an architectural affordance and never tested as a causal contributor. No infilling/edit surface. Its own headline (competitive, not better) already undercuts the motivation it repeats.
related_work.known_defects: A 9-model x 4-benchmark study that asserts the back-and-forth-editing rationale and then evaluates only left-to-right from-scratch generation is the same scoping failure we self-diagnosed locally -- it measures diffusion exclusively on AR's home turf. Cross-model comparisons are again cross-system (different weights/data/tokenizers).

related_work.citation: "Masks Can Be Distracting: On Context Comprehension in Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2511.21338
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (v1 2025-11-26, v2 2026-06-04). No OpenReview/venue record located.
related_work.what_it_covers: Directly relevant confound for the candidate's visibility factor: shows that despite bidirectional attention MDLMs exhibit a strong locality bias like ARLMs, and that appending the large number of mask tokens required for generation significantly degrades context comprehension -- masks act as distractors. Introduces a mask-agnostic loss to mitigate.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Context-comprehension/understanding tasks, not code generation and not decoding order. Does not swap attention masks at inference.
related_work.known_defects: Important implication for us: canvas length is a live nuisance variable for any bidirectional-advantage claim, because the right-side 'context' in from-scratch generation is mostly MASK tokens which actively hurt. Any clean from-scratch-vs-infilling contrast must hold canvas length fixed, or the surface effect is confounded with mask-count distraction.

diff.differentiation_statement: Two papers -- one pre-cutoff, one concurrent -- already perform a within-model left-to-right order clamp on code, so the candidate's stated core intervention is NOT new and its predicted null is partly already published. 2510.19990 (v1 2025-10-22, pre-cutoff) Appendix A Table 5 clamps Dream and LLaDA to block-size-1 L2R on HumanEval and finds L2R is not merely free but the BEST configuration for Dream (53.65 vs 32.92 pure any-order); its Table 8 already reports the proposed %-leftmost / distance-from-leftmost commitment diagnostic on HumanEval. Concurrent PARD (2607.24306) Figure 3 runs the same pure-leftmost clamp on HumanEval for SDAR and LLaDA. What no paper has done -- and what this candidate should be rebuilt around -- is the DECOMPOSITION plus the TASK-SURFACE INTERACTION under a common cost unit. Specifically: (1) no work crosses commitment order with attention visibility, so any-order commitment and two-sided visibility remain fused throughout the code literature; 2607.15893 separates them but only at d_model=512 on a synthetic induction task and explicitly flags large-scale extrapolation as open. (2) No work runs the order clamp on a code-specialised diffusion checkpoint: 2510.19990 uses Dream-7B and LLaDA, PARD uses SDAR/Fast-dLLM-v2/LLaDA2.1-Mini; Dream-Coder-7B and DreamOn-v0-7B -- the two models whose papers actually stake the "programming is non-sequential" motivation -- have never been clamped. (3) No work crosses order with task surface: every clamp lives on from-scratch generation only, so the one surface with genuine right-side context (infilling) is untested, and DreamOn's own infilling numbers carry no compute accounting at all. (4) Every existing clamp uses HumanEval/MBPP Base at L=128 with n reported as 500 on a 164-problem benchmark, whereas we run HumanEval+/MBPP+ (n=164/378) under evalplus untrusted_check with paired tests and matched NFE and matched wall-clock -- and our measured 512-vs-1024-NFE zero gain plus 94%->1.8% unparseable-rate curve shows the L=128 budget in prior work truncates the regime where these models actually work. (5) Concurrent 2608.05687 supplies the methodological template (commitment logging, 2x2, paired CIs, channel decomposition) but is reasoning-only -- grepping its full text finds no HumanEval, MBPP, Dream-Coder, or infilling evaluation -- so porting that template to code with a visibility axis added is differentiated, not a reproduction. One factual correction that materially improves the candidate: HumanEval-Infilling is NOT missing. All three splits are already on disk at data/infilling/ -- SingleLine (1033), MultiLine (5815), RandomSpan (1640) -- and RandomSpan is a split DreamOn did not evaluate. The interaction leg, which the candidate itself calls "the contribution", is fully unblocked and the stated workshop-downgrade risk is void.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2510.19990 (No Compute Left Behind), Appendix A Tables 5 and 8 -- pre-cutoff, ICLR 2026 Rejected Submission
followup_openings.defect: The published order clamp on code is an appendix side-result with four fatal protocol limits: L=128 generation budget; HumanEval only with Base tests rather than EvalPlus (and an unreconciled 'n=500' on a 164-problem benchmark); no MBPP on the order axis; and the any-order arm is confounded with an EOS pathology the authors themselves describe (pure any-order commits low-entropy EOS early and produces fewer non-EOS tokens), so the reported any-order deficit partly measures a termination/length bug rather than an ordering effect. No CIs, no paired tests.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run the clamp at protocol strength in our measured regime: HumanEval+ (n=164) and MBPP+ (n=378) graded by evalplus untrusted_check, at NFE 512 where we established the model is saturated (512 -> 1024 gives exactly 0.000 gain) rather than L=128 which truncates it; paired per-problem tests against our measured 7.65 / 5.04 pt CI half-widths; and add the EOS-suppressed and length-matched control arms that separate the ordering effect from the termination collapse. Sweep the alternative any-order samplers (maskgit_plus, topk_margin, entropy, alg_temp>0) that generation_utils.py already exposes, so 'any-order' is not silently instantiated as one greedy entropy sampler.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Converts a widely-cited appendix observation into a properly-powered result on the standard benchmark of record, and tells the field whether 'any-order hurts code' is an ordering fact or an EOS-collapse artifact -- which changes what practitioners should fix.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2506.20639 DiffuCoder (ICLR 2026 Poster) and arXiv:2509.01142 Dream-Coder 7B
followup_openings.defect: Both stake the bidirectional/any-order motivation for code and neither tests it causally inside one model. DiffuCoder's AR-ness metrics are purely observational, and its causal-sounding claim that dLLMs 'decide how causal their generation should be' rests on a temperature 0.2 -> 1.2 sweep that simultaneously changes token choice, position choice, and output diversity, evaluated by pass@10 which rewards diversity per se. Dream-Coder's 'sketch-first vs left-to-right vs interleaved, adaptively chosen per task' claim is supported only by post-hoc trajectory visualisations, with no ablation showing the adaptivity is load-bearing.
followup_openings.our_fix: Apply the clamp to the two checkpoints that actually make the claim (Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B and DreamOn-v0-7B, both on disk), holding weights, sampler, temperature, top_p, NFE and wall-clock fixed, and report cost in EvalPlus points. Decompose DiffuCoder's temperature confound: at fixed temperature vary only commitment order; at fixed order vary only temperature. Falsify Dream-Coder's adaptivity claim quantitatively by computing per-task AR-ness under the free sampler and testing whether per-task clamp cost is predicted by per-task AR-ness -- if the free sampler is already near-L2R on the tasks it solves, the adaptive-order story is decorative.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: The motivation for an entire subfield of code-diffusion work rests on a cross-system comparison plus an observational statistic. A within-model clamp on the exact checkpoints that make the claim is the identification these papers owe the reader, and our local sampler audit (top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 alone moved HumanEval +14.6 points, larger than most published diffusion-LM method gains) shows how easily this axis manufactures effects.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2602.01326 DreamOn (ICLR 2026 Poster)
followup_openings.defect: The headline infilling gains (Dream-Coder single-line 55.5 -> 92.1; multi-line 43.2 -> 63.8; SantaCoder-FIM 59.3 -> 79.0) are reported with no compute or NFE accounting whatsoever, so they are quality claims masquerading as capability claims. RandomSpanInfilling -- the split most sensitive to positional uncertainty, i.e. where the model must decide where to place tokens -- is omitted, as is any multi-span setting; Python only.
followup_openings.our_fix: Score the infilling leg with matched NFE and matched wall-clock using the vendored reference harness at vendor/DreamOn/eval/ (pinned 8a0a549, defaults already characterised: alg=entropy, alg_temp=0.0, steps=256, temperature=0.2, top_p=0.9, mask_expansion + delete_eos_token), and add the RandomSpanInfilling split already on disk (1640 items) alongside SingleLine (1033) and MultiLine (5815). Report infilling on the same token-cost axis we already built for the from-scratch Pareto figures, so infilling and from-scratch sit in one accounting.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Repairs exactly the error class we retracted three of our own results for -- an uncosted metric, and a metric that silently drops the expensive cases -- on the paper that owns the infilling surface, and adds the split where the order factor should bite hardest.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2607.15893 (Induction in Both Directions) x arXiv:2607.24306 PARD -- both concurrent
followup_openings.defect: 2607.15893's clean visibility-vs-order separation exists only at d_model=512 on a synthetic induction task, and the paper explicitly flags extrapolation to large-scale DLMs as open; moreover its 'left context only' condition is a training/architecture condition, not an inference-time mask swap on a bidirectionally-trained model, so it cannot say whether a causal-mask swap on a 7B bidirectional checkpoint degrades gracefully or collapses. PARD's clamp comparison is not NFE- or wall-clock-matched (pure AR commits 1 token/step while Confidence/Entropy commit variable numbers) and its own Table 3 shows commit width dominates: static leftmost k=2 already loses 20.1 points on Fast-dLLM-v2-7B, k=4 loses 46.8. PARD also finds the order effect FLIPS SIGN across families (pure AR best on SDAR +1.9, worst on LLaDA -4.2).
followup_openings.our_fix: Test the toy-scale prediction at 7B on real code by crossing commitment order with attention visibility in one weight set -- the causal-mask swap is a mask substitution because modeling_dream.py already plumbs a 4D additive mask to SDPA with is_causal hard-coded False (line 430) and adds the mask at lines 319-320. Critically, hold commit width fixed at 1 token/step across ALL order cells so we measure order and not width, which is where PARD's comparison is confounded; report both matched NFE and matched wall-clock. Run both Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B and DreamOn-v0-7B so the family-flip PARD observed is directly addressed rather than assumed away. Pre-register the degenerate-cell outcome: if the causal-mask cell collapses because the model never saw causal attention, that is itself the reportable finding that visibility and order are not separable by inference-time intervention in bidirectionally-trained checkpoints -- a genuine negative result about the limits of ablation-based mechanism attribution, not a failed experiment.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It is the only cell no one has run, it scales a mechanistic prediction from 512 dims to 7B on a real benchmark, and it fixes the width/order confound that makes every existing code clamp uninterpretable as an ordering result.

followup_openings.target_paper: arXiv:2606.14620 (Neither Parallel Nor Sequential) and arXiv:2511.21338 (Masks Can Be Distracting) -- measurement-validity threats to our own design
followup_openings.defect: Not defects to repair so much as traps we would otherwise fall into. 2606.14620's stated central contribution is that honest decoding-order measurement must handle trailing-EOS padding, within-regime confounding, commit non-monotonicity, block-size sensitivity, and large commit-batch ties, each of which can manufacture a decoding-order result that is not really there -- and it shows apparent L2R strength depends almost entirely on analysis granularity, so 'block size' can be an artifact of the ruler. 2511.21338 shows the large mask-token canvas required for generation itself degrades context comprehension, masks acting as distractors.
followup_openings.our_fix: Adopt 2606.14620's five-hazard protocol verbatim for our commitment-order diagnostic rather than inventing one -- report order statistics at multiple granularities, exclude trailing-EOS padding, handle ties explicitly, report commit-batch sizes -- so that a finding of 'the clamp is null because the free sampler was already near-L2R' cannot be a ruler artifact. Hold canvas length fixed across the from-scratch vs infilling contrast so the task-surface effect is not confounded with mask-count distraction per 2511.21338; if canvas cannot be matched, report the mask-count-matched control separately.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Our proposed mechanism-for-the-null (free sampler already L2R) is precisely the class of claim 2606.14620 demonstrates is easy to fabricate, and our surface contrast is precisely the class of claim 2511.21338 shows is easy to confound. Pre-empting both is what makes the interaction result survive review.
