diff.sharpened_claim: On code, the any-order commitment freedom of masked-diffusion LMs is worth approximately nothing on the surface those models are marketed for and everything on the surface they are never evaluated on -- and the two components of the advertised advantage are separately measurable. Holding one weight set, one sampler, commit width fixed at one token per step, and both NFE and wall-clock matched, we clamp commitment order to strictly left-to-right and independently clamp attention visibility to causal, on the two checkpoints whose own papers stake the "programming is non-sequential" motivation (Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, DreamOn-v0-7B), across two task surfaces (from-scratch: HumanEval+ n=164, MBPP+ n=378, evalplus untrusted_check, at the NFE-512 saturation point we measured rather than the L=128 budget prior work used; infilling: HumanEval-Infilling SingleLine/MultiLine plus the RandomSpan split DreamOn omitted, all three already on disk). The claim is the ORDER x SURFACE INTERACTION with a paired CI, not the from-scratch null -- the null is already published for Dream-7B/LLaDA at L=128 on HumanEval Base (2510.19990 Table 5, where L2R is in fact the best configuration) and for SDAR/LLaDA by concurrent PARD, so we cite it, replicate it at EvalPlus protocol strength on code-specialised checkpoints, and go past it. Two further things carry the paper independently of the interaction's sign: first, we supply the missing compute accounting for the infilling surface, where DreamOn's 55.5 -> 92.1 is reported with no NFE or wall-clock at all, placing infilling and from-scratch on one token-cost axis; second, we test at 7B on real code the toy-scale prediction of 2607.15893 that the DLM advantage requires two-sided visibility and vanishes under left-context-only, and we pre-register the degenerate outcome as reportable -- if the causal-mask cell collapses because the checkpoint never saw causal attention, then bidirectional visibility and any-order commitment are not separable by inference-time intervention in bidirectionally-trained models, a real and citable limit on ablation-based mechanism attribution rather than a failed cell. Throughout, the commitment-order diagnostic follows the five-hazard protocol of 2606.14620 (trailing-EOS padding, granularity, non-monotonicity, block-size sensitivity, commit-batch ties) so that "the clamp is null because the free sampler was already near-L2R" cannot be an artifact of the measuring ruler, and canvas length is held fixed across surfaces so the interaction is not confounded with the mask-as-distractor effect of 2511.21338.

blocking_gaps: NOT a gap but a correction that reshapes the whole candidate: Retractions 4 and 5 landed today (commit 1170ae6, DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md) and already answer this candidate's central question with the OPPOSITE framing. .73 ran the infilling leg on HumanEval-SingleLineInfilling n=1033 with a UNIDIRECTIONAL control: dream_fim (prefix+suffix) .7115 vs dream_prefix (prefix only) .4124 -- a +.299 gain from two-sided visibility on Dream-Coder itself. The candidate's predicted 'large clamp cost on infilling' interaction leg is therefore PARTLY MEASURED ALREADY, and the surviving finding is that the SAME task-framing gain appears in AR (qwen_fim .7638 vs qwen_prefix .5324, +.231), i.e. two-sided visibility is a property of the task interface, not of masked diffusion. Any writeup must start from this, not from 'nobody has evaluated infilling'.

The candidate's Factor-2 'causal-mask cell' is NOT a graceful ablation -- I ran it and the pre-registered degenerate outcome is what actually happens. On 6 HumanEval tasks at canvas=256/steps=256/T=0.1/top_p=0.95 with commit width pinned to 1: free/bidir 6/6 parseable, l2r/bidir 6/6, l2r/causal 6/6, but free/causal only 2/6, with visible corruption ('for    Check if there', docstring bleeding into code). A prefix-LM variant (prompt bidirectional, canvas causal) was WORSE: 0/2 parseable. So free x causal is not a measurable cell; the 2x2 collapses to a 3-cell design. The candidate anticipated this but priced it as a risk; it is a measured fact and must be pre-registered as the finding, not the fallback.

The proposed commitment-order diagnostic is unstable in exactly the way 2606.14620 warns, and I measured the instability. %-leftmost for the free entropy sampler on HumanEval/0 is 0.914 at canvas=256/T=0.1, 0.891 at canvas=512/T=0.1, 0.184 at canvas=256/T=0.0, and 0.033 at canvas=512/T=0.0. The T=0.0/canvas=512 cell commits EOS on 448 of 512 steps (87.5%); excluding EOS commits, %-leftmost rises 0.033 -> 0.266 and mean-distance-from-leftmost falls 249.22 -> 6.33. So 'the free sampler was already near-L2R' is true or false depending on temperature and canvas, and the T=0 number is an artifact of EOS-first collapse -- the very confound 2510.19990 has. The diagnostic is only reportable if EOS-stratified AND swept over temperature x canvas. (Good news: tie-breaking is NOT a hazard here -- only 4 of 1536 steps had argmax ties, and topk index-order vs random tie-break agreed on 99.87% of commits and gave identical %-leftmost 0.0273.)

Matched wall-clock is claimed but the clamp is not wall-clock-neutral and the candidate's 160 GPU-hour estimate ignores this. Measured on L20A at steps=512/canvas=512/T=0: native diffusion_generate 8.5-9.8 s/task; my external free/bidir loop 8.0-14.5 s; l2r/bidir 13.6-13.8 s; free/causal 18.6-19.5 s; l2r/causal 16.7-19.4 s. The causal cells are ~2x slower per task than native even though a single forward is the same cost (14.0 ms 'full' vs 14.4 ms zeros-4D vs 14.4 ms causal-4D at canvas 768), so the slowdown is materialization//broadcast of the LxL mask, not attention. Wall-clock matching must therefore be done by padding the faster arm or reported as an honest asymmetry, not asserted.

Flags: --order {free,l2r,r2l,random} --visibility {bidir,causal} --commit-width 1 --assert-native-equivalence. Cells: free/bidir, l2r/bidir, l2r/causal (free/causal recorded as degenerate, see risk). Grids: HumanEval+ n=164 and MBPP+ n=378, NFE=512, canvas=512, T=0.1 top_p=0.95, alg=entropy, alg_temp=0 -- identical to runs/dream_coder_instruct_{heplus,mbppplus}_r2 so the free/bidir cell must reproduce .707/.680. Grade with `python -m evalplus.evaluate`. Cost basis measured from runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus_r2/metrics.rank*.jsonl: 11.31 s/task HE+ (1854 GPU-s total), 10.57 s/task MBPP+ (3997 GPU-s); clamped cells run 1.5-2x slower -> ~0.5 GPU-h per (model,benchmark,cell) on L20A, ~1.5x that on H20.

STEP 3 (GPU, ~8 h) -- ORDER DIAGNOSTIC, EOS-STRATIFIED AND SWEPT. Same script, --log-commitments. Report %-leftmost and mean-distance-from-leftmost BOTH overall and excluding EOS/pad commits, at canvas in {256,512} x T in {0.0,0.1}. This is mandatory, not optional: my pilot shows the headline statistic moves 0.914 -> 0.033 across that grid purely from EOS collapse. Report commit-batch sizes and tie counts too (measured: ties are negligible, 4/1536).

STEP 4 (GPU, ~10 h) -- INFILLING ORDER LEG, REUSING .73's HARNESS. On zwfy6 add --order/--visibility to scripts/generate_infilling.py's run_dream_canvas (the fixed-canvas path is already the right shape: it pre-fills prefix + span_tokens masks + suffix). Run dream_fim x {free,l2r} x {bidir,causal} on SingleLine (n=1033) and on RandomSpan (n=1640, the split DreamOn omitted), scored by the existing scripts/score_infilling.py which delegates to evalplus untrusted_check and already has --self-test-n. Reuse the six existing arms as the visibility reference rather than re-running them. Measured cost: dream_fim was 0.393 s/task x 1033 = 406 GPU-s per arm, so all 4 order cells x 2 splits is well under 2 GPU-h.

STEP 5 (GPU, ~4 h) -- REPLICATION + POSITIVE CONTROL. Repeat Step 2's three cells on Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B (--base-continuation --add-bos-token, the protocol aligned in commit 3cef855) so the claim is not single-checkpoint. Add r2l and random order arms as the positive control (pilot: r2l 2/2 parseable, random 1/2) -- these prove the clamp mechanism can register a cost, so an l2r null is informative.

STEP 6 (no GPU, 3 h) -- PAIRED STATS. McNemar per-problem l2r vs free, plus paired bootstrap on the order x surface interaction, against the 7.65 / 5.04 pt half-widths. Report wall-clock and tokens_fed for every cell (the retraction-3 discipline: read process AND failure_process).

NODE: run Steps 2/3/5 on .73 (8x H20 idle, PROJECT_ROOT=/apdcephfs_zwfy6/.../dllm_draft_104, PYTHON=$ROOT/.venv_dream/bin/python) and Step 4 there too since Qwen2.5-Coder-7B and the infilling harness are already on that disk. Local wzc1 has GPUs 2/3/6/7 free but 0/1/5 busy; .82 and .104 are at 99% util (sampler audit, AR baseline) -- do not touch. Any new script written on wzc1 must be `scp -O`'d to zwfy6.
feas.risk:
The most likely outcome is a CONFOUNDED interaction, and I can already see its shape. Two of the three surviving cells produce a null that is over-determined: (a) the l2r/bidir clamp will be ~free on HumanEval+/MBPP+ because I measured the free entropy sampler committing leftmost on 89-91% of steps at the exact protocol we use (canvas 512, T=0.1) with mean distance-from-leftmost of 1.42 tokens -- so the clamp barely changes the realized trajectory and the "null" is nearly a tautology, not a finding about any-order freedom; and (b) the free/causal cell degenerates (2/6 parseable in pilot; prefix-LM variant 0/2), so the 2x2 never identifies the visibility x order interaction the paper is built on. That leaves only l2r/causal as an interpretable clamp, and it is a JOINT intervention, which is precisely the decomposition the candidate promised to deliver and cannot.

The second, worse failure mode is that the interaction leg gets scooped by our own repo. .73 already measured, today, that adding suffix context helps Dream-Coder +.299 AND helps Qwen2.5-Coder +.231 on the same split -- so "bidirectional visibility pays off on infilling" is a task-interface fact with no diffusion-specific content. If we run the order clamp on infilling and it too is ~free, the paper's headline reduces to "clamping order is free everywhere and clamping visibility breaks the model everywhere," which is a two-sentence negative result, i.e. workshop-scale, exactly the downgrade the positioning declared void.

Third, subtler: the order diagnostic can manufacture whichever mechanism we want. Same task, same weights, same NFE -- %-leftmost is 0.914 at (canvas 256, T=0.1) and 0.033 at (canvas 512, T=0.0), an 0.88 swing from two knobs neither of which is the intervention. If a single (canvas, T) cell is reported, the "free sampler was already L2R" mechanism is a choice, not a measurement.
feas.required_control:
TWO controls, both mandatory; the first is the direct analogue of retraction 2 (a pipeline stage that silently discarded its input) and the second of retraction 1 (a comparison that compared nothing).

CONTROL A -- NATIVE-EQUIVALENCE ASSERTION ON THE UNCLAMPED CELL. The clamp is implemented as an external re-implementation of generation_utils.py:410-455, so the whole design dies if that loop diverges from the released sampler: every "clamp cost" would then be measuring my loop versus their loop, which is retraction 2 with new labels. So the free/bidir cell must be produced by the SAME external loop with the clamp disabled, and the run must hard-assert, per task and before any scoring, that its output token ids are IDENTICAL to model.diffusion_generate at T=0 with the same seed/steps/canvas, aborting the shard on mismatch. I verified this passes today on HumanEval/0-3 (token-identical output; native 8.5-9.8 s/task vs external 8.0-14.5 s/task). Additionally assert the free/bidir cell reproduces the archived .707 / .680 from runs/dream_coder_instruct_{heplus,mbppplus}_r2 within noise -- if the unclamped arm does not land on our own published number, nothing downstream is interpretable.

CONTROL B -- ORDER-CLAMP POSITIVE CONTROL (r2l and random). An l2r null is worthless unless the instrument can detect a real ordering effect, and the instrument is easy to make inert: pin commit width to 1 and 89-91% of free commits are already leftmost, so an l2r clamp may be a near no-op by construction. Running r2l (strict rightmost) and uniform-random order under IDENTICAL weights, sampler, temperature, canvas, NFE and width=1 supplies the missing comparison: if r2l/random measurably degrade pass@1 while l2r does not, the null is a fact about L2R specifically; if all four orders score the same, the clamp is measuring nothing and the paper must be killed rather than written. Pilot indicates the control has teeth (r2l 2/2 parseable, random 1/2 -- i.e. random already shows corruption l2r does not). Pair this with the mandatory EOS-stratified, canvas x temperature-swept order diagnostic, since without stratification the "already-L2R" mechanism is a ruler artifact (0.033 -> 0.266 %-leftmost once the 87.5% EOS commits are removed).

lens.title: Structural Corruption Is Not Free: A Supervision-Density-Matched Control for AST-Guided Diffusion Training
lens.claim: Reported gains from AST-guided / structure-aware corruption in diffusion code LMs are confounded with supervision density and effective masking rate, and shrink or vanish under a control that matches the number of supervised positions per example. We claim the correct decomposition is: structural corruption changes (i) WHICH tokens are masked and (ii) HOW MANY are masked and how they cluster; prior work attributes the full gain to (i) while only (ii) is controlled by their random-masking baseline in expectation, not per-example.
lens.why_now: TreeDiff (2508.01473) claims a 13.3% RELATIVE improvement over random-token masking by masking tokens belonging to key AST nodes. AnCoder/AnchorTree (2602.17688, 2026-02-05) claims 'structurally anchored diffusion offers a parameter-efficient path to high-quality code generation' by prioritizing AST-salient tokens. Neither, per their abstracts, reports a supervision-density-matched control -- and this is exactly the confound we have hard local numbers on: our own BASELINE_STATS.md measures plain-SFT at mean 42.1 supervised masks per state (median 31) vs the hierarchical structural sampler at mean 16.3 (median 2), i.e. a 2.6x difference in mean and a 15x difference in median supervised positions, plus a 19.5% shorter mean canvas (137.6 vs 110.8). So switching to structural corruption silently changes the training signal density by a large factor, and 'AST-aware masking helps' and 'sparser, more clustered supervision helps' are not separated. My searches for masking-rate/noise-schedule ablations in masked diffusion returned 0-2 hits, none doing this control. We are unusually well-placed: scaffold_coder/corruption.py already implements the full masking machinery (RungMixtureSampler, GlobalBandSampler, HierarchicalBandSchedule, per-position band weights) and scaffold_coder/training/scaffold_sft_trainer.py is a working SFT trainer, and we have already built one matched control (plain-SFT) so we know the protocol.
lens.experiment: Three training arms from the SAME Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B init, SAME normalized 114,363-example split, SAME trainer/FSDP/batch/LR/epochs (the recipe is pinned in STAGE1_RESULTS.md: 8-way FSDP FULL_SHARD, global batch 128, micro 8/GPU, max_len 1024, 5 epochs, ~34.6 GPU-hours per arm on 8xH20): (B1) random-token masking at whatever rate the structural sampler induces -- the honest baseline; (B2) structural/AST-guided masking (the TreeDiff/AnCoder move, using our RungMixtureSampler); (B3) DENSITY-MATCHED random masking -- per example, mask the SAME NUMBER of tokens as B2 would, and match the cluster-size distribution (contiguous spans of matched length), but choose the spans at random rather than at AST boundaries. B3 is the control that isolates 'AST boundaries matter' from 'this many tokens, clustered this way, matter'. Add (B4) a shuffled-structure control: mask at AST-node boundaries drawn from a DIFFERENT random program's tree shape, matched in count and cluster size -- this kills the remaining 'any structure prior helps' explanation. Evaluate all four on HE+/MBPP+ with evalplus, at matched NFE and matched wall-clock, and separately report the low-budget regime (nfe 64/128) where structure should help most if it helps at all, plus the syntax-error rate (our NFE sweep shows unparseable output falls 94%->1.8% over the budget range, so syntactic validity is the mechanism structural priors claim to fix and must be measured directly, not inferred from pass@1). Also log the realized supervision density per arm to prove the match held. Cost: 4 arms x ~35 GPU-hours = ~140 GPU-hours training, on H20 or faster on B200; eval adds ~40.
lens.assets_needed: PRESENT: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B (the correct init, used by both prior stage-1 and plain-SFT so the comparison is apples-to-apples), scaffold_coder/corruption.py (RungMixtureConfig/RungMixtureSampler/Band/HierarchicalBandSchedule/GlobalBandSampler/_per_position_band_weights -- the masking machinery), scaffold_coder/sft_dataset.py + PlainMaskedSFTDataset (the existing matched-control path, scaffold.mode=plain), scaffold_coder/training/scaffold_sft_trainer.py (working, FSDP, weighted loss), scaffold_coder/{ir,parser,serialization}.py (AST typed-IR for boundary identification), the normalized 114,363-example dataset + eval split, COLLATOR_STATS/CANVAS_STATS/CORPUS_STATS/BASELINE_STATS.md (measured supervision densities to match against), data/evalplus/*, evalplus 0.3.1. NEEDS WRITING: the B3 density-matched-random sampler and the B4 shuffled-structure sampler (both are new sampling classes inside corruption.py, moderate). NOTE this is the ONLY candidate here requiring training, and it is the one that finally uses the idle B200-class GPUs and the barely-used trainer -- directly addressing the self-diagnosed 'zero training experiments' failure. MISSING: nothing blocking; verify vendor/verl + FSDP env still works on the target node before committing 140 GPU-hours.
lens.kill_criterion: Killed if B2 beats B3 by less than the paired CI half-width (7.65 pts at n=164 / 5.04 at n=378) on both benchmarks at all budgets -- i.e. AST boundaries add nothing once density and clustering are matched. That is the LIKELY outcome given our plain-SFT result (it took zero Pareto frontier points), and it is publishable as a negative result WITH the density measurement as the mechanism, but it caps the ceiling at short-paper/workshop. Conversely killed as a *repair* if B2 >> B3 >> B1 with large margins, which would VINDICATE TreeDiff/AnCoder and leave us only a confirmation. Hard abort before spending compute: if the arms cannot be made density-matched in practice (e.g. matching count and cluster size simultaneously is infeasible for the structural sampler's median-2 states), the control is not identified and the experiment should not run. Also at risk: 4 arms x n=164 is badly underpowered for small effects (MDE 15.5 pts unpaired), so MBPP+ (n=378) must be the primary and all tests paired.
lens.builds_on: arXiv:2508.01473 TreeDiff 'AST-Guided Code Generation with Diffusion LLMs' (2025-08-02) and arXiv:2602.17688 AnCoder/AnchorTree (2026-02-05). TreeDiff's claim: replacing random token masking with masking of tokens belonging to key AST nodes aligns corruption with code structure, yielding 13.3% relative improvement and better respect for grammatical boundaries and long-range dependencies. AnCoder's claim: anchoring the diffusion process on AST-derived hierarchical priors (resolving keywords and identifiers first) establishes a structural scaffold that guides remaining generation, parameter-efficiently. The shared defect: their control is random-token masking, which differs from AST-node masking in at least three ways at once -- which positions, how many positions, and how those positions cluster. AST nodes are contiguous multi-token spans of non-uniform size, so masking them changes both the count and the burstiness of supervision relative to i.i.d. token masking; the reported gain is therefore not attributable to structural awareness specifically. We have the unusual advantage of having MEASURED this confound in our own pipeline (42.1 vs 16.3 mean supervised masks, median 31 vs 2, 19.5% canvas difference, BASELINE_STATS.md), which is what lets us design the density- and cluster-matched control they lack, plus a shuffled-structure arm that ablates 'structure prior' from 'correct structure prior'. Adjacent and worth differentiating: 2603.15803 'Mask Is What DLLM Needs' (masked-data training paradigm) and 2605.16829 CDC (inference-time static analysis, not training-time corruption).

diff.sharpened_claim: AST-guided corruption in diffusion code LMs is reported to help, but published evidence cannot attribute the gain to *syntactic boundaries* specifically, because no prior work holds the CLUSTERING (contiguity/burstiness) of masked positions fixed while varying only where the mask boundaries fall. We first correct a widely-repeated misreading: TreeDiff (2508.01473) DOES match the per-example masked-token count (Algorithm 1: N=⌊ε_t·L⌋ via weighted sampling *without replacement*, plus a uniform-random fallback to top up to N), so the marginal masking-rate confound is already controlled there. The live, uncontrolled confounds are three: (i) SPATIAL CLUSTERING -- tier-weighted sampling over AST-aligned positions produces spatially bursty masks even at token granularity, and no random-masking baseline in TreeDiff, AST-T5, or AnCoder matches the realized run-length / contiguity distribution; (ii) REGION REALLOCATION -- TreeDiff applies AST masking only to the code region and i.i.d. masking to the reasoning region, so the *within-code* effective mask rate differs from the uniform baseline even at equal global ε_t, and TreeDiff never reports realized per-region density; (iii) STRUCTURE-IDENTITY -- no arm tests whether the *correct* tree is needed, versus any prior with matched shape statistics. We therefore run four arms from one Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B init on one pinned recipe: B1 i.i.d. random at matched global rate; B2 AST-tier-weighted (the TreeDiff move); B3 random masking with the per-example count AND realized run-length distribution of B2 matched, spans placed at non-AST offsets; B4 shuffled-structure -- boundaries drawn from a *different* program's AST, matched in count and cluster size. We report realized supervision density and run-length histograms per arm to prove the match held, and measure parse-failure rate directly (not inferred from pass@1) because syntactic validity is the mechanism these papers claim. Our decomposition of the effect into {rate, clustering, boundary-correctness} is the contribution; the null (B2≈B3≈B4) and the positive (B2>B3>B4) are both informative, and the null is the outcome our own plain-SFT control makes likely.
diff.differentiation_statement: No prior work isolates AST-boundary-correctness from mask-cluster geometry in diffusion code LMs, and that is the whole of our contribution. TreeDiff (2508.01473, 2025-08-02) compares tier-weighted AST masking against i.i.d. uniform masking; AST-T5 (2401.03003, 2024-01-05) compares AST-subtree corruption against vanilla T5 span corruption; AnCoder/AnchorTree (2602.17688, 2026-02-05) compares AST-depth-decayed anchor *loss weighting* against null/keyword/identifier anchoring; "Mask Is What DLLM Needs" (2603.15803, 2026-03-16) compares density-priority masking against uniform. Every one of these varies WHERE the mask lands and HOW IT CLUSTERS simultaneously, and none reports a control that fixes the realized run-length/contiguity distribution while relocating the spans off AST boundaries; none reports a shuffled/wrong-tree arm that asks whether the *correct* structure is needed rather than any structured prior. Two further differentiators are concrete rather than rhetorical. First, our B4 (boundaries drawn from a different program's AST, matched in count and cluster size) has no analogue anywhere in this literature -- it converts "structure helps" into the falsifiable "the right structure helps". Second, our SETTING is different in a way reviewers care about: TreeDiff fine-tunes LLaDA-8B on OpenCodeReasoning at ε_max=0.1 with a cosine-annealed noise ceiling and a per-sample P_mask=(1-ε_t)λ+ε_t reparametrisation; AST-T5 is a 226M encoder-decoder span-corruption pretrain; AnCoder is an 809M two-stage anchor-denoiser trained from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B. We use a 7B *code-specialised masked-diffusion* base (Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B) on OpenCoder opc-sft-stage2 under a single pinned recipe, i.e. the model family and scale where these methods are actually deployed and where none of the three has been tested. We also fix a metric defect shared by TreeDiff and the DLM literature: TreeDiff argues its gain comes from respecting "grammatical boundaries" but never measures parse-failure rate, inferring the mechanism from pass@1; AnCoder does report Syntax(%) and is the right template, and we adopt it, reporting parse-failure directly for every arm at every budget. Finally, we can state the confound magnitude from measured local numbers rather than assertion: our own BASELINE_STATS.md shows swapping a flat sampler for a hierarchical structural one moves mean supervised masks 42.1->16.3 and median 31->2 at fixed nominal schedule, which is the empirical existence proof that "change the sampler" silently changes the training signal geometry.

related_work.citation: Yiming Zeng, Jinghan Cao, Zexin Li, Yiming Chen, Tao Ren, Zhuochun Li, Dawei Xiang, Xidong Wu, Shangqian Gao, Tingting Yu. TreeDiff: AST-Guided Code Generation with Diffusion LLMs. arXiv:2508.01473 (v1 2025-08-02; v3 2026-01-06).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint on arXiv (v3). Semantic Scholar reports venue 'Proceedings of the First Workshop on Structured Understanding, Retrieval, and Generation in the LLM Era (SURGeLLM 2026)'; I could NOT confirm this acceptance on OpenReview -- OpenReview returns only the DBLP CoRR-2025 record for TreeDiff (venueid dblp.org/journals/CORR/2025), and a SURGeLLM Workshop (Proceedings Track) at ACL 2026 venue string does exist on OpenReview for other papers (e.g. RSAT) but no TreeDiff note under it, and no ACL Anthology hit. Treat as preprint, possibly ACL-2026 workshop; per project rule the S2 venue string alone is not authoritative.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest work and the primary target. Fine-tunes LLaDA-8B-Base/Instruct on 150k OpenCodeReasoning samples. Splits input into [prompt || reasoning || code]; prompt frozen, reasoning gets i.i.d. token masking, code gets AST-tier-weighted masking. Algorithm 1: mask budget N=⌊ε_t·L⌋, per-token weights by AST node tier (p_skel=0.15, p_data=0.42, p_cond=0.58, p_ctrl=0.60), WeightedSample without replacement, then uniform-random fallback fill to reach exactly N. Cosine-annealed ε_t from 0.1 to 0.001 with per-sample P_mask=(1-ε_t)λ+ε_t, λ~U(0,1). Headline: HumanEval+ 32.3->36.6 at T=512 (the '13.3% relative' figure); MBPP+ 32.8->33.3. Appendix C adds an AST span-level variant (Algorithm 2).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: (1) No control matching the CLUSTERING of masked positions: tier-weighted sampling over AST-aligned tokens is spatially bursty, and the i.i.d. baseline is not. (2) No realized per-region mask statistics: because AST masking is applied ONLY to the code region while reasoning gets i.i.d. masking, the effective within-code masking rate can differ from the uniform baseline at equal global ε_t, and this is never measured or reported. (3) No shuffled/wrong-tree arm, so 'AST boundaries matter' is not separated from 'any structured prior matters'. (4) Parse-failure/syntax-validity rate is never measured despite 'respecting grammatical boundaries' being the stated mechanism. (5) Untested on code-specialised diffusion bases (Dream-Coder) and untested outside 8B LLaDA.
related_work.known_defects: IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the candidate's premise: TreeDiff DOES match the per-example masked-token count (N=⌊ε_t·L⌋, sampling without replacement, plus fallback top-up), so the raw 'number of masked positions' confound the candidate asserts is already controlled here -- the surviving confounds are clustering, region reallocation, and boundary-identity. Other real defects: single seed, no variance/CI anywhere (n=164 HumanEval+, so the headline 32.3->36.6 = 4.3 pts is inside a ~7-8 pt paired CI half-width and is statistically unsupported as reported); no parse-rate measurement despite the syntax mechanism claim; the '13.3% relative' headline is cherry-picked -- it is the single best cell (HE+ @ T=512), while the same table gives only +0.3 on MBPP+ @ T=512 and +0.3 on MBPP+ @ T=256; AR baselines are copied from the EvalPlus leaderboard rather than re-run, so they are not matched in data/compute/decoding; the paper's own Table 2 shows AST-span masking LOSES to random on MBPP (39.7 vs 41.5 @ T=512), which already hints the effect is about span geometry rather than structure per se; the four tier weights (0.15/0.42/0.58/0.60) are hand-set with no sensitivity analysis; T is conflated with max generation length, so 'denoising steps' and sequence budget are not separable.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 date 2025-08-02, v3 2026-01-06); downloaded and text-extracted full PDF v3 (14pp) and read Sections 3.1-3.4, Algorithm 1, Algorithm 2 (Appendix C), Tables 1-3, Appendix A.2 hyperparameters. Venue: Semantic Scholar Graph API (reports SURGeLLM 2026); OpenReview API v2 notes/search (only DBLP CoRR-2025 record, no SURGeLLM note); ACL Anthology search (no hit).

related_work.citation: Anton Xue, Litu Rout, Constantine Caramanis, Sanjay Shakkottai. AnCoder: Anchored Code Generation via Discrete Diffusion Models. arXiv:2602.17688 (v1 2026-02-05). UT Austin.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint on arXiv. No OpenReview record found (notes/search for 'AnCoder', 'AnchorTree', and the exact title returns zero matching notes), no DBLP/S2 venue. Verified as preprint.
related_work.what_it_covers: AnchorTree: AST-derived hierarchical priors for anchored diffusion (builds on Anchored Diffusion Language Model, arXiv:2505.18456, 2025-05-24). Crucially this is a LOSS-WEIGHTING method, not a corruption/masking method: it sets the ANELBO anchor weight mu(l)=omega(l)*eta(l), where omega=1 for keyword+identifier tokens and eta(l)=gamma*exp(-beta*max(depth(l)-d0,0)) decays with AST depth (beta=0.7, d0=2, gamma tuned per strategy). Two-stage anchor(494M)+denoiser(315M)=809M architecture initialised from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B, three-stage training on OpenCoder. Reports BOTH Syntax(%) and Pass@1: HumanEval 65.58->74.72 syntax, 3.29->5.45 pass@1 vs 809M MDLM; MBPP 74.46->80.12, 6.34->9.10. Includes a nice Section 4.2 probe: unmasking AST ancestors of a target position beats unmasking random non-ancestor positions, in-out order best.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Does not touch the forward corruption process at all -- the noise schedule is plain cosine and masking stays i.i.d., so it cannot answer whether AST-aware CORRUPTION helps. Its Section 4.2 ancestor-vs-random probe is count-matched but not AST-depth-matched or distance-matched, so 'ancestors help' is partly confounded with token-type frequency (keywords like def/if/while are high-prior tokens regardless of tree role). No shuffled-tree control. Never tested at 7B or on a code-specialised diffusion base. Pass@1 in the 3-9% range means it is far off the usable regime and the ordering may not survive at 7B.
related_work.known_defects: HEADLINE DECODING CONFOUND: the flagship AnCoder rows use remask rate 0.1 while the MDLM baselines use remask rate 0.0 (stated in Section 5, 'Inference'), and the paper itself observes that remasking drives most of the test-time-compute scaling -- so the +2.16 pass@1 / +9.14 syntax headline versus MDLM is not a clean single-variable comparison. The paper further notes the remask rate is NOT incorporated into the time-indexed loss weight, i.e. train/inference mismatch. gamma is tuned PER anchoring strategy (0.03 AnchorTree / 0.1 Keyword / 0.01 Identifier) on the same HumanEval used for the headline, which leaks eval into hyperparameter selection and flatters the best-tuned arm. No seeds/CIs; the AnchorTree-vs-Keyword/Identifier gaps (74.72 vs 73.05 vs 72.65 syntax; 5.45 vs 4.57 vs 4.73 pass@1) are within plausible sampling noise for 164 problems x 20 samples with no reported variance. AR reference is re-evaluated at 494M and beats every diffusion arm by 5x on pass@1, which the paper acknowledges only in passing.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-02-05); downloaded and text-extracted full PDF (20pp) and read Sections 3.2-3.4, 4.1-4.3, 5 (Architecture/Training/Inference/Baselines), Table 1, and Appendix A.1/gamma ablation Table 5. OpenReview API v2 notes/search for 'AnCoder', 'AnchorTree', and full title -- zero records.

related_work.citation: Linyuan Gong, Mostafa Elhoushi, Alvin Cheung. AST-T5: Structure-Aware Pretraining for Code Generation and Understanding. arXiv:2401.03003 (v1 2024-01-05). ICML 2024.
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2024 (stated in paper/repo; pre-2025 so OpenReview verification not required by project rule). arXiv v3 2024-06-23.
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical structure-aware code-corruption paper and the strongest methodological precedent for our design. AST-Aware Subtree Corruption: recursive AST traversal masks subtrees with a tunable granularity theta (sampled per example in 5..100), plus AST-Aware Segmentation. Its Table 2 is a sequential-ablation ladder on identical architecture/data/compute: T5 44.2 avg -> +AST Segmentation 45.7 -> +AST Subtree Corrupt 47.0 -> +Mask 25% 47.9 -> Mask 50% 46.4, with HumanEval 5.2 -> 7.2 -> 9.6 -> 14.0 -> 14.3.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: THIS PAPER IS OUR STRONGEST MOTIVATING EVIDENCE and simultaneously the closest thing to the control we propose -- but it stops one step short. It matches the mask RATIO between vanilla T5 span corruption and AST-subtree corruption, yet the span-length distributions differ enormously (vanilla T5 mean span length 3 vs AST subtrees up to 100 tokens, explicitly acknowledged in Section 3.4). So even here, 'AST subtrees' is confounded with 'much longer contiguous spans', and no random-long-span control is run. Encoder-decoder T5 at 226M, not a decoder-only masked-diffusion LM, and no diffusion-specific noise schedule.
related_work.known_defects: The paper's own ablation quantifies our confound: going from 15% to 25% mask ratio alone moves HumanEval 9.6 -> 14.0 (+4.4), which is LARGER than the AST-corruption step itself (7.2 -> 9.6, +2.4). That is direct published evidence that masking-budget/geometry knobs can dominate the structural-awareness knob -- exactly the decomposition we propose, and the citation that makes our framing credible to a reviewer rather than speculative. Also: single ordering of the sequential ablation (no reverse order, so interactions between segmentation, subtree corruption and ratio are unidentified); no seeds/CIs; the 'random long span' control that would isolate span length from AST alignment is absent.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; downloaded and text-extracted full PDF v3 (13pp) and read Section 3.4 (Subtree Masking / theta), Section 4 Baselines, Section 5.1 controlled experiments, Table 2.

related_work.citation: Mask Is What DLLM Needs: A Masked Data Training Paradigm for Diffusion LLMs. arXiv:2603.15803 (v1 2026-03-16).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (PDF header reads 'Preprint. Under review.'). No OpenReview record found for the title; OpenReview title search returned only unrelated ICLR 2026 review notes.
related_work.what_it_covers: Nearest neighbour on the 'density' axis, and important because it independently invented HALF of our control. Information-Density-Driven Smart Noise Scheduler on LLaDA-2.0-mini: extracts info-dense hubs, applies Priority Masking with priority regions masked w times more often, and -- critically -- solves a probability-mass-conservation equation for p_base so the per-sample marginal noise level still equals the scheduler's sigma_t. Plus Complementary Priority Masking (train on both M and 1-M). ~4% avg gain over uniform across HumanEval/MBPP/GSM8K/MATH500; also reports w-sweep (0.1..10) and a hard-prior extreme baseline that underperforms.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Matches the MARGINAL rate per sample but NOT the clustering/contiguity of masked positions, and its priority regions are information-density hubs, not AST nodes -- so it neither tests nor controls syntactic-boundary correctness. No shuffled-prior control (its 'extreme prior w=10' is a strength sweep, not a wrong-structure arm). Code-specific structure and parse-failure rate are not measured. LLaDA-2.0-mini only, single scale.
related_work.known_defects: Establishes precedent for rate-conservation (which strengthens the reviewer case that rate-matching is table stakes and pushes our novelty onto clustering + boundary-identity -- we must cite it prominently or a reviewer will say we reinvented it). Its own defects: bias weight w is selected on the same four benchmarks used for the headline; complementary masking doubles the effective supervised positions per example, an unpriced compute/supervision advantage over the uniform baseline; 'information-dense hub' extraction is heuristic and never validated against an independent notion of density; block-diffusion block size 32 fixed, so results may not transfer to full-sequence diffusion; no seeds/CIs.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 2026-03-16); downloaded and text-extracted full PDF (10pp) and read Section 2.2 (Priority Masking + mass-conservation equation), Complementary Masking, Section 3 experiments, Section 3.4.4 ablation. OpenReview title search (no record).

Relevant to us as the reason AnCoder is loss-weighting rather than corruption: it means our B2/B3/B4 arms do NOT overlap AnCoder's mechanism at all, which is a clean differentiation point.

followup_openings.defect: The random-masking baseline is i.i.d. Bernoulli while TreeDiff's tier-weighted sampling over AST-aligned positions produces spatially CLUSTERED masks. The per-example token COUNT is matched (Algorithm 1: N=⌊ε_t·L⌋, weighted sampling without replacement + uniform fallback fill), but the run-length / contiguity distribution is not, and is never reported. So 'AST boundaries matter' is confounded with 'bursty supervision matters'.
followup_openings.our_fix: Add arm B3: random masking that reproduces, per example, B2's exact masked-token count AND its realized run-length histogram, but places the spans at non-AST offsets. Measure and publish realized count + run-length distributions per arm to prove the match. B2-vs-B3 is then a clean single-variable test of boundary alignment.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: If B2 == B3, the entire structure-aware-corruption literature's headline reduces to a span-geometry effect obtainable with no parser, no grammar, and no language-specific tooling -- a substantially cheaper recipe and a clean negative result with a measured mechanism. If B2 > B3, TreeDiff is vindicated with the control it lacks, which is itself a citable strengthening.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473)
followup_openings.defect: Region reallocation is uncontrolled and unmeasured. TreeDiff applies AST masking ONLY to the code region and i.i.d. masking to the reasoning region of [prompt||reasoning||code]. At equal global ε_t the realized WITHIN-CODE masking rate can therefore differ between TreeDiff and the uniform baseline, and no per-region realized density is ever reported. This is a genuine rate confound that survives Algorithm 1's global count matching.
followup_openings.our_fix: Log realized per-region supervised-position counts for every arm and add a region-matched variant where the within-code rate is forced equal across B1/B2/B3. Report the per-region density table as a first-class result, not an appendix note.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the one place where the candidate's original 'supervision density' intuition is actually correct for TreeDiff, and it is cheap to measure. A per-region density table either exonerates or indicts the headline, and no future paper in this line can omit it once published.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473) and AnCoder (arXiv:2602.17688)
followup_openings.defect: Neither tests whether the CORRECT tree is needed. Both compare 'AST-derived prior' against 'no prior', leaving 'any structured prior with these shape statistics' as an unexcluded explanation.
followup_openings.our_fix: Arm B4: draw masking boundaries from a DIFFERENT program's AST, matched in count and cluster-size distribution to B2. This is the wrong-structure control. It has a direct precedent in this project's own methodology (the --random_trunk control used in Paper C), so the design is proven, not speculative.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: B4 is the arm that turns a vague 'structure helps' into a falsifiable 'the right structure helps'. It is the single highest-information arm in the design and has no analogue in any paper found. If B2 == B4, the mechanism claimed by two papers is refuted while their empirical gains are preserved and re-explained.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473)
followup_openings.defect: Claims the mechanism is respecting 'grammatical boundaries' and 'syntactic coherence' but never measures parse-failure or syntax-validity rate -- the mechanism is inferred entirely from pass@1 plus one qualitative trajectory figure. AnCoder, by contrast, does report Syntax(%), showing the metric is standard and its absence in TreeDiff is a choice.
followup_openings.our_fix: Report parse-failure rate directly for all four arms at every budget, alongside pass@1, following AnCoder's Syntax(%) convention. Our own NFE sweep already shows unparseable-output rate falling 94%->1.8% (HE+) and 89%->1.6% (MBPP+) across the budget range, so parse rate is a live, high-dynamic-range variable in exactly the low-budget regime where structural priors should act -- and it can move independently of pass@1.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Construct validity: if structural corruption improves pass@1 without improving parse rate, the stated mechanism is wrong even if the method works. This decouples 'does it help' from 'does it help for the reason claimed', and it is nearly free to measure.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473)
followup_openings.defect: Statistically unsupported headline. The '13.3% relative improvement' is a single cell (HumanEval+ @ T=512, 32.3->36.6, i.e. 4.3 pts on n=164) reported with no seeds, no variance, and no CI, while the same table shows only +0.3 on MBPP+ at BOTH T=256 and T=512. Table 2 additionally shows AST-span masking LOSING to random on MBPP (39.7 vs 41.5 @ T=512).
followup_openings.our_fix: Make MBPP+ (n=378) the primary endpoint, use paired per-problem tests (McNemar / paired bootstrap) rather than unpaired comparisons, pre-register the budget grid, and report the full arm x benchmark x budget matrix with CIs rather than a best cell. Report the effect size against the paired CI half-width (~7.65 pts at n=164, ~5.04 at n=378) so readers can see what is and is not resolvable.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Even a pure replication with correct pairing and honest CIs is publishable here, because the headline number in the paper being replicated is inside its own noise floor. This also protects us: it forces us to state up front that our own 4-arm design at n=164 is underpowered for small effects.

followup_openings.target_paper: AnCoder / AnchorTree (arXiv:2602.17688, 2026-02-05)
followup_openings.defect: The headline comparison is not single-variable: AnCoder arms use inference remask rate 0.1 while MDLM baselines use 0.0, and the paper itself notes remasking drives most of the test-time-compute scaling. Separately, gamma is tuned per anchoring strategy on the same HumanEval that reports the headline, leaking eval into hyperparameter selection.
followup_openings.our_fix: Wherever we compare against an anchored/loss-weighted arm, hold the decoding protocol (remask rate, temperature, T) identical across arms and report a decoding-protocol sensitivity row. Our own measured sampler sensitivity (top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 moved HumanEval by +14.6 points) is the quantitative argument that decoding-protocol drift can swamp any of these method effects, and we can cite our own number for it.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A +14.6-point sampler effect versus a +2.16-point method effect is the strongest single sentence available for why matched-protocol controls are the contribution. It also generalises our paper from 'one control for one paper' to 'a protocol standard for structure-aware DLM claims'.

followup_openings.defect: Matches mask RATIO between vanilla span corruption and AST-subtree corruption but not span-length distribution (vanilla mean span 3 vs subtrees up to 100 tokens, explicitly acknowledged). No random-long-span control. Its own ablation shows the ratio knob alone (15%->25%) moves HumanEval +4.4 while the AST-corruption knob moves it +2.4.
followup_openings.our_fix: Cite AST-T5's Table 2 as published evidence that geometry/budget knobs can dominate the structural knob, and supply the missing random-long-span control (our B3) that AST-T5 never ran -- now in a decoder-only masked-diffusion 7B setting rather than a 226M encoder-decoder.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This converts our framing from 'we suspect a confound' to 'the field's own numbers show the confound is larger than the effect'. It is the citation that makes a reviewer accept the premise in one line, and it extends a 2024 ICML result to the 2026 diffusion setting.

followup_openings.target_paper: Mask Is What DLLM Needs (arXiv:2603.15803, 2026-03-16)
followup_openings.defect: Conserves the per-sample marginal noise level (solves for p_base so mean P(m_i=1) = sigma_t) but not clustering; its priority regions are information-density hubs rather than syntactic units; complementary masking silently doubles supervised positions per example relative to the uniform baseline, an unpriced advantage; w is tuned on the same benchmarks as the headline.
followup_openings.our_fix: Adopt and cite their rate-conservation trick as the correct baseline discipline (this is table stakes, not our novelty), then go beyond it on the two axes they leave open: cluster-geometry matching and boundary-identity (B3/B4). Also price supervised-position count explicitly per arm so no arm gets a free supervision subsidy.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Positions our contribution precisely rather than redundantly: rate-matching is solved, clustering and boundary-correctness are not. Pre-empts the strongest reviewer objection ('2603.15803 already did the density control').

followup_openings.target_paper: All four (TreeDiff, AnCoder, AST-T5, Mask-Is-What-DLLM-Needs)
followup_openings.defect: Every result lives at a single model scale and family: LLaDA-8B, 809M Qwen-init two-stage, 226M T5, LLaDA-2.0-mini. None tests a code-specialised masked-diffusion base at 7B. AnCoder's absolute pass@1 (3-9%) is far below the usable regime, so its ordering may not survive at competent scale.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the decomposition on Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B, a code-specialised 7B masked-diffusion model whose Instruct sibling we have already measured at HumanEval+ .707 / MBPP+ .680 with a full NFE sweep (nfe64 .018/.029 through nfe512 .707/.680). We therefore have a calibrated, high-competence reference curve to place every arm against, and can report the low-budget regime (nfe 64/128) where structural priors should act if they act at all.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Cross-family/cross-scale replication of a contested effect is independently publishable, and the 7B code-diffusion setting is where these methods would actually be deployed. Our existing NFE curve means arms are interpretable against a known frontier instead of in a vacuum.

diff.verification_notes:
MATERIAL CORRECTION TO THE CANDIDATE'S PREMISE (found by reading the PDF, not the abstract). The candidate's central claim is that TreeDiff's random-masking baseline controls masked-token count "in expectation, not per-example". This is FALSE as stated. TreeDiff Algorithm 1 sets N=⌊ε_t·L⌋ and selects exactly N indices by weighted sampling WITHOUT replacement, with a uniform-random fallback that tops up to exactly N when AST nodes are insufficient; Algorithm 2 (span variant) likewise breaks at c>=N and fallback-fills to N. So the per-example masked-token COUNT is matched between TreeDiff and its uniform baseline. The candidate's headline framing ("prior work attributes the full gain to WHICH tokens while only HOW MANY is controlled in expectation") must be rewritten or a reviewer who has read Algorithm 1 will reject the paper's premise outright. The surviving, genuine confounds -- which I verified are uncontrolled and unreported -- are (i) spatial clustering / run-length distribution, (ii) region reallocation (AST masking on the code region only, i.i.d. on the reasoning region, with no realized per-region density reported), and (iii) boundary-identity (no wrong-tree arm). The sharpened_claim reflects this corrected decomposition.

SECOND CORRECTION: the candidate treats AnCoder as "the TreeDiff move" (structural corruption). It is not. AnCoder/AnchorTree modifies the ANELBO anchor LOSS WEIGHT mu(l)=omega(l)*eta(l); its forward corruption stays i.i.d. cosine-schedule masking. So AnCoder is not a second instance of the confound we attack, and citing it as such is an error. It is still worth citing (it shares the missing wrong-tree control, and it supplies the Syntax(%) metric convention we should adopt) but it must be described as loss-weighting, not corruption.

THIRD: the candidate says "my searches for masking-rate/noise-schedule ablations in masked diffusion returned 0-2 hits, none doing this control." Partly outdated. arXiv:2603.15803 (2026-03-16, PRE-cutoff, so it does preempt on that axis) explicitly solves a probability-mass-conservation equation so the per-sample marginal noise level still equals the scheduler's sigma_t under priority masking. Rate-conservation under a non-uniform masking prior is therefore already published and must be cited as prior art rather than claimed. Our novelty has to rest on cluster-geometry matching (B3) and boundary-identity (B4).

FOURTH: the candidate's own local evidence does not support the claim it is used for. BASELINE_STATS.md (verified on disk at /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/BASELINE_STATS.md) does report mean supervised masks 42.1 vs 16.3, median 31 vs 2, mean canvas 137.6 vs 110.8. But that comparison is Plain-SFT vs this project's own HIERARCHICAL GLOBAL-BAND SCAFFOLD sampler -- a rung-based hierarchical scheme that compresses whole subtrees into line labels or holes. It is NOT TreeDiff-style tier-weighted token masking at a fixed budget N. So it demonstrates that "swapping in a structural sampler can silently change supervision density by 2.6x" in general, which is a legitimate motivating observation, but it is NOT evidence about TreeDiff's sampler specifically and must not be presented as such.

VENUE STATUS I COULD NOT CONFIRM: Semantic Scholar reports TreeDiff's venue as "Proceedings of the First Workshop on Structured Understanding, Retrieval, and Generation in the LLM Era (SURGeLLM 2026)". I could not corroborate this. OpenReview API v2 returns only the DBLP CoRR-2025 record for TreeDiff (venueid dblp.org/journals/CORR/2025, note id WbTS3QWNu8); a "SURGeLLM Workshop (Proceedings Track) at ACL 2026" venue string DOES exist on OpenReview (found via another paper, RSAT), but no TreeDiff note is filed under it, a direct notes query on that venue string returned 0, and ACL Anthology search returned nothing. Per the project's own rule (S2/DBLP lag badly for 2026 venues and are not authoritative), I have recorded TreeDiff as "preprint, possibly SURGeLLM@ACL-2026". This does not affect concurrency: v1 is 2025-08-02, comfortably pre-cutoff, so TreeDiff is prior art either way.

Other verification gaps: (a) I could not retrieve TreeDiff's or AnCoder's training code, so I cannot confirm the published algorithms match their implementations -- if a reviewer or we ourselves later find TreeDiff's code does NOT match Algorithm 1 (e.g. masks per-node Bernoulli without a budget cap), the candidate's original count-confound claim would be revived; worth checking before writing. (b) AnCoder reports no seeds/CIs, so my statement that its inter-anchoring-strategy gaps are within noise is my inference from n and effect size, not from reported variance. (c) I could not verify the candidate's asserted "19.5% shorter mean canvas" causal story or the claim that matching count and cluster size is infeasible for median-2 states -- the hard-abort condition in the candidate is real and untested, and a cheap CPU-only dry run of the B3 sampler on the 114,363-example split should gate the 140 GPU-hours. (d) Searches for a pre-existing cluster-matched or shuffled-structure control (arXiv full-text/title/abstract across ~20 query formulations, OpenReview, Semantic Scholar, DBLP, ACL Anthology) returned nothing, so I am confident B3/B4 are unoccupied -- but absence of search hits is weaker evidence than a positive find, and this control could plausibly be buried in an appendix I did not read.

SCOPE CAVEAT ON THE CEILING: with the premise corrected, the paper is a control-and-decomposition study of one pre-cutoff workshop-scale paper's mechanism claim, in a different model family and scale. Short-paper / workshop is the right target, matching the candidate's own stated ceiling. The strongest version bundles B4 (wrong-tree) plus the parse-rate construct-validity leg plus the per-region density table, and frames the whole as a protocol standard for structure-aware DLM claims rather than a referendum on TreeDiff.

blocking_gaps: MEASURED KILL OF THE CENTRAL CONTRAST (B2 vs B3). I reimplemented TreeDiff Algorithm 1 (tier weights 0.15/0.42/0.58/0.60, weighted sampling WITHOUT replacement to exactly N=floor(eps*L), uniform fallback) on the actual normalized corpus IR with exact fast-tokenizer offsets (fast==slow token ids on 400/400 examples). At TreeDiff's OWN eps_max=0.1 the clustering difference the whole sharpened_claim rests on is ~0.6%: mean run length TD 1.1135 vs iid 1.1064; pooled run-length histogram TD [2624,235,21,1,0,0,0] vs iid [2616,244,19,0,0,0,0]; frac runs>=3 0.0076 vs 0.0066; mean max-run 1.540 vs 1.522. Even at eps=0.5 (5x above TreeDiff's ceiling) it is only +10.0%. Reason is structural, not a bug: sampling without replacement at 10% density on ~84-token sequences with weights spanning only 4x, where the 'data' tier (w=0.42) is 48.9% of all tokens, is nearly i.i.d. B3 is therefore a near-null-by-construction arm -- the independent variable barely varies -- and 'B2 approx B3' would be uninterpretable, not a finding.

B4 AS SPECIFIED IS DEGENERATE (collapses onto B1). 'Boundaries drawn from a DIFFERENT random program's tree, matched in count and cluster size' cannot carry tier information about the program it is applied to. Measured masked-token tier composition L1 distance from B1: B2=0.2532, B4_donor_tree=0.0614, B4_permuted_labels=0.0302 (eps=0.1, 500 examples). B4 is 76-88% of the way back to B1, so it buys a second, noisier copy of B1 for ~15 GPU-hours. The 'highest-information arm in the design' is not identified.

THE REPO'S TYPED IR IS LINE/STATEMENT-LEVEL, NOT EXPRESSION-LEVEL AST, so assets_needed's claim that scaffold_coder/{ir,parser,serialization}.py provide 'AST typed-IR for boundary identification' is wrong at the granularity TreeDiff needs. Printed spans for a real example: RULE 'def ' / CONTENT TOKEN_HDR 'find_index_intersection(lst1, lst2)' / RULE ':' / RULE '\n' / RULE '    ' / CONTENT TOKEN_STMT 'result = []'. Content spans are WHOLE statements; there is no skeleton/data/conditional/control tier anywhere in ir.py (fields are node_id, depth, text/header/condition). I had to write a stdlib-ast char->tier map from scratch to run the probes above. tree_sitter_python 0.26.0 is installed as an alternative path, but either way this is new code, not existing machinery.

corruption.py's RungMixtureSampler IS NOT A TOKEN-LEVEL TIER-WEIGHTED MASKER and cannot serve as B2. It is a rung mixture (root_plan 0.20 / body_plan 0.30 / leaf_infill 0.50) that emits meta-tokens ([STMT]/[FUNC]/[HDR]/[BODY]), typed holes, and [expand]/[delete] edits, and calls extend_tokenizer() in the trainer. Using it as B2 would change the VOCABULARY and the canvas, not just the mask -- confounding the AST question with the meta-token intervention already measured (Scaffold HE+ .183 vs Plain .220). B2 needs a new Dataset class modeled on PlainMaskedSFTDataset (sft_dataset.py:238), not RungMixtureSampler.

TRAINING CANNOT RUN ON THE B200-CLASS GPUs, so 'this is the one that finally uses the idle B200-class GPUs' is false. The trainer needs hydra + verl + flash_attn (scaffold_sft_trainer.py:19 imports hydra; vendor/DreamOn/src/trainer/fsdp_sft_expand_trainer.py:30 does module-level 'from flash_attn.bert_padding import ...'; the pinned config sets attn_implementation=flash_attention_2). On wzc1 BOTH envs lack all of them -- /opt/conda/envs/dllm-env and .venv_b200 return hydra/verl/flash_attn/peft = MISSING, and there is no .venv_dream on wzc1 at all (gitignored; find returns only .venv_b200). The working env exists ONLY on zwfy6 (.venv_dream: hydra 1.3.4, verl 0.3.0.post1, flash_attn 2.7.3, peft 0.13.2 -- 'TRAINER IMPORT OK' verified on .73). But that env is torch 2.5.1+cu124 whose arch list stops at sm_90, so it cannot drive sm_100 L20A/B200. The only flash_attn wheel on disk is flash_attn-2.7.3+cu12torch2.5cxx11abiFALSE-cp311, built for torch 2.5, not the 2.11 on wzc1. Porting = building flash_attn for torch2.11/sm_100, a multi-hour build that may fail.

ONLY ONE NODE IS BOTH CAPABLE AND FREE. .73 = 8x H20 idle with a verified working .venv_dream and all three Stage-1 checkpoint trees on zwfy6. .82 = 8/8 GPUs at 99% (sampler audit). .104 = 8/8 at 99% running generate_evalplus_dream.py sampler_audit shards. So 4 sequential arms on one 8-GPU node, and the 16-card same-disk DDP option would require evicting the sampler audit that supplies this candidate's own decoding-protocol row.
