related_work.citation: Xue, Rout, Caramanis, Shakkottai. "AnCoder: Anchored Code Generation via Discrete Diffusion Models." arXiv:2602.17688 (v1 2026-02-05).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint only. Verified: Semantic Scholar returns publicationVenue = arXiv.org, venue "arXiv.org", year 2026, citationCount 0; OpenReview search returns no matching submission or camera-ready record; arXiv shows a single version with no Comments/Journal-ref.
related_work.what_it_covers: The second stated target, but on a different axis than the candidate assumes: AnchorTree intervenes on DENOISING ORDER, not on corruption. Forward noising is standard independent per-position masking. A two-network anchor-denoiser architecture (809M total: 494M anchor init from Qwen2.5-Coder-0.5B, 315M denoiser from its first 12 layers, causal attention converted to bidirectional) prioritises unmasking syntactically salient tokens (keywords, identifiers) in AST-root-to-leaf order. Trained in three stages on OpenCoder; evaluated on HumanEval (20 samples/prompt) and MBPP (10 samples/prompt) at T in {256,...,2048}, reporting syntactic validity and pass@1. Also contains a genuinely useful mechanism probe (Figure 5) showing that unmasking a target's AST ancestors closest-first helps prediction more than unmasking random non-ancestors.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Whether AST-specific structure matters once the architecture and the anchoring mechanism are held fixed -- the paper's own Null arm nearly answers this in the negative and the paper does not confront it. Also open: any scale above 809M, any regime where absolute pass@1 is off the floor, and whether the remask-rate asymmetry accounts for the margin.
related_work.known_defects: (a) Its own Null-anchoring (gamma=0, structure-agnostic) control captures most of the reported gain: HumanEval pass@1 MDLM-809M 3.29 -> Null 4.80 -> AnchorTree 5.45, so Null delivers +1.51 of the +2.16 total (70%) and AST-specific anchoring only +0.65; on MBPP 6.34 -> 8.64 -> 9.10, Null delivers +2.30 of +2.76 (83%) and AST only +0.46. The abstract's "structurally anchored diffusion offers a parameter-efficient path to high-quality code generation" is therefore mostly an architecture result mis-attributed to structure. (b) Unfair baseline at decode time, stated plainly in their Inference paragraph: "For AnCoder implementations, we use a remask rate of 0.1, which we have found to improve performance; MDLM baselines use a remask rate of 0.0." The treatment gets a decoding advantage the baseline is denied, and it is not ablated. (c) Absolute pass@1 of 3-9% is near the floor; ranking methods by sub-point differences at the floor does not license claims about behaviour at deployable scale. (d) No confidence intervals or paired tests on any comparison, despite 20/10 samples per prompt making them cheap. (e) Non-monotonicity across the compute sweep is left unremarked (e.g. Keyword anchoring HumanEval pass@1 4.88 at T=1024 falls to 4.57 at T=2048), which is the signature of noise at these effect sizes. (f) MBPP is used at its full 974 problems without the EvalPlus-hardened test suites, so "functional correctness" is measured against the weaker original tests.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; full PDF v1 downloaded and text-extracted; read Section 5 (Architecture / Training / Inference / Benchmarks / Baselines), Table 1, Tables 2-3, and Section 4's ancestor-unmasking probe verbatim; Semantic Scholar graph API for publicationVenue; OpenReview api2 notes/search.

related_work.citation: Wettig, Gao, Zhong, Chen. "Should You Mask 15% in Masked Language Modeling?" arXiv:2202.08005 (v1 2022-02-16).
related_work.venue_status: EACL 2023. Verified via arXiv abs page Comments field: "Accepted to EACL 2023. The code and pre-trained models are available at .../DinkyTrain".
related_work.what_it_covers: The strongest methodological precedent for the candidate's core insight, and it is NOT cited in the proposal. Explicitly studies "the interplay between masking rates and masking strategies" and finds that "uniform masking requires a higher masking rate compared to sophisticated masking strategies such as span or PMI masking" -- i.e. that a structured selector's apparent advantage is entangled with the corruption level it induces. Also decomposes masking rate into two opposing effects (more corruption = harder task; more predictions = better optimisation) and revisits BERT's 80-10-10 corruption.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Everything on our axis: it is encoder-only MLM for representation learning, evaluated on GLUE and SQuAD fine-tuning and linguistic probing, at BERT-base/large scale, on natural language. It sweeps a SCALAR rate rather than constructing a position-randomised control matched to a structured selector's conditional per-type/per-depth marginal. Nothing about generative masked diffusion, nothing about code, nothing about executable correctness, nothing at 7B, and no AST.
related_work.known_defects: Not a defect to repair so much as a citation we must foreground to survive review: a reviewer who knows this paper will say our insight is 2022 prior art unless we state precisely what is new (objective class, model family, scale, endpoint, and the conditional-marginal-matched randomisation as opposed to a rate sweep). Its own limits: single model family (BERT), single pretraining corpus, and downstream fine-tuning metrics that are only loosely coupled to generation quality -- so it cannot be cited as already having settled the generative-code case.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; arXiv abs page scraped for the Comments field naming EACL 2023 and the DinkyTrain code release; abstract read in full.

related_work.citation: Bitton, Bansal, Hessel, Schwartz. "Uniform Masking Prevails in Vision-Language Pretraining." arXiv:2212.05195 (v1 2022-12-10).
related_work.venue_status: Could not confirm a peer-reviewed venue: arXiv abs page has no Comments and no Journal-ref; ACL Anthology title search returned no hit; Semantic Scholar was rate-limited (HTTP 429) on repeated attempts. Treat as preprint unless re-verified.
related_work.what_it_covers: A same-shaped null result in a different domain. Separates the two MLM design choices explicitly ("the masking strategy, which determines which tokens to mask, and the masking rate, which determines how many") and shows that raising the masking rate improves downstream performance "while simultaneously reducing performance gap among different masking strategies, rendering the uniform masking strategy competitive to other more complex ones."
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Vision-language, non-generative, no code, no diffusion, no AST, no executable endpoint. Establishes that the rate/strategy confound generalises across modalities -- which raises our prior and supplies a framing precedent, but leaves the code-diffusion instance entirely untested.
related_work.known_defects: Rate and strategy are varied on a grid rather than a strategy's induced marginal being reproduced under position randomisation, so it demonstrates that the gap shrinks with rate without identifying the marginal as the causal channel. Also confined to ITM/VQA-style downstream metrics.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and abstract; arXiv abs page scraped for Comments/Journal-ref (both absent); ACL Anthology search (no hit); Semantic Scholar attempted but rate-limited -- venue status flagged as unverified.

related_work.citation: Levine, Lenz, Lieber, Abend, Leyton-Brown, Tennenholtz, Shoham. "PMI-Masking: Principled masking of correlated spans." arXiv:2010.01825 (v1 2020-10-05).
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2021 Spotlight. Verified via OpenReview api notes/search: record under invitation ICLR.cc/2021/Conference/-/Blind_Submission with venue "ICLR 2021 Spotlight" (plus a DBLP mirror at venue "ICLR 2021").
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical "principled non-uniform masking beats random masking" claim that the whole structure-aware-masking lineage inherits, using pointwise mutual information to mask correlated spans. Provides the intellectual template that TreeDiff and AnCoder instantiate with an AST instead of PMI.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Encoder MLM, natural language, 2020 scale; no rate-matched or marginal-matched control (Wettig et al. later showed its advantage is partly a rate effect). No code, no diffusion, no generative endpoint.
related_work.known_defects: Compares against uniform masking at a fixed 15% rate without varying the rate per strategy -- the confound Wettig et al. surfaced two years later. Useful for us as the historical anchor of the pattern we are auditing: the field has now run this exact confound at least three times (PMI 2020, TreeDiff 2025, AnCoder 2026).
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; OpenReview api notes/search returning the ICLR 2021 Blind_Submission record and "ICLR 2021 Spotlight" venue string.

related_work.citation: Shah, Chakraborty, Gupta. "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2607.24763 (v1 2026-06-04).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint, concurrent. Verified: arXiv submission history shows a single version, "[v1] Thu, 4 Jun 2026"; no Comments or Journal-ref; OpenReview search returns no matching submission.
related_work.what_it_covers: The methodological ally the proposal already names, and its date confirms concurrency (2026-06-04 is after the 2026-05-07 cutoff). Audits 7 MDLM REMASKING strategies on LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base by standardising actual NFE, enforcing multi-metric reporting, and controlling stochasticity; finds temperature explains most MAUVE variance and that "compute-matched comparisons reverse several published strategy rankings."
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It is an inference-time axis (remasking/decoding) on open-domain text (OpenWebText, LM1B) with MAUVE-style metrics. It says nothing about the training corruption schedule, nothing about code, and nothing about executable correctness -- so it cannot preempt us and in fact supplies an independent same-disease citation on an orthogonal axis.
related_work.known_defects: For our purposes the relevant limitation is scope: standardising NFE still uses a step-count-derived compute unit rather than tokens actually attended, which understates cost differences when canvas length varies across arms -- the refinement our cumulative_model_tokens accounting supplies. Also text-only, so its ranking reversals are not directly transferable to code.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473)
followup_openings.defect: The proposal's stated defect is imprecise and a reviewer with the PDF open will catch it. TreeDiff's Algorithm 1 DOES match the global mask count: it sets N = floor(eps_t * L) and random-fills N - c positions when AST candidates are insufficient, explicitly "maintaining the statistical properties required for stable training." What is never matched, never reported, and never randomised is the CONDITIONAL marginal: the probability that a masked position is AST-aligned at all, and its distribution over the Skeleton / DataFlow / CondLogic / ControlFlow tiers and over tree depth.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-aim arm D from a rate-matched control to a conditional-marginal-matched control. Measure arm C's empirical joint marginal over (AST-membership, node tier, depth, global t) across one full epoch, then in arm D draw the same number of masks with that same joint marginal but with positions chosen uniformly at random *within* each cell -- destroying the identity of the selected nodes while preserving the noise distribution. Report the measured marginals for A, C, and D as a table so the manipulation is auditable, and state the decision statistic as (C - A) vs (D - A) with paired McNemar tests per benchmark.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This converts a claim that is wrong as written into one that is both correct and sharper. It also rescues the whole candidate: without this correction the paper's central premise is refutable from TreeDiff's own pseudocode, which is a desk-reject-grade error.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473)
followup_openings.defect: The 13.3% relative headline is +4.3 absolute points on HumanEval+ (32.3 -> 36.6) at a single denoising budget, i.e. about 7 of 164 problems, from a single seed, with no confidence interval and no significance test. Binomial SE at p~0.35, n=164 is ~3.7pp, so the paired difference is not separated from noise. There is also an internal inconsistency: TreeDiff's MBPP+ T=256 cell reads 44.2 in Table 1 and 44.9 in Table 2, and at T=512 on HumanEval+ TreeDiff and AST-Span are exactly tied at 36.6, so the granularity ablation does not separate the method from span masking at the headline budget.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run every arm at >=3 seeds and report bootstrap 95% CIs on pass@1 plus McNemar paired tests on per-problem pass/fail vectors against arm A, at both NFE 512 and NFE 128. Pre-register the decision rule (already drafted in the kill criterion) and report the full arm x benchmark x budget grid rather than a selected cell. Publish per-problem outcome vectors so the paired statistics are reproducible.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It makes a null result publishable. A null with n=164 and no CIs is dismissed as underpowered; a null with seeds, paired tests, and a stated minimum detectable effect is a finding, and it simultaneously documents that the original positive claim was never powered to support its headline.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473)
followup_openings.defect: Cost accounting conflates two variables. The paper states that "the denoising steps T also denote the maximum generation length for each configuration," so its single T axis mixes compute with canvas size, and no token-level cost is reported. Compounding this, the AR rows in Table 1 are imported from the EvalPlus leaderboard while the diffusion rows use a nonstandard pass@1 defined as the top-1 candidate "selected by model log-likelihood" at n=1 -- so rows of the same table are not on the same metric. The baseline also degrades monotonically from T=256 to T=512 on every column (HE+ 34.8 -> 31.7), which is unexplained.
followup_openings.our_fix: Report cumulative_model_tokens as the primary cost unit alongside NFE for all four arms, and grade every arm with evalplus.evaluate / untrusted_check under one identical protocol at fixed temperature and top_p. Show the arms on a quality-versus-tokens frontier rather than a quality-versus-T curve, and read process AND failure_process so budget-truncated tasks are not silently dropped from the cost mean.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: We have already been burned twice by exactly this class of error -- NFE as a cross-family cost unit, and averaging only non-truncated tasks (retraction 3, which understated one arm's cost by 2.85x/3.69x). Landing the token-accounting critique on TreeDiff is a contribution we are unusually well-placed to make credibly, because we can cite our own corrected measurements as the worked example.

followup_openings.target_paper: AnCoder / AnchorTree (arXiv:2602.17688)
followup_openings.defect: The paper already contains the decisive control and does not confront what it shows. Its Null-anchoring arm (gamma=0, structure-agnostic, identical two-stage anchor-denoiser architecture) captures 70% of the HumanEval pass@1 gain over MDLM-809M (+1.51 of +2.16) and 83% on MBPP (+2.30 of +2.76), leaving AST-specific AnchorTree with +0.65 and +0.46 points -- unresolvable at n=164/974 with no CIs. The abstract nonetheless claims "structurally anchored diffusion offers a parameter-efficient path to high-quality code generation," attributing to structure what its own table attributes mostly to architecture.
followup_openings.our_fix: Cite the Null-vs-AnchorTree decomposition explicitly as independent pre-cutoff evidence for our thesis on the adjacent axis (denoising order rather than corruption), computing the attribution percentages the authors omit. This converts a presumed competitor into a supporting citation and lets us frame the paper as "two independent axes, same conclusion: the structural content of AST guidance contributes far less than the machinery built around it."
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It removes AnCoder as a threat and recruits it as evidence, and it means our null is no longer a lone contrarian datapoint -- it is a confirmation with a pre-cutoff, independent-team precedent hiding in that paper's own ablation row.

followup_openings.target_paper: AnCoder / AnchorTree (arXiv:2602.17688)
followup_openings.defect: Unfair baseline at decode time, stated openly in the Inference paragraph: "For AnCoder implementations, we use a remask rate of 0.1, which we have found to improve performance; MDLM baselines use a remask rate of 0.0." The treatment arms receive a decoding-time advantage the baselines are denied, it is tuned on the treatment, and it is never ablated -- so the +2.16/+2.76 margins are upper bounds that include a free inference-time gift. Separately, all absolute pass@1 values sit at 3-9%, i.e. near the floor, where sub-point rankings are uninformative, and non-monotonicity across the T sweep (Keyword 4.88 at T=1024 falling to 4.57 at T=2048) confirms noise dominance.
followup_openings.our_fix: Hold every decoding hyperparameter byte-identical across arms A/C/D (temperature, top_p, remask rate, NFE, canvas) and report the decoding configuration in a single shared table; additionally report the top_p sensitivity band, since we have already measured that moving top_p from 1.0 to 0.95 shifts HumanEval by +14.6 points -- larger than every method gain in either target paper. Run at 7B where absolute pass@1 is 20-25%, off the floor, so a null has real statistical power.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: The top_p finding is a decisive rhetorical asset: if a sampler knob we did not even intend to study moves HumanEval by 14.6 points, then 0.46-4.3 point method gains reported without protocol control are not interpretable. Our 7B setting is the untested regime that makes the null binding rather than a floor artefact.

followup_openings.target_paper: Our own arm B (depth-banded schedule_only), used as the motivating evidence
followup_openings.defect: Arm B is not a clean schedule-only manipulation and cannot support the proposal's claim of "a 6x degradation from a schedule change alone." The two dataset classes read different parquet columns: PlainMaskedSFTDataset loads [seq_id, prompt, response, total_tokens] while ScheduleOnlySFTDataset loads [seq_id, prompt, ir_json, total_tokens] and reconstructs its targets via _segmented_schedule_only_response(module, tokenizer). The supervised TARGET TEXT therefore differs between arms A and B -- B trains on IR-rendered code, A on the original response string. On top of that the two arms are not rate-comparable: our own SCHEDULE_ONLY_STATS.md records mean canvas 149.8 and mean supervised masks 61.4 for schedule-only versus 137.6 and 42.1 for plain, i.e. ~46% more masked positions on a ~9% longer canvas. So A-vs-B confounds target text, canvas length, and mask count with the schedule.
followup_openings.our_fix: Build arms C and D from the SAME target token sequence, and add an arm A' -- uniform masking on IR-rendered targets -- so the four-way comparison holds target text fixed and the decision statistic uses A' rather than A. First verify whether render(module_from_dict(ir_json)) round-trips to the response string; if it does, the confound collapses and A can be reused (document the check either way). Demote arm B from evidence to a cautionary appendix showing how many variables a "schedule change" silently moves, and drop the 6x figure from the motivation.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the reviewer objection most likely to kill the paper, and it is self-inflicted: a paper whose thesis is "your comparison confounds two variables" cannot rest its motivation on a three-way-confounded arm of its own. Fixing it costs one extra training arm out of the 60 GPU-hour budget and is the difference between a clean falsification and a rhetorical own-goal.

followup_openings.target_paper: Wettig et al. (arXiv:2202.08005, EACL 2023) and Bitton et al. (arXiv:2212.05195)
followup_openings.defect: Not defects in those papers -- a positioning hazard the proposal has not addressed. Both already establish the rate/strategy confound ("uniform masking requires a higher masking rate compared to sophisticated masking strategies"; "increasing the masking rate reduces the performance gap among different masking strategies, rendering the uniform masking strategy competitive"). Neither appears in the candidate's builds_on. A reviewer who knows them will charge that the insight is four-year-old prior art.
followup_openings.our_fix: Foreground both in the introduction as the prior that motivates the hypothesis, then state the four concrete transfers plainly: encoder MLM representation learning -> generative masked diffusion; GLUE/SQuAD/ITM -> executable correctness on HumanEval+/MBPP+ via evalplus untrusted_check; BERT-large/VL encoders -> 7B production code diffusion; and a scalar-rate sweep -> a conditional per-tier/per-depth marginal reproduced under position randomisation. Add the observation that the field has now run this same confound at least three times (PMI-Masking 2020, TreeDiff 2025, AnCoder 2026), which frames our contribution as closing a recurring methodological gap in a new regime rather than as a novel insight.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Framing the paper as "a known confound, never checked in the regime that now matters, and here is what happens when you check it" is both honest and more robust to review than claiming the insight is new -- and it upgrades two potential scooping citations into the paper's own motivation.

diff.verification_notes: Could not verify: (1) Venue status of Bitton et al., arXiv:2212.05195 "Uniform Masking Prevails in Vision-Language Pretraining" -- the arXiv abs page has no Comments and no Journal-ref, an ACL Anthology title search returned no hit, and the Semantic Scholar graph API returned HTTP 429 on every attempt. I have recorded it as preprint-unverified; do not assert a venue for it without a fresh check. (2) TreeDiff's Appendix A.2 tier weight values (p_skel, p_data, p_cond, p_ctrl) -- pdftotext did not cleanly recover the appendix tables, and no code is released. The proposal's own fidelity caveat therefore stands and should be strengthened: arm C is a reimplementation from the paper's textual description, and we should additionally report arm C's *measured* marginal so readers can judge how close our instantiation is regardless of the unrecovered constants. (4) I did not locate any paper that runs a conditional-marginal-matched randomisation control for structured masking in ANY setting -- generative or otherwise. Claims resting on weaker evidence: the assertion that TreeDiff's LR was possibly tuned only on the treatment arm is an inference from the phrase "5 x 10^-5 was selected as the optimal learning rate" with no per-arm sweep described -- it is a fair reviewer question, not a demonstrated fact, and should be phrased as such. Everything I state about TreeDiff's Algorithm 1 mask-count matching, its Table 1/Table 2 numbers and their 44.2-vs-44.9 inconsistency, and about AnCoder's Null-arm decomposition and its remask 0.1-vs-0.0 asymmetry, was read directly from the extracted PDFs and is quoted or arithmetic on quoted numbers. Our own arm A/B numbers (HE+ 21.95 / 3.66, MBPP+ 24.34 / 11.38) were confirmed on disk in /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/BASELINE_STATS.md, SCHEDULE_ONLY_STATS.md, and STAGE1_RESULTS.md; the arm A/B target-text divergence was confirmed by reading the differing parquet column lists at scaffold_coder/sft_dataset.py lines 238-247 (PlainMaskedSFTDataset) and 407-422 (ScheduleOnlySFTDataset), and the canvas/mask-count divergence from the comparison table in SCHEDULE_ONLY_STATS.md. blocking_gaps: ARM D IS NOT A VALID CONTROL UNDER THE WHOLE-NODE READING OF TREEDIFF -- THIS IS THE ONE GAP THAT MUST BE RESOLVED BEFORE ANY GPU IS SPENT. I implemented both readings of TreeDiff Algorithm 1 against the real corpus and measured a held-out statistic (masked-run-length) that the conditional marginal does NOT constrain. (a) If arm C selects whole AST nodes (span masking), C's mean masked-run-length is 22.9 tokens vs D's 6.1 -- a 3.79x gap that survives EXACT per-tier marginal matching (verified identical: CTRL 13082 / DATA 23106 / SKEL 328 / COND 12221 in both arms). D then differs from C in TWO ways (position identity AND contiguity), so C-vs-D no longer isolates 'which positions'; it is the same class of two-variable confound the paper accuses TreeDiff of. (b) If arm C samples per-position with tier weights (the literal Alg-1 reading), C/D run-length ratio is 1.013x and D IS clean. The positioning doc's "weighted-sampling step over I_ast" implies (b), but TreeDiff also reports an 'AST-Span' ablation, so the whole-node variant is in-scope for the field. DECISION REQUIRED: either commit to reading (b) and say so explicitly, or add span-length to the matched marginal (a 5-arm design). Cannot be deferred -- it determines the dataset class you build.

THE CANDIDATE'S MOTIVATING EVIDENCE (arm B, '6x degradation from a schedule change alone') IS CONFOUNDED, AND ONE OF THE THREE SUSPECTED CONFOUNDS IS REAL WHILE THE OTHER IS NOT. Good news, verified: render_module(module_from_dict(ir_json)) is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the `response` column on ALL 114,363 rows (0 mismatches, exhaustive not sampled). So the feared 'target text differs' confound does NOT exist. Bad news, verified: the TOKEN sequences differ on 1500/1500 rows because ScheduleOnlySFTDataset tokenizes each source-map span SEPARATELY (sft_dataset.py:842 _segmented_schedule_only_response), inflating token count 93.9 vs 81.53 mean = 1.152x, i.e. arm B trains on a ~15% longer token grid with different BPE boundaries than arm A. Combined with SCHEDULE_ONLY_STATS.md (canvas 149.8 vs 137.6, supervised masks 61.4 vs 42.1), A-vs-B confounds tokenization grid + canvas length + mask count with the schedule. The '6x' figure must be dropped from the motivation and arm B demoted to a cautionary appendix.

PER-PROBLEM OUTCOME VECTORS ARE NOT POWERED FOR THE STATED DECISION RULE, AND THIS KILLS THE KILL-CRITERION AS WRITTEN. The rule asks to resolve 'C > A+3pp AND D <= A+1.5pp'. Computed McNemar MDE at 80% power / alpha=.05: HE+ (n=164) 6.9-12.0pp depending on discordance rate; MBPP+ (n=378) 4.6-7.9pp; pooled (n=542) 3.8-6.6pp. Averaging 3 seeds only gets pooled to 3.1pp. Nothing in this design can resolve a 1.5pp null. The 3pp threshold is itself at/below single-seed MDE on HE+. The rule must be restated as an equivalence/non-inferiority test with a pre-registered margin the design can actually support (realistically ~5pp pooled at 3 seeds), or the paper must claim only 'no effect larger than X' with X stated honestly.

feas.concrete_plan:
## Pre-flight, no GPU (~1 day). Resolve the design ambiguity before spending compute.

**P0. Fix the arm-D validity question (blocking).** Reproduce my measurement, then commit in writing to one reading of TreeDiff Alg-1:
- Reading (b), per-position tier-weighted sampling: arm D as proposed is valid (C/D run-length 1.013x). Cheapest, and matches the positioning doc's "weighted-sampling step over I_ast". Recommended.
- Reading (a), whole-node/span selection: arm D must additionally match the masked-span-length distribution, or you have re-created the confound you are attacking. If you want to cover TreeDiff's own AST-Span ablation, this becomes a 5th arm (D-span: span-length-matched AND tier-matched, positions randomised).
State the chosen reading and report arm C's *measured* marginal, since TreeDiff Appendix A.2 tier weights were not recoverable and no code is released.

**P1. Fix the tokenizer grid so arms C/D sit on arm A's exact token sequence — no arm A' needed.** Verified: `transformers.Qwen2TokenizerFast(vocab_file=models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B/vocab.json, merges_file=.../merges.txt)` agrees with the slow `DreamTokenizer` on 20,000/20,000 responses (0 disagreements) and supplies `return_offsets_mapping` (the slow tokenizer raises NotImplementedError). Therefore: tokenize the RAW `response` string once (identical to `PlainMaskedSFTDataset`, sft_dataset.py:302), then map char offsets -> AST tier. This makes arm A a legitimate baseline and avoids the 1.152x inflation that contaminates arm B.

**P2. Build the tier map from `ast.parse`, not from `ir_json`.** Verified: `ir_json` is statement-granular only — node kinds are exactly {module, function, simple, for, if, while}, with no expression-level nodes, so TreeDiff's DataFlow tier (assigns/calls) is not expressible from it. `ast.parse` succeeds on 4000/4000 responses. Assign each char the tier of its **innermost** enclosing node (outermost-wins collapses to 96.2% CTRL and is useless): measured token-level shares DATA 40.8% / CTRL 36.2% / COND 21.1% / SKEL 0.7% / DEFAULT 1.2%, i.e. all four TreeDiff tiers are populated and separable. Corpus supports SKEL: 632 module-level imports and 1015 module-level non-func statements per 4000 rows. Keyword-vs-identifier split (12,383 KEYWORD / 33,837 IDENT per 1500 rows) is available via `tokenize.generate_tokens` for the AnCoder-style variant.

**P3. Write two dataset classes in `scaffold_coder/sft_dataset.py`,** modeled on `PlainMaskedSFTDataset` (lines 238-406) NOT on `ScheduleOnlySFTDataset` (407-620, the span-tokenizing one). Wire into `scaffold_coder/training/scaffold_sft_trainer.py` at the existing `elif mode == ...` dispatch (mode=="plain" at line 163, mode=="schedule_only" at line 195) as `mode=ast_tier` and `mode=ast_marginal`. Keep the t-sampling, `base_weight = min(maximum_weight, 1.0/t)`, per-sample weight normalisation, and role_ids byte-identical to plain so the only changed variable is which positions get masked. Dataloader cost is a non-issue: measured 0.48 ms/sample for the proposed path vs 0.39 ms for plain (1.21x) vs 1.36 ms for schedule_only (3.44x).

**P4. Emit the marginal-audit table as a first-class artifact.** Have both datasets log per-sample (t, tier, depth, n_masked, masked-run-lengths). Assert arm D's per-(tier,depth) masked counts equal arm C's within tolerance, and report C's and D's run-length distributions side by side. This table IS the paper's auditability claim.

## Execution (~44-50 GPU-hours, all on .73 which I verified is 100% idle: 8/8 GPUs at 0% util, 0 MiB)

Node: `.73` = `28.85.35.73` (omit `-p`; global ssh_config sets Port 36000), root `/apdcephfs_zwfy6/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft`, python `.venv_dream/bin/python`. Do NOT use .82 or .104 (both 8/8 at 98-99% util) and do NOT try to train on wzc1 LOCAL (no verl).

**Step 1 — train arm C, then arm D.** Copy `scripts/run_plain_sft_stage1_8gpu.sh` (the arm-A ground truth) to `_run_ast_tier_sft_stage1_8gpu.sh` / `_run_ast_marginal_sft_stage1_8gpu.sh`, changing only `scaffold.mode` and `default_local_dir`. Everything else is already matched by that script: `data.train_batch_size=128`, `micro_batch_size_per_gpu=8`, `max_length=1024`, `bucket_by_length=true`, `total_epochs=5`, `partial_pretrain=models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B`, and from `outputs/plain_sft_stage1/resolved_training_config.json`: lr 1e-5, betas [0.9,0.95], weight_decay 0.01, warmup_ratio 0.1, clip_grad 1.0, seed 1, flash_attention_2, gradient checkpointing on, lora_rank 0 (full FT), FSDP FULL_SHARD. 114,363/128 = 893 steps/epoch x 5 = 4465 steps, matching arm A exactly.
