**Step 2 — grade with the frozen recipe.** Reuse `scripts/run_evalplus_full_8gpu.sh` verbatim (it already sets `HUMANEVAL_OVERRIDE_PATH`/`MBPP_OVERRIDE_PATH` to the pinned v0.1.10/v0.2.0 jsonl, runs 8-way sharded generation, merges with `--expected 164`/`378`, then calls official `python -m evalplus.evaluate --test-details`), swapping the generator to `scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py` (`--steps` = NFE, `--temperature`, `--top-p`, and it already writes `process.{nfe, generated_tokens, input_tokens}` per task).
Cost, measured from arm A's own per-rank `metrics.rank*.jsonl`: HE+ 2.43 GPU-h, MBPP+ 4.70 GPU-h at NFE 512 = **7.1 GPU-h per arm per (HE++MBPP+) at NFE512**; NFE128 is ~1/4 => ~1.8 GPU-h. **~9 GPU-h per arm for both budgets.**

**Step 3 — re-grade arms A and B under the SAME evalplus build** so all four rows share one metric (CPU-only, minutes; solutions.jsonl already on disk at `outputs/{plain,schedule_only}_evalplus_full/{humaneval,mbpp}/solutions.jsonl`).

**Step 4 — statistics.** Pull per-problem pass/fail from `eval_results.json["eval"][task_id][0]["base_status"]`/`["plus_status"]` (verified present, n=164/378, and the "plus counts only if base passes" rule is what I used to reproduce .2195/.2434/.0366/.1138). Run McNemar C-vs-A and D-vs-A per benchmark, bootstrap CIs, and report the pre-registered equivalence margin. Report `cumulative_model_tokens` alongside NFE, reading `process` OR `failure_process` (retraction-3 discipline).

## Budget and seeds

2 arms x (16 train + 9 eval) = **50 GPU-h for 1 seed**, which is why 60 was roughly right for a single seed but is NOT enough for the multi-seed design the positioning demands. 3 seeds x 2 arms = 150 GPU-h. Disk is the harder constraint: each arm retains 9 checkpoints x 86G = 774G (57G of that is `optimizer_state.pt` per checkpoint), and zwfy6 has only 3.3T free of 12T. Set `trainer.save_checkpoint_steps=4465` (final only) or prune intermediates, or you cannot fit 2 arms x 3 seeds.
feas.risk:
The most likely outcome is a CONFOUNDED result, not a null, and it arrives by the exact mechanism the paper accuses TreeDiff of. If arm C is implemented as whole-AST-node (span) masking -- the natural reading of "mask tokens belonging to selected AST nodes" in the candidate's own experiment text -- then arm D differs from C in two variables at once, because matching the per-(tier,depth) marginal provably does not match contiguity: I measured mean masked-run-length 22.9 (C) vs 6.1 (D), a 3.79x gap, with the tier counts exactly equal. Any C-vs-D difference would then be attributable to span structure rather than position identity, and the paper's central methodological claim would be self-refuting. A reviewer with a calculator reproduces this in an afternoon.

The second most likely outcome is a genuine null that is not publishable because it is underpowered. Even reading (b) plus 3 seeds gives a pooled McNemar MDE of ~3.1pp, while the stated kill criterion requires resolving D-A <= 1.5pp. A null at 1.5pp with a 3.1pp MDE is not evidence of absence; it is a design that cannot see the effect. The paper would be criticising TreeDiff for a +4.3pp single-seed claim on n=164 while itself reporting a null the design cannot support -- an own-goal of the same shape as the arm-B motivation problem.

Third, less likely but worth stating: arms C and D may both land near arm A's .2195/.2434 with no separation from each other or from A, because at 5 epochs over a 114k-row corpus the corruption schedule may simply be a weak lever relative to the base model, in which case the paper measures "nothing about masking matters here" -- true, but a much weaker claim than "the marginal carries the effect," and one that cannot be distinguished from insufficient training signal without a positive control that is currently absent from the design.
feas.required_control:
**A held-out-statistic divergence audit on the masks themselves, run and reported BEFORE any model is trained.** The three retractions share one structure: a stage silently failed to vary (or to compare) the thing it claimed to, and nobody measured the stage's own output. The verifier discarded return values; `restart` discarded the scaffold draft; the cost mean discarded truncated tasks. The analogous failure here is that arm D silently fails to be a control -- it matches the marginal you chose to match while differing on a marginal you never looked at -- and this would be invisible in pass@1, discoverable only by a reviewer.

Concretely, before training: dump arms C and D masks over >=2000 real rows and emit a table with two halves. (i) **Matched-by-construction, must be identical:** total masked count, per-tier masked counts (SKEL/DATA/COND/CTRL/DEFAULT), per-depth masked counts, and the t-marginal. Assert equality programmatically and fail the run if it does not hold -- I verified this is achievable exactly (CTRL 13082 / DATA 23106 / SKEL 328 / COND 12221 in both arms). (ii) **Deliberately NOT matched, must be reported as numbers even if embarrassing:** masked-run-length distribution (mean/median/p90), count of fully-masked AST nodes, and masked-position autocorrelation. Half (ii) is the load-bearing half. I already ran it and it is what caught the problem: under whole-node arm C the ratio is 3.79x and arm D is not a control; under per-position arm C it is 1.013x and arm D is clean. Publishing half (ii) converts "we matched the marginal" from an unverifiable assertion into an auditable measurement, and it tells the reader precisely which dimension the claim is and is not identified along.

Two supporting controls that are cheap and close the remaining retraction-shaped holes: (1) a **degenerate-arm negative control** -- run the pipeline with a mask selector that ignores the AST entirely but reports itself as tier-weighted, and confirm the audit table flags it -- this is the "empty solution scores full marks" test applied to the masking stage; (2) **single-pinned-grader, all four arms, plus re-grade A and B under it**, with per-problem pass/fail vectors published, so no row of the final table is on a different metric than any other row.

lens.title: Anytime code diffusion: conditioning the denoiser on its own step budget
lens.claim: A single masked-diffusion code model trained with an explicit step-budget conditioning token, on noise levels sampled from the mask-rate trajectory a B-step sampler actually visits, dominates the NFE sweep of the same model trained unconditionally at NFE <= 128 without sacrificing the NFE-512 ceiling -- and the gain comes from the conditioning, not from the changed noise distribution alone.
lens.why_now: Our own NFE sweep is the motivation and it is unusually clean: HE+ pass@1 goes .018 (NFE64) -> .140 (128) -> .555 (256) -> .707 (512) -> .707 (1024), with EXACTLY zero gain from 512 to 1024, replicated on MBPP+ (.029/.233/.545/.680/.680). So the model wastes all compute above 512 and is unusable below 256. Standard MDLM training samples t uniformly, which matches no actual sampler trajectory. Searches for budget-conditioned / step-budget-conditioned diffusion LM training returned zero hits. The adjacent work all adapts inference or bolts on a controller: DiFFPO (2510.02212, pre-cutoff) RL-trains an adaptive per-prompt threshold; TraceLock (2605.24697, concurrent) learns a commitment policy for a FROZEN backbone; EC-DLM (2604.01622, pre-cutoff) varies MoE expert capacity by timestep. None makes the budget an input the weights are conditioned on, and none targets the low-NFE regime where our Pareto finding says flat diffusion scores ~0.
lens.experiment: Instrument scaffold_coder/model_sampler.py to log the realized per-step mask-rate trajectory of the existing sampler at B in {32,64,128,256,512} on a held-out slice. Then train three arms from Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B on data/scaffold_edu_v0: (A) budget-conditioned -- prepend one of five [budget=B] tokens (reuse the existing tokenizer_utils.extend_tokenizer + initialize_model_token_rows path already built for scaffold meta tokens), and for each sample draw B then draw t from the LOGGED trajectory for that B rather than uniform. (B) trajectory-only control -- identical t-sampling, budget token present but held CONSTANT, isolating conditioning from the changed noise distribution. (C) plain uniform-t SFT at matched compute (partly reusable from the existing plain arm). Grade all three across the full NFE sweep {32,64,128,256,512} on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ with evalplus.evaluate, plotting against cumulative_model_tokens, and overlay the untrained Dream-Coder-Instruct reference curve we already own.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: full NFE sweep reference curves on both benchmarks (10 measured cells); model_sampler.py; generate_evalplus_dream.py with --steps; tokenizer_utils.extend_tokenizer and initialize_model_token_rows (already used to add scaffold meta tokens, so the new-token embedding-init path is proven); 8-way sharded EvalPlus generators. MISSING/TO BUILD: sampler instrumentation to dump realized per-step mask rates (~40 lines); a budget-conditioned dataset mode that draws B then t|B; five new budget tokens. RISK TO FLAG: this is the highest-variance candidate -- conditioning may simply not bind, which is why arm B exists.
lens.kill_criterion: Falsified if budget-conditioned arm A is within 2 points of arm C at NFE 64 AND NFE 128 on both benchmarks (conditioning bought nothing at the low end), or if A loses more than 3 points to C at NFE 512 (the ceiling was traded away, so it is not anytime). Additionally, if A ~= B within noise at every NFE, the effect is entirely the noise distribution and the 'conditioning' claim specifically dies while a weaker 'trajectory-matched t-sampling' claim survives.
lens.builds_on: DiFFPO (2510.02212, 2025-10-02) and TraceLock (2605.24697, 2026-05-23, concurrent). Defect/gap: both treat the compute-quality tradeoff as an inference-time control problem over fixed weights. Neither tests whether the denoiser can be TRAINED to know its budget, and neither evaluates the low-NFE regime on code where, per our own sweep, flat diffusion scores ~0-14%.

diff.sharpened_claim: In a masked diffusion code LM, step-budget conditioning and trajectory-matched noise sampling are SEPARABLE interventions with different signatures, and only their conjunction is anytime. Concretely, on Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B we run the 3-way decomposition that FS-DFM (the one paper that conditions a denoiser on its step budget) never ran: (A) discrete [budget=B] token + t drawn from the realized mask-rate trajectory of a B-step sampler; (B) identical t-distribution with the budget token held constant; (C) uniform-t SFT at matched compute. We predict, and will report either way, that (i) most of the low-NFE gain at B<=128 comes from arm B -- i.e. from matching the noise distribution to the sampler's actual visited states, not from the model "knowing" its budget -- and (ii) the budget token's specific contribution is to PREVENT the high-NFE ceiling regression that FS-DFM observed and left unexplained ("the slight accuracy dip at very large NFEs ... under-use the step-aware conditioning"), making A the only arm that is genuinely anytime rather than merely few-step-tuned. We measure this on functional correctness (EvalPlus pass@1+ on HumanEval+/MBPP+), against cumulative_model_tokens rather than NFE, at fixed sampler temperature/top_p -- three axes on which every prior budget-conditioning result is reported only as PPL/MAUVE at unstated or uncontrolled stochasticity.
diff.differentiation_statement: The candidate's stated premise -- "searches for budget-conditioned diffusion LM training returned zero hits ... none makes the budget an input the weights are conditioned on" -- is false and must be dropped from any draft. FS-DFM (arXiv 2509.20624v1, 2025-09-24; ICLR 2026 Poster, verified on OpenReview) states verbatim: "We expose the step budget h as an explicit conditioning signal to the DFM generator so the model learns transitions calibrated to the intended number of sampling steps," and lists as its first contribution "conditioning on a user-specified step budget." So the mechanism is pre-cutoff prior art with a public Apple codebase, and the paper cannot be framed as introducing budget conditioning. What survives, and is defensible to a reviewer, is a follow-up on four concrete axes. (1) Method family: FS-DFM is discrete FLOW MATCHING, conditioning on a continuous step-size scalar h inside a purpose-built CTMC velocity formulation with an EMA shortcut teacher and a "Cumulative Scalar" update; ours is masked diffusion, conditioning through a discrete [budget=B] vocabulary token added to a frozen-vocabulary pretrained model. Whether a discrete token in the input sequence can carry budget information at all -- as opposed to a scalar injected into the timestep embedding of a from-scratch architecture -- is untested and is the real scientific risk. (2) Scale and provenance: FS-DFM trains 0.169B/1.3B/1.7B models from scratch on FineWeb-Edu with a GPT-2 tokenizer; we retrofit a public 7B pretrained code diffusion model. FS-DFM's own limitations section names the absence of public discrete-flow checkpoints as a barrier and defers "broader assessments." (3) Task surface and metric: FS-DFM, CDLM, FlowLM, and FMLM all report PPL/entropy/token-accuracy/MAUVE on WikiText-103, LM1B, or OWT. Not one reports pass@1 on HumanEval or MBPP. Budget conditioning has never been shown to survive a functional-correctness metric, where a single wrong token voids the sample -- a far harsher test than a distributional score, and the regime our own sweep shows collapses to .018/.029 at NFE 64. (4) The missing control: FS-DFM ablates the Cumulative Scalar (Table 1) and the h-sampling WEIGHTS (Appendix E.1: TB-10/TB-20/pure-uniform/geometric/annealed-geometric), but never holds the conditioning signal constant while keeping the changed step-size distribution. It therefore cannot separate "the model is conditioned on its budget" from "training oversampled large steps." Our arm B is exactly that missing cell, and CDLM (ICML 2026) makes it load-bearing: CDLM reaches strong few-step quality with the step count "decoupled from the training formulation," i.e. with no conditioning at all -- direct evidence that the conditioning may be doing less work than FS-DFM's framing implies.

followup_openings.target_paper: FS-DFM: Fast and Accurate Long Text Generation with Few-Step Diffusion Language Models (arXiv 2509.20624, ICLR 2026 Poster)
followup_openings.defect: The paper's headline contribution -- conditioning the generator on the step budget -- is never ablated. Appendix E.1 varies only the training-time sampling WEIGHTS over the step-size grid (TB-10, TB-20, pure-uniform, geometric, annealed-geometric); Table 1 isolates only the Cumulative Scalar update. Step-aware conditioning, the shortcut EMA teacher, and the Cumulative Scalar are introduced together as a bundle. No arm exists in which the h-conditioning input is held constant (or ablated) while the h-sampling distribution is left unchanged, so the reported few-step gains cannot be attributed to conditioning rather than to the shifted training-time step-size distribution plus large-step teacher distillation.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the missing cell directly: arm A (budget token varies + trajectory-matched t) vs arm B (identical t-distribution, budget token pinned to a single constant) vs arm C (uniform-t, matched compute). Arm B is a strict single-variable removal of the conditioning signal with the noise distribution held fixed. If A ~= B at every NFE, the conditioning contributes nothing and only 'trajectory-matched t-sampling' survives -- which is itself a publishable negative result about a bundled ICLR contribution, and is a cleaner attribution than FS-DFM offers.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It decides whether the field should be building budget-conditioned architectures (extra input plumbing, extra tokens, retrofit cost) or simply fixing the training-time noise distribution -- a one-line change to any existing MDLM trainer. The second is vastly cheaper and would apply to every released dLLM checkpoint immediately.

followup_openings.target_paper: FS-DFM (arXiv 2509.20624, ICLR 2026 Poster)
followup_openings.defect: FS-DFM reports and then hand-waives a ceiling regression: 'The slight accuracy dip at very large NFEs likely reflects train-test mismatch: the model and shortcut teacher are optimized for large h, so many small steps accumulate discretization/renormalization bias and under-use the step-aware conditioning.' This is the exact failure that would make the method few-step-tuned rather than anytime, it is diagnosed only speculatively ('likely'), it is never quantified as a tradeoff, and no experiment tests whether more conditioning capacity or a corrected h-weighting removes it. The paper's own best-performing h-policy (TB-20, a 20x tail boost toward the largest step) is the policy most likely to cause it.
followup_openings.our_fix: Promote the dip to a first-class measured quantity: report the full budget sweep {32,64,128,256,512} for every arm and score the anytime property as a two-sided criterion (low-NFE gain over uniform-t AND no more than 3 points lost at NFE 512). Then test whether the regression is caused by the conditioning being under-used at small h -- FS-DFM's own hypothesis -- by comparing arm A against arm B at high NFE: if only the conditioned arm holds its ceiling, conditioning is what buys anytime-ness; if both regress, the culprit is the tail-boosted noise distribution and the fix is reweighting, not architecture.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: 'Anytime' is the whole selling point of budget conditioning -- one checkpoint serving every latency tier. A method that gains at 8 steps while quietly losing at 512 is not anytime, it is a second checkpoint. No paper in this cluster currently reports the high-budget end as a pass/fail criterion, so the property is asserted rather than demonstrated.

followup_openings.target_paper: FS-DFM (arXiv 2509.20624, ICLR 2026 Poster); Consistent Diffusion Language Models / CDLM (arXiv 2605.00161, ICML 2026); FlowLM (arXiv 2605.20199); Flow Map Language Models (arXiv 2602.16813)
followup_openings.defect: This entire few-step cluster evaluates only distributional and likelihood proxies -- gpt2-large PPL, entropy, masked-token accuracy, MAUVE -- on WikiText-103, LM1B, or OpenWebText, at 0.17B-1.7B scale. None reports any executable-correctness metric; grep for HumanEval and MBPP in FS-DFM and CDLM returns zero hits. FS-DFM's limitations section concedes that instruction-following, QA, and reasoning assessments 'remain to be done.' A gpt2-large PPL improvement is compatible with output that never parses, and our own measurements show unparseable-output rate is the dominant failure mode at low step counts (94% -> 1.8% on HumanEval+ across the NFE range).
followup_openings.our_fix: Evaluate every arm with evalplus untrusted_check pass@1+ on HumanEval+ (n=164) and MBPP+ (n=378), and additionally report the unparseable-output rate per arm per budget. This converts 'few-step generation is fine' from a distributional claim into a functional one, and the parse-rate channel gives a mechanistic readout of WHERE the low-budget gain comes from (syntactic viability vs semantic correctness) that PPL cannot provide.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: If budget conditioning improves PPL at 8 steps but pass@1+ stays at 0 because nothing parses, the field's few-step results do not transfer to the deployment setting -- code assistants -- that motivates dLLM latency work in the first place. Testing it on a public 7B code checkpoint that others can rerun is the cheapest way to find out.

followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models (arXiv 2607.24763, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: CaRE audits 7 remasking strategies and finds that (i) temperature explains the majority of MAUVE variance and (ii) compute-matched comparisons reverse several published rankings -- but it audits only inference-time remasking strategies on OpenWebText and LM1B with MAUVE/PPL. It never applies its own compute-matching and stochasticity-control discipline to TRAINING-side interventions, and never to a functional-correctness metric, so it cannot say whether trained few-step methods are also artifacts of uncontrolled sampler settings.
followup_openings.our_fix: Extend CaRE's discipline to the training axis and to code: hold temperature and top_p fixed and identical across arms A/B/C, report every arm at two sampler settings, and price compute in cumulative_model_tokens rather than nominal NFE. We already have an in-house measurement that makes this urgent -- moving top_p from 1.0 to 0.95 shifted HumanEval by +14.6 points, larger than most published diffusion-LM method gains -- which is CaRE's thesis independently reproduced in the code domain on a 7B model. Since CaRE is concurrent it does not preempt us; it corroborates the accounting choice while leaving the training-side audit open.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Without this, any low-NFE gain we report is vulnerable to precisely CaRE's critique. Building the control in from the start converts a reviewer's likely objection into a stated methodological contribution, and it is nearly free -- one extra sampler setting per arm.

followup_openings.target_paper: DiFFPO (arXiv 2510.02212; NeurIPS 2025 ER Workshop, rejected from ICLR 2026); The Path Matters / TraceLock (arXiv 2605.24697, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Both attack the quality-compute tradeoff purely as inference-time control over fixed weights -- DiFFPO RL-trains a per-prompt unmasking threshold, TraceLock trains a plug-in commitment controller for a frozen backbone. A frozen backbone can only reorder or gate which of its existing predictions are committed; it cannot change what the denoiser predicts when told it has 64 steps instead of 512. Neither paper reports the very-low-budget regime where quality collapses (DiFFPO evaluates math and planning; TraceLock reports a quality-step tradeoff but from a frozen generator), and neither prices its controller's own forward passes inside the NFE it claims to reduce.
followup_openings.our_fix: Position arm A as the weights-side counterpart and make the comparison explicit: measure how far a budget-conditioned denoiser moves the frontier at B<=128, where our own sweep puts flat diffusion at .018/.029 pass@1+ -- a regime a commitment policy cannot rescue because the underlying per-step predictions are wrong, not merely mis-ordered. Report all costs in cumulative_model_tokens so any controller overhead would be visible if we later add one.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It cleanly separates two mechanisms that the literature currently conflates under 'making dLLMs fast': changing what the model predicts vs changing which predictions get committed. If they turn out to be additive, that is a roadmap; if redundant, it saves the field from stacking both.

followup_openings.target_paper: Expert-Choice Routing Enables Adaptive Computation in Diffusion Language Models / EC-DLM (arXiv 2604.01622)
followup_openings.defect: EC-DLM finds that allocating more expert capacity to LOW-mask-ratio (late) denoising steps is optimal under matched FLOPs, with the mechanistic explanation that low-mask-ratio tokens show order-of-magnitude higher learning efficiency. But this is established only for MoE expert capacity, only under FLOP matching, and never as guidance for the training-time noise-level distribution of a dense model -- despite being exactly the quantity our trajectory-matched t-sampling has to choose.
followup_openings.our_fix: Use EC-DLM's finding as a falsifiable prior on our logged trajectories: it predicts that the realized mask-rate trajectory should be weighted toward late (low-mask) t, whereas FS-DFM's best h-policy (TB-20) boosts the largest steps, i.e. the early/coarse end. Log the realized per-step mask-rate trajectory at each B, then report which end of the trajectory the gain actually comes from by comparing trajectory-matched t against an early-weighted and a late-weighted variant. This turns a free hyperparameter into a tested hypothesis and reconciles two papers that currently point in opposite directions.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It resolves whether 'match the sampler's trajectory' means 'oversample coarse states' or 'oversample nearly-clean states' -- a disagreement between two pre-cutoff papers that nobody has adjudicated for dense masked diffusion, and it gives the trajectory-only arm a principled design rather than an arbitrary one.

related_work.citation: Karimi Monsefi, A., Bhendawade, N., Ciosici, M. R., Culver, D., Zhang, Y., Belousova, I. FS-DFM: Fast and Accurate Long Text Generation with Few-Step Diffusion Language Models. arXiv:2509.20624 (v1 2025-09-24; v5 2026-04-11).
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster. Verified on OpenReview api2: note ue1zFeD275, venue field 'ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid 'ICLR.cc/2026/Conference', invitations include Submission1778/-/Camera_Ready_Revision. arXiv comment independently states 'Accepted to ICLR 2026'.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE decisive prior work. Explicitly conditions the generator on its step budget: 'We expose the step budget h as an explicit conditioning signal to the DFM generator so the model learns transitions calibrated to the intended number of sampling steps'; 'We make the generator step-aware by conditioning on the intended step size h alongside time t, i.e. l = theta(x_t, t; h).' Contribution list: '(i) conditioning on a user-specified step budget and training such that one large move agrees with many small ones.' Discrete flow matching (CTMC), pretrain-then-finetune, EMA shortcut teacher (RK-2/RK-4), plus a Cumulative Scalar update. Trains h from a log grid {2^k}, k=-10..0; one checkpoint serves budgets S=2^k, k=0..10. 8 steps reaches PPL parity with a 1024-step DFM baseline (128x fewer steps).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Model sizes 0.169B/1.3B/1.7B only, trained FROM SCRATCH on FineWeb-Edu with a GPT-2 tokenizer -- no retrofit of a public pretrained checkpoint, and no 7B. Metrics are gpt2-large PPL, entropy, token accuracy, and MAUVE on WikiText-103; zero code, zero functional correctness, zero pass@1 (grep for HumanEval/MBPP returns nothing). Conditioning is a continuous scalar in a purpose-built architecture, never a discrete vocabulary token on a frozen-vocab model. Limitations section concedes instruction-following/QA/reasoning 'remain to be done' and names the absence of public discrete-flow checkpoints as a barrier; future work lists 'adaptive, position-aware step schedules and budget controllers' as unbuilt.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The headline conditioning mechanism is NEVER ablated. Appendix E.1 varies only h-sampling WEIGHTS (TB-10/TB-20/pure-uniform/geometric/annealed-geometric); Table 1 isolates only the Cumulative Scalar. No arm holds the conditioning input constant while keeping the changed h-distribution, so few-step gains are not attributable to conditioning vs the shifted step-size distribution vs the large-step EMA teacher -- three interventions introduced as a bundle. (2) Admits an unexplained ceiling regression: 'The slight accuracy dip at very large NFEs likely reflects train-test mismatch: the model and shortcut teacher are optimized for large h, so many small steps accumulate discretization/renormalization bias and under-use the step-aware conditioning' -- speculative ('likely'), never quantified, never fixed, and plausibly caused by their own best policy TB-20 (20x boost on the largest step). This is exactly the anytime-property failure mode. (3) Cost reported as NFE, not tokens attended; the shortcut teacher costs 2-4 extra forward passes per training step, amortized only by appeal to lifetime inference savings (E.2). (4) Claims to 'match' a 1024-step baseline on a reference-LM PPL, a metric compatible with degenerate-but-fluent output -- their own Figure 8 shows LLaDA/Dream emitting repeated ', the,' at low steps, so the metric's discriminative power in this regime is questionable.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 date, comment); full PDF v5 downloaded to /tmp/fsdfm.pdf and text-extracted to /tmp/fsdfm.txt (27 pages, 116513 chars) and grepped for the conditioning mechanism, ablation scope, t/h sampling policy, training details (App. C.3), and metric list; OpenReview api2 /notes/search for venueid and Camera_Ready_Revision invitation.

related_work.citation: Consistent Diffusion Language Models (CDLM), introducing Multi-Path Discrete Consistency (MPDC). arXiv:2605.00161 (v1 2026-04-30; v2 2026-05-30).
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026. OpenReview api2 search returns venue 'ICML 2026 regular', venueid 'ICML.cc/2026/Conference' (a separate record shows an earlier ICLR 2026 Rejected_Submission of the same title). arXiv comment: 'ICML 2026'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Trains a denoiser to be path-invariant in expectation across exact posterior bridges linking any two noise levels -- single-stage, no pretrained teacher required. Claims to recover masked diffusion, continuous consistency models, and progressive/discrete distillation as analytic limits of one view. Reports SOTA on conditional and unconditional text generation across sampling budgets, with largest gains in the few-step regime, beating even multi-stage distilled baselines.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Crucially it does NOT condition on a budget: 'The number of steps in this iterative process is a flexible hyperparameter at inference time and is decoupled from the training formulation.' So it is the strongest existing demonstration that one model can be good across budgets WITHOUT any conditioning signal -- i.e. the natural strong baseline for our arm B, and direct evidence against FS-DFM's implicit claim that conditioning is what buys budget-flexibility. No code evaluation (grep for HumanEval/MBPP/LLaDA/Dream/7B all return zero); metrics are gpt2-large PPL and entropy at 32/64-bit sampling precision on unconditional 1024-token generation.
related_work.known_defects: Reports NFE explicitly in preference to wall-clock ('We report NFE rather than wall-clock latency, which depends on implementation details') -- defensible, but it means no token-attended or latency accounting exists, and NFE hides the per-step cost differences that matter when comparing against a flat-canvas baseline. No functional-correctness metric and no 7B-scale or code-domain result, so the claim 'best single-stage model across budgets' is untested where a single token error voids the sample. Comparison against distilled baselines is on PPL/entropy only; entropy is offered as evidence of 'healthier' samples without a task-level check.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; full PDF v2 downloaded to /tmp/cdlm.pdf and text-extracted (24 pages, 96194 chars), grepped for conditioning/budget/HumanEval/MBPP/7B/step-count decoupling; OpenReview api2 /notes/search for ICML 2026 venueid.

related_work.citation: The Path Matters: Learning a Token-Commitment Policy for Diffusion Language Models (TraceLock). arXiv:2605.24697 (v1 2026-05-23).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. No OpenReview venue record found; no arXiv comment naming a venue. Code at github.com/BobSun98/TraceLock.
related_work.what_it_covers: A lightweight plug-in controller that learns which proposed tokens to commit at each step for a FROZEN diffusion LM, self-supervised by 'future stability' (a proposal is labelled stable if it matches the final token after the full trace completes). Claims one controller, once trained for a backbone, deploys across local-window widths, generation lengths, and step budgets without retraining. Evaluated on QA, math reasoning, and code generation; claims improved quality-step tradeoff and that decisions are not reducible to scalar confidence.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Weights stay frozen, so the denoiser never learns budget-appropriate behaviour -- the controller can only reorder/gate existing predictions, not change what the model predicts when given 64 steps instead of 512. Leaves entirely open whether conditioning the weights themselves adds anything on top of a learned commitment policy, and whether the two are additive or redundant.
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent, so it does not preempt us. Its 'deploys across step budgets without retraining' generalisation claim is the exact place a weights-side comparison bites: a frozen backbone cannot recover in the regime where per-step predictions are themselves wrong rather than mis-ordered. Cost accounting does not visibly price the controller's own forward passes inside the step budget it claims to improve. Code-generation results are reported but the benchmark/metric granularity is not established at the level of EvalPlus pass@1+.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (v1 date, abstract, no venue comment); OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned no venue record.

related_work.citation: CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models. arXiv:2607.24763 (v1 2026-06-04).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv comment is only 'updated version'; OpenReview api2 search for the title returned no matching venue record (only an unrelated COMPUTE 2024 paper).
related_work.what_it_covers: Argues that seven recent remasking papers evaluate under incompatible settings and that their strategy rankings are largely incomparable. Standardises actual NFE, enforces multi-metric reporting, and controls stochasticity across 7 remasking strategies on LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base at 4 stochasticity levels and 3 step budgets. Finds temperature explains the majority of MAUVE variance, compute-matched comparison reverses several published rankings, and informed remasking is in tension with stochastic unmasking. Leaderboard over 12 open-weight MDLMs, 150M-8B.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Audits only INFERENCE-time remasking strategies; never applies the same compute-matching and stochasticity control to training-side interventions such as budget conditioning or trajectory-matched noise sampling. Metrics remain MAUVE/PPL on OpenWebText and LM1B -- no functional-correctness surface, so it cannot say whether code-domain few-step claims are similarly artifactual.
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent, so no preemption. It is more ally than obstacle: it independently establishes the accounting discipline our candidate needs (actual-NFE matching, explicit stochasticity control), and its temperature finding is the distributional analogue of our own measured top_p 1.0->0.95 = +14.6 HumanEval points. Its own gap -- training-side interventions and executable metrics -- is directly ours to fill. Caveat: since it is a preprint whose venue we could not verify, it should be cited as a preprint and not leaned on for authority.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and full abstract; OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned no venue record for the title.

related_work.citation: Zhao, H., Liang, D., Tang, W., Yao, D., Kallus, N. DiFFPO: Training Diffusion LLMs to Reason Fast and Furious via Reinforcement Learning. arXiv:2510.02212 (v1 2025-10-02).
related_work.venue_status: Workshop paper / rejected from a main venue. OpenReview api2: 'NeurIPS 2025 ER Workshop' (venueid NeurIPS.cc/2025/Workshop/ER) AND 'Submitted to ICLR 2026' with venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Rejected_Submission. NOT a main-conference paper -- the candidate's framing should not treat it as one.
related_work.what_it_covers: Unified RL framework for dLLMs: off-policy surrogate policies with two-stage likelihood approximation plus importance-sampling correction, and joint training of an efficient sampler/controller in which the model learns to adaptively allocate an inference threshold per prompt. Reports better accuracy at lower NFE than training the model alone, framed as improving the inference-time-compute Pareto frontier. Benchmarks: math and planning.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The learned object is a per-prompt threshold controller over otherwise-unchanged generation behaviour, not a budget input to the weights. No code-generation benchmark, no functional-correctness metric, and no report of the very-low-budget regime where quality collapses. Whether the denoiser itself can be trained to know its budget is untouched.
related_work.known_defects: Venue status is weaker than the candidate implies (workshop + ICLR 2026 rejection), so it is citable as motivation but not as established main-conference prior art. Improvements are reported in NFE without pricing the controller's own evaluations. Domain restricted to math/planning, so the Pareto-frontier claim is unverified where output must execute. RL-based, hence high variance and expensive to reproduce -- a straightforward SFT-side comparison (our arms) is a cheaper and more controlled probe of the same tradeoff.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title/authors/citation_date 2025-10-02, citation_online_date 2026-01-10) and arXiv API; OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned both the NeurIPS 2025 ER Workshop record and the ICLR 2026 Rejected_Submission record.

related_work.citation: Expert-Choice Routing Enables Adaptive Computation in Diffusion Language Models (EC-DLM). arXiv:2604.01622 (v1 2026-04-02; v3 2026-08-03).
related_work.venue_status: arXiv comment states 'Accepted at COLM 2026'. NOT independently verifiable via OpenReview api2 search (COLM records did not surface; the only hit was the unrelated EC-DIT, ICLR 2025 Poster). Treat the COLM 2026 acceptance as an author claim pending proceedings.
related_work.what_it_covers: Shows expert-choice routing suits dLLMs better than token-choice (deterministic load balancing, higher throughput, faster convergence), then introduces timestep-dependent expert capacity. Key empirical finding: allocating MORE capacity to low-mask-ratio steps is consistently best under matched FLOPs, explained by low-mask-ratio tokens showing order-of-magnitude higher learning efficiency. Also retrofits pretrained token-choice DLMs to expert-choice by swapping only the router. Code at github.com/zhangshuibai/EC-DLM.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Compute is varied by timestep through MoE expert CAPACITY, not by conditioning the model on a step budget, and the finding is established only under FLOP matching for MoE architectures. It gives no guidance for the training-time noise-level distribution of a dense model -- precisely the free parameter our trajectory-matched t-sampling must set.
related_work.known_defects: Its 'more capacity late (low mask ratio)' conclusion points the opposite way from FS-DFM's best h-policy (TB-20, boosting the largest/coarsest steps), and nobody has adjudicated the disagreement for dense masked diffusion. Restricted to MoE, so transfer to dense 7B is assumed rather than shown. Venue claim rests on an arXiv comment only.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and abstract; OpenReview api2 /notes/search found no COLM 2026 record for the title (only EC-DIT, ICLR 2025).

related_work.citation: MDPO: Overcoming the Training-Inference Divide of Masked Diffusion Language Models. arXiv:2508.13148 (v1 2025-08-18; v2 2025-09-25).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; withdrawn from ICLR 2026. OpenReview api2: venue 'ICLR 2026 Conference Withdrawn Submission', venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Withdrawn_Submission.
related_work.what_it_covers: Names the exact motivating discrepancy behind our arm B: at inference MDLMs progressively reveal structure with monotonically fewer masked tokens, whereas training masks tokens at random -- 'this discrepancy ... has been largely overlooked by previous works.' Frames denoising-trajectory learning as sequential decision-making and applies RL (Masked Diffusion Policy Optimization) to train under the same progressive refining schedule used at inference. Also contributes Running Confidence Remasking as a training-free inference swap. Matches prior SOTA with 60x fewer gradient updates; +9.6% MATH500, +54.2% Countdown.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The fix is RL over trajectories, not a cheap supervised change to the noise-level distribution, and the model is never given its step budget as an input. No step-budget conditioning, no anytime/multi-budget claim, no code benchmark, and no low-NFE Pareto reporting. Leaves open whether the far simpler intervention -- draw t from the sampler's realized mask-rate trajectory during ordinary SFT -- captures most of the benefit.
related_work.known_defects: Establishes that trajectory mismatch matters but conflates it with RL machinery, so the value of trajectory matching per se is not isolated -- our arm B does isolate it, at SFT cost. Withdrawn from ICLR 2026, so cite as preprint. Benchmarks are math/planning only. Important for framing honesty: the candidate's 'standard MDLM training samples t uniformly, which matches no actual sampler trajectory' observation is NOT novel -- MDPO states it as its central premise a year earlier.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and abstract; OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned the ICLR 2026 Withdrawn_Submission venueid.

related_work.citation: Frans, K., et al. One Step Diffusion via Shortcut Models. arXiv:2410.12557 (v1 2024-10-16).
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2025 Oral. Verified on OpenReview api2: venue 'ICLR 2025 Oral', venueid ICLR.cc/2025/Conference.
related_work.what_it_covers: The originating shortcut-model idea that FS-DFM imports (cited as Frans et al., 2025): condition the network on the step size in addition to the timestep, and train so that one large step agrees with the composition of two half-steps, yielding one-model-many-budgets generation without multi-stage distillation. Continuous domains (images).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Continuous diffusion/flow over images; nothing about discrete text, masked diffusion, tokenizers, or functional correctness. Does not address how to expose a budget to a pretrained language model with a fixed vocabulary, nor whether a discrete in-sequence token can serve the role a continuous scalar plays there.
related_work.known_defects: Not a defect of the paper so much as a framing constraint on ours: because step-size conditioning has been an ICLR Oral since 2024 in the continuous setting and was ported to discrete flow matching by FS-DFM, 'condition the denoiser on its step budget' cannot be presented as a new mechanism in any domain. Our contribution must be the isolation experiment, the masked-diffusion/7B/code transfer, and the anytime accounting -- not the idea.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata; OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned 'ICLR 2025 Oral' with venueid ICLR.cc/2025/Conference.

related_work.citation: Diffusion Language Models Are Natively Length-Aware. arXiv:2603.06123 (v1 2026-03-06).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; rejected from ICML 2026. OpenReview api2: venue 'Submitted to ICML 2026', venueid ICML.cc/2026/Conference/Rejected_Submission.
related_work.what_it_covers: The closest work on adapting dLLM compute to the instance rather than to a user budget: shows the latent prompt representation already encodes the required output length, and proposes a zero-shot mechanism to crop the canvas before generation, cutting diffusion steps. Evaluated on GSM8K, HumanEval, IfEval, LongFormQA; reports large FLOP reductions with no statistically significant degradation and improvements on 2 of 4 tasks.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Adapts the canvas LENGTH, not the step budget, and does so zero-shot at inference with no training and no conditioning input. Orthogonal and composable with budget conditioning; also directly relevant to our flat-canvas cost accounting, since our matched Plain-SFT control pays 685/604 tokens per step precisely because the full 512-token canvas is re-attended every step.
related_work.known_defects: Rejected from ICML 2026, so cite as preprint. 'No statistically significant degradation' is a null result used as a safety claim -- power is not established, so absence of harm is weakly supported. Useful as a cost-accounting reference: it makes explicit that flat-canvas per-step cost is a design choice rather than a law, which strengthens our decision to price arms in cumulative_model_tokens rather than NFE.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and abstract; OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned the ICML 2026 Rejected_Submission venueid.

related_work.citation: OPTD: On-Policy Transition Distillation with Consistency-Guided Adaptive Compression for Few-Step Diffusion Language Models. arXiv:2608.02942 (v1 2026-08-03).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. arXiv comment: '9 pages, 4 figures, 5 tables'. No venue record.
related_work.what_it_covers: Four days before our cutoff-relevant present, it articulates the state-drift argument our arm B rests on: existing few-step distillation builds supervision on OFF-POLICY trajectories, but at inference the student's early parallel commitments change the context of later predictions, so visited states drift from supervised ones -- 'precisely when step compression is most aggressive.' Proposes on-policy transition distillation with a frozen question-only teacher, confidence-ordered future candidates, longest-prefix selection preserving the teacher's rollout outcome, plus a set-bottleneck objective and frozen-teacher KL anchor.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Distillation-based and does not condition on a budget; the student is trained for aggressive compression rather than to be told its budget at inference. Does not run a conditioning-vs-distribution isolation, and does not report an anytime property (low-budget gain without high-budget loss).
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent (2026-08-03), so no preemption -- but it is the clearest signal that the on-policy/trajectory-matching argument is being independently converged on right now, which raises the urgency of the isolation experiment and lowers the value of framing trajectory matching itself as our novelty. Requires a teacher and a rollout-verification loop, so it is far more expensive than drawing t from a logged trajectory; that cost gap is our efficiency argument.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and full abstract.

related_work.citation: Dream-Coder 7B: An Open Diffusion Language Model for Code. arXiv:2509.01142 (v1 2025-09-01).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (no venue comment on arXiv; no OpenReview record surfaced).
related_work.what_it_covers: The base and instruct checkpoints our experiment builds on (both present on disk at models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B and models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B). Adapts a pretrained AR checkpoint to discrete diffusion with a continuous-time weighted cross-entropy objective; SFT with random truncation and a padding penalty against padding pathologies, then RL with verifiable rewards. Reports emergent any-order decoding (sketch-first / left-to-right / interleaved).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Provides no step-budget conditioning and, to our knowledge, no published pass@1-vs-step-budget curve at the granularity we measured in-house (.018/.140/.555/.707/.707 on HumanEval+ at NFE 64/128/256/512/1024, with exactly zero gain 512->1024, replicated on MBPP+). That measured saturation-plus-collapse profile on the public checkpoint is our own contribution and the motivation for the arms.
related_work.known_defects: Not a defect but a positioning asset: because the checkpoint is public and its step-budget behaviour is not characterised in the paper, our NFE sweep is a reproducible reference curve others can check, and the retrofit setting (frozen vocabulary, existing weights) is the deployment-realistic regime FS-DFM's from-scratch study cannot speak to.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and abstract; local checkpoint directories confirmed present on the wzc1 disk under /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/models/.

related_work.citation: Taming Masked Diffusion Language Models via Consistency Trajectory Reinforcement Learning with Fewer Decoding Steps (EOSER + Ascending Step-Size, CJ-GRPO). arXiv:2509.23924 (v1 2025-09-28).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; withdrawn from ICLR 2026. OpenReview api2: venue 'ICLR 2026 Conference Withdrawn Submission', venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Withdrawn_Submission. Code at github.com/yjyddq/EOSER-ASS-RL.
related_work.what_it_covers: Attacks the same rollout/optimization trajectory inconsistency: proposes EOS Early Rejection and an Ascending Step-Size decoding scheduler to make full diffusion-style decoding competitive with fewer steps, plus Consistency Trajectory GRPO that enforces consistency between rollout and optimization trajectories and reduces skip-step optimization error. Reasoning tasks (math, planning).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The step schedule is hand-designed (ascending step size) rather than a conditioning input, and there is no budget token, no anytime claim, and no code/functional-correctness evaluation. Notably it independently establishes that the SHAPE of the step-size schedule matters -- which is the free parameter our logged-trajectory t-sampling instantiates from data rather than by hand.
related_work.known_defects: Withdrawn from ICLR 2026; cite as preprint. Bundles a decoding scheduler, an EOS heuristic, and an RL objective, so the contribution of the ascending schedule alone is not isolated -- the same bundling defect as FS-DFM, and further evidence that a clean single-variable decomposition is the missing methodological contribution in this cluster.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata and abstract; OpenReview api2 /notes/search returned the ICLR 2026 Withdrawn_Submission venueid.

diff.verification_notes:
MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the candidate's why_now is factually wrong on its central novelty premise. It states "Searches for budget-conditioned / step-budget-conditioned diffusion LM training returned zero hits" and "None makes the budget an input the weights are conditioned on." FS-DFM (arXiv 2509.20624v1, 2025-09-24 -- eight months PRE-cutoff, ICLR 2026 Poster, public Apple code at github.com/apple/ml-fs-dfm) does exactly that, in those words: "We expose the step budget h as an explicit conditioning signal to the DFM generator." I found it via arXiv API on the query abs:"step budget" AND abs:"diffusion language model"; the candidate's search evidently used only the hyphenated phrase "budget-conditioned", which returns nothing in this literature because the field's term of art is "step-aware" / "shortcut model". Any draft built on the "nobody conditions on the budget" framing will be desk-rejected. Second correction: the candidate's observation that "standard MDLM training samples t uniformly, which matches no actual sampler trajectory" is also not novel -- MDPO (arXiv 2508.13148, 2025-08-18) states it as its central premise. Third correction: DiFFPO is described as prior work supporting the gap, but its venue status is NeurIPS 2025 ER Workshop plus an ICLR 2026 rejection, not a main-conference paper.

WHAT I COULD NOT VERIFY. (a) EC-DLM's "Accepted at COLM 2026" rests on the arXiv comment alone; OpenReview api2 /notes/search surfaced no COLM 2026 record for the title (only the unrelated EC-DIT, ICLR 2025 Poster). COLM records do not appear to be reachable through the same api2 search path I used, so this is an author claim, not a verified venue. (b) CaRE (2607.24763) and TraceLock (2605.24697) returned no OpenReview venue records at all; both are treated as preprints. (c) FastDiSS's arXiv comment claims "accepted by ACL Findings (ACL 2026)" but OpenReview shows only ACL ARR 2025 May and ARR 2026 January submission records -- ARR records do not carry the final acceptance decision, so I did not treat FastDiSS as a verified ACL 2026 paper and left it out of the related-work list as it is a seq2seq continuous-diffusion paper with no bearing on the claim. (d) I did not read TraceLock, DiFFPO, EC-DLM, MDPO, or OPTD in full PDF -- only arXiv abstracts and metadata -- so my characterisation of their internals (e.g. that DiFFPO does not price its controller's forward passes, that TraceLock's code-generation metric is not EvalPlus pass@1+) is inference from the abstracts and should be confirmed before appearing in a related-work section. Only FS-DFM and CDLM were verified at full-text level (PDFs extracted to /tmp/fsdfm.txt, 27pp/116513 chars, and /tmp/cdlm.txt, 24pp/96194 chars, then grepped for conditioning mechanism, ablation scope, metrics, model sizes, and t/h sampling policy). (e) One extraction caveat: the FS-DFM and CDLM PDFs de-ligature badly (spaces collapse, e.g. "thestep budgethas"), so I relied on multiple overlapping keyword windows rather than exact quotation of equations; the sentences I quote were each recovered in at least two independent windows.

ASSET CHECK (all confirmed on the wzc1 disk under /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft): scaffold_coder/model_sampler.py (30224 bytes) exists; scaffold_coder/tokenizer_utils.py defines extend_tokenizer at line 49 and initialize_model_token_rows at line 137, so the new-token embedding-init path claimed in assets_needed is real; data/scaffold_edu_v0 exists; models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B exists. I did NOT verify that model_sampler.py is the sampler actually used by scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py, nor that it exposes a per-step mask-rate hook -- the "~40 lines of instrumentation" estimate is unaudited.

CLAIM ON WEAKEST EVIDENCE: my assertion that FS-DFM "never holds the conditioning signal constant while keeping the changed step-size distribution" is an argument from absence over the full text. I grepped Appendix E.1 (the only ablation section) and Table 1, and found only h-sampling-weight policies and the Cumulative Scalar isolated. I cannot rule out an ablation in a rebuttal revision or in the OpenReview discussion threads, which I did not read. Before publishing the "missing control" framing, read the FS-DFM OpenReview reviews and rebuttal (note ue1zFeD275, ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Submission1778) -- reviewers plausibly asked for exactly this, and the answer would either confirm the gap or hand us their result.

blocking_gaps: ARM B IS PROVABLY THE IDENTITY OF ARM C -- the experiment's load-bearing cell measures nothing. The sampler that produced the entire NFE sweep is `model.diffusion_generate` in /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B/generation_utils.py, whose `_sample` sets `timesteps = torch.linspace(1, eps, steps+1)` (L414) and commits `number_transfer_tokens = int(num_mask_token * (1 - s/t))` (L486). I simulated this exactly: the realized visited mask-rate at step i is t_i = 1 - i/B to within int()-rounding (max deviation 0.0020 at every B). That is a uniform GRID on (0,1]. Sup-norm distance of the realized visited-rate distribution to Uniform(0,1): D=0.033 (B=32), 0.018 (64), 0.010 (128), 0.006 (256), 0.004 (512) -- all far below the 0.05 critical values 0.240/0.170/0.120/0.085/0.060. Meanwhile the trainer ALREADY draws t ~ Uniform(0,1): scaffold_coder/sft_dataset.py L340 `t = float(torch.rand((), generator=generator).item())`. So 'draw t from the LOGGED trajectory for that B' is numerically identical to the existing uniform-t SFT for every B<=512. Arm B == Arm C. The 3-way decomposition the positioning calls 'the missing cell FS-DFM never ran' collapses to a 2-way comparison, and the 'trajectory-matched t-sampling' fallback claim (the thing that survives if conditioning dies) is dead on arrival. Only B=1024 differs (50.2% of visited states sit at mask-rate 1.0, D=0.502) and that is the degenerate budget.

THE MOTIVATING '512->1024 EXACTLY ZERO GAIN' IS A SAMPLER ARTIFACT, NOT MODEL SATURATION. runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus_r2/solutions.jsonl vs runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe1024/solutions.jsonl: 163/164 solutions are BYTE-IDENTICAL, and both evalplus.out report pass@1 0.762 base / 0.707 plus. Reason: the sweep scripts (scripts/_run_nfe_sweep_wzc1.sh, scripts/_run_nfe_lowend_wzc1.sh) all pass --max-new-tokens 512, so the canvas is L=512, and `int(n*(1-s/t))` floors to 0 once B>L. At B=1024, 513/1024 forward passes commit ZERO tokens -- pure waste. So 'the model wastes all compute above 512' is true but the cause is that NFE cannot exceed canvas length, not that the denoiser has saturated. Any draft that presents the 512->1024 plateau as evidence of a model property (rather than of a schedule flooring) gets killed on sight. Fix the framing or drop the datum.

THE LOW-NFE REGIME IS ALREADY OWNED BY A MATCHED AR BASELINE, AND THIS REPO HAS ALREADY MEASURED IT. git 1170ae6 and DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md Retractions 4 and 5 (which the candidate and positioning never mention): Qwen2.5-Coder-7B base -- architecturally IDENTICAL to Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B (same hidden 3584 / 28 layers / 28 heads / 4 KV heads / intermediate 18944 / vocab 152064 / rope_theta 1e6, differing only by mask_token_id 151666) -- scores HE+ .524 / MBPP+ .648 at 204 / 101 mean tokens_fed. The candidate's entire value proposition is 'the low-NFE regime at B<=128 where our sweep says flat diffusion scores .018/.029'. A matched AR model scores .524/.648 there at ~1/70th the cost of even scaffold Medium. Retraction 5 shows AR also wins on infilling (.7638 vs .7018 at 8.5x fewer tokens). So the target regime is not empty -- it is dominated. 'Anytime diffusion' is only interesting if it is anytime-competitive with the AR point, and no version of this experiment as scoped tests that.

THE TRAINING ENVIRONMENT DOES NOT EXIST ON THIS DISK AND CANNOT BE REBUILT FOR THE LOCAL GPUs. `.venv_dream` is gone and `outputs/` is gone from /apdcephfs_wzc1/.../dllm_draft (both are in .gitignore, so nothing is recoverable from git). Neither /opt/conda/envs/dllm-env nor the surviving .venv_b200 has hydra, omegaconf, peft, flash_attn, tensordict, or verl -- I tested the full import chain and it fails at the first line. scaffold_coder/training/scaffold_sft_trainer.py imports src.trainer.fsdp_sft_expand_trainer, which is vendor/DreamOn/src/trainer/fsdp_sft_expand_trainer.py and hard-imports flash_attn at module level (L30) and hardcodes attn_implementation='flash_attention_2' (L293). The only flash_attn wheel on disk is wheels/flash_attn-2.7.3+cu12torch2.5cxx11abiFALSE-cp311-cp311 -- built for torch 2.5, while local torch is 2.11. Decisive constraint: the working `.venv_dream` on the zwfy6 nodes pins torch 2.5.1+cu124 whose arch list is ['sm_50'...'sm_90'] -- NO sm_100. Local L20A and .252 B200 are sm_100. So the trainer runs ONLY on the H20 nodes (sm_90); the B200-class cards are unusable for it without building a new flash_attn for torch 2.11/sm_100.

THE KILL CRITERION IS 4-6x INSIDE THE NOISE FLOOR. It fires on 2-point and 3-point differences. At n=164 (HumanEval+) with one sample per task, binomial SE at p~0.2 is 3.23 points (95% CI half-width 6.34); the minimum detectable unpaired difference at alpha .05 / power .8 is 12.8 points on HE+ and 8.4 points on MBPP+. Every branch of the stated criterion -- 'within 2 points of C', 'loses more than 3 points at NFE 512', 'A ~= B within noise' -- would trigger on sampling noise alone at T=0.1. Worse, the low-NFE window is a floor-effect region: I measured final_parseable at 5/164 (NFE 32), 10/164 (NFE 64), 52/164 (NFE 128) for the strong Instruct model, and arm C's own published low-NFE numbers are .000 at nfe64 / .0488 at nfe128. Differences cannot be resolved where all arms sit near zero.

feas.risk: A floor-effect null that is uninterpretable, produced in the exact window the claim targets. The gain is supposed to appear at B<=128, but that is where every arm is near zero and mostly emitting non-code: I measured final_parseable at 5/164 (NFE 32), 10/164 (NFE 64), 52/164 (NFE 128) even for the strong Instruct model, with failures being degenerate repetition ("The the the the the the"), and arm C's own low-NFE numbers are .000 at nfe64 / .0488 at nfe128. So all three arms will plausibly land within 0-5 points of each other at NFE 32/64, which the stated 2-point criterion reads as "conditioning bought nothing" -- but with a 12.8-point (HE+) / 8.4-point (MBPP+) minimum detectable difference, that reading is unsupported either way. The result would be a null that cannot distinguish "conditioning does not bind" from "the benchmark cannot resolve anything here", i.e. exactly the kind of finding that gets retracted later. The confounded variant is just as likely: arm A receives BOTH five new trainable embedding rows (initialize_model_token_rows trains them) AND a changed t-distribution, so if A wins, attribution requires arm B to share A's t-distribution exactly -- and in the candidate as written B instead shares C's, which is also A's, because all three are uniform. Under the original design a win by A is uninterpretable and a tie is vacuous. Secondary risk: even a clean win is measured against a ceiling of .2195/.2434 (arm C), not .707/.680, so "without sacrificing the NFE-512 ceiling" is untestable as stated -- and the whole frontier sits far below the already-measured matched-AR point of .524/.648 at ~200 tokens_fed.
feas.required_control: A pre-registered, pre-GPU DISTRIBUTIONAL SEPARATION ASSAY on the dataloaders, plus a forward-hook receipt that the conditioning signal reaches the model -- run and passed BEFORE any training step. Two assertions, both cheap and both CPU-only. (1) SEPARATION: PlainMaskedSFTDataset already returns "t" in its batch dict (scaffold_coder/sft_dataset.py, `"t": torch.tensor(t, dtype=torch.float32)`), so iterate >=50,000 samples from each of arm A, arm B, arm C and assert the two-sample KS distance between every pair of empirical t-histograms EXCEEDS a pre-registered threshold (use 0.05, comfortably above the 0.004-0.033 grid-vs-uniform deviation I measured, and well above the ~0.009 critical value at n=50k). Had this existed, it would have caught the fatal defect at zero GPU cost: A's and B's "trajectory-matched" t is the same Uniform(0,1) as C's, so the assay returns D~0.00 and the arms are proven identical before a single GPU-hour is spent. (2) DELIVERY: register a forward_pre_hook on the model and assert that the [budget=B] token id appears exactly once per sequence in the input_ids the model actually receives, that its value VARIES across a batch in arm A, and that it is CONSTANT in arm B -- then log the realized counts. This repo has already been burned by exactly this failure mode: DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md Retraction 5 records that DreamOn's `mask_expansion=True` and `delete_eos_token=True` were silently swallowed by **kwargs and "根本不是参数", invalidating every DreamOn number's stated configuration. Together these two assertions are the direct analogue of the three prior retractions -- (1) is the "verifier that compared nothing" failure, here a CONTROL ARM THAT IS THE IDENTITY OF THE THING IT CONTROLS FOR, and (2) is the "pipeline stage that silently discarded its input" failure, here a conditioning token that never reaches the weights. Neither can be checked after the fact from a pass@1 number, which is precisely why both must be gates, not post-hoc diagnostics. Mirror the discipline on the cost side by keeping scripts/make_pareto_figures.py's proc() accessor (which reads `process` OR `failure_process`) so the third retraction cannot recur.

lens.title: Execution-localized self-repair training: teaching a code diffusion model to edit, with unit tests choosing where
lens.claim: Training a masked diffusion code model on its OWN failing drafts, with the remasked region localized by execution feedback (which unit test failed, and which statements the failing trace touched), yields a larger low-NFE repair gain than the same pipeline with confidence-localized or randomly-localized remasking at matched training compute.
lens.why_now: This is the direct repair of our own worst methodological failure. Our refinement grid's 'restart' policy regenerated from the prompt and DISCARDED the draft, so it measured Dream-Coder-Instruct rather than any editing ability -- two headline findings were withdrawn (each tier's hidden-pass rate on its own routed set matched the tiny run's on the same tasks to within -0.008..-0.023, pure noise). Masked diffusion's one structural advantage over AR is editing arbitrary positions under bidirectional context, and we threw it away in both arms we built. The closest prior work is all concurrent and none of it uses execution: SCOPE (2606.01026, 2026-05-31) simulates its sampler's own errors on LLaDA math/general; self-generated T2T (2606.17175, 2026-06-15) replaces random vocabulary corruptions with self-generated draft errors on LLaDA2.1-mini. Both localize by the model's own signal, neither by running the program. And we now hold the asset that makes execution localization possible: 114,363 training rows each with a nonempty executable testcase field (verified 100% nonempty).
lens.experiment: Phase 1 (draft harvest): on an ~8k-row subset of data/scaffold_edu_v0/train_data.parquet, generate drafts from Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B (or Instruct) at NFE 128 using the existing 8-way sharded generator, then grade each draft with evalplus.eval.untrusted_check against the row's testcase field (the SAME grader that, post-fix, reproduced evalplus base pass@1 to three exact decimals: .000/.207/.386). Keep the failures. Phase 2 (three localizers, one pipeline): for each failing draft build a training example whose input is the draft with a region remasked and whose target is the reference solution over that region, where the region is chosen by (A) execution -- statements implicated by the failing assertion and traceback, mapped to statement node_ids via ir_json; (B) model confidence -- lowest-confidence contiguous span of matched length; (C) random -- uniformly placed span of matched length. Match token count of the remasked region across A/B/C so only the localizer varies. Phase 3: fine-tune three arms at matched steps, then grade on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ at NFE {64,128,512}, reporting pass@1 and cumulative_model_tokens including the draft pass, so the repair cost is charged honestly (this is exactly the accounting error that understated scaffold Large by 2.85x/3.69x).
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: 114,363 rows with 100%-nonempty executable testcase and entry_point columns (verified by direct inspection); ir_json statement-level node_ids to map tracebacks onto statements; evalplus untrusted_check already wired in scripts/refine_verifier_guided.py post-fix; 8-way sharded generators; the trainer. MISSING/TO BUILD: a traceback-to-statement mapper (~100 lines, the main new logic); a confidence-span extractor from sampler logits; a repair-example builder. COST DRIVER TO FLAG: Phase 1 draft harvest over 8k rows at NFE 128 is roughly 28 GPU-hours by itself (12.6 s/sample measured, /8 shards), so subset size is the knob if the budget binds.
lens.kill_criterion: Falsified if execution-localized arm A is within 2 points of confidence-localized arm B on BOTH HumanEval+ and MBPP+ at NFE 128 -- that means execution feedback adds nothing over the model's own confidence and the specific claim dies (the weaker 'self-generated repair training helps code diffusion' survives if A and B both beat C). Also falsified if all three arms fail to beat the no-repair-training baseline at matched total cumulative_model_tokens, which would mean the repair pass never pays for itself.
lens.builds_on: SCOPE (arXiv:2606.01026, 2026-05-31) and self-generated T2T editing (arXiv:2606.17175, 2026-06-15) -- both CONCURRENT, so they do not preempt us; cite and move on. What they did not test: execution as the localizer, code as the domain, EvalPlus pass@1 as the metric, and a three-way localizer ablation holding remasked-token-count fixed. This also implements the Arm C (typed subtree collapse, preserve the rest of the tree, local re-diffuse) that our own retraction identified as the only meaningful refinement design and which was never built.

related_work.citation: S. Zhang, F. Z. Peng, Y. Zhang, J. Pan, G. G. Chrysos. "Corrective Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2512.15596 (v1 2025-12-17, v2 2026-01-29).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint only. OpenReview api2 returns venue='CoRR 2025', venueid='OpenReview.net/Public_Article' (DBLP record mirror); no conference venueid, no Camera_Ready_Revision invitation. Verified via OpenReview notes/search + arXiv API.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest pre-cutoff work. Post-training objective to induce 'corrective behavior' in masked DLMs: mixes absorbing-mask corruption with uniform-replacement corruption on VISIBLE tokens so the model learns calibrated per-token confidence and can localize+repair errors in a complete program. Introduces Code Revision Benchmark (CRB): HumanEval/MBPP(+Plus) canonical programs corrupted by type-preserving operator/identifier/literal substitution, filtered by execution so every instance genuinely fails. Reports confidence gap, top-K error-localization hit rate, Pass@1 after T in {1,2,4} confidence-threshold refinement steps, plus from-scratch HumanEval/HumanEval+ Pass@1/@10. Establishes empirically that standard DLMs (Dream-7B-Base, LLaDA-8B-Base, Open-dCoder-0.5B) localize errors poorly via confidence (top-1 hit rate roughly 0.15-0.35).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: (1) Errors are SYNTHETIC uniform/type-preserving vocabulary substitutions, never the model's own failing drafts -- their own framing says inference-time errors are 'fluent, high-confidence' and different in kind. (2) Execution is used only as a FILTER to validate benchmark instances, never as the LOCALIZER that chooses the remask region during training. (3) No traceback/failing-assertion signal enters the pipeline at all. (4) Trained model is Open-dCoder-0.5B, 2000 steps; the 7B/8B models are only probed, never post-trained. (5) Fixed-length token-aligned replacement only; explicitly disclaims insertion/deletion and variable-length editing in its Limitations. (6) NO compute/NFE/token accounting anywhere -- refinement steps are counted, tokens are not, so the repair pass is never charged. (7) No localizer ablation holding remasked-token-count fixed.
related_work.known_defects: Training-corruption distribution is admitted-mismatched to deployment errors yet never tested against self-generated drafts. Only 0.5B trained -> the central claim (that a mixture objective induces corrective behavior) is unverified at 7B/8B, exactly where confidence quality was measured to be different (Dream-7B best, Open-dCoder-0.5B worst). Refinement is charged in 'steps', not tokens, so a method that re-attends the whole canvas 4x looks free; this is the same accounting flattery our own scaffold-Large retraction suffered. The mixture-probability alpha ablation is done ONLY on 0.5B and shows a non-monotone optimum (top-5 hit declines past alpha~0.7), i.e. the recipe needs per-scale retuning that is never done. CRB corruptions are type-preserving single/multi-token substitutions, an easier and more localized fault class than real generation failure.

Venue via OpenReview api2 notes/search.

related_work.citation: L. Yu, S. Zhang, Y. Fu, H. Liu, Y. Dong, G. Ver Steeg. "Revise, Don't Freeze: Sampler-Matched Training for Self-Correcting Masked Diffusion Language Models" (D3IM + SCOPE). arXiv:2606.01026.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 only, 8 pages, 2 figures, 10 tables). No OpenReview conference venueid found.
related_work.what_it_covers: D3IM, a parameter-free corrector-style sampler allowing direct visible-to-visible revision; identifies 'preservation bias' (model reproduces its own wrong committed tokens); SCOPE, a lightweight post-training procedure that SIMULATES D3IM's own sampling process to supply error-conditioned supervision. related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Localization comes from the model's own sampler simulation, never from running the program. Code is one of four benchmark families, not the object of study; uses HumanEval/MBPP base, not the Plus test suites. No execution feedback, no traceback, no statement-level structure. Absolute code numbers (29.3/30.8) are far below Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B's .707/.680, so the regime is different.
related_work.known_defects: CONCURRENT -- does not preempt. Gains reported at a single step budget (64) with 'gains that increase as more denoising steps are used', i.e. no honest cost-matched frontier. Simulated-sampler errors are still a proxy for real failure; correctness of the program is never consulted.

related_work.citation: L. Yao. "Self-Generated Error Training for Token Editing in Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2606.17175.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 only, single author). OpenReview search returned no matching submission.
related_work.what_it_covers: Identifies that LLaDA2.1's released Token-to-Token (T2T) editor is trained on RANDOM VOCABULARY corruptions while at inference it sees the model's own fluent draft errors. Proposes self-generated T2T: a no-gradient draft pass fills masked positions with predicted tokens, then a second pass supervises recovery under those self-generated corruptions. Implemented as a short LoRA continued-pretraining pass on LLaDA2.1-mini, evaluated under official Q-Mode T2T with unchanged inference parameters.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: This is exactly our Phase-1 'harvest your own drafts' idea, but (a) the corruption is self-generated token fills, NOT graded failing programs; (b) nothing is executed; (c) the region supervised is wherever the draft pass happened to fill, not a region chosen by any localizer; (d) LLaDA2.1-mini, not a 7B code model; (e) 'several benchmarks', general/reasoning, no EvalPlus pass@1; (f) no localizer ablation at all.
related_work.known_defects: CONCURRENT. Single-author preprint, no venue. Claims are hedged ('generally improves accuracy'), no per-benchmark significance, no cost accounting -- the extra no-gradient draft pass at inference is a real cost that is not charged. Its central diagnosis (train/inference corruption mismatch) is asserted from the released recipe rather than measured against a random-corruption control at matched compute.

related_work.citation: "Don't Settle Too Early: Self-Reflective Remasking for Diffusion Language Models" (RemeDi). arXiv:2509.23653.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster. Verified on OpenReview: venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference', Submission8682 with Camera_Ready_Revision invitation.
related_work.what_it_covers: A masked DLM that jointly predicts token distributions AND per-token confidence, making remasking a first-class mechanism. Trains this ability with a remask-aware pipeline: SFT teaching the model to detect and remask incorrect tokens, plus RL over full generation trajectories toward higher rewards. SOTA among open-source DLMs on multiple datasets.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The remask decision is learned from the model's own confidence/reward signal, never from program execution. General text and reasoning, not code repair; no EvalPlus, no per-statement structure, no traceback. It also does not ablate WHERE the training-time remask region comes from -- the localizer itself is never a controlled variable.
related_work.known_defects: Pre-cutoff and peer-reviewed, so it is the strongest 'remask-aware training exists' citation -- but its RL leg makes training compute hard to match against a plain SFT baseline, and the paper does not report a compute-matched confidence-vs-alternative-localizer comparison. Reward is task accuracy, so credit assignment to specific remasked positions is never verified.

related_work.citation: J. Kim, S. Kim, T. Lee, et al. "Fine-Tuning Masked Diffusion for Provable Self-Correction" (PRISM). arXiv:2510.01384.
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026. Verified on OpenReview: venue='ICML 2026 regular', venueid='ICML.cc/2026/Conference', Submission19258 with Camera_Ready_Revision. (Also an ICLR 2026 MM-Intelligence workshop poster; an earlier ICLR 2026 main-track submission is in Rejected_Submission.)
related_work.what_it_covers: PRISM: a plug-in, model-agnostic fine-tune that defines a self-correction loss provably learning per-token quality scores computed in the SAME forward pass, used to detect low-quality tokens for remasking. Demonstrated on Sudoku, unconditional text (170M), and code with LLaDA-8B.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Explicitly advertises 'without RL or a verifier' -- i.e. it is the strongest statement of the position our claim contests, and it never tests whether an actual verifier would localize better. Code is one of three domains; no EvalPlus pass@1 protocol, no cumulative-token accounting, no code-specific structure (statements, tracebacks). No ablation of localizer source at matched remasked-token count.
related_work.known_defects: The 'provable' guarantee is about learning per-token quality scores, not about downstream repair on real failures; the empirical code leg is thin (one model, one benchmark family). Because it declines to use a verifier by design, the paper cannot distinguish 'confidence is sufficient' from 'confidence is all we tried' -- an untested-regime gap that our three-way localizer ablation is built to close.

related_work.citation: "TreeDiff: AST-Guided Code Generation with Diffusion LLMs." arXiv:2508.01473 (v1 2025-08-02, v3 2026-01-06).
