related_work.what_it_covers: Replaces random token masking in TRAINING with AST-guided masking: selectively masks tokens belonging to key AST nodes so corruption aligns with syntactic structure. Fine-tunes LLaDA-8B-Instruct on ~150K samples; evaluates HumanEval(+)/MBPP(+) pass@1 against a matched 'LLaDA + Random Masking' control and AR baselines (CodeLlama 7B/13B, CodeQwen1.5-7B, DeepSeek-Coder-33B). Reports 13.3% relative improvement on HumanEval+ over random masking.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: This is the direct precedent for 'the choice of WHERE to mask during training matters for code diffusion' -- and it establishes the structural-vs-random contrast, which is our arm-C-vs-structure axis. But its localizer is purely STATIC (AST node type); nothing is executed, no unit test is consulted, no failing draft is harvested, and the task is from-scratch generation, not repair of an existing draft. Two-arm design (structural vs random) with no confidence arm and no token-count matching.
related_work.known_defects: Only a relative number (13.3%) is headlined; masked-token count is not obviously held equal between AST-masking and random-masking arms, so part of the gain could be a difference in effective corruption rate rather than in localization -- precisely the confound our matched-remasked-token-count design removes. No cost accounting. Venue is weak (workshop/preprint), so replication at another model family and with count-matching is open.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 date; full PDF downloaded and grepped for baselines/metrics/benchmarks; venue via OpenReview api2 + Semantic Scholar.

related_work.citation: "DiffuCoder: Understanding and Improving Masked Diffusion Models for Code Generation" (coupled-GRPO). arXiv:2506.20639.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster. Verified on OpenReview: venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference', Submission11408 with Camera_Ready_Revision.
related_work.what_it_covers: 7B code dLLM trained on 130B code tokens; systematic study of dLLM denoising behavior for code; coupled-GRPO RL with complementary mask noise; +4.4% on EvalPlus. Establishes that unit-test-derived reward can improve a 7B code diffusion model.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Test signal enters as a scalar RL REWARD over whole completions, never as a spatial localizer for a remask region. No draft-harvest-and-repair pipeline, no statement-level mapping, no repair-vs-no-repair cost accounting, no localizer ablation.
related_work.known_defects: Because it already shows unit tests help code diffusion via RL, it forecloses the weak version of our claim ('using unit tests helps') -- our claim must be specifically about test-derived LOCALIZATION beating confidence-derived localization at matched training compute. Its own gains are reported as EvalPlus deltas without NFE-matched frontiers.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 date; OpenReview api2 notes/search returned ICLR 2026 Poster venueid + Camera_Ready_Revision.

related_work.citation: "SelfAPR: Self-supervised Program Repair with Test Execution Diagnostics." arXiv:2203.12755; ASE 2022.
related_work.venue_status: ASE 2022 (conference). Verified via DBLP publ API: year=2022, venue=ASE, type='Conference and Workshop Papers' (plus a CoRR informal record).
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical prior art for 'use test execution diagnostics to train a repair model'. Generates 1,039,873 training samples by perturbing 17 open-source projects, EXECUTES every training sample, and encodes the extracted test-execution diagnostics into the model's INPUT REPRESENTATION so the model is steered toward the right fault type. Repairs 110/818 Defects4J bugs, beating supervised APR baselines.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Autoregressive/seq2seq encoder-decoder, Java, Defects4J -- no diffusion model, no masked denoising, no remasking. Crucially, execution diagnostics are appended as INPUT TEXT (a conditioning signal the model reads), never used to choose which positions get masked. Training samples come from rule-based perturbation of an existing program, not from the model's own graded failing drafts. No matched comparison against a confidence-localized or randomly-localized variant.
related_work.known_defects: The 'diagnostics help' claim is confounded with the self-supervised sample generation: the paper changes both the data source (project-specific perturbation) and the input representation (diagnostics) relative to prior mined-commit baselines, so the contribution of the execution signal alone is not isolated. This is the cleanest historical demonstration that our differentiator (execution signal as MASK LOCATION rather than as input text) is genuinely a different mechanism, and that even in AR the isolation experiment was never run.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abstract; DBLP publ API confirmed ASE 2022.

related_work.citation: "CYCLE: Learning to Self-Refine the Code Generation." arXiv:2403.18746; OOPSLA 2024 (Proc. ACM Program. Lang.).
related_work.venue_status: OOPSLA 2024 / PACMPL 2024. Verified via OpenReview api2 (venue='OOPSLA 2024' and 'Proc. ACM Program. Lang. 2024' DBLP records); arXiv comment states 'Camera-ready for OOPSLA'24'.
related_work.what_it_covers: Trains code LMs (350M/1B/2B/3B) to self-refine faulty generations using available feedback such as test-suite execution results; shows code LMs cannot self-refine well out of the box; up to 63.5% improvement on HumanEval/MBPP/APPS.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Autoregressive only; refinement is full-sequence regeneration conditioned on feedback text, not localized in-place editing. No diffusion, no remasking, no notion of WHERE to edit. Small scale (<=3B).
related_work.known_defects: No placebo/matched-budget control for the feedback content (the 2026 placebo literature shows this matters a great deal); gains are measured against a one-shot baseline that does not get the extra attempt, which confounds feedback value with retry value.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API v1 date + arXiv comment; OpenReview api2 returned OOPSLA 2024 and PACMPL 2024 records.

related_work.citation: "Try Again, Don't Look Back: Blind Resampling Outperforms Self-Repair in Small Code Models." arXiv:2607.26117.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1; code/pre-registrations on GitHub).
related_work.what_it_covers: Placebo-controlled, matched-output-budget comparison on MBPP+ at 1.5B/3B/7B of four retry conditions: blind resampling, content-free failure notice, genuine execution feedback, and feedback + verbal reflection. Blind resampling is strongest below 7B and statistically tied at 7B while using 2.5-5.5x fewer tokens; conditioning on the model's own failed attempt costs 6.1 points at 1.5B (p=0.006); the INFORMATIONAL CONTENT of execution feedback adds nothing measurable over the placebo. Attributes the harm to anchoring (33-68% near-identical reproductions vs 2-14% under blind resampling).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Autoregressive models only, prompt channel only (no weight-space localized training), MBPP+ only, and no diffusion model anywhere -- so its null does not transfer to bidirectional in-place editing where the draft is a canvas rather than a prefix to imitate. It also cannot test localization, because AR retry has no notion of a remask region.
related_work.known_defects: This is the single most dangerous concurrent result for our claim: it is direct evidence that 'execution feedback content' can be worth zero once you control the extra attempt. But it is also the best gift -- it hands us the required control design (matched-budget + content-free placebo + derangement) and identifies ANCHORING as the mechanism, which is exactly the failure mode our own withdrawn 'restart' arm inverted (we discarded the draft; they show conditioning on it can hurt). Concurrent, so it does not preempt.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API search + id abstract fetch; published=2026-07-28.

related_work.citation: "Form, Not Content? A Preregistered, Placebo-Controlled Evaluation of Learned Error-Conditioned Self-Repair Through Prompts and Weights in Frozen Small Code Models" (PoPE). arXiv:2607.12962. Companion: "Falsification, Not Exposure", arXiv:2606.31511 (2026-06-30).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1, 54 pages).
related_work.what_it_covers: Methodology (PoPE) for testing whether falsifying execution evidence is operationally usable by the same model, with channel-specific placebos that keep the scaffold but ablate task-relevant content or DERANGE the task-error assignment. Runs both a prompt channel and a WEIGHT channel (small-data adapter training) on 0.5-1.5B frozen code models. Weight channel: 8-8 tie between the error-content adapter and the intervention-free baseline (p=1.0), with the SHA-deranged placebo adapter AHEAD at 10 unlocks; content-attributable superiority not confirmed.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: 0.5-1.5B AR models, adapter-scale data, no diffusion, no localization (the adapter conditions on error text, it does not choose mask positions). Explicitly disclaims equivalence/non-inferiority, so it is a null, not a refutation.
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent. Tiny models and tiny data make the weight-channel null under-powered by construction. Its enduring contribution to us is the DERANGEMENT placebo: an arm whose localizer has the right shape and statistics but the wrong task-to-error assignment. Our proposed arm C (uniformly placed span of matched length) is a weaker placebo than derangement, because random placement also changes the region's syntactic character; adding a deranged-execution arm is the single highest-value design upgrade available.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API search + id abstract fetch for both 2607.12962 and 2606.31511.

related_work.citation: "Beyond Execution: Static-Analysis Rewards and Hint-Conditioned Diffusion RL for Code Generation." arXiv:2605.17174.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1). No OpenReview conference record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Systematic study of RL post-training for diffusion code generation along reward design, hint-conditioned sampling, and task difficulty. Finds execution-based rewards hit a 'capability cliff' on hard tasks; static checking is the strongest standalone execution-FREE reward (DiffuCoder HumanEval 53.9 -> 67.1); moderate AST-based hinting helps most on harder benchmarks; best reward depends on difficulty.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Reward design, not localization: nothing here chooses a remask region. No self-draft harvest, no repair training, no localizer ablation, no EvalPlus-Plus pass@1 with token accounting.
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent. Directly relevant as a threat AND an opening: it argues execution signal is weakest exactly where you need it (hard tasks with low pass rates), which predicts our arm A could underperform on the hard tail. It also supplies a natural 4th arm for us -- static-analysis/AST-localized remasking -- which is cheap, sidesteps the 28-GPU-hour execution harvest on hard rows, and would make our localizer sweep {execution, static, confidence, random, deranged} the most complete in the literature.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list abstract fetch; published=2026-05-16.

related_work.citation: "Constrained Code Generation with Discrete Diffusion" (CDC). arXiv:2605.16829.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1).
related_work.what_it_covers: Training-free neurosymbolic framework that intervenes in the reverse denoising process: constraint-aware denoising operators combine optimization with PROGRAM ANALYSIS to identify constraint-relevant regions of the intermediate program state and locally adjust the denoising trajectory. Improves functional-correctness, security and syntax constraint satisfaction with 'less corrective computation and more localized edits'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Training-free inference-time steering, not a training objective; program analysis (static), not test execution; no draft-harvest, no fine-tuning, no localizer ablation at matched compute.
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent. Establishes that program analysis can localize regions in the denoising state -- so a reviewer will ask why we do not compare to it; folding a static-analysis localizer into our arm set answers that pre-emptively. Its 'less corrective computation' claim is not reported as a token-level frontier.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list abstract fetch; published=2026-05-16.

related_work.citation: "Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking in Masked Diffusion Language Models." arXiv:2606.12232.
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 workshops (SPIGM poster and AdaptFM poster, both with Camera_Ready_Revision). Verified on OpenReview api2. Not a main-conference paper.
related_work.what_it_covers: Revisits post-hoc confidence-based remasking (WINO) and finds that under standard decoding (shorter block lengths) it brings little-to-no benefit over confidence-based unmasking alone; under non-greedy decoding it partially mitigates stochasticity-induced errors but exacerbates diversity collapse. Concludes benefits are highly setting-dependent.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Training-free remasking only; no training-time localizer, no code-repair setting, no execution.
related_work.known_defects: Concurrent, workshop-only. Valuable as external support for the premise that our arm B (confidence localization) is a weak incumbent -- but it also warns that confidence-remasking results swing with block length and decoding temperature, so our A-vs-B comparison must fix block length, temperature and top_p and report them, or the 2-point kill threshold will be swamped by protocol sensitivity (our own measurement: top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 moved HumanEval by +14.6 points).
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list abstract fetch; OpenReview api2 returned two ICML 2026 workshop venueids with Camera_Ready_Revision.

related_work.citation: "Remask, Don't Replace: Token-to-Mask Refinement in Diffusion Large Language Models." arXiv:2604.18738 (v1 2026-04-20, v2 2026-05-07). Supersedes withdrawn arXiv:2605.26436 "Targeted Remasking".
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv). The earlier version 2605.26436 carries an explicit author note that it is withdrawn and superseded by 2604.18738.
related_work.what_it_covers: Argues that LLaDA2.1's T2T replacement action is itself the limiting factor and proposes training-free Token-to-Mask (T2M) remasking: revoke suspicious commitments by resetting to [MASK] and re-predict from cleaner context. +13.33 on AIME 2025, +8.56 on CMATH. The superseded version validated three error-detection strategies (probability-based, trigger-mirrored, temporal-difference) across 12 benchmarks including coding.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Training-free; detection is model-internal (probability/temporal); math-dominant headline; no execution, no code-repair pass@1 protocol, no training-time localizer, no cost-matched frontier.
related_work.known_defects: Pre-cutoff and it establishes 'remask rather than overwrite' as the better self-correction primitive, which supports our design choice of remasking a region rather than editing tokens in place. Its own error detectors are exactly the arm-B family, tested only training-free; whether they survive as TRAINING-time localizers is untested. Version churn (a withdrawn sibling) means citation hygiene matters here.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list for both IDs; read the withdrawal comment on 2605.26436 pointing to 2604.18738.

related_work.citation: "OSCAR: Orchestrated Self-verification and Cross-path Refinement." arXiv:2604.01624.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1/v2).
related_work.what_it_covers: Formulates 'commitment uncertainty localization': given a denoising trajectory, identify positions whose CROSS-CHAIN entropy (over N parallel chains with randomized reveal orders) exceeds an unsupervised threshold, then perform targeted remasking conditioned on retrieved evidence. Introduces trajectory-level localization assessments (e.g. cross-chain divergence-at-hallucination). LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B on TriviaQA/HotpotQA/RAGTruth/CommonsenseQA. Ablations confirm localization and correction contribute complementary gains.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Training-free, factuality/QA domain, retrieval as the correction evidence -- not code, not execution, not training. But it is the pre-cutoff paper that most cleanly names LOCALIZATION as a separable component with its own metrics, and it shows localization and correction can be ablated apart.
related_work.known_defects: Pre-cutoff and it pre-empts the abstract framing 'localization is a first-class, separately-measurable component'; we should cite it for that framing rather than claim it. Its localizer needs N=4-16 parallel chains, i.e. a 4-16x cost that is not charged in a token-level frontier -- a strong follow-up target, and a reason our single-pass execution localizer is attractive on cost.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list abstract fetch; published=2026-04-02.

related_work.citation: "DreamOn: Diffusion Language Models For Code Infilling Beyond Fixed-size Canvas." arXiv:2602.01326; ICLR 2026 Poster. Base models: "Dream-Coder 7B" arXiv:2509.01142; "Dream 7B" arXiv:2508.15487.

diff.differentiation_statement: Every pre-cutoff paper that trains a masked diffusion model to repair its output localizes the repair region with a MODEL-INTERNAL signal, and every paper that uses program execution to train a repairer is autoregressive and injects the execution signal as INPUT TEXT rather than as a mask location. The closest work, Corrective Diffusion LMs (arXiv:2512.15596, 2025-12-17), is a genuine overlap and must be cited as such: same domain (code), same goal (make a masked DLM localize and repair errors), and it even uses execution -- but only as a filter to validate synthetic benchmark instances, never as the thing that chooses which positions get remasked during training. Its training corruption is uniform type-preserving vocabulary replacement, its trained model is Open-dCoder-0.5B, and its refinement is priced in "steps" with no token accounting. We differ on four axes a reviewer can check independently: (1) the errors are the model's OWN graded failing drafts, harvested and scored with evalplus untrusted_check, not synthetic substitutions -- CDLM's own framing concedes these differ in kind but never tests it; (2) the remask region is chosen by EXECUTION (which assertion failed, which statements the failing trace touched, mapped onto ir_json statement node_ids), a signal no prior diffusion work has ever used for localization; (3) the design is a three-way localizer ablation (execution / confidence / random) with remasked-token-count HELD FIXED, so the localizer is the only free variable -- TreeDiff (2508.01473) ran the closest thing to this, a structural-vs-random contrast, but with two arms, no confidence arm, and no evident count matching; (4) we charge the draft pass and the repair pass in cumulative_model_tokens on HumanEval+/MBPP+ at NFE {64,128,512}, which none of CDLM, RemeDi, PRISM, TreeDiff, SCOPE, or self-generated T2T does. On scale we act on a 7B code diffusion model where CDLM only probed (it measured that confidence quality differs sharply between Dream-7B and Open-dCoder-0.5B, then trained the 0.5B). SCOPE (2606.01026) and self-generated T2T (2606.17175) are both first public after 2026-05-07, hence concurrent: they establish the sampler-simulated and self-generated-draft corruption ideas on LLaDA-family math/general tasks, and we cite them as concurrent while noting neither runs the program, neither reports EvalPlus pass@1, and neither ablates the localizer.

followup_openings.target_paper: Corrective Diffusion Language Models (arXiv:2512.15596, 2025-12-17, preprint)
followup_openings.defect: The training corruption is uniform type-preserving vocabulary replacement on visible tokens, while the paper's own motivation is that deployment errors are fluent and high-confidence. It never tests its objective against the model's own failing drafts, and it never uses execution as a localizer -- execution appears only as a validity filter for CRB instances. It also trains only Open-dCoder-0.5B, after measuring that confidence quality differs substantially at 7B (Dream-7B was its best localizer, Open-dCoder-0.5B its worst), and it prices refinement in steps rather than tokens.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run CDLM's objective as our explicit arm-B-adjacent baseline at 7B on Dream-Coder, then swap only the corruption SOURCE (self-generated graded failures vs synthetic substitution) and only the LOCALIZER (execution-implicated statements vs lowest-confidence span), holding remasked-token-count and training steps fixed. Report the result on real from-scratch failures on HumanEval+/MBPP+ pass@1 with cumulative_model_tokens including the draft pass, and rerun their CRB protocol as a bridge so the comparison is legible in their own units.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts a diffuse 'we also do repair training' story into a targeted repair of a specific paper's two admitted weaknesses (synthetic-error mismatch, 0.5B-only), and it lets us report a scale result (0.5B -> 7B) that their own confidence measurements predict may not replicate. A negative result here is publishable too.

followup_openings.target_paper: Try Again, Don't Look Back (arXiv:2607.26117, 2026-07-28, concurrent) and PoPE (arXiv:2607.12962, 2026-07-14, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Both find that the informational CONTENT of execution feedback adds nothing over a shape-matched placebo at matched budget in small AR code models, and PoPE's weight channel found the SHA-DERANGED placebo adapter ahead of the error-content adapter. Neither can test localization, because AR retry has no remask region; both are confined to 0.5-1.5B (PoPE) or 1.5-7B prompt-channel (blind resampling) AR models, MBPP+-centric, with no diffusion anywhere. The anchoring mechanism they identify (33-68% near-identical reproduction when shown one's own attempt) is untested in a bidirectional canvas where only part of the draft is remasked.
followup_openings.our_fix: Import their control design wholesale and go one better: add a fourth arm A' = DERANGED EXECUTION, where the remask region is the execution-derived region computed from a DIFFERENT task's failure, mapped onto this task's statement ids with matched token count. That is a strictly stronger placebo than our arm C (uniform random span), because it matches the syntactic character and size distribution of arm A while destroying the task-to-error assignment. Also instrument the anchoring mechanism directly in the diffusion setting: measure token-level edit distance and fraction-of-draft-preserved between draft and repaired output per arm, which is a quantity AR retry cannot expose.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the strongest available claim: masked diffusion with partial remasking should be the ONE architecture where execution-localized self-repair escapes the anchoring trap that kills AR self-repair, because the model is handed a canvas with a hole rather than a prefix to imitate. If arm A beats A' and C, we have a mechanism-level result that survives the 2026 placebo literature. If it does not, we have the first placebo-controlled null for diffusion self-repair, which is itself a clean contribution and directly answers our own withdrawn refinement findings.

followup_openings.target_paper: PRISM / Fine-Tuning Masked Diffusion for Provable Self-Correction (arXiv:2510.01384, 2025-10-01, ICML 2026)
followup_openings.defect: It advertises learning per-token quality scores 'without RL or a verifier' as a feature, and therefore never measures what a verifier would buy. Code is one of three demo domains (Sudoku, 170M text, LLaDA-8B code) with no EvalPlus pass@1 protocol and no token accounting.
followup_openings.our_fix: Treat PRISM's confidence-quality head as the strongest instantiation of arm B rather than a strawman low-confidence span, and run the head-to-head PRISM-style localizer vs execution localizer at matched remasked-token count and matched fine-tuning steps on a 7B code model, scored with evalplus untrusted_check on HumanEval+/MBPP+ and charged in cumulative_model_tokens.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It turns our arm B from a weak baseline into the published state of the art for verifier-free localization, so a win is meaningful and a tie is an informative null ('a free forward-pass signal matches a program execution you paid for'), which is a publishable efficiency result either way and directly probes the peer-reviewed claim that no verifier is needed.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (arXiv:2508.01473, 2025-08-02, workshop/preprint)
followup_openings.defect: Two-arm design (AST-guided masking vs random masking) whose headline is a relative 13.3% on HumanEval+, with no evidence that the masked-token COUNT is equalized between arms -- so part of the gain could be an effective-corruption-rate difference rather than a localization difference. No confidence arm, no execution arm, no repair setting (from-scratch generation only), no cost accounting, weak venue.
followup_openings.our_fix: Add a static/AST-localized arm to our sweep (cheap: we already have ir_json statement structure) so the localizer axis becomes {execution, static-AST, confidence, random, deranged} at matched remasked-token count, and report the token-matched version of TreeDiff's contrast as a replication check at 7B on Dream-Coder rather than LLaDA-8B-Instruct.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It makes ours the first count-matched, multi-localizer ablation for code diffusion training, replicates a weak-venue result at a different model family, and answers the reviewer question 'why not just use static structure, which is free?' -- which also hedges the cost risk, since the static arm needs no 28-GPU-hour execution harvest.

followup_openings.target_paper: Beyond Execution (arXiv:2605.17174, 2026-05-16, concurrent) and Re-evaluating Confidence Remasking (arXiv:2606.12232, 2026-06-10, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: The first finds execution reward collapses on hard tasks (a 'capability cliff') and that static checking beats execution as a reward, but only for RL reward design, never for localization. The second finds confidence-remasking benefits are highly setting-dependent (block length, greedy vs non-greedy), i.e. that arm-B-style results swing with decoding protocol -- yet almost no paper in this space reports the frontier across those settings.
followup_openings.our_fix: Stratify our A-vs-B-vs-C comparison by task difficulty (using the draft-pass pass rate on the harvest subset as the difficulty proxy) to test whether execution localization inherits the capability cliff, and lock and report block length, temperature and top_p, sweeping at least two decoding settings. Our own measurement that top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 moved HumanEval by 14.6 points -- larger than most published diffusion-LM method gains -- makes this non-optional.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It pre-empts the two most likely reviewer objections (that our effect is a decoding artifact, and that execution signal is weakest where repair is needed most), and the difficulty stratification is a second, independent finding even if the headline A-vs-B gap is small.

followup_openings.defect: Both are training-free localizers that pay a large hidden multiple: OSCAR runs N in {4,8,16} parallel denoising chains to compute cross-chain entropy; CORE probes each token's sensitivity to masked-context perturbations. Neither reports a token-level or wall-clock frontier that charges this multiple, and neither is evaluated on code repair with EvalPlus pass@1.
followup_openings.our_fix: Include one training-free trajectory-based localizer (cross-chain entropy at N=4, the cheapest OSCAR setting) as an inference-time comparison point on the same cumulative_model_tokens axis as our trained arms, so the paper answers 'trained localization vs training-free localization at equal serving cost'.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It positions our contribution on the axis nobody in this literature reports -- honest cost -- which is the same axis on which our surviving scaffold-vs-vanilla result already lives, and it repairs a shared accounting defect across the entire remasking-localization literature rather than one paper's.

diff.sharpened_claim: For a 7B masked diffusion code model, WHERE you remask during self-repair training is a controlled, first-class design variable, and execution feedback is a better localizer than the model's own confidence at matched remasked-token count and matched training compute. Concretely: harvest Dream-Coder's own drafts on a subset of data/scaffold_edu_v0 (114,363 rows, 100% nonempty executable testcase and entry_point columns, ir_json statement node_ids -- all verified by direct inspection), grade them with evalplus untrusted_check, keep the failures, and build repair examples that differ ONLY in which region is remasked, across five arms held to identical remasked-token counts: (A) execution -- statements implicated by the failing assertion and traceback; (A') deranged execution -- the same construction computed from a different task's failure, the shape-matched content-ablated placebo demanded by the 2026 placebo-controlled self-repair literature; (B) confidence -- lowest-confidence contiguous span, instantiated as the strongest published verifier-free localizer rather than a strawman; (B-static) AST/structural span, the count-matched version of TreeDiff's contrast; (C) uniform random span. Score on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ at NFE {64,128,512}, chat and sampler settings locked and reported, charging BOTH the draft pass and the repair pass in cumulative_model_tokens, with per-problem paired tests (McNemar) rather than a raw percentage-point threshold. The headline result is the ordering of localizers on a cost-honest frontier plus a mechanism measurement AR cannot produce -- the fraction of the draft each arm actually preserves -- testing whether partial remasking under bidirectional context escapes the anchoring trap (33-68% near-identical reproduction) that makes AR self-repair lose to blind resampling.

And given this repo's own retraction #2 (a "restart" policy that regenerated from the prompt and silently measured the base model instead of any editing ability), the repair arms must be instrumented for draft-preservation, or a model that quietly rewrites the whole canvas will again be scored as if it had edited. Note the manifest shows this corpus was filtered using models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B, i.e. the same family we would train, so a self-selection check on the harvest subset is warranted.

blocking_gaps: FATAL AS WRITTEN -- the Phase-2 target is undefined. The design says 'input is the draft with a region remasked, target is the reference solution over that region'. I tokenized all 40 executable failing drafts from runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe256 against their canonical solutions with the Dream tokenizer: the minimal contiguous diff span covers 100% of the draft in 40/40 cases (mean 13.5 disjoint diff blocks, median 12; exact token-length equality 1/40 = 2.5%; span_draft==span_ref 1/40). A self-generated draft is an independent re-derivation, not an edit of the reference, so there is no aligned reference substring to supervise a localized region against, and no way to hold remasked-token-count fixed across arms. Contrast, measured on data/edit/humanevalpack_python.parquet (HumanEvalFix, which I found on disk and which the candidate does not mention): buggy->canonical diff span is median 4% of the program, 78.7% single-block, 90.2% of cases under 30%. Localized repair supervision is well-defined for aligned pairs and undefined for self-generated drafts. This is the same class as retraction #2 -- a pipeline stage whose input does not contain what the next stage assumes.

The execution localizer has almost no localizing power, and the specific signal named in the design does not exist. (a) I confirmed evalplus.eval.untrusted_check returns only (stat, details) -- a bool array over inputs, zero traceback/stderr text (grep for traceback/format_exc/exc/stderr in its source: 0 hits). The traceback the design depends on is only available via the assert-string harness in scripts/evaluate_correction_calibration.py, not the grader the candidate names. (b) On 400 sampled corpus rows with single-op seeded bugs, 59.2% of failures are assertion failures whose traceback names ONLY the assert line outside the function -- zero in-function localization; only 2.2% name an in-function statement. (c) 'Statements the failing trace touched' selects 72% of in-function statements on average (median 82%); 26% of the time the failing trace touches every statement, i.e. the localizer degenerates to 'remask everything'. (d) Even the strongest version (SBFL differential, failing-only-minus-passing statements) is EMPTY 24.4% of the time and still spans 67% of statements when nonempty. Arm A and arm C are therefore near-identical by construction, which guarantees the kill criterion fires for a measurement reason rather than a scientific one.

Harvest yield at the specified NFE 128 is far below what the budget assumes, because failures are overwhelmingly unparseable rather than executable. Measured on disk: HE+ nfe128 = 68.3% syntax_error vs 15.2% parses-but-fails, so only 25/141 = 17.7% of failures are executable (the only population where an execution localizer is even defined); MBPP+ nfe128 = 27%. I also ran a real 24-row harvest pilot on data/scaffold_edu_v0/train_data.parquet with the repo's own extract_python: 62.5% syntax_error, 8.3% pass, and only 32% of failures executable. Yield roughly triples at NFE 256 (HE+ 55%, MBPP+ 69%), so NFE 128 is the wrong harvest operating point -- but that doubles harvest cost per row.

The training environment does not exist on the machine I was given. scripts/run_plain_sft_stage1_8gpu.sh launches $ROOT/.venv_dream/bin/torchrun; .venv_dream is absent locally (only .venv_b200 exists, which lacks peft, verl, tensordict, hydra, omegaconf, flash_attn). /opt/conda/envs/dllm-env has torch+transformers+evalplus but NOT verl or peft, so scaffold_coder.training.scaffold_sft_trainer cannot import there. A working trainer env exists only on .104 (/apdcephfs_zwfy6/.../dllm_draft_104/.venv_dream: torch 2.5.1+cu124, transformers 4.46.2, peft 0.13.2, verl OK, TRAINER IMPORTS OK) -- which is on the OTHER disk (zwfy6 is not mounted locally) and is currently 8/8 GPUs at 98-100% util running the AR baseline. So 'we have the trainer' is true on exactly one node that is fully occupied and cross-disk from the data.

est_gpu_hours=70 omits Phase 3 almost entirely. The 28 GPU-hour figure is harvest only; it also uses 12.6 s/sample, whereas measured elapsed_seconds in runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe128/metrics.rank*.jsonl is 3.50 s (nfe128) / 6.11 s (nfe256), and my own pilot got 2.85 s at nfe128. The real omissions are 3-5 fine-tuning arms of a 7B model plus per-arm evaluation at NFE {64,128,512} on 164+378 problems, plus the arm-B confidence extractor (a leave-one-out or strided-mask pass over every draft, an extra forward-pass sweep per row).

The stated kill criterion is statistically inert, which the positioning already flags and I confirm numerically: at n=164 and p~0.2 the binomial SE is ~3.1pp, so a '2 points on BOTH benchmarks' threshold sits inside noise. Worse, the repo's own measurement that top_p 1.0->0.95 moved HumanEval by 14.6 points means a 2-point effect is ~7x smaller than a single sampler knob.
feas.concrete_plan:
GATE 0 (CPU only, ~0 GPU-h, do FIRST -- it can kill the whole candidate cheaply). Reuse my measurement scripts. (a) Re-run the localizer-power measurement over >=2000 rows of /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/data/scaffold_edu_v0/train_data.parquet, reporting for each candidate localizer the fraction of in-function statements selected and whether it contains the true fault. My n=221 numbers: trace-touched = 72% of statements (median 82%), degenerate-to-everything 26% of the time; SBFL differential empty 24.4%, else 67%. GATE: if the execution region cannot be made to select <40% of statements on >60% of rows, arm A is not distinguishable from arm C and the headline claim is dead -- stop here and write it up as a negative measurement result (this is publishable and costs no GPU). (b) Alignment gate: extend my diff-span measurement (Dream tokenizer, difflib.SequenceMatcher on token ids) over all executable failing drafts in runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe256 and runs/dream_instruct_mbppplus_nfe256. My result: 100% span, 13.5 blocks, 40/40. GATE: unless >30% of drafts admit a diff span under 40% of the draft, the "target = reference over the region" construction is undefined and MUST be replaced (see Gate 1).

GATE 1 (design repair, CPU). Because Gate 0(b) already failed on self-generated drafts, switch the supervision source to ALIGNED pairs, which exist on disk and the candidate overlooked: data/edit/humanevalpack_python.parquet (HumanEvalFix, 164 rows, buggy_solution + canonical_solution + bug_type, diff span median 4% of program, 78.7% single-block) and data/edit/canitedit.parquet (105 rows, before/after/tests). Also available: data/infilling/HumanEval-RandomSpanInfilling.jsonl for a supervision-free localization probe. Build the repair-example builder against these, where region and target are both well-defined and token counts CAN be matched. Keep self-generated drafts as a held-out DISTRIBUTION-SHIFT test set, not as training supervision -- that inverts the candidate's Phase 1/Phase 3 split and is the only version that is internally consistent.

GATE 2 (mechanism check -- ALREADY DONE, and it passed; ~0.2 GPU-h). I verified the load-bearing primitive that both retracted arms never tested: masked mid-sequence re-diffusion on models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B. Injecting mask_token_id=151666 at interior positions and calling diffusion_generate(max_new_tokens=1, steps=len(hole), temperature=0.1, top_p=0.95, alg="entropy") (a) repairs a seeded comparison-operator bug ZERO-SHOT with a 1-token hole and with a 3-token hole, and (b) leaves every non-masked position byte-identical (0/31, 0/29, 0/16 drift at hole sizes 1, 3, 16). So the editing mechanism works untrained and is region-confined. IMPORTANT CONSEQUENCE: a training-free execution-localized repair baseline must be run BEFORE any fine-tuning, or the paper cannot attribute anything to training. Note scripts/pilot_repair.py already implements exactly the loo-vs-random-vs-tail localizer comparison and has NEVER been run (no logs anywhere; only scripts/pilot_mech.py is newer). Run it first -- it is ~1 GPU-h and directly tests the A-vs-B ordering training-free.

GATE 3 (harvest at the corrected operating point, ~10-15 GPU-h). Only if Gates 0-2 pass. Harvest at NFE 256, not 128 (measured executable-failure yield 55% HE+ / 69% MBPP+ vs 17.7% / 27% at 128). Size from measured throughput (3.5 s/sample at nfe128, 6.1 s at nfe256 from runs/*/metrics.rank*.jsonl), not the 12.6 s/sample in the proposal. Grade with the assert-string harness scripts/evaluate_correction_calibration.py::evaluate_source (which returns full stderr and distinguishes empty_output / syntax_error / timeout / assertion_failure / runtime_error) -- NOT evalplus untrusted_check, which returns only (stat, details) and no traceback. Verified prerequisite: reference solutions pass their own testcase field 299/300 = 99.7%, and the corpus filter in scripts/build_normalized_dataset.py uses AutoTokenizer only (no model generation), so there is NO capability self-selection toward Dream-Coder despite manifest.json naming it as model_path.

GATE 4 (training, ~40-60 GPU-h, BLOCKED until an env exists). Prerequisite: stand up a trainer env. Fastest path is .252 (8x B200, same wzc1 disk as the data, currently 6/8 GPUs idle) by installing peft 0.19.1 from the on-disk wheels/peft-0.19.1-py3-none-any.whl plus tensordict/hydra/omegaconf; do NOT plan on .104 (correct env, but other disk and 8/8 GPUs at 99% util on the AR baseline). Reuse scaffold_coder/sft_dataset.py::PlainMaskedSFTDataset as the base class -- it already does mask-token substitution, loss_mask, and 1/t importance weighting on a flat canvas, and only its region-selection needs replacing. Arms, at matched remasked-token count and matched steps: A execution/SBFL, A' deranged-execution (region computed from a DIFFERENT task, the placebo the 2026 literature demands), B confidence, B-static AST, C uniform random. Score with evalplus at NFE {64,128,512}, charge draft+repair passes in cumulative_model_tokens, and use per-problem paired McNemar with multiple seeds rather than the inert 2-point threshold.
feas.risk: The most likely outcome is a CONFOUNDED null that looks like a scientific finding: arms A, B and C all converge because they are selecting nearly the same tokens. I measured that the design's own localizer ("statements the failing trace touched") selects 72% of in-function statements on average, median 82%, and degenerates to literally every statement 26% of the time; the strongest variant (SBFL differential) is empty 24.4% of the time and still spans 67% when nonempty. When arm A remasks ~75% of the body and arm C remasks a same-size random span of a body that is only 8.65 executable statements (median 8) long, the two regions overlap heavily by construction, so "A within 2 points of B" would be reported as "execution feedback adds nothing" when the truth is "the three arms were never different treatments." A second, sneakier confound: the corpus is short (median 4-5 statements, mean response 82 tokens, 44% of rows have <=4 statements), so on a large minority of rows there is no room for any localizer to differ from any other. The kill criterion as written cannot distinguish a real null from this degeneracy, and given the 2-point threshold is ~1/7 the size of the repo's own measured top_p sampler effect (14.6 points), whatever number comes out will be dominated by protocol choices. Third risk, from the concurrent literature and consistent with retraction #2: an untrained-but-capable model may already do the repair (I confirmed zero-shot in-place repair works), so a fine-tuned arm can post gains that are really just the extra edit pass, unless the training-free baseline from Gate 2 is measured on the identical cost axis.
feas.required_control: REGION-IDENTITY AND REGION-CONFINEMENT LOGGING, asserted per training example and per eval sample, with the run aborting on violation. Concretely, for every constructed example emit and archive: (1) the exact remasked token index set, its size, and the pairwise Jaccard overlap between arms A/A'/B/B-static/C on the SAME row -- then assert that mean cross-arm Jaccard is below a preregistered ceiling. This is the control that prevents the analogous failure to all three retractions: retraction #1 compared nothing, retraction #2 silently discarded its input, retraction #3 dropped the expensive cases; here the analogue is five "different localizers" that are secretly the same token set, so the experiment compares nothing while appearing to. If mean overlap is high, the correct output is "the localizers are not separable on this corpus," NOT "execution feedback does not help." (2) Because the target is only defined for aligned pairs, assert per example that the supervised region maps to a contiguous reference span and record diff-span-fraction and block count; refuse to build an example when the diff span exceeds a preregistered fraction of the program (on self-generated drafts this rejects 40/40, which is exactly the signal that the supervision source must change). (3) At eval, log per sample the fraction of the input draft left byte-identical plus draft->output token edit distance, so an arm that quietly rewrites the whole canvas cannot be scored as if it had edited a localized region -- this is the direct instrument for retraction #2's failure mode (the "restart" arm that regenerated from the prompt and measured the base model), and my Gate-2 measurement shows the mechanism genuinely is region-confined (0 outside-hole drift at hole sizes 1/3/16), so any observed whole-canvas rewrite is a pipeline bug rather than model behaviour. (4) Charge draft pass + repair pass in cumulative_model_tokens for EVERY sample including budget-truncated and unparseable ones, reading process OR failure_process, since dropping the truncated tail is precisely what understated scaffold Large by 2.85x/3.69x.

lens.title: Can training absorb a structural runtime? Distilling decoder-runtime commit orders into a flat-canvas diffusion student
lens.claim: Structure-derived generation orders are not transferable by supervision alone: a flat-canvas student trained on the exact commit-order trajectories of our typed-AST decoder runtime fails to reach the runtime's quality at the runtime's token cost, and a random-order control of equal step count is statistically indistinguishable from it -- which upgrades our Pareto-segmentation finding from 'two systems occupy different segments' to 'the structural runtime supplies something training on its orders cannot'.
lens.why_now: Our one surviving finding is that structural runtime and flat diffusion own disjoint segments of the quality-compute frontier with NO crossover: scaffold Medium holds the frontier at 13.98k HE+ tokens / 7.08k MBPP+ tokens (.177 / .354) where vanilla scores ~.000/.008 at 19-22k tokens, while the .707/.680 ceiling is exclusively vanilla's. The first question any reviewer asks is whether the cheap end is a property of the runtime or merely a training target nobody hit. This is also the exact open question the brief poses -- 'whether training on structure-derived generation orders helps' -- and unlike every heuristic order-learning paper we have a REAL generator of structural orders rather than a hand-designed one. Prior order-learning work optimizes a scalar order policy against the model's own signal (Gt-Margin/Where-to-Unmask 2602.09501 pre-cutoff; SAS/Scheduling Thoughts 2606.23567 concurrent; TraceLock 2605.24697 concurrent) -- none distills orders from an external symbolic runtime, and none asks whether a cheap structured decoder can be compiled away into flat weights. Both outcomes of this experiment are publishable, which is what makes it worth the GPUs.
lens.experiment: Phase 1: dump commit trajectories from Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B decoding through scaffold_coder/decoder_runtime.py on the 114k training set, recording at each runtime step the set of leaf tokens committed (decoder_runtime.commit_many at line 448 and committed_leaf_tokens at line 467 are verified present). Phase 2: convert each trajectory into a flat-canvas training sequence -- at runtime step k, mask every position not yet committed and supervise exactly the tokens committed at step k. This yields a fixed multi-token commit order per example with no meta-tokens and no typed holes, so the student is priced like vanilla (flat-canvas cost is 685 tok/step HE+ / 604 MBPP+, already measured). Phase 3: two arms -- (A) runtime-derived order; (B) random-permutation order with IDENTICAL step count and identical tokens-committed-per-step histogram, isolating 'this particular structural order' from 'any fixed multi-token commit order'. Grade both on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ at three matched cumulative_model_tokens budgets bracketing scaffold Medium's 13.98k/7.08k, and plot on the existing token-cost Pareto figures alongside scaffold Tiny/Small/Medium/Large and the vanilla NFE curve.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B (29GB); decoder_runtime.py with commit/commit_many/committed_leaf_tokens/completed_structural_subtrees/capacity_metrics (API verified by grep); the full capacity ladder already graded on both benchmarks (8 cells) as the teacher reference; scripts/make_pareto_figures.py and the figures directory; the matched Plain-SFT control as the flat-canvas price reference. MISSING/TO BUILD: a trajectory dumper that serializes runtime commit steps to a training format (~120 lines); the flat-canvas sequence converter. NOTE: no AR code teacher (Qwen2.5-Coder) exists on either wzc1 or zwfy6 -- verified by find on both -- so a reverse AR-to-diffusion variant of this candidate is blocked until the .104 agent's download lands.
lens.kill_criterion: The 'orders transfer' reading is falsified if student A at matched cumulative_model_tokens is more than 5 points below scaffold Medium on both benchmarks AND control B is within 2 points of A. The 'orders do not transfer' reading is falsified if A reaches within 2 points of scaffold Medium at matched cost while B does not -- in which case the segmentation collapses to a single frontier and our headline finding must be restated as 'the runtime is a training curriculum, not a necessary decoder'. Uninformative outcome (must be reported as such): both A and B reach scaffold Medium, meaning any fixed multi-token commit order suffices and structure is irrelevant.
lens.builds_on: Where-to-Unmask/Gt-Margin (arXiv:2602.09501, 2026-02-10) and SAS (arXiv:2606.23567, 2026-06-22, concurrent). Defect/gap: both learn orders from signals internal to the denoiser (ground-truth token margin, pathwise log-likelihood reward), so they can only rediscover orders the model already prefers. Neither tests distillation from an external symbolic decoder, and neither asks the compilation question -- whether a cheap structured runtime can be replaced by weights.

related_work.citation: Cheng et al. (?), "TreeDiff: AST-Guided Code Generation with Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2508.01473v3; published in Proceedings of the First Workshop on Structured Understanding, Retrieval, and Generation in the LLM Era (SURGeLLM 2026), ACL Anthology volume 2026.surgellm-1
related_work.venue_status: Workshop paper (SURGeLLM 2026, co-located ACL). Verified: ACL Anthology volume page https://aclanthology.org/volumes/2026.surgellm-1/ contains the TreeDiff abstract (77 papers in volume); Semantic Scholar reports venue='Proceedings of the First Workshop on Structured Understanding, Retrieval, and Generation in the LLM Era (SURGeLLM 2026)'; DBLP still lists CoRR 2025 only (typical lag). OpenReview search returns only the CoRR record.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest prior work on 'structure-derived masking for diffusion code LMs'. Uses AST node identity to bias the *corruption* process during SFT of LLaDA-8B-Instruct: instead of uniform random token masking, selectively mask tokens belonging to key AST nodes (code region gets AST-node masking, reasoning region gets random masking). Reports pass@1 on HE/HE+/MBPP/MBPP+ at T=256 and T=512, +13.3% relative on HumanEval+ at T=512 over a matched LLaDA+RandomMasking SFT control. Explicitly frames the goal as making the model 'internalize the compositional nature of programming languages' -- i.e. absorb structure into weights.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The structural signal is only *which AST node a token belongs to*, injected as a masking prior over independently-sampled corruption states. There is no external symbolic decoder, no generated commit trajectory, no per-step commit-set supervision, and no fixed generation order at all -- corruption is still stochastic. TreeDiff never asks whether a structural *runtime* (a decoder with typed holes, rule fixed-points, backtracking) can be compiled into weights, because it has no runtime. It also does not price generation in tokens: cost is reported only as denoising steps T (which it conflates with max generation length), so all quality-compute comparisons are step-based.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Cost accounting: T is used both as step count and as max generation length, so the T=256 vs T=512 columns confound compute with canvas size; no token-level cost is reported, so 'structural priors accelerate convergence' is a claim about steps, not compute. (2) The AR comparison is not a control: CodeLlama-7B/13B, CodeQwen1.5-7B, DeepSeek-Coder-33B numbers are copied from the EvalPlus leaderboard, are not matched in lineage/architecture/decoding to the LLaDA backbone, and are not cost-matched -- the headline 'an 8B diffusion model can match or exceed AR baselines' therefore rests on an unmatched comparison. (3) Only two step budgets, and the baseline *degrades* from T=256 to T=512 (35.4->32.3 HE+) while TreeDiff improves; a single-model non-monotonicity of that size with no seeds/CIs is fragile. (4) No control isolating 'AST node identity' from 'any non-uniform masking with the same per-step mask budget' -- the paper allocates a mask budget N with weights W[i] but the reported baseline is uniform, not weight-matched-but-structure-shuffled. (5) No seeds, no variance, single backbone (LLaDA), single language (Python).

related_work.citation: "AnCoder: Anchored Code Generation via Discrete Diffusion Models" (AnchorTree framework), arXiv:2602.17688v1
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. Verified: Semantic Scholar venue='arXiv.org' publicationVenue='arXiv.org' (0 citations); DBLP='CoRR 2026, Informal and Other Publications'; OpenReview title search returns no forum for this paper (only unrelated anchored-diffusion papers).
related_work.what_it_covers: Uses the AST to *prioritise the resolution order* of syntactically/semantically salient tokens (keywords like if/while, identifiers) during discrete diffusion decoding, establishing a 'structural scaffold' that guides the remaining generation. This is the closest prior work to the idea 'AST-derived generation order helps code diffusion', and it uses the word scaffold for the same concept we do.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Abstract-level only: it anchors on token *categories* from a static AST of the target, not on trajectories emitted by an executable structural decoder. It provides no negative/transferability result, no random-order control matched on step count and tokens-per-step, and (as far as the abstract states) frames the contribution as 'a parameter-efficient path to high-quality code generation' rather than asking whether the structural mechanism is necessary at inference time.
related_work.known_defects: Extremely thin public record: 0 citations, single version, no venue, and the abstract announces 'a family of models' without stating benchmarks, baselines, or numbers -- the claim 'structurally anchored diffusion offers a parameter-efficient path' is unquantified in the only text I could verify. I could not verify from the abstract whether it has an order-matched random control or any token-level cost accounting; treat as weak evidence.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API id_list (v1 only, 2026-02-05); Semantic Scholar graph API; DBLP publ API; OpenReview notes/search (no forum found). I read only the abstract -- I did not extract the PDF, so my characterisation of its controls is inferential and flagged in verification_notes.

related_work.citation: Asano, Kozuno, Saito, Baba, "Where-to-Unmask: Ground-Truth-Guided Unmasking Order Learning for Masked Diffusion Language Models" (Gt-Margin), arXiv:2602.09501v1
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (self-labelled 'Preprint. February 11, 2026.' on p.1). Verified: Semantic Scholar venue='arXiv.org' (8 citations); DBLP='CoRR 2026, Informal and Other Publications'; OpenReview title search returns no forum.
related_work.what_it_covers: Defines Gt-Margin, an ORACLE per-position order score computed from ground-truth tokens (margin between correct token and strongest alternative), shows the induced easy-first oracle order dramatically improves quality (GSM8K LLaDA-8B: Margin 0.605 -> Gt-Margin 0.845; Sudoku 0.995), then trains a supervised learning-to-rank *planner* to imitate that oracle order from masked contexts. Crucially it DOES include a Random order baseline, plus AR (L->R) and Inverse-AR, under a controlled one-token-per-step protocol where order score is the only varying component. This is the single closest paper to 'can order supervision be transferred?'
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The oracle is derived from the denoiser's own logits on ground-truth tokens -- an internal signal -- so it can only recover orders the model already prefers; it cannot express an externally-imposed structural order. It keeps the order machinery at inference (the planner is an extra module used during sampling), so it never asks the compilation question -- whether the ordering apparatus can be removed and absorbed into the base weights. Its decoding protocol is strictly ONE token per step for exactly L steps, so it says nothing about multi-token commit sets (which is exactly what a structural runtime emits). No code benchmarks at all (GSM8K/MATH/Sudoku/StrategyQA), no token-cost accounting, no 7B code LM.
related_work.known_defects: (1) Fully absorbing cost convention: the controlled protocol fixes exactly L unmasking steps for every method, so all orders are compute-identical by construction and the paper cannot say anything about quality-per-token -- the practically interesting axis. (2) L is chosen per dataset from the empirical completion-length distribution and then frozen, which advantages methods whose behaviour is length-insensitive and makes cross-dataset comparison of order effects confounded with padding. (3) The planner is trained on oracle orders that require ground-truth tokens, so there is a train/deploy asymmetry the paper does not bound: no measurement of how much of the oracle's Gt-Margin gain survives imitation (the abstract only claims 'improving reasoning accuracy'). (4) No code-generation benchmark, so the strongest structural domain is untested. (5) 8 citations, unpublished.

related_work.citation: "TRIMS: Trajectory-Ranked Instruction Masked Supervision for Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2604.00666v1
related_work.venue_status: Preprint ('Preprint. Under review.' in PDF running header). Verified: Semantic Scholar venue='arXiv.org' (0 citations); DBLP='CoRR 2026, Informal and Other Publications'; OpenReview title search returns no forum for this title.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest mechanism-level prior work. Explicitly identifies that 'standard training does not provide explicit supervision over token reveal order', and injects trajectory supervision into MDLM SFT via a trajectory-aware masking strategy: an external AUTOREGRESSIVE TEACHER supplies token-level difficulty signals, tokens are bucketed by difficulty, and buckets define a reveal order that shapes the training masks. Evaluated on LLaDA-Instruct and Dream-Instruct across GSM8K/MATH/MBPP/HumanEval. Its ablation compares three bucket-assignment strategies: difficulty-descending, difficulty-ascending, and RANDOM (uniform bucket assignment) -- i.e. it already has a random-order control at the bucket level.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The teacher is an AR LM providing a scalar per-token difficulty; the induced order is a difficulty ranking, not a structural derivation, and there is no symbolic runtime anywhere. The random control randomises bucket ASSIGNMENT but (per the ablation text) is not described as preserving a per-step commit-count histogram taken from a specific external trajectory. Its target metric is TPS (tokens predicted per step) -- a parallelism/throughput metric -- not quality at matched cumulative token cost, and it never asks whether an inference-time structural mechanism can be removed. Backbones are LLaDA-8B and Dream-Instruct-7B; Dream-CODER and code-specialised structural decoders are untested.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The headline axis is 'accuracy-parallelism trade-off' measured in TPS = tokens predicted per step, which is not a compute unit: a step that attends a 512-token canvas costs vastly more than an AR step, so higher TPS does not establish cheaper generation. Our own measurement (flat canvas 685 tok/step HE+ vs AR 204 tokens_fed total) makes this concrete. (2) No matched autoregressive baseline at matched token cost -- ironic, since an AR teacher is used to *supervise*, so the AR model's own quality/cost is available and never reported as a Pareto point. (3) The random-bucket control is reported only as a figure (Fig. 6) in an ablation, with no seeds or CIs, and 'TRIMS consistently outperforms on MOST benchmarks' with a stated MATH regression -- the exception is acknowledged but not analysed. (4) Difficulty is defined by the teacher, so the method inherits the teacher's tokenisation and its own train/inference mismatch; no measurement of order-fidelity (did the student actually adopt the taught order?). (5) 0 citations, under review.

related_work.citation: Kim et al., "Train for the Worst, Plan for the Best: Understanding Token Ordering in Masked Diffusions", arXiv:2502.06768v3 — ICML 2025
related_work.venue_status: Published, ICML 2025. Verified: DBLP lists 'ICML 2025, Conference and Workshop Papers' (plus a CoRR 2025 record); Semantic Scholar publicationVenue='International Conference on Machine Learning', 200 citations. This is the field-standard reference for the training/inference order asymmetry.
related_work.what_it_covers: The canonical statement of the tension our candidate probes: MDLMs must learn an exponentially large set of infilling subproblems at TRAINING time (theoretically and empirically intractable subproblems), but can choose order freely at INFERENCE time; adaptive inference-time order selection sidesteps hard subproblems, lifting Sudoku from <7% to ~90% and beating an AR model with 7x the parameters trained with teacher forcing on the right order.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: It is precisely the paper that predicts our candidate's likely outcome without testing it: it argues the *inference-time* order choice is where the leverage is, and that training cannot cheaply absorb it. But it never runs the distillation experiment -- it does not take a specific external order generator, supervise a student on its trajectories, and measure whether the student reaches the planner's quality at the planner's cost. Its orders are adaptive/model-derived (planners over the denoiser), not structurally derived; its tasks are logic puzzles and text, not code; it prices nothing in tokens.
related_work.known_defects: (1) The headline Sudoku result is on a highly-structured combinatorial task with a tiny effective vocabulary, and the paper's own framing does not bound how much of the 'adaptive order' gain survives on natural code/text -- generalisation to 7B code LMs is asserted-adjacent, not shown. (2) The 7x-parameter AR comparison is a parameter-count match, not a compute or token-cost match, so 'outperforming ARMs' is a per-parameter claim being read by the field as an efficiency claim. (3) Being pre-cutoff and heavily cited, it is the theoretical prior a reviewer will invoke against our candidate's novelty -- our differentiation must be the *empirical distillation test with a matched-histogram control*, not the conceptual observation.

related_work.citation: "Planner Aware Path Learning in Diffusion Language Models Training" (PAPL), arXiv:2509.23405v3 — ICLR 2026 Oral
related_work.venue_status: Published, ICLR 2026 Oral. Verified via OpenReview: notes/search returns venue='ICLR 2026 Oral', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference'. arXiv v3 comment field reads 'Camera ready version for ICLR2026'. (Semantic Scholar still says venue='arXiv.org' — a textbook instance of S2 lagging on 2026 venues.)
related_work.what_it_covers: Proves that the standard discrete-diffusion ELBO does not describe a denoiser decoded with a non-uniform PLANNER, derives a planned ELBO (P-ELBO), and trains with it (PAPL) so that training-time paths match planned inference paths. Reports +23% relative HumanEval pass@10 for code, 4x MAUVE on text, +40% on proteins. This is the strongest existing statement that you can and should train a model to match a chosen non-uniform generation path.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The planner is an inference-time sampling heuristic over the denoiser's own scores, not an external symbolic decoder, and PAPL's goal is to make training *consistent with* a planner that is still used at inference -- the opposite of our compilation question (can the mechanism be deleted?). It provides no random-path control matched on step count and per-step commit counts, does not report token-level cost, and does not measure whether the trained model retains the planned order when the planner is removed.
related_work.known_defects: (1) PAPL keeps the planner at inference, so the paper cannot distinguish 'training absorbed the path' from 'training became compatible with the path' -- exactly the confound our candidate resolves by removing the mechanism. (2) The reported code gain is pass@10, a sampling-budget-inflated metric; pass@1 at matched token cost is not reported, so the efficiency reading is unsupported. (3) Improvements are spread across three domains with one metric each (protein 40%, MAUVE 4x, HumanEval pass@10 23%), which maximises headline breadth but gives no single domain a matched-cost frontier. (4) No matched AR control at equal token cost. (5) An ICLR Oral makes the P-ELBO the objective a reviewer will ask us to compare against — our flat-canvas student is trained with plain masked-CE on fixed orders, which PAPL's own theorem says is mis-specified for a non-uniform path. This is a real threat to our Phase-2 design and we should either adopt P-ELBO for arm A or state explicitly that we are testing plain-SFT transferability and add P-ELBO as a third arm.
