STEP 1 (~45 GPU-h on .73) -- RE-ANCHOR THE GAP. Do NOT run the three proposed arms yet. Run ONE arm: plain corruption at schedule-only's exact optimization protocol and tokenization. Concretely, a PlainSegmented mode that reuses _segmented_schedule_only_response for tokenization but keeps plain's uniform-Bernoulli-t masking and plain's min(20,1/t)/supervised weighting, launched with micro_batch_size_per_gpu=8 and bucket_by_length=false (matching git show 1825ded:scripts/run_schedule_only_sft_stage1_8gpu.sh), 5 epochs, lr 1e-5, global batch 128, seed 1, from $ROOT/models/Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B on $ROOT/data/scaffold_edu_v0/train_data.parquet. Grade at NFE 512 and 128 on HE+ and MBPP+ using scripts/run_plain_evalplus_full_8gpu.sh's exact protocol (--steps 512 --max-new-tokens 512 --temperature 0.0, evalplus 0.3.1, HUMANEVAL_OVERRIDE_PATH/MBPP_OVERRIDE_PATH set, merge_evalplus_shards.py --expected 164/378). DECISION GATE: if this arm scores near 21.95/24.34, the 18.3-point gap is genuinely corruption-schedule-driven and Step 2 is worth 120 GPU-h. If it scores near 3.66/11.38, factors (iv)+(v) explain the whole regression, the "structure-aware noising hurts" paper does not exist, and you stop here with a much cheaper and more honest finding: an 18-point apparent structural-masking regression that was tokenization + batching. This gate is the entire value of the candidate and it costs one arm.

STEP 2 (~120 GPU-h, ONLY if Step 1's gate opens) -- THE DECOMPOSITION. All arms now inherit the Step-1 protocol (segmented tokenization, micro_batch 8, bucketing off) so factors (iv) and (v) are held fixed by construction rather than measured. Code needed in scaffold_coder/sft_dataset.py + corruption.py + the band block of scaffold_coder/training/config/scaffold_sft.yaml (est. 150-250 lines, one coder, isolated to schedule_only paths -- do not touch PlainMaskedSFTDataset or ScheduleOnlySFTDataset's existing behaviour; add new modes so the two endpoint arms stay bit-reproducible):
  - Arm (i) POSITIONS: keep the per-sample masked-count draw from the band clocks, but permute WHICH positions get masked uniformly at random. Implementation: compute the band probabilities and the resulting mask as today, then randomly reshuffle the mask vector while preserving its cardinality and preserving each position's weight base by position index (so weights follow structure, positions do not).
  - Arm (ii) MARGINAL: add an explicit decoupling so the mask-probability clock and the weight clock are separate fields. Rescale the mask-probability clock so the per-sample masked-count distribution matches the Step-1 arm's measured distribution (not just its mean -- match the distribution, since p99 is 283 vs 225 and the tail is where the cost lives). Hold the weight clock at the band value.
  - Arm (iii) WEIGHTING: with the same decoupling, hold positions and marginal at schedule-only and switch the weight to plain's global-t min(20,1/t) with total-mass normalization by supervised count.
  Grade every arm at NFE 512 AND 128 on both benchmarks, same protocol as Step 1.

STEP 3 (no GPU) -- REPORTING. Report per-arm pass@1+, parseable rate, syntax-error rate, mean supervised masks, mean total loss mass, and bootstrap 95% CIs (n=164 / n=378; at 6/164 passes the schedule-only CI is roughly 1.4-7.8%, so several arms will be statistically indistinguishable and this must be stated, not hidden). Report recovered fraction against the RE-ANCHORED Step-1 baseline, never against the raw 21.95. State explicitly that factors (iv) and (v) were removed by construction and cite the measured 1.151x tokenizer inflation and the 8-vs-16 micro-batch / bucketing-off-vs-on difference as the reason.

REUSE OF WORK RUNNING ELSEWHERE: the .82 sampler/decoding audit directly de-risks Step 1's and Step 2's grading -- our own top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 moved HE by +14.6 points, which is comparable to the entire effect we are trying to attribute, so freeze the sampler to whatever .82 concludes and report it. The .104 matched AR baseline gives the absolute reference ceiling for the ladder (3.66 / 21.95 / 70.7) at no extra cost. Do not duplicate either.
feas.risk: The most likely outcome is a CONFOUNDED result that looks like a clean decomposition. Concretely: the three proposed arms all inherit the span-segmented tokenizer (1.151x token inflation, 300/300 rows differ) AND schedule-only's optimization protocol (micro_batch 8, bucketing off) while being compared against a plain baseline that had neither. Whichever arm happens to correlate most with those two nuisance factors will be credited with "recovering the gap", and the paper will assert a mechanism for structure-aware noising that is actually a BPE-manifold and batch-composition artifact. That is exactly retraction #2's shape: a pipeline stage silently changing its input while the measurement is attributed to the intended variable. The second most likely outcome is a null that fires for the wrong reason -- the stated kill criterion (no arm recovers >4 of 18.3 points) will very probably trigger because ~1.15x of the 1.51x mask-count ratio and an unknown share of the syntax-error rate are tokenizer-driven and no proposed arm touches them, leading to the false conclusion "the regression is irreducibly interactive". Third: because arms (ii) and (iii) both flow through the single shared u at sft_dataset.py:518-527, a naive implementation will change both the marginal and the weights in each arm, so the "single-factor" labels will be wrong and the additive decomposition will not close even if the science is fine. Fourth, statistical: at 6/164 HE+ passes for the baseline arm, the bootstrap CI spans several points, so 4-point "recoveries" are within noise on n=164 and the decomposition may be unfalsifiable at this sample size regardless of how carefully the arms are built.
feas.required_control: A LIKE-FOR-LIKE RE-ANCHORED BASELINE ARM, RUN AND PASSED BEFORE ANY DECOMPOSITION ARM IS LAUNCHED (Step 1 above): plain uniform-Bernoulli corruption trained on the span-segmented tokenization at schedule-only's exact optimization protocol (micro_batch_size_per_gpu=8, bucket_by_length=false), everything else identical. This is the control that prevents the analogous failure, because it is the only measurement that partitions the 18.3 points into "attributable to the corruption schedule" versus "attributable to tokenization + batch composition" -- the two nuisance factors I verified on disk and which every proposed arm silently carries. It is the direct analogue of replacing the hand-rolled verifier with evalplus untrusted_check: it forces the comparison to actually compare the thing being claimed. Ship it with three mandatory assertions, each mapping to one prior retraction: (1) TOKENIZER PARITY ASSERT -- log, per arm, mean/p50/p99 response token count and assert every decomposition arm matches the re-anchored baseline's tokenization mode exactly (the code already has the right hook: sft_dataset.py:861-863 raises if the segmented encoding is not decode-reversible; extend it to also record and diff the token-count distribution across arms). This is the retraction-#2 guard: it makes it impossible for a stage to silently change its input. (2) SUPERVISION-BUDGET ASSERT -- log per-arm mean/p50/p99 supervised masks AND mean/p99 total loss mass from the actual dataloader (I measured 43.0/4.250 plain vs 63.7/1.824 schedule-only over 400 samples this way), and normalize arms by total supervised tokens rather than by epochs; refuse to report a "recovered fraction" if any arm's total supervision differs from the baseline's by more than 5%. This is the retraction-#3 guard: it stops the expensive/high-supervision tail from being dropped or unmatched. (3) PROTOCOL-PARITY ASSERT -- emit resolved_training_config.json for EVERY arm (only the plain arm has one today; the schedule-only arm does not, which is why the micro_batch and bucketing divergence went unnoticed for two weeks) and machine-diff micro_batch_size_per_gpu, bucket_by_length, save_checkpoint_steps, seed, lr, total_epochs, max_length and the launch commit hash across all arms, failing the run on any mismatch outside the one factor under test.

lens.title: Stage 2 for the structural checkpoint: is the low-cost Pareto segment a real property or an undertrained-checkpoint artifact?
lens.claim: The low-cost end of the quality-compute frontier held by the structural runtime is not an artifact of an unfinished checkpoint: a stage-2 run that repairs the semantic forgetting of stage-1 via frozen-Instruct-teacher forward KL plus a flat-state mixture raises the structural model's ceiling but does not produce a crossover into the high-quality region that flat diffusion owns.
lens.why_now: Our entire surviving finding rests on Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B, a checkpoint that is stage-1 ONLY -- a stage 2 was evidently intended and never run -- and whose known pathology is severe semantic forgetting from Base initialization plus five SFT epochs. The ladder peaks at HE+ .177 / MBPP+ .354 against Dream-Coder-Instruct's .707 / .680, so the structural arm is plainly capability-starved rather than architecturally capped, and a reviewer will read the 'no crossover' claim as a statement about an undertrained model. We already have evidence the repair works in miniature: frozen-teacher lexical KL preserved vanilla capability at 15/16 parse on a 16-task probe, and a [STMT] prior took deep-recursion failures from 16/16 to 0/16. The machinery is all in the trainer already (teacher_kl_weight, teacher_kl_temperature, teacher_kl_roles, teacher_kl_topk, teacher_partial_pretrain, teacher_sharding, backed by loss.shifted_masked_forward_kl), so this is a configuration and mixture-design run, not new code. This is the single largest threat to our headline claim and it is cheap to close.
lens.experiment: One stage-2 arm resuming from Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B global_step_4465, with three changes from stage 1: (1) frozen teacher set to models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B rather than Base, via teacher_partial_pretrain, with forward KL applied on the ordinary-code roles TOKEN_STMT/TOKEN_HDR/TOKEN_DOC at teacher_kl_topk=256; (2) a training mixture that reintroduces flat plain-masked states alongside the rung mixture, so flat-canvas competence is retained rather than overwritten; (3) 2-3 epochs at reduced LR. Controls: (A) stage-2 with teacher_kl_weight=0 -- isolates the KL from the extra epochs and the mixture; (B) stage-1 checkpoint unchanged, already fully graded. Then re-run the FULL capacity ladder (Tiny/Small/Medium/Large) on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ with the existing generator, and re-plot on the token-cost Pareto against the vanilla NFE curve. Report termination reasons per tier -- resolved vs depth_exhausted vs model_call_budget -- and read process OR failure_process so budget-truncated tasks are not silently dropped, since that omission understated scaffold Large's mean cost by 2.85x on HE+ and 3.69x on MBPP+.
lens.assets_needed: HAVE: Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B global_step_4465 (29GB, already copied to LOCAL); Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B as the frozen teacher; the complete teacher-KL path in the trainer and loss.py (verified: shifted_masked_forward_kl with temperature/topk/weights); RungMixtureSFTDataset and PlainMaskedSFTDataset for the mixture; the full 8-cell stage-1 capacity ladder as the reference; the corrected process_metrics cost accounting. HARDWARE CONSTRAINT TO FLAG: teacher_sharding defaults to replicated, so a frozen 7B teacher alongside a 7B FSDP student wants the 183GB-per-card class -- run on LOCAL 8xL20A or .252 8xB200, not on the 97.8GB H20s without offload.
lens.kill_criterion: The robustness claim is falsified if stage-2 scaffold Medium exceeds .30 HE+ at or below 14k cumulative model tokens -- that is a genuine crossover into territory we claimed is exclusively vanilla's, and the paper's headline framing must be rewritten. The claim is confirmed if stage-2 Medium stalls at or below .20 HE+ while the vanilla ceiling stays at .707. If control arm (A) matches the KL arm, the improvement is just more epochs and the teacher-KL mechanism specifically gets no credit.
lens.builds_on: Our own stage-1 capacity ladder and the abandoned teacher-KL / [STMT]-prior / elastic-leaf pilots. Not a follow-up to an external paper -- this is the robustness leg our own surviving finding requires, and it also closes out the never-run second stage the project always assumed. Note the separately documented dead end to avoid repeating: the [expand] length-control route fired 0 times after 64 steps of leaf-only training at expand-bonus 1/2/4, so stage 2 must NOT be a fourth attempt at the same thing -- length control needs an explicit length token or head if it is reopened at all.

diff.differentiation_statement: No paper published before 2026-05-07 makes this claim with this method in this setting, and the closest neighbours are separable on four axes at once. AnCoder (2026-02) is the only prior work that honestly reports that structurally-anchored diffusion still loses to its own autoregressive initialisation, but it does so at 809M against a 494M AR, at 3-9% absolute pass@1, with no cost accounting and no training-budget leg; TreeDiff (2025-08) reaches the opposite, more optimistic conclusion only by importing AR numbers from the EvalPlus leaderboard for entirely different model lineages, conflating denoising steps with canvas length, and reporting no token cost at all. Ours differs in (a) setting: a typed-AST decoder runtime with typed holes, template expansion, mutable tree state and expand/delete edits, not a corruption-schedule reweighting on a flat canvas; (b) control design: a matched-lineage AR pair that is architecturally identical to the diffusion backbone (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B vs Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B: same hidden 3584, 28 layers, 28 heads, 4 KV heads, intermediate 18944, vocab 152064, rope_theta 1e6, differing only by mask_token_id) plus a matched Plain-SFT control that shares checkpoint, split, corruption weighting and trainer with the scaffold arm and differs only in whether the structural machinery is present; (c) cost accounting: hook-measured tokens_fed and attended_context_sum, validated against closed-form prediction on 1084 task-runs, rather than NFE or wall-clock -- and we can show the two accountings disagree on at least one pairwise verdict, which is a stronger version of the cross-family-metric argument that Scaling Beyond Masked Diffusion (ICML 2026) makes for perplexity and that CaRE (concurrent) makes for NFE within the diffusion family only; and (d) the load-bearing new leg: an explicit training-budget arm that tests whether the structural arm's deficit is a checkpoint-maturity artifact, which is exactly the intervention that Capacity-Not-Format (concurrent) needs for its observational capacity story and that Diffusion-Beats-AR-in-Data-Constrained-Settings predicts should matter, and which no structural-diffusion-code paper has run. Separately and importantly, this is a robustness leg on our OWN finding rather than a follow-up to an external paper, so the prior-art risk was never the binding constraint here.

followup_openings.defect: The claim this candidate proposes to defend has already been retracted internally, and the candidate text does not know it. Retraction 4 (dated 2026-08-07 15:00, evidence on .104 at commits da24eb6 / ad748b1) shows a matched-lineage AR (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B) at HE+ .524 / MBPP+ .648 with mean tokens_fed 204 / 101, versus scaffold Medium at HE+ .177 / MBPP+ .354 with 13,980 / 7,080. AR is ~70x cheaper AND +0.29-0.34 higher quality -- strict Pareto dominance -- and it also dominates on attended_context_sum for MBPP+ while costing only 1.44x more on HE+ with +0.30 quality. Retraction 5 shows the same AR wins on infilling too (.7638 at 239 tokens vs DreamOn .7018 at 4923). So 'the low-cost Pareto segment held by the structural runtime' does not exist as a segment: AR owns it. The kill_criterion is also mis-specified -- it says the claim is falsified if stage-2 Medium exceeds .30 HE+ at <=14k tokens, but AR already achieves .524 at 204 tokens, so BOTH branches of the stated criterion now confirm nothing about the frontier.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-aim the experiment, keep the design. Stop asking 'is our frontier segment real?' and ask 'is the structural runtime's deficit against a matched-lineage AR a training-budget artifact or a paradigm ceiling?' Same checkpoint, same three arms, same full capacity ladder, same dual cost accounting -- but the reference line becomes matched AR rather than flat diffusion, and the reportable outcome is a quantified answer to 'how much of a structural-decoding deficit does a second stage buy back?' Rewrite the kill criterion against the AR line: the paradigm-ceiling reading survives if stage-2 Medium stays below AR pass@1 at every cost budget; it is falsified if stage-2 Medium reaches AR-competitive pass@1 at any budget below AR's own tokens_fed. Also fix the miniature-evidence premise: the repo shows the [STMT] prior at bonus=4 gave 16/16 nonempty-and-function but parse 0/16, and the best combination (seeded stmt=4 + bonus=4) reached only parse 8/16, later 7/16 after the leaf-elastic adapter -- so 'evidence the repair works in miniature' is much weaker than the candidate states, and a prior LoRA semantic-preservation arm already breached a pre-registered 40% vanilla-HE+ stop-loss at 35.98%.
followup_openings.target_paper: OUR OWN premise -- DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md Retraction 4 (repo /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Pursuing the candidate verbatim would spend 50 GPU-hours defending a sentence that our own harness deleted eight hours earlier, and would reproduce Retraction 4's root cause -- reasoning about a frontier without the field's natural baseline in it. Re-aimed, the same run answers a question that no external paper answers and that three separate papers (Capacity-Not-Format, Diffusion-Beats-AR-in-Data-Constrained, Bitter-Lesson) set up but leave open.

followup_openings.defect: It argues that teacher-KL self-distillation is the wrong vehicle for on-policy signal -- it 'inherits an extra forward pass, schedule sensitivity, and stylistic drift from the teacher' -- and shows data-side replay beats it on three AR backbones (BWT -13.93 to -0.65 at 10% replay). It never tests any non-autoregressive student, and never a student with an expanded vocabulary. Meanwhile the candidate commits to exactly the mechanism OPR argues against, and pays OPR's predicted cost literally: teacher_sharding defaults to replicated, so a frozen BF16 7B teacher alongside the FSDP student is what forces the run onto 183GB-class cards.
followup_openings.our_fix: Make stage 2 three-armed instead of two-armed: (A) teacher-KL as proposed, (B) KL-off with identical epochs and mixture, (C) OPR-style execution-filtered replay -- roll out the current scaffold checkpoint, filter with evalplus untrusted_check (we already use it as the corrected grader), replay survivors as ordinary SFT pairs. Arm C removes the teacher forward pass entirely, so it costs LESS than the proposed arm and frees the run to go on the H20s. Report BWT-style retention on a held-out vanilla-code probe alongside pass@1.
followup_openings.target_paper: On-Policy Replay for Continual Supervised Fine-Tuning, arXiv:2605.29495 (concurrent, 2026-05-28)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It turns a single-mechanism configuration run into a mechanism comparison, tests a concurrent claim in a modality its authors did not touch, and supplies a code-execution reward where OPR had to assume one. The three-arm version is a short paper on its own even if all three arms fail to reach AR.

followup_openings.defect: PAPL proves the standard discrete-diffusion ELBO does not describe a denoiser that is used with a non-uniform planner, and derives a planned ELBO. The scaffold runtime is an extreme non-uniform planner -- typed holes, deterministic template expansion, rule fixed-point, monotone C0 commit order -- yet stage 1 was trained with a corruption schedule that does not generate the states the runtime actually visits at inference. Neither PAPL nor anyone else has extended P-ELBO to a planner that MUTATES THE CANVAS (expand/delete, template instantiation), where the reverse process is not a reordering of a fixed-length chain at all. Correspondingly, the candidate's own design has no path-alignment arm.
followup_openings.our_fix: Add a path-aligned stage-2 objective: train on states sampled from the runtime's actual reachable commit order rather than from the offline corruption schedule. This is the principled reading of the repo's most striking pathology -- the model never emits [expand] despite an audited 17,883 expand targets in 5,000 states, and expand logits stay below ordinary lexical tokens through 64 steps of leaf-only training at three bonus levels -- which is exactly the train/inference path mismatch PAPL formalises, not a supervision shortage.
followup_openings.target_paper: Planner Aware Path Learning in Diffusion Language Models Training, arXiv:2509.23405 (ICLR 2026 Oral)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It gives the candidate a third possible explanation besides 'undertrained' and 'architecturally capped', namely 'trained on the wrong states', and it is the only one of the three that comes with an ICLR-Oral theoretical warrant. It also stops stage 2 from being a fourth attempt at the [expand] design that already failed, which the candidate itself flags as a hazard.

followup_openings.defect: Its headline that AST-guided masking 'narrows the performance gap between diffusion-based models and established autoregressive baselines' rests on AR numbers footnoted as cited from the EvalPlus Leaderboard for DeepSeek-Coder-33B, CodeQwen1.5-7B and CodeLlama-7B/13B -- none re-run in its harness, none architecture-matched to the LLaDA backbone. It also uses T as both denoising-step count and maximum generation length, so quality-vs-compute is confounded with canvas length, and it reports no token-level cost anywhere. Adaptation is LoRA-only by admitted hardware necessity. Its own span-level ablation underperforms random masking on MBPP without reconciliation.
followup_openings.our_fix: Publish the comparison TreeDiff could not: a matched-lineage AR re-run in the same harness with the same grader, step budget decoupled from canvas length, and hook-measured tokens_fed plus attended_context_sum. We already have all four ingredients (the architecture-identical Qwen2.5-Coder-7B / Dream-Coder-v0-Base-7B pair, the official evalplus grader with an empty-program negative control at 0.000, and forward_pre_hook cost instrumentation agreeing with closed form on 1084 task-runs), plus a matched Plain-SFT control TreeDiff has no analogue for.
followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff, arXiv:2508.01473 (2025-08-02, preprint)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts the most-cited structural-diffusion-code result from an encouraging trend into a measured verdict, and it is nearly free for us -- the harness exists and the numbers are mostly already collected.

followup_openings.defect: It states outright that all its diffusion models fall short of the AR baseline on both syntactic validity and pass@1, which is the honest version of our finding -- but only at 809M against a 494M AR, at 3-9% absolute pass@1 with no confidence intervals or seed variance, and with no cost accounting even though its two-tower anchor-denoiser architecture has strictly higher per-step forward cost than a single-tower MDLM of the same parameter count. It compares at equal parameters, not equal forward cost. And it runs exactly one training recipe per arm, so 'structural priors help but do not close the AR gap' is inseparable from 'we stopped training too early'.
followup_openings.our_fix: Replicate its verdict at 7B with an architecture-identical AR, price both towers in measured forward tokens rather than parameters, and add the training-budget leg it lacks. Our stage-2 ladder is the missing dimension: if the AR gap is invariant to a second stage at 7B, AnCoder's 809M conclusion generalises and hardens; if the gap closes materially, AnCoder's conclusion is revealed as a training-budget artifact of its own recipe.
followup_openings.target_paper: AnCoder, arXiv:2602.17688 (2026-02-05, preprint)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Either outcome is a citable strengthening or correction of the closest honest prior work, at a scale 8.6x larger, and it is the cleanest way to frame our result as building on the literature rather than merely reporting a negative.

followup_openings.defect: Both establish that structural output costs capability, and Capacity-Not-Format adds the sharper claim that the cost is a function of spare capacity -- but capacity is varied only by SWAPPING MODELS (Sonnet vs Haiku vs GPT-4o-mini vs Opus), never by training one model further, and the structure is always prompt- or schema-level in an autoregressive model. The Format Tax similarly decomposes the loss into prompt-induced and decoder-induced parts but never considers structure enforced by a generative runtime, and never a non-autoregressive model.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the within-model capacity intervention their observational story needs: hold the structural constraint exactly fixed (same runtime, same capacity ladder Tiny/Small/Medium/Large) and vary capacity by stage-2 training budget, in a masked-diffusion model where structure is load-bearing for generation rather than cosmetic for output format. Also add the Format-Tax remedy as a baseline -- generate freeform then reformat into the typed AST -- which is cheap and, if it wins, is itself the paper's most useful practical finding.
followup_openings.target_paper: Capacity, Not Format, arXiv:2606.09410 (concurrent) + The Format Tax, arXiv:2604.03616 (2026-04-04)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the single strongest available reframing of the candidate. It relocates a project-internal robustness check into an active cross-paradigm literature where our setup is the one intervention nobody can run with API models, and it makes the 'structure tax shrinks with capability' hypothesis testable rather than asserted.

followup_openings.defect: CaRE standardises ACTUAL NFE across seven remasking strategies and shows compute-matched comparison reverses several published rankings -- but it treats NFE as the unit to be standardised rather than questioned, stays entirely within the diffusion family, includes no AR arm, and measures MAUVE/perplexity on OpenWebText and LM1B rather than execution-graded code. Scaling Beyond establishes that perplexity is misleading across families and legitimises Pareto reporting, but its cost axis is sampling speed, which is hardware- and batch-dependent.
followup_openings.our_fix: Extend the compute-aware-protocol argument one level up: from intra-diffusion NFE to cross-paradigm, hardware-invariant measured tokens_fed and attended_context_sum, on execution-graded HumanEval+/MBPP+. We can exhibit the reversal concretely -- 685 tok/step for a flat 512-canvas vs 181 tok/step for the structural runtime (3.8x, invisible to any NFE-matched protocol), an AR model with no NFE analogue at all finishing in 101-204 total tokens, and at least one pairwise verdict that FLIPS between our two accountings (AR is 70x cheaper than scaffold Medium on tokens_fed but 1.44x more expensive on attended_context_sum for HE+). Also report the sampler-protocol magnitude alongside it: top_p 1.0 to 0.95 moved HumanEval by +14.6 points, exceeding most published diffusion-LM method gains.
followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE, arXiv:2607.24763 (concurrent) + Scaling Beyond Masked Diffusion Language Models, arXiv:2602.15014 (ICML 2026)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the most defensible standalone contribution in the whole dllm line, it is concurrent-safe, it needs no training at all, and it is the natural companion paper to whatever the stage-2 arm returns -- so it de-risks the 50 GPU-hours regardless of which way stage 2 goes.

followup_openings.defect: Both are entirely autoregressive, both assume teacher and student share a vocabulary and a factorisation, and neither addresses a student whose vocabulary was EXPANDED with new tokens. The recovery paper's central evidence is correlational (CKA alignment correlates with recovery) with no intervention that moves one without the other. Our repo documents precisely the failure mode their assumptions exclude: new structural output rows initialised from semantic word averages, so [IF]/[FOR]/[WHILE] row norms systematically beat [STMT] inside a restricted line vocabulary, and the four edit-source rows leak as literal Python text ('expandexpand', 'deletedelete') in 154/164 outputs -- LoRA can move hidden states but cannot separate near-identical output rows.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run frozen-teacher and self-distillation repair in a masked-diffusion student with an expanded structural vocabulary and report the new-token-row interference regime as a boundary condition on the SDFT claim. And supply the missing intervention for the recovery paper: the KL-off arm with identical epochs and mixture separates manifold realignment from additional optimisation, which is exactly the control their correlational result lacks. Note our KL mask must exclude all scaffold special IDs -- the repo audit found the original mask selected TOKEN_STMT/HDR/DOC roles that token-level [expand]/[delete] targets also use, so the pretrained teacher was being asked to match distributions on tokens it has never seen, consistent with expansions=0 across every run.
followup_openings.target_paper: Self-Distillation Enables Continual Learning, arXiv:2601.19897 (ICML 2026 spotlight) + Self-Distillation as a Performance Recovery Mechanism, arXiv:2604.15794
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It gives us a genuine extension of an ICML 2026 spotlight rather than a re-application, it names a concrete regime where a popular method's assumptions break, and the diagnosis is already half-written in our own logs.

related_work.citation: Y. Zeng, J. Cao, Z. Li, et al. "TreeDiff: AST-Guided Code Generation with Diffusion LLMs." arXiv:2508.01473 (v1 2025-08-02; v3 2026-01-06).
related_work.known_defects: (1) The AR baselines (DeepSeek-Coder-33B, CodeQwen1.5-7B, CodeLlama-7B/13B) are footnoted as "cited from the EvalPlus Leaderboard" -- they are entirely different model lineages, never re-run in the paper's harness, and none is architecture-matched to the LLaDA backbone; the claim of "narrowing the performance gap between diffusion-based models and established autoregressive baselines" therefore rests on cross-harness numbers. (2) T is used simultaneously as the denoising-step count AND the maximum generation length, so the quality-vs-compute axis is confounded with the canvas-length axis. (3) No token-level or FLOP-level cost accounting at all, so the flat canvas being re-attended every step is invisible. (4) LoRA-only adaptation, admitted as a hardware workaround, so the result speaks to adapter-scale structural bias, not full-parameter. (5) Span-level AST masking actually underperforms random on MBPP (39.7 vs baseline) -- reported but not reconciled with the headline.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. DBLP lists only "CoRR 2025"; OpenReview API v2 returns only the dblp mirror record (venueid=dblp.org/journals/CORR/2025), no conference venueid.

Decoupling (freeform then reformat, or extended thinking) recovers most lost accuracy. Recent closed-weight models show little format tax.

But its decomposition (prompt-induced vs decoder-induced) is exactly the decomposition our scaffold arm needs, and its "decouple then reformat" remedy is a strong, cheap baseline that would plausibly beat a trained structural runtime on our own benchmarks. It also implies the tax is a model-maturity property, not an inherent one -- which is the candidate's own hypothesis, arrived at independently in a different paradigm.

related_work.citation: "Capacity, Not Format: Rethinking Structured Reasoning Failures." arXiv:2606.09410 (2026-06-08).
related_work.known_defects: Closed/open API models, prompt-level schemas, no training intervention at all -- capacity is varied by swapping models, never by training the same model further. Our fix: vary capacity WITHIN one model via a stage-2 training budget while holding the structural constraint fixed. That is the intervention their observational capacity story needs, and it is the strongest reframing available for this candidate.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; no OpenReview/DBLP conference record found.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API abstract + metadata; OpenReview api2 notes/search (no matching venue record).
related_work.what_it_covers: Concurrent. Argues the format tax is capacity-dependent: models with headroom absorb JSON without degradation (Sonnet 88.7+-4.0 JSON vs 89.3+-1.7 CoT on MATH-Hard), while models near their limits degrade sharply via truncation (Haiku -36.2pp) and via pure capacity competition even with truncation eliminated (GPT-4o-mini -28.0pp). Uses information-matched prose controls and a four-level schema-complexity gradient; penalty scales with schema complexity (McNemar p<0.0001).
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent, so no preemption -- and it supplies the sharpest available theoretical frame for the reframed candidate: the structural tax is a function of SPARE CAPACITY, which predicts that a capability-starved stage-1 checkpoint should pay a large structure tax and that repairing capability should shrink it. That is precisely the hypothesis the stage-2 arm tests, in a paradigm they never touch.

diff.sharpened_claim: For a 7B masked-diffusion code model, the capability deficit of a typed-AST decoder runtime relative to an architecture-identical autoregressive checkpoint is not a curable artifact of an unfinished second training stage: resuming Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B for a compute-matched stage 2 -- under three mechanisms held at identical epochs, mixture and LR (frozen-Instruct-teacher forward KL on ordinary-code roles only with all scaffold special IDs excluded from the KL mask; the same run with teacher_kl_weight=0; and execution-filtered on-policy replay in place of the teacher) -- raises the structural arm's ceiling but leaves it Pareto-dominated by matched-lineage Qwen2.5-Coder-7B on both hook-measured cost accountings at every point of the Tiny/Small/Medium/Large capacity ladder on HumanEval+ and MBPP+. Read positively, this makes three contributions no prior work supplies: it is the first within-model test of the capacity-dependence hypothesis for structured generation (varying capability by training budget while holding the structural constraint fixed, rather than by swapping models as in Capacity-Not-Format); it is the first structural-diffusion-code result reported against an architecture-matched AR control with hook-validated cross-paradigm token accounting, which we show reverses at least one pairwise verdict that NFE-matched or step-matched protocols cannot see; and it identifies train/inference path mismatch, in the sense of PAPL's planned ELBO, rather than undertraining, as the residual explanation -- evidenced by structural edit actions that are never selected despite 17,883 supervised expand targets in 5,000 audited states. Fallback if the frontier does move: the same three arms quantify how much of a runtime-enforced structure tax a second stage buys back, which is a positive result of equal value.

feas.risk:
The single most likely outcome is a confounded null that cannot be attributed. Three protocol deltas are forced on this run before any science happens — fresh AdamW moments and a fresh cosine schedule (no `optimizer_state.pt` exists), a rebuilt dependency stack, and possibly sdpa instead of flash_attention_2 — so if stage-2 Medium lands at, say, .19 HE+, there is no way to distinguish "the structural deficit is a paradigm ceiling" from "the optimizer restart and the attention-kernel swap ate the gain". Arm B (KL-off, identical epochs/mixture) controls the *KL* but not any of those three, because it inherits all of them.

The second, sharper risk is a *silent* null of exactly the family of the three retractions. `shifted_masked_forward_kl` raises only when `weights[mask].sum() <= 0`; if `lexical_teacher_target_mask` returns an all-False mask for a micro-batch, `if lexical_mask.any():` at trainer line 707 simply skips the KL and the step proceeds with plain CE. Arm A would then be arm B wearing a different config, the two would agree perfectly, and the honest-looking conclusion "the teacher-KL mechanism gets no credit" would be an artifact of a mask that never fired — indistinguishable at the log level from a real negative unless `anchored_tokens` is recorded. That is the same shape as Retraction 2 (a pipeline stage that silently discarded its input).

Third: the structural arm may not clear the *runtime* gate at all. Every prior full-merge structural gate in SEMANTIC_PRESERVATION_GATE.md ended at 16/16 `depth_capacity_exhausted` or 0/16 parse, and `expansions` was exactly 0 in every single arm ever run. If stage 2 reproduces that, the ladder produces 0.000 across tiers and there is no frontier to compare — 210 GPU-hours for an uninterpretable floor. PAPL (arXiv:2509.23405, ICLR 2026 Oral) predicts precisely this: the runtime is an aggressive non-uniform planner and neither `RungMixtureSFTDataset` nor `PlainMaskedSFTDataset` samples the states the C0-monotone commit order actually visits, so more epochs on the wrong state distribution buys nothing.
feas.required_control:
A per-step KL-liveness assertion, logged and non-optional: emit `anchored_tokens` (already returned in `shifted_masked_forward_kl`'s metrics dict, and currently DISCARDED — trainer line 715 does `kl_loss, _ = ...`) plus the count of micro-batches where `lexical_mask.any()` was False, and hard-fail the run if the KL fires on fewer than a pre-registered fraction of steps. Plus a paired end-of-run diff: assert arm A and arm B checkpoints differ on the parameters the KL is supposed to move.

This is the control that prevents the exact failure we have had three times. Retraction 1 was a verifier that compared nothing; Retraction 2 was a stage that discarded its input and measured the wrong model; Retraction 3 was an average that dropped the expensive tasks. The analogous failure here is a KL term that never fires — the mask is silently empty for the states the mixture actually produces — so arm A ≡ arm B, and we publish "the teacher-KL mechanism specifically gets no credit" as a finding when in fact the mechanism was never applied. `if lexical_mask.any():` makes this failure completely silent: no exception, no NaN, loss curves look normal, and both arms converge to the same place for the most banal possible reason.

Two subordinate controls, both cheap, both required:
(1) Cost-accounting agreement assertion. Port `generate_evalplus_ar.py`'s closed-form-vs-hook check into the scaffold generator and assert equality per task-run (the AR path already validates on 1084 task-runs). Without it, any new `tokens_fed` on the scaffold side is an unvalidated number entering the same Pareto plot that Retraction 3 corrupted — and read every cost through `proc()` (`process` OR `failure_process`), never `process` alone.
(2) Negative control on the grader, re-run per arm, not inherited: submit an empty-program solutions.jsonl through `evalplus.evaluate` and assert pass@1 == 0.000. Retraction 1's failure mode was an empty solution scoring full marks; the assertion costs seconds and re-proves the grader is live in this arm's harness.

lens.title: Diffusion LMs Report Their Best Quality at Zero Parallelism: NFE Is Not a Cost Unit and Step-Saturation Is a Schedule Artifact
lens.claim: Dream-Coder-7B's reported quality optimum (HE+ .707 / MBPP+ .680 at 512 steps) occurs exactly where its unmasking schedule commits one token per step, i.e. at zero parallelism and a strictly left-to-right generation order; the widely-reported 'saturation past 512 steps' is not a model or dependency limit but an arithmetic property of the linear timestep schedule, which emits ~50% literal no-op forward passes once steps exceed canvas length. Consequently every published NFE-indexed quality curve for this model family conflates 'more denoising' with 'less parallelism', and NFE is not a valid cost unit for cross-family comparison.
lens.why_now: The parallel-decoding literature is extremely crowded (DUS 2506.19037, ParallelBench 2510.04767, DMax 2604.08302, LEAP 2605.10980, PARD 2607.24306) and nearly all of it reports speedups indexed on NFE/steps against a 'full-NFE' quality reference. CaRE (2607.24763, first public 2026-06-04) just argued seven remasking papers are mutually incomparable because nominal step counts were not controlled, and that compute-matched comparison reverses published rankings -- but CaRE standardizes NFE, it does not show the reference point itself IS the zero-parallelism corner, nor that steps>canvas is literally no-op. Our repo already contains the exact-fixed-point evidence (byte-identical outputs) that makes this unarguable rather than suggestive.
lens.experiment: Three legs. (1) ALREADY MEASURED: nfe512 vs nfe1024 on Dream-Coder-Instruct-7B is a hard fixed point -- 164/164 HE+ and 378/378 MBPP+ per-task outcomes identical, 163/164 and 376/378 solutions byte-identical, while wall clock rises 11.31 -> 24.23 s/task; simulating the timesteps=linspace(1,eps,steps+1) + int(nmask*(1-s/t)) rule in models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B/generation_utils.py:406-440 shows 514/1024 steps commit ZERO tokens and max tokens/step is 1. (2) ALREADY MEASURED: instrumenting generation_tokens_hook_func to log which canvas positions fill at each step gives Pearson(step,position)=0.999 and 97.2% rightward consecutive commits at nfe512 (and 0.999/95.8% at nfe128, nfe256) -- autoregressive at EVERY budget, max_parallel=2. (3) TO RUN: re-index the existing 6-point NFE sweep on tokens-per-step (canvas/steps) instead of steps, and add the missing canvas dimension -- a canvas x steps grid {128,256,384,512}^2 on HE+ (n=164), reporting pass@1+ against forwarded token-positions (steps x (prompt+canvas)) and wall clock, plus a Qwen2.5-Coder-7B AR+KV-cache reference at equal output length. Cross-family replication on LLaDA-8B-Instruct to show the schedule property is not Dream-specific.
lens.assets_needed: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B (have); runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe{16,32,64,128,256,1024}, runs/dream_coder_instruct_{heplus,mbppplus}_r2, runs/dream_instruct_mbppplus_nfe* (have, 6-point sweep both benchmarks); data/evalplus/{humaneval,mbpp}_plus.jsonl + evalplus 0.3.1 grader (have); scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py needs a --canvas flag decoupled from --steps (one-line; currently every launch script sets max_new_tokens==steps). MISSING: LLaDA-8B-Instruct weights (download via hy-proxy) for cross-family leg; the Qwen2.5-Coder AR reference is reportedly already running on .104 by another agent -- coordinate, do not duplicate.
lens.kill_criterion: Dies if the canvas x steps grid shows quality is governed by step count rather than tokens-per-step -- concretely if canvas256/steps256 (1 tok/step, half the compute) scores materially below canvas512/steps512 by more than sampling noise (>3 pts, HE+ n=164), meaning the long canvas carries information and 'more steps' is not reducible to 'less parallelism'. Also dies if measured commit order on LLaDA is not left-to-right (Pearson < 0.8), making the AR-collapse finding Dream-specific.
lens.builds_on: Follows up CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, first public 2026-06-04, NOT concurrent under the 2026-05-07 cutoff but only just -- cite carefully), which standardizes actual NFE across remasking strategies but evaluates OpenWebText/LM1B MAUVE rather than executable code and never shows the full-NFE reference is the zero-parallelism corner. Repairs the defect ParallelBench (2510.04767) approaches from the other side: it diagnoses conditional-independence damage from parallel decoding on synthetic list tasks, whereas we show the dual and more embarrassing fact on a real code benchmark -- at its best setting the model is not parallel at all, so reported quality is an AR number priced at 512x AR compute. Also externalizes our own retracted error class (NFE-as-cost-unit, Retraction 3). Distinct from PARD (2607.24306, 2026-07-27, concurrent) which notes block-diffusion LMs are L-to-R-aligned and proposes a sampler; ours is an evaluation-validity claim about the existing NFE curve.

diff.differentiation_statement: The candidate as written contains two claims of unequal standing, and the positioning must separate them. Claim A -- "the reported optimum is at ~1 token/step, i.e. the sampler is effectively autoregressive on code" -- is NOT novel: DiffuCoder (arXiv:2506.20639, 2025-06-25, ICLR 2026 Poster) defines local/global AR-ness precisely as consecutive-next-position commit rate, measures it on Dream-7B and DiffuCoder for HumanEval at steps=length=512, and states in plain text that "setting the number of diffusion timesteps equal to the sequence length [is] effectively resorting to token-by-token generation to enhance performance." DUS (2506.19037, ICML 2026) puts the AR-collapse in its abstract; ParallelBench (2510.04767, ICLR 2026) already plots real benchmarks against "# Tokens per Step" in App F.3 and reports wall clock in F.4. A reviewer who knows this literature will not accept leg (2) as a contribution. Claim B is defensible and, as far as an exhaustive search shows, unpublished: the *arithmetic* of the released linear schedule. No paper we found audits `timesteps=linspace(1,eps,steps+1)` with `int(n_mask*(1-s/t))` and reports that (i) once steps exceed canvas length the schedule emits literal zero-commit forward passes, (ii) the maximum commit per step (excluding the final flush) is exactly 1 for every steps>=512 at canvas 512, so the entire upper half of every published NFE sweep for this model is a strictly dominated region, and (iii) the resulting quality curve is therefore a hard fixed point, not a saturation. That last point is directly verifiable on our disk and stronger than anything in the literature: at steps 512 vs 1024 on Dream-Coder-Instruct, HumanEval+ pass@1 is 0.707 vs 0.707 with identical base pass@1 0.762, 150/164 solutions byte-identical (MBPP+: 335/378), while mean per-task wall clock rises 11.31s -> 24.23s (2.14x) -- i.e. 514 of 1024 forward passes are paid for and provably discarded. The paper this supports is not "dLLMs are secretly AR" (taken) but "the published step-indexed quality curve for this family has a computable dominated region, and the community's cost unit cannot see it." Differentiation from CaRE (2607.24763) is easy and needs restating in the candidate: CaRE's arXiv v1 is 2026-06-04, which is AFTER the 2026-05-07 cutoff, so it is CONCURRENT, not prior -- the candidate's builds_on field asserts the opposite and must be corrected. CaRE standardizes actual NFE on OpenWebText/LM1B MAUVE with base models; we work on executable code with EvalPlus grading on an instruct/code checkpoint, and we show the schedule-level *reason* NFE is the wrong unit rather than merely re-normalising it. Differentiation from ParallelBench: it re-indexes on tokens-per-step and concludes "existing benchmarks are uninformative, build a synthetic one"; we conclude "existing benchmarks contain a computable no-op region that invalidates the reference point," and we can prove it with byte-identity rather than the confounded slight-degradation curve F.3 itself concedes is dominated by model capacity. Differentiation from concurrent 2608.05687 (2026-08-06, ARR Aug 2026): it logs commitments on GSM8K/MATH-500 to explain reasoning failure and proposes frontier-gated commitment; we make an accounting claim about code benchmarks and never propose a sampler.

followup_openings.defect: AR-ness is a purely descriptive statistic reported at a single operating point (steps = length = 512) with no cost axis whatsoever -- no wall clock, no forwarded token-positions, no AR+KV-cache reference. The paper therefore establishes 'the sampler is nearly AR' but never draws the consequence that the quality number it reports is an AR number bought at hundreds of times AR compute. Its one gesture at compute ('less performance drop when decoding in half as many steps' after GRPO) is a two-point comparison with no accounting and no test.
followup_openings.our_fix: Attach the missing cost axis to their own metric. Report AR-ness (their exact local@k / global@k definitions, so the comparison is apples-to-apples) JOINTLY with (a) realised mean tokens-per-step, (b) forwarded token-positions = steps x (prompt + canvas), and (c) wall clock, across our full 6-point NFE sweep on Dream-Coder-Instruct with EvalPlus HumanEval+/MBPP+ grading. Add the Qwen2.5-Coder-7B AR+KV-cache reference at equal output length that no paper in this cluster has. This turns their descriptive statistic into a cost-validity result and simultaneously upgrades their code numbers from plain HumanEval to EvalPlus+.
followup_openings.target_paper: DiffuCoder (arXiv:2506.20639, ICLR 2026 Poster)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts the strongest overlap in the literature from a preemption into a citation-and-extension: we adopt their metric, supply the axis they omitted, and the conclusion changes from 'dLLMs are somewhat AR' to 'the field's headline quality numbers for this family are AR numbers with a diffusion price tag.'

followup_openings.defect: F.3 re-indexes GSM8K/IFEval/MATH on tokens-per-step and then explicitly concedes the leg is confounded: 'Even when decoding one token per step, these benchmarks already exhibit substantial difficulty, which implies that model capacity remains a dominant factor that cannot be separated from the analysis.' Its evidence on real tasks is a slight-degradation curve on one model (LLaDA 1.5), single A100, batch 1, appendix-only. It also never examines the steps > canvas regime at all, so the dominated region is invisible to its framing.
followup_openings.our_fix: Do the real-benchmark leg in a form immune to the capacity confound: instead of comparing accuracies across parallelism levels (where capacity dominates), exhibit a HARD FIXED POINT within one model at one canvas -- steps 512 vs 1024, identical pass@1 (.707/.707 HE+), 150/164 byte-identical solutions, 2.14x wall clock -- and derive it from the schedule arithmetic (514/1024 zero-commit steps). Capacity cannot explain a byte-identical output pair. Then extend their tokens-per-step axis leftward into the region they never enter (steps > canvas) and rightward with the canvas dimension they hold fixed.
followup_openings.target_paper: ParallelBench (arXiv:2510.04767, ICLR 2026 Poster), App F.3
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It repairs the exact weakness the authors flag themselves, on executable code with an official grader instead of synthetic list ops, and does so with an argument form (byte-identity) that no capacity or noise objection touches.

followup_openings.defect: CaRE standardizes 'actual NFE', i.e. it still counts forward passes. But a forward pass over prompt+512 canvas and one over prompt+128 canvas differ ~3x in FLOPs, so two settings matched on actual NFE are NOT compute-matched. Its evaluation is MAUVE on OpenWebText/LM1B with base models -- a distributional proxy known to be length- and temperature-sensitive, which is the very confound class the paper is diagnosing. No instruct or code checkpoint; no task-correctness metric.
followup_openings.our_fix: Propose forwarded token-positions (steps x (prompt + canvas)) as the cost unit and show it strictly refines actual-NFE by exhibiting a canvas x steps grid where actual-NFE is constant but FLOPs and quality are not. Evaluate on executable code with EvalPlus untrusted_check (a correctness metric, not a distribution proxy) on an instruct code checkpoint. Cite CaRE as concurrent agreement on the disease and position our unit as the next iteration of the cure.
followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE (arXiv:2607.24763, concurrent, 2026-06-04)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the cleanest 'we fix the closest paper' story available, and because CaRE is concurrent it costs us nothing on priority while giving the paper an obvious, reviewer-legible delta: NFE -> forwarded token-positions, MAUVE -> execution correctness, base -> instruct/code.

followup_openings.defect: Dream-Coder advertises 'flexible quality-speed trade-offs through adjustable inference steps' as an architectural advantage, but never reports a step/NFE protocol table, never reports tokens-per-step or wall clock, and ships a schedule whose upper half is provably no-op. The model card's own headline advantage is unfalsifiable as stated and false at the top of the range.
followup_openings.our_fix: Publish the missing protocol table for the released checkpoint: for each steps in {16..1024} at canvas 512, report simulated commits/step, count of zero-commit steps, max commit/step, measured pass@1+ on HE+/MBPP+, wall clock, and forwarded token-positions. Ship the one-line --canvas flag that decouples canvas from steps (currently every launch script sets max_new_tokens == steps, which is exactly why nobody has run the grid) and release the simulator so any dLLM's schedule can be audited before its curve is trusted.
followup_openings.target_paper: Dream-Coder 7B (arXiv:2509.01142) and Dream 7B (arXiv:2508.15487)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A reusable schedule-audit artifact plus a corrected protocol table for a widely used open checkpoint is a concrete community deliverable, and it makes the paper a resource rather than only a complaint.

followup_openings.defect: Both report enormous speedups (61.4x, 27.6x) against the vanilla dLLM baseline. That baseline is the un-cached, steps=length, ~1-token-per-step configuration -- i.e. the zero-parallelism corner. Neither paper states that its reference point is effectively an AR decode, so the speedup multiplier is inflated by an amount neither quantifies, and neither reports an AR+KV-cache model at equal output length as the ceiling.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-express a representative subset of these speedups against two additional denominators: (i) the same dLLM at its best FORWARDED-TOKEN-POSITION setting rather than at steps=canvas, and (ii) an AR code model with KV cache at equal output length. Report how much of the headline multiplier survives. Our nfe512-vs-nfe1024 fixed point already shows that ~2.14x of any such multiplier can be harvested by deleting no-op steps alone, with byte-identical output -- a free 2x that requires no method at all.
followup_openings.target_paper: DPad (arXiv:2508.14148) and Fast-dLLM (arXiv:2505.22618)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It gives the paper a constructive, quantitative punchline ('X of the published speedup is schedule slack, not method') instead of a purely negative one, and it is cheap: it reuses runs we already have.

followup_openings.defect: All four are concurrent (2026-05-10 or later) and all four measure or theorise realised commit order, but every one of them is on reasoning/likelihood surfaces (GSM8K, MATH-500, C4, OpenWebText) or on block-diffusion models, and every one converts the observation into a SAMPLER. None asks whether the accounting of the existing published curve is valid, and none touches the steps>canvas arithmetic.
followup_openings.our_fix: Cede the order-measurement ground explicitly (cite all four as concurrent, do not claim the AR-collapse finding as ours) and stake the claim entirely on the accounting: the dominated region of the schedule, forwarded token-positions as the unit, the byte-identical fixed point, the canvas x steps grid, and the EvalPlus code surface none of them evaluates. Use their order results as the mechanism we do not have to re-derive.
followup_openings.target_paper: Concurrent order-instrumentation cluster: 2608.05687 (Answer First Reason Later / ARR Aug 2026), 2606.00997 (LLaDA-2.1 reveal order), 2605.09303 (order collapse theory), 2607.24306 (PARD)
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Concurrency protects priority but not attention: if the paper's headline is 'dLLMs decode left-to-right', four concurrent papers make it look crowded. Re-centering on 'the curve has a computable no-op region and the cost unit hides it' makes the contribution structurally distinct from all of them.

related_work.citation: Gong et al., "DiffuCoder: Understanding and Improving Masked Diffusion Models for Code Generation", arXiv:2506.20639
related_work.known_defects: AR-ness is reported at a single (temperature, steps) point per model, so the temperature claim ('higher T = more parallel') is confounded with output quality -- the higher-T samples are also worse, and pass@1 vs pass@10 is used to paper over this. Figures 3/1 give AR-ness@k curves without CIs or n. The 'less performance drop at half the steps' claim (Fig 1c / App C.3) is a two-point comparison with no compute accounting and no statistical test. No AR baseline is priced against the dLLM at equal output length anywhere in the paper.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- verified on OpenReview api2 (venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', invitations include Camera_Ready_Revision). Also indexed as CoRR 2025 by DBLP.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata (published 2025-06-25); full PDF downloaded and text-extracted (27 pages) -- quoted section 4 / App A.2 verbatim; OpenReview api2 /notes/search confirmed ICLR.cc/2026/Conference + 'ICLR 2026 Poster' + Camera_Ready_Revision invitation.
related_work.what_it_covers: THE closest prior art for our leg (2). Introduces local/global AR-ness metrics that quantify exactly what we propose to measure: local AR-ness@k = fraction of steps where the newly unmasked token continues a strictly increasing consecutive run (k=1 is next-token); global AR-ness@k = fraction of steps unmasking one of the earliest k masked positions. Measured on Dream-7B and DiffuCoder for code (HumanEval) and math (GSM8K) at sequence length = diffusion timesteps = 512. Crucially, it states in plain text (section 4, and again in App. A.2): 'Another common practice among dLLMs is to set the number of diffusion timesteps equal to the sequence length, effectively resorting to token-by-token generation to enhance performance' -- i.e. the steps=length -> one-token-per-step -> AR fact is already published, in the same model family, on a code benchmark, 14 months before our cutoff. Also shows AR-ness declines with temperature (0.2->1.2) and after coupled-GRPO, and that the RL'd model degrades less when decoding in half the steps.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: (a) It never prices anything: no wall clock, no forwarded-token-positions, no cost-per-quality curve, no AR reference at equal output length. AR-ness is a descriptive statistic, not a cost-validity argument. (b) It never treats steps>canvas: no simulation or measurement of the linear-schedule int(nmask*(1-s/t)) rule, hence no no-op-step accounting and no exact-fixed-point demonstration. (c) It reports only steps=512 (one operating point) -- no NFE-indexed quality curve, so it cannot say the reported optimum IS the zero-parallelism corner. (d) Its code numbers are HumanEval base, not EvalPlus HumanEval+/MBPP+. (e) Canvas length and step count are never decoupled. (f) Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct (the released code-specialised checkpoint we use) is not evaluated; DiffuCoder is a different model.

related_work.citation: Kang, Galim, Oh et al., "ParallelBench: Understanding the Trade-offs of Parallel Decoding in Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2510.04767
related_work.known_defects: The headline analysis is on synthetic list operations (Copy/Reverse/Sort/Shuffle) whose token-dependency structure is chosen to be adversarial; generalisation to real code is asserted, not shown. App F.3 itself concedes that on real benchmarks 'model capacity remains a dominant factor that cannot be separated from the analysis' -- i.e. their real-benchmark leg is confounded and underpowered, which is exactly the leg we can do properly with a hard fixed point and a byte-identity argument. Wall-clock is a single A100, batch size 1, appendix-only. No AR+KV-cache reference at equal output length in the speed-quality figures.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- verified on OpenReview api2 (venueid=ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', Submission4642, Camera_Ready_Revision present). PDF header reads 'Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2026'.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (published 2025-10-06); full 39-page PDF downloaded and text-extracted, App F.3/F.4 read verbatim; OpenReview api2 confirmed ICLR 2026 Poster + Camera_Ready_Revision.
related_work.what_it_covers: Information-theoretic analysis plus a synthetic benchmark showing parallel decoding damages quality when token dependencies are strong. Critically for us, it ALREADY indexes quality on '# Tokens per Step' rather than steps -- the x-axis appears 198 times in the PDF -- and App F.3 runs exactly the re-indexing we propose on existing benchmarks: GSM8K/IFEval/MATH with LLaDA 1.5 at varying tokens-per-step, plus App F.4 wall-clock time-quality curves on an A100. It also includes a Left-to-Right Top-k unmasking arm and an oracle upper bound, and observes that all unmasking methods 'perform comparably when unmasking a single token per step'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Its F.3 conclusion is the opposite framing from ours: it says existing benchmarks show only 'slight accuracy degradation as parallelism increases' and are therefore uninformative, and it draws the lesson 'we need a new benchmark', not 'the published reference point is the zero-parallelism corner and NFE is an invalid cost unit'. It never (a) simulates or audits the linear timestep schedule, so no no-op-step arithmetic and no steps>canvas regime; (b) measures the realised commit order of the default sampler on a code benchmark (its L2R arm is an imposed sampler, not a measurement of what confidence/entropy decoding actually does); (c) evaluates Dream-Coder-Instruct or any EvalPlus (HumanEval+/MBPP+) metric -- HumanEval appears only as plain HumanEval, MBPP is absent; (d) decouples canvas length from step count in a grid; (e) prices forwarded token-positions (prompt+canvas re-attended per step) as opposed to steps/latency.

related_work.citation: "CaRE: Compute-aware Remasking Evaluation Protocol for Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2607.24763
related_work.known_defects: MAUVE on OpenWebText is a distributional-similarity proxy, not a task-correctness measure, so 'rankings reverse' is a claim about a metric known to be sensitive to length and decoding temperature -- precisely the confound the paper is diagnosing elsewhere. 'Actual NFE' still counts forward passes, not forwarded token-positions, so a long-canvas run and a short-canvas run at the same NFE are not compute-matched in FLOPs. Base models only (no instruct/code checkpoints). No venue.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-06-04, 'updated version' comment). OpenReview api2 search returned no venue record for this title; nearest hits were a different paper (2606.12232). No venue claim verified.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata for 2607.24763 (published 2026-06-04, i.e. AFTER the 2026-05-07 cutoff -- the candidate's builds_on field asserts 'NOT concurrent', which is WRONG); abstract read in full. OpenReview api2 /notes/search found no venue record.
related_work.what_it_covers: Audits 7 remasking strategies on LLaDA-8B-Base and Dream-7B-Base by standardizing ACTUAL NFE (not nominal step count), enforcing multi-metric reporting and controlling stochasticity; reports that compute-matched comparisons reverse several published strategy rankings and that temperature explains most MAUVE variance. This is the single closest work to our cost-unit thesis.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Evaluates OpenWebText/LM1B with MAUVE, not executable code; never shows the full-NFE reference point IS the zero-parallelism/AR corner; never shows steps>canvas is literally no-op; no realised-commit-order measurement; no canvas x steps grid; no AR+KV-cache reference. It fixes the comparison PROTOCOL between diffusion samplers; it does not invalidate NFE as a cross-family cost unit.

related_work.citation: (DUS) "Plan for Speed: Dilated Scheduling for Masked Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2506.19037
related_work.known_defects: The AR-collapse premise in its abstract is asserted-and-cited (to Gong et al. 2025 and Horvitz et al. 2025), never measured by them: they report only average pairwise token spacing per planner (App B.7), no consecutive-commit rate, no Pearson, no per-step commit histogram. Speedups are quoted against 'token-by-token MDLM decoding', i.e. they adopt the zero-parallelism corner as the quality anchor without problematising it. No steps>canvas arithmetic, no canvas x steps grid, no EvalPlus+ metrics, no AR+KV-cache reference at equal output length.
related_work.venue_status: ICML 2026 -- verified on OpenReview api2 (venueid=ICML.cc/2026/Conference, venue='ICML 2026 regular'). Note it also appears as an ICLR 2026 Rejected_Submission on OpenReview, and DBLP lists it as CoRR 2025.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (published 2025-06-23, v5 2026-05-25); full 24-page PDF downloaded and text-extracted (abstract, related work, App B.7 read verbatim); OpenReview api2 confirmed ICML.cc/2026/Conference 'ICML 2026 regular' and the earlier ICLR 2026 rejection.
related_work.what_it_covers: Its ABSTRACT states the AR-collapse premise as established background: 'existing samplers, which pick tokens to unmask based on model confidence, ignore interactions when unmasking multiple positions in parallel and effectively reduce to slow, autoregressive behavior.' In related work it attributes the empirical observation to Gong et al. 2025 (DiffuCoder) and Horvitz et al. 2025. Proposes a dilated scheduler; reports up to 5.8x wall-clock speedup over token-by-token MDLM decoding on HumanEval/MBPP/GSM8K/MATH500/BBH/MMLU-Pro; App B.7 measures average pairwise token distance per planner from generation traces.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Because the AR-collapse is background rather than result, DUS establishes that our leg (2) is considered COMMON KNOWLEDGE in the community -- which is the single most important positioning fact for this candidate. It leaves open the entire accounting layer: no schedule audit, no dominated region, no cost unit proposal, no canvas dimension, no EvalPlus code grading.

related_work.citation: "Rethinking the Generation Order of Block Diffusion Language Models" (PARD), arXiv:2607.24306
related_work.known_defects: Scoped to block diffusion LMs, so the 'L2R-aligned' analysis does not transfer to full-canvas masked models like Dream/LLaDA without argument. Speedups are 'over pure AR decoding with only a small quality gap' -- the gap is not bounded or tested statistically in the abstract. Method paper: no evaluation-validity audit, no cost-unit analysis, no schedule arithmetic, and (like the rest of the cluster) no forwarded-token-position accounting.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-07-27, comment '20 pages, 15 figures, 6 tables'). OpenReview api2 search returned no matching venue record.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + abstract (published 2026-07-27, therefore concurrent). OpenReview api2: no venue record found.
related_work.what_it_covers: Shows empirically AND analytically that block diffusion LMs are naturally more aligned with left-to-right decoding than earlier MDMs; proposes PARD, a training-free sampler preserving L2R unmasking while allowing parallel token commitment.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent and method-shaped, so it does not preempt an evaluation-validity claim. Leaves open the full-canvas masked family, the no-op-step region, and any cost accounting on code benchmarks.

related_work.citation: "Answer First, Reason Later: Commitment Order in Diffusion LLMs", arXiv:2608.05687
related_work.known_defects: Reasoning surfaces only (GSM8K, MATH-500) -- no executable-code benchmark and no EvalPlus grading. It frames the commitment-order finding as a reasoning-failure mechanism and immediately converts it into an intervention (frontier-gated commitment), so it never audits whether the published step-indexed quality curve is validly priced. No schedule arithmetic (no zero-commit-step accounting, no steps>canvas fixed point), no canvas x steps grid, no AR+KV-cache reference at equal output length. Its 'optimal window flips from w=1 at full refinement' result is our phenomenon viewed as a tunable knob rather than as an accounting error, so the two papers can co-exist but the framing overlap must be stated explicitly.
related_work.venue_status: Under review -- OpenReview api2 shows an ACL ARR 2026 August Submission titled 'Premature Commitment in Diffusion Language Models' (venueid=aclweb.org/ACL/ARR/2026/August/Submission, Preprint_Post_Submission invitation), almost certainly the same work under an earlier title. Not a published venue.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + abstract (published 2026-08-06 -- one day before today, clearly concurrent); OpenReview api2 /notes/search found the ARR 2026 August submission record.
related_work.what_it_covers: Logs EVERY token commitment during LLaDA-8B decoding on GSM8K (replicated on Dream-7B / MATH-500) -- the same instrumentation as our leg (2). Reports where in the trajectory the answer is committed (15-24%), collapse to answer-only on up to 90% of problems as canvas grows, a 2x2 prompt x decoder design with a +34.8pp interaction (95% CI [26.8, 42.8]), and a frontier-gated commitment intervention recovering 0.528 -> 0.852 while preserving up to 4x parallel decoding.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The strongest reason to abandon leg (2) as a contribution and re-centre on the accounting layer: a concurrent paper has already done trajectory-level commitment logging with proper statistics. It leaves open code/EvalPlus surfaces, schedule arithmetic, and the cost-unit claim entirely.

related_work.citation: "Decoding in Order-Agnostic Language Models: Chain-Rule Deviation and Uniform Spreading", arXiv:2606.00997
related_work.known_defects: Single model family (LLaDA-2.1) so the 0.49 nats/token order-sensitivity number has unknown generality; C4 + four downstream benchmarks, no code execution; the uniform-spreading theorem's link to downstream correctness is 'consistently associated', i.e. correlational, not causal. No compute accounting of any kind, no no-op-step arithmetic, no canvas dimension.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-05-31). No venue record found on OpenReview api2.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + abstract. OpenReview api2: no venue record.
related_work.what_it_covers: On LLaDA-2.1: reports that confidence-first decoding, though nominally order-agnostic, produces reveal orders 'close to left-to-right on content tokens'; that reveal order shifts target log-likelihood by up to 0.49 nats/token so likelihood mixes content difficulty with path artifacts; proposes Var(log q_t) as a decoding-path diagnostic.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Another concurrent confirmation that near-L2R reveal order is a measured, known property -- further evidence leg (2) is not a contribution. Leaves open code surfaces, cost units, and schedule auditing.

related_work.citation: "Path-Dependent Denoising: A Non-Conservative Field Perspective on Order Collapse in Diffusion Language Models", arXiv:2605.09303
related_work.known_defects: Theory and diagnostics only -- the abstract reports no model-scale experiments, no benchmark quality numbers, and no compute curves, so the framework is untested against any published NFE curve. No code tasks, no schedule arithmetic, no canvas dimension.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint (arXiv v1 2026-05-10, three days after the cutoff -> concurrent). No venue record found.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + abstract.
related_work.what_it_covers: Formalizes why fast dLLM decoding 'drifts toward autoregressive-like trajectories' via order-induced pseudo-joints and a local denoising circulation quantity; separates incompatibility-driven path dependence from conditional-dependence error in parallel updates; offers inference-only diagnostics for when decoding is genuinely order-free.

related_work.citation: "No Compute Left Behind: Rethinking Reasoning and Sampling with Masked Diffusion Models", arXiv:2510.19990
related_work.known_defects: Rejected at ICLR 2026 (OpenReview Rejected_Submission), so the claims have not passed review. It poses the 'why pay for all-position compute when L2R one-token-at-a-time is on par' question rhetorically and answers with new methods (reasoning-as-infilling, MED) rather than a quantified cost-unit audit. No no-op-step arithmetic, no canvas x steps grid, no EvalPlus code numbers, no realised-order instrumentation, no wall-clock or forwarded-token-position accounting.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint / rejected. OpenReview api2: ICLR.cc/2026/Conference/Rejected_Submission under the title 'Rethinking reasoning with Masked Diffusion Models'; also a Public_Article CoRR 2025 record.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API metadata + abstract; OpenReview api2 confirmed the ICLR 2026 Rejected_Submission record.

related_work.citation: "DPad: Efficient Diffusion Language Models with Suffix Dropout", arXiv:2508.14148

IMPORTANT for us: DPad is also a THREAT to our kill_criterion -- by showing distant suffix tokens can be dropped nearly free, it is prima facie evidence the long canvas carries little information, so our canvas x steps grid will likely pass the kill test but the empirical finding 'short canvas is fine' is partly pre-empted; the novelty must therefore sit in the accounting, not in the canvas result.

diff.sharpened_claim: The released Dream-Coder-7B unmasking schedule contains a computable dominated region that every published step-indexed quality curve for this family reports through. Simulating the shipped rule (timesteps = linspace(1, eps, steps+1); commits = int(n_mask * (1 - s/t))) at canvas 512 shows that from steps = canvas onward the schedule commits at most one token per non-flush step, and at steps = 2 x canvas it emits 514 of 1024 forward passes that commit literally zero tokens. The consequence is measurable and not merely asymptotic: nfe512 -> nfe1024 is a fixed point, not a saturation -- identical EvalPlus HumanEval+ pass@1 (.707/.707; base .762) and identical per-task outcomes on 164/164 HE+ and 378/378 MBPP+, with 150/164 and 335/378 solutions byte-identical, purchased at 2.14x wall clock (11.31 -> 24.23 s/task HE+). We therefore argue that steps and NFE are invalid cost units for this family and propose forwarded token-positions, steps x (prompt + canvas), demonstrating with a canvas x steps grid on HumanEval+ (n=164) that two settings matched on NFE can differ ~3x in FLOPs while two settings matched on tokens-per-step but differing in canvas can be quality-equivalent -- so the axis that governs quality is tokens-per-step, and the axis that governs cost is canvas x steps, and the literature's single 'steps' knob conflates them. We deliberately do NOT claim the AR-collapse finding: that the reported optimum sits at ~1 token/step under a near-left-to-right order is already established by DiffuCoder (2025-06, ICLR 2026) via its local/global AR-ness metrics, treated as background in DUS's abstract, re-indexed on real benchmarks by ParallelBench App F.3, and re-measured concurrently on reasoning tasks by 2608.05687 and 2606.00997; we cite all of these and take the collapse as given. Our contribution is the accounting layer nobody supplied on top of it: the schedule audit and its no-op region, the byte-identical fixed point that is immune to the model-capacity confound ParallelBench concedes vitiates its own real-benchmark leg, forwarded token-positions as a refinement of CaRE's concurrent actual-NFE standardization moved from OpenWebText MAUVE onto executable code with an official grader, a corrected protocol table for a widely used open checkpoint, the one-line --canvas flag that makes the grid runnable at all, and a released schedule simulator that lets any dLLM's step-indexed curve be checked for dominated regions before it is believed.
