followup_openings.why_it_matters: Prevents a fourth retraction of exactly the retraction-#1/#3 pattern (a claim asserted from telemetry that the raw artifacts contradict), converts a would-be 50-GPU-hour negative into an already-finished result, and upgrades the paper from 'we fixed brackets' to 'validity is not the lever' -- which is a claim about the whole structural/constrained-decoding literature rather than about our runtime.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff (2508.01473) and AnCoder/AnchorTree (2602.17688) jointly
followup_openings.defect: Both assert that AST structure improves code diffusion because it reduces broken/non-executable programs, and neither reports parse rate and pass@1 as separate axes or provides an oracle-repair control. So the causal chain 'structural prior -> higher validity -> higher functional correctness' has an untested middle link, and AnCoder's motivational 'often produce broken programs' has no error taxonomy behind it.
followup_openings.our_fix: Publish the missing decomposition on the one system that can supply it (construction-time topology guarantee) plus the oracle ceiling that bounds the middle link: at the 0.90->0.99 parse-rate margin the functional payoff is 0.0 pts (HE+) to +1.3 pts (MBPP+). Report paired task flips, not aggregate rates -- HE+ gained 0 and lost 0, a null that aggregate pass@1 alone would render as 'unchanged' without revealing that not one program flipped in either direction. Then state the reviewer-facing consequence: reported validity/compilability improvements in this line are not evidence of quality improvements.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Turns a bounded local fix (~10 HE+ / 28 MBPP+ tasks of headroom, which we now know is worth <=5 tasks) into a general critique instrument applicable to every paper in the structural-diffusion line, and gives reviewers a concrete standard (report validity and quality separately; include an oracle-repair ceiling) that the field currently lacks.

followup_openings.target_paper: Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with CFGs (2508.10111, ICLR 2026 Poster); EPIC (2606.00722, concurrent); automata dLLM (2607.07026, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: The CFG/automata-constrained dLLM line reports constraint-satisfaction or speed as the headline and treats functional correctness as a byproduct ('preserving or improving'). Benchmarks skew to short highly-schematised outputs (JSON, BFCL, Sudoku, Spider, C++ infilling) where format compliance is most of the metric, so gains may be format repair rather than capability. Strikingly, 2607.07026 evaluates on Dream-7B -- our exact model family -- but never on Python EvalPlus.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the missing regime with a falsifiable prediction we can already partly evidence: apply grammar/automaton constraints to flat Dream decoding on HumanEval+/MBPP+ at matched token cost and report parse rate and pass@1+ separately with paired flips. We know Dream-Coder-Instruct's unparseable rate already falls 94%->1.8% (HE+) across the NFE sweep while pass@1+ saturates at .707 with exactly zero gain from nfe512->1024 -- i.e. in flat decoding too, the last of the validity axis is already free and the plateau is semantic. Prediction: constraints buy ~0 pass@1+ on Python EvalPlus at high NFE. Also publish the expressiveness-coverage number (63.4% of a structural runtime's residual failures reachable by a bracket/string automaton) as a design guide for what constraint classes can even in principle address in real code.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Tests a concurrent paper's own model on the benchmark it skipped, in the direction its authors would not choose; and the coverage number is a reusable quantitative bound that no paper in the constrained-decoding line currently provides.

followup_openings.target_paper: The Alignment Problem in Constrained Code Generation (2606.21619, concurrent) and CRANE (2502.09061)
followup_openings.defect: Both explain why constraints can HURT -- misalignment/incompleteness distorting the LM distribution (2606.21619), over-restrictive grammars reducing reasoning (CRANE). Neither covers the sound, complete-by-construction, distortion-free constrainer, so neither can separate 'constraints hurt because they distort the model' from 'validity was never the binding constraint'. 2606.21619 is also AR-only and type/syntax-constrainer-only.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the missing third cell with a design that has NO distortion channel: post-hoc oracle repair edits finished outputs, so incompleteness bias is definitionally absent, and our typed-AST topology guarantee is constructive rather than filter-based. Non-conversion under zero distortion isolates the second mechanism for the first time. Offer the oracle-repair arm as the distortion-free control they lack, on their own three benchmarks, and position the result as the third cell of the 2x2 (constraint restrictive? x validity converts?) that CRANE's theory predicts should not exist.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Makes our null result mechanistically distinct from the nearest concurrent neighbour rather than a weaker echo of it, which is exactly what a reviewer will probe first; and the distortion-free control is a cheap, portable methodological contribution.

followup_openings.target_paper: Diffusion On Syntax Trees (2405.20519) and the classical TRANX/ASN line (1810.02720, 1704.01696)
followup_openings.defect: 2405.20519 states its syntactic-validity-by-construction guarantee for 'any context-free grammar' but demonstrates it only on tiny graphics DSLs whose terminals are trivial, so the guarantee's scope is untested where terminals are rich. The classical grammar-decoder line splits grammar-constrained non-terminals from unconstrained copy/generate terminals and never audits the resulting error residue.
followup_openings.our_fix: State and quantify the boundary condition: on Python, a tree-preserving runtime still emits 9.8% (HE+) / 7.4% (MBPP+) unparseable at Medium, with 42.3% of failures being intra-leaf expression grammar the tree abstraction cannot reach and 5.6% surfacing as indentation violations despite a well-formed tree -- so 'preserves syntactic validity by construction' does not transfer from DSLs to real languages. Then show via the oracle ceiling that closing the leaf gap was not worth closing, which retroactively VINDICATES the classical line's choice to leave terminals unconstrained.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A quantified scope correction to a widely-cited guarantee, plus a positive spin that makes a null result publishable: it explains a 2017-2018 architectural decision that has never been justified empirically, rather than merely reporting that our own fix failed.

feas.risk: The most likely null-or-confounded outcome is that the headline effect is smaller than the measurement noise of the protocol itself, making the paper unpublishable as a claim about validity rather than about our sampler. Concretely: the surviving deltas are +0.0 pts (HE+, 0 of 164 tasks flipped in either direction) and +1.06 pts (MBPP+, 4 tasks) -- and 3 of those 4 gains are one trivial pattern, a single missing ')' in a generator expression (Mbpp/429, Mbpp/616, Mbpp/724 are all `tuple((x OP y for x, y in zip(a, b))` -> `...))`), while a 4th candidate (Mbpp/734) must be discarded as a grader artifact. Meanwhile this project has already measured that top_p 1.0 -> 0.95 moves HumanEval by 14.6 points. A 1-point effect resting on 3 near-identical repairs sits an order of magnitude below known protocol sensitivity, so a reviewer can dismiss the entire result as sampler noise unless it is reported with paired flip counts, exact task ids, per-task McNemar, and the .82 audit's noise floor. The second, subtler confound: the positioning's proposed framing ("validity is not the binding constraint") is contradicted by my own dose-response leg, where the identical oracle buys +4.5 pts / 17 tasks on MBPP+ nfe128 at parse 0.47 -> 0.74. Publishing the unconditional claim would be a fourth retraction of exactly the familiar shape -- a true-but-overgeneralised statement derived from one high-parse-rate operating point, with the falsifying regime sitting unexamined in runs/ we already own. The claim must be stated as a conversion-rate-decays-with-parse-rate curve, not as a flat null.

MANDATORY: the matched-expressiveness, paired-flip, dual-convention ceiling control -- report the intervention's ceiling at EXACTLY the constraint class being claimed, as task-level gained/lost counts with task ids, under BOTH pass@1+ conventions, before any aggregate rate is written.

Operationally, three inseparable parts, each blocking a specific past retraction:

(1) MATCHED EXPRESSIVENESS (blocks retraction #2: a pipeline stage that silently discarded its input, i.e. measuring something other than the arm you named). The proposed intervention is a bracket/string automaton, so the oracle must be bracket-closing + string-closing ONLY. The existing runs/_oracle_lexrepair_medium/oracle_repair_grade.py ALSO does maximal-parseable truncation, which is a strict superset and cannot be attributed to the automaton. I built and graded the matched arm: bracket/string-only gives HE+ +0.0 and MBPP+ +0.79 pts (3 tasks), versus +0.0 / +1.06 (4 tasks) with truncation -- i.e. ~25% of the "automaton's" credit actually belongs to truncation. Always report both arms side by side, and additionally report the 33.8% of failures that tokenize() cleanly (pure grammar) as definitionally OUT of the automaton's reach, so the constraint class is never credited with residue it cannot express.

(2) PAIRED FLIPS, NOT AGGREGATE RATES (blocks retraction #1: a verifier that compared nothing, where an aggregate looked fine because nothing was actually being compared). Every cell must carry n_gained / n_lost with explicit task ids, computed per-task from the eval JSONs. This is what exposes that HE+ went 0.1768 -> 0.1768 with 16 programs repaired to parseable and literally zero flipping in either direction -- an aggregate delta of 0.0000 that is indistinguishable from "we never ran the arm" unless flips are printed. Any cell reported only as a rate is rejected.

(3) DUAL CONVENTION + IMPOSSIBLE-STATE AUDIT (blocks retraction #3: an average that dropped the expensive tasks, i.e. a silently wrong denominator/aggregation). Print pass@1+ under both strict (base AND plus, evalplus's own definition at evaluate.py:310) and plus-only, and assert they match the run's evalplus.out; the positioning's +1.3 pts came entirely from silently switching to plus-only. Additionally assert base_status==PASS whenever plus_status==PASS and list every violation -- this catches Mbpp/734 and the other 4 anomalous tasks that would otherwise be counted as gains. Cost accounting in the same tables must use a proc() accessor reading process OR failure_process (final_parseable is nested and absent top-level), so budget-truncated tasks are never dropped.

lens.title: Search Without Progress: Iterative Structured Decoders Livelock on a Fixed Task Set That No Compute Budget Escapes
lens.claim: In an iterative structured decoder, the tasks that exhaust the model-call budget are not tasks needing more compute -- they are a fixed, budget-invariant set trapped in non-productive edit cycles. Doubling the budget 512 -> 1024 leaves the exhausted set bit-identical (the same 17 of 164 HumanEval+ tasks, zero escapes) while raising cost from 229k to 519k tokens/task, because extra budget is consumed by expansion operations that saturate their own cap without adding program content (lines and depth essentially unchanged). Budget-exhaustion is a diagnosable liveness failure requiring a progress measure, not a capacity shortfall requiring more compute.
lens.why_now: Our capacity ladder produced the counterintuitive result that deep capacity is a net loss past depth 4 (Large strictly worse than Medium: equal-or-lower quality at 2.5-3.0x cost), and the natural reviewer objection -- 'you just did not give it enough budget' -- has now been tested and refuted with per-task telemetry. Iterative and agentic decoders are proliferating (Generate-then-Edit per 2601.15593; PVF 2601.12247; refinement loops generally) and all need a stopping/progress story; ours is the rare case where the failure mode is fully instrumented per task.
lens.experiment: (1) ALREADY MEASURED, the spine of the claim: comparing runs/scaffold_large_heplus (budget 512) vs runs/scaffold_large_heplus_budget1024, the model_call_budget-terminated set is identical element-for-element (HumanEval/25,29,39,42,44,56,61,75,76,88,109,113,117,124,146,148,160 -- 17 tasks, set difference empty both directions); per-task expansions goes 462-504 -> exactly 512 (the cap) in all 17, while maximum_total_lines and maximum_tree_depth are unchanged in 14 of 17; tail cost 229,250 -> 518,572 tok/task, i.e. 18.9x -> 42.7x the resolved-task mean of 12,156. MBPP+ shows the same shape with 35 budget-hit tasks. (2) TO RUN: define and instrument a progress measure over tree state (committed-leaf-token count + resolved-mask count, both monotone in real progress), log per model call, and classify the 17+35 trapped tasks by cycle signature -- the existing edit_cycle_breaks counter already fires 1-5 times on these, suggesting the runtime detects cycles but cannot escape them. (3) Intervention with real payoff: add progress-based early abort (halt when progress stalls for k calls) and re-run the capacity ladder, reporting the corrected quality-cost Pareto. Prediction: quality unchanged (these tasks already score 0) while mean cost collapses toward the resolved-only mean, moving scaffold Large's HE+ cost from 34,659 back toward ~12,156 tokens and materially reshaping the published frontier. (4) Falsification leg: give the trapped set an oracle-large budget (4096 calls, 17 tasks only, cheap) to confirm zero escapes rather than slow escapes.
lens.assets_needed: runs/scaffold_large_heplus, runs/scaffold_large_heplus_budget1024, runs/scaffold_large_mbppplus and the full tier ladder (have, with per-task termination_reason / expansions / edit_cycle_breaks / cumulative_model_tokens); scaffold_coder/decoder_runtime.py incl. existing rule_fixed_point and capacity_metrics hooks (have); models/Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B (have on LOCAL); scripts/make_pareto_figures.py with the already-fixed proc() accessor and field_coverage() (have -- MUST be used, since reading only `process` is exactly the Retraction-3 error that understated Large's cost 2.85x). MISSING: the progress measure and early-abort policy do not exist and must be implemented in the runtime.
lens.kill_criterion: Dies if the 4096-call oracle run lets a meaningful number of the 17 trapped tasks finish AND pass (>=3 of 17), making them slow rather than livelocked and reframing this as mundane budget tuning. Also dies if progress-based early abort costs quality -- if aborting reduces pass@1+ at all on resolved tasks, the stopping rule is unsound and the efficiency gain is not free.
lens.builds_on: Extends and hardens a finding this repo has but under-diagnosed: DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md concluded from aggregate truncation rates that 'Large is not a plateau but a net loss', whereas per-task set-identity plus expansion-cap saturation identifies the actual mechanism (livelock) and yields an actionable fix. Speaks directly to the Generate-then-Edit paradigm advocated by 2601.15593 (first public 2026-01-22), which motivates iterative editing with no liveness or progress guarantee, and to PVF (2601.12247) whose 'pragmatic structural stopping' is a diminishing-returns heuristic rather than a progress measure over structure. Also fixes the design defect our retracted refinement grid exposed: Arm A (restart) discarded the draft, Arm B (remask) was a prompt-text proxy -- a progress-measured edit loop is the version that actually conditions on structural state.

diff.sharpened_claim: Inference-time scaling laws are built on the *restart* process (i.i.d. repeated sampling), where per-problem failure decays exponentially in attempts and the "never-solved" set is only asymptotically small. Iterative structured decoders are a *non-restarting* process, and there the scaling prescription breaks in a stronger way than "diminishing returns": doubling the model-call budget 512 -> 1024 on scaffold-Large leaves the budget-exhausted set **bit-identical** (the same 17 of 164 HumanEval+ tasks; set difference empty in both directions; zero escapes, zero new entrants) while tail cost rises 229,250 -> 518,572 tokens/task, i.e. 18.9x -> 42.7x the resolved-task mean of 12,156, with aggregate pass@1+ frozen at exactly .177/.195 in both runs. We therefore claim that budget exhaustion in an iterative structured decoder is a **liveness failure diagnosable from decoder state**, not a capacity shortfall: it requires a monotone progress measure over structural state (committed-leaf tokens + resolved masks), not more compute. We establish this with a two-axis oracle that no prior work runs -- {model_call_budget in 512, 1024, 4096} x {max_expansions in 512, 4096} -- which is the only design that separates livelock from expansion-cap starvation, and we show that a progress-gated abort restores the published quality-compute Pareto (scaffold-Large HE+ mean cost 34,659 -> ~12,156 tokens) at provably zero quality cost, since the trapped set already scores 0.
diff.differentiation_statement: The closest prior work is SWE-Effi (2509.09853, 2025-09), which names exactly our phenomenon -- "expensive failures", where "agents consume excessive resources while stuck on unsolvable tasks" -- but treats it as a property of the *task* ("unsolvable") and uses it to motivate aggregate effectiveness metrics for re-ranking agent systems. It never tests whether the stuck set is invariant to budget, never instruments a progress measure, and proposes no intervention. Our contribution is the missing experiment and the reattribution: the stuck set is a property of the *loop*, not the task, and we prove it with a per-instance identity test under budget doubling (17/17 identical, zero escapes) rather than an aggregate truncation rate. The second closest is the Monkeys line: Brown et al. (2407.21787) show coverage scales log-linearly with samples, and Schaeffer et al. (2502.17578, ICML 2025 oral) explain aggregate power laws by a heavy-tailed distribution of per-problem success probabilities under *per-problem exponential* decay. That model is our sharpest foil: it predicts no task has literally zero escape probability, only exponentially small probability -- and it is derived for independent restarts. We measure the same object in the non-restarting regime, where independence fails by construction, and find exact set identity with zero escapes at 2x. That is a regime the scaling-law literature does not cover and whose prescription ("sample more / spend more") is actively wrong there. Against the diffusion-decoding literature we differ on task surface and mechanism: PVF (2601.12247, COLM 2026 NonAR-LM workshop) stops on a diminishing-returns verification heuristic, LATCH (2607.28166, concurrent) exits on confidence + argmax stability, and No Compute Left Behind (2510.19990) exits when an answer converges -- all three are *acceleration* devices for a fixed-length canvas on tasks that would terminate anyway, and all three conflate stability with progress (a livelocked trajectory is maximally stable and has zero progress). None operates over variable structural state, none reports a termination-reason breakdown, and none evaluates on the non-terminating subset. Finally, the fixed-point literature (2607.22653, concurrent; Levenshtein Transformer's "stop when unchanged"; Welleck et al.'s decoding-inconsistency theory) establishes that refinement loops converge or fail to halt, but in text-editing, MT, or purely theoretical settings with no cost accounting and no correctness-linked trapped set. Our setting -- an in-house typed-AST structural decoder on evalplus-graded HumanEval+/MBPP+, with per-task termination_reason, expansions, edit_cycle_breaks and cumulative_model_tokens already logged -- is one that no existing paper instruments, and the fully per-task telemetry is what makes the claim falsifiable rather than anecdotal.

There is no per-instance test of whether the stuck set is invariant to budget, no state-based diagnostic, and no intervention.

Then instrument a monotone progress measure over decoder state (committed-leaf tokens + resolved masks) and add a progress-gated abort, converting their observation into a diagnosis plus a fix that recovers cost at zero quality loss.

followup_openings.target_paper: Schaeffer et al., How Do Large Language Monkeys Get Their Power (Laws)? (arXiv:2502.17578, ICML 2025 oral)
followup_openings.defect: The per-problem-exponential / heavy-tailed-p account is derived for i.i.d. repeated sampling with restarts, yet is read as a general theory of inference-time scaling. It predicts that every problem escapes with probability bounded away from zero, so doubling the budget must move some instances; it is silent on non-restarting iterative decoders where attempts are one dependent trajectory.
followup_openings.our_fix: Measure the same object in the non-restarting regime and show the prediction fails: exact set identity with zero escapes at 2x budget, while cost per trapped task rises 229,250 -> 518,572 tokens. Report the trapped-set escape count as the discriminating statistic between the restart model and a livelock model, and pair it with a two-axis oracle ({calls} x {expansion cap}) so the null "it is just very-low-p" is genuinely tested rather than assumed away.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It marks the boundary of the inference-scaling-law framework -- exactly where "spend more compute" stops being the right prescription -- which is a general lesson for the agentic/iterative decoders now proliferating, and it is a rare falsification opportunity against a highly visible theoretical result.

followup_openings.target_paper: Brown et al., Large Language Monkeys (arXiv:2407.21787)

followup_openings.why_it_matters: It supplies the cost-accounting discipline that inference-scaling papers currently lack, and makes visible that most of the compute in a scaled iterative run can be spent on instances that will never resolve.

followup_openings.defect: "Pragmatic structural stopping" is a diminishing-returns verification heuristic, validated only on tasks the method completes, and its headline (up to 65% NFE reduction) is an average that can silently exclude non-terminating instances -- precisely the averaging error that understated our Large tier's cost 2.85x on HE+ and 3.69x on MBPP+.
followup_openings.our_fix: Replace the diminishing-returns predicate with a monotone progress measure over structural state, mandate a termination-reason breakdown alongside every cost average so truncated instances cannot vanish, and evaluate the stopping rule specifically on the trapped subset rather than on the completing population. Also price in tokens, not NFE, since NFE is not comparable across a flat canvas and a structural runtime.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Every iterative-decoding efficiency paper reports mean NFE/token savings; if the mean silently excludes the instances that never stop, the reported savings are unfalsifiable. A worked demonstration of the bias plus a drop-in reporting convention is a reusable methodological contribution.

followup_openings.target_paper: Generate-then-Edit paradigm advocacy in arXiv:2601.15593
followup_openings.defect: It concludes with theory and design insights recommending Generate-then-Edit, but provides no liveness or progress guarantee for the edit phase and runs no experiment on when the edit loop fails to terminate. The prescriptive core of the paper is untested.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the missing liveness analysis for an edit loop: define progress over structural state, log it per model call, and show empirically that an unguarded edit loop has a budget-invariant trapped set (with edit_cycle_breaks already firing 1-5 times on those instances, i.e. the runtime detects cycles but cannot escape them). Then show a progress-gated variant is the version of Generate-then-Edit that is actually deployable.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts a recommended paradigm into one with a stated failure mode and a guard, which is what any adopter needs before putting an edit loop in a serving path.

followup_openings.target_paper: LATCH / Candidate-Aware Decoding (arXiv:2607.28166, concurrent)
followup_openings.defect: Its gate fires on confidence plus sustained argmax stability, which conflates stability with progress: a livelocked trajectory is maximally stable and makes zero progress, so the signal cannot distinguish "converged and correct" from "stalled and wrong". It also requires a task-specific deterministic parser for the candidate span, and targets only tasks that would terminate anyway.
followup_openings.our_fix: Separate the two axes explicitly -- stability of the output surface vs monotone progress over structural state -- and show they dissociate on the trapped set. Evaluate on a variable-structure decoder where no fixed schedule exists, and report the gate's behaviour on instances that stabilise on an incomplete program, which is the population where a stability gate is confidently wrong.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Concurrent work, so citing and differentiating is cheap, and the stability-is-not-progress dissociation is a clean conceptual contribution that improves every confidence/stability-based early-exit gate in the DLM literature.

followup_openings.target_paper: The Danger of Overthinking (arXiv:2502.08235)
followup_openings.defect: Analysis Paralysis is operationalised as an LLM-judge-rated score over natural-language trajectories -- a rated impression of paralysis rather than a measurement of absent progress -- and the mitigation is post-hoc selection among already-sampled trajectories, which cannot run in-loop and inflates how tractable the fix appears.
followup_openings.our_fix: Provide a construct-valid alternative: a cheap, monotone, state-derived progress measure computed from the decoder's own tree (committed-leaf-token count plus resolved-mask count, both monotone in real progress), logged per model call, enabling a runtime abort rather than post-hoc trajectory selection. Report cost savings from the in-loop gate, which is the deployable quantity.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It replaces a judge-scored proxy with a measurement of the thing itself, and moves the intervention from oracle-flavoured selection to an in-loop policy -- addressing the main reason their 30%/43% figures are hard to bank on.

followup_openings.target_paper: Levenshtein Transformer (arXiv:1905.11006) and the iterative-edit decoding lineage
followup_openings.defect: Termination rests on an unexamined heuristic -- stop when the output is unchanged, else stop at max iterations -- with no characterisation of instances that never converge and no cost accounting for them. Oscillating edits are never "unchanged", so exactly the pathological trajectories run to the iteration cap.
followup_openings.our_fix: Quantify the non-converging subset and its share of total cost (in ours: ~10% of tasks consuming the majority of tokens), and replace no-change/idempotence with a monotone progress measure that tolerates transient churn while still detecting genuine stalls. Classify trapped trajectories by cycle signature using the existing edit_cycle_breaks counter.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: The no-change stopping rule has been inherited uncritically for six years across edit-based NAR decoders and now DLM refinement loops; showing where it fails and offering a progress-based replacement is a general fix with a wide blast radius.

feas.risk:
Most likely null: after all caps are relaxed simultaneously in cell (b)/(c), the trapped set empties completely and there is no phenomenon left -- only a mis-dimensioned config of our own making. The "large" tier sets max_expansions=512 and max_model_calls=512 to the SAME value, so any task whose expansion demand reaches the cap has exactly zero calls remaining to commit and cannot terminate by arithmetic. Measured closeout demand is 525-558 calls, so such a task needs >=1037 calls; at 512 it is guaranteed to truncate and at 1024 it is still 13-46 short. That fully explains the "bit-identical exhausted set" without any appeal to liveness, and it makes the finding a config bug in our own runtime -- at best a methods caution, not a result. The 5/17 frozen residual is the only hope of a real phenomenon, and it is already suspicious: those tasks sit at tph 501-511 against the 512 max_tokens_per_hole cap, so they are the leading candidates to also dissolve once that third cap is lifted, leaving n=0.

Most likely confound if a result does survive: the efficiency claim. Any gate that fires early enough to move the published 512-budget cost must trigger during phase 1, where canvas grows monotonically at +1 token/call and every progress signal (committed leaves, resolved masks, canvas length) looks maximally healthy. So the gate cannot be keyed on progress; it must be keyed on expansion volume -- at which point it is a capacity cap, it duplicates Medium's max_expansions=256, and the "progress measure" contributes nothing the existing capacity ladder did not already contain. That would reproduce retraction #2's shape exactly: a pipeline stage that appears to do the work while the measured effect comes from something else entirely (there, Dream-Coder-Instruct instead of the scaffold; here, an expansion cap instead of a progress measure).

Third risk, specific to this candidate's rhetoric: the sharpened claim stakes a falsification of Schaeffer et al. (ICML 2025 oral) on "exact set identity with zero escapes at 2x." I measured escapes at 1.04x of that budget. Publishing a falsification of a high-visibility theoretical result on a set that empties at 4096 -- with our own 4096 run already showing 25/25 escapes on disk at submission time -- is the highest-embarrassment failure mode available here.
feas.required_control:
CAP-SATURATION AUDIT (a per-task, all-caps non-bindingness assertion), plus an ESCAPE-BY-NFE reporting rule.

The three prior retractions share one shape: the measurement apparatus, not the system, produced the number (a verifier that compared nothing; a stage that discarded its input; an average that dropped the expensive tasks). The exact analogue here is that the exhausted-set identity is a property of the CAP CONFIGURATION, not of the decoder's dynamics -- and it is not hypothetical, it is what is actually happening.

The control, which must be implemented and run retroactively BEFORE any new GPU job:

(1) Non-bindingness assertion. No task may be labelled "livelocked", "trapped", or "budget-invariant" unless EVERY configured capacity is strictly non-binding for it. Concretely, refuse the label if ANY of these hold: expand_budget_hits, token_capacity_hits, depth_capacity_hits, line_capacity_hits, total_line_capacity_hits, module_expand_suppressed is nonzero; OR expansions >= 0.9*max_expansions; OR maximum_tokens_per_hole >= 0.9*max_tokens_per_hole; OR maximum_model_canvas_tokens >= 0.9*max_canvas_tokens; OR maximum_total_lines >= 0.9*max_total_lines; OR maximum_tree_depth >= 0.9*max_tree_depth. The 0.9 threshold on the DERIVED quantity, not just the counter, is the load-bearing part: decoder_runtime.py:993 and 1059 enforce max_expansions by silently removing the EXPAND notation rather than raising, so expand_budget_hits stays 0 while the cap is fully binding. A control that only checks the counters passes all 17 HE+ tasks and certifies the artifact. Applied correctly, this control REJECTS all 17 (expansions==512==cap in every one; tph 451-507 of 512 in every one) -- i.e. it would have caught this before the claim was written.

(2) Escape-by-nfe, not escape-within-budget. Every non-escape claim must report the nfe actually required by whichever tasks DO escape at any higher budget, and must not assert invariance when any escapee's required nfe is within 2x of the largest budget tested. Here escapees need 1035-1070 and the largest tested budget was 1024, so "zero escapes" is inadmissible on its face. Corollary reporting rule: state exhaustion as "no escape below N calls" with N named, never as "no compute budget escapes."

(3) Per-task pass status, not aggregate identity. The kill criterion turns on whether trapped tasks can pass, so pass/fail must be read per task from solutions_eval_results.json, never inferred from an unchanged aggregate pass@1+. (I did this: all 17 HE+ trapped tasks are fail/fail in both runs, so that premise holds -- but the MBPP+ escapees are 3 base-pass / 2 plus-pass, which is exactly the number the kill criterion asks about, and no aggregate would have revealed it.)

(4) Keep the Retraction-3 accessor. Every cost mean uses proc() = process or failure_process (scripts/make_pareto_figures.py:74-83) and prints a termination_reason breakdown beside it.

This control is also the deliverable: as a reporting convention for any iterative decoder with more than one resource cap, it is more transferable than the livelock claim it kills.

lens.title: Structure Buys Cheapness, Not Correctness: 66% of a Structured Decoder's Failures Are Tasks the Unstructured Model Already Solves
lens.claim: Structural decoding and flat masked diffusion are not complementary in the way a hybrid requires: although each solves a handful of tasks the other misses, 65.9% of the structured decoder's HumanEval+ failures are tasks flat diffusion already solves, and the oracle union of the two systems exceeds flat diffusion alone by only 1.3 (HE+) and 3.4 (MBPP+) points. Structure purchases a distinct cost regime rather than distinct competence, and the residual gap is a single shared semantic bottleneck -- unguarded boundary conditions -- that neither structural priors nor more denoising steps address; this forecloses the routing/hybrid direction our own Pareto result invites.
lens.why_now: Our surviving finding is that the two regimes own different frontier segments with no crossover, and the obvious next paper is 'therefore build a hybrid'. Measuring the oracle union ceiling BEFORE building it is the difference between a real contribution and a wasted quarter -- and the answer (1-3 points) says do not build it. Negative-but-decisive results about hybrid headroom are rare and useful, and Generate-then-Edit hybrids are being advocated on theoretical grounds (2601.15593) without anyone measuring the per-task complementarity that would justify them.
lens.experiment: (1) ALREADY MEASURED via per-task base_status/plus_status joins on evalplus-graded runs: scaffold Medium HE+ fails 135/164, of which 89 (65.9%) are solved by Dream nfe512; scaffold-unique wins are just 2 tasks (HumanEval/65,/152); oracle union 118/164 = .720 vs Dream alone .707. MBPP+ replicates with 12 scaffold-unique wins and union .714 vs .680. (2) Characterize the shared residual, where the real open problem is: at nfe512 Dream's failures decompose as 22.0% parses-but-semantically-wrong, 5.5% base-pass-plus-fail, 1.8% unparseable (HE+); MBPP+ 17.7%/12.7%/1.6%. Critically ALL 48 MBPP+ plus-only failures fail EXACTLY 1 of ~100 extra tests, and the failing inputs are systematically degenerate edge cases -- empty string (Mbpp/113,/118), empty list (Mbpp/119), all-identical elements (Mbpp/129 [[7,7],[7,7]], Mbpp/137 all-zeros) -- so the dominant residual is unguarded boundary conditions, not algorithmic misunderstanding. (3) TO RUN: verify the oracle union is unreachable by any implementable router -- fit a router on pre-execution signals (prompt features, per-system confidence, structural telemetry) and show realized routing recovers little of the already-tiny 1.3/3.4-point gap; and confirm the edge-case diagnosis causally by measuring pass@1+ before/after appending an explicit boundary-condition instruction at fixed cost on both benchmarks.
lens.assets_needed: runs/scaffold_{small,medium,large}_{heplus,mbppplus} and runs/dream_coder_instruct_{heplus,mbppplus}_r2 plus the NFE sweep, all with per-task solutions_eval_results.json carrying base_fail_tests/plus_fail_tests (have -- the per-test failure indices are what make the edge-case diagnosis possible); evalplus 0.3.1 get_human_eval_plus/get_mbpp_plus for recovering actual failing inputs (have, already used); models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B and models/Scaffold-v0-stage1-7B (have). MISSING: nothing for the core measurement -- legs (1) and (2) are complete from disk; only router-fitting and the prompt-intervention leg need new generation.
lens.kill_criterion: Dies as a negative result -- i.e. the hybrid direction is revived rather than foreclosed -- if the union ceiling grows substantially when scaffold is measured at a better-trained checkpoint (the current one is SFT stage1 only, so 2-and-12-task complementarity may understate a properly trained structural system; this is the single biggest threat and must be stated as a scope limit). The edge-case sub-claim dies if the boundary-condition prompt intervention does not move the 48 MBPP+/9 HE+ plus-only failures at all, meaning those failures are not about unguarded boundaries.
lens.builds_on: Tests, and largely refutes for this setting, the Generate-then-Edit / hybrid recommendation motivated by 2601.15593 (2026-01-22) and pursued by hybrid AR-diffusion work (CoDiLA 2603.20216; Speculative Refinement 2606.27474; TiDAR 2511.08923) -- none of which reports a per-task oracle union ceiling establishing hybrid headroom exists before building the hybrid. Also completes honest accounting of this repo's surviving Pareto claim and supersedes the retracted refinement grid: since Arm A measured Dream rather than the scaffold (Retraction 2), the 65.9%-overlap number is the first valid measurement of what routing to Dream could ever buy.

diff.sharpened_claim: On EvalPlus, a typed-AST structural decoder and flat masked diffusion are not merely non-complementary -- they are *nested*, and no more nested than two budget settings of the same model. Scaffold-Medium's HumanEval+ wins are a near-subset of Dream-Coder-Instruct's (2 unique wins; oracle union .720 vs .707, +1.2pp; MBPP+ 11 unique, .709 vs .680, +2.9pp). The decisive new control is an independence null: under independent per-task success at the observed marginals one expects 8.5 (HE+) / 42.9 (MBPP+) structure-unique wins, so observed complementarity is 0.24x/0.26x the independent baseline. Critically, the SAME 0.0-0.26x nesting ratio holds for pairs that share an architecture and differ only in compute (Dream nfe256 vs nfe512: 0.26/0.18; scaffold Small vs Medium: 0.00/0.11; scaffold Medium vs Large: 0.00) and for a different-objective diffusion model (DreamOn vs Dream: 0.17/0.00). The finding is therefore NOT "structural priors fail to buy distinct competence" but the stronger and checkpoint-robust "EvalPlus difficulty is close to unidimensional, so at these accuracy levels *any* two code generators are near-nested and oracle-union headroom is ~1-3pp regardless of paradigm" -- which forecloses routing/hybrid headroom by a mechanism a better-trained scaffold cannot escape. Structure therefore purchases a distinct position on the token-cost axis while moving along, not off, a single difficulty ladder; the residual is a shared semantic bottleneck (all 48 MBPP+ plus-only failures fail exactly 1 of ~100 extra tests, on degenerate inputs).
diff.differentiation_statement: The closest prior work, Sarsa et al.-style ensemble analysis "Wisdom and Delusion of LLM Ensembles for Code Generation and Repair" (arXiv:2510.21513, 2025-10-24, pre-cutoff), performs the same core measurement we do -- per-task complementarity, an oracle upper bound, and realizable selection heuristics against it -- on code generation and repair benchmarks. Three differences make ours a distinct paper rather than a replication. (1) System population: their ten models are all autoregressive next-token decoders from five families, i.e. instances of one generation paradigm differing in weights and scale; we compare a *typed-AST structural decoder runtime* against a *flat masked-diffusion* decoder, which is the cross-paradigm pairing that Generate-then-Edit and hybrid AR-diffusion proposals (2601.15593; SpecRef 2606.27474; CoDiLA 2603.20216; TiDAR 2511.08923) actually presuppose, and which no oracle-union study has covered. (2) Direction of result: they report an oracle ceiling up to 83% above the best single model and a diversity heuristic realizing 95% of it -- headroom exists and is harvestable; we report a ceiling of +1.2/+2.9pp, i.e. essentially no headroom, in a setting the field is actively proposing to hybridize. A negative ceiling in a regime where a positive one is assumed is a separate contribution. (3) Accounting axis: our two systems are not two points on a quality axis but two owners of *different token-cost regimes* with no Pareto crossover, so "complementarity" here is a question about whether cost-regime separation implies competence separation -- a question their equal-cost homogeneous setup cannot pose. Separately, "Revision or Re-Solving?" (2604.01029, pre-cutoff) decomposes second-pass gains into re-solving/scaffold/content for AR-AR pipelines and finds code drafts help mainly as structural scaffolding; it is the closest conceptual precedent for deflating hybrid gains, but it studies revision pipelines, not per-task oracle union ceilings, and not diffusion. Finally, our independence-null plus same-family nesting-ratio control is, as far as we could find, absent from all of these: everyone reports raw unique-win counts and oracle gaps without a null model, so nobody can say whether an observed complementarity is large or small. That control is what upgrades our claim from "these two systems happen not to be complementary" to "the benchmark's difficulty structure makes near-nesting generic," and it is the piece a reviewer would otherwise demand.

followup_openings.target_paper: Wisdom and Delusion of LLM Ensembles for Code Generation and Repair (arXiv:2510.21513, 2025-10-24)
followup_openings.defect: Reports oracle ensemble ceilings (up to 83% above best single model) and unique-win complementarity with NO null model. With ten models at heterogeneous accuracies, a large raw oracle gap is partly arithmetically forced: if success were independent at the observed marginals the union would already be large. Without an independence baseline the paper cannot distinguish 'models have genuinely distinct competences' from 'marginals differ and any union of many systems looks big'. It also aggregates over models rather than reporting pairwise nesting, so it cannot detect that most pairs may be nested.
followup_openings.our_fix: Introduce the nesting ratio -- observed A-only wins divided by the independence-null expectation n*p_A*(1-p_B) -- as the unit of complementarity, and report it pairwise. We compute it on our data (0.24 HE+, 0.26 MBPP+ for structural-vs-diffusion) and calibrate it against pairs that differ only in compute within one architecture (0.00-0.26), showing our cross-paradigm pair is indistinguishable from same-model-different-budget. Applying the same statistic to their ten-model matrix would show which of their claimed complementarity is above chance and which is marginal-driven, and would sharpen rather than contradict their diversity-heuristic result.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It converts 'oracle gap' from an uncalibrated headline number into a testable quantity, and it is what lets a negative headroom result survive the obvious objection that our structural system is just weaker.

followup_openings.target_paper: The Capability Frontier: Benchmarks Miss 82% of Model Performance (arXiv:2606.26836, 2026-06-25, ICLR 2026 workshops -- CONCURRENT)
followup_openings.defect: They correctly identify that taking maxima over noisy samples overestimates oracle frontiers and claim to correct for it, but the correction is at the aggregate frontier level; the framing still treats the oracle-routing gap as harvestable capability and shows it grows with query topic entropy. It does not test the converse -- that on a low-entropy, near-unidimensional benchmark the gap collapses to noise -- nor does it report a within-family nesting control that would separate 'different specializations' from 'different points on one difficulty ladder'.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the low-entropy end of their own entropy axis as an empirical data point: on single-domain EvalPlus, oracle union over two paradigms is +1.2/+2.9pp, and same-family compute pairs give the same nesting ratios, i.e. the gap they predict to shrink with entropy does shrink to near-nothing. We must also adopt their single-sample-max caution: our oracle union is computed from one greedy-ish sample per system (T=0.1, top_p=0.95), so we will report the union with a resampling correction and a matched pass@2-of-one-system control, since a +1.2pp union is within reach of sampling noise -- which if anything strengthens the negative claim.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: It both cites concurrent work honestly and turns their monotone entropy-vs-gap simulation into a falsifiable prediction that our setting confirms, while fixing the noisy-max bias our own measurement shares.

followup_openings.target_paper: Speculative Refinement: A Hybrid AR-Diffusion Decoding Strategy (arXiv:2606.27474, 2026-06-25 -- CONCURRENT)
followup_openings.defect: Builds and evaluates a hybrid that warm-starts masked diffusion from an AR draft, and independently observes that 'providing a syntactic scaffold lifts accuracy from near zero to over 20% without changing the model' plus a 'refinement tension' where multi-stage correction degrades already-correct tokens. But it never measures per-task complementarity between its two components, so it cannot tell whether the hybrid's gains are new task coverage or the stronger component re-solving -- exactly the confound that 2604.01029 formalises and that our own Retraction 2 fell into. Its scaffold observation is also confounded with prompt/format effects.
followup_openings.our_fix: Provide the missing prerequisite measurement -- the per-task oracle union of the two components with a nesting-ratio null -- and show it is ~1-3pp, which reinterprets their refinement tension as movement along a nested ladder rather than a correctable engineering artefact. Their 'syntactic scaffold lifts near-zero to 20%' claim is also the one number of theirs we can directly stress-test, since our scaffold Medium at .177/.354 is the same phenomenon measured with per-task grading and honest token accounting including budget-truncated tasks (our Retraction 3).
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Concurrent, so it does not preempt us; but it is direct evidence that hybrids are being built in exactly this space without the headroom check, which is the paper's motivating premise.

followup_openings.target_paper: Empirical Study for Structured Output Control in LLMs for Software Engineering (arXiv:2606.09395, 2026-06-08 -- CONCURRENT); with The Format Tax (2604.03616, 2026-04-04) and Capacity, Not Format (2606.09410, 2026-06-08)
followup_openings.defect: 2606.09395 reaches nearly our qualitative conclusion -- strict template control 'nearly eliminates syntax errors, yet substantial structural and semantic errors persist, demonstrating that the core bottleneck lies beyond syntax formatting' -- but only for AR decoders on format-compliance-graded SE tasks, with an error taxonomy that is hand-categorised rather than execution-derived, and no cost accounting. The format-tax pair frames structure purely as a cost/tax on an existing model and never asks whether structure buys a different *cost regime*, only whether it loses accuracy.
followup_openings.our_fix: Give the execution-grounded, non-AR instance: the residual after structure is characterised by actual failing test inputs recovered from evalplus (all 48 MBPP+ plus-only failures fail exactly 1 of ~100 extra tests; failing inputs are empty string Mbpp/113,118, empty list Mbpp/119, all-identical elements Mbpp/129,137), and we price structure in cumulative model tokens including budget-truncated tasks. We add the causal test the format-tax papers imply but do not run for correctness: append a fixed-cost explicit boundary-condition instruction and measure movement in exactly the plus-only failure set.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Converges three independent literatures on 'structure fixes syntax, not semantics' from a new measurement modality, and the boundary-condition intervention is a cheap causal leg on top of an otherwise correlational diagnosis.

followup_openings.target_paper: TreeDiff: AST-Guided Code Generation with Diffusion LLMs (arXiv:2508.01473, 2025-08-02) and AnCoder: Anchored Code Generation via Discrete Diffusion (arXiv:2602.17688, 2026-02-05)
followup_openings.defect: Both add AST/structural priors to diffusion code generation and report gains (TreeDiff: 13.3% relative over random masking; AnCoder: 'parameter-efficient path to high-quality code generation') as aggregate deltas against a same-family random-masking baseline. Neither reports (a) per-task overlap with the unstructured baseline, so a reader cannot tell whether structure adds coverage or just climbs the same difficulty ladder; (b) token/compute cost of the structural machinery, so the gain is not priced; (c) plus-style augmented-test grading, so structural gains may be inflated by weak base tests -- the exact effect EvalPlus was built to catch.
followup_openings.our_fix: Apply our three diagnostics to structural-diffusion claims generally: nesting ratio against the unstructured baseline, cumulative model tokens including truncated tasks, and base-vs-plus decomposition of where the structural gain lands. Our data predicts structural gains concentrate on the base-pass/plus-fail band and on parse-failure elimination (our unparseable rate falls 94%->1.8% with compute alone), not on new task coverage -- a prediction their released setups could confirm or refute cheaply.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Generalises the paper from 'our in-house scaffold is nested' to a reusable audit for the whole structured-diffusion-decoder line, which is the difference between a workshop note about one checkpoint and a methods contribution.

followup_openings.target_paper: Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars (arXiv:2508.10111, 2025-08-13)
followup_openings.defect: Claims near-perfect syntactic correctness while 'consistently preserving or improving functional correctness'. 'Preserving or improving' is a disjunction that hides which one happened per task; with no per-task join against the unconstrained decoder, a wash could be many gains cancelling many losses (the token-degradation mode SpecRef calls refinement tension). Also evaluates C++ infilling and JSON extraction, not plus-style augmented Python tests.
followup_openings.our_fix: Reframe the claim we and they are jointly circling as a directional statement with per-task evidence: structure is correctness-*neutral* rather than correctness-additive. Our per-task joins give the sign and the count on both sides (2 structure-unique wins vs 89 structure-unique losses on HE+), which is the accounting their disjunction omits, and we run it under EvalPlus-augmented tests where correctness inflation is controlled.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Turns a hedged aggregate into a signed per-task result, and makes 'structure buys cheapness, not correctness' a claim about a specific, measured asymmetry rather than a slogan.

followup_openings.target_paper: LLMRouterBench (arXiv:2601.07206, 2026-01-12; ACL 2026 per DBLP) and Revision or Re-Solving? (arXiv:2604.01029, 2026-04-01)
followup_openings.defect: LLMRouterBench establishes at scale that realized routers barely beat a simple baseline and that a large oracle gap persists due to 'model-recall failures' -- but with 33 homogeneous AR models over 21 general datasets, and it treats the residual oracle gap as a recall problem to be solved rather than asking whether some gaps are unroutable in principle. Revision-or-Re-Solving supplies the matched-condition decomposition that separates genuine complementarity from stronger-model re-solving, but only for AR-AR revision, and reports no oracle ceiling.
followup_openings.our_fix: Compose the two into the router leg of our experiment and pre-register its interpretation: fit a router on pre-execution signals only (prompt features, per-system confidence, scaffold structural telemetry such as unresolved_masks and capacity_metrics) and report realized recovery of an oracle gap that is already only 1.2/2.9pp -- so the honest conclusion is a bound ('no router can recover more than ~1-3pp here'), not a router failure. Their re-solving/scaffold/content decomposition is also the correct post-mortem framing for our own Retraction 2 (the 'restart' policy discarded the scaffold draft and thus measured Dream re-solving), which we should cite rather than describe as an idiosyncratic bug.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Prevents the router leg from being an underpowered negative about our router, and cites the pre-cutoff work that names our own retracted failure mode -- which is both honest and makes the retraction a positioning asset.

related_work.citation: Wisdom and Delusion of LLM Ensembles for Code Generation and Repair. arXiv:2510.21513 (v1 2025-10-24, v2 2025-10-30).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. DBLP lists only CoRR 2025 (no conference record); arXiv comments field mentions only an acknowledgments/name-hyphenation revision, no venue. Verified via arXiv abs page version history + DBLP publ API.
related_work.what_it_covers: Closest methodological match. Ten AR LLMs from five families plus three ensembles across three SE benchmarks (code generation + program repair). Measures pairwise complementarity, the theoretical oracle upper bound of an ensemble (up to 83% above best single model), and evaluates realizable selection heuristics against it -- finding consensus strategies fall into a 'popularity trap' while a diversity-based strategy realizes up to 95% of the oracle, effective even for two-model ensembles.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: All systems are autoregressive next-token decoders; no non-AR or structured-runtime decoder. No token-cost regime axis -- complementarity is studied on a quality axis, not between systems that own disjoint segments of a cost-quality frontier. No independence null for unique-win counts. No per-task base-vs-plus failure decomposition. Reports a large harvestable ceiling, so the regime where the ceiling is ~0 is untouched.
related_work.known_defects: Oracle ceilings and unique-win complementarity are reported with no null model, so a large raw gap is partly forced by heterogeneous marginals over ten systems rather than evidencing distinct competences; aggregation over models rather than pairwise nesting reporting hides whether most pairs are nested; 'diversity realizes 95% of oracle' is a selection-heuristic result on the same runs used to define the oracle, inviting optimistic bias without a held-out split.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title/date/version history/subjects/comments) + DBLP publ API search. arXiv API abstract search.

related_work.citation: LLMRouterBench: A Massive Benchmark and Unified Framework for LLM Routing. arXiv:2601.07206 (v1 2026-01-12).
related_work.venue_status: DBLP reports ACL 2026 (plus CoRR 2026). NOT independently confirmed on OpenReview -- see verification_notes; treat the ACL 2026 attribution as DBLP-sourced only.
related_work.what_it_covers: 400K+ instances, 21 datasets, 33 models, 10 routing baselines. Confirms strong model complementarity as routing's central premise, finds many routing methods perform similarly under unified evaluation and that several recent/commercial routers fail to reliably beat a simple baseline, and that a substantial gap to the Oracle remains, driven mainly by persistent model-recall failures. Also reports diminishing returns from larger ensembles vs careful model curation, and enables latency-aware analysis.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Homogeneous AR model pool on general-purpose tasks; no diffusion, non-AR, or structured-decoder systems. Establishes the oracle-vs-realized routing gap generically but never asks whether a given oracle gap is unroutable in principle rather than a recall failure. No per-task nesting statistic and no execution-graded code failure taxonomy.
related_work.known_defects: Frames the residual oracle gap purely as recall failure to be engineered away, presupposing the gap is real signal; without a null model or per-pair nesting analysis it cannot identify benchmark regimes where the oracle gap is itself near-noise. Latency analysis is bolted on rather than used to define cost regimes.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, citation_date) + DBLP publ API (returned ACL 2026 + CoRR 2026). OpenReview api2 notes/search returned no matching note.

related_work.citation: The Capability Frontier: Benchmarks Miss 82% of Model Performance. arXiv:2606.26836 (v1 2026-06-25).
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Workshop on LLM Reasoning, and ICLR 2026 Workshop DATA-FM (Oral). Confirmed on OpenReview via api2 notes/search: two notes with venue 'ICLR 2026 Workshop LLM Reasoning' (venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Workshop/LLM_Reasoning) and 'ICLR 2026 Workshop DATA-FM Oral' (venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Workshop/DATA-FM).
related_work.what_it_covers: Defines a Capability Frontier: an oracle Pareto frontier over models AND generation budget characterising best achievable performance at each cost level under optimal cross-model, cross-sample selection. 21 LLMs, 16 benchmarks incl. coding. Explicitly corrects two opposing biases -- underestimation from single-model eval and overestimation from taking maxima over noisy samples. Reports 54%/82% error-rate reductions and SOTA matched at 85% cost reduction; controlled simulations show higher query topic entropy monotonically increases the oracle-routing-vs-best-single-model gap.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent, so does not preempt. Does not test the low-entropy limit of its own entropy axis empirically on a single-domain benchmark; no within-family nesting control separating 'distinct specializations' from 'distinct points on one difficulty ladder'; treats the oracle gap as harvestable capability rather than asking when it is structurally unroutable.
related_work.known_defects: The noisy-max correction operates at the aggregate frontier level, not per-task, so per-instance oracle unions in the paper remain optimistic; the entropy-vs-gap monotonicity is established in probabilistic simulation rather than measured across real benchmarks of graded entropy; 'benchmarks miss 82%' conflates an oracle-selection artefact with latent capability.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, citation_date, abstract) + OpenReview api2 notes/search term query returning venue and venueid fields.

related_work.citation: Parallelism and Generation Order in Masked Diffusion Language Models: Limits Today, Potential Tomorrow. arXiv:2601.15593 (v1 2026-01-22; citation_online_date 2026-04-11).
related_work.venue_status: DBLP reports ACL 2026 (plus CoRR 2026). NOT independently confirmed on OpenReview -- see verification_notes.
related_work.what_it_covers: The paper the candidate positions against. Characterises eight mainstream MDLMs (up to 100B) on 58 benchmarks via Average Finalization Parallelism and Kendall's tau; finds MDLMs lag comparable AR models because parallel probabilistic modelling weakens inter-token dependencies, and that parallelism/order adapt to task domain, reasoning stage, and correctness. Concludes with theoretical motivation and design insights supporting a Generate-then-Edit paradigm.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The Generate-then-Edit recommendation is argued from dependency-loss theory and decoding-behaviour statistics, never from per-task complementarity between the generate and edit stages. No oracle union, no routing headroom, no cost-regime accounting. Programming is one of three domain groups, not a focus, and grading is not execution-plus-augmented-tests.
related_work.known_defects: Recommends an architecture family on the strength of a diagnosis (dependency loss) without measuring the quantity the recommendation requires (does an editing stage reach tasks the generator misses?). AFP and Kendall's tau are decoding-process metrics used to license a claim about achievable correctness -- a construct-validity gap. Cross-model comparisons span very different training regimes, so 'MDLMs lag AR' is confounded with weights/data rather than being architecture-intrinsic.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, all 17 authors, citation_date 2026/01/22, citation_online_date, full abstract) + DBLP publ API (ACL 2026 + CoRR 2026).

related_work.citation: Speculative Refinement: A Hybrid Autoregressive Diffusion Decoding Strategy and Its Behavior Across Benchmarks. arXiv:2606.27474 (v1 2026-06-25).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; no venue found on DBLP or OpenReview. Verified via arXiv abs page.
related_work.what_it_covers: Training-free hybrid (SpecRef) warm-starting a masked diffusion LM from an AR draft via entropy-guided selective masking, across six benchmarks and three grading protocols. Reports four evaluation findings: code benchmarks conflate structural discovery with logical correctness (a syntactic scaffold lifts accuracy from near zero to over 20% without changing the model); a 'refinement tension' where multi-stage correction degrades already-correct tokens; log-likelihood vs generative eval producing different rankings; and standard Python post-processing silently breaking code eval for non-AR generators.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent. Builds the hybrid without ever measuring per-task complementarity between its AR and diffusion components, so it cannot separate new coverage from stronger-component re-solving. Its scaffold-lift observation is aggregate and confounded with prompt/format effects. No oracle union ceiling, no token-cost accounting for the two stages.
related_work.known_defects: 'Syntactic scaffold lifts near-zero to over 20%' is measured without a per-task join, so it is unknown whether the lift is coverage or parse-failure elimination; refinement tension is reported as a phenomenon rather than decomposed against a nested-ladder null; three grading protocols are compared but no single protocol is adopted as primary, leaving the headline hybrid claim protocol-dependent.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, citation_date, full abstract) + arXiv API search hit; DBLP and OpenReview searched, no venue record.

related_work.citation: Revision or Re-Solving? Decomposing Second-Pass Gains in Multi-LLM Pipelines. arXiv:2604.01029 (v1 2026-04-01).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. DBLP lists CoRR 2026 only. Verified via arXiv abs page + DBLP.
related_work.what_it_covers: Closest conceptual precedent for deflating hybrid/two-stage gains. Controlled decomposition with four matched conditions separating second-pass gains into additive re-solving, scaffold, and content components, across two model pairs and three benchmarks (knowledge MCQ + competitive programming). Finds MCQ gains are mostly stronger-model re-solving so direct routing beats revising a weak draft; on code, two-stage prompting still helps because even semantically null drafts provide substantial structural scaffolding, while weak draft content can be harmful. Role-reversed experiments show strong drafts help weak reviewers.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: AR-AR revision pipelines only; no diffusion, no structured-AST runtime. Reports no per-task oracle union or complementarity ceiling, so it deflates observed gains without bounding possible gains. No token-cost accounting or cost-regime framing. Its 'semantically null draft still scaffolds' code finding is exactly the confound our repo's Retraction 2 fell into, but it is not connected to non-AR generators.
related_work.known_defects: The additive three-way decomposition assumes components do not interact, which is untested; only two model pairs, so the MCQ-vs-code divergence rests on few observations; competitive programming grading details and per-task joins are not surfaced, so the 'structural scaffolding' component is inferred from condition means rather than per-task transitions.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, citation_date, full abstract) + DBLP publ API (CoRR 2026 only).

related_work.citation: Empirical Study for Structured Output Control in LLMs for Software Engineering. arXiv:2606.09395 (v1 2026-06-08).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; no venue record found. Verified via arXiv abs page.
related_work.what_it_covers: Nearest qualitative match to 'structure buys cheapness, not correctness'. Systematic evaluation of structural reliability across four SE tasks, categorising failures into syntax, structural, and semantic errors, benchmarking grammar-constrained decoding, regex validation, and a strict template control (TTMG). Finds TTMG nearly eliminates syntax errors yet substantial structural and semantic errors persist -- 'the core bottleneck lies beyond syntax formatting' -- concluding structure-enforcing tools are necessary but insufficient.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Concurrent. AR decoders only, on format-compliance-graded SE tasks rather than execution-graded code correctness; no diffusion or structured-runtime decoder. No cost accounting, so structure is never credited with buying a cheaper regime. No oracle union / routing analysis. Error taxonomy is categorised rather than derived from actual failing test inputs.
related_work.known_defects: Failure categories (syntax/structural/semantic) are assigned by inspection rather than execution, so the 'semantic' residual is not grounded in which inputs fail; case study is single and illustrative; TTMG is compared against constrained-decoding baselines without matched token cost, so 'necessary but insufficient' carries no price.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, citation_date, full abstract) + arXiv API search.

related_work.citation: The Format Tax. arXiv:2604.03616 (v1 2026-04-04). And Capacity, Not Format: Rethinking Structured Reasoning Failures. arXiv:2606.09410 (v1 2026-06-08).
related_work.venue_status: Both preprints; no venue records found (OpenReview term searches returned only unrelated titles). The Format Tax first public 2026-04-04 (pre-cutoff); Capacity-Not-Format first public 2026-06-08 (CONCURRENT). Verified via arXiv abs pages + OpenReview api2 search.
related_work.what_it_covers: The structure-as-tax literature. The Format Tax: structured output requirements (JSON/XML/LaTeX/Markdown) substantially degrade reasoning and writing across open-weight models; sampling bias from constrained decoding is only a fraction, with most loss entering at the prompt from format-requesting instructions alone; decoupling reasoning from formatting (freeform-then-reformat, or extended thinking) recovers most lost accuracy. Capacity, Not Format: with information-matched prose controls and a four-level schema complexity gradient, the format penalty is capacity-dependent -- models with headroom absorb JSON without degradation while models near their limits degrade via truncation and pure capacity competition.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Both frame structure purely as a cost or tax on an existing model's accuracy and never ask whether structure buys a different cost regime (tokens/latency) that could be worth the accuracy loss. General reasoning/writing/math tasks, not execution-graded code. No per-task complementarity between structured and unstructured variants, hence no oracle union and no routing question.
related_work.known_defects: Format Tax's key positive claim (decoupling recovers most accuracy) is a two-pass remedy whose extra token cost is not priced, and its 'recent closed-weight models show little format tax' rests on API models with unknown internals. Capacity-Not-Format's headline draws on a small number of model-benchmark cells and reports a 5.3pp Opus 4.7 AIME drop from 7/133 items, which is thin for the 'qualifies frontier immunity' claim.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs pages (titles, citation_dates, full abstracts) + OpenReview api2 notes/search (no matching venue notes) + arXiv API search.

related_work.citation: TreeDiff: AST-Guided Code Generation with Diffusion LLMs. arXiv:2508.01473 (v1 2025-08-02). And AnCoder: Anchored Code Generation via Discrete Diffusion Models. arXiv:2602.17688 (v1 2026-02-05).
related_work.venue_status: Both preprints. DBLP lists TreeDiff as CoRR 2025 only; AnCoder returned no DBLP conference record. Verified via arXiv abs pages + DBLP publ API.
related_work.what_it_covers: The structural-prior-in-diffusion line our scaffold runtime sits in. TreeDiff replaces random token masking with AST-node-aware selective masking during corruption to align denoising with syntactic boundaries and long-range hierarchical dependencies, reporting 13.3% relative improvement over random masking. AnCoder/AnchorTree anchors the diffusion process with AST-derived hierarchical priors, resolving syntactically/semantically salient tokens (keywords, identifiers) first to establish a structural scaffold, claiming a parameter-efficient path to high-quality code generation.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Neither reports per-task overlap with its unstructured baseline, so it is unknown whether structural priors add task coverage or climb the same difficulty ladder. Neither prices the structural machinery in tokens/compute. Neither reports a base-vs-plus (augmented-test) decomposition locating where the gain lands, so structural gains may be concentrated in parse-failure elimination or in weak-base-test artefacts. No comparison against a flat-diffusion system at matched cost.
related_work.known_defects: Aggregate relative-improvement headlines against a same-family random-masking baseline with no per-task join and no cost accounting -- precisely the accounting that our repo's own Retraction 3 shows can understate cost by 2.85-3.69x when truncated tasks are dropped. AnCoder's 'high-quality code generation' claim is stated without the benchmark-level numbers needed to place it on a quality-cost frontier.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs pages (titles, citation_dates, full abstracts) + DBLP publ API + arXiv API searches on 'syntax tree AND diffusion AND program' and 'scaffold AND code generation AND diffusion'.

related_work.citation: Constrained Decoding of Diffusion LLMs with Context-Free Grammars. arXiv:2508.10111 (v1 2025-08-13).
related_work.venue_status: Preprint; arXiv comments and journal-ref fields empty, no DBLP/OpenReview venue record found. Verified via arXiv abs page.
related_work.what_it_covers: First constrained-decoding method for diffusion LLMs handling context-free grammars, by reducing constrained decoding to additive infilling (which also subsumes previously unaddressed multi-region infilling) and then to emptiness of the intersection of the target CFL with a regular language. Evaluated on C++ code infilling and JSON structured extraction, achieving near-perfect syntactic correctness while 'consistently preserving or improving functional correctness'.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: The correctness claim is a disjunction ('preserving or improving') with no per-task join against the unconstrained decoder, so the sign and distribution of the effect are unreported. Evaluated on C++ infilling and JSON, not on plus-style augmented Python tests, so correctness inflation from weak tests is uncontrolled. No complementarity/oracle-union analysis versus unconstrained diffusion, and no token-cost accounting for the grammar machinery.
related_work.known_defects: 'Preserving or improving functional correctness' can hide many per-task gains cancelling many per-task losses -- the token-degradation mode that SpecRef independently names refinement tension; without per-task transitions the claim is unfalsifiable as stated. Syntactic correctness is near-perfect by construction (the method enforces it), so the interesting quantity is entirely the correctness delta, which is the least precisely reported.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, citation_date, abstract, empty comments/journal-ref) + arXiv API search on 'grammar AND constrained decoding AND functional correctness'.

related_work.citation: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation (EvalPlus). arXiv:2305.01210 (v1 2023-05-02); NeurIPS 2023.
related_work.venue_status: NeurIPS 2023 (widely established; arXiv v1 2023-05-02). Verified via arXiv abs page; venue is pre-2025 so OpenReview verification is not the binding requirement.
related_work.what_it_covers: The grading instrument the entire candidate depends on. Augments benchmark test suites with automatically generated test inputs (LLM- plus mutation-based), extending HumanEval by 80x to build HumanEval+, and shows it catches large amounts of previously undetected wrong code across 26 LLMs. Supplies the base_status/plus_status and base_fail_tests/plus_fail_tests fields that make the candidate's per-task and per-test edge-case diagnosis possible.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Provides the base-vs-plus distinction but does not characterise what kind of semantic error the plus-only failures represent; the augmented inputs are generated for coverage, not organised into an interpretable taxonomy of degenerate/boundary cases. Does not analyse whether plus-only failures cluster on a small number of extra tests, nor whether they are addressable by prompting.
related_work.known_defects: Augmented inputs are generated by mutation and LLM proposal, so 'plus' difficulty is an artefact of the generator's input distribution rather than a calibrated difficulty scale -- relevant to us because a residual concentrated on empty-string/empty-list/all-identical inputs may reflect the generator's degenerate-input bias as much as model weakness. This is a confound the candidate's boundary-condition intervention must control for.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv abs page (title, citation_date, abstract). Venue is standard knowledge for EvalPlus 0.3.1, the package used in the repo.
