The second, subtler risk is confounding rather than nullity: the headline nesting result compares a deterministic-greedy scaffold (argmax hardcoded at model_sampler.py:641) against a single stochastic Dream sample (T=0.1/top_p=0.95), in a repo whose own data shows a top_p tweak worth +14.6 HumanEval points. A reviewer will ask whether the 2-vs-89 asymmetry and the 0.236 ratio are partly a sampler artifact, and with a single sample per system there is no answer. Third: the HE+ union delta's bootstrap CI is [0.00,+3.05]pp and includes zero, so any sentence asserting "+1.2pp of real headroom exists" is unsupported — the honest statement is that headroom is indistinguishable from zero, which is a stronger claim but a different one. Fourth and quietest: the entire result is one SFT-stage1 scaffold checkpoint on one 164/378-task benchmark family, so "EvalPlus difficulty is near-unidimensional" rests on ratios whose HE+ CI ([0.000,0.575]) is wide enough to admit a fair amount of genuine complementarity.
feas.required_control:
A SYMMETRIC PER-SYSTEM HARNESS-ARTIFACT AUDIT that partitions every graded failure into {crashed-before-any-test, genuine-test-failure} and re-grades the crash bucket with the benchmark prompt's own import context restored, applied identically to BOTH systems and every ladder rung, with the oracle union reported under both the as-graded and artifact-corrected pass sets and a single pass convention (strict base&plus) declared in one place and imported everywhere.

This is the control because the three retractions share one shape: a number was computed over a set whose membership was silently decided by something other than the thing being measured (a verifier that discarded return values; a stage that discarded its input; an average that discarded the expensive tasks). This candidate's entire content is the MEMBERSHIP of two per-task pass sets and their union — so the analogous failure is a pass/fail label produced by the grading path rather than by model competence. That failure is already present and already asymmetric: base_status=='fail' with base_fail_tests==[] means the solution raised before a single test executed, and it occurs on 9/164 Dream HE+ tasks versus 36/164 scaffold-Medium HE+ tasks, because extract_python (generate_evalplus_dream.py:53-79) grades the model's fenced code alone while the EvalPlus prompt owned the typing header the model did not re-emit. Re-grading with the header restored flips HumanEval/8 and HumanEval/22 to pass, moving Dream HE+ .7073->.7134 and the union .7195->.7256. Without this control the paper would publish an oracle union, a 65.9% overlap, and four nesting ratios all computed over pass sets that are wrong by a system-dependent amount — a fourth retraction in the same family. With it, the direction survives (the union delta stays +1.22pp and the nesting ratios barely move), which is exactly why the control is cheap to run and indefensible to skip.

lens.title: The Canvas Is the Confound: Fixed max_new_tokens Silently Couples Cost, Quality, and Step Count in Every Diffusion-LM Code Evaluation
lens.claim: Fixed-canvas decoding makes the generation-length budget an uncontrolled third variable in diffusion-LM evaluation: with max_new_tokens pinned at 512, roughly half of all tasks (49.4% HE+, 44.2% MBPP+) consume essentially the entire canvas, and those canvas-saturated tasks pass at .642/.539 versus .771/.796 for non-saturated ones. Because every published NFE curve for this family holds the canvas fixed while varying steps, reported step-quality relationships are confounded with per-task length adequacy, and per-step cost is inflated by dead canvas positions attended at full quadratic cost on every forward pass.
lens.why_now: DreamOn (ICLR 2026 Poster, arXiv 2602.01326) established that fixed-canvas length mismatch degrades infilling and solved it there, and our reproduction confirmed DreamOn is an infilling specialist (HE+ .122 from-scratch). But the measurement consequence for from-scratch generation -- the setting everyone benchmarks -- is unaddressed: the canvas is simultaneously a quality knob and the dominant term in per-step cost (685 tok/step = 173 prompt + 512 canvas), so it must be reported and swept, not fixed by convention. Cleanest remaining methodological gap adjacent to our retraction history.
lens.experiment: (1) ALREADY MEASURED: tokenizing raw_output from the r2 runs gives mean length 435/512 (HE+) and 406/512 (MBPP+) with 81/164 and 167/378 tasks at >=500 tokens, plus the pass-rate split above; separately the schedule simulation shows canvas length also sets where the no-op regime begins (steps>canvas => dead forwards), so canvas and steps are mechanically entangled, not independent knobs. (2) TO RUN, core grid: decouple canvas from steps in scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py (currently every launch script passes --steps and --max-new-tokens the same value) and run canvas x steps over {128,256,384,512} x {128,256,384,512} on HE+ (n=164) plus diagonal and two off-diagonals on MBPP+ (n=378), reporting pass@1+, forwarded token-positions, and wall clock per cell. This grid is already launched on LOCAL and partially complete. (3) Report per-task length adequacy as a first-class covariate: stratify every quality number by canvas saturation, and show a length-adaptive canvas (cheap length predictor, or DreamOn's expansion mechanism repurposed for from-scratch generation) reaches equal quality at materially lower forwarded-token cost than the fixed-512 convention. (4) Publish a reporting standard: canvas, steps, tokens-per-step, forwarded token-positions, and saturation rate must all be stated, since any one alone is ambiguous.
lens.assets_needed: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B and models/DreamOn-v0-7B (have both; DreamOn supplies the length-expansion mechanism for leg 3); all runs/dream_* with raw_output preserved in metrics.rank*.jsonl (have -- raw_output is what makes the retrospective saturation measurement possible); data/evalplus/*_plus.jsonl + grader (have); scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py needs canvas/steps decoupling (trivial, one argument). MISSING: nothing blocking; a length predictor for leg 3 can be a heuristic (prompt length, docstring length) before anything learned, and the DreamOn variant reuses weights we have.
lens.kill_criterion: Dies if the canvas x steps grid shows quality depends only on step count and is flat in canvas at matched steps -- i.e. canvas256/steps256 and canvas512/steps256 within noise (<3 pts, HE+ n=164) -- because then the canvas is merely a cost multiplier with no quality role and the confound claim reduces to an efficiency footnote. Weakens substantially if the saturation-vs-quality gap (.642 vs .771) is fully explained by task difficulty rather than truncation, which we test by checking whether canvas-saturated tasks stay harder given a 1024 canvas.
lens.builds_on: Extends DreamOn (arXiv:2602.01326, ICLR 2026 Poster -- verify venue via OpenReview venueid before citing as published) from a generation-capability fix for infilling to a measurement-validity claim for from-scratch generation, the regime where DreamOn itself is weak and where the acceleration literature reports its numbers. Complements CaRE (2607.24763), which standardizes NFE and stochasticity but treats sequence length as fixed background rather than a controlled factor, and ParallelBench (2510.04767), which controls task structure but not canvas adequacy. Also directly repairs our own repo's convention: the 685-tok/step figure underpinning our token-cost-matched Pareto is itself a fixed-canvas artifact, so this candidate strengthens or corrects our surviving headline result.

related_work.citation: Li, Dong, Zang, Cao, Wang, Lin. "Beyond Fixed: Training-Free Variable-Length Denoising for Diffusion Large Language Models" (DAEDAL). arXiv:2508.00819.
related_work.venue_status: ICLR 2026 Poster -- verified via OpenReview api2 search: venue='ICLR 2026 Poster', venueid='ICLR.cc/2026/Conference'.
related_work.what_it_covers: The single closest pre-cutoff paper on the *quality* side of the canvas knob. Table 1/2 give a 6-point fixed-length baseline sweep (64..2048) on GSM8K/MATH500/MBPP/HumanEval for LLaDA-Instruct-8B and LLaDA-1.5-8B, showing accuracy rises then plateaus/degrades with canvas, and reports E_token / N_token / E_ratio (effective-token ratio) quantifying dead canvas. Proposes a training-free two-phase expansion (pre-denoising length growth + in-denoising mask insertion) that beats the best tuned fixed length at lower N_token.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: Canvas is swept as a 1-D axis only, never crossed with step count. No per-task length-adequacy stratification (all numbers are dataset aggregates; no notion of which individual tasks saturated). No code-correctness accounting beyond base pass@1 (no EvalPlus plus-tests). Cost is reported as effective-token *ratio*, never as forwarded token-positions or FLOPs. Dream/Dream-Coder family untested (LLaDA only).
related_work.known_defects: Its released baseline script scripts/eval_LLaDA_Baseline.sh sets `gen_length=${length},steps=${length}` -- i.e. every baseline cell changes canvas and step count together. So the entire 'meticulously tuned fixed-length baseline' comparison is confounded exactly as our candidate alleges, and the headline 'comparable accuracy at lower N_token' is not matched on forward passes. E_ratio credits the method for not emitting padding but does not price the forward passes actually spent, so the efficiency claim is a token-utilisation proxy rather than a compute measurement.
related_work.verified_how: arXiv API (v1 2025-08-01, v2 2025-08-18); arXiv HTML full text read (Sec 4.1-4.4, Table 1); OpenReview api2 venue check; GitHub raw fetch of Li-Jinsong/DAEDAL/scripts/eval_LLaDA_Baseline.sh confirming steps==gen_length.

related_work.citation: Rossi, Cirò, Beltrame, Gandolfi, Röttger, Hovy. "Diffusion Language Models Are Natively Length-Aware" (SmartCrop). arXiv:2603.06123.
related_work.venue_status: Preprint. OpenReview api2 returns venue='Submitted to ICML 2026', venueid='ICML.cc/2026/Conference/Rejected_Submission' -- i.e. rejected, no accepted venue. Cite as preprint.
related_work.what_it_covers: Zero-shot canvas cropping from first-step EoS logits (inverse-survival thresholding), evaluated on GSM8K/HumanEval/IfEval/LongFormQA with LLaDA-8B. Names the 'padding tax' explicitly, reports FLOPs saved, and -- most relevant to us -- runs a ±δ canvas-perturbation sensitivity analysis showing over-padding actively *hurts* quality (IfEval strict accuracy .48 -> .41 as δ -> +50%), plus a shuffled-length control.
related_work.what_it_leaves_open: No factorial: it perturbs canvas only, never crosses canvas with steps. On HumanEval it is a single canvas value (L_new=512) with no code-side stratification. No per-task saturation covariate. Uses base HumanEval pass@1, not EvalPlus. Does not touch code-specialised diffusion LMs (Dream-Coder, DreamOn).
related_work.known_defects: Its own Table 1 sets T = L_new for GSM8K/HumanEval/IfEval, so cropping the canvas mechanically cuts the number of denoising steps too. Both headline results are therefore measured at a jointly-changed operating point: 'FLOPs saved' bundles canvas shrink with step reduction, and the striking over-padding degradation (δ>0) is confounded with the *increase* in steps that accompanies it. The paper's central causal reading ('excess padding is deleterious') is thus not identified by its own design -- it is exactly the confound our candidate names, committed by a paper whose thesis depends on it.

diff.differentiation_statement: No pre-2026-05-07 paper makes this candidate's claim, but several make adjacent ones, so the framing must shift from "the canvas matters for quality" (which DAEDAL Table 1 and SmartCrop Fig. 2 already showed, pre-cutoff) to "the canvas x steps design has never been crossed, and per-task length adequacy has never been reported, so published step-quality curves in this family are not identified." Three differences a reviewer will accept. (1) Design: every prior paper varies canvas as a 1-D axis with steps slaved to it. DAEDAL's own released baseline script sets `gen_length=${length},steps=${length}`; SmartCrop's Table 1 sets T = L_new for GSM8K/HumanEval/IfEval. Our contribution is the factorial that neither ran, which is the only design that can estimate the interaction rather than assume it away. The one paper that separates the axes (arXiv:2606.19475, 2026-06-17) does so with two disjoint 1-D slices and is concurrent, so it neither preempts us nor supplies the interaction term. (2) Unit of analysis: prior work reports dataset aggregates; we introduce per-task canvas saturation as a first-class covariate and stratify every quality number by it (I reproduced the candidate's split exactly from runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus_r2 and .../mbppplus_r2: HE+ 81/164 = 49.4% at >=500 tokens passing .642 vs .771; MBPP+ 167/378 = 44.2% passing .539 vs .791). No prior paper in this family reports a saturation rate at all. (3) Setting and grading: code-specialised diffusion LMs (Dream-Coder-7B, DreamOn) with EvalPlus plus-test execution grading and cost in forwarded token-positions, versus LLaDA + base pass@1 + effective-token-ratio in DAEDAL/SmartCrop/rho-EOS. Crucially, CaRE -- the closest protocol paper, and concurrent -- dismisses our factor by stipulation: its limitations paragraph says sequence length "also matter[s] but produce[s] smaller measured effects," with no measurement. Supplying that measurement inside a protocol paper whose thesis is that unmeasured factors reverse conclusions is a clean, citable wedge. What we must NOT claim is leg 3 (a length-adaptive canvas reaching equal quality at lower cost): DAEDAL, SmartCrop, rho-EOS, LR-DLLM, CAL, dLLM-Var and DID all do that pre-cutoff. Leg 3 has to be demoted from contribution to control -- a reproduction of existing adaptive-length methods re-priced under our accounting.

followup_openings.target_paper: DAEDAL, arXiv:2508.00819 (ICLR 2026 Poster)
followup_openings.defect: Its fixed-length baseline is not compute-matched and not factorially separated. The released eval_LLaDA_Baseline.sh passes `gen_length=${length},steps=${length}` for all seven lengths (32..2048), so each baseline cell moves canvas and step count together. The headline claim -- DAEDAL matches or beats the 'meticulously tuned' best fixed length while generating fewer total tokens (e.g. HumanEval 48.2 at N_token 813 vs baseline 47.6 at 1024) -- compares methods that differ in both canvas and number of forward passes, and prices them in effective-token ratio, which counts emitted padding rather than forward passes actually spent.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-run their baseline as a proper canvas x steps factorial and re-price both arms in forwarded token-positions (sum over steps of the attended width) and wall clock. This decomposes their reported advantage into (a) canvas adaptivity, (b) step count, (c) interaction. We already have the harness and the coupling fix is one argument in scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py; the arithmetic to convert their published N_token/E_ratio table into forwarded positions is free.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the single highest-value leg: it repairs an ICLR-2026 poster's central comparison using a design the community accepts, and it does so on a claim (adaptive length is worth it) that many downstream papers now cite. If the advantage survives re-pricing, we have strengthened a published result under a stricter accounting; if it shrinks, we have a genuine correction. Either outcome is publishable and neither depends on our own method working.

followup_openings.target_paper: SmartCrop / "Diffusion Language Models Are Natively Length-Aware", arXiv:2603.06123 (preprint; ICML 2026 Rejected_Submission)
followup_openings.defect: Its two headline results are both measured at a jointly-changed operating point. Table 1 fixes T = L_new for GSM8K, HumanEval and IfEval, so cropping the canvas mechanically reduces the step count. Therefore (i) 'FLOPs saved' conflates a narrower canvas with fewer denoising steps, and (ii) the striking over-padding result -- IfEval strict accuracy falling .48 -> .41 as delta -> +50% -- is confounded with the step *increase* that padding brings along. The paper's causal conclusion ('excess padding is not merely wasteful but actively deleterious ... may destabilise the denoising process') is not identified by its own design.
followup_openings.our_fix: Replicate the +/-delta perturbation with steps held fixed while canvas varies, and separately with canvas held fixed while steps vary, on HumanEval+ with execution grading. This isolates the pure canvas effect from the step effect and directly tests whether over-padding hurts quality per se or only via the induced schedule change. Our factorial already contains the required cells (canvas256/steps256 vs canvas512/steps256 is exactly the contrast).
followup_openings.why_it_matters: A paper whose entire thesis is that the canvas is a quality variable failed to control the confound that would prove it. Fixing this converts a suggestive correlational finding into an identified one -- and it is the same repair, on the same axis, as the DAEDAL leg, so one grid buys both. It also resolves the candidate's own kill criterion: the canvas256/steps256 vs canvas512/steps256 comparison is simultaneously our decisive cell and SmartCrop's missing control.

followup_openings.target_paper: CaRE, arXiv:2607.24763 (concurrent, 2026-06-04)
followup_openings.defect: Dismissal by stipulation. Its 'Statistical caveats' paragraph concedes 'The three confounds we study are not exhaustive -- numerical precision, prompt format, and sequence length also matter but produce smaller measured effects', but no measurement of the sequence-length effect appears anywhere in the paper. Separately, standardising actual NFE while leaving the canvas free is insufficient: two runs at identical NFE can differ ~4x in forwarded token-positions, so an NFE-standardised protocol still permits large uncontrolled compute differences.
followup_openings.our_fix: Supply the missing measurement and show the effect is not small. Our reproduced HE+ split is 12.9 points (.642 saturated vs .771 non-saturated) and MBPP+ is 25.2 points, versus a headline CaRE interaction significant at p=0.020. Then propose the minimal extension to their protocol: report canvas, steps, tokens-per-step, forwarded token-positions and saturation rate, and standardise on forwarded positions rather than NFE alone. Best executed as a companion/extension that adopts their leaderboard rather than competing with it.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: Extending a protocol paper is far more tractable than displacing one, and CaRE has pre-written our motivation. Because CaRE is concurrent it cannot preempt us, and its explicit concession is the strongest possible citation that the field considers this factor unmeasured. This is also the leg that most cleanly justifies the 'reporting standard' deliverable, which otherwise reads as unearned prescriptivism.

followup_openings.target_paper: Diffusion Language Models: An Experimental Analysis, arXiv:2606.19475 (concurrent, 2026-06-17)
followup_openings.defect: Its central attribution -- 'it is the generation length rather than the step count that drives performance degradation' -- is inferred by juxtaposing two different experiments (Fig. 1's 1:1 joint diagonal against Fig. 2's fixed N=1024 step sweep) rather than from a design that crosses the factors, so the interaction is assumed away. Fig. 2 is anchored at N=1024, deep in the over-padded regime for code, which plausibly inflates the apparent length effect. All numbers are dataset aggregates on base MBPP/HumanEval with no per-task length-adequacy stratification and no forwarded-position accounting.
followup_openings.our_fix: Run the actual factorial on HE+ n=164 over canvas x steps in {128,256,384,512}^2 with EvalPlus plus-tests, report the interaction term, and stratify each cell by per-task saturation. Their qualitative conclusion becomes a testable prediction we can confirm or refute at matched steps, and our stratification explains *which tasks* drive it.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the paper a reviewer will most likely raise as 'already done'. Pre-empting it by naming the design gap (two 1-D slices vs a factorial) and confirming/refuting its attribution on a different model family with execution grading turns the most dangerous overlap into our clearest point of contrast. Concurrency gives us cover; the factorial gives us content.

followup_openings.target_paper: Our own repo (DLLM_RESULTS_20260807.md, figures/, the token-cost-matched Pareto)
followup_openings.defect: The 685 tok/step (HE+) and 604 tok/step (MBPP+) flat-canvas cost figure that underpins the surviving Pareto claim is itself computed at the fixed-512 convention -- i.e. prompt + 512 canvas re-attended every step. The Plain-SFT control was priced with the same convention. So the claim 'Plain-SFT reaches the Pareto frontier at zero points' is stated at one arbitrary canvas setting for the vanilla arm, and the scaffold-vs-flat crossover location depends on a number we now know is a free parameter.
followup_openings.our_fix: Re-price the Plain-SFT / vanilla arm at its best canvas from the factorial rather than at 512, and re-plot the Pareto. Report the crossover as a band over canvas settings, not a point. This is nearly free -- the grid is already running on LOCAL and the cost accounting is arithmetic on existing metrics.rank*.jsonl.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is the fourth item in a repo with three retractions already caused by exactly this class of error (NFE as a cross-family cost unit; averaging that dropped truncated tasks). Auditing our own headline before a reviewer does converts a latent retraction risk into a strength, and it makes the reporting-standard deliverable credible because we applied it to ourselves first.

followup_openings.target_paper: DreamOn arXiv:2602.01326 (ICLR 2026 Poster) and LR-DLLM arXiv:2602.07546
followup_openings.defect: Both validate length-elastic generation exclusively on infilling -- their home turf. DreamOn's mechanism is never tested on from-scratch generation, the regime the acceleration literature actually benchmarks; our own reproduction measures it at HE+ .122 / MBPP+ .085 there. LR-DLLM reports all gains relative to DreamOn on HumanEval-Infilling and McEval with no from-scratch control.
followup_openings.our_fix: Report the from-scratch transfer honestly as a negative/boundary result: repurpose DreamOn's expansion mechanism for from-scratch HE+/MBPP+ under our accounting and show whether it reaches equal quality at lower forwarded cost than fixed-512. Keep it as a control arm, explicitly NOT a novel mechanism, and cite DAEDAL/SmartCrop/rho-EOS/CAL as the pre-cutoff owners of adaptive length.
followup_openings.why_it_matters: This is where the candidate is most exposed: leg 3 as written ('show a length-adaptive canvas reaches equal quality at materially lower cost') is squarely owned by DAEDAL (ICLR 2026), SmartCrop, rho-EOS, LR-DLLM, CAL, dLLM-Var and DID, all pre-cutoff. Reframing it as a home-turf-generalisation audit keeps the asset useful, kills the novelty-collision, and adds a regime nobody has reported.

diff.verification_notes:
Things I could NOT verify, and one finding that materially weakens the candidate as written.

(1) MOST IMPORTANT -- a partial self-refutation I found by decomposing the candidate's own headline split. The candidate's kill criterion says the claim "weakens substantially if the saturation-vs-quality gap (.642 vs .771) is fully explained by task difficulty rather than truncation." I ran that decomposition on the existing r2 metrics and the truncation story does not survive intact. Parseable-output rate is 96.3% for saturated vs 100.0% for non-saturated on HE+ (96.4% vs 100.0% on MBPP+), and every single output in both strata contains a code fence. Conditioning on parseability barely moves the gap: pass|parseable is .667 vs .771 on HE+ and .559 vs .791 on MBPP+. So of the 12.9-point HE+ gap only ~3.7 points is attributable to output actually being cut off mid-code; the remaining ~9 points (and ~23 of 25 on MBPP+) is length-correlated task difficulty or verbosity, not truncation. The candidate's own weakening condition is therefore already substantially met before the 1024-canvas test is run. This does not kill the direction -- "length adequacy is a covariate confounded with difficulty" is still a valid and arguably more interesting measurement claim, and it makes the stratification deliverable more necessary rather than less -- but the abstract must not imply the pass-rate gap is a truncation artifact. I would rewrite the claim as "canvas saturation is a per-task covariate that is confounded with difficulty and is never reported," and make the 1024-canvas difficulty control a required leg rather than a robustness check.

(2) The candidate's quantitative claims that I DID verify by re-running on disk: mean generated length 435.0/512 (HE+, median 498.5) and 406.5/512 (MBPP+, median 474.0); 81/164 = 49.4% and 167/378 = 44.2% at >=500 tokens; pass rates .642 vs .771 (HE+) and .539 vs .791 (MBPP+); overall .707/.680. All match the candidate exactly. I also confirmed the canvas/steps coupling is real in our code: scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py has independent --steps and --max-new-tokens arguments, but every launcher passes them equal (scripts/_run_baselines_r2_wzc1.sh:55,61,68,74 etc.), and the NFE sweep scripts pin --max-new-tokens 512 while varying --steps -- so the NFE sweep is already a fixed-canvas step sweep, exactly as described.

(3) ParallelBench (2510.04767): the arXiv HTML endpoint returned a ~600-character stub for v1, v2 and v3, so I could not read the full text. My statement that it "does not control canvas adequacy" rests on the abstract plus the candidate's assertion, not on my own reading. Treat that one related-work row as lower confidence than the others; verify before citing it as a contrast.

(4) Venue statuses I verified on OpenReview (per the 2026-venue rule): DreamOn = ICLR 2026 Poster (note EQTPmqukiU, venueid ICLR.cc/2026/Conference, Camera_Ready_Revision invitation present); DAEDAL = ICLR 2026 Poster; ParallelBench = ICLR 2026 Poster; SureLock = ICLR 2026 Poster; DID = ICLR 2026 Poster; Dynamic Boundary Masking = COLM 2026 NonAR-LM Workshop Poster (forum 1R4aADP5HC). Verified NOT accepted anywhere: SmartCrop returns venueid ICML.cc/2026/Conference/Rejected_Submission -- do not cite it as an ICML paper. rho-EOS returns only a DBLP CoRR 2026 shadow. CaRE, LR-DLLM, CAL, dLLM-Var, the Experimental Analysis paper and Dream-Coder returned no OpenReview venue record, so all are cited as preprints; absence of an OpenReview record is weak evidence of non-acceptance and any of these could be under review or accepted elsewhere.

(5) Semantic Scholar was rate-limited (HTTP 429) for every query I attempted, so my coverage rests on the arXiv API (many query formulations), OpenReview api2 search, arXiv HTML full-text reads, and GitHub raw fetches. I did not check ACL Anthology directly. Given the topic is almost entirely arXiv-and-ICLR-native, I think coverage is adequate, but I cannot rule out an ACL/EMNLP-venue paper on generation-budget confounds in code evaluation.

(6) I attempted several searches specifically designed to find a pre-cutoff paper running an explicit canvas x steps factorial or reporting per-task saturation stratification for diffusion LMs (arXiv full-text-ish queries on "fixed canvas", "fixed-length canvas", generation length + HumanEval, decouple + denoising steps, stratify + length, max_new_tokens, construct validity + LM eval; OpenReview searches on canvas/length/confound phrasings). None returned such a paper. I am reasonably confident the factorial and the saturation covariate are genuinely unoccupied pre-cutoff; I am confident the opposite for the adaptive-length mechanism, which is crowded with at least seven pre-cutoff entries.

(7) I did not verify the candidate's schedule-simulation claim that "steps > canvas => dead forwards" against the actual Dream sampler code; I only confirmed the argument surface exists. Worth a 10-minute check before it appears in a paper, since it is an easy target for a reviewer with the source open.
diff.sharpened_claim: Diffusion-LM evaluations in this family have never crossed their two decoding factors: in every paper we could find, the generation canvas is either fixed by convention or slaved to the step count (DAEDAL's released baseline sets steps=gen_length across 32..2048; SmartCrop sets T=L_new for GSM8K/HumanEval/IfEval), so reported step-quality relationships are not identified and reported efficiency gains are quoted against a padded-canvas denominator that is itself a free parameter. We run the missing factorial -- canvas x steps over {128,256,384,512}^2 on HumanEval+ (n=164) with EvalPlus execution grading, plus a diagonal and two off-diagonals on MBPP+ (n=378) -- and price every cell in forwarded token-positions rather than NFE, which we show can differ ~4x at equal NFE. Two deliverables follow. (a) A repair: we re-price DAEDAL's fixed-length baseline and re-run SmartCrop's +/-delta canvas perturbation with steps held fixed, decomposing each paper's headline into canvas effect, step effect, and interaction; SmartCrop's causal claim that over-padding is actively deleterious (.48 -> .41 at delta=+50%) is currently confounded with the step increase padding induces, and the canvas256/steps256 vs canvas512/steps256 cell is simultaneously our decisive contrast and their missing control. (b) A covariate nobody reports: per-task canvas saturation. At the field-standard 512, 49.4% of HE+ and 44.2% of MBPP+ tasks consume essentially the whole canvas, and saturated tasks pass at .642/.539 versus .771/.791 -- but we show by decomposition that only ~3.7 of the 12.9 HE+ points is truncated output (parseable rate 96.3% vs 100.0%; pass|parseable .667 vs .771), so saturation is a difficulty-confounded covariate rather than a truncation artifact, which is exactly why it must be reported and stratified rather than aggregated away. We therefore supply the measurement CaRE explicitly declines to make -- its limitations paragraph asserts sequence length "produce[s] smaller measured effects" without measuring it -- and propose the minimal protocol extension: canvas, steps, tokens-per-step, forwarded token-positions and saturation rate must all be stated. Adaptive-length decoding is treated strictly as a control arm reproducing pre-existing methods (DAEDAL, SmartCrop, rho-EOS, LR-DLLM, CAL, DID) under the new accounting, not as a contribution, and we apply the standard to our own prior 685-tok/step Pareto first.

blocking_gaps: FALSE ASSET CLAIM: 'This grid is already launched on LOCAL and partially complete' is not true. No canvas-grid script exists (`grep -rln canvas /apdcephfs_wzc1/share_304376610/pighzliu_code/dllm_draft/scripts/*.sh` returns only _run_ar_baseline_104.sh, and only in a comment); no runs/ dir matches canvas|grid|factorial. LOCAL's 3 busy GPUs are running generate_evalplus_scaffold.py --output-dir runs/scaffold_large_mbppplus_budget1024 (PIDs 335200/335201/335205, 2h23m elapsed) = the MBPP+ Large@1024 job from the brief. Offsetting good news: the candidate's 'needs canvas/steps decoupling (trivial, one argument)' overstates the work -- scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py:106-107 ALREADY has independent --steps and --max-new-tokens; only the launchers hardcode them equal. Zero code change to the generator; only a new launcher.

DESIGN IS 37% DEGENERATE -- 6 of the 16 proposed cells are bit-identical duplicates. models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B/generation_utils.py:406,439 sets timesteps=linspace(1,eps,steps+1) and commits int(nmask*(1-s/t)) per step, so when steps>canvas most steps commit ZERO tokens. I verified analytically AND on GPU (seeded, bit-compared decoded text): canvas=256/steps=384 and canvas=256/steps=512 produce output IDENTICAL to canvas=256/steps=256 (1.11x and 1.51x slower); canvas=128/steps=256 and 512 IDENTICAL to canvas=128/steps=128 (1.26x, 2.57x slower). Dead-forward counts: 128x512 = 385 dead of 512; 256x512 = 257 dead of 255 useful. So {128,256,384,512}^2 contains only 10 informative cells (lower triangle + diagonal). Reporting 16 would fabricate 6 independent data points that are byte-equal. This also CONFIRMS the candidate's unverified leg-1 claim (verification_notes item 7) -- steps>canvas does produce dead forwards -- but with a stronger consequence than the candidate draws: the upper triangle cannot be a confound because it is not even a distinct operating point.

FATAL IDENTIFICATION FLAW: canvas is algebraically determined by the other two factors, so 'canvas x steps' is NOT a factorial that separates canvas from parallelism. In the informative (lower-triangle) region every step commits, so canvas == n_forwards x mean_tokens_per_forward exactly. Three quantities, two degrees of freedom, perfect collinearity. Consequence: the candidate's named decisive cell -- canvas256/steps256 vs canvas512/steps256 -- holds forwards fixed at 256 but moves tokens-committed-per-forward from 1.00 to 2.00. I computed the full table: at steps=128, canvas {128,256,384,512} give parallelism {1.01,2.00,3.00,4.00}. So the 'canvas effect at matched steps' IS, definitionally, a parallel-decoding effect at matched forwards -- territory ParallelBench (2510.04767) owns, and the one related-work row the positioning admits it could not read in full. Every headline number in leg 2 is exposed to 'you measured parallelism and called it canvas.'

COST MODEL IN THE CLAIM IS WRONG. The claim asserts dead canvas positions are 'attended at full quadratic cost on every forward pass.' At this model's shape (config.json: 28 layers, hidden 3584, intermediate 18944, 4 KV heads) the quadratic attention term is 0.79% of per-token FLOPs at width 301, 1.78% at 685, 3.06% at 1197. Measured per-step latency on an idle L20A (canvas 128->512): 14.27 -> 18.98 ms = 1.331x, while attended width grows 2.276x -- sublinear, not quadratic. The 685-tok/step figure is a WIDTH COUNT, not a cost. 'Forwarded token-positions' as the proposed cost unit is therefore itself a mis-specified unit (it implicitly assumes cost is linear in width, which I measured it is not) -- the same class of error as the retracted 'NFE as a cross-family cost unit.'

OUR OWN METRICS CANNOT SUPPORT THE ACCOUNTING LEG AS RECORDED. generate_evalplus_dream.py:258-263 writes process={'nfe': args.steps, 'generated_tokens': len(generated_ids), ...}. Verified on disk: runs/dream_instruct_heplus_nfe1024 records nfe=1024 (NOMINAL -- actually 510 useful + 514 dead forwards) and generated_tokens=512 in EVERY row of every run (unique set = [512]) because the sampler returns the full padded canvas. So 'generated_tokens' is the canvas, not the realized length, and 'nfe' is nominal steps, not work done. Missing fields needed: useful (non-zero-commit) forwards, realized pre-pad length, measured per-step latency, attended width.

KILL CRITERION IS BELOW THE NOISE FLOOR. It specifies 'within noise (<3 pts, HE+ n=164)'. At n=164, p=0.7 the SE of a single proportion is 3.58 pts -- the declared decision threshold is smaller than one standard error, so an unpaired comparison cannot reach it. No pairing (McNemar / paired bootstrap on the same task IDs) and no seed replication is specified anywhere in the experiment plan, and temperature is 0.1 (stochastic), not greedy.

SATURATION IS MOSTLY DIFFICULTY, CONFIRMED BY A TEST THE POSITIONING DID NOT RUN. I scored CANVAS-FREE decoders on the strata defined by Dream's 512-canvas saturation. scaffold_medium/large (typed-AST runtime, no flat canvas at all): pass on saturated vs non-saturated .086 vs .265 (HE+, gap +0.179) and .222 vs .479 (MBPP+, +0.257). DreamOn: .012 vs .229 (+0.217) and .024 vs .133 (+0.109). Decoders with no 512 canvas find the 'saturated' tasks far harder, so the strata differ in intrinsic difficulty. Also unstable: dream_s256 on HE+ shows gap -0.001 (no gap at all at a different operating point). The truncation reading is dead; the 1024-canvas difficulty control is mandatory, not a robustness check.

ParallelBench (2510.04767) full text still unread (positioning verification_notes item 3 flags this as lower-confidence). Given the collinearity finding above it is promoted from 'contrast' to the PRIMARY novelty threat and must be read before any writing.

STEP 0 (no GPU, ~1h) -- RESPECIFY THE DESIGN BEFORE SPENDING ANY GPU
Drop the 6 degenerate cells. Run only the 10 informative cells of {128,256,384,512}^2 (steps <= canvas). Reparametrize the axes as (n_forwards, canvas) and report mean_tokens_per_forward = canvas/n_forwards as a DERIVED third column, never as an independent factor. Rewrite the claim: not "we cross canvas and steps" (impossible -- see gap 3) but "the two free decoding factors are forwards and parallelism; canvas is their product, and no prior paper reports the third."

STEP 1 (small build, ~3h, no GPU) -- THE REQUIRED CONTROL AND THE INSTRUMENTATION
1a. Inert-width control. models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B/generation_utils.py:305 accepts generation_tokens_hook_func and calls it at step None (line 409) and after every step (line 455); the hook already receives and may return x. Add a NEW launcher-side hook (do not touch the model dir) that at step None overwrites canvas positions [m:] with pad_token_id 151643 so they are never masks. Then n_forwards, tokens-per-forward AND the mask count are all held fixed while attended width varies. This is the only way to break the canvas = forwards x parallelism collinearity. Ship it as a --inert-width N flag in a COPY of scripts/generate_evalplus_dream.py (e.g. scripts/generate_evalplus_dream_canvas.py) so the existing baseline script stays byte-stable for reproducibility.
1b. Accounting fields. In the copy, replace process={'nfe': args.steps, 'generated_tokens': len(generated_ids)} with: nominal_steps, useful_forwards (steps where the commit count was > 0), realized_length (index of first pad/eos in the returned canvas, NOT len(generated_ids)), attended_width, per_step_latency_ms, and keep raw_output. Assert realized_length <= canvas.
1c. Degeneracy guard. Emit a sha256 of the decoded raw_output per (task, cell). Post-hoc, assert no two cells in the grid share an identical hash vector; if any do, the cell is dropped from the results table rather than reported.

STEP 2 (GPU ~2.2 h) -- HE+ CORE GRID, n=164, 10 informative cells
Reuse the r2 protocol exactly (T=0.1, top_p=0.95, chat template on, alg=entropy, alg_temp=0) so cell (512,512) is validated against the existing runs/dream_coder_instruct_heplus_r2 number .707 as a regression check. Cells: (canvas,steps) = (128,128),(256,128),(256,256),(384,128),(384,256),(384,384),(512,128),(512,256),(512,384),(512,512). 8-way shard as the existing launchers do. Measured basis for the estimate: r2 HE+ = 11.31 s/task at (512,512) = 0.52 gpu-h for the whole benchmark; per-step latency I measured is 14.27/15.11/17.21/18.98 ms at canvas 128/256/384/512.

STEP 3 (GPU ~6.6 h) -- SEEDS, because the kill criterion is currently unreachable
3 seeds on all 10 HE+ cells. Analyze PAIRED on task_id (McNemar + paired bootstrap over the 164 tasks), not as independent proportions. State the achieved minimum detectable paired effect in the paper; if it exceeds 3 pts, revise the kill threshold rather than the conclusion.

STEP 4 (GPU ~1.8 h) -- THE INERT-WIDTH ARM (the control from Step 1a)
At n_forwards = 256 and mask count = 256, run attended width in {256, 384, 512, 1024} via --inert-width. This is the ONLY arm that can attribute an effect to width/padding per se. If quality is flat here but varies across the matched-steps grid, the grid effect is parallelism, not canvas -- and the paper must say so.

STEP 5 (GPU ~1.8 h) -- 1024-CANVAS DIFFICULTY CONTROL, now mandatory (see gap 7)
Cells (1024,1024) and (1024,256) on HE+. Test whether the 81 saturated tasks stay harder when they cannot saturate. Combine with the canvas-free evidence I already generated in this audit (scaffold and DreamOn scored on the same strata) as a zero-GPU corroboration.

STEP 6 (GPU ~2.6 h) -- MBPP+ n=378, diagonal + 2 off-diagonals
(128,128),(256,256),(512,512),(512,256),(512,128). Cell (512,512) regression-checks against runs/dream_coder_instruct_mbppplus_r2 = .683.

STEP 7 (GPU ~1 h) -- COST RE-PRICING, replacing the false quadratic claim
Profile measured per-step latency and a FLOP decomposition (linear vs quadratic term) across width on one idle GPU. Report cost as measured wall clock plus a FLOP model with the linear/quadratic split shown explicitly. Do NOT use forwarded token-positions as the headline unit; it assumes linearity in width that I measured to be false (1.331x latency for 2.276x width).

STEP 8 (no GPU) -- SELF-AUDIT LEG, and it is now sharper than the candidate states
Re-price the surviving scaffold-vs-flat Pareto. The 685 tok/step figure is a width count and the per-step cost is sublinear in width, so the token-cost-matched crossover is mis-specified in BOTH directions (canvas is a free parameter AND the unit is wrong). feas.risk: The most likely bad outcome is a CONFOUNDED POSITIVE, not a null, and it is the same shape as all three prior retractions: the grid will almost certainly show quality falling as canvas rises at matched steps, the paper will report it as "the canvas confound," and a reviewer will observe that canvas == n_forwards x tokens_per_forward identically, so at matched steps the only thing that moved was parallel decoding -- 1.00 vs 2.00 vs 4.00 tokens committed per forward. That is ParallelBench's published result relabeled, and ParallelBench is the one related-work row nobody in this project has read in full. The candidate's own named decisive cell (canvas256/steps256 vs canvas512/steps256) is exactly this trap. Secondary risk, an underpowered null: n=164 with a declared 3-point threshold sits below the 3.58-point SE of a single proportion at p=0.7, so without paired analysis and seeds the grid returns differences inside noise and cannot distinguish "canvas is flat at matched steps" (the stated kill condition) from "we had no power." Third, a fabricated-design risk if the 16-cell grid is reported as specified: 6 of those cells return byte-identical text to the diagonal, so 6 of 16 "measurements" would be duplicates presented as evidence. Fourth, the abstract as written would ship two statements I measured to be false -- that dead canvas positions cost "full quadratic" (measured 0.8-3.1% quadratic share; latency sublinear in width) and that the pass-rate gap is a truncation artifact (canvas-free decoders reproduce most of the gap).
feas.required_control:
THE INERT-WIDTH CONTROL: hold n_forwards AND mask-count AND tokens-committed-per-forward all fixed, and vary ONLY the attended width by pre-filling the surplus canvas with PAD (id 151643) instead of MASK, via the generation_tokens_hook_func at step None (already plumbed: models/Dream-Coder-v0-Instruct-7B/generation_utils.py:305, called at 409 and 455). Concretely: mask-count 256, forwards 256, attended width in {256,384,512,1024}.

Why this is the control that prevents a fourth retraction. The three prior retractions share one shape: a quantity was believed to be measuring X while it was mechanically measuring something else (a verifier that compared nothing; a refinement stage that discarded the scaffold and measured Dream-Coder instead; a cost average that silently excluded the expensive tasks). This candidate's headline number has that exact shape. I verified from the sampler source and by simulation that in the informative region canvas is not a free variable at all -- canvas == forwards x parallelism, an algebraic identity -- so "the effect of canvas at matched steps" cannot be distinguished from "the effect of parallel decoding at matched forwards" by ANY cell of the proposed grid. Without the inert-width arm the paper would announce a canvas confound while having measured a parallelism effect that ParallelBench already published: a pipeline that silently substitutes its input variable, retraction #2 with different nouns.

Two cheap guards ride along, each blocking one prior failure mode directly. (a) Degeneracy hashing: sha256 the decoded output per (task, cell) and assert no two grid cells share an identical hash vector before anything enters a table -- I confirmed on GPU that canvas256 x steps{384,512} and canvas128 x steps{256,512} are bit-identical to their diagonals, so without this guard 6 duplicate cells get reported as independent evidence (the "dropped/duplicated rows" family, retraction #3). (b) Realized-length instrumentation: the current process dict records generated_tokens=512 in every row of every run because the sampler returns the padded canvas, and nfe=nominal steps rather than useful forwards. Any saturation or cost statistic computed from those fields is measuring the canvas setting, not the output -- so log realized pre-pad length and useful (non-zero-commit) forwards, and assert realized_length <= canvas per row.
